It is located in the village of Revsnes, near the bridge to the island of Stokkøya. The church is located right at the south end of the Stokkøy Bridge from the mainland to the island of Stokkøya. It is one of two churches in the Åfjord og Stoksund parish which is part of the Fosen prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The red, wooden church was built in a cruciform style in 1825 using plans drawn up by the architect Christian Ancher Collett and another unknown architect. The church seats about 200 people.

storfosna-kirke-Q7620013.d: Storfosna Church (Norwegian: Storfosna kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Ørland Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located on the island of Storfosna. It is one of the churches for the Ørland parish which is part of the Fosen prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1913 using plans drawn up by the architect Johan Kunig. The church seats about 150 people. The church has about 12 scheduled Sunday worship services per year.

storsteinnes-kapell-Q7620344.d: Storsteinnes Chapel (Norwegian: Storsteinnes kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Balsfjord Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located on the south side of the village of Storsteinnes. It is one of the churches for the Balsfjord parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1968. The church seats about 200 people.

strinda-kirke-Q7623891.d: Strinda Church (Norwegian: Strinda kirke, historically Moholt kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the Strinda area in the city of Trondheim. It is the church for the Strinda parish which is part of the Strinda prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in a cruciform design with a Neo-Gothic style in 1900 using plans drawn up by the architects Lars Solberg and Johan Christensen. The church seats about 300 people.

strindheim-kirke-Q7623893.d: Strindheim Church (Norwegian: Strindheim kirke, historically: Bromstad kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the Strindheim area in the city of Trondheim. It is the church for the Strindheim parish which is part of the Strinda prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The modern, red, brick church was built in a rectangular style in 1979 using plans drawn up by the architect Elisabeth Fidjestøl. The church seats about 240 people.

stugudal-kapell-Q7628576.d: Stugudal Chapel (Norwegian: Stugudal kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tydal Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the village of Stugudalen, about 20 kilometres (12 mi) southeast of the municipal center of Ås. It is one of the churches for the Tydal parish which is part of the Stjørdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The red, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1957 by the architect John Egil Tverdahl. The church seats about 124 people.

sula-kapell-Q7635934.d: Sula Chapel (Norwegian: Sula kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Frøya Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located on the island of Sula. It is one of several churches for the Frøya parish which is part of the Orkdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in a long church design in 1925 using plans drawn up by the architect Martin Pettersen. The church seats about 200 people.

bryn-stasjon-Q764143.d: Bryn Station (Norwegian: Bryn stasjon) is a railway station on the Trunk Line located in the Bryn neighborhood of the Gamle Oslo borough of Oslo, Norway. Situated 3.89 kilometers (2.42 mi) from Oslo Central Station, it features two platforms. The Loenga–Alnabru Line passes through the station without a platform. Bryn is served by the L1 line of Vy's Oslo Commuter Rail. The station is also nearby Bryn school. The station was opened on 1 September 1854, but was originally only a halt to test brakes. Ticket sales commenced in 1858. A new, brick station building was erected in 1884.

susendal-kirke-Q7648858.d: Susendal Church (Norwegian: Susendal kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Hattfjelldal Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Svenskvollen in the Susendal valley. It is one of the churches for the Hattfjelldal parish which is part of the Indre Helgeland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The brown, wooden church was built in a long church style in 2001 using plans drawn up by the architect Jim Inge Bøasæter. The church seats about 150 people.

saheim-kraftverk-Q7665805.d: The Såheim Power Station is a hydroelectric power station located in Rjukan, Telemark, Norway, operated by Norsk Hydro. It operates at an installed capacity of 185 MW, with an average annual production of 1,033 GWh. The station building from 1915 was designed by architects Thorvald Astrup and Olaf Nordhagen.

fjernsynshuset-Q7696959.d: The Television House (Norwegian: Fjernsynshuset) is one of the main buildings at NRK headquarters at Marienlyst in Oslo. The other main building is the Broadcasting House. The building was designed by Nils Holter and Jan Bauck and opened in 1969. News productions at the Television House include content for Dagsrevyen (TV), Dagsnytt (radio), NRK Nyheter (radio), and online news services.

tempe-kirke-Q7698248.d: Tempe Church (Norwegian: Tempe kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the Lerkendal area in the city of Trondheim, between the old European route E6 highway and Lerkendal Stadion. It is one of the churches for the Nidelven parish which is part of the Strinda prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white plastered brick church was built in a long church style in 1960 using plans drawn up by the architect Roar Tønseth. The church seats about 240 people.

terningmoen-Q7702950.d: Terningmoen is a military camp (or base) in Elverum Municipality, Norway. The base trains and houses parts of the Norwegian Army such as: His Majesty the King's Guard (HMKG) (First two months of service) Norwegian Home Guard HV-05 (district 5 of the Home Guard) Norwegian Military Academy (The first year) Some TRADOK-units (Norwegian army transformation - and doctrine commando) Forsvarets Logistikkorganisasjon (FLO) (Logistics and support) The base is also the location of a guard company "Vakt og Sikring Kompani Østerdalen", which has the responsibility of the protection of the camp.

aulestad-Q771841.d: Aulestad is a farm and writer's house museum in Follebu in Innlandet county, Norway. It is located along County Road Fv255 (Bjørnsonvegen) between Vinstra and Hovemoen. The farm is best known as the former residence of Karoline and Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson. Nobel Laureate Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson lived here with his family from 1875 until his death in 1910. The farm is still owned by members of the Bjørnson family. The manor was added to The Sandvig Collections at Lillehammer after Karoline Bjørnson's death in 1934. In 1935 Aulestad opened as a museum. It serves as a museum of Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson's life and work. Since 2011.

sr-fron-kirke-Q7723954.d: Sør-Fron Church (Norwegian: Sør-Fron kyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Sør-Fron Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. It is located in the village of Hundorp. It is the church for the Sør-Fron parish which is part of the Sør-Gudbrandsdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Hamar. The white, stone church was built in an octagonal design in 1792 using plans drawn up by the architect Svend Aspaas. The church seats about 750 people. Because of size (750 seats) and central location in the Gudbrandsdalen valley, it has been nicknamed the Gudbrandsdalen cathedral (Norwegian: Gudbrandsdalsdomen).

lindesnes-fyr-Q773320.d: Lindesnes Lighthouse (Norwegian: Lindesnes fyr) is a coastal lighthouse at the southernmost tip of Norway, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) southwest of the village of Høllen in Lindesnes Municipality in Agder county. The present lighthouse was built at the southern tip of the Lindesnes peninsula in 1915, although the station was first built in 1656 to mark the entrance to the Skagerrak and the Baltic Sea from the North Sea. The current 16.1-metre (53 ft) tall lighthouse is cast iron with a granite foundation. The lighthouse is painted white, with a red top. The light sits at an elevation of 50.

alnes-fyr-Q773792.d: Alnes Lighthouse (Norwegian: Alnes fyrstasjon) was established in 1852 to guide fishing boats safely to the harbor of the small fishing community of Alnes on the north side of the island of Godøya in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The lighthouse sits about 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) northwest of Leitebakk.

kjeungskjr-fyr-Q773807.d: The Kjeungskjær Lighthouse (Norwegian: Kjeungskjær fyr) is a coastal lighthouse in Ørland Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. The lighthouse is located on a tiny island at the mouth of the Bjugnfjorden about 3.5 kilometres (2.2 mi) west of the village of Uthaug and 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) south of the village of Nes.

colosseum-kino-Q774976.d: The Colosseum Kino in Oslo, Norway is the largest cinema in Northern Europe and the largest THX cinema in the world. It is distinguished by its large spherical dome.

kongsseteren-Q7761700.d: The Royal Lodge or The Royal Villa (Norwegian: Kongsseteren, The King's Seter) is located in Holmenkollen in Oslo, Norway, and is in the Norwegian royal family's private possession. The property is used mainly in winter, and the royal family usually celebrates Christmas there, and stays at the Royal Lodge during the Holmenkollen Ski Festival every year. King Haakon VII and Queen Maud received the Royal Lodge as a gift from the Norwegian people for the coronation in 1906. It was financed by a fundraising campaign. The villa was designed by architect Kristian Hjalmar Biong, who won the architectural competition with their project "Slot over Slot.

titran-kapell-Q7810227.d: Titran Chapel (Norwegian: Titran kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Frøya Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the village of Titran on the western tip of the island of Frøya. It is one of several churches for the Frøya parish which is part of the Orkdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in an octagonal design in 1873 by the builder Petter Snekker. The church seats about 200 people.

tovik-kirke-Q7829488.d: Tovik Church (Norwegian: Tovik kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tjeldsund Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Tovik. It is the church for the Tovik parish which is part of the Trondenes prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1905 using plans drawn up by the architect N. Saxegaard. The church seats about 200 people.

trandumskogen-Q7833396.d: Trandumskogen is a forest located in Ullensaker, Akershus county, Norway. It was the site of one of the first discoveries in May 1945 of German mass graves in Norway. The German executioner Oscar Hans was the officer in command of the unit performing the executions. In total 173 Norwegians, 6 British and 15 Soviet citizens were executed in Trandumskogen. Many had been sentenced to death by the German occupation forces, but there was also a great number who were subject to arbitrary executions. Most were resistance fighters, while the Russians were prisoners in German prison camps who had tried to escape.

trany-fyr-Q7835513.d: Tranøy Lighthouse (Norwegian: Tranøy fyr) is a coastal lighthouse in Hamarøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located along the Vestfjorden, about 2.5 kilometres (1.6 mi) west of the village of Tranøy.

trefoldighetskirken-Q7842656.d: Trinity Church (Norwegian: Trefoldighetskirken) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Arendal Municipality in Agder county, Norway. It is located in the central part of the town of Arendal. It is the church for the Trefoldighet parish. It is also the seat of the Arendal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Agder og Telemark. The red, brick, neo-Gothic church was built in a cruciform basilica design in 1888 using plans drawn up by the architect Christian Fürst. The church seats about 850 people.

ulvysund-Q7880876.d: Ulvøysund is a village and an outport in Lillesand Municipality in Agder county, Norway. The village lies on the east side of the Kvåsefjorden on the island of Ulvøya. Just northeast of Ulvøysund is the entrance to the Blindleia inland waterway which leads towards the town of Lillesand. The village is connected to the mainland by road. The nearby village of Ribe lies about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) straight north of Ulvøysund. The village was historically used as an outport along the Skagerrak coast for the large ships that couldn't navigate inland through the archipelago to the towns on the mainland.

valkyrie-plass-Q7911778.d: Valkyrie plass is a square in Oslo, Norway, located one block southeast of Majorstuen. The square is triangular in shape, and bounded by the streets Valkyriegata, Bogstadveien and Jacob Aall's gate. It is named after Norse female warrior deities called the valkyries. The Common Tunnel of the Oslo T-bane system passes beneath Valkyrie plass, and there was a station beneath the square from 1912 to 1985. The station was built there due to a tunnel collapse when 800 cubic metres of rock fell into the tunnel under construction. On 7 January 1985 the station, which was very close to Majorstuen station was closed. The square is still served by the Oslo Tramway with two tram lines.

vanylven-kirke-Q7915283.d: Vanylven Church (Norwegian: Vanylven kyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Vanylven Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located in the village of Slagnes, on the shore of the Vanylvsfjorden. It is the church for the Vanylven parish which is part of the Søre Sunnmøre prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Møre. The white, plastered brick church was built in a rectangular design in 1864 using plans drawn up by the architect Georg Andreas Bull. The church seats about 320 people.

vard-fyr-Q7915576.d: Vardø Lighthouse (Norwegian: Vardø fyr) is a coastal lighthouse located on the island of Hornøya, just off the coast of the town of Vardø in Vardø Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is the easternmost lighthouse in Norway.

vassfjellkapellet-Q7916936.d: Vassfjell Chapel (Norwegian: Vassfjellkapellet) is a chapel in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in a rural area northeast of the mountain Vassfjellet, about 1.5 kilometres (0.93 mi) west of the village of Tanem. There is no direct road access to the chapel, but there is a 1-kilometre (0.62 mi) long hiking path from a parking lot located on the road to the north. It is an annex chapel for the Klæbu parish which is part of the Heimdal og Byåsen prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1974 by the architect students Steinar Romedal, Jan Oddvar Hareide, I. Tolo, and O. Holen.

vega-kirke-Q7918256.d: Vega Church (Norwegian: Vega kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Vega Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Gladstad on the island of Vega in the Vegaøyan archipelago. It is the main church for the Vega parish which is part of the Sør-Helgeland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1863 to replace an older church. The building was consecrated on 14 July 1864 by the Bishop Carl Peter Parelius Essendrop. The church seats about 430 people.

vigelandmuseet-Q7928869.d: The Vigeland Museum (Norwegian: Vigelandmuseet) is a museum dedicated to Gustav Vigeland in Frogner, Oslo. It is located outside Frogner Park, which includes the Vigeland installation with sculptures by Gustav Vigeland. Inside the park, close to Vigeland Museum, is Frogner Manor with Oslo Museum and the Henriette Wegner Pavilion, a small art gallery. The museum is dedicated to Norway's most famous sculptor, Gustav Vigeland (1869–1943). The museum is Vigeland's former studio and residence. His urn and ashes are located in the tower of the museum. He designed his own bronze urn and burial monument, located above his apartment on the 2nd floor.

villa-fyr-Q7930388.d: Villa Lighthouse (Norwegian: Villa fyrstasjon) is a deactivated lighthouse in Flatanger Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. The lighthouse was built in 1839 and it was decommissioned in 1890. Villa Lighthouse is located on the island of Villa in the Folda sea. The 15-metre (49 ft) tall tower was built of granite, soapstone, and brick. It was constructed in a hexagonal shape. The lighthouse was built in 1839 and was the first lighthouse in Norway that was built north of the Trondheimsfjord. It was one of the six coal-fired lighthouses built in Norway during the 1800s, and it is generally considered to be the best preserved of them all. In 1859, it was upgraded to burn liquid fuels.

dal-stasjon-Q798535.d: Dal is a railway station located in Dal in Eidsvoll, Norway. The station is located upon the Trunk Line and was opened in 1854. The station is served by commuter trains with hourly services to Oslo Central Station and Drammen Station, a service which Dal functions as the terminal station for.

afjord-kirke-Q8077109.d: Åfjord Church (Norwegian: Åfjord kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Åfjord Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the village of Årnes, just east of the Åfjorden and west of the lake Stordalsvatnet. It is one of two churches in the Åfjord og Stoksund parish which is part of the Fosen prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1879 using plans drawn up by the architect Knut Guttormsen. The church seats 430 people. It was consecrated on 9 October 1879 by Bishop Andreas Grimelund.

akersvika-Q8077146.d: Åkersvika is a 424-hectare (1,050-acre) wetland nature reserve and Ramsar site in Hamar, Norway. It became Norway's first Ramsar site in 1974. Vikingskipet, the speed skating venue for the 1994 Winter Olympics, was built in the site, creating controversy. European Route E6 also runs through the site, and the Norwegian Public Roads Administration has plans to expand the road to a four-lane motorway.

rland-kirke-Q8079226.d: Ørland Church (Norwegian: Ørland kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Ørland Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the town of Brekstad, along the Trondheimsfjorden. It is one of the churches for the Ørland parish which is part of the Fosen prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, stone church was built in a long church style during the 12th century. The church seats about 330 people.

verbygd-kirke-Q8079277.d: Øverbygd Church (Norwegian: Øverbygd kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Målselv Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the Øverbygd area of Målselv Municipality, about 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) southwest of the village of Skjold. It is the main church for the Øverbygd parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1867 by the architect Jacob Wilhelm Nordan. The church seats about 280 people. The church was consecrated by Bishop Carl Peter Parelius Essendrop.

baroniet-rosendal-Q808714.d: Barony Rosendal (Norwegian: Baroniet Rosendal) is a historic estate and manor house situated in the village of Rosendal in Kvinnherad Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. The barony was built in the 17th century by Danish noblemen on the old estate of the Norwegian noble Galte family, the current barony estate making out the historical farms of Hatteberg, Mel and Eik.

basarene-Q809780.d: Oslo Bazaars (Basarene Kirkeristen) are located at Oslo Cathedral, along the streets Karl Johans gate and Dronningens gate in Oslo, Norway. The buildings of the bazaar constitute a continuous facility that encircles three sides of the quarter with Oslo Cathedral.

bergen-domkirke-Q819531.d: Bergen Cathedral (Norwegian: Bergen domkirke) is a cathedral in the city of Bergen in Vestland county, Norway. It is the episcopal seat of the Church of Norway's Diocese of Bjørgvin as well as the seat of the "Bergen domkirke" parish and the seat of the Bergen domprosti (arch-deanery). It is part of the Church of Norway. The first recorded historical reference to this church is dated 1181. It retains its ancient dedication to Saint Olaf. The cathedral seats about 600 people.

flavr-fyr-Q821462.d: Flåvær fyr is a coastal lighthouse in Herøy Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The lighthouse is located on the island of Vardholmen which is in the Flåværet archipelago in the Herøyfjorden. The lighthouse is located southwest of the town of Fosnavåg and the village of Eggesbønes and it is located north of the island of Gurskøya. The 13.8-metre (45 ft) tall lighthouse was first built in 1870, and it was renovated in 1887 and 1914. In 1952 it was connected to the electrical power grid, and it was fully automated in 1979.

hidra-kirke-Q8262682.d: Hidra Church (Norwegian: Hidra kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in the large Flekkefjord Municipality in Agder county, Norway. It is located in the village of Kirkehamn on the island of Hidra. It is the church for the Hidra parish which is part of the Lister og Mandal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Agder og Telemark. The white, wooden church was built in a octagonal design in 1854 using plans drawn up by the architect Christian Heinrich Grosch. The church seats about 700 people.

vegayene-Q829084.d: Vegaøyan (Norwegian) or the Vega Archipelago (English) is a group of islands in the Norwegian Sea in Nordland county, Norway. The archipelago is mostly located in Vega Municipality. Since 2004, the archipelago has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This cluster of around 6,500 small islands just south of the Arctic Circle, surrounds the main island of Vega and has been inhabited since the Stone Age. Other larger islands in the group include Igerøya, Ylvingen, and Søla.

hove-kirke-Q847909.d: Hove Church (Norwegian: Hove kyrkje) is a historic parish church of the Church of Norway in Vik Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Vikøyri on the Arnafjord, an arm of the Sognefjord. It was historically the main church for Hove parish in the Diocese of Bjørgvin. The gray, stone church was built in a long church design in a Romanesque style around the year 1170 using plans drawn up by unknown architect. Since about 2016 the church has been the base for the Hove Church Music Festival (Hove kyrkjemusikkfestival) run by local cultural personality, Jens Brekke, and an American early music chamber choir. The church seats about 35 people.

heddal-stavkirke-Q852020.d: Heddal Stave Church (Bokmål: Heddal stavkirke, Nynorsk: Heddal stavkyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Notodden Municipality in Telemark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Heddal. It is the church for the Heddal parish which is part of the Øvre Telemark prosti in the Diocese of Agder og Telemark. The wooden, triple nave stave church was built in a long church design around the year 1200 using plans drawn up by an unknown architect. The church seats about 180 people. The church is one of the 28 surviving stave churches in Norway and it is considered to be the largest of the stave churches.

det-kongelige-slott-Q863932.d: The Royal Palace (Norwegian: Slottet or Det kongelige slott) in Oslo was built in the first half of the 19th century as the Norwegian residence of the French-born Charles XIV John, who reigned as king of Norway and Sweden. The palace is the official residence of the current Norwegian monarch while the crown prince resides at Skaugum in Asker west of Oslo. The palace is located at the end of Karl Johans gate in central Oslo and is surrounded by the Palace Park with the Palace Square in the front.

stensgard-kirke-Q8731323.d: Stensgård Church (Norwegian: Stensgård kirke) is "long church" (Norwegian: langkirke) dating from 1902 in the municipality of Nannestad in Akershus county, Norway. The church is part of the Church of Norway and it belongs to the deanery of Øvre Romerike in the Diocese of Borg. The building can accommodate 92 people. The cornerstone was laid in a simple ceremony on Saint John's Day in 1901. It was consecrated on November 26, 1902 in a mass celebrated by Bishop Anton Christian Bang attended by eight priests.

ullensaker-kirke-Q8732384.d: Ullensaker Church is a church in Ullensaker, Norway, located 10 km (6.21 mi) southeast of Oslo Airport, Gardermoen. It is the fourth church that has been located almost there since the 12th century. The present church was built in concrete in 1958 and has been given the nickname "Romeriksdomen" ("The Romerike Cathedral") locally because of its monumental character.

bryn-kirke-Q8733240.d: Bryn Church (Norwegian: Bryn kirke) is a long church (Norwegian: langkirke) located in Rykkinn in the municipality of Bærum in Akershus county, Norway. The church functions both as a road church and is the parish church for Bryn.

hvik-kirke-Q8734139.d: Høvik Church is a cruciform church in Bærum in Akershus county, Norway. The building is in brick and has 500 seats.

tanum-kirke-Q8734962.d: Tanum Church (Tanum kirke) is a church located at Bærum in Akershus county, Norway.

bjrnsund-fyr-Q879885.d: Bjørnsund Lighthouse (Norwegian: Bjørnsund fyr) is a coastal lighthouse in Hustadvika Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The lighthouse is located on the small island of Moøya in the Bjørnsund islands, about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) west of the village of Bud on the mainland.

solum-prestegard-Q67179756.d: Solum Vicarage is situated to the south-west of Solum Church, on the other side of Klovholtvegen. Three buildings in the vicarage grounds are listed: the main building, the tenant’s cottage and a gazebo. The main building is a two-storey log-built structure with vertical panelling and a hipped roof. The building was originally constructed in 1715, but was rebuilt several times during the 19th century and has had its current appearance since 1842. According to the Opplysningsvesenets fond, the tenant’s house dates from the 19th century, whilst the age of the gazebo appears to be unknown. The main building and the tenant’s house were painted in the summer of 2018.

klostergata-20-Q67206692.d: Klostergata 20 is a listed property, situated near Moss town centre. The property is currently listed under the Planning and Building Act. The house is considered worthy of preservation due to its age and the fact that it forms part of a historic setting along Kongeveien.

klostergata-22-Q67206713.d: Klostergata 22 is a detached house, situated on Klostergata in Moss. The building is listed under the Planning and Building Act. The house is worthy of preservation due to its age and its significance as part of an old street setting in Moss. The house was built in the Swiss style before 1885. It has pointed roof pitches facing east and west, and a monopitch roof facing east.

klostergata-24-Q67206760.d: Klostergata 24 is situated in Moss, where the property is zoned for residential use under the 2005 local development plan. The house is currently listed under the Planning and Building Act (BPL). The date of listing was 4 January 2018. The building underwent renovation following its registration with the Norwegian Cultural Heritage Register in 1986. Klostergata got its name because the first section of the route from Moss to Værne Abbey in Rygge begins here. Furthermore, Klostergata was formerly part of a road known as Kongeveien. This road stretched all the way from Oslo to Copenhagen and was extremely important for the transport of goods, the spread of news and cultural influences. The street on which the house stood was formerly a craftsmen’s street.

det-ankerske-waisenhus-Q67365894.d: The Anker Orphanage is a foundation established in 1778 by Bernt Anker and his wife Mathia Collett. The aim was to establish and run an orphanage in Christiania, which would care for and bring up children aged 7–13, until they reached the age of 16. Priority was given to orphaned children from the civil service and middle classes, and in particular to children in need who were related to the Anker family. The orphanage was initially housed in a detached property with a garden between Grensen and Akersgata, but had to cease operations in 1822 when the foundation lost its initial capital. The sale of property and donations enabled operations to resume in 1848, and the foundation then purchased Akersveien 31, where it was able to resume its activities from 1851.

klostergata-26-Q67380686.d: Klostergata 26 is a plot of land on Klostergata in Moss where (as of 2025) there are four buildings: Klostergata 26 (built before 1807), 26A (built in 1807), 26B (built between 1904 and 1914) and a storeroom. All the buildings were listed on 4 January 2018 under the Planning and Building Act. Many of the houses in Klostergata were listed because they were considered worthy of preservation due to their age and authenticity. The houses are also representative as part of a historic street setting along Kongeveien. Klostergata was formerly a street of craftsmen and a working-class neighbourhood, and stood in contrast to Skarmyra.

klostergata-6-Q67380783.d: Klostergata 6 is a block of flats, formerly a farmstead, situated on Klostergata in the ‘centre’ of Moss. The block was listed in 2018 under the Planning and Building Act. The old farmhouse at Klostergata 6 was built in the Empire style in the Klommesten district; the name Klostergaten was adopted in 1882, having previously been known as Radet until that year. From 1907, it was given the modernised name Klostergata. Until 1957, it formed part of National Road 1 from Oslo, which, within the town limits, ran from Kambo to Tigerplassen, down Verket, Kongens gate and Klostergata before continuing on to Halden. The street now runs from Innfartsveien southwards to the junction of Ryggeveien and Dyreveien. Previously, it began as an extension of Kongens gate, at the current traffic lights junction.

klostergata-8-Q67380860.d: Klostergata 8 is a residential property on Klostergata in Moss. The house was used as a butcher’s residence in the 19th and 20th centuries. The house is listed under the Planning and Building Act. The house was built around the 1850s and is situated next to Klostergata 8A (Moss), which was probably built around the 1930s. This is confirmed by its functionalist architecture. The addresses were separated in 1960.

kapteinsgarden-i-uskedal-Q67519027.d: Kapteinsgården in Uskedal is a listed officers’ residence dating from the 18th century, situated in Uskedal in the municipality of Kvinnherad. The house was built by Johan Koren Dahl, commander of the Northern Sunnhordland Company, in 1775; at that time, the sea reached right up to the garden beside the house. He was the son of Mathias Dahl, the steward of the barony of Rosendal until 1746 and a war commissioner. The house was later named after Captain Christian Lerche Dahl, who, amongst other things, served as mayor of Kvinnherad for a time in the early 19th century. The Dahl family owned large estates throughout Western Norway, including in Etne and Sogn, and for a long time they were one of the most powerful families in Kvinnherad.

espevr-hummerpark-Q67528556.d: Espevær Lobster Park is a former marine farm on Espevær in Bømlo municipality, which is now run as a museum. The lobster park was established in the late 19th century by the Stavanger-based company Christian Bjelland AS. Two coves were cordoned off, and a roof was built over them to ensure a consistent temperature for optimal growing conditions. At its peak, the park housed 24,000 lobsters, which were then collected by large well boats to be served on the dining tables of wealthy Europeans. Espevær Lobster Park was listed by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage in 1993. Two years prior to this, the Society for the Preservation of Ancient Monuments and the Espevær Housewives’ Association had begun restoration work on the park; this work was completed in 1994.

kvilekval-Q67597285.d: Kvilekvål is a farmstead in Voss municipality dating from the first half of the 19th century. The farm is situated on steep terrain 2.5 km east of Evanger, on the north bank of the River Vosso. The farmstead comprises two buildings listed as cultural heritage sites: a main house known as the Knute Nelson-stova and a barn. The main house is named after Knute Nelson (originally Knud Evanger), who emigrated from Norway and went on to become a governor and senator in the USA. The Vassvøri parish council has regularly organised Knute Nelson Day at Kvilekvål.

olavskrossen-Q67598591.d: Olavskrossen is a medieval stone monument situated in Vossevangen in the municipality of Voss. Olavskrossen is shaped like a cross and, according to tradition, is said to have been erected by St Olav in the year 1023 when he travelled through the area to convert the Norwegian people to Christianity. However, there are no reliable historical sources to support this, and the first mention of the stone in written sources dates from 1670. There is also some uncertainty as to whether the stone currently stands where it was originally placed. The memorial is situated in a green space, is 165 cm high and 89 cm wide.

sanda-stikningsbu-Q67603570.d: Sandå survey hut is situated in Ulvik municipality and was built in 1896 as part of the preparatory work for the Bergen Railway. It was the first building to be erected in connection with the construction of the railway line. It was later converted into a keeper’s cottage. Together with the keeper’s cottages at Fagernut and Slirå, Sandå is listed as a cultural heritage site as they are well preserved and represent the history of the construction of the high-mountain section of the Bergen Railway.

borgstua-i-kinsarvik-Q67605533.d: Borgstua in Kinsarvik is a listed building situated next to Kinsarvik Church. It is believed to have been built in 1763 or 1764. In 1957, the farmhouse was moved to its current location, and at the same time a cellar was built beneath it.

broch-huset-Q67606851.d: The Broch House is a building in the centre of Utne in Ullensvang municipality. The building was erected by Jakob Johannesson Winæs in 1828, and its architecture was strongly influenced by the prevailing architectural style in Bergen. It is a two-storey building constructed of log timber. Until around 1900, the building was known as the ‘Jacob House’. From this building, a trading business was operated under a licence granted by Bergen’s town privileges, which conferred exclusive trading rights in the area. In 1836, a post office was also established in the building. The concept of privileged trading posts in the districts was abolished when the new Trade Act came into force in 1842, but the Broch House continued to operate as a country store throughout the 19th and 20th centuries.

poppelgarden-Q67620631.d: Budal, Nordre Budal or Poppelgården is a farm with a listed farmhouse on Tjøme in Færder municipality, Vestfold. The farmstead at Nordre Budal is situated on the east side of Vestveien on Tjøme. The listed main building forms part of a farmstead comprising a barn and an outbuilding. The outbuilding is thought to be of the same age as the main house.

ytters-Q67621271.d: Yttersø is an old wooden building in Larvik municipality. The address is Elveveien 46.

askviknes-voksenpsykiatrisk-senter-Q6765.d: Askviknes Children’s Home was a children’s home established in 1900 by the Norwegian Mission for homeless children. The children’s home was situated in Os municipality in Hordaland, and had capacity for 25 children. The children’s home was for vagrant children, those voluntarily placed there by their parents, or those placed there by the guardianship authorities. The admission age was under 4 years. Askviknes was the first children’s home established by the Norwegian Mission for the Homeless. The property is now owned by Bjørnafjorden Municipality, which is responsible for its operation and supervision.

os-prestegard-Q67653754.d: Os Vicarage is a vicarage in Os, Hordaland, which has served as the residence associated with Os Church. The property is situated just behind the church and is thought to have been built in the second half of the 17th century. In addition to the main building, the farmyard contains a storehouse, a garage and outbuildings, as well as a medieval smokehouse. Os Vicarage was listed as a cultural heritage site in 2001.

holmestrand-politistasjon-Q67731196.d: The old Holmestrand police station is a listed building situated at Kirkegaten 15 in Holmestrand. It was built in 1864 as the town hall; the building subsequently served as a courthouse and a detention centre, but has functioned as a police station since the 1950s. In 2003, the Director-General for Cultural Heritage ensured that the police station was listed as a cultural monument.

skrivergarden-egersund-Q68091958.d: Skrivergården in Egersund is a listed district magistrate’s residence in the Empire style, situated in the centre of Egersund and built between 1825 and 1850. The building is located close to the sound between the town and Eigerøya. The building’s main façade features an entrance marked by four sturdy columns. The columns extend across the ground and first floors, forming the foundation for the dormer extensions. The building has a hipped roof with dormer extensions on both sides. The ground floor is partly built of natural stone and partly of brick. The upper storey is constructed of log timber, half-split logs and vertical timber framing, which is also used internally on the ground floor. The client was a lawyer who had studied in Copenhagen.

fogdahuset-hana-Q68160919.d: Fogdahuset Hana is a listed building in Sandnes and is considered to be the oldest of the buildings still standing in the town. The farmstead at Hana is mentioned in sources dating back to 1470. The oldest parts of the house standing there today probably date from the 17th century. Fogdahuset got its name when the bailiff Oluf Zachariassen bought the farm in 1720; Fogdahuset was a ‘bailiff’s farm’ with a courtroom and a prison. In 1924, it was decided to list the building as a cultural monument. In October 1989, a fire broke out in the building, causing significant fire damage to the south-eastern part of the house. Sandnes Municipality purchased the house in 1999 with a view to restoring it and using it as a community centre, but little was done in the early years.

strandgaten-16-Q68350296.d: Strandgaten 16 – also known as Steinstad – is a residential building in Sokndal municipality in Rogaland. The house is one of the cultural heritage sites that form part of the listed cultural environment at Sogndalstrand. The house was built in the latter half of the 19th century. In January 2019, the Director-General of Cultural Heritage criticised Sokndal municipality for a lack of fire safety in the old wooden houses in Sogndalstrand. The municipality then wished to install a new fire alarm system at Strandgaten 16 and 18 as a pilot project.

b-prestegard-Q68813041.d: Bø Vicarage, or Holmen Farm, is situated a few hundred metres north-east of Bø Church, at Prestevegen 4. The farm’s history is said to date back to before the Viking Age. It is not known exactly when the farm became a vicarage, but its status as such is confirmed in 1527. A number of farms and farmsteads were eventually brought under the vicarage’s control, and the village of Bø lies on what was once the vicarage’s land. The vicarage land was eventually subdivided and sold, and the vicarage compound itself – comprising the main building, storehouse and garden – was sold in 2006 to the Bø Vicarage Foundation. The foundation aims to preserve the local cultural heritage, and the farm is used for various cultural purposes. The main building and the storehouse are listed buildings.

haugvaldstadminne-8-Q68899506.d: Haugvaldstadminne 8 is a listed building in Stavanger municipality. The building was constructed around 1770. In the 1830s, John Haugvaldstad took over the property; at the time, he was the city’s wealthiest citizen as well as a prominent figure in the Haugianer community. He did not live in the house himself, but it is believed that he arranged for it to be refurbished and that, as part of this, a landscape painting that had been painted directly onto the wall was covered up. It was not until 1972 that this painting was uncovered, and the building was subsequently listed as a cultural monument.

konsul-frederik-hansens-hus-Q68899774.d: Consul Frederik Hansen’s house is a listed building on Skagen in Stavanger municipality. Its street address is Skagen 18. The building was constructed in the early 18th century, but it is unclear who the architect was. It has been extended several times since then; in 1787, the building was given its distinctive façade with nine Ionic pilasters, which still stand today. Ole Smith Plough established a trading business in the house in 1768; the business was later taken over by the Danish consul Frederik Hansen, from whom the building takes its name. In 1923, the building was listed under the 1920 Building Preservation Act. The Director-General of Cultural Heritage has ranked it as one of the finest surviving examples of Norwegian Rococo architecture.

engels-minde-Q68902712.d: Engels Minde is a listed country house in the late Empire style in Stavanger municipality. Its postal address is Engelsminnegate 22. The main house was built between 1851 and 1853, and the name Engels minde derives from Engel Hansen Særvold, a merchant from Os in Hordaland. It was his son, Hans Engel Hansen, who built the house and named it in honour of his father. During the Second World War, the estate was requisitioned by the German forces and was used, amongst other things, as a detention centre. In more recent times, Engels minde has been restored, and in 1980 the building was listed as a cultural monument by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage.

jelsa-prestegard-Q68916512.d: Jelsa Vicarage is an Empire-style farmstead in Suldal municipality which has served as the vicarage for Jelsa Church since the 17th century. The farmstead was originally called Berg, but is now known as Jelsa Vicarage. The main house currently standing on the estate was built in 1843, whilst an extension was added in 1850. It was the parish priest, Edvard Wilhelm Vedøe, who had the pleasure of being the first to move into the new vicarage. In 1946, the farm underwent modernisation. In 1991, the vicarage was listed as a cultural heritage site by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage.

sandsgard-Q68918023.d: Sandsgård is a manor house in Tysvær, Rogaland. The estate comprises a total of nine buildings; the main house was completed in 1777, but it is believed that parts of the building are considerably older. The main house was listed by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage in 1923.

husantunet-Q68919307.d: Husantunet, situated in Alvdal, is one of the country’s best-preserved historic farmsteads. It forms part of the Nordøsterdal Museum and is also known as the Alvdal Museum. The oldest surviving buildings date from the 18th century. Of the 17 buildings on the farm, 15 are listed by the Norwegian Directorate for Cultural Heritage.

vestre-moland-prestegard-Q69054159.d: Vestre Moland Vicarage is situated north-west of Vestre Moland Church. The estate is believed to have been a vicarage and church property throughout the Catholic period, but was confiscated by the Crown in 1536 during the transition from Catholicism to Lutheranism. In June 1573, Jørgen Hanssøn complained at the synod in Stavanger that he did not have a vicarage, but had to rent one ‘from the laity’. This matter was brought before the king, and on 5 July 1577 the king replied that he should be granted a free farm, and Vestre Moland once again became a vicarage. The tenant’s house was originally built in the 17th century. The left-hand section was built around 1770 during the tenure of the vicar Andreas Bjørn. Bjørn also laid out a large garden surrounded by a fence. The storehouse dates from 1830.

opdal-prestegard-Q69059268.d: Opdal Vicarage or Uvdal Vicarage (farm no. 73) was the vicarage for Uvdal Stave Church in the municipality of Nore and Uvdal in Buskerud. The stave church was built on the vicarage grounds on the upper side of what is, as of 2019, County Road 2810. The Nore and Uvdal Rural Heritage Centre was separated from the vicarage in 1960 and comprises the Vicarage House (or School House) and the Vicarage Barn from the old vicarage, as well as other buildings that have been moved to the site. The barn was built in 1627–28 and is a listed building. The farmhouse dates from the 18th century. The open-air museum is open to the public during the summer months and also hosts events at other times of the year. The curate lived at the vicarage until 1816, when he moved to Nore.

rogneby-Q69093960.d: Rogneby is a manor house in Østre Toten in the Innlandet region. Early sources refer to it as Ranaby or Ranabýr. The estate is situated close to Kraby station on the Skreiabanen railway line, which is now disused. In the 19th century, Rogneby was a powerful estate with 11 tenant farms attached to it. The main building was constructed in 1810 in the Classical style, featuring a temple-style gable and columns. In 1923, it was listed as a cultural monument under the Building Preservation Act of 1920. Today, the farm comprises a total of 1,093 dekar, of which 646 dekar is arable land and 394 dekar is woodland.

tuft-stavkirke-Q69356278.d: Tuft Stave Church (Tupta kirkja) was a medieval stave church, probably built around the year 1200. The church’s longitudinal axis was oriented in a south-west to north-east direction. On a map from 1772, the stave church is marked in the eastern part of the cemetery of that time. The church site is situated on land ceded from Tuft Nedre (farm number 5). The new Tuft Church was built on a plain adjacent to the southern side of the old churchyard, which has since been extended. The church site is still in use and lies approximately 1 kilometre north of the centre of present-day Hvittingfoss in Ytre Sandsvær (now in Kongsberg municipality). Locally, the site is known as Tuftmoen and was previously also used as a parade ground (‘Exerceer Plads for det Laurdalske Compagnie’).

ramstadslottet-Q7290308.d: Ramstadslottet is a hill in Rælingen municipality in Akershus. It rises to a height of 394 metres above sea level and is the third-highest peak in Østmarka. An area of 2.1 square kilometres surrounding the peak was designated as the Ramstadslottet Nature Reserve in 2001. The area, which also includes Barlindåsen, features three sites with primeval-like woodland and rare species. One of Østmarka’s largest spruce trees also stands nearby.

snarum-kirke-Q7499106.d: Snarum Church is a single-nave long church with a west tower, built of red brick between 1868 and 1869 at Snarum in Modum municipality, Buskerud. Permission to build a new church was granted by a royal resolution issued in 1865, and construction of the new church began in 1868; it was consecrated on 21 October 1869. The church is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to Modum parish; it is administered by the Modum Church Council in Eiker deanery, which is part of the Diocese of Tunsberg. Access to the church is via Krøderveien–Lofthusveien from the south or Snarumsveien–Lofthusveien from the north. The architect of the church was Georg Andreas Bull. The church has a seating capacity of approximately 230.

asker-kirke-Q7588955.d: Asker Church is a long church dating from 1879 in Asker municipality. The church serves as the deanery church for Asker deanery. The Asker parish and parish district encompass Asker town centre and Skaugum. The Crown Prince’s family, who reside at Skaugum, often attend services at this church. The building has a capacity of 600. Tor Øystein Vaaland was the parish priest in Asker from 2014 to 2019. Karoline Astrup has been the parish priest since 2019.

auli-kapell-Q7589060.d: Auli Church is a long church in Nes in Akershus County. It was built as a chapel using private funds on land belonging to the Søndre Auli farm in 1904–1905 and consecrated on 23 January 1907. The chapel belonged to Udenes parish until 1998, when it was upgraded to a parish church in Årnes parish. The building is timber-framed and has 150 seats. The architect of the church was Hjalmar Welhaven. Auli had previously been a separate parish in the Middle Ages. At that time, the church probably stood at Mellom-Auli, where a field to the east of the farm is still called Kjerkejordet.

aurskog-kapell-Q7589171.d: Aurskog Chapel is the burial chapel at Aurskog Church in Aurskog-Høland municipality, Akershus county. It was built in 1964. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 125. In 2009, it acquired the Grönlund organ from Oppegård Church.

aurskog-kirke-Q7589260.d: Aurskog Church is a long church dating from 1881 in Aurskog-Høland municipality in Akershus county. The church is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Østre Borgesyssel deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 580. The organ was built by August Nielsen in 1882. The militarily neutral zone agreed between Norway and Sweden as part of the Karlstad Peace Treaty of 1905 was defined as running from ‘the south-western end of Dyrerudtjern’ to ‘Urskog Church’ and on to ‘the southern end of Holmtjern’.

bjrke-kirke-Q7589349.d: Bjørke Church is a long church dating from 1696, situated in Maura, in the north of Nannestad municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has 178 seats; it was constructed by Oluf and Christopher Vestby, together with Jens Laage, under a contract dated 10 April 1696. The pulpit and altarpiece were painted by the priest and colonel Kjell Stub (1607–73), who was parish priest in Ullensaker. The church’s processional cross was carved by woodcarver Arne Oskar Johansen (1923–2009) and painted by his granddaughter Ingrid Johansen (1976–).

bjrkelangen-kirke-Q7589423.d: Bjørkelangen Church is a rectangular church, built in 1925 in the municipality of Aurskog-Høland, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Østre Borgesyssel deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 250.

blaker-kirke-Q7589500.d: Blaker Church is a long church dating from 1881, situated in Blaker in Lillestrøm municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 450. The church was designed by Otto Schønheyder.

dalen-kirke-Q7589585.d: Dalen Church, formerly Dalen Chapel, is situated in Gansdalen in Lillestrøm municipality, Akershus county, and was consecrated on 14 November 1905. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The chapel was built of timber and stands on the grounds of the Gans farm. The site was donated at the time by the then owner – merchant Westbye Egeberg. The architect was Gudmund Hoel. The church bell dates from 1691 and was brought from Fet Church. The furnishings date from the time of its construction, whilst the interior of the chapel was repainted in 1955 by Kristoffer Eriksen Ganer. He also created the stained-glass window above the altar. In 1997, the chapel was granted the status of a church. The chapel underwent a major refurbishment around

drbak-kirke-Q7589679.d: For other churches with the same name, see Our Saviour’s Church. Drøbak Church, or Our Saviour’s Church, is a timber-framed cruciform church, consecrated in 1776 in Frogn municipality, Akershus county. It is situated in Drøbak parish in the Søndre Follo deanery. The church was a gift from the merchant Niels Carlsen (1734–1809) and his wife Martha Zachariasdatter. It contains several old portraits, as well as a richly decorated Rococo interior, the altarpiece and pulpit of which were funded by Martha’s father, Zacharias Simonsen Wesseltoft. The church’s design was influenced by the older Church of Our Saviour in what was then Christiania, now Oslo Cathedral. Domenico Erdmann led the restoration work to mark the 150th anniversary in 1926.

feiring-kirke-Q7589932.d: Feiring Church is a long church dating from 1875 in Eidsvoll municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and the church has 200 seats. The church contains furnishings from earlier churches, including an altarpiece and a choir stall dating from the early 17th century and 1693 respectively. From 1895 to 1925, an altarpiece featuring a copy of Adolph Tidemand’s painting *The Resurrection* from Bragernes Church was used. Access to the site is via the Rv33. There is a churchyard adjacent to the church.

fenstad-kirke-Q7590012.d: Fenstad Church is a cruciform church dating from 1703 in Nes, in Akershus county. It is the oldest church in the municipality, having been built three years before Udenes Church. The church is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 300.

fet-kirke-Q7590093.d: Fet Church is a long church dating from 1890 in Lillestrøm municipality in Akershus. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The church replaced a timber church dating from 1681, which stood roughly where the burial chapel stands today. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 360. It was refurbished in 2007/2008.

frogn-kirke-Q7590265.d: Frogn Church is a long church dating from 1999, situated in Frogn municipality and parish, Søndre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The building is constructed of Leca and has a capacity of 240. The old church burnt down in 1994. It was a long church dating from 1859, built of timber in the Neo-Gothic style.

frogner-gamle-kirke-Q7590357.d: Frogner Old Church is a long church dating from around 1180, situated in Lillestrøm municipality in Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is constructed of stone and has a capacity of 90. The church is referred to as ‘Frauna kirkia à Gauteið’ in Bishop Eystein’s land register from 1359. The church burnt down in 1918. Frogner New Church was initially built to replace the small medieval church, but it was eventually decided to restore the old church. The walls were repaired in 1936, and the floor and ceiling in 1948. The restoration was completed in 1977. Following the fire, a runic inscription was discovered on a stone in the wall just west of the south portal.

furuset-kirke-Q7590543.d: Furuset Church is a long church dating from 1879 in Ullensaker municipality in Akershus. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is constructed of brick and has a capacity of 300.

garder-kirke-Q7590621.d: For Garder Church in Nordre Land, see Østsinni Church. Garder Church is a long church dating from 1881 in Vestby municipality, Akershus county. It is situated in Garder parish in Søndre Follo deanery. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 175. The altarpiece was painted by Christen Brun, based on a copy of Adolph Tidemand’s altarpiece ‘Christ in the Cloud’ in Tyristrand Church.

gjerdrum-kirke-Q7590775.d: Gjerdrum Church is a cruciform church dating from 1686 in Gjerdrum municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 270. Beneath the church there is a crypt where the church builder Anders Simonsen (1628–1696) is buried.

gjfjell-kirke-Q7590872.d: Gjøfjell Church (formerly a chapel) is a long church dating from 1900, situated at Fagerstrand in Nesodden municipality, Akershus county. It is situated in Gjøfjell parish in the Søndre Follo deanery. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of approximately 300. The architect was Holger Sinding-Larsen. The altarpiece was created by Nicolai Meidel. It depicts Christ bestowing his blessing against a background of vine tendrils. Motifs of the Fall of Man are woven into the tendrils. The pulpit and baptismal font are both made of wood and date from 1900. The windows in the chancel feature two small stained-glass panels depicting the Last Supper. The current organ is a pipe organ by Olsen & Jørgensen with six stops, dating from 1907. It was restored in 2006/07. There is a churchyard adjacent to the church.

greverud-kirke-Q7590968.d: Greverud Church is a church built in a rectangular (cubic) shape, dating from 1967, in Nordre Follo municipality, Nordre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The architect is Harald Hille. The building is constructed of concrete and brick and has a capacity of 300. The church has a French-inspired Baroque organ from 1991, supplied by the Swedish organ builder Knut Kaliff.

hakadal-kirke-Q7591048.d: Hakadal Church is the parish church for Hakadal in Nittedal. The church belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery. The present church building dates from the early 17th century, around 1610, and is rectangular in shape. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 150. The church is a roadside church.

heggedal-kirke-Q7591131.d: Heggedal Church is a long church dating from 1931 in Heggedal, in the municipality of Asker. It belongs to Asker Deanery. The chapel was consecrated on Palm Sunday, 12 April 1931. The carpenters came from Heggedal Trevarefabrikk and the timber was sourced from Telemark and Skjellestad. Thanks to voluntary labour and donations, the construction cost was low, at just 40,000 kroner. The church was painted white in 1950, having previously been brown/tar-coloured. Between 2018 and 2019, the church was refurbished and fitted with a new staircase and ramp to improve accessibility, a new roof, a fresh coat of exterior paint, a new sound and lighting system, and a new organ.

heni-kirke-Q7591371.d: Heni Church is a rectangular church, built in 1864 in Gjerdrum municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has 220 approved seats. The church houses a crucifix dating from the 14th century. Access to the site is via the Rv120.

holmen-kirke-Q7591450.d: Holmen Church belongs to the Asker deanery in the Diocese of Oslo and was consecrated on 28 November 1965 by Bishop Johannes Smemo. The church was designed by architect MNAL Knut Knutsen in a square shape that is a recurring feature throughout the church’s exterior and interior. It is situated on a hill at Slependen in Asker municipality. The church serves the areas of Holmen, Hvalstad, Billingstad, Nesøya, Nesbru and Slependen. The building is constructed of concrete and has 340 seats, with a further 200 available in the open parish hall. A parish hall on the same floor has approximately 50 seats. On the lower floor are a youth hall and a scout hall, with a combined capacity of 200 seats. An extension built in 1984 houses offices and a nursery, as well as a loft space for smaller gatherings.

holter-kirke-Q7591540.d: Holter Church is a long church dating from the 1600s in Nannestad municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 208.

hovin-kirke-Q7591618.d: See the index page for other instances of the church name Hovin. Hovin Church is the oldest church in Ullensaker municipality and is situated in the centre of Hovingrenda. It is a timber-framed cruciform church that was consecrated in 1695. The church is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The master builder responsible for its construction was Oluf Iversen Helmen, who fell to his death whilst working on the tower. Incidentally, the active parish priest, Thomas Rosing (son of Bishop Hans Rosing), drew on his connections with skilled carpenters and tower builders. Much of the church’s furnishings have been transferred from an older church.

hurdal-kirke-Q7591693.d: Hurdal Church is a long church dating from 1681 in Hurdal municipality in Akershus. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 250. The oldest part dates from 1681, whilst the present nave is an extension added in 1793. The chancel features ornamentation and rose-painted decorations from the 1680s. These were uncovered during restoration work in 1955. There is a considerable amount of old furnishings, including a crucifix from the 1300s.

hvitsten-kapell-Q7591764.d: Hvitsten Church is a long church dating from 1903, situated in Vestby municipality, Søndre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 100. The church was designed by Harald Sundby.

ingeborgrud-kirke-Q7591922.d: Ingeborgrud Church is a long church in Nes, in Akershus county. The building was erected as a chapel at Ingeborgrud in Skogbygda in 1904–05 and consecrated on 1 February 1906. It now has the status of a church. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The church is timber-built and has a capacity of 330. It has a long-term maintenance plan and is not a listed building. The churchyard was consecrated before the church, as an auxiliary churchyard, in 1885.

klodsbodding-kapell-Q7592145.d: Klodsbodding Chapel (or Klodsbodung Chapel) is a chapel in Stadu, Nes, in Akershus County. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is brick-built and has a capacity of 80. It was built as a burial chapel in 1906 and was consecrated as a church in 1955.

kolbotn-kirke-Q7592237.d: Kolbotn Church is a rectangular-shaped church, built in 1932 in Kolbotn in the municipality of Nordre Follo, Nordre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The church was consecrated on 28 August 1932. The building is constructed of stone in the Neo-Romantic style with medieval influences and has a capacity of 250. It was designed by the architect Olav Olson, who also designed Ljan Church and Strømmen Church during the same period. The chancel features three stained-glass windows by Rolf Klemetsrud, dating from 1932.

krakstad-kirke-Q7592422.d: Kråkstad Church is a church in Kråkstad in Nordre Follo municipality, Nordre Follo deanery in Akershus. It is square in shape and dates from 1150. The building is constructed of stone and has a capacity of 200. The tower was built in 1882.

langhus-kirke-Q7592594.d: Langhus Church is a church situated in Langhus in the municipality of Nordre Follo, in Akershus. The church was built in 1975. It is a brick-built church with a seating capacity of 600. It is the largest church in Follo. Work on the church began in 1956 but was not realised and completed until 1975. The church was built with the intention of serving as a meeting place for activities other than just church services. In the basement, a number of group rooms and a lounge were built. Initially, the Langhus Scout Group used the premises, and the church was also used as a school for a period whilst Vevelstadåsen School was being extended.

langset-kirke-Q7592721.d: Langset Church is a long church dating from 1859 in Eidsvoll municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed. It was originally built as a cruciform church based on the same plans as Flå Church in Hallingdal, but in 1891 the transepts were demolished. The interior was altered in 1928–30 according to plans by Arnstein Arneberg. The altarpiece features a copy of Adolph Tidemand’s painting *The Baptism of Jesus* from Trinity Church in Oslo. There is a churchyard adjacent to the church.

lillestrm-kirke-Q7592822.d: Lillestrøm Church is a rectangular-shaped church, built in 1935 in Lillestrøm municipality, Akershus county. It belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery. The building is constructed of concrete and brick and was built in the ancient basilica style. The church can accommodate 600 visitors. Lillestrøm Church houses one of Henrik Sørensen’s depictions of Christ. On the blue apse wall, he has painted Christ al fresco (on wet plaster) as a young man, fair-haired and beardless. The church later served as the inspiration for Notodden Church, which was completed in 1938. The two churches are virtually identical in appearance, interior and altarpiece.

lken-kirke-Q7592904.d: Løken Church (Høland Church) is a long church dating from 1883 in Aurskog-Høland municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Østre Borgesyssel deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has 700 seats. This is the third church to be built at Løken. The two previous ones stood by the old cemetery further to the south-west. The organ was built by August Nielsen in 1884 and refurbished by Norsk Orgel- og Harmoniumfabrikk in 1965.

lrenskog-kirke-Q7592983.d: Lørenskog Church is a church in Lørenskog municipality in Akershus county. It belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery. The church is rectangular in shape and was built of stone between 1150 and 1250. It has 117 seats. The church houses a statue of St Laurentius from the 12th century, an altarpiece from 1647, and a pulpit from 1658 in the Oslo Renaissance style. Right next to the church, at the top of the pine-clad Hammerberget, is a small freshwater spring called Olavskilden. It is said to have come into being when Thor, in a fit of anger over the construction of the church, threw his hammer but missed and struck the rock behind it. This caused the spring to gush forth.

mangen-kapell-Q7593065.d: Mangen Chapel is a long church dating from 1903 in Aurskog-Høland municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Østre Borgesyssel deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The chapel was designed by engineer Haneborg and built by master builder Martin Johnsen, son of Gulbrand Johnsen. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 150. The chapel was previously served by priests from both the Nes and Aurskog parishes. Today, the chaplaincy belongs to Aurskog.

mari-kirke-Q7593161.d: Mari Church is a rectangular church built in 1761 in Enebakk municipality, Nordre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The church was consecrated by Bishop Fredrik Nannestad in 1761. The church became the property of the municipality in 1880. St Mary’s Church is situated on high ground overlooking Mjær and large parts of Ytre Enebakk. Access to the site is via the Rv120 and Rv155.

mogreina-kirke-Q7593246.d: Mogreina Church is a long church dating from 1912 in Ullensaker municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 110. The architect of the church was Ole Stein.

nannestad-kirke-Q7593312.d: Nannestad Church is a long church dating originally from the Middle Ages (1150–1250), but rebuilt in 1693, in Nannestad municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The church is built of stone and has 206 seats. Access to the site is via County Road 120 and County Road 529.

nes-kirke-Q7593463.d: Nes Church is a long church dating from 1860 in Nes, Akershus. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The church is built of brick and, stylistically, is a Neo-Romanesque church with strong historical features. Inside, it has side galleries on both sides, giving the church a capacity of approximately 450. The architect was P. H. Holtermann. The interior of the church has been repainted several times, most recently in 2008 when the original colours from 1860 were restored. Originally, the church was known as Store Nes Church. At Nestangen, there are ruins of a stone church dating from around 1100, which was extended into a cruciform church in 1697 and burnt down in 1854.

nesodden-kirke-Q7593553.d: Nesodden Church is a Romanesque-style long church dating from the 12th century, situated in Nesodden municipality, Søndre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The church celebrated its 800th anniversary in 1975. It is situated just east of the vicarage on the eastern edge of the Nesodden plateau.

nittedal-kirke-Q7593624.d: Nittedal Church is a long church dating from 1869 in Nittedal municipality, Nedre Romerike deanery in Akershus county. The building is timber-framed and can seat 375 people. The church was designed by Jacob Wilhelm Nordan and built by master builder Gulbrand Johnsen from Nes. The church has been renovated several times, and when the roof cladding (copper) was replaced some time ago, the small towers that stood at each corner were also removed. On the very site where the church was built, there once stood a medieval stone church known as Dal Church. It is also referred to as Olavskirken. The old walls are still preserved to a height of 1 metre and can be viewed beneath the present church.

nordby-kirke-Q7593687.d: Nordby Church is a long church dating from 1826 in Ås municipality, Søndre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 140. The church was built by Lieutenant Jørgen Brochmann after he had demolished the old Nordby Church.

oppegard-kirke-Q7593792.d: Oppegård Church is a rectangular church, built in 1876 in Svartskog in the municipality of Nordre Follo, Akershus county. The building is timber-framed and has 125 seats. It was built under the supervision of master builder Andreas Keitel and consecrated on 1 November 1876.

stenstad-kirke-Q7594106.d: Østenstad Church is a working church built in 1980 in Østenstad and Blakstad in Asker municipality. The building is made of brick and has a capacity of 530.

statholdergaarden-Q7604124.d: Stattholdergården, or Grünergården, is situated at Rådhusgata 11 in Kvadraturen, Oslo, and is a listed building dating from the 1640s. It was built by the master of the mint, Peter Grüner, whose name is inscribed in wrought iron on the façade. Governor Ulrik Fredrik Gyldenløve lived in the house in the late 17th century, hence the name adopted by the restaurant in this building in 1957, which in more recent times has also become the building’s nickname. Prior to that, it was known as Calmeyergården, after the timber merchants Mathias Calmeyer, who owned it from 1766, and his son Henrik Calmeyer, who owned it from 1800 to 1820.

stensparken-Q7703624.d: Stensparken is a hill in Fagerborg, in the St. Hanshaugen district of Oslo. The hill is elongated and consists of ‘knollekalk’, i.e. limestone embedded in a darker shale matrix. The southern part of the hill is a landscaped park, whilst the northern part (Blåsen) is a rocky outcrop offering views over the city. The park was developed between the 1890s and the 1940s. Roughly in the middle of the park, there is a pond in the summer. There is a small café and a table tennis table there. Within the park, there is a fenced-off area that used to be a children’s playground. In the 19th century, Stensparken and St. Hanshaugen were the only green spaces left for the capital’s general public from the magnificent royal gift that had once been the Christiania city common.

sre-harildstad-Q7717513.d: Søre Harildstad (or Harildstad, søre) (farm number 183, property number 4) is a farm in Nedre Heidal in Sel municipality. The farm has been awarded the Olavsrosa quality mark by Norwegian Cultural Heritage. The entire farm complex at Søre Harildstad was listed in 1923. In the summer, guided tours of the old buildings are available, and accommodation and catering are offered by prior arrangement. The farm is situated on a hillside roughly halfway up the south-west-facing slope in Heidal, where the vast majority of the village’s old farms are located.

bakke-bru-Q804444.d: Bakke Bridge is a bridge over the River Sira, between Lake Sirdalsvannet and Lake Lundevatnet in Flekkefjord municipality in Agder, and is Norway’s oldest suspension bridge for road traffic. Georg Daniel Barth Johnson, an engineer and road inspector in Agder, designed the bridge following a study trip to England in 1838. The bridge opened in 1844 and formed part of the West Coast Main Road between the capital and Stavanger until 1948. The road then split, so that travellers could either head for the farms on the western side of Lake Sirdalsvannet (Virakveien now runs the entire distance to Tonstad), or cross Tronåsen to reach Moi and continue further west. The route formed part of the inland postal road to Stavanger.

deichmans-hovedbibliotek-pa-hammersborg-.d: Deichman’s Main Library at Hammersborg was the main library of the Deichman Library, Oslo Municipality’s public library, located at Hammersborg in central Oslo, close to the Government Quarter, Trinity Church and the Swedish St Margaret’s Church. The building opened as the main collection and lending centre for the Deichman Library in 1933. The library closed for the last time in 2019, and its operations were moved to Deichman Bjørvika, which opened in 2020. In September 2020, the building was sold to Møller Eiendom. Møller Eiendom is developing the historic Deichmanske building in Oslo into Deich – the Nordic region’s largest venue for photography. Spanning 14,000 square metres, the site will bring together a photography museum, meeting spaces and catering venues, all centred around photography.

stai-stasjon-Q81958.d: Stai Station is a railway station on the Røros Line. The station is situated at Stai in Stor-Elvdal municipality and opened in 1875, two years before the entire Røros Line was opened. The station building was designed by the architect Georg Andreas Bull and was constructed in 1873; it was listed by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage in 2002 on the grounds of preserving an architecturally, architectural, building-historical and railway-historical site dating from the opening of the Røros Railway. The station is unstaffed and local trains only stop here upon direct request to the conductor. The distance from Stai station to Oslo S is 237.42 km.

raholt-kirke-Q8729461.d: Råholt Church is a long church dating from 1888 in Eidsvoll municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is constructed of rendered brick.

rlingen-kirke-Q8729633.d: Rælingen Church is a long church dating from 1828 in Rælingen municipality, Nedre Romerike deanery in Akershus county. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 250. The church contains a special chandelier from the 14th century, as well as a pulpit and a baptismal font dating from 1661. The church was privately owned until 1854. Organ: Organ builder: Spigseth Consultant: Bjørklund 19/II+P Action: Mechanical Wind supply: Sløyfelade Date of construction: 10 October 1987

setskog-kirke-Q8729896.d: Setskog Church is a long church dating from 1874 in Aurskog-Høland municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Østre Borgesyssel deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The church incorporates some reused materials from the previous church (1846), which stood at the Bunes Vestre farm, north of Lake Setten. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 190. Access to the site is via County Road 21.

siggerud-kapell-Q8730028.d: Siggerud Church is a long church dating from 1905, situated in Siggerud in Nordre Follo municipality, Nordre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 140. It was designed by Holger Sinding-Larsen. The church was fitted with a new organ by Norsk Orgel-Harmoniumfabrikk AS in 1992. The organ has 10 stops, 1 manual and a pedalboard. One stop (Subbass 16') comes from the old Hollenbach organ that stood in Ski Church until 1952.

skedsmo-kirke-Q8730158.d: Skedsmo Church is a cruciform church dating from 1180, situated in Lillestrøm municipality in Akershus county. It belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery. Much of the building dates back to its construction in 1180. The building is made of stone and has a capacity of 560.

ski-middelalderkirke-Q8730291.d: Ski Medieval Church is a long church in Nordre Follo municipality, Nordre Follo deanery in Akershus county. In 2010, the Central Place Names Register ruled that the name ‘Ski Medieval Church’ (not ‘Ski Church’) should be used in official contexts. The church site is situated to the east of Ski town centre, near the oldest settlement on the site. There is an Iron Age burial ground near the church, and the site bears traces of ancient roads and old agricultural practices. A granary stood next to the church until 1874. The church stands relatively unobstructed on top of a moraine ridge, with Kirkeveien to the north and the churchyard on the slope to the south. The church is in the Romanesque style. During a major renovation in 1860, the original openings in the masonry walls were destroyed.

skoklefall-kirke-Q8730558.d: Skoklefall Church, also known as Skoklefall Chapel, is a long church dating from 1936 in Nesodden municipality, Søndre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The building is timber-framed and seats approximately 130 people. The altarpiece, pulpit and baptismal font were all crafted and decorated by Terje Grøstad in the 1960s. Skoklefall Church does not have a churchyard. The foundation stone for the church was laid on 16 January 1935 by the then Bishop of Oslo, Johan P. Lunde. The architect was Carl Michalsen. The building was constructed by master builders and carpenters from Hallingdal: Arnfinn and Knut Hodnungseth, and Knut Blakkestad. Even the timber they used came from Hallingdal.

skrukkeli-kapell-Q8730857.d: Skrukkeli Chapel is a long church dating from 1923 in Hurdal municipality, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and has 118 seats. The architecture is inspired by the Isum complex at Maihaugen.

skarer-kirke-Q8731000.d: Skårer Church is a square-shaped church, built in 1978 in Lørenskog municipality, Akershus county. It belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery.
