The church was designed by the architect Aksel Fronth. Bishop Andreas Aarflot laid the foundation stone on Ascension Day 1977, and the church was consecrated the following year. The church has three galleries and seats 430 people. The church’s vision is: ‘Grace for all, a place for you’.

strmmen-kirke-Q8731672.d: Strømmen Church is a long church dating from 1929, situated in Strømmen in the municipality of Lillestrøm in Akershus county. It belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery. The building is constructed of stone and has a capacity of 330. It is built of natural stone in the Neo-Romanesque style and is situated on a hill just north-west of Strømmen town centre. The architect of the church was Olav Olson. His employer, Strømmen Trævarefabrik, was a strong driving force behind the church’s construction and contributed both the plot of land and a substantial sum of money. The church was originally intended to be built of timber, but the plans were altered during the project.

saner-kirke-Q8731811.d: Såner Church is a church built in 2000 in Såner, just outside Hølen in Vestby municipality, Akershus. The parish of the Church of Norway covers Hølen and Son. It belongs to the Søndre Follo deanery. The old church, which burnt down on 25 May 1995, was a long church dating from 1880.

sndre-hland-kirke-Q8731928.d: Søndre Høland Church (Hemnes Church) is a cruciform church dating from 1866, situated in Hemnes in the municipality of Aurskog-Høland in Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Østre Borgesyssel deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The plans for the church were drawn up by Anders Haneborg, based on Christian H. Grosch’s designs for Båstad Church. The master builders were Gulbrand Johnsen and Andreas Sand. The building is timber-framed and has a capacity of 450. The painting in the altarpiece was painted by Christen Brun as a copy after Adolph Tidemand, and the motif is his popular Resurrection scene from Bragernes Church in Drammen. The Kleberstein baptismal font was taken from the former church.

srum-kirke-Q8732053.d: Sørum Church is a long church in Lillestrøm municipality in Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. Sørum Church was consecrated to St Peter and St Paul on St Blaise’s Day, 3 February, though the exact year is unknown. In 2016, the church’s 850th anniversary was celebrated. Magnus Erlingsson’s saga recounts an attack at Rydjokul in Sørum during the winter of 1166–67. Rydjokul Church is thought to have stood a couple of kilometres south-east of the present church, closest to the river, until it was swept away by a landslide, and may have been replaced by the present Sørum Church. The building is constructed of stone and has a capacity of 340. The door knockers and baptismal font date from the Middle Ages.

udnes-kirke-Q8732223.d: Udenes Church is a cruciform church dating from 1706 in Nes, in Akershus county. The church stands on a hill, surrounded by the River Glomma and cornfields. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is timber-framed and was later clad with panelling. It has a capacity of 350. Both the pulpit and the altarpiece were crafted by Oluf Granberg and were made when the church was new. The church underwent significant alterations in 1860, both in that the timber walls were clad with panelling and the tower was moved from the centre to above the porch. In 1913, the church was altered once again. On that occasion, Arnstein Arneberg created a new ceiling over the chancel, as well as decorations on the gallery walls.

vestby-kirke-Q8732534.d: Vestby Church is a long church dating from 1886 in Vestby municipality, Søndre Follo deanery in Akershus county. The building is constructed of stone and has a capacity of 350. The church was designed by the architects Henrik Nissen and Holm Munthe as a brick long church in the Neo-Gothic style.

arnes-kirke-Q8732737.d: Årnes Church is a rectangular-shaped church (long church) dating from 1878 in Nes, Akershus county. It is part of the Church of Norway and belongs to the Øvre Romerike deanery in the Diocese of Borg. The building is constructed of brick and has a capacity of 375.

as-hovedkirke-Q8733004.d: Ås Church is the parish church for the parish of Ås in Ås, and the deanery church for the Søndre Follo deanery.

vre-rlingen-kirke-Q8733120.d: Øvre Rælingen Church is a square-shaped church, built in 1973 in the municipality of Rælingen, Akershus county. It belongs to the Nedre Romerike deanery. The building is constructed of masonry and has a capacity of 440.

eiksmarka-kirke-Q8733577.d: Eiksmarka Church (formerly Grinilund Church) is a long church built in 2014 in Eiksmarka, Bærum municipality, Akershus county. A church built in 1959 was demolished in 2013 and a new church was built and consecrated on 23 March 2014. The name was changed from Grinilund Church to Eiksmarka Church in December 2018. The building is constructed of concrete and timber and has a capacity of 340. The altarpiece was created by Tor Lindrupsen.

haslum-kirke-Q8733735.d: Haslum Church is a cruciform church dating from around 1190, situated in the municipality of Bærum in Akershus. The building is constructed of whitewashed quarry stone. The church serves as both a roadside church and the parish church for the Haslum parish.

haslumseter-kapell-Q8733874.d: Haslumseter Chapel is a sports chapel in Bærumsmarka, in the municipality of Bærum, Akershus county. The chapel was designed by Magnus Poulsson and built after his death, with his son Anton Poulsson acting as the architect in charge of the project. The chapel is run by the parishes of Bærum and West Oslo. Services are held almost every Sunday at 12.00. Coffee, waffles, soft drinks/mineral water and chocolate are on sale.

helgerud-kirke-Q8734012.d: Helgerud Church is a working church dating from 1982, situated in Gjettum in the municipality of Bærum within the Diocese of Oslo. It is the main church of Helgerud parish, established in 1976 when the former Vestre Bærum parish was divided into the three new parishes of Bryn, Helgerud and Tanum. Helgerud parish covers the central area stretching from Sandvika town centre towards Valler, Dønski, Rud, Gjettum, Hauger and on to Kolsås. Helgerud Church is built of red brick and was designed by architect Harald Hille. The church was consecrated in March 1982 by the then Bishop Andreas Aarflot. The church is situated on a small hill above Sandvika, close to Bærum Hospital, with Kolsåstoppen to the north-east.

jar-kirke-Q8734279.d: Jar Church is a rectangular church built in 1961 in the municipality of Bærum, Akershus county. The building is made of brick and has a capacity of 460.

snarya-kirke-Q8734812.d: Snarøya Church is a working church built in a rectangular shape in 1968 in Bærum municipality, Akershus county. The church’s address is Snarøyveien 126. The building is made of concrete and has a capacity of 250. The pulpit is made of concrete. Snarøya Church, designed by architects Odd Østbye and Harald Hille, was awarded the Betongtavlen architecture prize for 1985.

steras-kirke-Q8735161.d: Østerås Church is a working church built in 1974 in Bærum municipality, Akershus county. The building is constructed of brick and has a capacity of 690. An architectural competition was held in connection with the church project, and by the submission deadline on 15 February 1971, a total of 47 designs had been received. On the question of which project to recommend, the jury was divided into two factions. The majority favoured the ‘Jubilate Deo’ project, designed by architects Ashish Krishna and Viggo Kippernes. Østerås Church was conceived and planned as a working church. Flexibility in the broadest sense has been a key principle in its design.

blaafarvevrket-Q882820.d: Blaafarveværket, or the Blue Colour Works, was a mining and industrial company located at Åmot in Modum in Buskerud, Norway, which existed from 1776 to 1898, and which was Norway's largest mining company in the first half of the 19th century. The works mined cobalt ore and manufactured by smelting blue cobalt glass (smalt) and cobalt blue (cobalt aluminate) pigment. It is currently a large open-air industrial museum and an art gallery; it is the largest and best preserved mine museum in Europe, and one of Norway's most visited attractions.

bod-domkirke-Q890127.d: Bodø Cathedral (Norwegian: Bodø domkirke) is a cathedral of the Church of Norway in Bodø Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the town of Bodø. It is the church for the Bodø domkirke parish which is also the seat of the Bodø domprosti (deanery) and the seat of the Bishop of the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The concrete church was built in a long church basilica style in 1956 using plans drawn up by the architects Gudolf Blakstad and Herman Munthe-Kaas. The church seats about 850 people.

elverhy-kirke-Q893025.d: Elverhøy Church (Norwegian: Elverhøy kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tromsø Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the city of Tromsø. It is the church for the Elverhøy parish which is part of the Tromsø domprosti (arch-deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The church was built in its current location in 1974 and it now seats about 435 people.

botsfengselet-Q894848.d: Botsfengselet is a former national prison for long-term prisoners located in Oslo, Norway, at the former Åkebergløkka, Grønlandsleiret 41. The prison was designed by Heinrich Ernst Schirmer and was built starting in 1844, coming into use in 1851. The prison chapel was designed by architect Jacob Wilhelm Nordan and came into use in 1887. In 1970, Ullersmo Prison took over as the prison for long-term prisoners in Norway, and Botsfengselet was rehabilitated to serve as a department of the district prison in Oslo (Norwegian: Oslo Kretsfengsel) starting from 1975. The prison is listed as a protected site.

voie-kirke-Q9006848.d: Voie Church (Norwegian: Voie kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Kristiansand Municipality in Agder county, Norway. It is located in the Møvik neighborhood in the district of Voiebyen in the borough of Vågsbygd in the city of Kristiansand. It is the church for the Voie parish which is part of the Kristiansand domprosti (arch-deanery) in the Diocese of Agder og Telemark. The red, brick church was built in a fan-shaped design in 1990 using plans drawn up by the architect Arild Lauvland. The church seats about 300 people, but it can be expanded to about 500 people.

tana-kirke-Q9016653.d: Tana Church (Norwegian: Tana kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Deatnu-Tana Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Rustefjelbma. It is the main church for the Tana parish which is part of the Indre Finnmark prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The unique, brown, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1964 using designs drawn up by the architect Esben Poulsson (1907-1974) to replace the old church that was burned down by the retreating German forces towards the end of World War II. The church seats about 300 people.

polmak-kirke-Q9016689.d: Polmak Church (Norwegian: Polmak kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Deatnu-Tana Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Polmak, just east of the border with Finland. It is one of the churches for the Tana parish which is part of the Indre Finnmark prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1853 using plans drawn up by the architect J.H. Nebelong. The church seats about 120 people.

esviken-Q9018383.d: Esviken (formerly Esvigen) is a villa surrounded by an elaborate garden. It is located on a former farm on Leangbukta bay between Vettre and Konglungen in Asker, Norway.

suosjavrre-kapell-Q9030039.d: Šuoššjávri Chapel (Northern Sami: Šuoššjávrri kapealla, Norwegian: Suosjavrre kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Karasjok Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Šuoššjávri. It is an annex chapel for the Karasjok parish which is part of the Indre Finnmark prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The wooden church was built in a rectangular style in 1968 by the architect Ernst Nilsen. The church seats about 75 people and serves the rural western part of the municipality.

halsa-kirke-Q9078531.d: Halsa Church (Norwegian: Halsa kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Meløy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Halsa. It is the church for the Halsa parish which is part of the Bodø domprosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1960 using plans drawn up by the architect Kirsten Wleügel Knutssøn. The church seats about 400 people. The building was consecrated on 22 May 1960 by the Bishop Hans Edvard Wisløff.

sviny-fyr-Q908184.d: Svinøy Lighthouse (Norwegian: Svinøy fyrstasjon) is a fully automated lighthouse situated on the island of Svinøy in the sea off the Stad peninsula. It is located within Herøy Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, on the western coast of Norway. The island lies within sight of the mainland and it is 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) from the nearest island. The island of Skorpa is located about 11 kilometres (6.8 mi) to the east. The island is 300 metres (980 ft) east to west and 900 metres (3,000 ft) north to south. The island rises 35 metres (115 ft) out of the sea and is exposed to severe climatic conditions year round.

erkna-fyr-Q908192.d: Erkna Lighthouse (Norwegian: Erkna fyr) is a coastal lighthouse located in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It was established in 1869, and automated in 1988.

grasyane-fyr-Q908212.d: Grasøyane Lighthouse (Norwegian: Grasøyane fyr) is a coastal lighthouse in Ulstein Municipality in Møre og Romsdal, Norway. It sits on the small island of Grasøya, about 5.5 kilometres (3.4 mi) northwest of the island of Hareidlandet on which Ulstein Municipality is located and it is 9.1 kilometres (5.7 mi) east of Runde Lighthouse.

ulla-fyr-Q908222.d: Ulla Lighthouse (Norwegian: Ulla fyr) is a lighthouse just off the north end of the island of Haramsøya in Haram Municipality, Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The lighthouse sits on the very small island of Ulla, about 1.5 kilometres (0.93 mi) northwest of the Ullasund Bridge. The light at the top of the 10-metre (33 ft) tall tower emits a white, red or green light, depending on direction, occulting twice every 10 seconds. The light sits at an elevation of 22 metres (72 ft) above sea level. In October 1944, the lighthouse and the surrounding buildings were attacked by allied airplanes. The lighthouse was badly destroyed, and not rebuilt until after the war in 1950.

haugjegla-fyr-Q908231.d: Haugjegla Lighthouse (Norwegian: Haugjegla fyr; also spelled: Hauggjegla) is a coastal lighthouse located in Smøla Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located on a waveswept skerry about 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) north of Veiholmen on the north side of the island of Smøla. The lighthouse is only accessible by boat. The lighthouse is listed as a protected site.

ona-fyr-Q908251.d: Ona Lighthouse (Norwegian: Ona fyr) is located on the small island of Ona in Ålesund Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The lighthouse is built on Onakalven, the highest cliff on the island overlooking the harbor and the few, clustered wooden houses on this small island. The original rotating Fresnel lens remains in use.

hellevik-fyr-Q911787.d: Hellevik Lighthouse (Norwegian: Hellevik fyr) is a coastal lighthouse in Haram Municipality in Møre og Romsdal, Norway. It was first established in 1880, and was automated in 1973. The lighthouse was replaced by a smaller automated light in 1988. The 6-metre (20 ft) tall tower has a light on top that emits a white, red or green light, depending on direction, occulting once every 6 seconds. The present lighthouse is located about 400 metres (1,300 ft) west of the original lighthouse building.

storholmen-fyr-Q911805.d: Storholmen Lighthouse (Norwegian: Storholmen fyr) is an active lighthouse in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county on the west coast of Norway. This remote lighthouse is located on a tiny skerry about 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) due north of the tiny island of Erkna and 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) northwest of the populated island of Vigra. The light is lit from 16 July until 21 May. It is not lit during the summer because it is unnecessary due to the midnight sun. The lighthouse was only accessible by boat in calm seas during the summer, since boats cannot land on the tiny island. Goods and people had to be hoisted onto the island from the sea.

flatflesa-fyr-Q911848.d: Flatflesa Lighthouse (Norwegian: Flatflesa fyr) is a coastal lighthouse located in Aukra Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The lighthouse lies on the small island of Flatflesa, about 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) west of the island of Gossa and about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) east of the island of Sandøya. The original lighthouse was established in 1902 and in 1988 a new automated tower was completed. The 11-metre (36 ft) tall round, cylindrical, fiberglass tower is white with two black stripes. The 30,800 candela light emits white, red, or green light (depending on direction) occulting three times every 10 seconds. The light can be seen for up to 11 nautical miles (20 km; 13 mi).

munkeliv-kloster-Q922112.d: Munkeliv Abbey (Norwegian: Munkeliv kloster) was a Benedictine abbey located at Nordnes in Bergen, Norway. It was one of the oldest monasteries in Norway, and also one of the wealthiest and best-documented. There are no visible remains today.

grip-fyr-Q923101.d: The Grip Lighthouse (Norwegian: Grip fyrstasjon) is located in the Grip archipelago in Kristiansund Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The lighthouse was built between 1885 and 1888 on the 7-metre (23 ft) high islet of Bratthårskollen, north of Gripholmen.

rrvik-kirke-Q923649.d: Rørvik Church (Norwegian: Rørvik kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Nærøysund Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the town of Rørvik on the island of Inner-Vikna. It was one of the churches for the Vikna parish which is part of the Namdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The modern, concrete and glass church was built in a long church design in 2019 using plans drawn up by the architect Ogmund Sørli. The church seats about 250 people, but can be expanded up to about 400 people.

statsministerboligen-Q944124.d: Inkognitogata 18 is the official residence of the Prime Minister of Norway. It is located in Oslo, the capital of Norway. The residence was completed in 2008 and is a complex of new and old buildings. It includes the original buildings on Parkveien 45, Inkognitogata 18, Riddervolds gate 2, which have been connected with new structures, and the gardens of Parkveien 45 to 47. The Prime Minister's private residence is in Inkognitogata 18 while the official residence and government representation rooms are in both Parkveien 45 and Inkognitogata 18. Riddervolds gate 2 is the official residence for visiting foreign dignitaries. The complex totals an area of 3030 m2.

hamar-stasjon-Q94466.d: Hamar Station (Norwegian: Hamar stasjon) is a railway station of the Dovre Line and the Røros Line located in downtown Hamar, Norway. Located 126.26 kilometers (78.45 mi) from Oslo Central Station, it is served by long-distance and regional trains on the Dovre Line, as the terminus for regional trains on the Røros Line. All trains are operated by SJ Norge, except the regional trains between Lillehammer and Oslo, which are operated by Vy. A side platform and an island platform are in regular use. The station handled 1,062,300 passengers in 2008. The station opened on 23 June 1862 as the western terminus of the narrow-gauge Hamar–Grundset Line, today the Røros Line.

lillehammer-stasjon-Q94523.d: Lillehammer is a railway station located in downtown Lillehammer, Norway, on the Dovre Line. The station was opened in 1894 with the construction of the railway between Hamar Station and Tretten Station. The station got a major overhaul before the 1994 Winter Olympics in Lillehammer. It is located 184.18 kilometers (114.44 mi) from Oslo Central Station and at 179.5 meters (589 ft) above mean sea level. Lillehammer is served by express trains to Trondheim and is the terminus of the regional trains north to Åndalsnes, and south to Oslo and Drammen. Express trains and regional trains to the north are operated by SJ Norge, regional trains to the south are operated by Vy.

dyna-fyr-Q952272.d: Dyna Lighthouse (Norwegian: Dyna fyr) is a coastal lighthouse on a reef south of Bygdøy, in Oslofjord, Oslo, Norway. It was established in 1875 and automated in 1956. In 1992 the lighthouse was renovated as a private banqueting facility, available for parties of 20-40 persons from Easter to Christmas.

ringve-musikkmuseum-Q960829.d: Ringve Museum is Norway's national museum for music and musical instruments, with collections from all over the world.

vikingskipshuset-Q961220.d: The Viking Ship Museum (Norwegian: Vikingskipshuset på Bygdøy) is located on the Bygdøy peninsula in Oslo, Norway. It is temporarily closed from September 2021 until 2027. It is part of the Museum of Cultural History of the University of Oslo, and houses three Viking era burial ships that were found as part of archaeological finds from Tune, Gokstad (Sandefjord), Oseberg (Tønsberg) and the Borre mound cemetery.

jessheim-stasjon-Q979157.d: Jessheim Station (Norwegian: Jessheim stasjon) is a railway station at Jessheim which opened in 1854. It is 44.60 kilometers (27.71 mi) from Oslo Central Station and has an elevation of 203.8 meters (669 ft) above mean sea level. The station is part of Norway's first railway, the Trunk Line, which ran from Kristiania (today known as Oslo) to Eidsvoll. The railroad had at the time of construction in 1854 named it Trøgstad, but due to the confusion with the town named Trøgstad in Østfold the name was changed in 1897 to Jessum.

kvaly-kirke-Q982564.d: Kvaløy Church (Norwegian: Kvaløy kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tromsø Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Kaldfjord on the island of Kvaløya. It is the church for the Kvaløy parish which is part of the Tromsø domprosti (arch-deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a cruciform style in 1962 using designs drawn up by the architect Gunnar B. Haugen. The church seats about 260 people.

hillesy-kirke-Q982711.d: Hillesøy Church (Norwegian: Hillesøy kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tromsø Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the Brensholmen area on the western part of the island of Kvaløya. It is the church for the Hillesøy parish which is part of the Tromsø domprosti (arch-deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1889 by the architect D.G. Evjen. The church seats about 300 people.

ullsfjord-kirke-Q982713.d: Ullsfjord Church (Norwegian: Ullsfjord kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tromsø Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Sjursnes on the eastern shore of the Ullsfjorden. It is the main church for the Ullsfjord parish which is part of the Tromsø domprosti (arch-deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1862 by the architect Christian Heinrich Grosch. The church seats about 300 people.

svalbard-Q25231.d: Svalbard (US: SVAHL-bar(d), UK: also SVAL-, Urban East Norwegian: [ˈsvɑ̂ːɫbɑr]), formerly Spitsbergen or Spitzbergen, is a Norwegian archipelago that lies at the convergence of the Arctic Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean. North of mainland Europe, it lies about midway between the northern coast of Norway and the North Pole. The islands of the group range from 74° to 81° north latitude, and from 10° to 35° east longitude. The largest island is Spitsbergen (37,673 km2), followed in size by Nordaustlandet (14,443 km2), Edgeøya (5,073 km2), and Barentsøya (1,288 km2). Bjørnøya or Bear Island (178 km2) is the most southerly island in the territory, situated some 147 km south of Spitsbergen.

operahuset-i-oslo-Q43280.d: The Oslo Opera House (Norwegian: Operahuset) is the home of the Norwegian National Opera and Ballet, and the national opera house in Norway. The building is situated in the Bjørvika neighbourhood of central Oslo, at the head of the Oslofjord. It is operated by Norwegian Directorate of Public Construction and Property, the government agency which manages property for the Norwegian government. The structure contains 1,100 rooms in a total area of 49,000 m2 (530,000 sq ft). The main auditorium seats 1,364 and two other performance spaces can seat 200 and 400. The main stage is 16 m (52 ft) wide and 40 m (130 ft) deep.

kongsberg-slvverk-Q59046.d: Kongsberg Silver works (Kongsberg Sølvverk) was a mining operation at Kongsberg in Buskerud county in Norway. The town of Kongsberg is the site of the Norwegian Mining Museum (Norsk Bergverksmuseum).

singsas-stasjon-Q63799.d: Singsås Station (Norwegian: Singsås stasjon) is a railway station located in the village of Singsås in Midtre Gauldal Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located along the Rørosbanen railway line. The station is served three times daily in each direction by the Trøndelag Commuter Rail service between Røros and Trondheim. The service is operated by SJ Norge.

frogner-kirke-Q8911689.d: Frogner Church is a cruciform church dating from 1694 in Lier municipality, Buskerud county. The building is constructed of stone and has a capacity of 370. The church was built on the ruins of a medieval church which burnt down following a lightning strike in 1651. This church was first mentioned in 1327, but it probably predated the 13th century. Access to the site is via County Road 23 and National Road 285.

elle-takeklokke-Q9016253.d: Elle Fog Bell is a fog bell located south of Drøbak on the eastern side of the Oslo Fjord. The bell tower is made of wood and built in the Swiss style. The tower has largely been preserved in its original state and is of both lighthouse-historical and architectural value as a distinctive cultural monument. The fog bell is therefore listed under the Cultural Heritage Act.

sndre-langara-takeklokke-Q9149057.d: The Søndre Langåra fog bell is a fog bell situated at the northern tip of Søndre Langåra in the Inner Oslo Fjord. The structure was established in 1896. The fog bell is housed in a free-standing tower built in the Swiss style. The foghorn complex also includes a residential building constructed after 1900, as well as outbuildings and a boathouse. The tower has largely been preserved in its original state and, according to the Directorate for Cultural Heritage, was possibly the only manned foghorn in the country. Søndre Langåra is of great value both in terms of lighthouse history and architecture and is therefore listed under the Cultural Heritage Act. Søndre Langåra Fog Bell is available to rent for overnight stays, sleeping five people, as part of the Kystled Oslofjorden trail.

rombak-stasjon-Q9313063.d: Rombak station (Northern Sami: Ruoppák), originally known as Sildvik station, is a station on the Ofot Line in Narvik. The station opened in 1902. It serves as a station for passenger services on the Ofot Line and has direct train connections to Narvik, Kiruna and Luleå. Since June 2008, passenger services have been operated by the Swedish state-owned company SJ. The station is connected to the road network, but access is only possible if you have a driving licence and a key to the barrier on Sildviksveien.

steinvik-stasjon-Q94457.d: Steinvik station is a railway station on the Røros Line. The station is situated near the hamlet of Steinvik in Stor-Elvdal municipality and opened in 1875, two years before the Røros Line was completed. The station building was designed by the architect Georg Andreas Bull and was built in 1873. The brewery building next to the station building was designed by the architect Peter Andreas Blix and was built in 1874. The station was known as Stenvigen from its opening in 1875 and was spelled Stenviken from 1878. Since 1 September 1922, the name has been Steinvik. The station was closed and downgraded to a halt in 1985. The station buildings were sold to private owners. Since 2002, local trains have only stopped here upon direct request to the conductor.

kavringen-fyr-Q9531755.d: Kavringen Lighthouse was built in 1892 and is situated on Søndre Kavringdynge in the western approach channel to the Port of Oslo.

roseslottet-Q97014918.d: Roseslottet is an art installation at Frognerseteren in Oslo, created by the brothers Vebjørn Sand and Eimund Sand. It marked the 80th anniversary in 2020 of Norway’s occupation by Nazi Germany and the 75th anniversary of the country’s liberation. The art park features paintings and installations that tell the story of the Second World War in Norway and of the fundamental principles of democracy, the rule of law and humanism, which were suspended during the occupation. The name ‘Roseslottet’ is inspired by the German non-violent resistance group ‘The White Rose’. Former head of intelligence Kjell Grandhagen served as a mentor for Roseslottet. During the launch of the project on 9

klostergata-7-og-7a-Q97209560.d: Klostergata 7 and 7A is a building comprising two flats – 7 and 7A – situated on Klostergata (Moss).

indery-kapellangard-Q98821924.d: Inderøy Vicarage or Røvika Vicarage (farm number 14/1) is a former vicarage situated west-south-west of Sakshaug in Inderøy, Trøndelag. The vicarage was first mentioned in 1490. It comprises four listed buildings: the main building, erected before 1840; a tenant’s cottage dating from 1840; a storehouse from the 1930s; and a stone cellar from the 17th century. Olaf Jørstad was the tenant here from 1913 to 1954. When the compulsory residence requirement for clergy was abolished, Inderøy Chaplain’s Farm was put up for sale on the private market to limit the expenses of its former owner, the Opplysningsvesenets Fond. As of 2022, the property is privately owned.

indery-prestegard-Q98821943.d: Inderøy Vicarage, or Li Vicarage (farm number 117/1), is situated north of Sakshaug and Straumen on the island of Inderøya in Trøndelag. The vicarage was first mentioned in 1668. A main building erected in 1802–04 and a storehouse were listed in 1992. There is also a farm building dating from 1916 and a tenant’s cottage from 1926. The vicarage is privately owned. Trygve Wang was a farmer here.

folkets-hus-Q98880430.d: Henrich Gerners gate 7 (Cultural Heritage ID 86058), formerly known as Kong Carl, is an old two-storey brick house built by David Chrystie in 1817. It was built in the Empire style and is situated on Henrich Gerners gate in the centre of Moss, near the Odeon Cinema. At that time, Norway was still in union with Sweden, and King Carl IV was on the throne. The house’s original name was ‘Kong Carl’, and it is therefore believed that it was named after the king, King Carl IV, who ruled the country at that time.

kongens-gate-32-Q98897049.d: Kongens gate 32 is a residential and commercial building located in Moss municipality. The building comprises two storeys, as well as a basement and an attic. Today, the premises house Standard Sport AS, as well as two occupied flats. The building is currently protected under the Cultural Heritage Act and is therefore classified as a cultural heritage site (ID: 231609-0). The building is currently preserved as part of a cohesive environment, together with the other houses on Kongens gate that were rebuilt following the town fire of 1881. After the building was rebuilt in 1881, its original (intended) function – retail, residential and settlement – was restored.

haffnergarden-Q98903710.d: Haffnergården is a house and listed building at Storgata 26 in Moss. The building has had this address since 1841 and dates back as far as the 18th century. It has had several different addresses over the years. When the building was first converted from a farmstead to a house, it was at Storgaden 38a; it then became number 22 in 1868, and has been number 26 ever since. The building currently comprises two storeys of flats and a potato cellar which is no longer in use. The building is yellow in colour, with a dark grey plinth featuring fine white wooden details and columns on the façade.

veteranstasjonen-Q98908713.d: MIL Veteran Station is a former petrol station at 26 Lars Hilles gate in Bergen. The station was built in 1928 and remained in operation until 1998. It was granted provisional listed status in 2016 and was finally listed in September 2020. The station was originally designed by architect Sverre Losnedal, who drew on the architectural style of Greek temples when designing it. Six columns once adorned the façade, but now only two remain. The station was renovated in the years following its closure, and in 2005 it opened as a museum. Among the brands that have operated at the station are MIL, BP, Norol and Statoil.

enhjrningsgarden-Q98930185.d: Enhjørningsgården is a street and complex of buildings in Bergen that runs from Bryggen to Bryggestredet. The estate was originally called Einarsgard and was a single farmstead at Bryggen. The first known tenant at Einarsgard was Hermann Skult, who took a lease on the farm in 1259. Later, the farm was owned by Jon Torsteinsson (clerk and notary to Eirik Magnusson and Håkon V) from 1304 to 1311, and from 1395 the farm was purchased by Germans. The Germans held the farm for several hundred years, and it is they who gave it the name ‘Enhjørningsgården’, as they called the farm ‘Der Einhornsgarten’, which was most likely just a slip of the tongue. The farm burnt down in 1702 and was rebuilt as it stands today.

hakadal-verk-Q37114.d: Hakadals Verk is a former ironworks in Hakadal, in the municipality of Nittedal. It may have been Norway’s oldest ironworks; there was probably an ironworks on the site as early as the 15th century. The works are situated by the Hakadalselva river, north-west of Hakadal Church. It was originally called Hadeland Ironworks and was established around 1550. Initially, the ironworks sourced its ore from the surrounding area; this ore was mined from the hills in Hakadal and Gjerdrum. Until it was closed down in 1814, Dalsgruva in Gjerdrum was the works’ main mine in the local area. Ore was also sourced from Grua in Hadeland. After a while, ore began to be transported by ship from Southern Norway to Vækerø.

andorsengarden-Q45835.d: Andorsengården is a building at Store Elvegate 5/6 in the centre of Mandal in Agder. Construction of the building began in 1801 and was completed in 1805 by Mathias Knutzen. It is constructed of brick-filled half-timbering with panelling on the exterior. Architecturally, it blends in well with Mandal’s other old timber-framed buildings, although Mandal Church is the only other building in Mandal town constructed in a similar style. The building was erected during the economic boom of the Napoleonic Wars. As a result of the economic downturn, Mathias Knutzen was forced to sell the building to Consul Gulow Andorsen in 1822 for 1,500 speciedaler. This was a small sum compared with the 44,000 speciedaler that Knutzen himself had spent on its construction.

glamos-stasjon-Q63803.d: Glåmos station is a railway station on the Røros Line at Glåmos in Røros municipality, Trøndelag county. The station was established in 1877 under the name Jensvold as a staffed station for handling trains, passengers and freight. In 1921, the station’s name was changed to Jensvoll, whilst in 1939 it was renamed to its current name, Glåmos. The station and the station area, comprising the goods shed, platform and the remains of the station garden, were listed in 1997 by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage, and is regarded as a valuable national cultural heritage site and one of the best-preserved station areas from the opening of the Røros Railway back in 1877. Glåmos station is situated at an altitude of 638.4 metres above sea level and 412.54 km from Oslo Central Station.

kverkilhaugen-Q101129478.d: Kverkilhaugen is an Early Iron Age hillfort in Inderøy municipality in Trøndelag, which is now a listed cultural heritage site. Kverkilhaugen is situated on top of Kverkilberget, 180 metres above sea level. Kverkilberget rises from a ridge of agricultural land. The summit has natural defences to the north and west, with steep slopes. The cultural heritage site consists of the remains of a wall built of small slabs and rubble. The wall is between half a metre and one and a half metres wide. Its height varies between half a metre and one metre, and the wall is approximately 75 metres long. In the ravine to the north of the fortification wall, eight skeletons were found at one time between 1800 and 1820, lying in succession up the ravine. The discovery was made in connection with limestone quarrying.

martinskirken-Q10577865.d: St Martin’s Church is a former church in Stavanger. It is mentioned in sources dating from 1286 to 1330. St Martin’s Church was probably in use from the mid-13th century until 1537. In the Cathedral, there was a choir cope on which the back of the cope depicts Martin of Tours. The choir cope is therefore probably from St Martin’s Church. As the cope is dated to around 1500, St Martin’s Church may have remained in use until the Reformation. The church was named after the saint Martin of Tours, who is known as one of the earliest French monks and lived at the end of the 4th century.

slevik-batteri-Q10671559.d: Slevik Battery (1808–15) was a fortification at Slevik in Onsøy, established in 1808 during the Napoleonic Wars to protect the Norwegian archipelago fleet against attack. The battery was intended to prevent landings in Slevik Bay, which was a good anchorage. Slevik Battery was equipped with around thirteen guns from Moss Ironworks. Other buildings included stores for provisions, ammunition, a kitchen, materials, a brewery and the guards’ quarters. The planning was overseen by Major-General Hans Christopher Gedde, whilst Infantry Lieutenant Hans Johan Julius Lemvig (1788–?) and his assistant, Second Lieutenant Mathias Hjorth (1783–1850), were in charge of day-to-day management. During the war with Sweden in 1814, Norwegian forces had to be evacuated to the battery at the beginning of August.

baddereidet-fangeleir-Q108678124.d: Baddereidet prison camp was a prison camp during the Second World War in Kvænangen municipality in Troms county, established in 1942. The camp is also known as Veiskaret Prison Camp, and together with Veidal Prison Camp, it formed Kommando Kvænangen, which was an external command under Grini. The satellite camp operated from August to November 1942 and was the northernmost of Grini’s so-called satellite camps. The work on constructing the snow tunnel and snow screens was led by Operation Todt. The camp was guarded by the Wehrmacht.

krabbestig-fetts-fk-nr-1-og-2-freldemyra.d: The rock carvings at Færeldemyra are an automatically protected rock art site and soapstone quarry at Krabbestig on Husevågøy in Kinn municipality, Vestland. The site is registered in the Cultural Heritage Search with cultural heritage ID 35550 under the name ‘Krabbestig – Fetts fk.nr.1 and 2 Færeldemyra, Rock Art’. The site consists of rock carvings featuring ship figures, pits and other figures, and is situated on a rock face protruding from Færeldemyra. A distinctive feature of the site is that the same rock face also bears traces of the extraction of clay pots. Færeldemyra is thus a complex archaeological heritage site with traces of both rock art and later exploitation of raw materials.

husab-Q108709646.d: The rock carving site at Husabø features two ships carved into the rock face. The carvings date from the Bronze Age (1800–500 BC). Both ships have vertical lines symbolising the crew on board. The lower ship lies almost horizontally, approximately 1.4 m above the base of the rock face. The ship has stems at the bow and stern. It has at least 20 lines. The length of the ship from stem to stem is approximately 90 cm. The length of the crew lines averages approximately 6 cm. The upper ship is also positioned almost horizontally, some 1.8 m higher up. This one also has stems at the bow and stern, and at least 19 crew lines. The length of the ship from stem to stem is approximately 90 cm.

hesthagaberget-Q108709925.d: Hesthagaberget is a rural fort dating from the Migration Period in Norway and is situated on the summit of a hill along the western shore of Steinsfjorden, just a few tens of metres east of the E16, where the road plunges down the slope towards Steinsletta at the southernmost point, in Hole municipality. The fortification is also situated just a few hundred metres south-south-west of the old royal estate of Stein in Hole, known from Norse saga literature. The remains of the walls are indistinct and heavily overgrown. The most clearly visible section is located approximately 45 metres north of the south-eastern corner of the fortification. The inner castle area has a distinct plateau at its southern end. Hesthagaberget does not appear to have had a well or any other source of water.

brennpasan-lystadmoen-Q108710154.d: Brennpåsan is an Iron Age soapstone quarry in Lillestrøm municipality in Akershus. The quarry is situated at Lystadmoen, south of Sørum, and together with Piggåsen in Fet and Bergskjul in Blaker, forms a line of quarries that were in use during the same period. The entire hill contains claystone, but the deposit only outcrops in a few places. Larger quantities of claystone vessels from the Viking Age in Romerike have been found here than elsewhere in Eastern Norway, which is likely linked to the quarries in this area. In addition to pots, baksteheller, loom weights, fishing weights and spindle whorls were also produced. The quarry is situated on the northern slope of a ridge and consists of at least 15 pits and shafts. Surrounding the site are several heaps of waste rock.

berg-kirkested-Q108710345.d: Berg Church, also known as Svabu Church after the local community, is a church that no longer exists in what later became the parish of Ringsaker. The church is mentioned by Jens Nilssøn as having been destroyed before 1598. The stone foundations were still visible around 1800 in the ground to the east of the houses on the Mellom-Berg farm. In more recent times, skeletal remains were often found in the ground nearby on a meadow known as Kirkejordet. The foundation is interpreted as the stone plinth for a wooden church. Between 1323 and 1440, priests at Steinberg are frequently mentioned; this was probably separated from Berg as a parish. A large part of the land tax at Berg – 3 huder – was payable to the Ringsaker priest in 1570.

elborg-i-borykilen-Q108714748.d: Elborg in Borøykilen is a listed beach cottage on Borøy in Tvedestrand. The house, which dates from the late 18th century, is a two-storey building with a central hall. The property also includes a single-storey boathouse dating from the early 1800s; this too is listed. The foundations of an outbuilding that burnt down in 1953 or 1954 are protected under the Planning and Building Act. Outside the main house is a large stone jetty. The house is also known as Lauritz Larsen’s house. Elborg is one of the oldest properties on Borøya and comprises a number of plots in various locations on the island. Several islets off Borøykilen belong to the farm. Elborg forms a small part of a large cultural heritage environment.

victoria-hotell-ellingsens-hotell-Q10871.d: The Victoria Hotel, also known as Ellingsen’s Hotel, is a listed, two-storey wooden building constructed in 1846 with a late Empire-style façade, situated in the centre of Egersund. At the rear, the building has been extended with a Swiss-style wing dating from around 1900. The hotel is situated at Strandgaten 41. The building forms part of a cultural environment of national interest that encompasses large parts of Egersund town centre.

strand-internat-Q108715527.d: Strand is a local administrative district and a hamlet at the southern end of Langfjordvatnet in Sør-Varanger, Finnmark. Before the roads were built in the area, travel between the coast and Øvre Pasvik was by boat along Langfjorden and Langfjordvatnet. The beach at the far end of Langfjordvatnet thus became a small hub. The local community had 178 inhabitants in 2017. There has long been a school in the village, and in 1905 it became important to assert Norwegian sovereignty in the area. That year, a new school building with a boarding house was inaugurated, and the building took on an important symbolic role. The school building was extended in both 1914 and 1928. This building is one of the few that was spared during the burning of Finnmark in 1944.

langelandsfjell-Q108717967.d: Langelandsfjell is the highest point on Hidra in Flekkefjord municipality. The nearest higher point is Kjørsfjellet on the mainland to the north-west. In days gone by, the summit was used as a watchtower, and during the Napoleonic Wars there was a semaphore station here. Today, there is a memorial stone here, erected in 1914, commemorating the National Assembly at Eidsvoll.

rrvik-gard-Q108720484.d: Rørvik Farm, or Rørvikgården, is a cultural heritage site in Hamarøy in Nordland. The farmstead is situated by Finnosen, on the western shore of Tysfjorden, about eight kilometres south-east of Storjorda and nine kilometres north/north-east of Drag. The complex dates from the late 19th century and consists of the main building (built in 1776), an outbuilding, a stable and woodshed, a barn and a cowshed. The listed status also covers stone walls, boathouses at Finnosen and Båtstøvatnet, the farm’s old cultivated land and parts of the nearest outlying land. A mill on the site is not included in the listed status. Both the exterior and interior are well preserved.

mallnitz-leiren-Q108727886.d: The Mallnitz camp in Norddalen, in the municipality of Storfjord in Troms county, was a forced labour camp for Soviet prisoners of war from 1944 until the end of the Second World War in 1945. The conditions were appalling and a great many prisoners died. Of the 350 prisoners of war who were put to work building a new defence fortification in Lyngenfjorden, only 18 survived.

fangeleir-Q108728024.d: Ellenes Prison Camp is a cultural heritage site on Lista in Farsund municipality. From 1941 to 1945, there were a large number of Soviet prisoners of war on Lista; they were stationed at the airfield and the coastal forts. The remains of Varnes Fort lie approximately 2 km away (by road).

molstad-kirkested-Q108729556.d: Molstad Church is a former wooden church in Østre Toten municipality, Innlandet county. It served as the parish church for Kolbu parish and was replaced by Kolbu Church in 1730, before being demolished. The church stood on the grounds of the vicarage a few hundred metres west of the present church. Parts of the church’s furnishings were reused in the new church, including several catechism panels. The columns beneath the organ loft are also thought to date from the older church. In the 1570s and later, Molstad Church served as an annex church within the Toten parish, though it had probably had its own vicar during the Middle Ages. *Norske kirker* describes it as a log-built long church dating from around 1300.

djupvik-kirkestue-Q11143699.d: Djupvik Church Hall is a long church dating from 1980 in Kåfjord municipality, Troms county. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 110. Access to the site is via the E6.

evje-Q111804033.d: Evje is a manor house in Rygge, in the municipality of Moss in Østfold. Evje was sold to Johan H. Andresen Jr. in 2020.

gamle-bjelland-bru-Q112236370.d: The Old Bjelland Bridge is a concrete arch bridge spanning the Mandalselva river at Bjelland in Lindesnes municipality, Agder. It is a foot and cycle bridge connecting the Skjeggestadlia local road on the east bank of the river with Marnarveien on the west bank. The Director-General for Cultural Heritage listed the bridge on 17 April 2008, together with Bjelland Bridge, which lies about 100 metres further south. The county council is responsible for its maintenance.

blindheimsvik-dyrefredningsomrade-Q11961.d: The Blindheimsvik Wildlife Sanctuary (Norwegian: Blindheimsvik dyrefredningsområde) is located on the south side of Vigra island in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The area received protection in 1988 "to preserve an important wetland area with its habitat, bird life and other wildlife", according to the conservation regulations. The area consists of a long shallow bay with large tidal areas. Many small streams empty into the bay, where there are beach meadow areas rich in various species. The bay is important as a resting place for ducks and waders, and as an overwintering site and nesting site for wetland birds.

hersvik-kirke-Q11975228.d: Hersvik Church (Norwegian: Hersvik kyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Solund Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Hersvikbygda, on the northern part of the island of Sula. It is one of the three churches for the Solund parish which is part of the Nordhordland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Bjørgvin. The white, wooden church was built in a long church design in 1891 using plans drawn up by the architect Jacob Wilhelm Nordan. The church seats about 168 people.

husy-kirke-Q11976192.d: Husøy Church (Norwegian: Husøy kyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Solund Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Kolgrov, on the western coast of the island of Ytre Sula. It is one of the three churches for the Solund parish which is part of the Nordhordland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Bjørgvin. The white, wooden church was built in a long church design in 1896 using plans drawn up by the architect Peter Andersen. The church seats about 174 people.

roaldsand-dyrefredningsomrade-Q11998042.d: The Roaldsand Wildlife Sanctuary (Norwegian: Roaldsand dyrefredningsområde) is located on the east side of Vigra island in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The area received protection in 1988 "to preserve an important wetland area with its habitat, bird life and other wildlife", according to the conservation regulations. The area consists of several long shallow sandy beaches, some with wind-blown sand. The beaches are open to northeast with no protection from islets or skerries. Ninety-five species of plants have been identified in the area, many of which are rare. The area is a resting and overwintering place for migratory birds.

rrvikvagen-dyrefredningsomrade-Q11998925.d: The Rørvikvågen Wildlife Sanctuary (Norwegian: Rørvikvågen dyrefredningsområde) is located on the west side of Vigra island in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The area received protection in 1988 "to preserve an important wetland area with its habitat, bird life and other wildlife", according to the conservation regulations. The bay is a large shallow inlet with large tidal areas. Many streams empty into the bay, and together with drifting accumulations of seaweed and kelp this creates a basis for plentiful food for wildlife. The inner part of the bay is shielded by a belt of pebbles, where there are ponds and lagoons.

tordenskioldeika-Q12006942.d: The Tordenskiold Oak (in Norwegian:Tordenskioldeika) in Kjølhalskogen in Horten, Norway is one of the oldest trees in Norway. The tree trunk is very hollow, so the tree is almost split in two. The oak was protected by a royal decree on December 9, 1921. It is not possible to say how old the tree is, but it goes for at least 800, maybe close to 1,000 years. The tree has been supported and bolted to hold the trunk together, and a fence has been set up around the tree as a hedge on the day it falls. The biggest threat to the tree was in 1993, when it was discussed both to lift the conservation and to have the heavily enclosed tree removed.

vatneleiren-Q12009120.d: Vatneleiren is a military base located in Sandnes Municipality in Rogaland county, Norway. It was constructed just east of the Hanafjellet mountain just outside the city of Sandnes by the German Army during the German occupation of Norway in World War II, and has been used by the Norwegian Army since 1945. After the Cold War ended the number of soldiers stationed there gradually decreased, and the base is now mainly used by the Norwegian Home Guard. The Agder og Rogaland Heimevernsdistrikt 08 (Agder and Rogaland Home District 08) is based here, covering the two southernmost counties of Rogaland and Agder.

herlaugshaugen-Q120199283.d: The Herlaug Mound (Norwegian: Herlaugshaugen) is a grave mound and ship burial situated on the island of Leka at Skei in Leka Municipality, Norway. The mound dates from about year 700, during the Mervinger Age, and would have been used for a norse funeral for a prominent figure. It is the oldest known ship mound in Scandinavia. The mound is about 60 metres (200 ft), which makes it one of the largest such mounds in Norway. Parts of it have been severely damaged due to excavations during the 18th century.

halandsdal-kirke-Q14389985.d: Hålandsdal Church (Norwegian: Hålandsdal kyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Bjørnafjorden Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Eide at the southern end of the Øvre Hålandsdalen valley, just east of the village of Holdhus. It is one of the churches for the Fusa parish which is part of the Fana prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Bjørgvin. The white, wooden church was built in a long church design in 1890 using plans drawn up by the architect Karl Hansen Askeland. The church seats about 250 people.

sr-spitsbergen-nasjonalpark-Q1577229.d: Sør-Spitsbergen National Park (Norwegian: Sør-Spitsbergen nasjonalpark, English: South Spitzbergen National Park) encompasses the southern end of Spitsbergen island in the Svalbard archipelago, Norway. The park was opened in 1973 and includes Wedel Jarlsberg Land, Torell Land and Sørkapp Land. Over 65% of the region is ice cap, with much of the rest tundra.

giske-dyrefredningsomrade-Q17776167.d: The Giske Wildlife Sanctuary (Norwegian: Giske dyrefredningsområde) is located in the Makkevika inlet on the island of Giske in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The area received protection in 1988 "to preserve an important wetland area with its habitat, bird life and other wildlife", according to the conservation regulations. The inlet is a resting place for wetland birds, especially waders, and it is also an important overwintering place and has a strong nesting population. Six of the bird species that have been observed here are of international importance, 21 species are of national importance, and 35 are of regional importance.

giske-vatmarksystem-Q17776168.d: The Giske Wetlands System (Norwegian: Giske våtmarkssystem) is a Ramsar site located in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It consists of six separate protected areas: two nature reserves and four wildlife sanctuaries. One of the nature reserves lies on the island of Giske and the five other areas are located on the island of Vigra in the same municipality. The areas have been protected as a Ramsar site since 1996 because of their importance for migratory birds. There are large shallow areas with mudflats exposed during low tide. A lot of seaweed (Fucales and kelp) accumulates there, providing good conditions for birds in search of food.

rrvikvatnet-naturreservat-Q19368957.d: The Rørvikvatnet Nature Reserve (Norwegian: Rørvikvatnet naturreservat) is located on the southeast part of Vigra island in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The area received protection in 1988 "to preserve an important wetland area with its appertaining plant communities, bird life, and other wildlife", according to the conservation regulations. The reserve consists of a small shallow pond surrounded by marsh and cultivated land. It is a nesting area for wetland birds and is also an area that birds pass through during migration.

synesvagen-naturreservat-Q19368958.d: The Synesvågen Nature Reserve (Norwegian: Synesvågen naturreservat) is located on the southwest part of Vigra island in Giske Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The area received protection in 1988 "to preserve an important wetland area with its appertaining plant communities, bird life, and other wildlife," according to the conservation regulations. The area is a shallow bay with a seashore rich in species and large tidal banks and sandy areas. The north and east sides have a beach meadow with small ponds and transition into a flat marshland. It is considered one of the most conservation-worthy seasides in the county.

mellandsvagen-naturreservat-Q19368962.d: The Mellandsvågen Nature Reserve (Norwegian: Mellandsvågen naturreservat) is located on the western part of the island of Skardsøya in Aure Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. Since 1996, the nature reserve has had the status of a Ramsar site because of its importance for migratory birds. The area received protection in 1988 "to preserve an important wetland area with its appertaining plant communities, bird life, and other wildlife", according to the conservation regulations. The Mellandsvågen Wildlife Sanctuary (Norwegian: Mellandsvågen dyrefredningsområde), which measures 12.2 square kilometers (4.

harya-vatmarksystem-Q19373693.d: The Harøya Wetlands System (Norwegian: Harøya våtmarkssystem) is a Ramsar site located on Harøya island in Ålesund Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It consists of six separate protected areas: three nature reserves plus a large wildlife sanctuary containing two smaller bird sanctuaries. The areas have been protected as a Ramsar site since 1996 because of their importance for migratory birds. Harøya has large shallow areas with mudflats where seaweed collects. In the inner parts of the island there are marshy areas, and along the beaches there are damp beach meadows. The island is important as an overwintering area and resting area for birds migrating in the spring and fall.

sandland-kapell-Q2792160.d: Sandland Chapel (Norwegian: Sandland kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Loppa Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Sandland. It is an annex chapel for the Loppa parish which is part of the Alta prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1971 using plans drawn up by the architect Reidar Martinsen.

skrolsvik-kapell-Q289887.d: Skrolsvik Chapell (Norwegian: Skrolsvik kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Senja Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Skrollsvika on the southwest coast of the island of Senja. It is an annex chapel for the Tranøy parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1924. The church seats about 170 people.

elvegardsmoen-Q3051809.d: Elvegårdsmoen is a military training camp site in Narvik Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the inner end of Herjangsfjorden, on the southeast side of the village of Bjerkvik. The site was of some importance during the German invasion of Norway in April 1940 and the subsequent Norwegian Campaign. The camp was occupied by German forces on 9 April 1940, and it was recaptured by soldiers from the French Foreign Legion during the Battles of Narvik on 13 May 1940.

medby-kapell-Q322816.d: Medby Chapel (Norwegian: Medby kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Senja Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Medby on the west coast of the island of Senja. It is an annex chapel for the Torsken parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1937. The chapel seats about 170 people.

flakstadvag-kirke-Q322876.d: Flakstadvåg Chapel (Norwegian: Flakstadvåg kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Senja Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Flakstadvåg on the west coast of the island of Senja. It is an annex chapel for the Torsken parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1925 by an unknown architect. The chapel seats about 150 people.

brstad-kirke-Q3392620.d: Brøstad Church (Norwegian: Brøstad kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Dyrøy Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Brøstadbotn. It is one of the churches for the Dyrøy parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1937 using plans drawn up by the architects Bersvend Thoresen Elvevold and Martin Jakobsen. The church seats about 180 people.

vingenfeltet-Q3435970.d: The Vingen rock carvings (Norwegian: Vingenfeltet) are a set of petroglyphs located along the Frøysjøen strait in Bremanger Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. They are located about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) straight east of the village of Berle and about 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) south of the village of Rugsund. The area is accessible by boat or by a 4 to 5 kilometres (2.5 to 3.1 mi) hike from the nearest roads.

masy-kirke-Q4456978.d: Måsøy Church (Norwegian: Måsøy kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Måsøy Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is located in village of Måsøy on the island of Måsøya. It is one of the churches for the Måsøy parish which is part of the Hammerfest prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, concrete church was built in a long church style in 1953 using plans drawn up by the architect Eyvind Moestue. The church seats about 120 people.

ramsund-kapell-Q4576093.d: Ramsund Chapel (Norwegian: Ramsund kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Tjeldsund Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Ramsund. It is an annex chapel in the Tjeldsund parish which is part of the Trondenes prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1964. The chapel seats about 250 people. The chapel was rebuilt in 1970 after a fire.

astafjord-kirke-Q4576153.d: Astafjord Church (Norwegian: Astafjord kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tjeldsund Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Grov. It is the church for the Astafjord parish which is part of the Trondenes prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, concrete church was built in a fan-shaped design in 1978 using plans drawn up by the architect Harald Hille. The church seats about 300 people.

frya-kirke-Q4576259.d: Frøya Church (Norwegian: Frøya kyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Bremanger Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Kalvåg, on the southern coast of the small island of Frøya. It is the church for the Frøya parish which is part of the Nordfjord prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Bjørgvin. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1865. The architect was the painter artist Anders Askevold from the nearby Askvoll Municipality. The church seats about 400 people.

fjelldal-kapell-Q4576342.d: Fjelldal Chapel (Norwegian: Fjelldal kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Tjeldsund Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Fjelldal. It is an annex chapel in the Tjeldsund parish which is part of the Trondenes prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1960, using plans drawn up by the architect Birger Stoltenberg. The chapel seats about 140 people.

tjongsfjorden-kirke-Q4576353.d: Tjongsfjorden Church (Norwegian: Tjongsfjorden kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway, located in Rødøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It stands in the village of Tjong on the mainland in the northern part of the municipality. It is one of the churches in the Rødøy parish, which is part of the Nord-Helgeland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1962, based on plans drawn up by the architect Per Myrvold. The church seats approximately 280 people.

sandhorny-kapell-Q4576513.d: Nordstranda Chapel (Norwegian: Nordstranda kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Gildeskål Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Lekanger on the west side of the island of Sandhornøya. It is an annex chapel in the Gildeskål parish which is part of the Bodø domprosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1963 using plans drawn up by the architect Kirsten Wleügel Knutssøn. The chapel seats about 160 people.

lkta-kirke-Q4576597.d: Løkta Church (Norwegian: Løkta kirke) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Dønna Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Sandåker on the island of Løkta. It is an annex chapel in the Dønna parish which is part of the Nord-Helgeland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1968. The chapel seats about 90 people.

sulitjelma-kapell-Q4576621.d: Sulitjelma Chapel (Norwegian: Sulitjelma kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Fauske Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Sulitjelma. It is an annex chapel in the Sulitjelma parish which is part of the Salten prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The small, red, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1996 on the site of the new church graveyard on the south side of the village since the old graveyard for the Sulitjelma Church had no more room to expand.

srfjorden-kapell-Q4576918.d: Sørfjorden Chapel (Norwegian: Sørfjorden kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Gildeskål Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Sørfinnset. It is an annex chapel in the Gildeskål parish which is part of the Bodø domprosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland, although the chapel building is not owned by the parish, it is privately owned by the local residents of the Sørfjorden farms. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1927 using plans drawn up by the architect Thomas Strandskogen. The chapel seats about 300 people. The church is used for worship services about four times each year.

okkelberg-kapell-Q4576980.d: Okkelberg Chapel (Norwegian: Okkelberg kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Stjørdal Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the village of Skjelstadmarka. It is one of the churches for the Hegra parish which is part of the Stjørdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1905 using plans drawn up by the architect Ole Andresen. The church seats about 200 people.

fiplingdal-kirke-Q4577021.d: Fiplingdal Church (Norwegian: Fiplingdal kirke) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Grane Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located on the north side of the tiny village of Leiren on the north end of the lake Nedre Fiplingvatnet. It is an annex chapel for the Grane parish which is part of the Indre Helgeland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The red, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1946 to serve as a mission house. The church seats about 70 people. The building was consecrated as a "chapel" on 6 December 1964. In 2012, the chapel was renovated and a new bathroom was completed.

fosnes-kapell-Q4577334.d: Fosnes Chapel (Norwegian: Fosnes kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Namsos Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located at Fosnesvågen, on the northeastern coast of the island of Jøa. It is an annex chapel for the Fosnes parish which is part of the Namdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden chapel was built in a long church style in 1926. The church seats about 45 people. The church is not regularly used for services, but it is used for funerals at the adjacent cemetery. There is an annual worship service held at the chapel once each summer at Olsok.

lund-kapell-Q4577470.d: Lund Chapel (Norwegian: Lund kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Namsos Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. It is located in the village of Lund. It is an annex church for the Fosnes parish which is part of the Namdal prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nidaros. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1965. The church seats about 105 people.

hol-kirke-Q4583131.d: Hol Church (Norwegian: Hol kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Vestvågøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located on the southeastern edge of the town of Leknes on the island of Vestvågøya. It is the church for the Hol parish which is part of the Lofoten prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a cruciform style in 1806 using plans drawn up by an unknown architect. The church seats about 300 people.

solund-kirke-Q4884485.d: Solund Church (Norwegian: Solund kyrkje) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Solund Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Hardbakke on the western coast of the island of Sula. It is one of the three churches for the Solund parish which is part of the Nordhordland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Bjørgvin. The white, wooden church was built in a long church design in 1860 using plans drawn up by the architect Christian Henrik Grosch. The church seats about 200 people.

forlandsyane-fuglereservat-Q5469853.d: Forlandsøyane Bird Sanctuary (Norwegian: Forlandsøyane fuglereservat) is a bird reserve at Svalbard, Norway, established in 1973. It includes Forlandsøyane off Prins Karls Forland. The protected area covers a total area of around 5,400,000 square metres.

grtavr-kirke-Q5612893.d: Grøtavær Church (Norwegian: Grøtavær kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Harstad Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Grøtavær on the island of Grytøya. It is one of the churches for the Vågsfjord parish which is part of the Trondenes prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1915 using plans drawn up by an unknown architect. The church seats about 200 people.

tunheim-Q59920004.d: Tunheim is an abandoned coal mining village on Bear Island, Svalbard, Norway. It lies in the northeast of the Island, a few kilometers east of the Bjørnøya Radio Station, and directly adjacent to Kapp Bergersen. To its south is Miseryfjellet, the tallest mountain on Bear Island. Coal mining activities were run by the Stavanger company and were at their height around 1915–1925 and 182 people lived in the village's 25 houses, but then the mining was given up as unprofitable. A radio station was built in 1919 and a meteorological station in 1923, operated by the Geophysical Institute in Tromsø.

kirkenesmoen-kapell-Q6415660.d: Kirkesnesmoen Chapel (Norwegian: Kirkesnesmoen kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Målselv Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located along the Målselva river about halfway between the villages of Bardufoss and Skjold. It is an annex church for the Øverbygd parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1975 by the architect Nils Gang at the architecture firm Harry Gangvik A/S. The church seats about 220 people.

srkapp-fuglereservat-Q6514249.d: Sørkapp Bird Sanctuary (Norwegian: Sørkapp fuglereservat) is a bird reserve at Svalbard, Norway, established in 1973. It includes Sørkappøya and other islands off Sørkapp Land, Spitsbergen. The protected area covers a total area of 3,599ha

lundenes-kirke-Q6704129.d: Lundenes Church (Norwegian: Lundenes kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Harstad Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Lundenes on the island of Grytøya. It is one of the churches for the Vågsfjord parish which is part of the Trondenes prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The red, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1974 using plans drawn up by the architect Osvald Flakstad. The church seats about 200 people.

u-864-Q700927.d: German submarine U-864 was a Type IXD2 U-boat of Nazi Germany's Kriegsmarine in World War II. On 9 February 1945, she became the only submarine in history to be sunk by an enemy submarine while both were submerged. U-864 was sunk by the British submarine HMS Venturer, and all 73 men on board died.

salangsdalen-kapell-Q7403629.d: Salangsdalen Chapel (Norwegian: Salangsdalen kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Bardu Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the southern part of Bardu in the Salangsdalen valley, just east of the European route E06 highway and not far from the Polar Park. It is an annex chapel for the Bardu parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The brown, wooden church was built in 1981 using plans drawn up by the architects Dalsbø and Østgård. The church seats about 110 people.

straumen-kapell-Q7622312.d: Straumen Chapel (Norwegian: Straumen kapell) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Sørreisa Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the village of Sørreisa. It is one of the churches for the Sørreisa parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, brick church was built in a rectangular design in 1973 using plans drawn up by the architect Elisabeth Breen Fidjestøl. The church seats about 170 people. There is a free standing bell tower to the east of the main entrance. The church includes a parish hall, offices, and lounge area that includes two ping pong tables.

sundene-Q7639663.d: Sundene is a village in Færder Municipality in Vestfold county, Norway. The village is located on the island of Tjøme, about 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) to the north of the village of Tjøme, about 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) to the north of the village of Svelvik, and about 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) to the northwest of the village of Grimestad. A bridge connects Sundene with the village of Kjøpmannskjær which lies about 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) to the northwest on the island of Nøtterøy. The village of Sundene and the surrounding countryside had a population (in 2007) of 345.

srfjorden-kirke-Q7666611.d: Sørfjorden Church (Norwegian: Sørfjorden kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Rødøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Sørfjorden on the mainland in the southern part of the municipality. It is one of the churches in the Rødøy parish which is part of the Nord-Helgeland prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1916 using plans drawn up by the architect O.M. Olsen. The church seats about 130 people.

vre-bardu-kapell-Q8079284.d: Øvre Bardu Chapel (Norwegian: Øvre Bardu kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Bardu Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located along the Sørdalselva river in the Sørdalen valley in eastern Bardu. It is an annex chapel for the Bardu parish which is part of the Senja prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1971 using plans drawn up by the architect Petter Bratli. The church seats about 200 people.

valjok-kirke-Q9030018.d: Valjok Church (Norwegian: Valjok kirke) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Karasjok Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Váljohka. It is an annex chapel for the Karasjok parish which is part of the Indre Finnmark prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The small, red, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1932 by the architect Harald Sund. The church was built to serve the inhabitants in the northeastern part of the municipality, along the Tana River. The church seats about 60 people. The interior colouring is remarkable, with strong red and blue detail set against golden, unpainted woodwork.

brenna-kapell-Q9030328.d: Brenna Chapel (Norwegian: Brenna kapell) is a chapel of the Church of Norway in Porsanger Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Brenna. It is an annex chapel for the Porsanger parish which is part of the Indre Finnmark prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Nord-Hålogaland. The white, wooden church was built in a long church style in 1971 by the architect Edvard Bruvoll. The church seats about 55 people.

helleristningene-pa-foss-Q116631126.d: The rock carvings at Foss are a large site containing Bronze Age rock art in Horg, Melhus, Trøndelag. Since the 1950s, rock art has been found at 55 different sites at Foss in Melhus. The rock carvings are situated in the terraced landscape on the eastern side of the Gauldalen valley.

akersberg-gruver-Q11957118.d: The Akersberg Mines, or Akersberget Mines, are a disused silver mine in Oslo. The mine is situated on the rocky outcrop east of Gamle Aker Church, sloping down towards Maridalsveien. Visible remains of the silver mines can still be seen here in the form of the rock face that borders the churchyard to the east, and one or more adits. It is believed to be the country’s oldest mine. In *Historia Norvegiae*, a brief history of Norway written in Latin in the 1170s, mention is made of a mine in Oslo, called ‘Dragehullene’, which is rich in silver. It states: ‘Likewise, near the town of Oslo there is a great wealth of silver, but a powerful stream has now closed it off to people, so that it lies hidden beneath the rocky outcrops.’ This description fits the Akersberg mine well.

amtmannsnes-Q11957751.d: Amtmannsnes is a low headland and a settlement in Alta on the north-eastern side of Komsafjellet at the head of the Altafjord. Amtmannsnes is also one of the five rock art sites in Alta included on UNESCO’s World Heritage List. The first figures were discovered in 1977; since then, more than 500 figures have been identified, spread across five sites. They are estimated to be between 4,000 and 5,000 years old and mainly depict people, reindeer and patterns. Traces of other human activity have also been found in the same area.

arbeiderboligen-pa-stlen-Q11958528.d: The workers’ housing at Stølen, also known simply as ‘Boligen’, is situated in the Stølen neighbourhood of Bergen.
