The building is the oldest surviving workers’ housing complex built by a philanthropic society in Norway. The building was constructed between 1853 and 1854 by the Philanthropic Society for the Construction of Workers’ Housing, based on designs by city architect Hans Hansen Kaas, assisted by Lieutenant Carl Fredrik Diriks (‘Fyrdiriks’). Originally, two long residential blocks were built, both with two storeys. Each block contained 24 flats, each comprising one room and a kitchen, spread across three stairwells. In 1865, one of the blocks was destroyed by fire. The remaining building was also damaged in a fire in 1980 and was at serious risk of demolition.

arnatveit-gard-Q11958999.d: Arnatveit Farm, farm number 288 and property number 2, is situated at the very top of Oppetveiten in Arnatveit, in the Arna district of Bergen. In the farmyard stands one of the country’s few surviving secular timber-framed houses from the Middle Ages, dating from 1533. The main house (gnr 288 and bnr 4) was automatically listed by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage in 1996. The listing covers the exterior, interior and fixtures attached to the walls, as well as a 5-metre buffer zone around the building.

aubeberget-Q11959577.d: Aubeberget is a small mound in Stavanger featuring a site of Bronze Age rock carvings. The mound is situated right next to Hafrsfjord, in Sunde in the Madla district. It is located below the Aubeberget housing cooperative, next to a football pitch. As a cultural heritage site from the Bronze Age, the rock carvings are automatically protected under the Cultural Heritage Act. The Norwegian Directorate for Cultural Heritage’s ID number is 54248. The site consists of 96 figures, spread across three areas on the rocky outcrop. One group is located in the western part, right at the foot of the rocky outcrop. Two groups are situated further east and slightly higher up the rock face. Most of the figures depict boats, but there are also wheel crosses and circles. The largest ship is 2.10 metres long, and the second-largest is 1.90 metres.

auran-kirke-Q11959655.d: Auran Church was a church at Auran in Skatval, in the municipality of Stjørdal. The church was associated with the large estate on the site – which has since been divided up several times – and can be traced back as far as the 12th century. In 1589, Auran, Fløan and Skjølstad – three Catholic churches that were no longer considered necessary – were closed down. This left four churches in the parish of Stjørdal: the main church at Værnes and the annexes at Skatval, Hegra and Leksdal (Lånke). These churches were to be served by two priests. On the initiative of the Skatval Historical Society, a commemorative plaque has been erected in honour of Auran Church.

betel-bedehuskapell-Q11960902.d: Betel Prayer House Chapel is a church built in a rectangular shape in 1926 in Bø, in the municipality of Vesterålen, Nordland county. The chapel belongs to the Bø and Malnes parish in the Vesterålen deanery. The building is made of timber and has a capacity of 200.

blomberg-Q11961615.d: Blomberg (approx. 450 metres above sea level) is an abandoned mountain farm by the Geirangerfjord. The buildings have been restored by the Friends of Storfjorden in consultation with the Directorate for Cultural Heritage. From the farm, there are views of the fjord and the waterfalls Brudesløret, De syv søstrene and Friaren. It is one of several farms situated on or beneath exposed mountain slopes in Geiranger, alongside farms such as Megardsplassen, Horvadrag, Matvik, Knivsflå and Skageflå. The sightseeing boat MS ‘Geirangerfjord’ departs from Geiranger town centre. From the fjord, the journey up to Blomberg takes 60 minutes; it is slightly shorter to Knivsflå, a 40-minute walk, and even shorter still to Skageflå, a walk of around 25 minutes.

borgklinten-Q11961963.d: Borgklinten, near Ottersbo in Ørland municipality, is a rocky outcrop featuring a village fort dating from the Migration Period. The site was probably constructed sometime between the years 0 and 600 as a place of refuge for the surrounding village. The foundation of the fortress is the hard-to-reach hill known as Litj-Borgklinten itself. Stone walls, approximately 100 metres in length, were then built on this hill to make the site even more difficult to capture. It is likely that the wall may have been constructed in combination with a palisade of wooden logs, but no remains of such a structure have been found. At some other fortified sites, however, traces of wooden defences have been found on top of the walls.

bruuns-repslageri-Q11962423.d: Bruun’s rope-making workshop is situated at Fjøsangerveien 71 in the Årstad district of Bergen. There used to be two rope-making mills here: the Mathisen mill, dating from 1856, and the Sørvig mill, dating from 1831–1833. In 1996, the Mathisen mill burnt down. Following this, Fjøsangerveien was widened to four lanes.

budsjord-gard-Q11962520.d: Budsjord Farm is a listed medieval farm in Dovre municipality in the Innlandet region. The farm was run with a traditional and varied livestock operation until the 1950s. The farmyard comprises 17 listed buildings. Old furnishings and farm implements have been preserved. The farm was formerly under the jurisdiction of the Diocese of Nidaros. The name of the farm derives from ‘Biskupsgjerdi’, which means ‘the bishop’s fenced-in land’. In the past, the archbishop owned the farm along with several other farms in Dovre. Recent research into the old reindeer-trapping facilities in Dovre suggests that it was the trapping of wild reindeer that made the village so interesting to the archbishop, amongst others.

dronningberget-Q11966098.d: Dronningberget is a hill on Bygdøy in the Frogner district of Oslo, which was developed as a park in the 18th century. The restoration and re-establishment of Dronningberget as a park was the Government’s gift to King Harald V and Queen Sonja on their 70th birthdays on 21 February and 4 July 2007 respectively. Dronningberget was designated a nature reserve in 2012.

dvergsten-Q11966224.d: Dvergsten is a farm in Gran in Hadeland, south of Brandbu town centre. According to Rygh, the name derives from ‘Dvergasteinn’. There is, in fact, a large stone on the farm, and in folklore, dwarves were said to live in stones. According to local tradition, the stone was thrown by the troll (‘the dwarf’) during the Battle of Brandbu when he was disturbed by the church bells at the old church in Tingelstad. He failed to throw it far enough, and the stone came to rest where the farm was later built. The stone still lies between the main building and the farm outbuilding at Dvergsten. It was probably quarried at Mæna, which lies about five kilometres further north. The farm is one of the largest in Gran municipality and had its own farm chapel in the Middle Ages.

evenes-vatmarkssystem-Q11968194.d: The Evenes wetland system is a Ramsar site in Evenes municipality in Nordland and Tjeldsund municipality in Troms, comprising five separate nature reserves which, both collectively and individually, constitute valuable wetland areas: Tennvatn Nature Reserve in Tjeldsund, established in 1995; Myrvatn Nature Reserve in Tjeldsund, established in 1995; Sommervatnet Nature Reserve in Evenes, established in 1997; Kjerkvatnet Nature Reserve in Evenes, established in 1997; and Nautå Nature Reserve in Evenes, established in 1997

fjellbratakollen-Q11969068.d: Fjellbråtakollen (550 metres above sea level) is an Iron Age fortification, a so-called ‘bygdeborg’. The fortification is situated on a side hill of Somdalskollen (615 metres above sea level), just north of Somdalen and Sommamoen and only a few kilometres north of Hallingby and south-west of Samsjøen, in Ytre Ådal in Ringerike municipality. Just south-west of Fjellbråtakollen lies the old cadastral farmstead of Bergsund (farm no. 276), now divided into the large estates of Østre and Vestre Bergsund, which lie on either side of the Ådalselva river. Østre Bergsund lies between European Route 16 through Ådal and the Ådalselva river. A little to the south of Bergsund lies the old cadastral farm Somdalen (gnr. 275) along the River Somma, which rises in the south of Lake Samsjøen and flows into the River Ådalselva.

fokstugu-veggarasje-Q11969326.d: The Fokstugu roadside garage was built in the Dovrefjell mountains in the early 1940s. Snow-clearing crews used the garage to store their snow-clearing equipment so that the main road could be kept open. Inside the garage, there is now a Peterfres snow blower from 1943, which was developed by the Swiss engineer Konrad Peter. The garage is a listed building.

foldryskipet-Q11969331.d: The Foldrøy shipwreck is a shipwreck that was discovered in the summer of 1958 off the steamship quay at Foldrøyhamn, Foldrøy on Bømlo, after the scheduled ferry MS ‘Bremnes’ had dredged sand from the seabed. Closer examination revealed that it was a medieval shipwreck that had been partially preserved in the seabed sand. In 1965, the wreck remains were removed from the waters off the quay following reports that a vessel had struck the wreck and torn away a section of it. Most of the archaeological material at the site has probably been removed, but it was possible to carry out a survey and a detailed examination of the wreck remains.

fondal-gard-Q11969418.d: Fondal Farm is a typical Nordland farm dating from around 1880, with its residential buildings almost entirely intact. The farm is situated in Fonndalen on the southern shore of Holandsfjorden in Meløy municipality, Nordland. The farm is of considerable environmental value and is an important source of knowledge about the architectural traditions of the region. It has played a key role as accommodation for tourists visiting Saltfjellet and Svartisen, and is comparable to the Swiss-style timber hotels of Western Norway from the same period. No other farm with a similar function has been preserved in Nordland.

foynegarden-Q11969814.d: Foynegården in Tønsberg is the town’s best-preserved merchant’s estate. The entire estate has been preserved, comprising the merchant’s house itself facing Nedre Langgate, and the boathouse facing the jetty and harbour. Between these buildings lay the cowshed and stables, the hayloft and the garden. Foynegården is an 18th-century patrician house. Svend Foyn was born here in 1809. According to the Director-General of Cultural Heritage, the house is characterised by a symmetrical and elegant façade design in a simple classical style with understated detailing. Dendrochronological studies show that the house was built in 1752 or shortly afterwards. Much of the interior fittings and décor date from the early 19th century.

fredriksodde-Q11970113.d: Fredriksodde was a small fort built slightly south of Larkollen in Østfold county. The fort was intended to protect the local harbour. It was built following the outbreak of the Great Northern War, and the first construction costs can be traced back to Quartermaster-General Caspar Schøller in 1711, with an order for a redoubt with a Corps de Garde. The fort takes its name from King Frederick IV’s visit in 1719. Tordenskiold mentions the harbour no fewer than 34 times, and he himself anchored there with the ship of the line ‘Laaland’ for three days in 1717. After the Great Northern War ended, the fort was of lesser importance, but was maintained until 1730. Today, only the remains of the gunpowder cellar can be found in a garden at Larkollen.

glomadeltaet-landskapsvernomrade-Q119722.d: The Glomå Delta Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Rana municipality in Nordland. The landscape conservation area is located in Langvassgrenda and comprises the delta where the rivers Glomåga and Nordelva flow into Lake Langvatnet. The area is designated as a wildlife sanctuary because it is a wetland area with birdlife and valuable bog and marsh vegetation. The area was established in 1997 and covers 5.9 km². County Road 355 runs along the northern edge of the landscape conservation area.

grunnfarnes-bedehus-Q11972738.d: Grunnfarnes Prayer House is a prayer house dating from 1948 in Senja municipality, Troms county. The prayer house has a capacity of 75.

grabrdreklosteret-i-tnsberg-Q11973023.d: The Grey Friars’ Monastery was a Franciscan monastery in Tønsberg. It was probably founded in the 1240s, during the reign of Håkon Håkonsson. The monastery remained in existence until it was destroyed in the town fire of 1536. The walls were subsequently used as a quarry, and are said to have been completely gone by 1551. The monastery was founded following a donation from King Håkon Håkonsson to his son, the future King Magnus Lagabøte. The monastery church was soon moved to the Premonstratensian monastery at Dragsmark in Båhuslen. It is unclear whether it was the church building itself that was moved, or whether it was the privileges associated with the church that were transferred. However, the monastery did have a church dedicated to Saint Catherine in 1277.

haudegen-Q11974436.d: Haudegen (or Wetterstation Haudegen) is a disused German meteorological station dating from the Second World War, situated on the eastern side of Wordiebukta in Rijpfjorden, in the south of Prins Oscars Land in the northern part of Nordaustlandet on Svalbard. The station was established in the autumn of 1944 to improve access to meteorological information, as several German meteorological aircraft and ships had been shot down or sunk during the war. The German soldiers stationed there surrendered on 4 September 1945 and are regarded as the last German unit to formally capitulate, almost four months after all other German forces had surrendered. The station was headed by Dr.

hauerseter-leir-Q11974439.d: Hauerseter Camp is a military camp in Akershus which serves as the headquarters for the Norwegian Armed Forces’ dog training school, but is also frequently used by various units of the Home Guard. The camp is centrally located just north of Jessheim, close to the railway line and the E6 motorway. Hauerseter has been used as a military training ground since the late 19th century. The camp, with its substantial complex of buildings, was constructed by German forces during the Second World War to store explosives and ammunition for supply to Gardermoen Military Airfield. There are still numerous old German buildings in the area, though many have also been demolished. In the outer part of the camp, there are several areas where the Germans laid cobblestones, deep in the forest.

hellandsbygd-kapell-Q11974865.d: Hellandsbygd Chapel is a long church dating from 1956 in Sauda municipality, Rogaland county. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 50. Hellandsbygd Chapel was converted from a prayer house into a chapel in 1956. The chapel has a meeting and activity hall.

helleristningene-ved-vangdal-Q11974885.d: The rock carvings at Vangdal consist of two sites of rock carvings near Vangdal, approximately nine kilometres south of Norheimsund in Kvam, on the north side of the Hardangerfjord in Hordaland. The rock carvings are situated close to County Road 49, Vikøyvegen, between Norheimsund and Strandebarm, on a steep rocky outcrop, Salthammeren, just east of the road. They are spread across two sites. The younger of the two dates from the Bronze Age and is situated at the foot of the cliff; it consists of several ship carvings. These are easily accessible from the south side of the rest area at the site. On the upper side of the rock face lies a field featuring three animal figures, probably deer, and a stylised human figure.

holmestrand-museum-Q11975695.d: Holmestrand Museum is a town museum in Holmestrand, Vestfold. The museum is housed in the former Holstgården mansion, built in 1756, with its entrance on Nils Kjærgate. Holmestrand Museum is a private museum, owned and run by the Holmestrand Museum Association. Holmestrand Museum traces the development of the town and the surrounding district from the 16th century onwards and houses paintings, models and equipment from Holmestrand’s sailing ship era, as well as the classic interiors of the Holst and Graarud rooms. The museum holds cultural-historical artefacts and a photographic archive by Louise Wold comprising around 29,000 images. These are held by Vestfoldmuseene IKS. The building is a patrician house built in 1756 by Fredrik Christensen Holst, and was originally square in plan.

horsvr-naturreservat-Q11975849.d: Horsvær Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in the municipalities of Brønnøy, Sømna and Bindal in Nordland. The reserve was established to ‘preserve a coastal area of national importance, with its naturally associated flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding, moulting and wintering ground for seabirds’. The area comprises several small islets, including Gimsan, Terjan, Gjøvan, Horsvær, Hensteinen and Storbraken. It covers an area of 170.4 km², of which 169.1 km² is marine area. Within the nature reserve lie the Hensteinen, Horsvær and Gimsan bird sanctuaries. A large proportion of South Helgeland’s breeding sites for the lesser black-backed gull are found here.

kastellet-gard-Q11980373.d: Kastellet Farm was originally a smallholding belonging to Nordseter Farm, dating from the 1750s. In 1813, a fine main building was erected, alongside the old building from the 18th century. The house is constructed of log timber, with external panelling of more recent date. In 1832, the farm was purchased by Jørgen Wright Cappelen, the founder of J. W. Cappelen’s publishing house. Kastellet has now been completely renovated both inside and out and is a rare example of its kind in Oslo, as well as one of the very oldest large houses still standing in the Nordstrand district. Inside, one can still admire the original wide pine floors and timber walls. The house is now located at Kastellveien 2 D, just below Ekebergveien, directly south of the Kastellet tram stop.

kokkeplassen-Q11981418.d: Kokkeplassen is a property on Hisøy in Arendal. Kokkeplassen is what is known as a ‘lystgård’, a type of country house that townspeople built on the outskirts of towns in the late 18th century and during the 19th century. Such country estates were used for leisure and socialising, but also for farming. The name of the place dates back to the timber trade era, when Dutch merchants who came to collect timber anchored at the site and gave it its name, presumably because they prepared their meals there. The main house on the estate was originally built as a summer residence in 1792 in the Rococo/Empire style by the solicitor Peder G. Ussing. He was married to Anne Marie and gave it to her as a wedding present. For more than 100 years, the estate was known as Marienlund.

laukhella-kapell-Q11983444.d: Laukhella Chapel was a long church built in 1949 in Lenvik municipality (since 2020: Senja), Troms county. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 100. The chapel was deconsecrated on 5 June 2011.

lille-rygge-Q11984014.d: Lille Rygge is now the name of the former Rygge Airport in Rygge, Østfold.

lund-bygdemuseum-og-kulturbank-Q11986987.d: Lund Local History Museum and Cultural Centre is situated at Lund Vicarage, approximately 300 metres along County Road 1, south of Moi town centre. The museum is housed in the old vicarage barn. It holds a collection of nearly 10,000 artefacts. Lund’s history, which traces a transition from agriculture to industry, is reflected in the museum’s collection. The museum has regional responsibility for woodcraft and boasts particularly rich collections in the fields of woodturning and cooperage. The museum was opened in 1976 by Salve O. Salvesen. He launched the idea of a ‘cultural bank’ where the residents of Lund could preserve their ‘roots’ for the enjoyment of young and old alike. On the other side of the county road lies the smallholding ‘Haien’ and a historic apple orchard.

mandal-sykehus-Q11988010.d: Mandal Hospital was a hospital in Mandal in Vest-Agder. The decision to build the hospital was taken in 1877, and work on the site began in the summer of 1878. Mandal Hospital was completed and opened on 9 October 1879. The hospital was built on ‘Lille Simons Bakke’. It was financed by grants from the spirits company, totalling NOK 20,612. This sum covered materials, labour costs and furnishings, including 12 beds. The hospital was built by master builder Carl Weyergang. Among other things, he also built Lord Salvesen’s cabin in Åseral and the summer residence at Risøbank.

mjelde-kirke-Q11989657.d: Mjelde Church was a church in Nedre Mjelde in Mjeldalen, in the parish of Haus on the island of Osterøy in Vestland County. It probably dates from the 12th–13th centuries and was originally a stave church, situated alongside an early Christian burial ground. It was rebuilt in the 17th century and served as a private church for the Mjelde estate until it was demolished in 1866. The Garmann family (Herman Garman) owned the church for a long time and endowed it with generous gifts. The Mjeldegodset estate passed out of the Garmann family’s hands in the early 19th century and was purchased by the local council in the 1860s, but it is now in a state of disrepair and has virtually disappeared. The Mjeldegodset estate comprised several buildings and a large rose garden to the west of the main building. All traces of these have vanished.

msvasstangen-landskapsvernomrade-Q119904.d: The Møsvasstangen Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area in Vinje municipality, Telemark. The nature reserve is situated on a headland jutting out into Lake Møsvatnet (919 metres above sea level) and has had Ramsar Site status since 1996, due to its importance for migratory birds. The area was designated a protected area in 1989 to preserve a beautiful, distinctive and largely unspoilt natural landscape featuring interesting deposits from the last ice age, finely formed string bogs, a rich and rare birdlife, and abundant cultural heritage sites from the ironworks. The conservation area is relatively large, comprising a vast expanse of relatively undisturbed bog, some woodland and a few small bodies of water. There are various types of bog in the area, ranging from nutrient-poor bogs to nutrient-rich bogs.

nedre-knive-Q11991052.d: Nedre Knive (34/306) is a registered farm in the Åskollen district of Drammen, with the address Svelvikveien 260, 3037 Drammen. The farm probably takes its name from the hill, Knivåsen, which in turn probably derives its name from its shape, which was likened to a knife. Until 1853, the farm was undivided and stretched from the Drammen Fjord across the ridge towards Eiker. The second, separated holding is situated on the western slope of Østbygda. Before 1870, the village road along the shore ran through the farmyard of the lower farm. Aasa Salmundsdatter of Selvik in Sande was the owner of the farm in 1351; she bequeathed it in 1396 to the Order of the Brothers of the Cross at Tunsberg and Hovedøen Abbey. At the time of the Reformation, the farm probably became crown property.

nedrestrand-Q11991068.d: Nedrestrand is the name of farm number 3 in Gaular municipality (since 2020, Sunnfjord municipality), Vestland county. The farm is situated on the south side of Hestadfjorden, with County Road 421 passing through the farm. The farm is divided into the following holdings: Holding 1, Holding 2 (the Indrebø site), which was separated from Holding 1 in 1928

nrstad-Q11992920.d: Nærstad (farm no. 90) (the first part is probably derived from the Old Norse male name Neriðr) is an old large farmstead in the former Norderhov parish, now Ringerike municipality in Buskerud. The buildings are situated on a hill just west of the E16 and the River Randselva, between the former Hvalsmoen camp and Eggemoen. The farm is mentioned in a number of charters from 1528 (NRJ. IV 148) onwards. The coordinates in the top right-hand corner refer to Nærstad fort.

olavskjelda-pa-leirskogen-Q11993512.d: Olavskjelda at Leirskogen is a spring in Leirskogen in Sør-Aurdal municipality. According to legend, St Olav is said to have stopped here on his mission to spread Christianity in 1023. The soldiers accompanying him were thirsty, so Olav thrust his sword into the ground, and fresh water gushed forth from beneath a rock. There are several such St Olav’s springs around the country, and they are all associated with similar legends. As with the other springs, legend has it that this one also has healing properties. Analyses of the spring water have shown that it contains heavy metals and should not be drunk in large quantities. A warning sign has therefore been erected on site stating that the water contains dangerous minerals.

oppenborgen-Q11993957.d: Oppenborgen is a collective term for the two closely situated rural fortifications ‘Ormekula’ and ‘Slotteberget’, two prehistoric defensive structures that were probably built in Ringerike during the Late Roman Iron Age–Migration Period (corresponding to 200–600 AD). The area is situated in a hilly, coniferous woodland known as Raukleiva, though most people regard it as part of Kilemoen. Raukleiva is within walking distance just east of the modern settlement at the top of Oppenåsen and a short distance north-north-west of the old manor farms of Kile and Follum, in Ringerike municipality. This is just a few kilometres from the ancient farmstead of Ve, which was probably of great importance to the large burial ground at Veien, synonymous with Buskerud County’s 1,000-year-old site.

rdymannen-Q11998878.d: The Rødøy Man is a figure in a larger rock carving site at Tro on the island of Rødøy in Alstahaug municipality in Nordland. The carving was discovered by Gutorm Gjessing in 1933. The figure is considered to be one of the earliest depictions of a skier in Norway and is dated to the Late Stone Age, around 2000 BC. It forms part of a larger, south-west-facing rock carving site (Rødøy 1), which also features another, incomplete carving of a person on skis, two nisse figures, three elk figures, a seal and two boats. In 2016, the rock carving was vandalised with a sharp object.

rstyan-landskapsvernomrade-Q11998935.d: The Røstøyan Landscape Conservation Area was established in 2002 and is situated in Røst municipality in Nordland. The area is designated as a wildlife sanctuary and covers an area of 69,864 daa, of which 66,929 daa is marine area. The landscape conservation area was established on account of its natural and cultural landscape, including its botany, geology and wildlife, and is protected under the 2011 Ramsar Convention. Within the landscape conservation area, Norway’s largest population of puffins (Fratercula arctica) nests on the five important seabird islands of Vedøya, Storfjellet, Ellevsnyken, Trenyken and Hernyken. On Hernyken, there is also a dedicated field station used for research into seabirds.

sarpsborg-vestre-batteri-Q11999599.d: The Sarpsborg Western Battery is situated north of Sarpsborg town centre, east of Lake Tunevannet. The battery was built as early as 1899 to protect the combined railway and road bridge at Sarpefossen. The fortification was initially designed to accommodate four guns, with their lines of fire directed towards Sarpefossen. Two further guns were later added to the right flank, capable of covering the Glomma river down to the ferry crossing at Sandesund. The structure is built of rough-hewn granite with a low parapet at the front. Behind the emplacement is an open battery area. Niches for ammunition are recessed into the parapet. At the rear of the left flank is the orientation table with several sight lines. The orientation table was normally the battery commander’s combat position.

skipshelleren-Q12000997.d: Skipshelleren is a rock shelter at Straume in Vaksdal municipality. The distance from the deepest part of the shelter to the open sky (the drop) is around 15 metres at its greatest. The ceiling height is even more impressive, at a full 30 metres. The name is said to derive from the fact that the cave was used in earlier times as a winter storage place for boats. The cave lies on the south side of the strong tidal current known as Øvre Bolstadstraumen, which connects the Bolstadfjorden and Vikafjorden fjord arms. The first archaeological excavations at Skipshelleren took place in 1930–1931. These excavations were prompted by local people who had submitted finds from the area around Skipshelleren which they believed would be of interest to the university.

sklinna-naturreservat-Q12001095.d: Sklinna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Leka municipality in Trøndelag. The reserve was established in 2003 ‘to preserve a distinctive island and archipelago area at the outer reaches of the Namdal coast, where botanical, zoological and geological features, both on land and at sea, contribute to the area’s unique character. The area is of great natural scientific value. It is of particular value as a breeding habitat for a number of seabird species, including the auks’. The Sklinna archipelago lies approximately 20 west of the island of Leka. Sklinna Lighthouse is situated here, and the fishing settlement had year-round residents until around 1900, after which it continued to be used as a fishing settlement.

skollerud-Q12001159.d: Skollerud is a farm in Ytre Ådal in the former Ådal parish, now part of Ringerike municipality in Buskerud. The farm was originally registered as number 55. When the new Ådal parish was established in 1857, the farm was given farm number 8, but after Ådal parish was incorporated into the new, larger municipality of Ringerike, the farm number became 278. In the land register of 1647, it had a land tax of 45 lispund of grain, and only Semmen had a higher land tax in Ådal at that time, at 68 lispund. Skollerud was divided into two holdings for a long time, but in the 19th century the two holdings were successfully merged again. Skollerud also served as an agricultural college for a time.

slettnes-kapell-Q12001466.d: Slettnes Chapel is a disused chapel in the style of a long church, built in 1956 and situated at Slettnes on Sørøya in Hammerfest municipality, Finnmark county. The chapel is built of wood and has 90 seats. It was decommissioned in 1972, but is now used once every summer.

storheia-Q12003468.d: Storheia is a disused ski jumping facility in Kristiansand. The facility is situated at Glitre in Dalane and consists of three ski jumps measuring K78, K50 and K24. The ski jumping centre was built in 1935 as a joint venture between the workers’ sports clubs Kristiansand Arbeider Idrettslag (which merged with Lund Idretts Forening in 1937 to form AIK Lund) and Fagen 32. AIK Lund was struggling with heavy debt, and in the winter of 1940, Fagen 32 presumably took over full ownership of the ski jump at Storheia. In 1948, Fagen 32 and Oddersjaa organised a national Olympic qualifying competition at Storheia, the largest event held on the hill to date, attracting 12,000 spectators. Ernst Knudsen set a hill record of 67.5 metres.

svenska-kyrkan-i-narvik-Q12004342.d: The Swedish Church in Narvik was consecrated in 1950. It was previously the town’s Swedish Seamen’s Church. The church was designed by the architects Jan Inge Hovig in collaboration with Bo Grefberg. The Swedish Church is now owned by Narvik Municipality and has been designated a listed building. The Swedish Seamen’s Welfare Board began its operations in Narvik in 1947, and the Swedish Seamen’s Church was completed three years later. At that time, due to the ore exports from Kiruna, there were many Swedish seafarers in Narvik. In the 1970s, the proportion of Swedish seafarers began to decline, as the ore ships were reflagged and manned by foreign seafarers. This trend continued over the next two decades.

syretarnet-Q12004606.d: The Acid Tower is a former absorption tower located at Rjukan Business Park in Rjukan, Tinn municipality. The tower now stands outdoors, is 23 metres high and consists of large blocks of Drammen granite with blue asbestos joints and 58 iron tie-rods with tension rods on each of the tower’s flat sides.

ster-bedehuskapell-Q12004690.d: Sæter Prayer House Chapel is a chapel dating from 1969 in Osen municipality, Trøndelag county. The chapel has a capacity of 70. It was consecrated on 5 October 1969 by Bishop Tord Godal.

svareid-kapell-Q12004710.d: Sævareid Chapel is a chapel dating from 1956 in Bjørnafjorden municipality in Vestland county. It was originally built as a burial chapel, but was extended to include a chancel and sacristy in 1961. That same year, the building was consecrated as a chapel. The chapel is situated above the Henanger farm, on the road from Sævareid towards Kilen. The building is timber-framed and seats 100 people. It consists of a nave and a lower chancel flanked by sacristies. The building has no tower, but a simple four-sided turret with a copper roof. The altar, pulpit and baptismal font are made of pine. The chapel has an electric organ. The churchyard beside the chapel was opened in 1956.

slvsberget-Q12004749.d: Sølvsberget is a prominent peak in the otherwise gently undulating terrain between Gran and Tingelstad in Hadeland, in the Innlandet region. Sølvsberget lies approximately two kilometres west of Granavollen and Søsterkirkene in Gran. Its distinctive profile stems from the fact that it is an ancient volcanic vent that once forced its way up through the sedimentary rocks in the area. The summit lies at 493 metres above sea level and is a slightly smaller counterpart to Brandbukampen further north. The plateau at the summit of Sølvsberget covers approximately 15 dekar and is bordered by large embankments of earth and stone to the south and west. The northern and eastern slopes are partly precipitous and difficult to access.

tanamunningen-naturreservat-Q12005148.d: The Tanamunningen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tana Municipality, Finnmark. The nature reserve encompasses a river delta at the mouth of the River Tana and has held Ramsar Site status since 2002, due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1991 to protect a large and distinctive delta area of international importance as a resting and feeding ground for wetland birds. The area comprises Northern Norway’s largest contiguous salt marshes and interesting riverbank vegetation. During every flood, the River Tana transports large quantities of sediment, which is deposited in sandbanks down towards the estuary.

tanemsborgen-Q12005163.d: Tanemsborgen consists of the remains of a rural fortress on Tanemsåsen in Trondheim municipality. Remains of the wall run all the way round the top of Tanemsåsen. Archaeological investigations suggest that the fort was built around 500 BC, towards the end of the Bronze Age or the beginning of the Early Iron Age. There are few definitive answers as to why and by whom the fort was built, but it is assumed that the village fort was constructed as a defence against external attackers. It is thought that there was a palisade on top of the wall encircling the hill. There is considerable uncertainty surrounding both this fort and similar finds of village forts elsewhere in Norway. Within what was once the wall, there is also a small pond.

torvetjnnstua-Q12007177.d: Torvetjønnstua originates from a farm by Møsvatn. It was moved to Lognvik Farm in 1941 and, according to Johan Meyer’s accounts, is one of the finest examples of Telemark’s interior design we have. The cottage was subsequently sold on in 1961 and now stands on the Neset farm near Totak, specifically at Totakstrondi.

ulendeltaet-naturreservat-Q12008275.d: Ulendeltaet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and a Ramsar site in Lierne municipality in Trøndelag. The reserve was established in 1984 ‘to preserve an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area’. Ulendeltaet is situated at the mouth of the Innerdalselva river in Ulen, at an altitude of approximately 350 metres above sea level. It is a plain-like wetland area formed by alluvial deposits from the river, and is partially flooded during high water. Along the river grows a swamp forest of spruce and birch; behind this lies a large belt of willow and extensive marshes, characterised by tuft-forming grey moss. The area was designated a Ramsar site in 2011.

aslandsgrend-Q12011674.d: Åslandsgrend is a hamlet in Fyresdal municipality in Telemark. The hamlet lies high and open above the main valley, at an altitude of 500–550 metres above sea level, facing south. Åslandsgrend has yielded many finds from the Viking Age, including axes, a bronze bowl-scale and a sickle, and there are several burial mounds in the hamlet. Åslandsgrend has many listed buildings on farms and a cultural landscape that is maintained through farming, as well as by grazing sheep and horses. The county plant and the orchid Søstermarihand can be found in several places in Åsland. The area has been designated by the Norwegian Environment Agency as a particularly valuable cultural landscape. The hamlet had its own school from 1863 to 1950, which was also attended by pupils from neighbouring hamlets. The old schoolhouse, dating from 1926, is now used as a community centre.

vretana-kapell-Q12012030.d: Øvretana Chapel is an octagonal church dating from 1956 in Seida, in the municipality of Tana, Finnmark county. The building is made of wood and has a capacity of 150. It was designed by architects Trond Dancke and Inge Fred Dervo. There is a cemetery next to the chapel, which is situated right next to County Road 890.

kong-ysteins-havn-Q12322582.d: King Øystein’s harbour at Agdenes lies at the far end of Trondheimsfjorden. The complex was built in the early 12th century for military purposes. It is mentioned in the Saga of Håkon Håkonsson and in Snorri’s sagas of the kings. The Saga of the Sons of Magnus states that King Øystein (c. 1088–1123) had a ‘harbour built where there had previously been none’. The site was opened to the public in the summer of 2001.

anfinnsbrue-Q12713432.d: Anfinnsbrue, Anfinnsbrua or Arnfinnsbrua is situated at Dovregubbens Hall near Vålåsjø in Dovrefjell. The bridge was built around 1820 across the isthmus between Vålåsjøen and Avsjøen – known as the Anfinns-osen – and forms part of the old Trondheim Road. The bridge is a stone arch bridge, and Paul Paulsson Tofte, the farmer at Tofte in Dovre, was responsible for its construction. Paul Paulsson was also responsible for the construction of the stone arch bridge over the River Jora between Lesja and Dovre, and over the River Ula in Sel. Both of these bridges were blown up during the last war. The prefix ‘Anfinn’ in the name of the bridge and the river bend derives from the fact that, in the 18th century, a person of that name attempted to settle in this area.

ramsy-fort-Q136383998.d: Ramsøy Fort was a military battery established by German invasion forces in 1942 on the island of Ramsøy in Askøy municipality. It was Ramsøy’s strategic location on the Hjeltefjord and its control over the approach to Bergen from the north that led to the battery being situated on the island. From the outset, it was equipped with four 10.5 cm field artillery guns, which were originally French and had been captured as spoils of war. In June 1943, these were replaced with 8.8 cm anti-aircraft guns (flugabwehrkanone). The wartime battery was decommissioned and dismantled after the war, but bunkers remain in the terrain in several places.

ordfrarsteinen-Q14325915.d: Ordførarsteinen is a Sámi sacrificial site situated between Stormyra and Lapphaugvatnet, south-east of Fossbakken, in the municipality of Lavangen in Troms. The site is a listed cultural monument dating from the Sámi Iron Age. It consists of a boulder approximately five metres high, with smaller stones in front of it, which together form a plateau. There are also other Sámi sacrificial stones near Ordførarsteinen. The stone was given its current name in the 1930s, after the then mayor, Brattberg Aa, was on an inspection visit in connection with the construction of a road in the area, when the local population served the mayor, his guests and the workers by the stone.

heggelia-kapell-Q14326123.d: Heggelia Chapel is a long church dating from 1961 in Målselv municipality, Troms county. The building is made of wood and has 150 seats. Beneath the church hall is a basement used for social events, not least in connection with the soldiers at Bardufoss and in Heggelia’s need for Christian fellowship. The chapel was designed by the Norwegian Armed Forces’ district architect for Nord-Hålogaland, J. Bjørhovde and O. Flakstad.

carl-knudsen-garden-Q14565776.d: The Carl Knudsen Farm is a historic estate in Lillesand. It is situated at Nygårdsgade 1 and consists of a main house with several outbuildings. The buildings are listed and currently house the Lillesand Town and Maritime Museum. The main house was built in the late Empire style, influenced by English architecture, in 1826, with a half-hipped roof and English sash windows. It has recently been restored to its original colour, which clearly shows the strong influence of English brick architecture. The outbuildings were constructed in stages, but no clear chronology has yet been established. Shipowner and timber merchant Johannes Grøgaard was the original builder of the house. He ran a general store on the ground floor of the main house.

villa-busk-Q17195193.d: Villa Busk is a private residence in Bamble municipality in Telemark, designed by architect Sverre Fehn and built in 1989 for record company director Terje Welle Busk. As early as 1993, the house, its furnishings and the surrounding grounds were listed by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage due to their distinctive design and the interplay between the building and the natural environment. The aim is to preserve this as an example of architecture of particularly high quality from this period. The house is the most recent property to be listed in Norway. It comprises a 40-metre-long main wing with a slate-roofed corridor running the length of the building, and a tower containing two bedrooms, a living room, a utility room and a bathroom. The tower and the main wing are connected by an internal bridge that runs transversely across the main wing.

femundshytta-Q17770832.d: Femundshytta was a smelting works on Lake Femunden in Engerdal municipality, Hedmark, which operated from 1743 to 1822. The Røros copper works were surrounded by sparse pine forest, and once this had been cleared, it became cheaper to transport the copper ore 5.5 mil from the Storwartz mine to Femundshytta than to transport enormous quantities of coal in the opposite direction. The ore was hauled by horse or ox across frozen watercourses, or on barges when Lake Femunden was navigable. During the period when the smelter was in operation, 11 farms were affiliated with it, and over 60 people lived and worked there. There was also a travelling school here. The farms practised livestock farming in addition to the men’s work at the smelter.

grunnfjorden-naturreservat-Q17778664.d: Grunnfjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Øksnes municipality in Nordland. The reserve was established to ‘preserve an important wetland area with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife. It is particularly important to safeguard the wetland area’s vital importance for wetland birds throughout the year, as well as to preserve a botanically valuable salt marsh area.’ The area comprises Grunnfjorden, a marshland area on Langøya and part of Gisløya. The area covers 17,724 dekar, of which 7,500 dekar is land, 500 dekar is freshwater and 6,700 dekar is marine area.

hamnsundhelleren-Q17782021.d: Hamnsund Cave is a cave situated in Hamnsund in Haram municipality. The cave lies 60 metres above sea level and was formed as a fire pit. Remains of animals and birds from the Stone Age have been found in the cave.

strmmen-gamle-bru-Q18522021.d: The old Strømmen Bridge is a truss bridge in Båtsfjord, built in 1929. It is situated approximately 15 metres west of the current Strømmen Bridge on Fiskeværvegen and is now reserved for pedestrians and cyclists. The bridge was built as part of the road network in Båtsfjord in the late 1920s, at a time when many Norwegian bridges were being constructed using steel truss structures. It has a span of approximately 25 metres and a width of 2.4 metres. The old Strømmen Bridge was listed by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage on 17 April 2008, as part of a nationwide listing of bridges owned by the Norwegian Public Roads Administration. Båtsfjord Municipality has subsequently launched projects to document and preserve the bridge as a cultural heritage site.

bjelland-bru-Q18647813.d: Bjelland Bridge is a concrete arch bridge at Bjelland in Lindesnes municipality in Agder. It spans the Mandalselva river along County Road 462, and has replaced the Old Bjelland Bridge, built in 1864, since 1961. The Director-General of Cultural Heritage listed the bridge on 17 April 2008, together with the Old Bjelland Bridge.

havmyran-naturreservat-Q19323575.d: Havmyran Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hitra municipality, Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated in an area of heathland, marsh and bog in the south-western inland part of the island of Hitra, and has had Ramsar site status since 2002 due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1982 to preserve a large, representative and unspoilt landscape of bogs and heathland with oceanic vegetation, and an important wetland area with a rich and interesting birdlife. 12 km² of the reserve consists of bog – mainly nutrient-poor rainwater bog – 3 km² consists of ponds and other freshwater bodies, whilst the remainder is solid ground. The terrain is relatively flat and lies between 60 and 80 metres above sea level. The bedrock consists of diorite, a deep-seated rock that weathers slowly.

skogvoll-naturreservat-Q19368928.d: Skogvoll Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Andøy municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve is situated at Skogvoll on the north side of Andøya, both along the coast and in a marshland area within Skogvollvatnet, and has had Ramsar site status since 2002, due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1983 to preserve a large and important wetland area with its associated flora and fauna, particularly in view of the protected marshlands and the rich birdlife. The area covers approximately 55 km², of which around 30 km² is water. It contains several different types of bog and plant species, and exhibits great morphological and vegetational diversity.

tufsingdeltaet-naturreservat-Q19368950.d: The Tufsingdeltaet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the Tufsingdalen valley in Os municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 1981 to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the distinctive landscape features, vegetation, the particularly rich and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. The nature reserve lies on both sides of the lower reaches of the River Tufsinga and around its outlet into Lake Femunden, at an altitude of approximately 660 metres above sea level, and has Ramsar site status due to its importance for migratory birds. The river meanders near its mouth, and at the river’s estuary there is a distinctive bird’s-foot delta with many islands, covered in willow thickets.

hynna-naturreservat-Q19368951.d: Hynna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gausdal municipality in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve is situated between Hornsjøen and Ropptjern in the Gausdal Vestfjell mountains, and has held Ramsar Site status since 2002 due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1990 to preserve a large and varied wetland area and a bog. The area comprises a large and varied wetland landscape featuring bogs, marshes, lakes, ponds, streams, rivers and wooded glades. It is an important breeding ground for wetland birds. There are many birds and many bird species in the area, and vulnerable bird species have also been recorded.

malselvutlpet-naturreservat-Q19368983.d: The Målselv Estuary Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site at the mouth of the River Målselva in the municipalities of Målselv and Lenvik in Troms. The reserve was established in 1995 ‘to preserve a river estuary with constantly changing islets and sandbanks, salt marshes and floodplain woodland adapted to this natural environment, and the rich birdlife, with particular emphasis on the large concentration of dabbling ducks during the migration seasons’. Most of the area lies in Målselv, whilst a few small areas to the north are in Lenvik. The estuary where the river flows into Målselvfjorden is a large delta dominated by sand, with deciduous woodland and wooded islets. The salt marshes have distinctive vegetation, and there are floodplain forests of grey alder and birch.

horta-naturreservat-Q19368985.d: Horta Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the Horta archipelago in Leka municipality, Trøndelag. The area was established in 2003, together with the Horta Wildlife Sanctuary. In 2013, the two protected areas were designated as a Ramsar site. The nature reserve comprises three areas totalling 5.5 km², including on and around Fuholmen. The 24 km² wildlife sanctuary acts as a supplementary buffer zone around and between the three sites. Horta is an important breeding ground for the lesser black-backed gull, the shag, the great cormorant, the black guillemot and the red-throated loon.

jren-vatmarksystem-Q19376643.d: The Jæren wetland system is a Ramsar site spanning six coastal municipalities in Jæren, Rogaland, comprising a total of 22 separate protected areas: nature reserves, landscape conservation areas and biotope protection areas. The area includes, amongst other things, sea beaches with sand dunes and shallow lakes. Since 1985, the areas have shared the status of a Ramsar site due to their importance for migratory birds. The number of sub-areas was expanded in 2002. The Jærstrendene Landscape Conservation Area, a conglomerate of protected areas established in 2003, comprises several types of protected areas, including eight bird sanctuaries. Six of these eight form part of the Jæren wetland system, and the remaining two – Raunen and Håstein-Kjør – are also being considered for upgrade to Ramsar status.

kalkovnen-pa-brnnya-Q19376794.d: The lime kiln on Brønnøya is a listed lime kiln in Sandbukta on Brønnøya in Asker municipality. It is approximately nine metres high and has a base area of 6.5 by 6.5 metres. The kiln was probably built when Anders Haagensen started a lime-burning business on the island in 1847. It remained in operation until 1888. During 2012 and 2013, large sections of the lime kiln collapsed. The Directorate for Cultural Heritage, Asker municipality and Akershus county council have collectively pledged or allocated more than half a million kroner to safeguard the cultural monument, which stands on private land. Restoration work is due to begin in May 2014 and is estimated to cost over 4 million kroner.

lahaugmoen-leir-Q19378736.d: Lahaugmoen Camp was a Norwegian military camp at Gjelleråsen in Skedsmo. The Army Medical Corps trained personnel at Lahaugmoen until the camp was closed down in 2002. The area has since been developed into a business park. Several of the military buildings have been listed and restored for use.

leir-bru-Q19379165.d: Leir Bridge is an arch bridge at Vie in Grong, built in 1905. It is visible from County Road 760 and is currently in use as a footbridge. County Road 760 now crosses the Leirelva via a concrete culvert, approximately 15 metres south-east of the bridge. The bridge is constructed of reinforced concrete. The bridge was listed by the Directorate for Cultural Heritage on 17 April 2008.

st-olavs-gate-27-Q19390148.d: St. Olavs gate 27 is a block of flats in Oslo built in 1846. The building was previously a guesthouse, and Rikard Nordraak, who composed the melody for ‘Ja, vi elsker’, lived in this house for a time.

valstads-samlinger-Q19394222.d: The Valstad collections form part of the Asker Museum and are located in Kunstnerdalen in Asker. The farmstead/residence was donated by the artist couple Tilla (1871–1957) and Otto Valstad (1862–1950) in 1949, and is known as an artists’ home for the Valstads and their friends and fellow artists in the so-called Asker Circle. Øvre Valstad Farm has a history dating back to the 1850s, when the farm was acquired and developed by Otto Valstad’s father. Tilla and Otto Valstad married in 1893, moved to Asker in 1899 and took over the farm in 1902.

sterhus-bru-Q19399367.d: Østerhus Bridge is a beam bridge that crosses the Logna river at Kyrkjebygda in Åseral, Vest-Agder. The bridge was built in 1953 and is now used as a footpath and cycle path alongside Kaddeberg Bridge on County Road 455. It is situated around 15 metres to the west of the latter and is formally part of the county road. The Director-General for Cultural Heritage listed the bridge on 17 April 2008.

randya-fort-Q2130835.d: Randøya Fort (German: Marine Artillerie Batterie 1./502 Randöen) is a disused coastal artillery fort situated on Østre Randøya, approximately 13 km south-east of Kristiansand, just inside the range of Grønningen Lighthouse. The fort was built by the Germans during the occupation of Norway and taken over by the Norwegian Armed Forces after the war. It was decommissioned in the late 1990s. The island is also a recreational area, featuring, amongst other things, a family-friendly bathing beach on the west side of the island. The fort area is quite large, and there are excellent opportunities for walking and exploring old military installations.

mab-3-511-bjarkoy-Q21707788.d: Naval Coastal Battery 3./511 Bjarkøy (MKB 3./511) (German: Marine Artillerie Batterie 3./511 Bjarköy) was a German coastal fort in Harstad municipality in Troms, on the island of Bjarkøya north of Harstad. The fortification consisted of four gun emplacements with 15.5 cm guns, with a range of 18,000 m. The fort was constructed in 1941 and became operational the same year. In September 1944, the battery was transferred to a Naval Coastal Battery. In addition to the gun emplacements, the fort was equipped with bunkers, barracks and trenches. The fort was proposed for listing by the Director-General of Cultural Heritage in 2015.

sr-odal-prestegard-Q26924663.d: Sør-Odal Vicarage, or Strøm Vicarage, is situated just west of Strøm Church. Both the church and the vicarage have roots dating back to the Middle Ages. The buildings on the vicarage grounds are of varying ages. The main building, dating from 1818, is a two-storey log-built house with vertical panelling on the exterior. It is in the Empire style. The tenant’s cottage is thought to date from slightly before the mid-1800s, and the storehouse dates from 1791. The brewery dates from the 1920s, and a farm building was erected in 1924. There is also a carriage house and a smithy. The farm is currently operated as a tenant farm. The vicarage is considered to be of high ecclesiastical cultural value. A number of the buildings are listed.

tollboden-Q28837165.d: The customs house in Larvik, also known as Den Gamle Tollbod, was built in 1714 by the merchant and master mason Johan Andreas Blume. The building burnt down in 1728. It is not known for certain how much of the masonry structure was destroyed in the fire. The building was rebuilt in 1730 and extended by two bays. It was listed by the Director-General of Cultural Heritage in 1922. The Director-General described the building as one of Norway’s best-preserved masonry structures from the first half of the 18th century. The building’s architecture is unique in Norway. Apparently, one has to go to Helsingør in Denmark and visit the customs house there to find anything similar. After the church, it is Larvik’s second-oldest stone building. In 1952, the building underwent extensive restoration.

helgesteinen-Q29032649.d: ‘Helgesteinen’ is an ancient sacred site on the Brekke farm in Ørsta. It is a fairly large, round stone situated by the old road that once ran through Brekke. In Norway, there are many legends and traditions from early Christian times concerning religious gathering places out in the countryside, and we have evidence of this in names such as ‘Kirkesteinen’, ‘Kirkehelleren’ and similar. In Ørsta, Helgesteinen is such a place, and it was probably used as a religious meeting place as early as the Catholic era (before 1537). People – it could have been one or more – would gather by the stone, perhaps on Sundays when there was no service in the church, but probably just as often on Friday mornings.

helleristningene-i-herand-Q2907231.d: The rock carvings at Herand consist of around 150 agricultural carvings at Bakke, near the village of Herand in Ullensvang municipality, Hordaland. The rock carving site is thought to be around 3,000 years old, dating from the Late Bronze Age (1100–500 BCE). The motifs range from ships and people to sacrificial pits, rings and fertility symbols. The site is notable for its many erotic motifs. It is situated just off National Road 550 to Utne, 500 metres east of the quay in Herand, in an area known as Kalhagen. On a rocky outcrop known as Mariskarvet, there are 85 figures depicting, amongst other things, boats, people, footprints, water, rings and pits. Interpretations of the motifs suggest themes of the life cycle, religion, abundant harvests, the sun and rituals.

nes-prestegard-Q32622510.d: Nes Vicarage (Gamle Nes Farm, or simply Nes) is the historical and etymological origin of the name of Nes municipality in Akershus. The vicarage is now situated at Disen. Although the farm no longer exists as a separate entity, the name lives on both as the name of the municipality and in a number of public and ecclesiastical contexts within the Romerike municipality.

de-samiske-samlinger-Q3367239.d: The Sámi Collections (Northern Sámi: Sámiid Vuorká-Dávvirat) in Karasjok is the main museum for Sámi art, culture and history. It was established in 1972 and serves as the administrative headquarters for RiddoDuottarMuseat, a consolidated entity comprising four museums. The four museums are the Sámi Collections in Karasjok, Kautokeino Village Museum/Guovdageaidnu gilišillju, Porsanger Museum and Kokelv Sea Sámi Museum. The Sámi Collections house around 5,000 artefacts. In addition to this, there is an art collection comprising around 800 works. There is also an open-air museum here with over a dozen buildings.

sunnylven-prestegard-Q66975082.d: Sunnylven Vicarage in Stranda municipality is situated on the hillside north of Hellesyltfossen, whilst the church stands on the hillside to the south. The neoclassical main building was designed by Ole Landmark and built in 1921. At the rear of this building stands a listed storehouse dating from the 17th or 18th century, which was moved to this site from the former vicarage around 1860.

klostergata-17-Q67186397.d: Klostergata 17 is a residential building situated on Klostergata in Moss. The building is listed under the Planning and Building Act.

vre-forra-naturreservat-Q7116432.d: The Øvre Forra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Meråker, Verdal, Levanger and Stjørdal, in Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated at the point where Lake Feren flows into the River Forra, and has Ramsar status due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1990 to protect a large area of marshland with rich flora and fauna, virtually untouched by human intervention. According to the Norwegian Directorate for Nature Management, the area covers 102,538 dekar, whilst the regulations state that the area is approximately 108 square kilometres.

nyrud-Q75818515.d: Nyrud is a settlement farm, police station and cultural heritage site in the Pasvik Valley in the municipality of Sør-Varanger. The site is situated just over 100 kilometres south of Kirkenes, at the terminus of County Road 8850. The farm was established around 1920, and of the buildings on the property, the main house and one of the two storehouses are original. Since 1993, the farm has been situated within the Pasvik Nature Reserve.

b-yabreen-Q2803023.d: Bøyabreen is a glacier in the Fjærland area of Sogndal Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located inside Jostedalsbreen National Park, and it is a side branch of the large Jostedalsbreen glacier.

kjenndalsbreen-Q3219709.d: Kjenndalsbreen is a glacier in Stryn Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. The 19-square-kilometre (7.3 sq mi) glacier is a side branch of the Jostedalsbreen glacier, and is included in the Jostedalsbreen National Park.

supphellebreen-Q4579193x.d: Supphellebreen is a glacier in the Fjærland area of Sogndal Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) north of the village of Fjærland. It is located inside Jostedalsbreen National Park. It is a side branch of the main Jostedalsbreen glacier. The glacier is split into an upper and a lower part, with a non-glaciated area between. The glacier reaches down to an elevation of 60 metres (200 ft) above sea level, the lowest glacier level in southern Norway. The Bøyabreen glacier lies just northwest of Supphellebreen.

storglaciaren-Q4124356.d: Storglaciären (Swedish for The Great Glacier) is a glacier in Tarfala Valley in the Scandinavian Mountains of Kiruna Municipality, Sweden. The glacier is classified as polythermal having both cold and warm bottom temperatures. It was on Storglaciären that the first glacier mass balance research program began (immediately after World War II), which continues to the present day; this is the longest continuous study of its type in the world. Storglaciären has had a cumulative negative mass balance of -17 m between 1946 and 2006. The program began monitoring the Rabots Glaciär in 1982, Riukojietna in 1985, and Mårmaglaciären in 1988.

jarlshola-Q6160343.d: Jarlshola (English: The Cave of the Jarl) is a small cave in Melhus Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. The cave is near the small Rimul farm, just outside the village of Melhus. It is thought to be the hiding place of Håkon Sigurdsson (also known as Hákon Sigurðsson, Hákon Earl) and Tormod Kark (or Þormóðr Karkr, the slave of the Jarl) on their last night before the infamous murder at Rimul.

setergrotta-Q12000053.d: Setergrotta (or Setergrotten) is a karst cave in Røvassdalen in Rana Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It has a total depth of 50 metres (160 ft) and an explored length of 2.4 kilometres (1.5 mi). It is probably connected to the nearby Grønligrotta. The cave contains large galleries and sediments from the latest ice age and younger. It was created 200,000–300,000 years ago.

gr-nligrotta-Q1551739.d: Grønnligrotta is a marble karst cave in Rana Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the valley of Røvassdalen, and was first explored in 1914. It has a total depth of 107 metres (351 ft) and explored length of 2 kilometres (1.2 mi). It is probably connected to the nearby Setergrotta. The cave is equipped with artificial lights and open for tourists.

korsvika-Q6432678.d: Korsvika is a small residential area in the Lade area in the city of Trondheim in Trøndelag county, Norway. Korsvika is located in the Østbyen borough in Trondheim Municipality. It has several small beaches and the Ladestien trail runs through the area. Korsvika is also the site of "Korsvika barnehage", a local kindergarten.

trollfjorden-Q1029073.d: The Trollfjord or Trollfjorden is a fjord in Hadsel Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. The 2-kilometre (1.2 mi) long fjord cuts into the island of Austvågøya and flows out into the Raftsundet strait. The fjord has a narrow entrance and steep-sided mountains surrounding it. The name is derived from troll, a figure from Norse mythology. The fjord is a popular tourist attraction due to the beauty of its natural setting. It is only accessible by boat or by a nearby 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) hike over very rugged terrain. The Hurtigruten's ships on the route between Bergen and Kirkenes detour into Trollfjorden. It is also popular with other cruise lines.

hvervenbukta-Q14435684.d: Hvervenbukta is a swimming and recreation area southeast of the city center of Oslo, Norway, located at the shores of Bunnefjorden in the borough of Søndre Nordstrand, and not far from Ljan and Holmlia. The area originally belonged to Ljan mansion. The main building here was from 1765, and burned down in 1913. Former Aker municipality took over the properties in 1937. Some of the remaining buildings in the area is now used by artists and artisans. The site has one of Oslo's most popular beaches, with swimming opportunities along the sandy beach and from the rocks along the fjord.

innv-rfjorden-Q3440578.d: Innværfjorden is a small fjord in Bømlo Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It lies on the south of the village of Rubbestadneset on the eastern side of the island of Bømlo. The 3.5-kilometre-long (2.2 mi) fjord flows to the west from the Stokksund strait. The Innværfjorden stretches west from the island of Osparøya between Justenakken and Rubbestadneset and then heads a little southwest. The outermost part of the fjord is about as long as it is wide, and on the south side lies Klenesvågen and Ekornsætre. Along the west side of the fjord lies the small village of Innvær, after which the fjord is named.

stegastein-Q628686.d: Stegastein is a scenic overlook on Sogn og Fjordane County Road 243 in Norway. The 30-metre (98 ft) long and 4-metre (13 ft) wide platform of steel and laminated pine overlooks Aurlandsvangen and the Aurlandsfjord. This project is part of a national program of tourist routes commissioned by the Norwegian Highway Department.

vuosaarenhuippu-Q5407039.d: Vuosaarenhuippu is a recreational area in the northern part of Vuosaari in eastern Helsinki, Finland. Earlier it was the Vuosaari dumping ground and a place where land masses from construction sites were deposited. Through ecological restoration the area has been turned into a natural-like environment, the scale of which is unprecedented in the history of Helsinki. A large number of both flora and fauna inhabit the area. There are paths connecting the area to the nearby Mustavuori protected area.

trolltunga-Q1512593.d: Trolltunga (lit. 'the troll tongue') is a rock formation situated at an elevaton of 1,126 metres (3,694 ft) above sea level in Ullensvang Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. The cliff juts horizontally out from the mountain, about 700 metres (2,300 ft) above the north side of the lake Ringedalsvatnet. Popularity of the hike to Trolltunga and rock formation itself has exploded in recent years. The increased popularity has turned Trolltunga into a national icon and a major tourist attraction for the region. Until 2010, fewer than 800 people hiked to Trolltunga each year.

preikestolen-Q746223.d: Preikestolen or Prekestolen (English: 'Pulpit Rock' or 'Pulpit') is a tourist attraction in Strand Municipality in Rogaland county, Norway. Preikestolen is a steep cliff which rises 604 metres (1,982 ft) above Lysefjorden. Atop the cliff, there is an almost flat top of approximately 25 by 25 metres (82 ft × 82 ft). Preikestolen is located near the western part of the fjord, and on its north side. Tourism at the site has been increasing in the early 21st century, with 300,000 visitors in 2024, making it one of the most-visited natural tourist attractions in Norway. BASE jumpers often leap from the cliff. Due to its increased popularity, the most used path to the site (a 3.8-kilometre (2.

engabreen-Q1769599.d: Engabreen is a glacier arm of Vestre Svartisen in Meløy municipality in Nordland. Engabreen has varied in size and previously covered Lake Engabrevatnet, which became ice-free in the mid-20th century. In the 1720s, Engabreen expanded and destroyed the Storsteinsøyra farm in the process. Between 1999 and 2024, the glacier arm has retreated by 800 metres.

odinsbreen-Q11214452.d: Odinsbreen is a glacial cascade on the Jostedalsbreen glacier and is one of three glacial cascades leading down to the Austerdalsbreen glacier. Odinsbreen is situated near Veitastrond in Luster municipality, Vestland county. Odinsbreen has a height difference of approximately 900 metres.

torsbreen-Q11214554.d: Torsbreen is a glacier tongue on the Jostedalsbreen glacier and is one of three glacier tongues leading down towards the Austerdalsbreen glacier. Torsbreen is situated near Veitastrond in Luster municipality, Vestland county. Torsbreen has a height difference of approximately 900 metres and is so steep that ice avalanches occur frequently.

skalebreen-Q11213663.d: Skålebreen is a glacier in Stryn municipality in Vestland. The glacier lies between Bødalen and Erdalen, east of Lovatnet. Skålebreen is connected to Tindefjellsbreen to the north-west.

h-galmebreen-Q11242857.d: Høgalmebreen is a glacier arm of Myklebustbreen on the border between the municipalities of Sunnfjord and Stryn in Vestland. The highest point on the glacier is 1,712 metres above sea level, and this peak is the 701st highest in the country among mountains with a primary factor of at least 50 metres.

bohrsbreen-Q11241444.d: The Bohr Glacier is a glacier tongue of the Jostedal Glacier in Stryn municipality in Vestland. It is situated on the western side of the glacier, just west of Lodalskåpa.

bjorlings-glaciar-Q3373289.d: The Björling Glacier is a glacier (Swedish: glaciär) in the Kebnekaise massif in Kiruna municipality, situated on the slopes of Kebnetjåkka below Kebnekaise’s southern peak. Its tongue extends down towards Kitteldalen. Björling Glacier is named after Johan Alfred Björling, who climbed the southern peak via what is now known as the Västra route. The glacier has a slowly decreasing area of 1.47 km², a maximum depth of 225 m, an average depth of 94 m and a volume of 139 km³.

st-lsnosbreen-Q20553124.d: The Stølsnos Glacier is a glacier near Stølsnostindane in Jotunheimen, in Årdal municipality in Vestland. It lies 15 km south-east of the Hurrungane mountain range on the eastern side of the Utla Valley. The glacier covers an area of 1.35 km² and is 1.7 km long. Its highest point is 1,930 metres above sea level and its lowest point is 1,480 metres above sea level.

koldedalsbreen-Q11234939.d: The Koldedalsbreen is a glacier in Årdal municipality in Vestland, just west of Lake Tyin, between Koldedalstinden to the north and Breikvamsnosi to the south. As a result of melting, the glacier is now divided into several sections, and between these lies an unnamed mountain peak 1,822 metres above sea level. It has been proposed to name the peak simply ‘1822’.

rabots-glaciar-Q7713109.d: The Rabot Glacier is a large glacier (Swedish: glaciär) on a valley slope on the north-western side of the Kebnekaise mountain range in Lapland, Sweden. It was first scientifically described by Valter Schytt in 1947 and 1959, and later by K.A. Brugger (1992). Stroeven and van de Val (1990). The earliest record of the glacier dates from 1883, when the French geographer Charles Rabot photographed part of it whilst climbing Kebnekaise for the first time. In 1910, it was visited by Enquist, who carried out detailed photographic documentation of the entire glacier.

slingsbybreen-Q11213659.d: Slingsbybreen is a glacier in Årdal municipality in Vestland county. Slingsbybreen lies to the east and south-east of Store Skagastølstind. The glacier is named after William Cecil Slingsby, who crossed it during the first ascent of Storen in 1876. Today, the route across Slingsbybreen is less frequently used, partly because the glacier has receded significantly and is more difficult to cross.

midtmaradalsbreen-Q11213411.d: The Midtmaradalsbreen is a glacier in Årdal municipality in Vestland county. The glacier is situated at the head of the Midtmaradalen valley, between Midtmaradalstindane and Storen, in the Hurrungane mountain range in the western part of Jotunheimen. The river Midtmaradøla flows from the Midtmaradalsbreen glacier.

gjertvassbreen-Q11214373.d: The Gjertvass Glacier (also spelled Jervvass Glacier) is a glacier in the eastern part of Hurrungane in Jotunheimen. It lies north of Styggedalstindane and Gjertvasstind, in the municipality of Luster. The glacier drains into the Gjertvassdalen and Utladalen valleys. The River Utla flows into the Årdal. The book *Skifører for Hurrungane* describes four different routes to Gjertvasstind, and all of them mention the Gjertvassbreen.

maradalsbreen-Q11213278.d: The Maradalsbreen is a glacier in Luster municipality in Vestland county. The glacier is situated at the head of the Maradalen valley, south of the Styggedalstindane mountains, in the Hurrungane mountain range in the western part of Jotunheimen. The river Maradøla flows from the Maradalsbreen glacier.

eldalsbreen-Q11237042.d: Eldedalsbreen is a glacier in Luster municipality in Vestland, situated just above the village of Veitastrond. It lies just east of the Svardalsbreen glacier and between Svardalen to the north and Eldedalen to the south. The summit, which is no longer covered by permanent ice, lies 1,673 metres above sea level.

trollkyrkja-Q12007498.d: Trollkyrkja, or Trollkirka, in Hustadvika municipality consists of three limestone caves with underground streams and waterfalls. There used to be four caves, but one has collapsed. It is easy to explore the caves. A river with waterfalls flows through the cave system, and in some places daylight streams in. The Molde and Romsdal Tourist Association made Trollkyrkja well-known, secured it and made it accessible in 1890. The association was responsible for its upkeep until the then municipality of Fræna took over responsibility in the late 1980s.

bolgb-rra-Q11961811.d: Bolgbørra is a hole right through the mountain on the island of Bolga in Meløy municipality in Nordland, about 80 metres above sea level. Bolgbørra was formed by the sea and ice during the last ice age, around 9–10,000 years ago. At that time, the shoreline was level with Bolgbørra.

neskilen-Q11991173.d: Neskilen is a bay and a locality in Eydehavn, in Arendal municipality. Neskilen is situated on the mainland side of Tromøysund, at the mouth of the protected Moland watercourse, over which the Neskil Bridge on County Road 410 spans. From Neskilen, small vessels can follow the Rånene river through channelled river courses up to Rånehølen, Langangsvannet and Sagene in Austre Moland. At Sagene, there were up to six sawmills. Before the industrial town of Eydehavn was established in the early 1900s, Neskilen was a bustling place. There was extensive construction of sailing ships here, and timber was shipped out from Sagene.

maren-Q3378044.d: Maren is a lake in central Södertälje, in the east of Södermanland, Sweden. The lake is now connected to the Baltic Sea section of the Södertälje Canal, which means that the water in the lake is now brackish. Maren lies between Slussholmen and Strandgatan, and Marenplan is situated on one of the lake’s shores.

grannesvagen-Q11972467.d: Grannesvågen is a cove on the eastern side of Hafrsfjord in Sola municipality, Rogaland. Sola municipality has developed parks and walking areas around Søresvågen. Ytraberget lies to the south of Grannesvågen. The Våganes Football Club’s facilities are situated at Grannesvågen, comprising several gravel and artificial turf pitches, as well as a grass pitch. Grannesvågen is also home to the Våganes Boat Club, which has a small-boat harbour here. Elsewhere in the area, there are several building plots and some land used for seaweed farming.

nordhasselvika-Q11991793.d: The Nordhasselvika Bird Sanctuary is a protected habitat in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The area was designated a sanctuary in 1987 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitats in the area. Nordhasselvika is regarded as a beautiful natural and cultural landscape. The bay is so shallow that the 6-metre isobath lies 700 metres from the shore. The area features both a pebble beach and sandy beaches. It is the most important migration site for waders on Lista, particularly in Sævika and at Litle-Rauna, and is also of great importance as a wintering area.

s-mmevagen-Q118119391.d: Sømmevågen is a bay in Sola municipality and forms the southernmost part of Hafrsfjord. The bay is home to the seaplane harbour at Stavanger Airport, Sola. National Road 509 runs past and forms the boundary between Sømmevågen and Sola Airport’s north-south runway.

trosbyfjorden-Q11072908.d: Trosbyfjorden is a fjord in the very south of Bamble municipality in Telemark. It stretches just over 2 km from the mouth between Kjønnøya and Rødlandet on the mainland, all the way to Trosby. According to an old legend, the area around Trosby is said to have been inhabited by a group of immigrants who originated from the Black Sea region. They are said to have arrived in 500–600 AD in their own flat-bottomed barges with high bows and square sails. A common misconception in Bamble is that Trosby means ‘the farmstead’ of the ‘believers’. However, recent research suggests that the name refers to a religious sacrificial custom practised by the immigrant people. This custom is no longer in use, either at Trosby or elsewhere in Bamble.

geitfjellet-Q20019128.d: Geitfjellet is a mountain in Bymarka, Trondheim. It rises to a height of 416 metres above sea level. The mountain lies in the north-east of Bymarka and was designated a protected area, together with the surrounding coniferous forest (a total of 2,600 daa), by a municipal resolution in 1965. The name probably derives from the fact that, when viewed from Trondheimsfjorden, the mountain’s shape resembles that of a goat. The conservation of Geitfjellet in 1965/1966 came about as a result of pressure against potential development and technical interventions in the latter half of the 1950s, stemming both from several proposals for a cable car to the mountain, and fears of military interest in Geitfjellet, similar to that shown in Gråkallen. Just west of Geitfjellet, between the mountain and Driftsvegen, lies the Dreyers minne cabin, which was built in 1936.

kongens-utsikt-Q19377887.d: Kongens utsikt is a scenic spot in Hole municipality in Ringerike. It is situated west of Kleivstua on a mountain plateau approximately 400 metres above Tyrifjorden/Steinsfjorden. The site is known for its views over large parts of Hole and Ringerike. It is named after King Karl Johan, who visited the site in 1832. The viewing platform here was originally built of wood a few years later, but was demolished and rebuilt in stone – complete with railings and benches – in 1880.

nordre-stange-varde-Q11257316.d: Nordre Stange varde is a hill on the border between Indre Østfold and Marker municipalities in Østfold. It rises to 291 metres above sea level and is the highest point in the former municipality of Eidsberg. At the summit there is a viewing tower, and there are blue-marked trails from Ørje, Rakkestad and Mysen. 1.5 kilometres further south lies Søndre Stange Varde, which rises to 277 metres above sea level. Both Stange varde sites feature burial mounds, probably dating from the Bronze Age. Such mounds are often found on old boundary lines and, as in this case, far into the forest.
