Løvstakken and the forests nearby are popular hiking areas among the locals since it is essentially located in the central area of Norway's second largest city. Gullsteinen, a large hill located south of the summit of Løvstakken, is also part of the mountain massif and borders the protected forest area of Langeskogen.

rundemanen-natb9c47f87.d: Rundemanen is a mountain in Bergen Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is considered one of the Seven Mountains which surround the city centre of Bergen, its elevation of 568 metres (1,864 ft) makes it the second highest of them all. The mountain is a part of the same massif as the neighboring mountains of Fløyen, Blåmanen, and Ulriken, but is not easily visible from the city centre of Bergen since it sits behind Fløyen. Still, Rundemanen's low-difficulty trails that offer scenic views of neighboring mountains and islands west of Bergen make them popular footpaths, only taking about 3-4 hours to traverse from Bergen's city center.

veslesmeden-nata97bca43.d: Veslesmeden is a mountain in Dovre Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,015-metre (6,611 ft) tall mountain is located in the Rondane mountains and inside the Rondane National Park, about 18 kilometres (11 mi) northeast of the town of Otta and about 37 kilometres (23 mi) southeast of the village of Dombås. The mountain is surrounded by several other notable mountains including Digerronden and Høgronden to the northeast, Rondeslottet to the east, Storsmeden to the south, Sagtindan and Trolltinden to the west; Gråhøe and Vassberget to the northwest; and Stygghøin to the north. The mountain is easily hiked from the cabin Rondvassbu (DNT).

storstyggesvanatinden-nat826bc404.d: Storstyggesvånåtinden or Storsvånåtinden is a mountain in Lesja Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,212-metre (7,257 ft) tall mountain lies within Dovrefjell-Sunndalsfjella National Park, about 20 kilometres (12 mi) north of the village of Dombås in the Svånåtindan mountains. The mountain is surrounded by several other mountains including Nørdre Svånåtinden which is about 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) to the north, Snøhetta which is about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) to the northeast, Skredahøin which is 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) to the south, and Mjogsjøhøe and Mjogsjøoksli which are about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) to the southwest.

veslfjellet-natd018c8f8.d: Veslfjellet is a mountain in Vågå Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 1,743-metre (5,719 ft) tall mountain is located in the Jotunheimen mountains within Jotunheimen National Park. The mountain sits about 44 kilometres (27 mi) southwest of the village of Vågåmo and about 30 kilometres (19 mi) northwest of the village of Beitostølen. The mountain is surrounded by several other notable mountains including Kollhøin and Besshøe to the northwest, Besseggen and Gloptinden to the west, Bukkehåmåren to the southwest, and Heimdalshøe to the southeast. The lake Bessvatnet lies just north of the mountain.

skarasalen-natead4dfeb.d: Skårasalen is a mountain in Ørsta Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The 1,542-metre (5,059 ft) tall mountain has the seventh largest prominence (1,383 metres or 4,537 feet) of all mountains in Norway. The mountain is located about 5 kilometres (3 mi) south of the village of Sæbø and the Bondalen valley in the Hjørundfjorden area of the municipality. The nearby mountain, Jakta, lies directly to the east on the opposite side of the fjord. Skårasalen lies within the Sunnmørsalpene mountain range along the southern shores of the Hjørundfjorden. Access is easiest from the Kvistad valley on the western side.

storen-natf89eeadf.d: Storen or Store Skagastølstinden is the third highest peak in Norway. It is situated on the border between Luster Municipality and Årdal Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. The 2,405-metre (7,890 ft) mountain is part of the Hurrungane range. The mountains Vetle Skagastølstindane and Midtre Skagastølstindane lie immediately to the north of this mountain and the mountains Sentraltind and Gjertvasstind lie immediately to the east of this mountain. The summit is a popular destination for mountaineers, but it is fairly difficult to climb. The first ascent of Storen was made by William Cecil Slingsby on 21 July 1876.

storebj-rn-natc0e7dd3d.d: Storebjørn (lit. 'Big Bear') is a mountain in Lom Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,222-metre (7,290 ft) tall mountain is located in the Jotunheimen mountains within Jotunheimen National Park. The mountain sits about 40 kilometres (25 mi) southwest of the village of Fossbergom and about 33 kilometres (21 mi) northeast of the village of Øvre Årdal. The mountain lies in the Smørstabbtindene mountains and it is surrounded by several other notable mountains including Rundhøe to the northeast; Stetinden and Stehøe to the east; Gravdalstinden to the south; Kalven to the northwest; and Veslebjørn, Sokse, Kniven, and Store Smørstabbtinden to the north.

kleneggen-nat3ed66f7b.d: Kleneggen or Høgbøra is a mountain in Molde Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county. The 1,964.7 metres (6,446 ft) tall mountain is the highest point in Molde Municipality (it was part of Nesset Municipality prior to 2020). The mountain peak is located in the alpine mountain area between the Eikesdalen valley in Molde Municipality and the village of Verma in the Romsdalen valley (in Rauma Municipality). From the top, there are views along Eikesdalsvatnet lake.

trolltinden-nat35df35df.d: Trolltinden (a.k.a.: Sagtinden) is a mountain in Dovre Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,018-metre (6,621 ft) tall mountain is located in the Rondane mountains and inside the Rondane National Park, about 18 kilometres (11 mi) northeast of the town of Otta and about 35 kilometres (22 mi) southeast of the village of Dombås. The mountain located in a group of mountains called Smiubelgen. The mountain is surrounded by several other notable mountains including Veslesmeden and Storsmeden to the southeast; Ljosåbelgen and Bråkdalsbelgen to the south; Sagtindan and Indre Bråkdalshøe to the west, and Gråhøe and Vassberget to the northwest.

olavtoppen-nat09bc0e82.d: Olavtoppen, occasionally anglicised as Olav Peak, is the highest point of Bouvet Island, a volcanic island and dependency of Norway, and the remotest island on Earth. Olavtoppen is located north of the center of the island, immediately south of Kapp Valdivia, and rises 780 meters (2,560 ft) above sea level. It was first ascended on 21 February 2012 by Aaron Halstead, Bruno Rodi and Jason Rodi Olavtoppen is ranked 36th by topographic isolation.

stors-lnkletten-nat195a1e2b.d: Storsølnkletten is a prominent mountain in Alvdal Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 1,827-metre (5,994 ft) tall mountain lies about 20 kilometres (12 mi) southwest of the village of Alvdal. The mountain is easily recognizable due to its saddle form with two peaks. The higher summit (to the southeast) reaches an elevation of 1,827 metres (5,994 ft) and the lower summit (to the northwest) has an elevation of 1,690 metres (5,540 ft). The lower summit is known as Spisskletten or Storsølnkletten lille.

newtontoppen-natdc72b8e1.d: Newtontoppen (Newton Peak) is the largest and highest mountain in Svalbard, at 1,713 metres (5,620 ft). Its peak is the highest point on Svalbard. It is located at the north east corner on the island of Spitsbergen in the Chydeniusfjella range. The nearest settlement is the formerly Soviet coal mining settlement Pyramiden. The mountain is mostly made of Silurian granite. The mountain was first ascended by Helge Backlund on 4 August 1900.

rondslottet-natd3931db3.d: Rondslottet is the highest mountain in the Rondane mountain range in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,178-metre (7,146 ft) tall mountain sits on the border between Dovre Municipality and Folldal Municipality, just north of the border with Sel Municipality. There is a trail leading to the summit.

bruri-nat1c8bd8d8.d: Bruri is a mountain in Lesja Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,001-metre (6,565 ft) tall mountain lies in the Svånåtindene mountains. It lies about 1.5 kilometres (0.93 mi) northeast of the mountain Storstyggesvånåtinden and about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) south of the mountains Store Langvasstinden and Larstinden. There are two small glaciers on the west side of Bruri.

oksskolten-nat675b35f8.d: Oksskolten (Norwegian; lit. 'Bulls Head') or Uktsiesnjurhtjien åejjie (Southern Sami) is a mountain in Hemnes Municipality in Nordland County, Norway. At 1,916-metre (6,286 ft) tall, it is the highest point in Nordland county, the highest in Northern Norway, and has Norway's eighth largest primary factor. The mountain lies just south of the lake Gresvatnet in the Okstindan mountain range east of the village of Korgen and north of the lake Røssvatnet. The first recorded climb was by Peder Stordal in 1883. In order to get to the summit, climbers must cross the glacier to the north. The large Okstindbreen glacier lies to the west of the mountain.

halti-nat97fcad98.d: Halti (Finnish: Halti, rarely Haltiatunturi, Northern Sami: Háldičohkka, Swedish: Haldefjäll) is a fell at the border between Norway and Finland. The peak (elevation 1,365 m (4,478 ft)) of the fell, called Ráisduottarháldi, is in Norway, on the border Nordreisa Municipality and Gáivuotna Municipality (Kåfjord), about one kilometre (5⁄8 mile) north of the border with Finland. The highest point of the fell on the Finnish side is at 1,324 m (4,344 ft) above sea level, and thus the highest point in the country. The Finnish side of Halti belongs to the municipality of Enontekiö in the province of Lapland.

midtronden-vest-natb169130d.d: Midtronden is a mountain in Dovre Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,060-metre (6,760 ft) tall mountain is located in the Rondane mountains and inside the Rondane National Park, about 25 kilometres (16 mi) northeast of the town of Otta and about 40 kilometres (25 mi) southeast of the village of Dombås. The mountain is surrounded by several other notable mountains including Høgronden to the east; Rondeslottet to the south; Veslesmeden, Storsmeden, Sagtindene, and Trolltinden to the southwest; Gråhøe and Vassberget to the west; and Digerronden and Stygghøin to the northwest. The mountain has two peaks.

digerronden-nat96e097f7.d: Digerronden is a mountain in Dovre Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,015-metre (6,611 ft) tall mountain is located in the Rondane mountains and inside the Rondane National Park. It is one of the ten mountains in the park that are over 2,000 metres (6,600 ft) in elevation. The mountain has a characteristic pyramidal shape and it is located about 24 kilometres (15 mi) northeast of the town of Otta and about 40 kilometres (25 mi) southeast of the village of Dombås.

langlitinden-nat011c3331.d: Langlitinden is the highest mountain on the island of Andørja and is also the highest mountain on any Norwegian island (except Beerenberg, Jan Mayen). It is located on the northeastern part of the island in Ibestad Municipality in Troms county, Norway, just to the south of the Mjøsund Bridge and just northwest of the shore of the Astafjorden. The mountain is 1,276 m (4,186 ft) tall.

moldulh-i-nat3528063b.d: Moldulhøi is a mountain on the border of Skjåk Municipality and Lom Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 2,044-metre (6,706 ft) tall mountain is located in the Breheimen mountains and inside the Breheimen National Park, about 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) south of the village of Bismo. The mountain is surrounded by several other notable mountains including Lomseggje and Lendfjellet to the east, Storhøe to the south, Sandgrovhøi and Hesthøi to the southwest, Hestdalshøgdi to the west, and Tverrfjellet to the northwest.

hesth-i-natf16db523.d: Hesthøi is a mountain on the border of Skjåk Municipality and Lom Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 1,954-metre (6,411 ft) tall mountain is located in the Breheimen mountains and inside the Breheimen National Park, about 12 kilometres (7.5 mi) south of the village of Bismo. The mountain is surrounded by several other notable mountains including Sandgrovhøi and Moldulhøi to the northeast, Storhøe to the southeast, Hestbreapiggan and Steinahøfjellet to the southwest, and Hestdalshøgdi and Tverrfjellet to the northwest.

vinjeronden-nat0a4c99c6.d: Vinjeronden is a mountain in Innlandet county, Norway. It is one of the ten mountains in the Rondane mountain range measuring over 2,000 metres (6,600 ft) in height. The 2,044-metre (6,706 ft) mountain is a tri-point that lies on the border of the three municipalities of Dovre, Folldal, and Sel. The mountain Rondeslottet lies immediately to the north, the mountains Storronden and Rondvasshøgde lie to the southeast, and Svartnuten lies to the southwest. The mountain is easily accessed by hiking from the Rondvassbu tourist cabin (run by the Norwegian Mountain Touring Association), on the way from Rondvassbu to Rondeslottet, which is the highest mountain in Rondane.

weyprechtbreen-nat11ff5d9a.d: Weyprecht Glacier (Norwegian: Weyprechtbreen) is a glacier in Jan Mayen. It is the longest glacier located in the Beerenberg area. The glacier is named after Austro-Hungarian Arctic explorer Karl Weyprecht.

kjerulfbreen-nat363994f3.d: Kjerulf Glacier (Norwegian: Kjerulfbreen) is a glacier in Jan Mayen. It begins at the Hakluyttoppen slope, in the outer crater edge of the Beerenberg. The Kjerulf Glacier and both its neighbors, the Weyprecht Glacier in the west and the Svend-Foyn Glacier in the east, are the most active glaciers in the island. The glacier was named after Norwegian geologist Theodor Kjerulf (1825–88), founder of the Geological Survey of Norway, during the Norwegian North-Atlantic Expedition 1876-1878 led by Henrik Mohn.

renardbreen-nat54aea8ef.d: Renardbreen (The Fox Glacier) is a glacier in Wedel Jarlsberg Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier has a length of about 8 kilometers (5.0 mi). It is located between the ridges of Activekammen and Bohlinryggen, and debouches into Recherche Fjord.

fridtjovbreen-nata098f222.d: Fridtjovbreen is a glacier in Nordenskiöld Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about 14 kilometers, and debouches into the bay Fridtjovhamna at the northern side of Van Mijenfjorden. The name stems from a hunting vessel used during the Torell expedition to Spitsbergen. The lower part of the glacier is included in the Nordenskiöld Land National Park. To the west of Fridtjovbreen is the mountain Ingeborgfjellet, a characteristic ridge and an easily recognizable landmark viewed from sea.

aldegondabreen-nata5a3248b.d: Aldegondabreen is a glacier in Nordenskiöld Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Norway. It is named after Infanta Adelgundes, Duchess of Guimarães. The glacier has a length of about 5.5 kilometers. It flows from Qvigstadfjellet, Christensenfjella and Hermod Petersenfjellet towards Grønfjorden.

vestfonna-nat82e6de63.d: Vestfonna is an ice cap located on the western part Nordaustlandet in the Svalbard archipelago in Norway. The glacier covers an area of about 2,500 km2. It is the third largest ice cap in Svalbard and Norway by area, after Austfonna and Olav V Land.

s-rfonna-natbd3c51d1.d: Sørdomen (The Southern Dome) is an ice dome of Austfonna at Nordaustlandet, Svalbard. The glacier cap of Austfonna has two significant ice domes, Sørdomen and Norddomen further north. The part of Austfonna west of Sørdomen is called Palanderisen.

nordenskioldbreen-nat733a1f63.d: Nordenskiöldbreen (Nordenskiöld Glacier) is a glacier in Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is named after Finnish geologist Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld (1832–1901).

tunabreen-nat64da8903.d: Tunabreen is a glacier stream at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier is about 23 kilometers long, and divides Sabine Land from Bünsow Land. It starts from Lomonosovfonna, flows southwards between the mountains of Langtunafjella and Ultunafjella, merges with Von Postbreen, and the combined glacier debouches into Tempelfjorden.

esmarkbreen-natab1983db.d: Esmarkbreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is named after geologist Jens Esmark. The glacier has a length of 15 kilometers, and debouches into the bay Ymerbukta at the northern side of Isfjorden.

christensenbreen-nat69f40c2d.d: Following is a list of glaciers of Bouvet Island in Antarctica. This list may not reflect recently named glaciers in Bouvet Island.

posadowskybreen-nat815c2f7f.d: Following is a list of glaciers of Bouvet Island in Antarctica. This list may not reflect recently named glaciers in Bouvet Island.

horntvedtbreen-nat3dad0708.d: Following is a list of glaciers of Bouvet Island in Antarctica. This list may not reflect recently named glaciers in Bouvet Island.

linnebreen-nat7ae2d384.d: Linnébreen is a glacier in Nordenskiöld Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Norway. It is named after Swedish botanist Carl Linnaeus. The glacier has a length of about 3.5 kilometers, and flows from the mountain of Systemafjellet towards the valley of Linnédalen. It is proximate to the mountain of Christensenfjella.

hellefonna-natfcf375d9.d: Hellefonna is a glaciated area in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is located between Kjellströmdalen and Sassendalen, and comprises several smaller glaciers, including Jinnbreen, Innerbreen, Marmorbreen, Skruisbreen and Sveigbreen. The area is named after topographer Sigurd Gunnarson Helle.

skruisbreen-nat19f25bd6.d: Skruisbreen is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about seven kilometers, and is a branch of Hellefonna. A nearby mountain is Kropotkinfjellet.

elfenbeinbreen-nat88f69872.d: Elfenbeinbreen is a glacier stream in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about twelve kilometers, and extends from the southern part of the ice cap Nordmannsfonna. The glacier is one of the two main sources to the river Agardhelva, which flows through Agardhdalen towards Agardhbukta.

sveigbreen-natb5c45388.d: Sveigbreen is a glacier stream in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about eleven kilometers, and extends the southern part of the ice cap Hellefonna, south of Kropotkinfjellet. The glacier is one of the two main sources to the river Agardhelva, which flows through Agardhdalen towards Agardhbukta.

luitpoldbreen-nat33072000.d: Luitpoldbreen is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is named after Luitpold, Prince Regent of Bavaria. The glacier is a tributary to Hayesbreen. The mountain of Jebensfjellet is surrounded by Luitpoldbreen, Hayesbreen and Königsbergbreen.

nordmannsfonna-natcd1c2290.d: Nordmannsfonna is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard Norway. The glacier covers an area of about 250 km2, is located between Sassendalen and Storfjorden, and extends from Jebensfjellet to the north to Roslagenfjellet and Eistraryggen to the south. The glacier consists of a number of sub-glaciers or side glaciers, and drains both westwards to Sassendalen and eastwards to Storfjorden.

hayesbreen-nat0f994389.d: Hayesbreen is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is named after American politician and Arctic explorer Isaac Israel Hayes. The glacier has a length of about eighteen kilometers, and debouches into the bay of Mohnbukta. Surrounding mountains are Aagaardfjellet to the north, Jebensfjellet to the south, and Panofskyfjellet where Hayesbreen joins the glacier of Königsbergbreen.

konigsbergbreen-nat034ddf8c.d: Königsbergbreen is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is named after the German town of Königsberg. The glacier has a length of about seven kilometers, and is a tributary to Hayesbreen. A nearby mountain is Jebensfjellet.

rabotbreen-nat34705fd3.d: Rabotbreen is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier is a tributary glacier to Fimbulisen, and is located in the upper part of Sassendalen. Nearby mountains are Bairdfjellet and Moskusryggen.

usherbreen-natfc0f7972.d: Usherbreen is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about 9.5 kilometers, and is located between Kroghfjellet and Domen. Usherbreen is a tributary glacier to Nordmannsfonna, and debouches towards Storfjorden. It is named after Scottish businessman Thomas Leslie Usher.

ulvebreen-natebffb13a.d: Ulvebreen is a glacier in Sabine Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is named after Arctic explorer Erik Andreas Ulve. The glacier is a tributary to Nordmannsfonna, and debouches into the bay of Dunérbukta.

heksebreen-natede6504c.d: Heksebreen ("The Witch Glacier") is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about 3.5 kilometers, and is a tributary glacier to Eidembreen. The glacier is located south in the mountainous district of Trollheimen, and is surrounded by the mountains of Heksefjellet, Runebomma, Trollungen and Stortrollet.

stallobreen-nat528a85e1.d: Stallobreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about 4.5 kilometers, and is located between the mountains of Stallofjellet, Sparrefjellet and Heksefjellet, near the glacier complex of Eidembreen. Stallobreen is named after the stallo creature in Sami folklore.

austgotabreen-nat36f45bf8.d: Austgötabreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier has a length of about six kilometers, and is located between Huldrefjellet, Huldrehatten and Motalafjella. It is named after the Swedish county of Östergötland.

eidembreen-natd3ee9aa8.d: Eidembreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about eighteen kilometers, and debouches into Eidembukta in Forlandsundet, between St. Jonsfjorden and Isfjorden. The glacier is named after Norwegian politician and naval officer Ole Thorenius Eidem. Eidembreen belongs to the mountain and glacier complex of Trollheimen. Further north are Austgötabreen and Huldrebreen, and to the south are Stallobreen and Heksebreen.

venernbreen-natd3f33ce9.d: Venernbreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about fifteen kilometers, and is located between the mountains of Sparrefjellet and Kinnefjellet. The glacier is named after the Swedish lake of Vänern. The nunatak of Tussekallen, in the mountainous district of Trollheimen, is located between the glaciers of Venernbreen and Eidembreen.

kjerulfbreen-natcd2e562a.d: Kjerulfbreen (Kjerulf Glacier) is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about 7.5 kilometers, and is debouching into the Trygghamna bay at the northern side of Isfjorden. The glacier is named after Norwegian geologist Theodor Kjerulf.

sveabreen-nat7d909689.d: Sveabreen is a glacier between Oscar II Land and James I Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of 30 kilometers (19 mi), stretching from Kongsvegpasset at an altitude about 750 meters (2,460 ft), and debouching into Nordfjorden.

l-vliebreen-nata60ab966.d: Løvliebreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about five kilometers, and is located between the mountain ranges of Gunnar Knudsenfjella and Holmesletfjella. The glacier debouches northwards towards St. Jonsfjorden. It is named after Norwegian businessperson Andreas Løvlie along with the nearby mountain of Løvliefjellet.

vestgotabreen-nate2d98075.d: Vestgötabreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about seven kilometers, and is located between Løvliefjellet and the mountain ranges of Holmesletfjella and Motalafjella. The glacier is named from the Swedish province of Västergötland.

hydrografbreen-nat5fb41042.d: Hydrografbreen ("The Hydrographer Glacier") is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier has a length about eight kilometers, and extends from the mountain range of Holmesletfjella to Jørgenfjellet.

bullbreen-natcf97bf19.d: Bullbreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about six kilometers, originates from Svartfjella, runs between Holmesletfjella and Bulltinden, and debouches into St. Jonsfjorden. The glacier is named after Norwegian military officer and politician Karl Sigwald Johannes Bull.

tavlebreen-nat522b7973.d: Tavlebreen (The Slate Glacier) is a glacier in Nordenskiöld Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier is located between Sinaiberget and Lagerlöfhøgda, flowing from Lovberget towards Passdalen. It has a length of about five kilometers.

nansenbreen-nat67df6259.d: Nansenbreen is a glacier in Oscar II Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about fourteen kilometers and is located west of Gestriklandkammen at the northwestern side of Isfjorden, debouching into the bay of Borebukta. It is named after Arctic explorer Fridtjof Nansen. The glacier exhibited a significant surge of about two kilometers in 1946, and has since gradually retreated.

kvit-yj-kulen-nat221362f2.d: Kvitøyjøkulen is a large icecap on the island of Kvitøya in the Svalbard archipelago. The icecap covers most of the island, which has an area between 600 and 700 square kilometers.

svartisen-tjahppisjieg-a-tjahppisjieg-a-.d: Svartisen is a collective term for two glaciers located in Nordland county in northern Norway. It is part of Saltfjellet-Svartisen National Park, located in the Saltfjell mountain range. The glaciers are located in the municipalities of Beiarn, Meløy, Rana, and Rødøy. Svartisen consists of two separate glaciers that are separated by the 1-kilometre (0.62 mi) long Vesterdalen valley. The two glaciers are: Vestisen or Vestre Svartisen ("western Svartisen") has an area of 221 square kilometres (85 sq mi) which makes it the second largest glacier on the Norwegian mainland after the Jostedalsbreen glacier. (There are larger glaciers on Svalbard.

folgefonna-natb760b613.d: Søndre Folgefonna (lit. 'Southern Folgefonna') is the third largest glacier in mainland Norway, and is the largest of the three glaciers constituting Folgefonna. The glacier is located at the base of the Folgefonna peninsula in Vestland county, along the border of Ullensvang Municipality, Etne Municipality, and Kvinnherad Municipality. The highest point on the glacier is 1,660 m (5,446 ft) above sea level and its lowest point is 490 m (1,608 ft) above sea level. The glacier is located inside Folgefonna National Park.

folgefonna-nat55f8fd4a.d: Midtre Folgefonna (lit. 'Central Folgefonna') is a glacier located in the Hardanger region of Vestland county, Norway. It is one of the three glaciers that make up the large Folgefonna glacier. It is located along the border of Ullensvang Municipality and Kvinnherad Municipality between the Nordre Folgefonna and Søndre Folgefonna glaciers on the Folgefonna peninsula. In 1969, the glacier was listed at 13 square kilometres (5.0 sq mi). In a book by glaciologist Olav Orheim from 2009 the area is listed as only 9 square kilometres (3.5 sq mi). The glacier drains partly to the Maurangerfjord to the west, and partly to the Sørfjorden to the east.

folgefonna-nat41585cd3.d: Nordre Folgefonna (lit. 'Northern Folgefonna') is one of the largest glaciers in mainland Norway. It is the northernmost of the three glaciers that make up Folgefonna. The glacier is located on the Folgefonna peninsula in the Hardanger and Sunnhordland regions of Vestland county. The 26-square-kilometre (10 sq mi) glacier lies along the borders of Kvinnherad Municipality and Ullensvang Municipality. Its highest point is 1,640 m (5,381 ft) above sea level, and its lowest point is 990 m (3,248 ft) above sea level. The glacier lies almost entirely inside Folgefonna National Park.

hardangerj-kulen-natff831052.d: Hardangerjøkulen (lit. 'Hardanger Glacier') is the sixth largest glacier in mainland Norway. It is located in Eidfjord Municipality and Ulvik Municipality in Vestland county. It is located about 16 kilometres (9.9 mi) northeast of the village of Eidfjord, about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) south of the village of Finse, and about 20 kilometres (12 mi) west of the village of Haugastøl. Hardangerjøkulen's highest point is 1,863 m (6,112 ft) above sea level, and is the highest point in Hordaland county. Its lowest point is 1,050 m (3,440 ft) above sea level. The largest measured ice thickness on Hardangerjøkulen was 380 metres (1,250 ft), but it has been getting thinner during the 20th century.

veobrean-natdcad93da.d: Veobrean is a glacier in Lom Municipality and Vågå Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. The 9-square-kilometre (3.5 sq mi) glacier is located within the Jotunheimen National Park. The glacier is located on the west side of the mountain Veotinden, north of the mountain Store Memurutinden, east of Veobreahesten, Veobretinden, and Leirhøi, and south of Veopallan.

alfotbreen-nat46f8a0a9.d: Ålfotbreen is a glacier located in Vestland county, Norway. The 17-square-kilometre (6.6 sq mi) glacier is located in the Nordfjord region and it straddles the borders of Bremanger Municipality, Kinn Municipality, and Gloppen Municipality. It is located west of the village of Hyen, south of the village of Ålfoten, and east of the village of Svelgen. The glacier reaches an elevation of 1,385 metres (4,544 ft) at its highest point. The area surrounding the glacier, closer to the Nordfjorden, is one of the wettest places in Norway, getting an average of 5,600 millimetres (220 in) of rainfall each year.

simlebreen-vatjamjakjiehkke-natb586a2b4.d: Simlebreen (Norwegian) or Vátjamjåkjiehkke (Lule Sami) is a glacier in Beiarn Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. The 21-square-kilometre (8.1 sq mi) glacier lies about 20 kilometres (12 mi) north of the much larger glacier named Svartisen, making it the 18th largest glacier on the Norwegian mainland. However a 2018 study concluded that the glacier's area had diminished from 22-square-kilometre (8.5 sq mi) in 1999, to 17.5-square-kilometre (6.8 sq mi) in 2018. The mountain Simletinden lies on the East side of the glacier, reaching a height of 1,329 metres (4,360 ft).

jostefonni-natb7889d0c.d: Jostefonni is a glacier is located in Vestland county, Norway. It covers an area of around 11 square kilometres (4.2 sq mi) in Sunnfjord Municipality and Sogndal Municipality. Jostefonni was formerly a part of the large Jostedalsbreen glacier, but it is no longer connected to the main glacier. It sits inside the Jostedalsbreen National Park, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) east of the village of Haukedalen and about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) northwest of the village of Fjærland. The Grovabreen glacier lies about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) north of this glacier.

grovabreen-nat5cca102d.d: Grovabreen is a glacier is located in Vestland county, Norway. It covers an area of about 20 square kilometres (7.7 sq mi) in Sunnfjord Municipality in the Sunnfjord region. The highest point on the glacier sits at an elevation of 1,636 metres (5,367 ft) above sea level. The glacier is part of Jostedalsbreen National Park, just south of the lake Jølstravatnet. The village of Skei lies about 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) north of the glacier and the village of Haukedalen lies about 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) southwest of the glacier. The Jostefonn glacier lies about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) to the south of this glacier; both are located at the north end of the Gaularfjellet mountains.

jostedalsbreen-nat673cdf5f.d: Jostedal Glacier or Jostedalsbreen (Norwegian) is the largest glacier in continental Europe. It is in Vestland county in Western Norway. Jostedalsbreen is located in the municipalities of Luster, Sogndal, Sunnfjord, and Stryn (all in Vestland county), plus the northeastern tip of the glacier extends into Skjåk Municipality (in Innlandet county). The highest peak in the area is Lodalskåpa at a height of 2,083 metres (6,834 ft).

nigardsbreen-nat5c08375a.d: Nigardsbreen (lit. 'the Nigard Glacier') is a glacier arm of the large Jostedalsbreen glacier. Nigardsbreen lies about 30 kilometres (19 mi) north of the village of Gaupne in the Jostedalen valley in Luster Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is located just west of the Jostedøla river. The Breheimsenteret museum is located 11 kilometres (6.8 mi) south in the village of Jostedal. In front of the Nigardsbreen glacier is the lake Nigardsbrevatnet where there is a small boat to transport visitors to the glacier. There is also a bus to take visitors to the glacier.

fannarakbreen-natcb567d16.d: Fannaråkbreen is a glacier in Luster Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It covers an area of about 6.2-square-kilometre (2.4 sq mi), and consists of three parts. The glacier covers the eastern and northern sides of the mountain of Fannaråki, and is located within the Jotunheimen National Park.

myklebustbreen-natfadf1317.d: Myklebustbreen is the seventh largest glacier in mainland Norway. It is located along the borders of Sunnfjord Municipality, Gloppen Municipality, and Stryn Municipality in Vestland county. Its highest point is located just below the nunatak Snønipa, with an altitude of 1,827 metres (5,994 ft). The lowest point on the glacier is at an elevation of 890 metres (2,920 ft) above sea level. The villages of Byrkjelo and Egge both lie on the European route E39 highway which runs north and south, about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) east of Myklebustbreen. The Oldedalen valley lies to the east of the glacier.

briksdalsbreen-natd58c947c.d: Briksdalsbreen (lit. 'the Briksdal glacier') is one of the most accessible and best known arms of the Jostedalsbreen glacier. Briksdalsbreen is located in Stryn Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. The glacier lies on the north side of the Jostedalsbreen, in Briksdalen (lit. 'the Briks valley') which is located at the end of the Oldedalen valley, about 25 kilometres (16 mi) south of the village of Olden. It is located inside Jostedalsbreen National Park. Briksdalsbreen terminates in a small glacial lake, Briksdalsbrevatnet, which lies 346 metres (1,135 ft) above sea level.

sp-rteggbreen-nat3ce81ca0.d: Spørteggbreen is a glacier in Luster Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is the 12th largest glacier in Norway. It lies between the Jostedalsbreen and Harbardsbreen glaciers. The 28-square-kilometre (11 sq mi) glacier lies inside Breheimen National Park. The village of Jostedal lies 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) to the west and the village of Skjolden lies 12 kilometres (7.5 mi) to the southeast. Grånosi (in the northeastern part of the glacier) is the highest point on the glacier at 1,750 metres (5,740 ft) above sea level, and the lowest point is at 1,270 metres (4,170 ft) above sea level.

austerdalsbreen-natc255cea7.d: Austerdalsbreen is a glacier in Luster Municipality in Vestland, Norway. It is a side branch of the Jostedalsbreen glacier, and is included in the Jostedalsbreen National Park. The glacier is fed by the three steep glaciers Odinbreen, Torbreen and Lokebreen. The lower, flat part of the glacier displays a characteristic fishbone or lobster tail pattern.

gihtsejieg-a-natc2631566.d: Gihtsejiegŋa is one of the largest glaciers in mainland Norway. It is located in Narvik Municipality in Nordland county, about 20 kilometres (12 mi) southeast of the village of Kjøpsvik, on the border with Sweden. The name of the glacier comes from the Lule Sami language. The elevation of the glacier ranges from 1,500 to 870 metres (4,920 to 2,850 ft) above sea level. The highest point of the glacier sits right below the summit of the 1,520-metre (4,990 ft) tall Bjørntoppen.

frostisen-ruostajiek-a-natd18c2918.d: Frostisen (Norwegian) or Ruostajiekŋa (Northern Sami) is a glacier in Narvik Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is one of the larger plateau glaciers in Norway. Frostisen covers an area of about 25 square kilometres (9.7 sq mi), and its elevation ranges from 840 to 1,710 metres (2,760 to 5,610 ft) above sea level. The glacier lies near the Skjomen fjord, a branch of the Ofotfjorden, just southwest of the town of Narvik. The village of Elvegård lies about 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) east of the glacier. The lakes Geitvatnet, Isvatnet, Kjelvatnet, Nordre Bukkevatnet and Søre Bukkevatnet lie southwest of the glacier.

blamannsisen-almajalosjieg-a-nate856727c.d: Blåmannsisen (Norwegian) or Ålmåjalosjiegŋa (Lule Sami) (English: Blåmann Glacier) is the fifth-largest glacier in mainland Norway. It is located on the border of Fauske Municipality and Sørfold Municipality in Nordland county, Norway—just 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) west of the border with Sweden. Its highest point is 1,560 metres (5,120 ft) above sea level and its lowest point is at an elevation of 810 metres (2,660 ft). Three outlet glaciers extend from the icecap. A small outlet spills over a subglacial ridge to the north damming an unnamed lake resulting in occasion outburst floods. To the east a large outlet extends towards the lake, Leirvatnet. A further outlet descends steeply to the west.

strupbreen-nat8efb07be.d: Strupbreen is a glacier located in Lyngen Municipality in Troms county, Norway. The 8.7-square-kilometre (3.4 sq mi) glacier is located in the Lyngen Alps, about 12 kilometres (7.5 mi) north of the village of Lyngseidet. Historically, the glacier has at times reached all the way down to the Lyngenfjorden. Today the end of the glacier lies about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) from the shoreline, with a small stream of water flowing from the glacier to the fjord. The glacier, at about its Little Ice Age maximum extent shed ice blocks onto the shoreline below. This formed a cone of ice separated from the main glacier snout. This cone was used as an ice supply for fishing vessels.

okstindbreen-nat80f73615.d: Okstindbreen is the eighth-largest glacier in mainland Norway. Okstindbreen is also the largest of the 19 glaciers in the Okstindan area, which together covered about 46 km² in 2010. The area of Okstindbreen itself decreased by 31% over 10 years, from 53.6 km² in 2012 to 36.9 km² in 2022. Okstindbreen comprises an ice field including Vestisen, Vestre Okstindbreen, Austre Okstindbreen, Bessedørbreen, Steikvassbreen, Vestre Svartfjellbreen, and Oksfjellbreen. The largest outlet glacier from Okstindbreen is Austre Okstindbreen, measured to be 14 km² in 1996. It drains towards the valley Oksfjelldalen, located northeast of Oksskolten, the highest mountain in Northern Norway.

valhallfonna-nat917b54cc.d: Valhallfonna is an ice cap in Ny-Friesland at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is located west of Hinlopen Strait and northeast of Åsgardfonna. The glacier covers an area of about 1,000 km2.

asgardfonna-nataa40a00e.d: Åsgardfonna is a glacier in Ny-Friesland on Spitsbergen, between Wijdefjorden and Lomfjorden. The glacier covers and area of about 1,230 km2 (470 sq mi). It is named after Åsgard in Norse mythology. Earlier names of the glacier are Åsgårdfonna and Névé dôme Asgård. A study published in the scientific journal Nature in 2025, based on sediment analyses from the lakes of Berglivatnet and Lakssjøen, suggests that the ice cap of Åsgardfonna survived and possibly expanded in periods during the warmer-than-present Holocene climatic optimum.

veteranen-nat6fcf40bd.d: Veteranen (The Veteran) is a glacier in Ny-Friesland at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It has a length of about 25 kilometers and a width of up to five kilometers. The glacier debouches into Lomfjorden, and is connected with Kvitbreen at the other side of Trebrepasset. The name of the glacier was suggested by Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld in 1863.

gjegnalundsbreen-nat67ec8eec.d: Gjegnalundsbreen is a glacier is located in Vestland county, Norway. The 13-square-kilometre (5.0 sq mi) glacier sits on the borders of Bremanger Municipality and Gloppen Municipality. The glacier sits on the eastern side of the 1,670-metre (5,480 ft) tall mountain Blånibba, inside the Ålfotbreen landscape protection area which also includes the nearby Ålfotbreen glacier. The highest point on the glacier is at an elevation of 1,590 metres (5,220 ft) above sea levelThe Nordfjorden and Hyefjorden are located just north and east of the glacier. The village of Hyen lies about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) south of the fjord.

langfjordj-kelen-bartnatvuonjiehkki-nat3.d: Langfjordjøkelen (Norwegian) or Bártnatvuonjiehkki (Northern Sami) is a glacier that is located on the border of Finnmark and Troms counties in Norway, making it one of the northernmost glaciers on the mainland of Norway. The 8-square-kilometre (3.1 sq mi) glacier is located on the border of Loppa Municipality and Kvænangen Municipality. The highest point on the glacier reaches 1,050 metres (3,440 ft) above sea level. Between publication of maps in 1976 and 2012, the snout of the Langfjordjokelen is shown to have retreated by approximately 1,400 metres (4,600 ft). The glacier is currently being studied by glaciologists as the snout is retreating faster than any other glacier in Europe.

ksfjordj-kelen-aksovuonjiehkki-nat4e8b7b.d: Øksfjordjøkelen (Norwegian) or Ákšovuonjiehkki (Northern Sami) is the ninth largest glacier in mainland Norway. The glacier is located in Troms and Finnmark counties. The 42-square-kilometre (16 sq mi) glacier lies on the border of Loppa Municipality (in Finnmark) and Kvænangen Municipality (in Troms). The highest point was earlier known to have an elevation of 1,204 metres (3,950 ft). It is now 1,191 metres (3,907 ft) due to glacier shrinkage. The mountain Svartfjellet lies just north of the glacier in Loppa Municipality. That is another of the highest points in Finnmark county. The lowest point on the glacier has an elevation of 330 metres (1,080 ft).

svartfjellj-kelen-nat1330b38c.d: Svartfjelljøkelen is a glacier in Loppa Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway. The glacier has an area of 4.13 square kilometres (1.59 sq mi). The highest point of the glacier reaches an elevation of 1,082 metres (3,550 ft) above sea level, and the lowest point on the glacier is 414 metres (1,358 ft) above sea level. The glacier is located about 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) east of the village of Bergsfjord and about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) to the southwest of the village of Nuvsvåg.

sulitjelmaisen-sallajieg-a-nat149e10df.d: The Sulitjelma Glacier (also: Sulitjelmaisen (Norwegian), Sállajiegŋa (Lule Sami), or Salajekna (Swedish)) is one of the largest glaciers in mainland Norway. The 24-square-kilometre (9.3 sq mi) glacier is located in mostly in Norway, but the eastern part crosses over into Sweden. The Norwegian part is in Fauske Municipality in Nordland county, about 40 kilometres (25 mi) east of the town of Fauske. The Swedish part (where it is referred to as Salajekna) lies on the border of Arjeplog Municipality and Jokkmokk Municipality in Norrbotten County. When the whole glacier is considered, it is the largest glacier in Sweden.

fresvikbreen-natfa2faa36.d: Fresvikbreen is a glacier on the south side of the Sognefjord in Vik Municipality in Vestland, county, Norway. It lies between the Seljedal valley in the west, and the Storedal valley in the east. It is located about 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) southwest of the village of Fresvik and 11 kilometres (6.8 mi) southeast of the municipal center of Vikøyri. The glacier has an area of 15 square kilometres (5.8 sq mi) and its highest point is 1,648 metres (5,407 ft) above sea level. Fresvikbreen is the 23rd largest glacier on the Norwegian mainland.

harbardsbreen-nat19440780.d: Harbardsbreen is the 10th largest glacier in mainland Norway. It is located on the south side of the Tverrådalskyrkja mountain in the Breheimen mountain range in Luster Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. The 36-square-kilometre (14 sq mi) glacier is inside Breheimen National Park, just northeast of the Spørteggbreen glacier. The village of Skjolden lies 18 kilometres (11 mi) south of the glacier. Its highest point lies 1,950 m (6,398 ft) above sea level and its lowest point 1,250 m (4,101 ft) above sea level.

tunsbergdalsbreen-nat6b234cb0.d: Tunsbergdalsbreen is a glacier in Luster Municipality in Vestland, Norway. It is a side branch of the Jostedalsbreen glacier, and is included in the Jostedalsbreen National Park.

erdmannbreen-nat71619321.d: Erdmannbreen is a glacier in Nordenskiöld Land at Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is named after Swedish geologist Axel Joachim Erdmann. The glacier has a length of about six kilometers, and is surrounded by the mountains of Malmberget, Ytterdalsgubben and Kosterfjellet. The river of Ytterdalselva originates from Erdmannbreen and flows through the valley of Ytterdalen to the bay of Van Muydenbukta.

vre-buarbreen-natbf05f362.d: Buarbreen is a glacier in Ullensvang Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is an offshoot of the large Folgefonna glacier. The small glacial arm reaches down into the Buardalen valley, just 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) southwest of the town of Odda. The glacier is split into two parts, one on either side of a small mountain peak. Both sides drain into the Jordalselvi river which flows out through the valley into the lake Sandvinvatnet.

jordbrugrotta-nata5dec6c8.d: Jordbrugrotta is a cave in the upper parts of Plurdalen by the river in Rana Municipality in Nordland county in Norway. The cave is named after the farm Jordbrua further down the valley. The cave is situated about two kilometers south of the dam at Kallvatnet. Jordbrugrotta was discovered during the Second World War. In 1949 an attempt to enter via Sprutfossen and into the main system did not succeed. In 1953 Jakob Otnes from NVE described parts of the cave and reported that during the winter they had succeeded in entering 500 meters into the mountain via Sprutfossen. In 1959 an expedition from NTH visited the cave but did not make a report.

radiohola-nat352355aa.d: Radiohòla (lit. 'the radio cave') is a natural shelter used by the Norwegian resistance during the Second World War. It served as a hiding place for a radio that brought news from the British, during a time of which radios were banned and the German occupants arrested and prosecuted those found in possession of one.

gjendebu-nat1a947715.d: Gjendebu is the oldest cabin of the Norwegian Mountain Touring Association (DNT). The cabin lies 995 metres above sea level, by the western end of the lake Gjende, central in Jotunheimen. It is accessible by hiking along marked trails, or by boat over Gjende from Gjendesheim. The cabin was built in 1871 and was at that time 45 m² and with 12 beds, today there are 119 beds. Neighbouring cabins are Gjendesheim, Memurubu, Fondsbu, Olavsbu, Leirvassbu and Spiterstulen.

leirvassbu-nat988deaf3.d: Leirvassbu is a mountain lodge of the Norwegian Trekking Association (In Norwegian, Den Norske Turistforening – DNT) located in the Leirdal in the county Oppland in the middle of Norway. The lodge has a capacity of 205 beds. The hut is located about 1400 meters above sea level in the high mountains Jotunheimen. Several walks are possible. It is located at the end of a side road off Norwegian County Road 55, the Sognefjellsvegen, just before Lake Bøvertunvatnet. Surrounding places are Bøvertun, Krossbu and Elveseter.

memurubu-nat96d13ef3.d: Memurubu is a tourist hut in Norway, at the end or start of the famous Besseggen hiking trail. Memurubu is originally an old mountain pasture dating back to 1872, but has had tourists just as long. Cows are still grazing around the tourist hut, which lies at the mouth of the river Muru in the valley Memurudalen. After a fire destroyed the original lodge in 1998 it was rebuilt. The new facility has a few family rooms with shower and bathrooms, although most of the 150 bunks are in double or quadruple occupancy rooms. Memurubu was the fourth cabin in Norway set up by Norwegian Mountain Touring Association (DNT) but is now privately owned, though members of DNT obtain cheaper prices.

gjendesheim-nat8be8f2d6.d: Gjendesheim Turisthytte has been a staffed lodge with Norwegian Mountain Touring Association (Norwegian: Den Norske Turistforening – DNT). It is located in the heart of the Norwegian mountains in Vågå Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. DNT Oslo og Omegn has been the proprietor since 1878. The lodge can accommodate 170 guests in bedrooms with 1, 2, and 4 beds in four dormitories. The standard is simple; with bunks and bathroom facilities. Gjendesheim is situated at the east end of Gjende lake, at an elevation of 1,000 metres (3,300 ft) above sea level. It is located about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) from Maurvangen off Norwegian County Road 51.

spiterstulen-turisthytte-nat18b5aa65.d: Spiterstulen is a former mountain farm, now a tourist station in the valley Visdalen in Lom Municipality in Innlandet county, Norway. Spiterstulen lies about 1,100 metres (3,600 ft) above sea level, between the two highest mountains in Norway, Galdhøpiggen and Glittertinden. It is the largest tourist cabin in Jotunheimen, with around 230 beds. It is reachable by car between March and October. Spiterstulen was originally a cabin for shepherds. In 1836 it was extended for guests for the first time, since one of the paths used to cross the mountain was nearby (the Visdalen path reaches an elevation of 1,490 metres (4,890 ft), slightly higher than the present Norwegian County Road 55).

glitterheim-nat996a64c5.d: Glitterheim is a mountain cabin in the valley of Veodalen in Jotunheimen, Norway. It is owned by the Norwegian Mountain Touring Association (DNT). The cabin lies 1,384 meters above sea level, at the foot of the mountain Glittertind. It was designed by architect Hjalmar Welhaven, and built in 1901.

bellingstua-natf3586847.d: The Norwegian Trekking Association (Norwegian: Den norske turistforening, DNT) is a Norwegian association which maintains mountain trails and cabins in Norway. The association was founded on 21 January 1868 with the scope "to help and develop tourism in this country". Today the goal is to work for simple, secure and environmentally friendly outdoor activities. DNT has currently more than 300,000 individual members, and 57 local chapters. It also has several "honorary members", prominent people who have shown a keen interest in Norwegian nature and given the country publicity as a tourist destination, among them Kofi Annan and Katie Melua.

euroopan-vapaareititetty-digitaalinen-ka.d: The E6 European long distance path or E6 path is one of the European long-distance paths from the northwest tip of Finland through Sweden, Denmark, Germany and Austria to the Adriatic coast in Slovenia. A second section starts again in Greece to finish in Turkey.

st-olavsleden-dagsetapp-sul-vuku-nat4bae.d: St. Olavsleden (English: St. Olav's Path; Swedish: S:t Olavsleden), is a pilgrim's way between Selånger outside Sundsvall in Sweden and Nidaros Cathedral in Trondheim in Norway, commemorating Saint Olaf who was King of Norway from 1015 to 1028. St. Olavsleden was one of the Pilgrim's Routes. From the 1970s until 2012, it was called the Mittnordenleden. Today St. Olavsleden stretches 564 kilometres (350 mi) from the Bothnian sea in the east to the Atlantic Ocean in the west through two countries and eleven municipalities. The trail is marked with the St. Olav symbol, which marks all the so-called St. Olav roads (Swedish: S:t Olavsvägar), leading towards Nidaros Cathedral. St.

stmarka-nasjonalpark-natb8a8166e.d: Østmarka National Park is a Norwegian national park established in 2023. It covers an area of 54 km² in Østmarka in Oslo and the Akershus municipalities of Nordre Follo, Lørenskog, Rælingen and Enebakk. The national park was established ‘to preserve nature for its own sake and to ensure that future generations have access to more unspoilt natural areas for recreation, outdoor pursuits and physical activity.’

prester-dkilen-naturreservat-nat756629ca.d: The Ilene and Presterødkilen Ramsar Site is a wetland system in Tønsberg municipality, Vestfold, established in 1985. The site comprises two nature reserves: Ilene Nature Reserve and Presterødkilen Nature Reserve. Both nature reserves comprise extensive wetland areas, a large proportion of which are shallow areas that are exposed at low tide. Together, the two areas form a single Ramsar site. Presterødkilen is a shallow fjord arm with extensive mudflats at low tide. Ilene contains areas of marshland, wet meadows, pastures and woodland. Ilene lies to the west of Tønsberg town centre, whilst Presterødkilen lies to the east of the town centre.

ramndalen-naturreservat-nat1f3e9360.d: Ramndalen Nature Reserve is situated on the Romeriksåsene hills east of Hakadal Church. Most of the area lies in Nittedal, but a small part lies in Gjerdrum, bordered by a power line to the east. The elevation gradient is fairly gentle; the central area lies at 350–370 metres above sea level, with Kirkebyhøgda at 408 metres above sea level in the south-west being the highest point. The lowest point is where the reserve borders Nordre Ravndalstjern to the south, at 281 metres above sea level. The reserve was extended in 2023 and now covers 2,162 dekar. The slopes feature nutrient-rich seepage water and rich vegetation, including, in places, calcareous pine forest and broad-leaved deciduous forest. Elsewhere, poorer spruce and pine forests predominate.

stordamsmyra-naturreservat-nate9c8dd98.d: Stordamsmyra Nature Reserve is situated at the northern end of Stordammen, a good three kilometres north of the town of Fredrikstad in Østfold. The reserve comprises Stordamsmyra itself and a narrow buffer zone on the western and eastern sides. The marsh stretches 1.25 km in a north-east to south-west direction and is 50–100 metres wide. The bog was formed by the encroachment of vegetation from the north into Stordammen. Stordammen is a reservoir originally dammed in 1809, and this has resulted in a high groundwater level in the bog. The bog is therefore a minerogenic flat bog, dominated by poor loose-soil and soft-mat vegetation. Areas with richer vegetation are also found, and these include the red-listed orchid, the narrow-leaved marsh orchid.

s-ndre-haugstenasen-naturreservat-nat214.d: The Søndre Haugstenåsen Nature Reserve is situated on the hillside east of the Regimentsmyra shooting range in Fredrikstad municipality, between Begby to the north and County Road 107 (Torsnesveien) to the south. To the east, the reserve borders on farmland. The conservation values are particularly linked to the vegetation, which comprises several different types. To the south, there are a number of small fissure valleys, containing clay, shell gravel and sand. Here, an oak forest grows with hazel in the undergrowth. Some trees have a trunk diameter of over 50 cm. In the wettest areas, black alder also grows, sometimes with stilt roots. And in Svarteklova, in the south-east of the reserve, a number of rare fungi species have been recorded, several of which are on the Red List, including the pink large-spined fungus.

j-rstadmyra-naturreservat-nat4a9ca2ce.d: Jørstadmyra Nature Reserve is a bog area just east of Skjebergkilen, in the south of Sarpsborg municipality. The bog is a groundwater-fed (minerogenic) flat bog, dominated by minerotrophic mat vegetation and tussock vegetation. It is one of the few, and the largest, intact bogs on the Østfold coast. The bog is also known as Langmyr.

fuglen-og-myr-naturreservat-natabdefced.d: Fuglen Nature Reserve is situated east of Store Erte, in the far east of Halden municipality. The reserve’s eastern boundary follows the Nøstholvassdraget watercourse, which also forms the municipal boundary with Aremark. The bedrock consists of gneiss, which is mainly structured in a north-south direction. The terrain lies above the marine limit, and the mineralised loose sediments are largely bottom moraines. The forest is dominated by pine; in the east, between Krokvann and Koven, the pine forest is between 250 and 350 years old. There are also some spruce, black alder, aspen and weeping birch, particularly in the south. Timber was previously floated down the Nøstholvassdraget watercourse, and there are traces of selective felling in the forest. Nowadays, only beavers fell trees, particularly in the north-west near the outlet of Duvlemyrtjern.

ra-naturreservat-natf4e8c8fe.d: Øra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Fredrikstad municipality, Østfold. The nature reserve is situated to the east of the mouth of the Glomma river and has held Ramsar Site status since 1985, due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1979 to protect large shallow areas which, at low tide, take on the character of mudflat areas and which are used as resting places during the spring and autumn bird migration periods. The area is also used for breeding, moulting and overwintering. The vegetation consists, amongst other things, of common reed, common bulrush, sea rush and heart-leaved rush, which provide an important food source for the most common species, including the whooper swan, mute swan, mallard, teal, goldeneye and common snipe.

kjennetjern-naturreservat-nat64ef181b.d: The Kjennetjern Nature Reserve comprises Lake Kjennetjern itself and the surrounding wetland areas. The lake lies 18 metres above sea level, surrounded by farmland just south of the Kjenne farm on Onsøy in Fredrikstad municipality. The lake lies on marine sediments, mostly clay. It is very shallow and nutrient-rich, and consequently heavily overgrown. Water lilies cover large parts of the lake. Other vegetation includes, amongst other things, common reed, common cattail, common rush and yellow flag iris. Kjennetjernet is the only remaining small lake situated on clay soil outside the Raet area in Østfold. As of 1989, 69 different wetland bird species had been recorded at the site, several of which are rare.

skjebergkilen-naturreservat-nat6898a187.d: Skjebergkilen Nature Reserve is situated at the innermost part of Skjebergkilen, where the Skjebergbekken stream flows into the sea. The reserve encompasses the innermost part of the inlet as well as the adjacent marshes and wet meadows. The aim of the conservation area is to preserve an area of threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats. The area is particularly important as a resting and breeding site for birds.

fuglevikbukta-naturreservat-nat34ecea1c.d: Fuglevikbukta Nature Reserve is a shallow bay in the Østerelva river on the eastern side of Kråkerøy in Fredrikstad municipality. The bay lies in the brackish water zone at the mouth of the Glomma, and the area is regularly exposed at low tide. At the innermost part of the bay, a large area is overgrown with common reed, and black alder grows where the bay meets the mainland. Along the stream by Fuglevik Farm, there is also other lush deciduous woodland. The area rarely freezes over and is particularly important as a wintering ground for several bird species, and as a resting place for migratory birds. As of 1986, 52 different species of wetland birds had been recorded in the area. All wildlife and plants – including dead shrubs and trees, lichens and fungi – are protected against damage and destruction.

brattas-naturreservat-nate498af62.d: Brattås Nature Reserve is situated east of Femsjøen and north of Stenselva in Halden municipality. Almost the entire area is an old burnt area resulting from a forest fire in 1911. One of the aims of the conservation is to monitor vegetation development in an area where no intervention has taken place since the fire. Most of the humus layer was burnt away, so that a humus layer of any thickness is now only found in the fissure valley. Combined with a gneiss bedrock, this results in very poor and unremarkable vegetation. The forest still has a youthful character, with aspen and birch as the predominant pioneer species.

skarakilen-naturreservat-nat68567cee.d: The Skårakilen Nature Reserve comprises a stretch of the Seutelva river in Fredrikstad municipality, as well as the wetlands on both sides. The reserve extends approximately 1.5 kilometres northwards from the industrial area at Ørebekk, between the railway line, Mosseveien and the Skåra farms. The west bank of the river is dominated by a large reed bed. At the western end, towards Mosseveien, there is a swamp forest. On the eastern side, there are wet meadows used as pastureland. As of 1986, 41 wetland bird species had been recorded in the area, including ducks, waders, rails and passerines. Several of the species are rare in Norway, including the bearded tit. A large population of the invasive species giant hogweed has also been discovered, and measures have been put in place to combat it.

hansemakerkilen-naturreservat-nat5902d69.d: Hansemarkerkilen (historically Hansemakerkilen) is the innermost part of Grimsøykilen, on the eastern side of the Grimsøy peninsula in Sarpsborg municipality. The nature reserve encompasses the inlet on the southern side of Grimsøy Bridge, together with the adjacent beaches and wetlands. The purpose of the conservation is to safeguard a diverse wetland area of high botanical value, and an important breeding site for wetland birds. As of 1986, 22 species of wetland birds had been recorded in the area. The reserve is crossed by Holmenveien over Holmensalta.

ramsas-naturreservat-nat1f19a33c.d: Ramsåsen Nature Reserve is situated in Vestmarka, in the south-west of Bærum municipality. The nature reserve covers Ramsåsen’s 2.5 km-long eastern slope down towards Jordbrudalen and consists of high cliffs, wooded and bare scree slopes, rock faces and a deeply incised valley, Ramsåsdalen. In many places within the reserve, the terrain is difficult to access and the forest has therefore been little affected by forestry. The reserve features many types of vegetation, including old broad-leaved deciduous forest with a high density of important key elements. To the north of Ramsåsdalen lies a classic elm-lime forest, forming a narrow strip between high cliffs at the top and open scree slopes at the bottom. The deciduous forest, dominated by elm, lime and hazel, consists of large trees.

viernbukta-naturreservat-natbc6bb529.d: The Viernbukta Nature Reserve on Brønnøya in Asker municipality was established on 27 June 2008. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a representative and virtually untouched wetland area with a wide variety of plant communities, rich wetland flora including several rare species and elements of deciduous forest, as well as a large, virtually untouched and well-developed blood cranesbill meadow containing rare species. The aim is also to safeguard an important resting and feeding area for birds, and an important habitat for the common shelduck.

nes-ytjern-naturreservat-natb24833d6.d: The Nesøytjern Nature Reserve comprises Nesøytjern on Nesøya in Asker municipality, and the catchment area surrounding the lake, together with some additional land. The reserve was designated on 10 March 1978 and covers approximately 500 daa. The lake is not significantly affected by inflows from surrounding areas. Together with its catchment area, the lake probably constitutes the only reasonably intact natural environment of this type on the Cambrian-Silurian rocks of the Inner Oslo Fjord. The reserve features a wide variety of rich vegetation types and forest types that are otherwise rare in Norway. Rich swamp forest is one of our most endangered forest types, the area of which has been greatly reduced. Development, drainage and logging of these areas are among the greatest threats.

triungsvann-naturreservat-nat0ad8a464.d: Triungsvann Nature Reserve is a wetland area in Bærumsmarka that straddles the border with Oslo. The nature reserve was designated on 2 October 1992 and covers an area of 564 dekar. The name Triungsvann comes from ‘tri’, meaning three, and older maps also show that there were originally three lakes. The lake’s outlet was dammed during the war to divert more water to the neighbouring lakes Bogstadvannet and Østernvann. Downstream of the dam, there are also remains of older dams.

ramstadslottet-naturreservat-natdfe80df2.d: The Ramstadslottet Nature Reserve in the municipalities of Rælingen and Lørenskog was established by royal decree on 7 December 2001. The nature reserve covers a total area of just over 2 km². The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a representative coniferous forest in the Eastern Norway region, characterised by great variation in topography and forest vegetation, including all natural flora and fauna. The area is hilly, stretching from 220 metres above sea level up to Barlindåsen at 398 metres above sea level. It is home to some of the largest spruce trees recorded in Eastern Norway, as well as pine trees that are around 300 years old.

slattumsr-a-naturreservat-nat379b6515.d: Slattumsrøa Nature Reserve is a wooded area in Lillomarka, Nittedal municipality, and covers 1,443 da. The nature reserve lies to the west of Skytta in Nittedal, and is bounded by a power line to the east, a cross-country ski trail to the south-east and the county boundary with Oslo to the south-west. Within the reserve lie the ponds Romstjern, Lusevasan and the majority of Bleiktjern, all of which drain into Steinbruvannet in Oslo, outside the reserve. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a large area of remaining old-growth forest with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems and species, as well as the area’s natural ecological processes. The area contains a significant amount of deadwood and sections with a continuous presence of deadwood.

r-verkollen-naturreservat-nat5594eef7.d: Røverkollen is a hill on the border between the municipalities of Oslo and Nittedal. The summit, at 404 metres above sea level, lies in Oslo, approximately 70 metres south of the municipal boundary. A TV mast stands here as a landmark, clearly visible for miles around. Just north of the TV mast stands a concrete viewing tower, with an external spiral staircase and a roofed canopy. There are also several ancient burial mounds on Røverkollen. The old Bergensveien road ran along the foot of Røverkollen, on the south and west sides. According to tradition, this was a favourite haunt of highwaymen. The area features a wide variety of vegetation types. In places, there are calcareous rocks which support extremely rich vegetation types, sharply contrasted with the otherwise poor vegetation elsewhere.

djupdalen-og-kjaglidalen-naturreservat-n.d: The Djupdalen and Kjaglidalen Nature Reserve is situated in Hole in Buskerud and Bærum in Akershus. It was established on 20 March 2015 through the merger of the Djupdalen Landscape Conservation Area and the Kjaglidalen Nature Reserve, both of which were designated on 14 June 2002. The new nature reserve covers an area of 4,436 dekar. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve an area comprising a distinctive geological fault zone featuring rhomboid porphyry rock, and which contains threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats. The protected area consists of a fault valley stretching from the Isi waste facility in a north-north-westerly direction towards Bureheim. The valley is V-shaped and the valley floor is characterised by the Isielva river and its erosive action.

krokkleiva-naturreservat-natddcad8fb.d: Krokkleiva Nature Reserve consists of a distinct rift valley (also known as a gorge) on the western edge of the Krokskog Plateau, just south of Sundvollen. The name Krokkleiva refers to the steep track through the gorge, which was formerly part of the Kongeveien road between the capital and Ringerike. The bedrock dates from the Cambrian–Silurian period, and the topography creates a distinctive climate with local variations. The forest is dominated by spruce; there are also both vulnerable and rare species. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but ordinary hunting is permitted, as is the gathering of berries and edible mushrooms. Motorised traffic is prohibited, and open fires are also not permitted.

karlshaugen-naturreservat-natb93df650.d: Karlshaugen Nature Reserve was originally donated by the landowner Harald Løvenskiold to the Eastern Norway branch of the National Association for Nature Conservation in Norway (now the Norwegian Society for Nature Conservation). The area generally has very shallow topsoil, overlying a bedrock of syenite. The vegetation types are very sparse, dominated by blueberry spruce forest, with some heather and bilberry pine forest. The area is relatively untouched, but there are some old traces of logging.

kongsrudtjern-naturreservat-natf5d4dfee.d: Kongsrudtjern Nature Reserve is situated on the ridge between the Glomma and Leira rivers in Lillestrøm municipality. The terrain ranges from 148 to approximately 230 metres above sea level. Kongsrudtjernet itself is shallow and lies at the lowest point in a marsh-covered valley floor surrounded by steep mountain walls, in the centre of the reserve. Following the establishment of a beaver lodge at the outlet just outside the reserve to the south, the lake has risen and spread out into the surrounding marshlands. The area is a well-known zoological site, home to five species of amphibians and a rich insect life, particularly in terms of dragonflies. In the north-west, Breimosen and Breimosetjern constitute a valuable habitat for the great crested newt. The area is exceptionally varied and features an unusually wide range of vegetation types.

m-rkgonga-naturreservat-nat7b8b6f1e.d: Mørkgonga Nature Reserve (approximately 1,539 daa) is a nature reserve situated on the steep slope along the Krokskog Plateau down towards Steinsfjorden in Buskerud. A little way to the north of the reserve, just west of Gyrihaugen, lies Mørkgonga itself, a ‘gjell’ – that is, a distinct fissure in the lava plateau covering Krokskogen. The reserve, covering 1,564.9 daa (as per the map), was established on 7 December 2001 and consists of deciduous and coniferous woodland in gorges and on steep slopes. The Norwegian Mapping Authority uses the spelling ‘Mørkganga’. The majority of the nature reserve lies within Ringerike municipality, but a small part also extends into Hole municipality. The area features well-developed deciduous forest (elm and lime forest), aspen forest and interesting rock vegetation.

oppkuven-smeddalen-naturreservat-nat32a7.d: The Oppkuven-Smeddalen Nature Reserve was established on 23 June 1995 and is situated in Krokskogen, in the municipality of Ringerike. Oppkuven (704 metres above sea level) is one of the highest peaks in the Oslomarka. The summit area is gently undulating, featuring hillocks, bogs and small ponds. Smeddalen cuts into the Oppkuven massif as a narrow rift valley from the east-north-east. The forest is dominated by large, old spruce trees. The area probably contains the forest landscape most closely resembling primeval forest in the whole of Marka. The so-called ‘Gamla’ on Oppkuven is one of Norway’s oldest living spruce trees, estimated to be as much as 458 years old (2003). The tree is now dead and is thought to have been so since around 2012. When it was discovered in 1994, the tree was believed to be the oldest spruce in the Nordic region (Rolstad et al.

tverrbergkastet-naturreservat-nat3fb9641.d: Tverrbergkastet Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern side of Holsfjorden, north-east of Lier, between the fjord and County Road 285. The terrain is quite steep, so the topsoil is sparse. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a coniferous forest area that has been little affected by human intervention. The vegetation consists of a species-rich low-herb spruce forest, including marsh marigold. Along the river in Djupdalen, in the southern part of the area, there is a deciduous forest of the elm-lime type. In the driest areas, there is low-growing pine forest. Cycling is not permitted off existing roads, and open fires are prohibited all year round.

asd-ljuvet-naturreservat-nat7ad5d8db.d: Asdøljuvet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lier municipality in Buskerud. It consists of Asdøljuvet and a strip of woodland on either side of it, on valley slopes up to 120 metres high. The purpose of its protected status is to preserve the geological features and plant communities found in the gorge. The landscape and natural environment are distinctive and, in addition to interesting geology, feature special types of vegetation including deciduous broad-leaved woodland and ravine vegetation – including rare species – as well as tall spruce forest on the shaded side. The area was established as a nature reserve on 7 December 2001 and covers an area of 401 daa. The reserve is situated approximately two kilometres south of Sylling and is accessible from the car park on County Road 285.

brumundsj-en-harasj-myra-naturreservat-n.d: The Brumundsjøen-Harasjømyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in the municipalities of Ringsaker and Hamar in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 1981 as the Brumundsjøen Nature Reserve ‘to protect the vegetation, the distinctive and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area’.

vesle-rokosj-en-naturreservat-nat6da8087.d: The Vesle Rokosjøen Nature Reserve comprises an area around Lake Rokosjøen and Mount Rokoberget in Løten municipality, on the border with – and just across the border into – Elverum municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 18 December 1981. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. Motorised traffic is prohibited. Camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography are prohibited. County Road 1848 crosses the nature reserve, and traffic is nevertheless permitted there. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area and to protect the vegetation, the particularly rich and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’ The vegetation consists of woodland and wetlands.

tanarkj-len-naturreservat-natdfe2f830.d: Tanarkjølen Nature Reserve is a wetland area to the west of the northern end of Lake Osensjøen in Åmot municipality. The area comprises various types of bog, including both precipitation bogs and groundwater bogs. The most common type is the eccentric precipitation bog. Among the groundwater bogs, one finds, amongst others, string bogs, flat bogs and gently sloping hill bogs. The vegetation is mostly dominated by undemanding species. However, in the northernmost part of the area, there are also species with more demanding habitat requirements. The critically endangered bird, the four-spotted sparrow, has been recorded in the area. In addition, one can find cranes, lapwings, common snipes, curlews, green sandpipers, dunlins, green-winged teals, yellow wagtails and reed buntings. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction.

klekkefjellet-naturreservat-nat81c46320.d: Klekkefjellet Nature Reserve is situated east of Budor, in the north of Løten municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 1993 ‘to preserve a relatively undisturbed coniferous forest area that provides a good cross-section of forest communities and mire types’. The forest is a typical subalpine coniferous forest with sparse tree cover, and the trees grow slowly. A 260-year-old spruce and a 390-year-old pine have been found in the area.

strykenasen-naturreservat-nate7b2fd56.d: Strykenåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated south-east of Mjøndalen and the E134 in Drammen municipality. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve coniferous forest on calcareous soil, which is home to a very rich and rare flora of vascular plants. The bedrock in the area consists of biotite granite and calcareous rocks. The vegetation comprises coniferous and deciduous trees, including weeping birch, maple, ash, lime, oak, hazel, aspen, willow, grey alder and rowan. Strykenåsen Nature Reserve was established on 13 December 2002 and covers an area of 2,084.2 dekar, situated at altitudes ranging from 80 to 350 metres above sea level.

barmen-naturreservat-nat1b00e60a.d: The Barmen Nature Reserve encompasses the wooded areas surrounding the Jonsknuten mountain peak in Kongsberg municipality. The reserve was established in 2005 and covers 15.5 km². The aim is to preserve an area that has been little affected by recent human activity, although there are also areas characterised by mining from earlier times. There is a predominance of poor vegetation types, but there are also patches of species-rich herbaceous flora.

solbergfjellet-naturreservat-nata56ed817.d: Solbergfjellet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Drammen municipality. It consists of rocky terrain and scree in the upper sections, with a few pine trees, and pine forest and mixed coniferous forest. The summit of the ridge lies at approximately 400 metres above sea level, and the south-facing rock face drops more or less vertically for a couple of hundred metres to where the terrain begins to level out around the settlement at Solbergelva. Solbergfjellet Nature Reserve was established in 1993 and covers an area of 690 dekar. Ten rare (Red Listed) vascular plants and eight species of fungi have been found there. At the time of its designation, the reserve contained the country’s largest populations of the red helleborine. However, the presence of the fly orchid also gives the reserve national significance.

s-terasen-naturreservat-natd58b863f.d: The Sæteråsen Nature Reserve was established in 1993 and revised in 2018. Sæteråsen was the first coniferous forest reserve in Vestfold. The nature reserve features a rich spruce forest that has been little affected by logging in recent times. In the autumn of 1986, the Ministry of the Environment set up a coniferous forest committee. The committee was tasked with drawing up the main guidelines for coniferous forest conservation work in Norway. This ultimately led to the creation of conservation plans for each region of the country. In 1991, Sæteråsen was given the highest priority in the conservation plan for coniferous forests in Eastern Norway. Two years later, the area was designated a nature reserve. The Sæteråsen Nature Reserve is owned by the state.

bremsasen-naturreservat-natda0fe726.d: Bremsåsen Nature Reserve is situated four kilometres south of Mjøndalen town centre in Drammen municipality. The ground in the area consists mainly of silty shale, calcareous mudstone (a massive, non-shaly sedimentary rock comprising roughly equal amounts of silt- and clay-sized particles) and smaller areas of ekerite. The vegetation in the area consists mainly of coniferous forest and bog. The reserve was originally established in 1986 with an area of 260 dekar; in 2002, it was extended to 876 dekar. Twenty-one Red List species have been recorded in the reserve: 11 vascular plants, 6 fungi, 2 tree species and 2 bird species.

ullebergasen-naturreservat-nat543446bc.d: Ullebergåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve south of Kongsberg that was designated on 24 April 1992. Ullebergåsen comprises a well-developed ridge of Ordovician limestone, approximately 2 km north-east of Lande on County Road 40. The area consists of continuous, lush herb- and grass-rich limestone pine forest, with particularly rich vegetation on the eastern slopes. The undergrowth features a very significant number of orchids.

marifjell-naturreservat-natbb46d3f4.d: The Marifjell Nature Reserve comprises an area to the west of Lake Hurdalssjøen in the municipalities of Gran and Nannestad. The area was designated a protected area on 19 December 2008 and is included in the forest conservation plan.
