The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large area of remaining old-growth forest with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems and species, as well as the area’s natural ecological processes. The area comprises forest with typical mountain forest characteristics and smaller areas of swamp forest and nutrient-rich forest types. The area is of particular scientific and educational significance as an example of this type of boreal taiga element in Eastern Norway. The area is unique in terms of its size and unspoilt nature.”

gullenhaugen-naturreservat-natc7c87952.d: The Gullenhaugen Nature Reserve is situated in the south-east of Gran municipality, on the ridge between Hadeland and Hurdal. The reserve covers a fairly large area of spruce forest comprising trees of all ages and stages of decomposition (continuum forest), with a significant proportion of large living and dead trees. There are large populations of rare and endangered bryophytes here.

rinilhaugen-naturreservat-nat65d6308b.d: Rinilhaugen Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern shore of Langvatnet, east of Grua in Lunner municipality. The vegetation consists of blueberry spruce forest. The forest is largely unspoilt and otherwise typical of the region. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but it is permitted to pick edible mushrooms and berries.

sandtjern-naturreservat-nat50647757.d: Sandtjern Nature Reserve is situated just off European Route 6, east of Mogreina in Ullensaker. The reserve is mainly forested and encompasses Sandtjern and Nordkulpen. The ponds are situated in separate kettle holes and form part of a system of kettle-hole lakes and protected areas on the Hauersetertrinnet plateau. Both lakes have inflowing streams but no outflows. In Nordkulpen, there is a healthy population of the rare and Red Listed pale violet.

kulpasen-naturreservat-nat517f02b0.d: Kulpåsen Nature Reserve (360 daa) preserves a rich and damp coniferous forest and a population of the lichen ‘huldrestry’; it was established on 9 July 1993 and is a small ridge between Løvlia and Gyrihaugen in Krokskogen, situated in Ringerike municipality. The area contains a rich and moist spruce forest. There is also a relatively large population of the lichen ‘huldrestry’ within the reserve. Kulpåsen is situated in an important outdoor recreation area.

svenskestutjern-naturreservat-nat21dfbda.d: The Svenskestutjern Nature Reserve is situated east of Trondheimsveien, near the Jessheim nursing home in Ullensaker. The area comprises Svenskestutjern and Bonntjern, along with adjacent woodland and marshland. Both lakes lie in separate kettle holes, but whilst the water level in Bonntjern follows the groundwater level, Svenskestutjern is influenced solely by precipitation and is very nutrient-poor. Svenskestutjern is considered to be of international conservation importance. Bonntjern is naturally nutrient-rich. In recent years, there has been considerable variation in the water level here, with the result that the submerged vegetation, including the Red Listed ‘blanktjønnaks’, has disappeared.

holtnesdalen-naturreservat-nat09005608.d: Holtnesdalen is a ravine valley between Holmsbu and Rødtangen, by the Drammensfjord in the south-west of Hurumlandet in Asker municipality. Over time, a small stream with many tributaries has carved out deep, dark valley troughs in the clay soil, with ferns and deciduous woodland on the clay and coniferous woodland on the outcrops of Drammen granite. The entire valley, covering 262 dekar, was designated a nature reserve in 1974, with an extension in 2007. The nature reserve was established to protect an important area of broad-leaved forest, where all Norwegian broad-leaved tree species except beech are found. Here, there are examples of black alder–marsh forest, grey alder–ash forest, grey alder–ash forest and elm–lime forest. Well-developed moss communities are also found in the stream gorges.

lang-ya-naturreservat-nat0dafc3e8.d: The Langøya Nature Reserve on Langøya in Holmestrand was established in 1988. The shells of millions of dead marine animals – from 80 different species – formed Langøya 300 to 400 million years ago. 5,500 years ago, the island emerged from the sea. Today, Langøya provides important insights into the fossil-bearing rocks of the Oslo Field. The island has remnants of a calcareous pine forest and several rare plants. Here we find both the fly orchid and mistletoe, both of which are protected species. More than 300 plant species and 600 butterfly species have been recorded on Langøya. The three-kilometre-long island consists of limestone. The oldest, flat quarries in the north of the island were worked using manual labour and wheelbarrows. These are now in the process of regaining their natural vegetation.

ertsvikskj-r-naturreservat-nat35ea6514.d: Ertsvikskjær Nature Reserve was established on 15 December 1978. It is situated south-east of Ersvika, at the very tip of Hurumlandet, in Asker municipality. The nature reserve encompasses the approximately 10 dekar Ersvikskjæret islet and the sea up to 50 metres from the shore around the islet. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect birdlife. Several different species of gull, eider and mute swan breed on the islet. From 15 April to 15 July, access to the nature reserve is prohibited. The bedrock on the islet consists of gneiss, and the islet has some scattered shrub vegetation. The land area north of the islet is not protected, but just 500 metres further east on the mainland lies the Sandbukta–Østnestangen Nature Reserve.

sandbukta-stnestangen-naturreservat-nat2.d: The Sandbukta-Østnestangen Nature Reserve was established on 14 December 2007. It comprises Østnestangen, Sandbukta to the west of the headland and Steinvika to the west of the headland. The nature reserve is situated on the south coast of Hurumlandet in Asker municipality. The area was protected to preserve a site with a wide variety of vegetation types and special habitat types. The area features a natural gradation from the open sea and well-developed sandy beaches to woodland comprising elements of natural forest, swamp forest and deciduous broad-leaved forest. Several Red List species are found here, and parts of the area are of very high entomological conservation value. The conservation regulations stipulate, amongst other things, that: Open fires and the use of barbecues outside designated areas are prohibited.

solfjellasene-naturreservat-nata56b24e9.d: Solfjellåsene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the south coast of Hurumlandet in Asker municipality. The nature reserve was established on 13 February 2002 and covers an area of 296 dekar. The reserve stretches between Rusodden, east of Rødtangen, and Skjøttelvik, in the south-west of Hurumlandet. The reserve comprises a beach area and a low hill of calcareous Cambrian–Silurian rocks. The beach area is devoid of tree vegetation, whilst further inland there are deciduous broad-leaved forests and calcareous pine forests. The area features herb-rich limestone woodland and a significant proportion of old broad-leaved trees, including many lime trees on limestone-rich soil, as well as stands of black alder coastal woodland. By the sea, there are limestone outcrops with a rich flora and a large number of interesting and rare species.

m-len-naturreservat-nat49c648bb.d: Mølen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve off the coast of Hurumlandet in Asker municipality, comprising the entire island of Mølen. The nature reserve covers an area of 184 dekar and was established on 9 December 1977. Mølen Nature Reserve boasts a rich variety of plant species. This is due to both the warm climate and the calcareous soil. The bedrock on the island is gneiss; the presence of lime in the soil is due to shell sand in marine deposits. There is a great deal of thermophilic deciduous woodland on the island, including elm and lime trees. The island is home to mistletoe and other rare species such as hairy violet and fingered lark’s-spur.

smaskj-r-fuglefredningsomrade-nat9e25e63.d: The Småskjær Bird Sanctuary comprises two islets in the middle of the Oslo Fjord off Drøbak, just south of Oscarsborg, as well as the sea area 50 metres offshore. The islets are a breeding ground for several species of gull and a number of eider ducks. On the southernmost islet, the main breeding species are the lesser black-backed gull and the grey gull, whilst on the northernmost islet, the lesser black-backed gull and the black-headed gull breed. The latter is listed as ‘critically endangered’ (CR) in Norway. The birdlife in the reserve is protected against harm and unnecessary disturbance, and it is prohibited to carry out any activities that impair the birds’ habitat. All access is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving. Furthermore, dogs must always be kept on a lead.

s-ndre-verks-ya-naturreservat-nat318f096.d: The Søndre Verksøya Nature Reserve is situated off the coast of Hurumlandet in Asker municipality. The nature reserve was established on 14 December 2007. Verksøya lies in the Drammensfjord on the eastern side of the Svelvikstrømmen strait, just south of the village of Verket. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an area of salt meadows that are rare in the region, and a distinctive and nationally important insect fauna. The island features meadow vegetation comprising salt-tolerant grass species and herbs. Typical plants in the driest part of the salt marsh include meadow foxtail, sea rocket, yellow bedstraw and field wormwood. Closer to the beach in the south, there are depressions with a somewhat wetter character, featuring species such as cat’s-tail, blue moor-grass and adder’s-tongue. The sandy beach area has a rich and distinctive insect fauna.

gr-nsanddammen-dyrefredningsomrade-nat29.d: The Grønsanddammen wildlife conservation area is situated in the grounds of Grønsand Farm and was previously used as a water source for livestock. The pond is now part of a golf course and is prone to overgrowth. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect a population of great crested newts and smooth newts and their habitat. The newts are protected against collection and harm, and it is not permitted to do anything that could damage their habitat within the conservation area. This includes, amongst other things, new planting, drainage, filling, levelling, fertilisation and other forms of pollution. Furthermore, it is not permitted to light bonfires or barbecues, nor to remove plants or parts of plants from the area.

rambergbukta-naturreservat-nat2f538df8.d: Rambergbukta is a shallow bay on the western side of Jeløya in the Oslo Fjord. The nature reserve encompasses the northern part of the bay, the small islet of Flantorsk, as well as a strip of salt marsh and some woodland along the shore. The highest point rises 4 metres above sea level. The area lies on the migratory route along the Oslofjord and is an important resting area for ducks and waders. It is also an important breeding ground for waders and passerines. A large part of the area is exposed at low tide. The flora of the salt marshes has, since time immemorial, developed in conjunction with grazing by livestock. When livestock farming ceased, the marshes began to become overgrown. Grazing is now in the process of being reintroduced in the area.

tofteskogen-naturreservat-nat33cc567b.d: Tofteskogen Nature Reserve is situated in Hurummarka on the Hurum peninsula in Asker municipality. The nature reserve was established on 9 July 1993 as the Østre Askedalen Nature Reserve. On 10 June 2005, it was significantly expanded and renamed Tofteskogen Nature Reserve. In 2020, the nature reserve was further expanded towards the west. The nature reserve covers an area of 2,970 dekar between Stikkvannskollen in the north and Langvann in the south. It features old coastal coniferous forest (particularly spruce forest) and varied mixed woodland, with very important stands of yew and winter oak. The nature reserve is situated right in the heart of Hurumlandet. In the late 1980s and early 1990s, there were plans to build a new main airport for Eastern Norway in the area.

fuglevik-naturreservat-nat3cc3a566.d: Fuglevik Nature Reserve is a small reserve just north of Rambergåsen Nature Reserve, in the centre of Jeløya in Moss municipality. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry at the top and sandstone below. In the lower part, the vegetation is characterised by an ash-snelle forest, which is a very rare forest type both in Norway and in the rest of Europe. This forest type grows in areas with abundant groundwater flowing through well-drained soil. The ground layer here contains an abundance of woodrush, as well as both large-flowered lily of the valley and wreath lily of the valley. Further up, there are also bog bilberries, plenty of bluebells and other species. On the flatter area at the top, a pond was previously excavated, where species-rich vegetation has now established itself.

langsetdammen-dyrefredningsomrade-nataf6.d: The Langsetdammen Wildlife Reserve encompasses Langsethdammen near Sætre in Asker, and the surrounding shoreline. The aim is to protect a population of great crested newts and smooth newts. The pond is an artificial reservoir and was originally created as an ice dam. The newts are protected against collection and harm, and it is not permitted to do anything that could damage their habitat within the conservation area. This includes, amongst other things, planting new vegetation, drainage, filling, levelling, fertilising and other forms of pollution. Furthermore, it is not permitted to light bonfires or barbecues, nor to remove plants or parts of plants from the area.

tofteholmen-naturreservat-nat7950f2e7.d: Tofteholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve off the coast of Hurumlandet in Asker municipality. The nature reserve was established on 20 June 1919, as one of the first nature conservation areas in Norway. The island is owned by the Norwegian Society for the Conservation of Nature. The islet lies south of the village of Tofte, in the heart of the Breiangen fjord area in the Outer Oslo Fjord. Together with Ranvikholmen and the island of Mølen, Tofteholmen has the highest average temperature in Norway. The whole of Tofteholmen, covering 118 dekar, is protected to safeguard the island’s flora, fauna and geology. Parts of Tofteholmen consist of the rock type gabbro, as well as sedimentary rocks, which, through weathering, provide good soil for plants. The island has one of the most diverse populations of vascular plants, lichen species and insects in Norway.

storskj-r-naturreservat-nat1b93c1be.d: Storskjær Nature Reserve is situated off the coast of Hurumlandet in the municipality of Asker. It was established on 15 December 1978 and covers an area of 30 dekar. Storskjær is situated in Drøbaksundet in the Oslo Fjord, just east of the village of Storsand and directly south of Oscarsborg Fortress. It is an important breeding ground for grey gulls. Between 15 April and 15 July, access to the islet and the surrounding waters is prohibited. The Oslofjord Tunnel runs directly beneath Storskjær.

haraldsfjellet-naturreservat-nat70601427.d: Haraldsfjellet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on Hurumlandet in Asker municipality. It stretches across the southern half of the Haraldsfjellet ridge and down to the sea at Breiangen, east of Skjøttelvik. The reserve was established on 13 December 2002 and covers an area of 997 dekar. Haraldsfjellet is home to calcareous pine forest and several rare species of vascular plants. Among others, privet, fly orchid, dragon’s head and other relatively rare plant species grow here. There is a path across the mountain. The coastal path along Hurumlandet runs through the reserve right down to the sea.

solbergdammen-dyrefredningsomrade-nat27f.d: The Solbergdammen Wildlife Reserve is situated just north of Solberg Farm, just under three kilometres north of Filtvet in Asker municipality. The area comprises an artificial pond and the surrounding shore zone. The pond was originally used for irrigation in fruit and vegetable production. The aim is to protect a population of great crested newts and smooth newts and their habitat. The newts are protected against collection and harm, and it is not permitted to do anything that could damage their habitat within the conservation area. This includes, amongst other things, new planting, drainage, filling, levelling, fertilisation and other forms of pollution.

veal-s-naturreservat-nat6a6dabfd.d: Vealøs Nature Reserve comprises an area around the islet of Vealøs. It is situated near Tofte on the Hurum peninsula in Asker municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 16 July 2009 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched islet, as well as the adjacent marine areas, with their naturally associated flora and fauna. The area is unique in that it is of particular value as a breeding ground for seabirds. This objective also applies to important, vulnerable and protected botanical species.’

ranvikholmen-naturreservat-natbea1a5d5.d: Ranvikholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve off the coast of Hurumlandet in Asker municipality. The nature reserve was established on 14 December 2007. The islet lies just west of Tofteholmen, south of the village of Tofte, in the part of the Oslo Fjord known as Breiangen. Ranvikholmen, together with Tofteholmen and Mølen, has the highest average temperature in Norway. The whole of Ranvikholmen, covering 80 dekar, is protected to preserve the island’s flora, fauna and geology, as well as its seabird breeding grounds. Parts of the island consist of gabbro, as well as sedimentary rocks, which, when weathered, provide good soil for plants. A colony of harbour seals is found on the Tofteholmen islands, Ranvikholmen and Mølen.

delingsdalen-naturreservat-nat39e560df.d: The Delingsdalen Nature Reserve is situated in the north-west of Nordre Follo municipality, between Bunnefjorden and Gjersjøen. The reserve is dominated by coniferous forest, featuring a variety of forest types such as low-herb spruce forest, tall-shrub spruce forest and rich swamp forest. The area comprises a well-developed old-growth forest with minimal human impact. In addition, the area is widely used for recreational purposes, particularly by residents of Oppegård.

blylagsdammen-dyrefredningsomrade-nate50.d: Blylagsdammen is situated on the eastern side of Nesodden, close to the border with Frogn municipality. The water is dammed up by about five metres at the outlet at the southern end, bringing the lake’s level to 40.5 metres above sea level. The lake was used for ice cutting from the 1870s until 1932. The purpose of the wildlife conservation area is to preserve rare and endangered amphibians such as the great crested newt, the smooth newt and the pointed-snouted frog, as well as rare insects, and the species’ habitats. The pond is also home to the common toad, and both grey herons and tufted ducks have been recorded. In the northern part, the conservation area is crossed by Blylagsveien. A management plan has been drawn up for the pond.

slattmyra-naturreservat-natb3569cf6.d: Slåttmyra Nature Reserve (also known as Slåttemyrene) lies between Movatn and Nittedal station, just south of the Gjøvik Line, in a gently undulating spruce forest area. The bedrock consists of Cambrian–Silurian rocks which are rich in calcium and provide good nutrient conditions. The mires are dominated by rich, and in some cases extremely rich, mire vegetation. The hill mires in particular have a very species-rich and interesting flora. Over 200 different vascular plants have been recorded in the bog, including ten species and three hybrids of orchids. Among these is the bog orchid, one of the few species that is specifically protected in Norway. The hay meadow was used for haymaking and livestock grazing – hence its name – until well into the 1950s.

thors-ma-naturreservat-nat6ad2eaea.d: Thorsøma Nature Reserve comprises a shallow coastal area, including Orebukta and the adjacent beaches on the western side of Tosekilen, in the south-east of Fredrikstad municipality. The flat mudflat is partially exposed at low tide. The area is considered in conjunction with other wetlands around the mouth of the Glomma river and is regarded as one of the most important between the Skjeberg and Øra nature reserves. The vegetation includes, amongst other things, sea rush and common reed marshes, as well as small woodlands of black alder. As of 1986, 59 species of wetland birds had been recorded. The flora and fauna, including dead shrubs and trees, are protected against damage and destruction.

s-ylandsvatnet-naturreservat-nat189e8b72.d: Søylandsvatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hå municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1996 to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site. Søylandsvatnet is of value as a breeding ground for several wetland species, such as the moorhen, coot, black-headed gull, tufted duck, mallard, teal, gadwall and ruff. The lake also has conservation value as a resting and wintering site for whooper swans. The area is one of 22 protected areas forming part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

aholmen-naturreservat-nat930fd7a2.d: Åholmen Nature Reserve is situated in Andøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises the Åholmen headland, south of Å on the eastern side of Andøya. The area covers 1,956 dekar, of which 1,325 dekar is land, 25 dekar is freshwater and 606 dekar is sea. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife. The area is particularly important as a migration route for pink-footed geese and a breeding ground for wetland birds.

ris-ysundet-naturreservat-nat83fd882a.d: Risøysundet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Andøy municipality in Nordland. The reserve was established to ‘preserve an important wetland area with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife. It is particularly important to protect the area’s botanically valuable coastal zones and to safeguard its rich birdlife.’ The nature reserve comprises the north-western part of Risøysundet, as well as a coastal area on Andøya. The area covers 5,043 dekar, of which 860 dekar is land, 290 dekar is freshwater and 3,890 dekar is marine area. The wetland areas in Risøysundet constitute one of the most important elements of Andøya’s wetland system.

s-rmela-naturreservat-nat3f8e1b10.d: Sørmela Nature Reserve is situated on the southern part of the western side of Andøya in Nordland. The nature reserve lies north of Sørmela, on the western side of Andøya. The area covers 1,317 dekar, of which 570 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect one of the largest and best-developed sand dune systems in Nordland, which is considerably larger than any system in, for example, Trøndelag and Troms.

bleikmorenen-naturreservat-nat867fe013.d: Bleikmorenen Nature Reserve is situated just south-west of Bleik in Andøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers 1,235 dekar. The area has been designated a protected area to safeguard a site of great Quaternary geological value.

hundholmen-naturreservat-nat56204ab4.d: Hundholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Værøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve consists of a group of islets on the east side of Værøya. The area covers 464 dekar, of which 380 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds.

oddan-naturreservat-natef82da7e.d: Oddan Nature Reserve is situated at Sørvågen in Moskenes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 28 dekar, of which 12 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a protected area to safeguard a significant breeding colony of black-legged kittiwakes.

oks-naturreservat-natc0d012a6.d: Oksø Nature Reserve comprises an area near Oksøy Lighthouse in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. There is a ban on access to the reserve from 15 April to 15 July inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

tverrelvdalen-naturreservat-nate1d4c47c.d: Tverrelvdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Alta. The reserve covers an area of 2.382 km² on the eastern side of the lower part of the Tverrelvdalen valley, in Borraslia between Lille-Borras and Borras. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a forested area with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes. Among its special features is the large proportion of dwarf pine forest in the area.

vassbotndalen-naturreservat-natd64cedb7.d: Vassbotndalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Alta. The reserve covers an area of 1.459 km² at the bottom of the Vassbotn Valley, south of Storvatnet in Talvik. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a rich deciduous forest area, featuring a large, lush and largely unspoilt grey alder forest.

nordre-pollen-naturreservat-nat5b44dd41.d: The Nordre Pollen Nature Reserve is situated north of Lake Pollevannet in Ås municipality, Akershus. The reserve was established in 2005 and represents a classic type of coastal coniferous forest on the Oslofjord. Nevertheless, there is great diversity, with low-growing pine forest, mixed coniferous and heathland forest, blueberry spruce forest and rich low-herb spruce forest, as well as elements of other forest types. Close by lies the Pollen Nature Reserve, with its deciduous broad-leaved forest, which was designated a protected area in 1982.

pollen-naturreservat-nat66ecdac4.d: Pollen Nature Reserve is a steep, west-facing slope at the northern end of Lake Pollevannet in Ås municipality. The vegetation consists of deciduous broad-leaved woodland of the elm-lime and grey alder-ash types, with ash being the dominant tree species. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. The vegetation is protected from destruction, including dead trees and shrubs. However, picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Motorised traffic is prohibited.

rullestadtjern-naturreservat-nat1619c729.d: Rullestadtjernet is situated in Nordre Follo municipality in Akershus, north-east of the town of Ski. The lake is nutrient-rich with lush marsh vegetation and is an important habitat for waterbirds. Together with the surrounding marshlands, the lake was designated a nature reserve in 1992. The reserve is used as an educational area for local schools, but access is prohibited from 1 April to 30 September.

stensj-vann-naturreservat-nat77087a1f.d: Østensjøvannet is a lake situated between the farms of Holstad and Østensjø in the far east of Ås municipality in Akershus, close to the border with Nordre Follo municipality. The lake is also known as Holstadvannet, and lies 89 metres above sea level. The area is an important wetland and was designated a nature reserve in 1992. Apart from the shoreline along the E18, access to the area is prohibited from 1 April to 30 September. The lake is very nutrient-rich and has a rich and varied range of shoreline and aquatic vegetation. The lake drains westwards via Bølstadbekken (which further downstream becomes Syverudbekken) into Årungen, and therefore also affects the water quality in Årungen.

jakobsholmen-lilleholmen-og-rundholmen-n.d: The Jakobsholmen, Lilleholmen and Rundholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Farsund municipality. It consists of three islets off Spindslandet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 2 October 1981. The reserve is part of the seabird conservation plan. Camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography are prohibited, and from 15 April to 15 July inclusive, all access is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is “to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.”

nesheimvann-naturreservat-nat2a900e05.d: Nesheimvann Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1988 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the protected area is to preserve a wetland of international importance. Nesheimsvannet may be the most important lake in the context of wetlands in Southern Norway, particularly as a resting and feeding area for migratory birds during the spring and autumn migrations. The lake is shallow and nutrient-rich, and at its northern end there is a large marsh area. A total of 195 bird species and 5 subspecies have been recorded in the area: geese, ducks and waders. The lake rarely freezes over and is therefore used for wintering by, for example,

rauna-naturreservat-nat3c03582d.d: Rauna Nature Reserve comprises the island of Rauna, south of Vanse in Farsund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

r-yrtj-nn-naturreservat-natce35a323.d: Røyrtjønn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Farsund municipality in Agder. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1988 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve an important wetland area with a rich and distinctive birdlife. Røyrtjønn lies just within the Lomsesanden beach area and is a partially overgrown and highly nutrient-rich lake. The overgrowth has created a fen of national conservation value, with occurrences of rare marsh plants. The pond is a breeding ground for, amongst others, warblers and ruffs, and serves as both a wintering and stopover site for starlings during migration. A total of 88 bird species have been recorded here, 27 of which are wetland birds.

skydskj-r-naturreservat-nata368c475.d: Skydskjær Nature Reserve consists of a skerry situated close to the town of Farsund in Farsund municipality. ferkingstad-yene-naturreservat-nat688f52.d: The Ferkingstadøyene Nature Reserve consists of a group of islands and the sea within a 1 km radius around the islands, west of Karmøy in Karmøy municipality. vre-eide-naturreservat-nat93395816.d: The Øvre Eide Nature Reserve is a protected flat bog, west of Kopervik in Karmøy municipality. The protected area extends eastwards from Nordre Brekkevann and curves upwards towards Øvre Eidevegen, where it also widens out. The nature reserve was designated in 1986 on the grounds that the area is particularly diverse, with a wide range of special species.

naut-y-longholmen-og-bukkholmen-naturres.d: The Nautøy, Longholmen and Bukkholmen Nature Reserve comprises the island of Nautøya in Bokn municipality and the islets of Longholmen and Bukkholmen in Tysvær municipality. heglane-naturreservat-natc147a829.d: The Heglane Nature Reserve comprises Austre and Vestre Imsen, Kvitholmen and Higgelen, and the surrounding area. nord-talgje-naturreservat-nat5fc1d955.d: Nord-Talgje Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Finnøy municipality in Rogaland, which was established on 26 November 2004. The nature reserve covers a total area of 2.11 square kilometres, of which 1.24 square kilometres is marine area. The area comprises a distinctive coastal landscape and boasts an unusually rich variety of plant species.

norheims-y-og-lamholmen-naturreservat-na.d: The Norheimsøy and Lamholmen Nature Reserve consists of two islets in Nedstrandsfjorden in Stavanger municipality. kattholmen-naturreservat-nat35dcbc7b.d: Kattholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet situated between the islands of Halsnøya and Bokn in Stavanger municipality. kje-y-naturreservat-nat737be8ae.d: Kjeøy Nature Reserve comprises the islet of Hidlekjeøya in Hidlefjorden, in the municipality of Strand. The area was designated a protected area on 7 May 1982 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important seabird site with the plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to the seabirds and their breeding grounds.’

kj-rholmane-naturreservat-nat956e68e5.d: The Kjørholmane Nature Reserve is situated on a chain of islets south-west of the island of Rott in Sola municipality. The Kjørholmane Nature Reserve was established by royal decree on 7 May 1982 and is a seabird reserve. Since 2003, the reserve has formed part of the Rott-Håstein-Kjør bird sanctuary, and since 2011 the entire bird sanctuary has also been designated a Ramsar site. This is an important breeding area for seabirds and a habitat for seals, particularly harbour seals. Kjørholmane is home to the largest colony of shags in Norway south of Runde. There are also breeding populations of great cormorants, black guillemots, razorbills, puffins, kittiwakes, guillemots, guillemots and fulmars. There are also colonies of grey gulls, lesser black-backed gulls and black-headed gulls.

kyrkjeskjeret-naturreservat-nat84fe3803.d: The Kyrkjeskjeret Nature Reserve consists of a skerry at the southern end of the island of Fogn in Stavanger municipality. langholmen-larsholmen-og-larsholmskjeret.d: The Langholmen, Larsholmen and Larsholmskjeret Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets north of Idse in Strand municipality. reilstad-grasholmen-naturreservat-natb66.d: Reilstad – Grasholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet off Finnøy in Stavanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 May 1982 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. tade-naturreservat-natb9be89ce.d: Tåde Nature Reserve consists of an islet in the middle of Fognafjorden in Stavanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 May 1982 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important seabird site with the plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to the seabirds and their breeding sites.’

alvevatnet-naturreservat-nat16eac001.d: Alvevatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Klepp municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1996 to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site. Alvevatnet’s most important conservation function is as a breeding ground for various wetland birds, including a large colony of black-headed gulls. The area is one of 22 protected areas that form part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

gausel-naturreservat-nat3287980e.d: Gausel Nature Reserve, also known as Gauselskogen, is a 53 dekar protected area at Gausel in Stavanger. The nature reserve was designated on 21 December 1984 and is situated to the west of National Road 44. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a lush woodland area with a rich variety of birdlife, in an otherwise urban setting. The reserve comprises deciduous woodland, mainly oak, with some elm, birch, beech, hazel and maple. The undergrowth is very abundant. The forest has an exceptionally rich bird life and constitutes an important breeding ground for passerines. The latest records from 2009 show that the breeding population is in sharp decline. Photographs from the late 1800s show that the area was fairly open at that time.

grannesbukta-naturreservat-nat3a53c336.d: Grannesbukta Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sola municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area lies on the eastern side of Hafrsfjorden and was designated a protected area in 1996 to preserve a marine wetland area. The whole of Hafrsfjorden is of international importance as a resting and wintering area for wetland birds. The most important foraging areas consist of large mudflats with intertidal zones, and these are protected under Ramsar status. The area is one of 22 protected areas that form part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

harvalandsvatnet-naturreservat-nat39d9db.d: Harvalandsvatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sola municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1996 to preserve an important breeding, resting and stopover site. The lake is a breeding ground for several species of wetland birds and is important as a stopover and wintering site for whooper swans, Bewick’s swans and mute swans. The area is one of 22 protected areas that form part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

linemyra-naturreservat-nat1965e6c3.d: Linemyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Time, on Jæren in Rogaland. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1996 to preserve an open lowland bog, which is an important breeding ground. The area constitutes a small remnant of the Jæren peat bog which, despite major changes, still has ecological conservation value as an example of a biotope and habitat type that is rapidly disappearing from Jæren. The bog is an important breeding habitat for a great many birds. The area is one of 22 protected areas forming part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

lonavatnet-naturreservat-nat0a064f14.d: Lonavatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Sandnes and Klepp in Jæren, Rogaland. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1996 to preserve an important wintering ground for ducks and whooper swans. Lonavatnet is also an important breeding ground with a dense population of reed warblers, several pairs of mute swans, coots and ducks. The area is one of 22 protected areas that form part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

smokkevatnet-naturreservat-nat098ff58f.d: Smokkevatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Time municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1996 to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site. The lake is a breeding ground for several wetland birds, particularly the common snipe, and serves as a resting and wintering area for ducks. The area features vegetation worthy of protection, including endangered species such as the common sedge and soft sea-grass. Due to its importance for migratory birds, the area is one of 22 protected areas forming part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

strandnesvagen-naturreservat-nat75a7a496.d: Strandnesvågen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sola municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area is situated on the western side of Hafrsfjorden and was designated a protected area in 1996 to preserve an important migration and wintering site. The whole of Hafrsfjorden is of international importance as a resting and wintering area for wetland birds. The most important foraging areas consist of large mudflats with intertidal zones, and these are protected under Ramsar status. The area is one of 22 protected areas forming part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

ksnevadtj-nn-naturreservat-natc37e7bc9.d: Øksnevadtjønn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Klepp municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area was designated a protected area in 1996 as an important breeding ground for wetland birds. The lake and the protected area contain important remnants of bog and heathland, but are of greatest significance as a breeding site for black-headed gulls, nesting mute swans, coots, moorhens, several species of duck and a dense population of reed warblers. The area is one of 22 protected areas that form part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

vollholmen-naturreservat-nat4bee46b6.d: Vollholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet within the Nordre Rennesøy Bird Sanctuary in Stavanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 May 1982 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the area’s birdlife and the birds’ habitats, as well as all plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the reserves.’

myklebustvatnet-naturreservat-nat9f049de.d: Myklebustvatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Herøy municipality. It comprises an area on Bergsøya. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 May 1988. The reserve is included in the wetland conservation plan. From 1 March to 31 October inclusive, all access is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife’. Eight species of breeding ducks, 12 species of waders and many species of small birds have been recorded in the reserve.

heddedalane-naturreservat-nat1f2b635c.d: Heddedalane Nature Reserve is a forested area situated on the northern side of Bandak at an altitude of between 72 and 800 metres above sea level. The area is characterised by steep slopes on soil rich in basaltic rock. The flora is unusually rich, with several rare species and a significant presence of thermophilic plants such as wood sorrel, wood green-eye, lily of the valley, red helleborine and white wood anemone.

storsteinfjell-naturreservat-natc40dfb1e.d: Storskog Nature Reserve is a wooded area situated below Raudbergnuten on the north side of Bandak. The area is of particular educational and scientific value as a specialised site for studying how vegetation regrows and changes following a forest fire. Storskog is unique in that it features natural forest with a wide variety of forest types and productivity levels at an altitude of nearly 900 metres above sea level.

gaupesteinmarka-naturreservat-nata340500.d: Gaupesteinmarka Nature Reserve is situated approximately 5 km east of the town of Ski, south of County Road 154 and west of County Road 120. The area takes its name from a huge rock situated at the crossroads right on the border between the municipalities of Nordre Follo, Enebakk and Indre Østfold. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a large and relatively undisturbed area of forest and landscape, representing poor to moderately rich forest types with spruce and pine in low-lying areas above the marine limit in the bedrock region of south-eastern Norway. The area is characterised by barren pine ridges with poor low-pine forest and heather-blueberry forest.

godmatdalen-naturreservat-natef2daa1b.d: The Godmatdalen Nature Reserve comprises an area within the Vassfaret and Vidalen Landscape Conservation Area in the municipality of Sør-Aurdal. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 June 1985 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve typical high-altitude coniferous forest slopes that are of particular importance to wildlife.’

gr-nknuten-naturreservat-nat83e9e68b.d: The Grønknuten Nature Reserve (11,707 daa) consists of a high-altitude coniferous forest area with an unspoilt character; it was established on 9 July 1993 and amended by Royal Decree 14 February 2014 pursuant to Section 34 of the Act of 19 June 2009 No. 100 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The nature reserve is situated in Holleia, on the border between the municipalities of Modum and Ringerike in Buskerud. The managing authority is the County Governor of Buskerud.

haverstingen-naturreservat-nat89713ff0.d: Haverstingen Nature Reserve is a 2,572 dekar forest area situated in the municipalities of Ringerike, Flå and Krødsherad in Buskerud County; it was designated a protected area by Royal Decree of 10 June 2005 and subsequently revised. New regulations were laid down by Royal Decree 16 December 2011 pursuant to the Act of 19 June 2009 No. 100 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), Section 34, cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of the Environment. Amended by Regulations No. 284 of 15 March 2013 (in force from 1 July 2013) and No. 1069 of 4 August 2014. The purpose of establishing the Haverstingen Nature Reserve is to preserve a forested area as an ecosystem, including all its natural flora and fauna.

hestebrennajuvet-naturreservat-nat231c63.d: The Hestebrennajuvet Nature Reserve, also known as the Hestbrennjuvet Nature Reserve (approximately 2,222 daa), was established by Royal Decree 16 December 2016 pursuant to Section 34 of the Act of 19 June 2009 No. 100 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and the Environment. The area was extended on 23 June 2026. The nature reserve is intended to protect an area of old-growth forest undergoing natural forest dynamics. Its conservation values are linked, amongst other things, to old spruce and aspen forests, and the area has great potential for biodiversity. The Hestebrennajuvet Nature Reserve is situated at Hestebrenna in the Ådalsfjellene mountains, not far from Tjuvenborgen.

middagsknatten-naturreservat-nata0973656.d: The Middagsknatten Nature Reserve comprises an area within the Vassfaret and Vidalen Landscape Conservation Area in Sør-Aurdal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 June 1985 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve typical high-altitude coniferous forest slopes that are of particular importance to wildlife.’

ramberget-naturreservat-nat20f96b48.d: Ramberget Nature Reserve (2,150 daa) is a distinct hilly area rising towards Ramberget, on the western side of Sperillen in Vestre Ådal and approximately 5 km south of Nes in Ådal, in Ringerike municipality in Buskerud. The altitude varies between 150 and 542 metres above sea level. There are few traces of past logging, and some areas have the character of primeval forest. The reserve was established by Royal Decree of 9 July 1993 and is intended to preserve a coniferous forest area covering a wide range of altitudes, with a broad spectrum of vegetation communities. The site contains a rich altitudinal gradient of coniferous forest, some of which is of high quality, ranging from 150 to 480 metres above sea level. The uppermost sections consist of stunted pine forest vegetation.

ramfoss-naturreservat-natb842a724.d: Ramfoss Nature Reserve is situated on the west bank of the Snarumselva river, near Ramfoss power station, in the north-west of Modum municipality, Buskerud. The reserve was established in 2002 to preserve a highly productive forest area on gravel deposits and a rich flora of endangered lichen species. In June 2023, the reserve was extended to include an area to the south along the river.

s-ndre-dyttholknatten-naturreservat-nat6.d: The Søndre Dyttholknatten Nature Reserve comprises an area within the Vassfaret and Vidalen Landscape Conservation Area in the municipality of Sør-Aurdal. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 June 1985 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve typical high-altitude coniferous forest slopes that are of particular importance to wildlife.’

tretjerna-naturreservat-nat2429a1ef.d: Tretjerna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Søndre Land municipality. The area was designated on 21 December 2007 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a relatively undisturbed forest area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area is of particular importance as a natural forest area and as a habitat for many vulnerable fungal species, whilst also fulfilling an important landscape-ecological function.”

hovstjern-naturreservat-nat80914388.d: The Hovstjern Nature Reserve comprises Hovstjern near Gran/Ringstad in Gran municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 12 October 1990 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to demanding and rare migratory and breeding wetland birds.’

igulsrud-naturreservat-natb34a864a.d: Igulsrud Nature Reserve is situated on Igulsrudhaugen, east of Randsfjorden in Jevnaker municipality, between the farms of Igulsrud and Tømmerås. The bedrock in the area consists mainly of limestone and clay shale from the Ordovician period. This gives rise to calcareous soil, providing the basis for demanding vegetation. The forest is a calcareous coniferous forest containing both spruce and pine, and there is a great deal of deadwood. The reserve is home to ten Red Listed species of soil-dwelling fungi, and the rare combination of limestone forest and abundant deadwood is also of great value. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but it is permitted to forage for edible mushrooms and berries. Campfires are not permitted, nor is cycling or horse riding.

lysen-naturreservat-nat585c104b.d: The Lysen Nature Reserve comprises an area by Randsfjorden near Brandbu in Gran municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 21 December 2007 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest area with minimal signs of human intervention, together with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area is of particular scientific importance as a habitat for a very interesting and rare fungal flora associated with calcareous coniferous forest, and because it represents exceptionally well-developed examples of rare calcareous coniferous forest types.”

prestegarden-naturreservat-natda257220.d: Prestegarden Nature Reserve is situated on the west bank of the River Leira, below Holter Church and the vicarage, in the south of Nannestad municipality, Akershus. The reserve lies on marine deposits 130–170 metres above sea level and comprises a ravine landscape with deeply incised stream valleys and very lush vegetation.

hyggen-mellom-dyrefredningsomrade-nat284.d: The Hyggen Nature Reserve is situated just above Slettvold Sawmill at Hyggenvika in Asker municipality. The reserve consists of a small pond and the surrounding shore area. The pond was constructed in 1970 for agricultural irrigation purposes. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect a population of great crested newts and smooth newts and their habitat. The newts are protected against collection and harm, and it is not permitted to do anything that could damage their habitat within the conservation area. This includes, amongst other things, new planting, drainage, filling, levelling, fertilisation and other forms of pollution. Furthermore, it is not permitted to light bonfires or barbecues, nor to remove plants or parts of plants from the area.

s-ndre-h-rtekollen-naturreservat-natdbcb.d: The Søndre Hørtekollen Nature Reserve comprises the slope on the south-eastern side of Hørtekollen near Sylling in Lier municipality. The bedrock consists of Cambrian–Silurian rocks, which provide the basis for nutrient-rich landslide soil. A thermophilic deciduous forest of the elm-lime type grows here. Lime is the dominant tree species. The vegetation is protected, including dead trees and shrubs. However, it is permitted to pick berries and edible mushrooms.

braks-ya-naturreservat-nat2923045c.d: Braksøya Nature Reserve is situated in Hole municipality in Buskerud and covers an area of approximately 40 dekar. The nature reserve was designated on 15 January 1988. Braksøya is an island in Steinsfjorden, just east of Garntangen and about 1 km east of the municipal centre, Vik. It is in the coastal zone of the island that the areas of geological conservation value are found. The island consists of shale and limestone from the Silurian period (440–395 million years ago). The bedrock on the island is used as a reference for the entire Silurian strata of the Oslo Field. Of particular interest is the development of so-called spot reef structures. The island also has a limestone pine forest worthy of conservation. A limestone pine forest worthy of conservation can also be found on Braksøya. The island is widely used for outdoor recreation.

gullerudtjern-naturreservat-nata7321680.d: The Gullerudtjern Nature Reserve (257 daa) was established by Royal Decree 13 December 2002 pursuant to the Nature Conservation Act of 19 June 1970 No. 63, Section 8, cf. Sections 10, 21, 22 and 23. Proposed by the Ministry of the Environment. The nature reserve is situated in Gullerudmarka, approximately 5 km south of Hønefoss, in Ringerike municipality, Buskerud. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a forest area as an ecosystem, including all its natural flora and fauna, as well as the associated charophyte lake (Gullerudtjern). Notable features include the fact that this is a calcareous woodland area with a very rich flora of rare and endangered soil-dwelling mycorrhizal fungi. Among other species, the knotted flower grows at the south-western end of the lake.

hurumasen-burudasen-naturreservat-nateaf.d: The Hurum/Burudåsen Nature Reserve (406 daa) preserves a cross-section of the various types of limestone pine forest; it was established on 9 July 1993 and forms a distinct north–south-running limestone ridge (cuesta) east of Steinssletta and is situated in the municipalities of Ringerike and Hole in Buskerud. The ridge is dominated by a relatively herb-rich limestone pine forest with a consistently significant proportion of mosses. There are fragments of calcareous dry grasslands. Burudåsen has one of the most well-developed areas of lichen-dominated calcareous pine forest in Ringerike, particularly at the southern-western end of the ridge. The area is of geological and geomorphological interest and constitutes one of the most characteristic landscape features (questa) in Ringerike.

svenadalen-naturreservat-nat8a5e15fb.d: The Svenådalen Nature Reserve is situated on the steep valley slopes in the lower part of the Svenå Valley, south-east of Hauger/Haugerenga in Jevnaker. The area features a rich variety of lowland forest types and contains dead wood at all stages of decomposition. There are also many vulnerable plant species here. Wildlife and vegetation are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting is also permitted in accordance with other regulations. Motorised traffic is prohibited, with a few exceptions, including the use of the existing road (Svenåveien) through the reserve.

danmark-naturreservat-nat9b01fae5.d: The Danmark Nature Reserve is situated on an east-facing slope just south of Frogn Church in Frogn municipality. The nature reserve covers an area of approximately 18 daa. The land is entirely privately owned. The reserve represents a landscape feature that is in the process of disappearing from today’s cultural landscape. The oak grove is a remaining fragment of former deciduous forests, and its current character is the result of past grazing. The area is probably the best-preserved grazing pasture in the region. The oak trees in the area show a good range of ages, which helps to ensure the continuity of the oak forest. The old oak trees are home to a rich variety of flora and fauna, including wood-dwelling fungi, lichens, birds and insects.

gulltjernmosen-naturreservat-nat7c9e17e1.d: Gulltjernmosen Nature Reserve is situated between Lyseren and Øyeren on the municipal boundary between Enebakk and Spydeberg in Akershus. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a large and varied mire complex where one finds various types of ombrotrophic mires (rainfall mires) and minerogenic mires (groundwater mires), as well as several species of botanical interest.

knardal-naturreservat-nat6601b22a.d: Knardal Nature Reserve is situated on the western side of the slope leading down to the innermost part of Bunnefjorden in Frogn municipality. The purpose of designating Knardal Nature Reserve is to preserve a small, varied area of deciduous broad-leaved forest. Today’s deciduous broad-leaved forest sites are remnant habitats from a previously warmer climate, and the forests also constitute northern outposts of Central European forest types. Norway therefore has the world’s northernmost deciduous broad-leaved forests, but these have been greatly reduced as the areas have been put to other uses. Within a relatively limited area, the vegetation conditions are highly varied. In dry sections at the top of the hillside, elm-lime forests with hawthorn grow.

n-revann-naturreservat-nat1726bc8f.d: Nærevannet is a lake in Nordre Follo municipality in Akershus, east of the town of Ski. It lies 131 metres above sea level and covers an area of 0.63 km². Nærevannet was the main source of water for the town of Ski from 1935 to 1985, and served as a reserve source until 1988, with the resulting restrictions on access to and use of the lake. The vegetation is typical of nutrient-rich lakes in Eastern Norway, and the area was designated a nature reserve in 1992. There is currently no ban on access to the area, but windsurfing is prohibited between 1 April and 1 August. The lake is a popular fishing spot; species found here include pike, perch, roach, bream and rudd.

smihagen-naturreservat-natdba87693.d: Smihagen Nature Reserve is situated on a small ridge between Årungen and Frogn Church in Frogn municipality. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a large area of broad-leaved deciduous forest. Today’s broad-leaved deciduous forest sites are remnant habitats from a previously warmer climate, and the forests also constitute northern outposts of Central European forest types. Norway therefore has the world’s northernmost deciduous broad-leaved forests, but these have been greatly reduced as the areas have been put to other uses. The forest consists mainly of elm-lime forest and grey alder-ash forest with a great deal of maple, ash and elm in the tree layer. The shrub layer consists mainly of ash, hazel and aspen. Oak occurs on well-drained sites and can reach impressive sizes in places.

stenerudmyra-naturreservat-nate710b54d.d: Stenerudmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Indre Østfold in Østfold. The nature reserve is situated along the old municipal boundary between Hobøl and Spydeberg, south-west of Spydeberg Varde. The fen lies on marine deposits within a 3.5 km long depression in the bedrock. The most important conservation values are the fen’s unique hydrology, including the fen lake Stenerudtjernet and the presence of transitional fen. It is likely that cranes nest on the fen.

prinsesseasen-naturreservat-nat652e25f9.d: Hengsåsen is a hill on Bygdøy in the Frogner district of Oslo. It was designated a nature reserve in 2012, and was named the Prinsesseåsen Nature Reserve after Princess Ingrid Alexandra in 2019.

geitungsholmen-naturreservat-nat680230ee.d: The Geitungsholmen Nature Reserve comprises Geitungsholmen in Asker municipality in the Inner Oslo Fjord, as well as the adjacent marine areas. Geitungsholmen lies to the east of Slemmestad town centre and to the east of Slemmestadodden. The protected area on the islet itself covers 6 dekar. The protected marine areas cover approximately 13 dekar around the western part of the islet. The protected area is not registered in the land register for the property.

knerten-naturreservat-nat6fe9992d.d: The Knerten Nature Reserve encompasses the small island of Knerten and the surrounding marine area, within the Steilene archipelago in Nesodden municipality. The bedrock consists of layered limestone and clay shale from the Ordovician period. The highest point on the island is at its northern tip, 8.0 metres above sea level. The purpose of designating the Knerten Nature Reserve is to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites. The island has long been an important breeding site for the grey gull and the black-backed gull. In recent years, there has also been an increase in the numbers of eider ducks and barnacle geese. The conservation regulations stipulate that the reserve comprises ‘the island of Knerten and the adjacent marine areas within a distance of approx.

lille-bjerk-yskj-r-naturreservat-nat0d2a.d: The Lille Bjerkøyskjær Nature Reserve consists of a skerry off Bjerkøya in Asker municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 15 December 1978 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

sundbyholmene-naturreservat-nat307792f5.d: The Sundbyholmene Nature Reserve consists of two large islets and one small one, east of Båtstø and north of Håøya in the Inner Oslo Fjord, in the municipality of Asker. There is a lighthouse on the northern islet. The islets belong to the Sundby farm in Røyken. The conservation area is not registered in the land register for the property, although four other sites belonging to the farm are registered as conservation areas.

skogerholmen-naturreservat-natf09a9e73.d: Skogerholmen Nature Reserve is situated south of Brønnøya in the inner Oslo Fjord. The islet is the type locality for the geological formation which has been named the Skogerholm Formation. This is a layer of sedimentary rocks from the Ordovician period. On Skogerholmen (or Skaueren), the formation is 33.06 metres thick. The terrain on the island alternates between rocky outcrops and depressions where meadow vegetation and shrub and scrub communities are found. A total of 145 vascular plants have been recorded, many of which are characteristic of calcareous grasslands in the inner Oslo Fjord. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected, but hunting and trapping are permitted in accordance with the Wildlife Act.

terneholmen-naturreservat-nata5c174fe.d: Terneholmen Nature Reserve consists of a skerry off Langåra in Asker municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 15 December 1978 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

ulvungene-naturreservat-natd77151e5.d: The Ulvungene Nature Reserve consists of a couple of islets off Nesøya in Asker municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 15 December 1978 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

ulykkesskj-r-naturreservat-nat5ff8e509.d: Ulykkesskjær Nature Reserve consists of a skerry off Nesøya in Asker municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 15 December 1978 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

saltstutlia-naturreservat-natcde180c1.d: Saltstutlia Nature Reserve is situated in Aust-Torpa in Nordre Land, in the Innlandet region. The area is a coniferous forest reserve covering 9,151 dekar, and lies on the eastern shore of Lake Dokkfløyvatnet on the border with the Gausdal state common land. The reserve was designated on 2 September 2005. The purpose of the designation is to preserve a relatively untouched natural area that is quite large and has been little affected by recent logging activities.

endelausmyrene-naturreservat-nat883f985d.d: Endelausmyrene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Ringsaker municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 1981 ‘to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the vegetation, the characteristic and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area’. Endelausmyrene consists of large, open flat bogs with patches of string bogs. The vegetation is largely low-nutrient, with bearded sedge, bottle sedge and dwarf birch as the most common species. Several different species of peat moss grow on the bogs. Together with three other nature reserves, the area was designated a Ramsar site in 2011 under the collective name ‘Hedmarksvidda Wetland System’.

lavsj-myrene-malikj-len-naturreservat-na.d: The Lavsjømyrene-Målikjølen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and a Ramsar site in Målia, in the north of the municipalities of Løten and Hamar in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 2001 ‘to preserve the area in its natural state and as a landscape feature with its associated flora and fauna’. Lavsjømyrene and Målikjølen form a large, intact mire landscape of international conservation value. It consists of string bogs, hill bogs and flat bogs. The mires are home to a particularly rich variety of birdlife. The mires are situated north-west of Nordhue. Together with three other nature reserves, the area was designated a Ramsar site in 2011 under the collective name ‘Hedmarksvidda Wetland System’.

bergesj-en-naturreservat-natc035d2a7.d: Bergesjøen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Elverum municipality in the Innlandet region. The protected area encompasses the entire lake Bergesjøen, the esker situated in the middle of it, and a small area of land to the north-east of the lake. The site was designated a nature reserve on 22 December 1989. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve the unique geology in the form of the esker situated in the middle of the lake. This esker runs the entire length of the lake and almost divides it in two. The landform is highly distinctive and well-defined.

kvannbekken-naturreservat-nat2bf58e7b.d: Kvannbekken Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åmot municipality. It comprises an area to the west of the Glomma river, just north of Rena. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a coniferous forest area and a stream gorge with a great diversity of rich vegetation types within a small area. The area is home to, amongst other things, rare species and species that are close to their northern limit in Hedmark.’ Animals found in the area or passing through it include elk, roe deer, foxes, badgers, hares, squirrels and martens.

r-tkj-len-naturreservat-nat210dbad3.d: Røtkjølen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Elverum municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve is situated in a wetland area in the Ulvå Valley. Approximately 1 kilometre south of Røtkjølen lies the Ulvåkjølen Nature Reserve. Both were established at the same time on 12 December 1981. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve this important wetland area and the particularly interesting birdlife associated with it. The river Ulvåa flows through the south-eastern part of the reserve and is an important habitat for beavers. Approximately half of Lake Graslanddammen lies within the boundaries of the nature reserve. Mammals and birds, as well as their nests and eggs, are protected within the reserve’s boundaries. Hunting is permitted only for hares and deer.

ulvakj-len-naturreservat-nat0ec5cd5e.d: The Ulvåkjølen Nature Reserve is a wetland area situated on both sides of the Ulvåa river in the north-east of Elverum municipality. The bedrock consists largely of nutrient-poor sparagmite, but there are also areas with more nutrient-rich Cambrian–Silurian rocks. Large areas therefore support vegetation comprising species with low to moderate nutrient requirements, but in places there are also more nutrient-demanding plants, such as valerian, meadowsweet, wood cranesbill, bog asphodel and bog bilberry. Along the Ulvåa river runs a belt of birch swamp forest. This is a habitat for beavers. The critically endangered willow bunting has also been recorded here. The marshlands are important as a breeding ground for waders such as the lapwing, common snipe, wood snipe, green sandpiper, common snipe and curlew.

steinsodden-naturreservat-nat5010728e.d: Steinsodden Nature Reserve is situated on a headland on Lake Mjøsa, just south of Moelv in Ringsaker municipality. Its primary purpose is to protect an important site at the very northern end of the Oslo geological field. This is where the so-called Ringsaker Inversion can be seen. During the Caledonian orogeny, the strata were compressed so intensely that they were inverted, with younger strata lying beneath older ones. At Steinsodden, there is an almost complete sequence of strata from the Cambrian and Lower Ordovician. Such continuous stratigraphic sequences are rare in the Oslo Field. The conservation area covers both the geology and the vegetation. The area has varied vegetation, including the red-listed plant species ‘firling’ in a habitat type that is highly endangered (EN).

langodden-naturreservat-nat92a7659c.d: Langodden Nature Reserve is situated on a headland jutting out into Lake Mjøsa, just south of Brumunddal in Ringsaker municipality. The aim is to protect a site that is important for understanding the fossil-bearing rocks of the Oslo Field. Langodden has excellent outcrops, both as rocky shores along the beaches and inland. The southern side of the headland features outcrops of Eocambrian or Cambrian Ringsaker quartzite. This rock is a beach deposit and is rare on a global scale. The rock contains trace fossils and fossilised burrows of various types.

nygardsmyrene-naturreservat-nat57d51d12.d: Nygardsmyrene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Eidskog and Sør-Odal in the Innlandet region. It was designated on 18 December 1981, at which time it was known as the Nygårdsmyra Nature Conservation Area. Following an expansion in November 2016, the reserve covers 4.4 km². The purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the vegetation, the characteristic and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area’.

stimannsberget-naturreservat-nat9f9795e3.d: Stimannsberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Skøyen, Sør-Odal, 12 kilometres south of Skarnes. The reserve is a damp coniferous forest area that was designated on 13 December 2002. It covers 0.4 square kilometres. The purpose of the designation is to preserve the forest area as an ecosystem, including all its natural flora and fauna. Notable features include habitats for lichen species associated with a consistently damp microclimate and, in places, a large amount of dead wood. The State Administrator for Innlandet is the managing authority for the reserve.

lindasmyra-naturreservat-nat4eeaabfe.d: Lindåsmyra Nature Reserve consists of a bog two to three kilometres east of Magnor, along the western bank of the River Veksa near the Swedish border. The reserve is situated in Eidskog municipality. It was designated a nature reserve on 7 December 2001 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The mire is a characteristic eccentric precipitation mire with a well-formed layer structure and edge woodland. The aim of the conservation is to preserve this distinctive landscape feature. The bedrock consists of gneiss, which results in poor soil, but most of the vegetation derives all its water and nutrients from rainfall. Few species can grow on such bogs, but pine trees are found scattered throughout. The bog’s highest point is near the south-western edge, sloping towards the north and east. The bog is divided into three sections, separated by gullies.

s-rkilampi-naturreservat-nat1257a91b.d: Særkilampi Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the Swedish border in the far east of Kongsvinger municipality. The nature reserve covers 4,785 dekar and was designated as such on 9 July 1993. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an area of coniferous forest comprising poor pine forest and moderately rich spruce forest in the southern boreal forest zone. There is also an adjacent nature reserve on the Swedish side of the border. There are traces of past fires here, and controlled burning was probably used as a silvicultural method to encourage the growth of young trees following felling. Following the establishment of the nature reserve, on 17 November 1994 the Norwegian Mapping Authority adopted ‘Særgilamp’ as the official spelling of the lake that gave the nature reserve its name.

gardsj-en-naturreservat-nat276d55ce.d: The Gardsjøen Nature Reserve consists of a meandering lake and a small area of marshland to the south of the lake. The nature reserve is situated south of Kirkenær in Grue municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 18 December 1981. The reserve is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the distinctive landscape features, vegetation, the particularly rich and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’ Gardsjøen is important for migratory birds and is also significant for breeding birds. A total of 137 species have been recorded, including 22 waders and 10 species of duck.

valberget-naturreservat-natb88833b5.d: Vålberget Nature Reserve is situated on a north- and west-facing hillside approximately four kilometres east of Svullrya in Grue municipality. The bedrock consists of gneiss, and the vegetation is dominated by blueberry spruce forest and small-fern spruce forest, with some large-fern spruce forest in places. The forest is relatively even-aged, but there are glens with younger trees. There are also some deciduous trees such as birch, willow, rowan, grey alder and aspen, mostly on the steepest sections. Most of the deadwood is in the early stages of decomposition. The vascular plant flora is unremarkable, but one endangered moss species has been recorded. Among the fungi and lichen species, several indicator species for old-growth forest have also been found.

maliskj-ra-naturreservat-nat9f3a10ee.d: Maliskjæra Nature Reserve is situated on a steep east-facing slope to the west of Lake Rotnesjøen in Grue municipality. The vegetation consists of high-quality coniferous forest, with a distinctive contrast in vegetation types from the base to the top of the slope. Here, there are both blueberry spruce forests and low-herb spruce forests, with patches of large-fern and small-fern spruce forests as well. At the top of the reserve, low-growing pine forest dominates. The trees are generally of a fairly uniform age (200–250 years), and traces of a previous forest fire have been found. The reserve is a habitat for a number of bird species, such as the willow warbler, bullfinch, treecreeper, wren and three-toed woodpecker. And particularly in the lower, more damp parts of the slope, conditions are favourable for several specialised and rare species.

r-nnasmyra-naturreservat-nate9ccad08.d: Rønnåsmyra Nature Reserve is an eccentric raised bog situated between the Glomma river and Lake Hukusjøen in the north-west of Grue municipality. It is one of the few remaining eccentric raised bogs of any size. Most such bogs are now heavily affected by human intervention. The bog is a precipitation bog, where the vegetation is supplied with water solely from rainfall. There are relatively few plant species that can grow on such bogs. The highest point is at the northern edge, and to the south there is a pattern of long ridges or strings running across the direction of the slope. Cowberry, heather, cranberry and bog bilberry grow on these ridges. In the wetter areas between the ridges, we find, amongst other things, bog rush and sundew, as well as several species of peat moss.

vestre-lukashaugen-og-bornoberget-naturr.d: The Vestre Lukashaugen and Bornoberget Nature Reserve is a gently undulating landscape with old-growth forest in Finnskogen, in the east of Grue municipality, just over two mil from Kirkenær. The bedrock consists of quartzite and gneiss, with a layer of loose material of varying thickness. The area contains various types of spruce and pine forest, as well as small bogs and watercourses. The forest has been managed since the Finns began using it in the 17th century, mainly through selective felling and clear-cutting followed by controlled burning.
