The reserve is now a forest landscape characterised by multi-layered, naturally regenerated woodland that has been little affected by modern forestry. The swamp forests are for the most part undrained, but there is little deadwood and litter.

arkj-len-naturreservat-natc2961b00.d: Årkjølen Nature Reserve is situated in the far east of Stange municipality and in the north of Nord-Odal municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 1993 to preserve a high-altitude coniferous forest area that has been little affected by logging. The forest grows on nutrient-poor soil, and there is a great deal of old-growth forest here, featuring both dead trees and fallen timber.

gjesassj-en-naturreservat-natf32024ab.d: Gjesåssjøen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åsnes municipality. It consists of Lake Gjesåssjøen, which lies north of Flisa. The area was designated a nature reserve on 31 May 2002. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. Motorised traffic, camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography or similar purposes are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area and to protect the vegetation, the characteristic and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’ Around 150 bird species have been recorded around Lake Gjesåssjøen. 65 of these are wetland birds. Black-headed Gulls, Coots, Great Crested Grebes and Reed Warblers breed regularly in the nature reserve.

klokken-naturreservat-natecb63b7f.d: Klokken Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åsnes municipality and comprises 550 dekar of wooded area around the Klokken peak, 498 metres above sea level. The reserve was established on 5 March 2010. The summit area consists of multi-aged and slightly multi-layered spruce forest. Two core areas contain old spruce forest, in some places with a great deal of deadwood. On the west-facing slope, areas of even-aged cultivated spruce forest alternate with deciduous-rich mixed forests of aspen and birch. There is considerable variation in the impact of logging within the area. There are a number of nutrient- and heat-demanding vascular plants and fungi within the reserve. Several Red Listed species of fungi and lichens have been recorded, including the chocolate polypore, taiga spiny cap, black-zone polypore and spreading beard lichen.

glorvikmyra-naturreservat-nat572acbc7.d: Glorvikmyra Nature Reserve consists of a bog area in Finnskogen in Åsnes municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 7 December 2001. The reserve is part of the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve, in its natural state and as a landscape feature, a diverse mire complex comprising eccentric flat mires with associated vegetation and fauna.’

kynndalsmyrene-naturreservat-nat361649b4.d: The Kynndalsmyrene Nature Reserve consists of a mire area in Finnskogen in Åsnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 December 2001. The reserve is included in the mire conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve, in its natural state and as a landscape feature, a predominantly ombrotrophic mire complex with special hydrological conditions and associated vegetation, flora comprising rare and threatened species, and fauna.’ Among the bird species recorded are the curlew, the common snipe, the dunlin, the teal, the mallard, the tufted duck, the black-headed gull, the common gull and the yellow wagtail.

kynneggene-naturreservat-nat0919cf04.d: The Kynneggene Nature Reserve is situated on the west bank of the River Flisa, south of its confluence with the River Kynna. The reserve comprises large, well-formed eskers, which form part of a larger esker system between Glorvikmyra and Velta. These are elongated ridges of sand and gravel deposited by rivers beneath the glacier as it melted at the end of the last ice age. The area also features other Quaternary geological landforms and is of natural history value. All activities that affect the natural environment are prohibited, including drainage, the extraction or filling of earth, the construction of buildings, the laying of overhead or underground cables, and the installation of sewer pipes, amongst other things. Motorised traffic is prohibited.

starmoen-naturreservat-natf31f0753.d: Starmoen Nature Reserve is situated along the western side of Starmovegen (county road 2146), south of the Starmoen motor racing circuit in Elverum municipality. The reserve comprises an area of wind-blown sand dunes (drift sand). The pine forest is in the process of recovering following the major forest fire here in June 1976. The vegetation is nevertheless sparse and is covered in places by wind-blown sand. The sand dunes were formed from well-sorted glacial river deposits dating from the end of the last ice age. All activities that affect the natural environment are prohibited, including drainage, the extraction or filling of earth, the construction of buildings, the laying of overhead or underground cables, and the installation of sewer pipes, etc. Motorised traffic is prohibited.

smoldalen-naturreservat-nat97015252.d: Smoldalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Trysil municipality. It comprises an area between Drevdalen and Ljørdalen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 2 September 2005 and extended on 20 December 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited, with the exception of cycling on paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large area of old spruce and pine forest with patches of woodland that are virtually unaffected by logging. b.

bj-rkodden-naturreservat-nat41b56c6a.d: Bjørkodden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Engerdal municipality. It comprises an area by Lake Femunden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 2 September 2005. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a natural forest area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. Notable features of the area include many old pine trees and a good supply of deadwood.’

kvernlia-naturreservat-nat39fb9448.d: The Kvernlia Nature Reserve is situated near Femunden in Os municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 2 September 2005 and is included in the forest conservation plan. It is ‘part of a core area of old-growth pine forest in southern Scandinavia’. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched natural area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. Of particular note are the area’s stands of old pine and deadwood.”

tufsingdeltaet-naturreservat-nat740144a5.d: The Tufsingdeltaet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the Tufsingdalen valley in Os municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 1981 to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the distinctive landscape features, vegetation, the particularly rich and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. The nature reserve lies on both sides of the lower reaches of the River Tufsinga and around its outlet into Lake Femunden, at an altitude of approximately 660 metres above sea level, and has Ramsar site status due to its importance for migratory birds. The river meanders near its mouth, and at the river’s estuary there is a distinctive ‘bird’s foot’ delta with many islands, covered in willow thickets.

bj-reggene-naturreservat-nat59882c3b.d: The Bjøreggene Nature Reserve is situated in the municipalities of Tolga and Os in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve lies on the east bank of the Glomma, from the mouth of the Bjøra river and approximately 3 km southwards. It covers an area of 4,198 dekar, of which approximately 3,900 dekar lies in Tolga and the remainder in Os. The area is protected to preserve a distinctive landscape and a site of natural historical interest featuring important Quaternary geological landforms, including terraces, eskers and kettle holes.

galadalen-naturreservat-nata09f415b.d: Galådalen Nature Reserve is situated in Tolga municipality in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve lies in a side valley of Holøydalen, approximately 20 km south-east of Tolga town centre. It covers an area of 2,956 dekar. The area is protected to preserve an intact mountain valley with hillside bogs, some of which have unusually steep slopes and transition into flat bogs at the valley floor, along with the associated vegetation and fauna.

olafloen-naturreservat-nat5e6db823.d: Olafloen Nature Reserve is situated in Tolga municipality in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve lies to the north of Øvre Tallsjøen. It covers an area of 1,440 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a largely undisturbed, diverse mire ecosystem.

storfloen-naturreservat-natbd95660a.d: The Storfloen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Dalsbygda in Os municipality. The area was designated a protected site on 7 December 2001 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve, in its natural state and as a landscape feature, a large mire complex comprising minerotrophic string mires, mixed string mires, mixed island mires, flat mires and hill mires, and large areas of rich and extremely rich bogs, with associated vegetation and fauna.’ ‘Minerotrophic bogs are bogs or bog vegetation supplied with groundwater that has been in contact with mineral soil.’

storflotj-nna-naturreservat-natbd1b4464.d: The Storflotjønna Nature Reserve comprises an area near Dalsbygda in Os municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 December 2001 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve, in its natural state and as a landscape feature, a largely undisturbed, complex mire area, including palsas and significant areas of extremely rich mire, with associated vegetation and fauna.’

telvanglia-naturreservat-nat888950f4.d: Telvanglia Nature Reserve is situated in Tolga municipality in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve lies at the tree line on the hillside north of Teldalsvola and north-west of Bannarhøa. It covers an area of 1,698 dekar. The area has been protected to preserve a distinctive landscape and an area of natural historical interest featuring important Quaternary geological landforms, including a well-formed esker system.

flensmarka-naturreservat-natf74f334b.d: Flensmarka Nature Reserve is a long, narrow area two to three mil south-east of Røros. The area stretches from the slopes leading up to Stenfjellet, south of Håsjøen, and inland to the western shore of Femunden. Its proximity to Røros suggests that the area and the forest have been subject to long-term human influence, yet there are still many old pine trees here (300–400 years old). In places, there is a great deal of boulder field. The area is representative of the region’s nutrient-poor pine forest and is believed to be the largest, most intact pine forest area near Røros. Both wildlife and vegetation are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting is also permitted in accordance with other regulations.

lille-korssj-en-naturreservat-nat2b0c743.d: The Lille Korssjøen Nature Reserve comprises an area on the border between the municipalities of Røros and Os. The area was designated a protected area on 4 December 1992 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest type comprising old, coarse pine forest on relatively nutrient-rich soil.’

ripan-naturreservat-natd31536a0.d: The Ripan Nature Reserve comprises an area south of Tynset in Tynset municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 2 April 1976. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a well-developed glacial river delta with a number of instructive and scientifically valuable Quaternary geological features such as beach ridges, meltwater channels, dead ice pits, landslide pits and flood moraines.’

stormyra-naturreservat-natdd643575.d: Stormyra Nature Reserve is a varied area of marshland between the Glåma river and the Røros Railway, around five to eight kilometres south-west of Tynset town centre. Large parts of the bog are wooded, and the area features both rich and poor forest bog vegetation, as well as some deciduous woodland towards the Glåma river. Both the three-leaved sedge and the Finnmark sedge have been recorded here; both are rare in southern Norway and are listed as ‘near threatened’ (NT) on the Red List. The area is an important breeding site for a large number of bird species, including the crane and the short-eared owl.

s-rsj-en-naturreservat-natc5975521.d: The Sørsjøen Nature Reserve comprises an area south of National Road 3 at Nytrøa in Tynset municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 18 December 1981 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the vegetation, the characteristic and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’ Bird species found in the area include the Eurasian wigeon, lapwing, redshank, green sandpiper and common snipe.

vardmoan-naturreservat-nat192c19f6.d: Vardmoan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Alvdal municipality. It comprises an area to the west of the village of Alvdal. The area was designated a nature reserve on 22 December 1989. The reserve forms part of the conservation plan for Quaternary geology. Motorised traffic is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a distinctive landscape and an area of natural historical interest with important Quaternary geological features, including large and well-formed terraces at various elevations.’

frekmyr-naturreservat-nat358e8169.d: Frekmyr Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Folldal municipality. It is situated near Rondane National Park on the watershed between the rivers Grimse and Atna, and is protected to preserve the landscape as it was formed by the melting of the ice. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a distinctive landscape and an area of natural historical interest with important Quaternary geological features, including eskers, terraces and kettle holes.’ County Road 27 runs through the nature reserve from Stadsbuøyen, southwards to the southern boundary of the reserve, and a few kilometres north of Stadsbuøyen to Fisketjønne in the north. Apart from the county road, motorised traffic is not permitted, with exceptions including driving on snow or ice.

grimsmoen-naturreservat-nat22c7ed11.d: Grimsmoen in Folldal is the largest deposit of unconsolidated sediment in inland Norway. The massive layers of sand and gravel were deposited whilst the area lay at the bottom of a glacial lake. During the last glacial period, the glacier drained water northwards through Atndalen towards Folldal, and in the process, eskers, drainage channels, moraine ridges and dead ice pits were formed here, indicating the pathways along which the material was transported. On top of the sand deposit, one can see, amongst other things, sand dunes formed when fine-grained, dry sand is carried by the wind and deposited into dunes in the same way as in a desert. This is because the sediments at the top of the deposit were very fine-grained. This sediment was blown into dunes shortly after deglaciation.

langmyra-naturreservat-natab1dbc56.d: Langmyra Nature Reserve comprises an area in Tylldalen on the border between the municipalities of Rendalen and Tynset. The area was designated a nature reserve on 18 December 1981 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve, in its original state, a mire complex with interesting mire structures (eccentric raised bog elements, a forest edge zone and lagg) and an interesting vegetation zonation with various swamp forest communities between open bog and firm ground’.”

nekmyrene-naturreservat-natffa4d583.d: Nekmyrene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rendalen municipality. It consists of a mountainous area dominated by marshes in the north of the municipality, at an altitude of 880 to 940 metres above sea level. The area was designated a nature reserve on 18 December 1981. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the vegetation, the rich and interesting birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’ The marshlands constitute an important breeding ground for wetland birds. Ten species of duck and 13 species of waders have been recorded within the area.

hesjemarka-naturreservat-nat48351d01.d: Hesjemarka Nature Reserve consists of a bog area near Sollia Church, on the southern side of the Finnsjøvola mountain in Stor-Elvdal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 7 December 2001. The reserve is part of the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve, in its natural state and as a landscape feature, an area dominated by rich and extremely rich hill mires, with associated vegetation and fauna.’ Bird species observed breeding in the reserve include the golden plover, the common snipe, the yellow wagtail, the bluethroat, the reed bunting and the short-eared owl.

osdalen-naturreservat-nata1a7eb3d.d: Osdalen Nature Reserve is situated at the very top of Osdalen in the east of Rendalen municipality, near the border with Engerdal, south of Grøndalen. The area features well-developed roge moraines, which are distinctive Quaternary geological landforms. These are irregular ridges deposited across the direction of ice flow and the course of the watercourse. The area, which is largely quite flat, is characterised by marshy areas interspersed with moraine ridges and small ponds. This makes the area a relatively important breeding ground for a number of wetland birds. Species found here include the common snipe, the little curlew and the yellow wagtail, as well as the common sandpiper, the green sandpiper and several species of duck.

osdalssj-h-gda-naturreservat-nat7f5abc71.d: Osdalssjøhøgda Nature Reserve is a large reserve in the south-east of Rendalen municipality, near the border with Engerdal. Around half of the area is covered by coniferous forest growing on poor bedrock consisting of sandstone and conglomerate. Selective felling has taken place in the area, and there are also traces of past forest fires. Intensive lichen harvesting has allowed large areas of heather to establish themselves. In the long term, the heather will once again be outcompeted by white beak-sedge. The reserve was established in 2002, but the area had already been protected against logging and cabin construction as early as 1963.

rangkl-vhammeren-naturreservat-natdb6187.d: Rangkløvhammeren Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rendalen municipality. It comprises an area on the western side of Lake Storsjøen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a coniferous forest area with distinctive flora and fauna; in particular, the area is floristically rich compared with the species-poor coniferous forest that dominates this part of Østerdalen.’ Chaffinches, willow warblers, robins, redwings, ravens and hazel grouse are common bird species here, but pygmy owls, sparrowhawks, red-backed shrikes, blackcaps and garden warblers can also be found in the reserve.

helakmyrene-naturreservat-natb7cc4a8c.d: The Helakmyrene Nature Reserve consists of a bog area at Storfjellsætra in Ringebu municipality, on the border with Stor-Elvdal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 18 January 1985 and is included in the bog conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a very large, diverse and mineral-poor mire complex which, due to its size, configuration, location within the landscape, elevation and vegetation, makes it valuable as a reference area and educational resource, and to preserve one of the larger and most distinctive mire areas in the county.”

skardseterlia-naturreservat-nat8899620a.d: Skardseterlia Nature Reserve comprises an area near Skjerdingfjellet in Ringebu municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 2 September 2005 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a largely untouched natural area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area is of particular educational and scientific significance as a long-established forest research site. The area is distinctive because it has a steep elevation gradient and, in places, good continuity of deadwood and good populations of rare and vulnerable species, in addition to the presence of all types of spruce and pine forest vegetation found in the region in their natural state.”

asdalstj-rna-naturreservat-nat1888a8cd.d: The Åsdalstjørna Nature Reserve comprises an area south of the Hirisjøhøgdene hills in Ringebu municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 12 October 1990 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to breeding ducks and waders.’

augga-naturreservat-nat93c8daab.d: Augga Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Lillehammer and Gausdal. It comprises an area to the west of Lillehammer on the border between the two municipalities. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a highly productive coniferous forest area with rare and threatened plant species, particularly in view of a particularly rich occurrence of the lichen species Huldrestry.’

bardsengbekken-naturreservat-nat2639a0e0.d: Bårdsengbekken Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Øyer and Gausdal. It comprises an area west of the Gudbrandsdalslågen river, between Hafjell and Tretten. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a coniferous forest area and a stream gorge with an exceptionally rich and varied flora and vegetation, particularly in view of the presence of rare plant species, including the so-called ‘huldre plants’.”

djupadalen-naturreservat-natbeb4162a.d: Djupådalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lillehammer municipality. It comprises an area to the west of Jørstadmoen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a highly productive coniferous forest area with rare and threatened plant species, particularly in view of the rich occurrence of the lichen species Huldrestry.’

flokoa-naturreservat-natdbaa0641.d: Flokoa Nature Reserve is situated along the Floka and Storbekken streams in the west of Lillehammer municipality, near Veslsetra between County Road 250 and County Road 2518. The area consists of a stream gorge, and the main conservation concern is a well-developed waterfall spray zone with rich populations of threatened and vulnerable species. Wildlife and vegetation are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting is also permitted in accordance with the relevant regulations. Motorised vehicles, cycling and horse riding are prohibited, and campfires are only permitted at ‘designated campfire sites’. There are roads leading to the reserve from both the north and the south-east.

flamyra-naturreservat-nat5022d7c5.d: Flåmyra Nature Reserve is situated on the hillside in Aust-Torpa, in the municipality of Nordre Land in the Innlandet region. The area is a large, groundwater-fed flat bog complex covering 989 daa. The bog lies adjacent to the municipal boundary with Gjøvik. Flåmyra was designated a nature reserve on 18 January 1985. The bog is of significant landscape value and is virtually untouched. It is also home to the Lapland buttercup orchid, for which this is one of its southernmost locations in Norway.

favang-naturreservat-nat7cdeaf38.d: Fåvang Nature Reserve comprises a section of the Gudbrandsdalslågen river where it flows into Losna in Ringebu municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 12 October 1990 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large and varied wetland area, its vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to migratory and breeding waterbirds.’

hundorp-naturreservat-nat0f541450.d: Hundorp Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sør-Fron municipality. It comprises a section of the Gudbrandsdalslågen river east of Hundorp. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. The use of rowing boats, canoes and similar means of transport on Olstadtjønnet and Grafferdammen is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a large and varied wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to migratory waterbirds.’

nordaa-s-raa-naturreservat-nat17a9d697.d: The Nordåa-Søråa Nature Reserve comprises an area where the Nordåa and Søråa rivers converge to form the River Våla at Ringebu in Ringebu municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 9 July 1993 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve two river gorges with an exceptionally rich and varied flora and vegetation, particularly in view of the presence of rare and threatened plant species.’

opsahl-naturreservat-nat4a080c04.d: Opsahl Nature Reserve comprises an area north of Fåvang Church in Ringebu municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 4 September 1981 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests/rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a special occurrence of dry grassland vegetation with hazel, which is of great phytogeographical interest.’

rolla-naturreservat-nated454974.d: The Rolla Nature Reserve comprises an area east of Losna on the border between the municipalities of Øyer and Ringebu. The area was designated a protected area on 9 July 1993 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a highly varied and relatively unspoilt coniferous forest area with a large proportion of rich vegetation types and a very rich and rare flora, including the so-called “huldre plants”.’

slaseterlia-naturreservat-nat0cc11771.d: Slåseterlia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Lillehammer and Øyer in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 2007 as a result of the ‘voluntary forest conservation’ initiative. The area is representative of humid mountain spruce forest and bears the hallmarks of near-primeval forest.

svarverud-naturreservat-nat4ce8bc43.d: Svarverud Nature Reserve is situated on the steep slope leading up to Svarverudberget on the western side of Gudbrandsdalen, on the border between the municipalities of Øyer and Lillehammer. Although the soil consists mainly of glacial and landslide deposits, a lush elm and lime forest grows here, home to several demanding plant species. In 2021, the elm was classified as ‘critically endangered’, as the species has shown a significant decline due to Dutch elm disease and grazing by deer. The vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees, is protected against all damage and destruction, ‘except for that resulting from free access’.

svenstad-naturreservat-natc373da18.d: Svenstad Nature Reserve comprises an area in the Frya river gorge in Ringebu municipality. The area was first designated as a protected area on 4 September 1981, extended on 19 March 2021, and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents specific types of natural environment in the form of a large, varied and well-developed river gorge featuring a mixed deciduous forest with grey elm, scree vegetation and other rich forest and habitat types. The forest is in a natural state with a considerable amount of deadwood. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it provides a habitat for many rare, vulnerable and endangered species, particularly vascular plants, lichens and mosses.’

rotlia-naturreservat-nat2615916f.d: Rotlia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and deciduous forest on the shores of Lake Mjøsa, between Stange and Tangen in Stange municipality in the Innlandet region. Rotlia Nature Reserve is an important habitat for a variety of plant species. It was designated a nature reserve by royal decree on 5 February 1971. The purpose of the conservation order was to preserve a deciduous broad-leaved forest in the inland region of Eastern Norway, along with its associated plant communities, fungi, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. This deciduous forest has been there since it spread out following the last ice age. And it is, or was, the only location inland or the northernmost limit for several plant species.

buttekvern-naturreservat-natb9a00dc6.d: Buttekvern Nature Reserve is a deciduous forest surrounded by built-up areas in Brummunddal, in Ringsaker municipality. The reserve lies between Furnesvegen and Kongsvegen, just south of the junction with Mørkvedvegen. The area is marshy, with bedrock consisting mainly of quartzite. The vegetation comprises a black alder swamp forest, with some grey alder and spruce. Black alder is the only European tree species that can tolerate having its roots submerged in water, and one of the threats to the reserve is past ditching and lowered groundwater levels. Consequently, other tree species such as spruce are gaining a foothold. Another threat is the presence of non-native species. All vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees, is protected from destruction.

begna-naturreservat-nat6c0f7f8f.d: Begna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Nord-Aurdal and Sør-Aurdal. The area was designated a nature reserve on 13 December 2002, extended on 10 June 2005, further extended on 23 June 2026, and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a relatively undisturbed forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular scientific importance as a habitat for a very interesting cryptogamic flora with significant populations of rare and threatened species, where the large population of a particular lichen species is especially valuable.

berd-la-naturreservat-nat13dc7472.d: Berdøla Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sel municipality in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve is situated west of the River Sjoa near Heidal, between the mountain farm settlements of Kvernbrusætrin and Høgsætrin, and extends towards Kvernbrusflyi and Heidalsmuen. It comprises a stretch of just over 7 km of a deep and narrow tributary gorge, featuring a mosaic of plant communities and an exceptionally rich diversity of species. There is a high proportion of alpine plants further up the gorge, many of which are calcareous. The area is home to several rare plant species. The gorge is accessible for brown trout fishing via a steep descent from Kvernbru. The nature reserve was established on 9 July 1993 to preserve a tributary gorge with an exceptionally rich and varied flora.

blessumkalvkveen-naturreservat-nate5cb91.d: The Blessomkalvkvee Nature Reserve is situated 750–850 metres above sea level, north of County Road 51 near Randsverk in Vågå municipality. The vegetation consists of sparse, coarse-grained pine forest on tall-herb land. This is a rare type of vegetation.

dokka-naturreservat-nat432844d5.d: Dokka Nature Reserve is situated in the wooded slopes above Dokka town centre in Nordre Land municipality. The area lies south-east of Østsinni. The nature reserve was designated on 9 July 1993 and, following a subsequent expansion, now covers a total of 573 daa. Dokka Nature Reserve is a relatively undisturbed woodland area comprising a distinctive, seasonally moist calcareous pine forest with a species-rich flora. The area is considered to be of national conservation importance.

dokkadeltaet-naturreservat-nat32504ea1.d: The Dokkadeltaet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Nordre and Søndre Land in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve is situated at the mouth of the River Dokka where it flows into Randsfjorden, and has had Ramsar Site status since 2002 due to its importance for migratory birds. Most of the protected area consists of water, but the protection also extends to beaches, islands and sandbanks in the delta. The reserve was established in 1990 to safeguard its role as a resting place for wetland migratory birds in spring and autumn. These include the whooper swan, bean goose, pintail, smew, marsh harrier and double-crested cormorant. The area is also a breeding ground for several species of waders. The most common is the teal.

evjemyra-naturreservat-nat6b66a7cf.d: The Evjemyra Nature Reserve comprises an area near Tranalia on the border between the municipalities of Søndre Land and Gjøvik. The area was designated a protected area on 18 January 1985 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve one of the larger, unspoilt and scenically distinctive mire complexes in Eastern Norway, and to preserve a large minerogenic flat mire complex with interesting vegetation and featuring plant species of phytogeographical importance.’

fjellsj-kampen-naturreservat-nat2092d15c.d: The Fjellsjøkampen Nature Reserve is situated in Hurdal municipality in Akershus, and in Østre Toten municipality in Innlandet. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1983 and extended to its current boundaries on 19 December 2008. However, as early as 1962, 170 mål of the area were privately protected by the owner, Mathiesen Eidsvold Værk. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a large area of remaining old-growth forest, with its natural ecosystem, habitats and species. The area is home to woodland that closely resembles primeval forest. It is of particular scientific and educational significance as an example of a spruce forest climax community, typical of the higher-altitude parts of the central Eastern Norway region.

fodnesasen-naturreservat-nat91f7623d.d: Fodnesåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Nord-Aurdal municipality. It comprises an area near Fagernes. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a relatively undisturbed coniferous forest area with a high proportion of rich vegetation types and a very rich plant life.’

hakas-ter-naturreservat-nat200e3258.d: Håkåsæter Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sør-Fron municipality. It comprises an area by Lake Håkåsætervatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a varied and relatively unspoilt coniferous forest area that is typical of the region’s habitat types, whilst a large part of the area features rich vegetation types of great value for research and education.’

jarenvatnet-naturreservat-nat829cd5a4.d: The Jarenvatnet Nature Reserve comprises the southern half of Lake Jarenvatnet in Gran municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to migratory, breeding and moulting waterbirds and a rich and interesting variety of vegetation and flora.”

langtjedn-naturreservat-nat378c91e7.d: Langtjedn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Etnedal municipality. It comprises an area near Gamlestølen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. Camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area and an interesting marshland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to breeding ducks and wading birds.’

lindstad-naturreservat-nat8c332fc2.d: Lindstad Nature Reserve is a small area on the north side of County Road 249 near Lindstad in Snertingdal, Gjøvik. The area features highly species-rich vegetation in the typical form of an elm-lime forest. Motorised traffic is prohibited, with a few exceptions. The vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees, is protected against all damage and destruction, ‘except where this results from free access’.

murulonin-naturreservat-natf740d010.d: Murulonin Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Nord-Fron municipality. It comprises an area near Muvatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a relatively undisturbed coniferous forest area, consisting mainly of nutrient-poor pine forest types, and a wetland area with a rich and interesting birdlife.’

sanddalstjedn-naturreservat-nat42d3ac14.d: Sanddalstjedn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Øystre Slidre municipality. It consists of a wetland area just north of Vinstre. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. Camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography are prohibited. From 1 May to 31 July inclusive, the use of rowing boats, canoes or similar means of transport is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area and its vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to breeding ducks and waders.’

skjellingshovde-naturreservat-nat0dcb88d.d: Skjellingshovde Nature Reserve is situated on the border between the municipalities of Sør-Aurdal, Nordre Land and Søndre Land in Innlandet County. The reserve covers 28,560 daa and was designated a protected area on 26 September 2008. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a forested area as an ecosystem, including all its natural flora and fauna. The area has special qualities as one of the few remaining large, contiguous and well-consolidated areas of old-growth natural coniferous forest in Norway without significant human intervention. The area features a variety of natural, forest and vegetation types that make it representative of the coniferous forest in the region.

smadalsvatni-naturreservat-natfc2158d6.d: The Smådalsvatni Nature Reserve is situated at an altitude of around 1,070–1,100 metres above sea level in Smådalen in the municipality of Lom, just north of Jotunheimen National Park. The reserve encompasses Smådalsvatni and the river Smådøla from Steinvatni down to Kjellarkrokan, as well as the surrounding land, with wetlands and dry meadows. The area has a rich variety of both terrestrial and aquatic vegetation. Some of the aquatic plants are found here at the upper limit of their range.

svarttjernmyra-naturreservat-natea525141.d: Svarttjernmyra Nature Reserve is situated in the north-west of Jevnaker municipality, on the ridge between Randsfjorden and Ådalen. The reserve covers a large string bog and is one of the few untouched string bogs in Eastern Norway. The vegetation is protected against all damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Motorised traffic is prohibited, but hunting is permitted in accordance with the Wildlife Act.

svennesvollene-naturreservat-nate5a21139.d: Svennesvollene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gjøvik municipality. It comprises an area near Biri. The area was designated a nature reserve on 2 October 1981. The reserve is included in the wetland conservation plan. All water-based traffic is prohibited from 15 April to 1 June inclusive and from 15 August to 1 November inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a fully developed stand of grey alder and hawthorn forest and to preserve a shore and shallow-water area of great importance for birdlife during the spring and autumn migrations.’ The reserve is an important migration site for birds and is also used for breeding. 198 bird species have been recorded in the area, 59 of which are Red List species.

uri-naturreservat-nat3c9632f1.d: Uri Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vang municipality. The area lies just north of Vangsmjøse, rising steeply from just under 500 metres above sea level to almost 700 metres. It was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horses and carts, and riding off existing roads is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a relatively unspoilt coniferous forest area with forest and vegetation types that are rare in this region’.

vindflomyrene-naturreservat-natad3b6585.d: The Vindflomyrene Nature Reserve is a large, groundwater-fed string bog in the municipalities of Østre Toten and Hurdal. The largest strings and patches are found in the southern half of the bog. Here, the longest strings are up to 250 metres long. The reserve is home to the northernmost occurrence of Sphagnum angermanicum and the southernmost occurrence of Caexe adelostoma in Eastern Norway. A forest track runs alongside the reserve to the north-east and south-west.

ktmyrene-naturreservat-nata3481886.d: The Øktmyrene Nature Reserve comprises an area north of Sperillen and west of Randsfjorden in Søndre Land municipality. The area was designated a protected site on 18 January 1985 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a typical hill bog complex which, due to its size and varied vegetation, is well suited to both education and research.’

ynad-n-naturreservat-nat43e6ec6e.d: Øynad'n Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Vestre Slidre and Vang. It consists of a wetland area near the lakes Helin and Storfjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to breeding wetland birds.’

ytjernet-naturreservat-nat85b03612.d: The Øytjernet Nature Reserve comprises an area on the border between the municipalities of Søndre Land and Gjøvik. The area was first designated as a nature reserve on 9 July 1993, covering 1,349 dekar. The reserve was extended on 21 June 2017 to nearly 3,600 dekar and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a relatively varied forest area with a significant proportion of old-growth natural forest and rich occurrences of the rare and vulnerable lichen species Huldrestry. Furthermore, the purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity in terms of habitat types, ecosystems, plant and animal species, and natural ecological processes.

tretjernmyra-naturreservat-nat06b39d13.d: Tretjernmyra Nature Reserve is situated in the south-east of Eidsvoll municipality, in a forested area with extensive marshland, close to the border with Nes municipality. Tretjernmyra is a concentrically structured rain-fed bog, with the highest point near the centre of the bog. From the highest point, there is a distinct slope in all directions, but least towards the east. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a small, concentrically structured rain-fed bog.

breimosen-naturreservat-nat1b366e91.d: Breimosen Nature Reserve is a bog area north of County Road 169 in Lillestrøm municipality. The area is mainly a precipitation bog with sparse vegetation. The bog has complex slope and drainage conditions. There is a small pond in the northern part of the bog, and an area affected by groundwater divides the site. The purpose of the conservation area is to safeguard this complex bog system. The bog is also of great value as a bird habitat.

midtfjellmosen-naturreservat-natd68e4fc8.d: Midtfjellmosen Nature Reserve is a wetland area in Aurskog-Høland municipality in Akershus. The area was designated a protected site in 1992 to safeguard an important rain-fed bog area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife. The nature reserve lies between Nordre and Søndre Mangen, in an area with gentle topography, extensive bogland and several small lakes and ponds. The bog is a gently domed rain-fed bog sloping towards the east and west. The central part is dominated by tussock vegetation and loose soil, creating distinct landforms. Dwarf birch grows on the hummocks, whilst lichen species and rusty peat moss dominate the ground. The area is of national importance as a breeding and rearing ground for birds, and is of great significance for several vulnerable and rare bird species.

prestehesten-naturreservat-nat61a0569a.d: The Prestehesten Nature Reserve is situated on the ridge between Øyeren and Bjørkelangen in Akershus County. The area consists mainly of a large, roadless forest area with a high proportion of old-growth forest. Bedrock predominates, and the forest is a mixture of spruce and pine of low to medium quality. The area forms part of the woodland belonging to Aurskog Vicarage.

storfelten-naturreservat-natfa31aa57.d: Storfelten Nature Reserve is a wetland area in Mangenskogen in the municipality of Aurskog-Høland, which was designated a protected area in 1981 to safeguard an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife. The reserve has been extended on two occasions, in January 2013 and December 2021, and covers 8,283 dekar as of 2022. Storfelten is a large, representative and undisturbed mire area comprising flat mires and precipitation mires. The precipitation-dominated sections are partly eccentric in shape, with tussock ridges and elongated hollows. There are several bog pools within the area. Storfelten is of high value as a bird habitat.

hellesj-vann-naturreservat-nat934bc5b6.d: Hellesjøvann Nature Reserve is a lake and wetland area in Aurskog-Høland municipality that was designated a protected area in 1992 to safeguard an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife. There is a ban on fishing in the area from 1 April to 15 July, with certain exceptions. Hellesjøvannet is a nutrient-rich lake surrounded by farmland, pastures and woodland. It is around 2 metres at its deepest point. The lake is particularly important as a breeding ground for birds such as the great crested grebe, mute swan, mallard, teal, moorhen, coot, black-headed gull, reed warbler and reed bunting. The very lush and dense reed beds around the lake provide good living conditions for species such as common reed, common cattail, river sedge and various sedge species.

kollerudvika-naturreservat-nat7c5a8089.d: Kollerudvika Nature Reserve is a lake and wetland area in Aurskog-Høland municipality that was designated a protected area in 1992 to safeguard an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife. The nature reserve is situated in the north-east of Øgderen. The lake lies within a beautiful cultural landscape, and there are extensive agricultural areas, particularly to the east of the lake. The water is relatively nutrient-rich and Kollerudvika has a particularly well-developed reed bed. The aquatic vegetation is otherwise characterised by marsh plants and, to a lesser extent, floating-leaved plants. Reed and common bulrush are the dominant species amongst the marsh plants, whilst common reed, common cattail, yellow water lily and white water lily are typical representatives of the floating-leaved plants.

kollasen-naturreservat-nat713e1150.d: The Kollåsen Nature Reserve is situated between County Road 36 and Lake Langen in the east of Ski municipality. The area comprises an entire hill massif with slopes facing in all directions and, in places, small-scale ravine topography. The ecological diversity is relatively high. Coniferous forest dominates the area, consisting mainly of pure spruce forest, but there is also some mixed forest with pine and some pure pine forest on peaks and barren areas. Scattered throughout are large numbers of aspen and some birch, willow and rowan. The nature reserve is of particular scientific value as a low-lying area within the boreonormal coniferous forest zone that is virtually untouched by recent human intervention. The exception is a power line that runs right through the area.

kragtorpvika-naturreservat-nat1b8d1f28.d: Kragtorpvika Nature Reserve is a lake and wetland area in Aurskog-Høland municipality that was designated a protected area in 1992 to safeguard an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife. The nature reserve is situated in the south-east of Øgderen. The lake lies within a beautiful cultural landscape, and there are extensive agricultural areas, particularly to the east of the lake. The water is relatively nutrient-rich, and Kragtorpvika has particularly well-developed common reed vegetation. The aquatic vegetation is otherwise characterised by marsh plants and, to a lesser extent, floating-leaved plants. Reeds and common bulrush are the dominant species amongst the marsh plants, whilst common cattail, common pondweed, yellow water lily and white water lily are typical representatives of the floating-leaved plants.

midtsj-vann-naturreservat-nat819312ff.d: Midsjøvannet lies 129 metres above sea level in Nordre Follo municipality in Akershus, east of the town of Ski. The lake is fed by Nærevannet and drains via Rullestadtjernet into Gjersjøen and Bunnefjorden. The lake and its shoreline were designated a nature reserve in 1992. The flora is protected, and motorised traffic is prohibited. The lake is home to pike, perch and several other species, and is a popular fishing spot. A bathing area has also been established by the lake.

dalbo-naturreservat-nat01648f3a.d: Dalbo Nature Reserve is situated near Dalbo Farm in the Kolsås-Dælivann Landscape Conservation Area and is a 14-dekar nature reserve in the municipality of Bærum. The reserve was designated on 15 December 1978 on the following grounds: ‘A deciduous forest of the snelle–ash type with woodrush. A very rare forest community found near springs with calcareous seepage water in areas with high rainfall. The stand is one of the largest of this forest type in Norway, and is probably unique in Northern Europe.”

geitholmen-naturreservat-nat9b04bc8b.d: The Geitholmen Nature Reserve on Geitholmen in Bærum municipality was established on 27 June 2008. Geitholmen is situated on the outer side of Snarøya, just off Snarøykilen. The site consists of a gently sloping limestone heath and a valuable coastal zone facing the sea on the southern part of Geitholmen. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a special natural area comprising an almost untouched and rich limestone grassland of great botanical value, as well as a valuable salt marsh. The area is distinctive due to its south-facing location. Limestone grasslands of this size are very rare. The meadow is relatively flat, with no shading trees or scrub. Among the most interesting plant species is the dragon’s head.

hvalskj-ret-naturreservat-nat67d7e163.d: Hvalskjæret Nature Reserve consists of a skerry situated close to Hvalstrand beach in Asker municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 15 December 1978 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

kalv-ya-naturreservat-nat2a17388e.d: Kalvøya Nature Reserve is a protected coastal area on the north side of Kalvøya, consisting of Upper Ordovician rocks from levels 4a to 5b in the Oslo Field. The rocks consist of calcareous sandstone deposited in a channel, as well as alternating layers of clay and limestone typical of the Cambrian–Silurian strata of the Oslo Field. Established as a nature reserve on 15 January 1988, covering 15 daa.

kjeholmen-naturreservat-nata6161574.d: The Kjeholmen Nature Reserve covers most of the island of Kjeholmen, north of Grimsøya, between Ostøya and Snarøya in the municipality of Bærum. It is home to a well-developed limestone pine forest with a ground vegetation layer typical of the islands in the inner Oslo Fjord. To the south and east, there are also coastal rock outcrops and limestone grasslands with a high level of biodiversity. A total of 226 different plant species have been recorded on the island, including the Norwegian priority species Oslo sedge and rognasal. The reserve also contains liquorice grass, on which many butterflies depend throughout their life cycle, not least the critically endangered liquorice grass blue. Furthermore, the red-listed plant ‘queen’s sedge’ has been recorded, but it has not been found again since.

kolsastoppen-naturreservat-natf2f5bf5d.d: Kolsåstoppen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kolsås, Bærum.

krakholmen-fuglefredningsomrade-nat9c87e.d: The Kråkholmen Bird Sanctuary is a habitat conservation area on the south-western headland of Kråkholmen in Asker, and the sea area 50 metres offshore. The bird sanctuary is primarily home to black-headed gulls and common gulls, whilst the rest of the island is also home to common terns and herring gulls. Both plants and birds in the area are protected against damage and destruction. It is also prohibited to carry out any activities that might alter the birds’ natural environment. Access is prohibited both on land and at sea during the period from 15 April to 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving.

lagmannsholmen-naturreservat-nat99d71648.d: The Lagmannsholmen Nature Reserve comprises the island of Lagmannsholmen in Bærum, together with the sea extending approximately 50 metres out from the island, and the coastal zone on the mainland within the Fornebulandet area. The islet is barren, and the bedrock consists of sedimentary rocks from the Ordovician geological period. The rock is rich in fossils, and the stratification in the so-called ‘floors’ 4b and 4c is visible within the reserve. The site is of great scientific value. Lagmannsholmen is also an important breeding ground for the black-headed gull, a species that has seen a significant decline in the Oslo Fjord since the 1980s. Access to Lagmannsholmen and the surrounding waters is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July. Furthermore, it is not permitted to remove fossils from the solid rock.

lille-ya-naturreservat-natc1eb88b6.d: The Lilleøya Nature Reserve at Fornebu in Bærum municipality was established on 27 June 2008. Lilleøya is a peninsula jutting out from Oksenøya between Holtekilen and Storøykilen, in the north-west of the Fornebu peninsula. This is the largest area of relatively natural vegetation remaining on Fornebu. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a distinctive area with a unique habitat characterised by a wide variety of vegetation types and many rare species. The area is of particular value due to its high level of biodiversity and is well suited as a reference area for research and teaching.

m-kkalassene-naturreservat-nat1565c9a1.d: The Møkkalassene Nature Reserve comprises three islets south-east of Snarøya in Bærum, as well as the sea up to 50 metres offshore. The islets have been an important breeding site for black-headed gulls, a population that has seen a dramatic decline since the 1980s. However, the number of black-headed gulls has shown some recovery since 2005. There is a ban on access to the area from 15 April to 15 July, and on bringing dogs all year round.

naturreservat-s-r-for-furuholmen-naturre.d: Borøyskjær is a skerry just south of Furuholmen, off Borøya in the municipality of Bærum. The skerry and the surrounding sea area within a 50-metre radius are protected as the Nature Reserve south of Furuholmen. The purpose of the protection is to preserve the environment, particularly with regard to seabirds. A census in 2005 revealed that the islet was home to the largest colony of breeding common terns in the fjord, as well as a number of black-headed gulls. Both species are on Norway’s Red List. The birdlife in the reserve is protected against harm and unnecessary disturbance, and it is forbidden to carry out any activities that impair the birds’ habitat. All access is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July, and all hunting, trapping and the use of firearms are prohibited between 1 March and 1 October. Furthermore, dogs must always be kept on a lead.

paradisbukta-naturreservat-nat219bba85.d: Paradisbukta Nature Reserve comprises a shallow bay with surrounding beaches, as well as a rocky ridge on the south-eastern side of Grimsøya in Bærum municipality. The bedrock consists of clay shale, which provides calcareous growing conditions. The vegetation consists largely of salt marshes and calcareous dry grasslands, both of which are critically endangered at national level. The rocky ridge provides shelter from the wind, and the bay itself is one of the very few inlets in the Oslo Fjord that remains virtually untouched. Here, both sea purslane and a large population of sea rush can be found. To the south, there is a transition to wet meadows and marshes, where we find, amongst other things, the sword lily. Wildlife and plant life on land and in the water are protected against damage and destruction, but hunting is permitted in accordance with current regulations.

presteskj-r-naturminne-natdaaf2cce.d: The Presteskjær Natural Monument is situated at Holmen in Asker municipality. It was established on 15 January 1988. The purpose of the conservation order is to protect a site of importance for understanding the fossil-bearing rocks of the Oslo Field. Presteskjær Natural Monument is a small islet near Holmenskjær Natural Monument. Presteskjær and Holmenskjær together form a comprehensive picture as representative sites for the Upper Ordovician (Stage 5a).

prinseskj-r-naturreservat-nat4eda8b81.d: Prinseskjær Nature Reserve consists of a skerry and the sea within a 50-metre radius of it, on the north-western side of Ostøya in Bærum municipality. The purpose of the reserve is to protect the habitat of flora and fauna, particularly seabirds. All access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July inclusive.

rogneskj-r-fuglefredningsomrade-nat31d14.d: The Rogneskjær Wildlife Sanctuary is a habitat conservation area comprising a skerry just west of Kråkholmen off Vettre in Asker municipality, as well as the surrounding sea area within a 50-metre radius. The skerries are a breeding ground for a number of seabird species, now dominated by the lesser black-backed gull. Both flora and birdlife are protected against damage and destruction, and any activities that may impair the birds’ habitat are prohibited. Furthermore, all access is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving.

sandholmen-naturreservat-nat378f6fcc.d: Sandholmen Nature Reserve comprises a small islet at the innermost part of Hundesundet in Bærum, and the surrounding sea area to the north-west. Surveys have shown significant fluctuations in the number of breeding seabirds in the Oslofjord. Many species tend to change their breeding sites from one season to the next, and the number of birds at a particular site can therefore vary considerably from year to year. Nevertheless, it is important that there are areas which are undisturbed and set aside for the birds’ reproduction. Within the reserve, vegetation and wildlife, including nests and eggs, are protected against any damage, destruction or unnecessary disturbance. Camping and lighting fires are prohibited, and from 1 March to 1 October inclusive, all access to the reserve is prohibited.

stor-ykilen-naturreservat-nat599c64ba.d: The Storøykilen Nature Reserve encompasses the southern side of Storøykilen and a somewhat larger area at the innermost part of the inlet near Fornebulandet in Bærum municipality. The bay is shallow and a large part of the area is covered by wetland vegetation. In places, the bedrock is exposed, consisting of calcareous, sedimentary rocks from the Cambrian–Silurian period. Drought-tolerant calcareous vegetation is found here. Further inland, the landscape is characterised by large oak and lime trees. The site is important as a resting and feeding ground for migratory birds, but also as a wintering ground for several species of passerines. Motorised traffic is not permitted, nor are rowing boats, canoes, windsurf boards or similar craft.

svartskj-ra-naturreservat-nat1a95fe46.d: Svartskjæra Nature Reserve consists of a marine wetland area in a shallow bay with three skerries on the eastern side of Ostøya in Bærum municipality. The purpose of the reserve is to protect the habitat of flora and fauna, particularly seabirds. All access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July inclusive.

syd-oust-naturreservat-nata8756fa1.d: The Syd Oust Nature Reserve mainly comprises a shallow bay sheltered by a small headland just offshore, to the south of Ostøya in Bærum municipality. Its conservation value lies in its plant life and fossil deposits. The bay is influenced by the tides, and in the transition zone between sea and land there is marsh and wet meadow vegetation, densely populated with common reed. Further inland, the landscape transitions to salt marshes, where, amongst other things, sea arrowgrass can be found. And along the rocky ridge at the edge of the reserve, there are communities of blood-red campion and calcareous dry rocky slopes. The vegetation, wildlife and bedrock within the reserve are protected against damage and destruction, and it is not permitted to carry out any activities that might alter the natural environment.

tuemyr-naturreservat-nat4936a184.d: Tuemyr Nature Reserve lies on both sides of the municipal boundary between the municipalities of Asker and Bærum in Akershus, about one kilometre north-east of Store Sandungen in Vestmarka. The bog is an intact flat bog that slopes gently towards the south. The bedrock consists of Permian alluvial deposits, which provide fertile ground for rich and lush vegetation. It is easily accessible via a forest track from Vestmarkssetra.

vendelholmene-naturreservat-nat0e82a9e9.d: The Vendelholmene Nature Reserve on Brønnøya in Asker municipality was established on 27 June 2008. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a virtually untouched natural area in the form of a small archipelago with distinctive coastal marshes and unique salt marsh communities, including the endangered salt-marsh community, which includes several Red List species, along with habitats for salt-meadow flora and species-rich calcareous dry grassland communities. A total of 106 vascular plants have been recorded on the three islets. The somewhat marshy shorelines provide excellent growing conditions for salt marsh flora, and there is a large population of the rare species, sea rush.

vensasmyra-naturreservat-natce6533bc.d: The Vensåsmyra Nature Reserve consists of a bog area adjacent to the boundary of the agricultural land to the east of the Vensås farms in Lommedalen, in the municipality of Bærum. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve one of the few remaining rich fens in the inner parts of the Oslofjord area. To the west, the bog borders on cultivated land, and to the east on Bærumsmarka. The area around the bog is characterised by rich wet woodlands. The bog is predominantly a flat bog with moderately rich and rich solid mat vegetation. The bog serves as a representative site for this habitat type in the region.

skotta-naturreservat-nat9607cdb6.d: Skotta Nature Reserve is situated on a west-facing slope south of Skotta Farm in Bærum, surrounded by the Kolsås-Dælivann Landscape Conservation Area. The nature reserve consists of a broad-leaved deciduous forest growing on a bedrock of sedimentary rocks from the Cambrian–Silurian geological period. Norway’s broad-leaved deciduous forests are the northernmost in the world, and the forest in this reserve is of the elm-lime type with hawthorn. It is not permitted to remove any vegetation from the area, not even dead wood or fallen branches.

bjerkas-naturreservat-nat04583f0c.d: The Bjerkås Nature Reserve in Asker municipality was established on 27 August 2008. It is situated at Bjerkås, between Vollen and Slemmestad. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a large, coherent and distinctive area containing several nationally rare habitat types that are representative of the Cambrian–Silurian landscape in the inner Oslo Fjord. The reserve consists of two limestone ridges, a glacial dam and two smaller fields that form a natural unit. The area is extremely rich in species, and Norway’s largest known population of the plant vetch is found here. The elm-lime forest contains several Red Listed fungi species.

kvistemyrdammen-dyrefredningsomrade-nat6.d: Kvistemyrdammen is situated right by the sea, south of Fjellstrand on the western side of Nesodden in Akershus. The lake is dammed and has served as a water source for the quarry right next to it. The purpose of the wildlife sanctuary is to conserve rare and endangered amphibians such as the great crested newt, the smooth newt and the pointed-snouted frog, as well as rare insects, and the habitats of these species. Within the conservation area there is also a separately protected settlement site dating from the Early Stone Age. The area is bounded to the north by Kvistemyrveien.

andotten-naturreservat-nata4328117.d: Andotten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hasvik municipality. The reserve covers an area of 0.303 km² in the north-west of the island of Sørøya. Approximately 0.1 km² of this is land area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. The bird cliff is home to black guillemots, shags, great cormorants and kittiwakes. Most of the birds nest on the north side of the headland.

eidvagen-naturreservat-nat897ca78d.d: Eidvågen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hammerfest municipality. The reserve covers an area of 0.302 km² east of Eidvågen on the island of Seiland. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. Black guillemots build their nests on a cliff face approximately 50 metres high that drops steeply into the sea at the far end of Eidvågen. It is unusual for black guillemots to breed so far from the open sea. A few pairs of kittiwakes also breed on the cliff.

goskamark-naturreservat-nat2eba03ca.d: Goskamark Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated in the municipality of Alta. The reserve covers 4.07 km² of woodland on the eastern bank of the Eibyelva river, approximately 20 km south of Alta, and lies at altitudes ranging from 70 to 280 metres above sea level. The reserve aims to preserve a forest area with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes. The area comprises a largely undisturbed pine and birch forest with great ecological diversity. The forest is typical of the pine forests in the Alta and Eiby valleys. 0.175 km² of the forest on the terraces was protected as early as 1928. This area was granted the status of an administratively protected forest reserve on 17 June 1969, and the reserve was extended in 1974 to 0.8 km².

gossjohka-naturreservat-natb4924b4c.d: The Goššjohka Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Karasjok. The reserve covers an area of 1.284 km² where the River Goššjohka flows into the Anarjohka. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a virtually untouched deciduous forest area as an ecosystem, with all its natural flora and fauna. The area comprises birch and willow woodland, dominated by green willow. The shrub layer consists of juniper, wild currant, hawthorn, silver willow, pale willow and green willow. Common species in the herbaceous layer include wood small-reed, silver grass, wood sorrel, slender sedge, white clover, wood cranesbill, cowberry, white-leaved thistle, Lapland buttercup, field cowberry and greater speedwell.

isberglia-naturreservat-natdd6492a8.d: Isberglia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated in the municipality of Alta. The reserve covers 1.18 km² of the western side of the upper part of the Tverrelvdalen valley. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a forested area with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes. The area features patches of calcareous pine forest, a forest type that is rare in Finnmark and provides a habitat for rare plant species.

korsfjorden-naturreservat-nat3e3a7c4d.d: Korsfjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Alta. The reserve covers an area of 0.528 km² on the southern side of Kufjellet, just north of Korsfjorden. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a virtually untouched deciduous forest area as an ecosystem, with all its natural flora and fauna. The bedrock consists of mica schist with layers of calcareous rock. The area features low-herb forest with calcareous and thermophilic vegetation, and an exceptionally high number of species. The tree layer consists of birch and goat willow, with some grey alder, rowan, hawthorn and aspen. Juniper is characteristic of the shrub layer and indicates that the area is former pasture land.

krokelvosen-naturreservat-nat27c1d4bd.d: Krokelvosen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated in the municipality of Alta. The reserve covers 0.139 km² of the fjord at Leirbotn, of which 0.08 km² is on land. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a coastal area with well-developed salt marsh vegetation, featuring a wide variety of plant communities and plant species.

latharimoen-naturreservat-nat2bce327c.d: Latharimoen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on Lathari (Sami: Láhttar) in Alta municipality. The reserve covers an area of 0.179 km² between the mouths of the Altaelva and Transfarelva rivers, facing out towards the Altafjord. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a forest area with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes. Heather-pine forests of this type on sandy terraces are rarely found to be so little affected by human intervention. In Finnmark, this is the only place where one can find continuous pine forest stretching right down to the sea.

leirbotndalen-naturreservat-nat644ee643.d: Leirbotndalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Alta. The reserve covers an area of 1.157 km² of the Leirbotndalen valley, approximately 3 km up the valley. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a virtually untouched deciduous forest area as an ecosystem with natural flora and fauna. The area is a terraced landscape, with pine trees on the terraces. The grey alder forest is found in the lower sections along the Kvandalselva and Lakselva rivers. Part of the area comprises rich birch forests above the road. In particular, the stream course along the Kvandalselva and the banks of the Lakselva feature lush and tall grey alder and tall-shrub birch forests. Wood cranesbill, globeflower, dog’s tooth violet, meadowsweet and valerian are common in the ground layer.

lille-kam-ya-naturreservat-natf4371588.d: Lille Kamøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hammerfest municipality. The reserve covers an area of 1.585 km², of which approximately 0.6 km² comprises the land area of Lille Kamøya, with the remainder being the surrounding sea area. Lille Kamøya lies just north of Store Kamøya and Sørøya. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. Lille Kamøya is home to Norway’s largest colony of shags. Other species breeding on the island include the black guillemot, common murre, eider, black-headed gull, grey gull and black-backed gull. The puffin is believed to breed here. Razorbills, red-billed terns, oystercatchers, turnstones and ringed seals have been observed. The bird colonies are found particularly in the far north and far south of the island.

maze-naturreservat-nat6ab55d34.d: Maze Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kautokeino municipality. The reserve covers an area of 0.231 km², on the west bank of the Kautokeino River in Maze. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a virtually untouched deciduous forest area as an ecosystem, with all its natural flora and fauna. The nature reserve encompasses a low-lying, flood-prone peninsula in the Kautokeino River, Ájanjárga, downstream from the village of Máze. Elsewhere along the Kautokeino River, birch forests dominated by cowberry and blueberry are prevalent. The area features well-developed willow woodland with green willow as the dominant species, but also includes birch, hawthorn, mountain willow and rowan in the tree layer. In places, there is a significant proportion of hawthorn. In addition to green willow, the shrub layer includes wild currant, mountain willow and pale willow.

nordsandfjorden-naturreservat-nat5430258.d: Nordsandfjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hasvik municipality. The reserve covers an area of 0.802 km² in the north-west of the island of Sørøya. Approximately 0.7 km² of this is land area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a large sandy fjord with its associated dune system and vegetation. Nordsandfjorden has Arctic flora. A total of 174 species and subspecies of vascular plants have been recorded here. Large quantities of calcareous sand provide a habitat for many calcium-demanding species. Among other things, a number of orchids grow here: green-winged orchid, coralroot, wood orchid, spotted orchid, red helleborine, lady’s slipper, mountain white orchid and lesser twayblade. There are ruins in the area that bear witness to past settlement and agriculture.

oahcesaisuolu-naturreservat-nat7a276b1f.d: The Oahcesaisuolu Nature Reserve is situated approximately 18 kilometres south-west of the town of Karasjok in Karasjok municipality, Finnmark, and comprises a small islet in the Karasjohka river consisting of river sediments. The nature reserve covers an area of 334 daa and is home to a dense forest of downy birch. Other common species include silver grass, wood sorrel, white clover, wood cranesbill, cloudberry, greater speedwell and willow thickets. There is a large abundance of Finnmark chickweed, as well as other berries, grasses and sedge species. The purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched deciduous forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna.’ There are areas of old hay meadows here. The area is of scientific importance as a typical example of continental birch forest.

saksfjorden-naturreservat-nat0c2308d0.d: Saksfjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hammerfest municipality. The reserve covers an area of 1.002 km² at the innermost part of Saksfjorden in the north of Sørøya. Approximately 0.5 km² consists of land around the fjord. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a virtually untouched sandy fjord with its associated sand dune system and vegetation. The sand dune system is characterised by strong wind exposure. The vegetation is varied. The foreshore vegetation consists of Arctic radish and sea purslane. Further inland are light-coloured and grey dunes that give way to species-rich dune grasslands, featuring, amongst others, red fescue, mountain avens and Siberian chive. The area is surrounded by steep mountains, and significant sand drift up the mountainsides is a characteristic feature.
