storgalten-naturreservat-nat2905ad6d.d: Storgalten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated near the old, burnt-down trading post of Galten in Hasvik municipality. The reserve covers the islands of Lyngøya and Flatøya, an area of 1,066 km² in Galtefjorden on the island of Sørøya. Approximately 0.35 km² of this is land area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. The black guillemot colony is situated on a steep mountainside on Storgalten. Other birds that breed here include the great cormorant, grey gull, black-backed gull, kittiwake and eider.

svartbotn-naturreservat-natdc44d6fa.d: Svartbotn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Hammerfest. The reserve covers an area of 2.213 km² in the north-east of Sørøya. Approximately 2 km² is land area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a largely undisturbed sandy fjord with its associated dune system and vegetation. The sandy shore at Svartbotn is approximately 300 metres wide, and the sand dunes extend several hundred metres inland into the valley, which is surrounded by fairly steep mountains. The foreshore is dominated by sea thrift and some sea lavender and sea sandwort. The beach dunes are poorly developed and the foreshore largely merges directly into young dune grassland dominated by yarrow.

s-rsandfjorden-naturreservat-nat15e6b48e.d: Sørsandfjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hasvik municipality. The reserve covers an area of 1.795 km² in the north-west of the island of Sørøya. Approximately 1.5 km² of this is land area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a large sandy fjord with its associated dune system and vegetation. The sandy beach, the dune front and the dune grasslands form a well-developed and instructive system. The dune grasslands feature distinct raised beach ridges that illustrate land uplift. The vegetation is varied and comprises a high number of plant species, including some thermophilic species. The area features a northern occurrence of rich birch forest, ferns and tall herbs in the undergrowth. The sandy beach is approximately 1 km long and the dune grasslands extend approximately 1.2 km inland.

bihkkacohkka-naturreservat-nat947a2790.d: The Bihkkacohkka Nature Reserve comprises an area near the Børselva river in Porsanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 29 June 2007 and is included in the conservation plan for deciduous forests/rich deciduous woodlands. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched deciduous forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna. Notable features include calcium-demanding vegetation on dolomite soil and a high number of species, including abundant populations of orchids. The area is unique in that it comprises several vegetation types and boasts a high level of species diversity. Safeguarding the natural environment within the nature reserve is important for Sámi culture and economic use. The area must be available for reindeer herding.”

b-rselvdalen-naturreservat-nateefcc421.d: The Børselvdalen Nature Reserve comprises an area along the River Børselva in Porsanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 29 June 2007 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests/rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched deciduous forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna. Notable features include calcareous vegetation on dolomite soil, riparian vegetation, pine trees at their northern limit and a large river pool. The area is distinctive as a site with rich, diverse vegetation comprising calcium-demanding species and elements of pine. Safeguarding the natural environment within the nature reserve is important for Sámi culture and economic use.

ekker-ya-naturreservat-natb4c2feeb.d: Ekkerøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vadsø municipality in Finnmark. It is situated on the Ekkerøy peninsula, around 15 kilometres east of the town of Vadsø. The purpose of the reserve is to preserve an important bird cliff, as well as the associated flora and fauna. The reserve is very easily accessible.

f-rdesmyra-naturreservat-natcac4d032.d: Færdesmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Sør-Varanger. The reserve was established to preserve a distinctive and markedly frost-affected bog area featuring palsas and tall tussocks. The tallest palser mounds are just over 3 metres high and are clustered together in a small area just north of Færdesvann. The palses at Færdesmyra, as is often the case elsewhere in East Finnmark, are associated with kvabb deposits where the great late-glacial meltwater rivers once flowed into the sea. Kvabb is coarser than clay and finer than sand, and causes the most frost heave of all soil types. Færdesmyra is, on the whole, a nutrient-poor bog.

gj-kvassneset-naturreservat-nate38dacc1.d: Gjøkvassneset Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Sør-Varanger. The reserve is situated on a headland on Lake Gjøkvatnet, around 5 kilometres north-east of Øvre Pasvik National Park. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a forested area with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes. The conservation value is particularly linked to the area’s primeval forest character. The forest is relatively varied. In the far east, there is forest in its optimal phase, with high tree density and slender trees reaching heights of 13–14 metres. In most of the area, the forest is dominated by trees in the mature phase, standing 16–18 metres tall, where the canopy is partly breaking up and younger trees have established themselves in places.

hanadalen-naturreservat-natba52a816.d: Hanadalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tana municipality in Finnmark. The area was established in 2007 and covers an area of 2.76 km². The nature reserve was established to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous forest. Hanadalen has rich birch woodland with tall herbaceous plants and patches of birch woodland with low-growing herbs. The dominant species are wood cranesbill, sweet woodruff and lady’s mantle. Other commonly occurring species include globeflower, meadow buttercup, wood sorrel, white-leaved thistle and great speedwell. Locally, valerian, dog’s mercury, meadowsweet, wood sorrel, woodruff and mountain nettle form dense, tall stands. Among the shorter herbs, four-leaved mare’s-tail is worth mentioning, as it is not common in Finnmark. Lifiol is abundant and characteristic of the low-growing herbs in the area.

harrelv-naturreservat-natcc40934d.d: Harrelv Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tana municipality in Finnmark. The area was established in 2007 and covers 683 dekar. The nature reserve was established to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous forest. The nature reserve is characterised by a rich grey alder and willow forest. Along the river, willow and birch are most common, but grey alder occurs almost continuously along the riverbank and dominates in areas prone to flooding. The area is probably the world’s northernmost occurrence of large tracts of old grey alder forest, and the heat-loving strutsevings is likely to have reached its absolute northern limit here.

julelvdalen-naturreservat-nat3db318d8.d: Julelvdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tana municipality in Finnmark. The area was established in 2007 and covers an area of 0.30 km². The nature reserve was established to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous forest.

kinaroddsandfjorden-naturreservat-nate8b.d: Kinaroddsandfjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Lebesby in Finnmark. It was established on 20 December 1991, and the purpose of the conservation area was to preserve a sandy fjord and its associated dune system. The reserve is situated at the head of Kinnar-Sandfjorden, 4 kilometres south of Kinnarodden.

kirkeneshalv-ya-dyrelivsfredning-nat49df.d: The Kirkenes Peninsula Wildlife Reserve is a protected area in the municipality of Sør-Varanger in Finnmark. It was established on 20 October 1961 under the Nature Conservation Act of 1954, and encompassed the peninsula between the Pasvik River in the east and Langfjorden in the west, bounded to the south by a line running from the north-western corner of Boris Gleb south-westwards via Bjørnevatnet and the Bjørnelva to Langfjorden. Within the area, all mammals and birds are protected throughout the year. Today, this protection is probably regarded as an anachronism. The protected area is said to have been established to prevent workers at the former Syd-Varanger mines from shooting all the wildlife on the Kirkenes Peninsula in their spare time.

langfjorddalen-naturreservat-nat3869bd29.d: Langfjorddalen/Laggu Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Gamvik and Lebesby in Finnmark. It was established on 29 July 2007, and the purpose of the conservation was to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous forest. The reserve covers a 17-kilometre-long section of the Langfjord Valley.

neiden-og-munkefjord-naturreservat-natf7.d: The Neiden and Munkefjord Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Sør-Varanger, established by royal decree on 12 December 1991. The area is situated at the mouths of the Neidenelva and Munkelva rivers on the southern side of the Varangerfjord. It consists mainly of tidal flats and shallow waters, with only a small portion comprising land. The rivers deposit sand and mud banks, which are partially exposed at low tide. A large inflow of fresh water and strong tidal currents create nutrient-rich conditions. The area is home to several rare plant species, such as the Finnmark snowbell, the kolamelde and, not least, the Neiden saltgrass, which is found nowhere else in the world. In spring, there are many red-throated loons and black-throated loons, whilst the goosander is a common species in late summer.

nesseby-naturreservat-nat372cec8e.d: Nesseby Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated outside the village of Nesseby in Nesseby municipality, Finnmark. The nature reserve encompasses Løkholmen, the tidal bay within it and the headland south of Nesseby Church. It has a total area of 753 dekar, of which 660 dekar is sea. The nature reserve was established in 1991 to preserve an important resting area for wetland birds. At low tide, large mudflats are exposed, rich in soft-bottom fauna that provide food for waders such as the sandpiper, dunlin, little stint, tundra sandpiper, bar-tailed godwit, ruff, Lapwing, Common Snipe and ducks.

oksevagdalen-naturreservat-nat9889180d.d: Oksevågdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lebesby municipality in Finnmark. It was established on 29 June 2007, and the purpose of the conservation was to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous forest. The reserve is situated on the north side of Oksevågdalen, around 3 kilometres east of Kjøllefjord.

omgangsstauran-naturreservat-natca03aa40.d: Omgangsstauran Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated at the easternmost tip of the Nordkinn Peninsula in Gamvik municipality, Finnmark. The nature reserve consists of a 6-kilometre-long, 200–250-metre-high sheer cliff, as well as part of the inland mountain plateau and the adjacent area of the sea. The reserve was established in 1983, and the purpose of the protection was to preserve an important bird cliff, along with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife associated with it. The bird cliff is home to breeding black guillemots, great cormorants, guillemots, razorbills, kittiwakes and gulls. Shags have also been recorded.

ovdalsdasvarri-naturreservat-natc7f4bb1b.d: Ovdaldasvarri Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tana municipality in Finnmark. The area was established in 1983 and covers an area of 13.93 km². The nature reserve was established to preserve a large field of fossilised drifting sand dunes. The sand dunes were formed on the tundra landscape that existed in the area after the inland ice sheet had retreated following the last ice age. The sand dunes give the landscape a gently undulating character. A sparse birch forest grows in the area.

roddinesset-naturreservat-nat54eb952a.d: The Roddinesset Nature Reserve comprises a geologically interesting area by the Porsangerfjord. County Road 98 runs through the area. The nature reserve is situated in Porsanger municipality. It was designated a nature reserve on 19 May 1967. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a typical and beautiful system of beach ridges that illustrates the retreat of the sea following the last ice age.’

slettnes-naturreservat-nat820be815.d: Slettnes Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gamvik municipality, Finnmark. The nature reserve is situated on the Nordkyn Peninsula, on one of the few uninhabited coastal plains along the Finnmark coast, and has held Ramsar Site status since 2002, due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1996 to preserve a distinctive, low-lying beach and marsh landscape. The flat coastal plain stands out markedly from the mountainous terrain elsewhere on the Nordkyn Peninsula. There are numerous water bodies and areas of marshland and willow thickets here, which provide breeding and resting grounds for a large number of wading bird and duck species.

store-sameti-skjelvatnet-naturreservat-n.d: Store Sametti – Skjelvatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Sør-Varanger. It is situated in the Pasvik Valley and covers an area 18 kilometres long and 3–6 kilometres wide, which is roughly bounded to the west by the watershed with the Sandneselva river. The reserve was established on 21 December 2000 and covers an area of 79.9 km². The purpose of the reserve is to protect a coniferous forest area with all its natural flora and fauna.

storelvosen-naturreservat-nat37f1cb48.d: Storelvosen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vadsø municipality in Finnmark. It is situated at the mouth of the Storelva river, around 15 kilometres east of the town of Vadsø. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve an important wetland area, with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. The area comprises a large and well-formed subarctic salt marsh with many plant communities and a large number of species. The site serves as a resting place for wetland birds and a breeding ground for certain species.

tanamunningen-naturreservat-nat921020cb.d: The Tanamunningen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tana Municipality, Finnmark. The nature reserve encompasses a river delta at the mouth of the River Tana and has held Ramsar Site status since 2002, due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1991 to protect a large and distinctive delta area of international importance as a resting and feeding ground for wetland birds. The area comprises Northern Norway’s largest contiguous salt marshes and interesting riverbank vegetation. During every flood, the River Tana transports large quantities of sediment, which is deposited in sandbanks down towards the estuary.

torskefjorddalen-naturreservat-nat6c392f.d: Torskefjorddalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lebesby municipality in Finnmark. It was established on 29 June 2007, and the purpose of the conservation area was to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous forest. The reserve encompasses the upper part of the sheltered valley within Store Torskefjorden, a small side fjord of Laksefjorden. The valley is home to one of the country’s northernmost birch forests of any size.

trollfjorddalen-gulgo-naturreservat-nat1.d: The Trollfjorddalen/Gulgo Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Berlevåg municipality in Finnmark. The area was established in 2007 and covers an area of 11.36 km². The nature reserve was established to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous forest. With its tall birch forest, Trollfjorddalen (or Gulgofjorddalen) stands out markedly from the barren landscape of the Varanger Peninsula. In addition to birch, rowan and willow are also found here. The rich vegetation provides a habitat for a variety of passerines.

varangerbotn-naturreservat-nat9109bc03.d: Varangerbotn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated at Varangerbotn in Nesseby municipality in Finnmark. The nature reserve encompasses the inner part of Meskefjorden, within a line stretching from Veineset in the south to Hándalriddu in the north, as well as the adjacent land area. It has a total area of 1,181 dekar, of which 200 dekar is land and the remainder is sea. The nature reserve was established by Royal Decree of 20 December 1991 to preserve an area of beach, foreshore and shallow water with a rich bird life and well-developed, varied salt marsh vegetation.

vestertana-naturreservat-nata24558a4.d: Vestertana Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tana municipality in Finnmark. The area was established in 1991 and covers 847 dekar, of which 50 dekar is land area. The nature reserve was established to preserve a distinctive beach and foreshore area with well-developed salt marshes featuring Arctic plant communities. The foreshore and shallow-water areas within the reserve are important as resting places for wetland birds. The salt marsh at the innermost part of Vestrertana is one of the most diverse east of Porsanger. Here, there are, amongst other things, large areas of carpet saltgrass and Arctic sedge. The extensive foreshore has a characteristic pattern of gravel and sandbanks. On the innermost banks, sea sandwort and sea purslane grow.

hjelms-ya-naturreservat-nat377a46ba.d: Hjelmsøya Nature Reserve comprises an area at the very northern tip of Hjelmsøya in Måsøy municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 January 1983 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’

hjelms-ysandfjorden-naturreservat-nate91.d: The Hjelmsøysandfjorden Nature Reserve comprises an area on Hjelmsøya in Måsøy municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 20 December 1991 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a sandy fjord with its associated dune system and vegetation, as well as a breeding area for seabirds.’

horn-ya-og-rein-ya-naturreservat-natff3c.d: The Hornøya and Reinøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated north/north-east of Vardøya in Vardø municipality, Finnmark. The nature reserve comprises the two larger islands, Reinøya and Hornøya, as well as the islets of Avløysa and Prestholmen, situated approximately two kilometres north-east of the centre of Vardø town. It covers an area of 1,968 dekar, of which 500 dekar is marine area. The nature reserve was established in 1983 to preserve an important bird cliff and the associated animal, bird and plant life linked to the area. The islands are an important breeding ground, including for several Red Listed bird species, and are home to one of Europe’s largest gull colonies.

sanden-naturreservat-nat21174ec7.d: The Sanden Nature Reserve comprises the isthmus between Eidnesbukta and Østerbotn on the island of Ingøya in the municipality of Måsøy. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 December 1991 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area comprising salt marshes, sandy beaches and sand dunes, and the associated vegetation. In the westernmost part of the area, there is an interesting salt marsh, whilst the wide bay on the eastern side, Sanden, has a large sandy beach. On the isthmus between these beaches lies a well-developed system of sand dunes.”

reisautl-pet-naturreservat-nat3de22e36.d: The Reisautløpet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site at the mouth of the Reisa River in Nordreisa municipality, Troms. The reserve was established in 1995 ‘to preserve a large river delta that includes one of the three most valuable salt marshes in Northern Norway, and where a number of wetland bird species are observed during the migration periods’. The estuary where the river flows into the Reisafjord is a river delta featuring sandbanks and salt marshes, salt meadows, brackish water meadows and pools. The vegetation of the salt marshes is characterised by both southern and northern, subarctic features. The estuary is an important migration and foraging area for seabirds and waders, with large numbers of common goldeneyes, smews, dabbling ducks, waders and terns. The salt marshes are of international conservation value in a botanical context.

dankarvagvatn-naturreservat-nat6fe8ca3f.d: Dankarvågvatn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the north of Kvaløya in Tromsø municipality, Troms. It comprises a wetland area by Lake Dankarvågvatn (5.5 metres above sea level), around three kilometres south-east of Kvaløyvågen, with terrain consisting of small hills surrounded by marshes and water. The area features lush aquatic vegetation, nutrient-poor bogs, heathland and birch forest. It serves as a breeding ground for several species of ducks, waders and gulls. During the spring migration, large numbers of waders stop here to rest. There are also significant numbers of ducks and waders in the area during the autumn migration, and to some extent throughout the rest of the autumn as well.

for-ya-naturreservat-natcbcf67f8.d: Forøya Nature Reserve consists of an island at the outer edge of Malangen in Balsfjord municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 4 June 2004 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 15 July inclusive, access to land within the conservation area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a medium-sized island with its associated flora and fauna. The area is of particular importance for seabirds.’

kobbevagen-naturreservat-nat4dc64559.d: Kobbevågen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the Malangs Peninsula in Tromsø municipality, Troms. The nature reserve is situated on the shores of Balsfjorden and has Ramsar Site status due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1995 to conserve a large intertidal zone and its associated marine areas. The heart of the area is the intertidal zone, together with the adjacent shallow marine areas, marshes and beach areas in Kobbevågen. Several small streams and rivers flow through the area, which also includes a small but well-developed salt marsh.

malselvutl-pet-naturreservat-nat25ff6a28.d: The Målselv Estuary Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site at the mouth of the River Målselva in the municipalities of Målselv and Lenvik in Troms. The reserve was established in 1995 ‘to preserve a river estuary with constantly changing islets and sandbanks, salt marshes and floodplain woodland adapted to this natural environment, and the rich birdlife, with particular emphasis on the large concentration of dabbling ducks during the migration seasons’. Most of the area lies in Målselv, whilst a few small areas to the north are in Lenvik. The estuary where the river flows into Målselvfjorden is a large delta dominated by sand, with deciduous woodland and wooded islets. The salt marshes have distinctive vegetation, and there are floodplain forests of grey alder and birch.

rakkfjordmyran-naturreservat-natf2c7b03e.d: Rakkfjordmyran Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tromsø municipality in Troms. It comprises a bog area in the Rakkfjord watercourse in the north of Kvaløya. The area is dominated by nutrient-poor hill bogs, interspersed with streams, pools and patches of woodland. The reserve has a rich and varied birdlife and is one of the county’s most important breeding grounds for wetland birds. Several bird species that breed here are otherwise uncommon in this part of Troms. The reserve was established in 1983 to preserve a fine example of a bog area typical of the region.

sagelvvatn-naturreservat-nata7833d01.d: Sagelvvatn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Balsfjord municipality in Troms. It comprises a wetland area at the southern end of Lake Sagelvvatnet, consisting of bogs and marshes around the mouths of two small rivers, the Tømmerelva and the Langvasselva. It is a valuable stopover site for many different wetland birds, some of which breed here. Species include the horned grebe, teal, wigeon, common snipe and black-headed gull. The reserve was established in 2004 to conserve a distinctive area of bogs and wetlands.

spilder-ya-naturreservat-nat56de0f6c.d: Spilderøya Nature Reserve consists of an island in Malangen in Balsfjord municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 4 June 2004 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 15 July inclusive, access to the land within the conservation area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a medium-sized island with its associated flora and fauna. The area is of particular importance for seabirds.’

kvitsanden-landskapsvernomrade-nat3b8757.d: The Kvitsanden Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Røros municipality in Trøndelag. The area was established in 2004 and covers 0.4 km². The Landscape Conservation Area is one of the largest areas of wind-blown sand in the Norwegian interior.

bj-rnmyra-naturreservat-natd130a1d2.d: Bjørnmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tillermarka, in Tiller, Trondheim. The nature reserve was established on 21 December 1990 to protect a clearly defined raised bog situated in the lowland region of Trøndelag. The area covers 121.6 dekar. The bog consists mainly of ombrotrophic vegetation, including plants such as bog rush, white bog sedge and bear’s-beard. See the habitat mapping. The purpose of the protection is to preserve a type of habitat that is rare in Norway. Bjørnmyra derives all its nutrients from rainwater and is classified as a precipitation bog. Plant species that survive on very little nourishment thrive here. The bog contains elements of an eccentric raised bog.

bymarka-naturreservat-natfa3020b1.d: The Bymarka Nature Reserve covers an area in the heart of Trondheim’s urban forest, stretching from County Road 715 in the north along the Trondheim Fjord and southwards between Gråkallen and Storheia. The area is characterised by various types of spruce forest, including mountain forest, as well as bare mountain slopes. The area bears the marks of past selective felling and grazing.

hukkelvatna-naturreservat-natfa9f9308.d: Hukkelvatna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Trøndelag. It comprises Hukkelvatna (Storhukkelvatnet / Litlhukkelvatnet) and the surrounding marsh and wetland areas, situated in Midtre Gauldal municipality. It was designated a nature reserve by royal decree on 23 December 1983. The area covers 10,450 dekar, of which 1,100 is water. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an important wetland area with its associated flora and fauna. It is one of the largest wetland areas in Sør-Trøndelag.

lauglolia-naturreservat-nat7d048da5.d: Lauglolia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Trondheim, just above Gaulosen and south-west of the village of Ringvål. The nature reserve was established on 16 December 2001 to protect a fine elm forest with thermophilic flora and coarse coniferous woodland. The elm forest in the area is among the largest and most lush in the Trondheim region. The area was originally a pure deciduous forest reserve, but was expanded in 1992 to include 45 da of spruce-dominated forest. The spruce forest in the nature reserve is coarse-grained and fast-growing, with trees over 25 m tall.

leira-naturreservat-natb1f37424.d: Leira Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Trondheim, situated between the Nidelva and Leira rivers. The nature reserve was established on 6 February 1987 to protect an area of deciduous forest consisting of grey alder and some elm. The elm trees are, in some cases, quite large, and the concentration of this species is greatest in two areas: one at Nedre Leirfoss, and one halfway between Nedre Leirfoss and Øvre Leirfoss. In the very south of Leira Nature Reserve, there are also some ash trees.

r-rmyra-naturreservat-nat94e94cd8.d: Rørmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the outskirts of Bymarka in Trondheim. The nature reserve was established on 21 December 1990 to protect an eccentric raised bog with a rich variety of flora, situated in the lowland region of Trøndelag. The bog is rich in species, including bog myrtle, bog crowfoot, meadow sedge, bog rush, mountain chickweed and brown sedge. The ombrotrophic parts of the bog are dominated by dwarf birch and heather.

garbergmyra-naturreservat-nate94b131b.d: Garbergmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Orkland municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 December 1990. Garbergmyra is situated near Garberg Farm, just south of County Road 65 between Storås and Rindal. The reserve covers an area of 322 dekar. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a mire that is highly diverse in terms of flora and vegetation within the region, as well as to preserve a hay-meadow mire associated with the nearby listed farmstead, Garberg Farm. Garbergmyra is an old hay-meadow, and there are still remains of at least one hayloft on the site. The vegetation consists mainly of bog (85 per cent), including hill bogs, flat bogs and open bogs, but also some woodland such as pine forest, swamp forest and tall-herb forest.

grandefj-ra-naturreservat-nat3ce076b8.d: Grandefjæra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Ørland municipality, Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated in a shallow tidal flat area between Grande/Beian and Hoøya/Uthaug on the western side of the Ørland Peninsula, and has Ramsar site status due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1983 to preserve an internationally important wetland area with its vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife. It is the largest of the four sub-areas in the Ørland wetland system, which collectively encompass all sides of the Ørland Peninsula. Grandefjæra is the largest contiguous intertidal/shallow-water area in the county. The shoreline stretches for 10 km, and as the waters are very shallow, 5–6 km² are exposed at low tide.

grytdalen-naturreservat-nat0d517c84.d: Grytdalen Nature Reserve is a Norwegian nature reserve in Orkland municipality in Trøndelag. Covering 39,000 daa, Grytdalen Nature Reserve is one of the largest nature reserves in Norway. The entire reserve forms part of the Songli Experimental Farm estate. Grytdalen comprises the upper part of the valley that runs from Krokstadøra south-eastwards towards Songli. For the most part, the valley is gentle and wide, with large marshes at the valley floor. The bedrock consists mainly of granodioritic gneiss. There are also some meta-aracose and quartz gneiss, biotite schist and greenstone. Grytdalen was originally one of the first 16 areas proposed as a national park in Norway, in 1964. The area was eventually protected by Royal Decree No. 4.

grytelva-naturreservat-natabfdf9de.d: Grytelva Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hitra municipality, Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated in the north-west of Hitra and is home to one of the island’s two salmon rivers, the Grytelva. The reserve was established in 2001 to preserve a lush coastal pine forest with a rich variety of flora, of which there is otherwise little on Hitra. The area was extended by approximately 1,000 dekar in November 2016.

havmyran-naturreservat-nataa6673f9.d: Havmyran Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hitra municipality, Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated in an area of heathland, marsh and bog in the south-western inland part of the island of Hitra, and has had Ramsar site status since 2002 due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1982 to preserve a large, representative and unspoilt landscape of bogs and heathland with oceanic vegetation, and an important wetland area with a rich and interesting birdlife. 12 km² of the reserve consists of bogs – mainly nutrient-poor rainwater bogs – 3 km² comprises ponds and other freshwater bodies, whilst the remainder is solid ground. The terrain is relatively flat and lies between 60 and 80 metres above sea level. The bedrock consists of diorite, a deep-seated rock that weathers slowly.

helgebostad-ya-naturreservat-natb2c4c26a.d: Helgebostadøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hitra municipality, Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated on Helgebostadøya, facing Straumsfjorden. The reserve was established in 1992 to preserve one of the very few herb-rich pine forests right on the coast of Central Norway, as well as to preserve an interesting mosaic of vegetation.

krakvagsvaet-fuglefredningsomrade-nat57a.d: The Kråkvågsvaet Wildlife Reserve is a protected habitat in Ørland municipality, Sør-Trøndelag. The reserve comprises some coastal areas, but consists mainly of a shallow sea area between the islands of Storfosna and Kråkvåg, and to the north of Storfosna, which is an important breeding, resting and wintering area for seabirds and migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1983 to safeguard a vital part of Ørland’s wetland system and to preserve the area’s rich birdlife, particularly with regard to breeding and wintering loons, divers, diving ducks, waders and other waterbirds. It is the second-largest of the four sub-areas within the Ørland Wetland System Ramsar site, and the only one of the four that is not located on the Ørland Peninsula itself.

sj-myrasen-naturreservat-natab131aea.d: Sjømyråsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hitra municipality, Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated south of Lake Melandsjøen. The reserve was established in 1987 to protect one of the richest hazel woodland sites in Trøndelag and to safeguard an area of value for education and research.

sol-ya-naturreservat-nat5403957f.d: Soløya Nature Reserve consists of an islet at the mouth of Mistfjorden in Heim municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 9 September 2005 as one of eight reserves in Trøndelag. The reserve is part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, access to the land within the protected area is prohibited. The reserve neighbours the Røstøya Nature Reserve. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched island and the adjacent marine area with its natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding ground for seabirds.’

stormyra-inntian-naturreservat-nat01bf8d.d: Stormyra, Inntian Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the island of Inntian in Frøya, Trøndelag. The protected area is a coastal bog situated inland on the island. Like most similar coastal bogs, the bog has been used for peat extraction, but to a limited extent. The reserve was established in 1990 to preserve a typical coastal raised bog with areas of open terrain.

vassholmen-naturreservat-nat9d51d03e.d: Vassholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on Frøya in Trøndelag. The area has been designated a nature reserve because it serves as a breeding ground for seabirds. The area comprises Vassholmen and Vasskjæret, along with the adjacent islets to the west of Humlingsværet.

austdalen-naturreservat-nat6aecd6c4.d: Austdalen Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area in Roan, in Åfjord municipality, Trøndelag. The area is protected ‘to safeguard an exceptionally large and well-developed stand of deciduous forest in the outer parts of Trøndelag and to preserve a very beautiful landscape’. The area contains elm and hazel woodland of considerable size, as well as rock and forest-edge vegetation. It provides a habitat for passerines and roe deer. The reserve was designated to preserve an exceptionally large and well-developed stand of broad-leaved deciduous forest. The reserve lies at an altitude of 25–200 metres above sea level, south-east of County Road 6312, near the centre of Roan.

buholman-naturreservat-natf45542ce.d: The Buholman Nature Reserve comprises an area near Seter in Osen municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 9 September 2005 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, access to land on Kvitholmen, Sandholmene, Persholmen and Buholmen is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a distinctive and virtually untouched island and coastal area and the adjacent marine area with its natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding, moulting and wintering site for seabirds.’

hosensand-landskapsvernomrade-nat7ac6815.d: The Hosensand Landscape Conservation Area, which includes a protected area for plant life, is a conservation area on Stokkøya in Åfjord municipality in Trøndelag. It has been designated to ‘protect a site with very special qualities as a botanical conservation area, including a drifting sand field which, as far as is known, is unique in this part of the country, and a juniper forest and birch forest which, due to the shell sand substrate, form quite exceptional vegetation types’.” The conservation area is situated in Hosenvika on the western side of Stokkøya, facing out towards Frohavet. The juniper population is large and one of the largest in Norway. Coastal plants, southern thermophilic species and mountain plants all grow on the rocky outcrops by the beach, including demanding plant species such as the red-winged orchid.

h-ydalmoan-naturreservat-nata925e73a.d: Høydalmoan Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area in Norddalen, in Åfjord municipality, Trøndelag. The area is protected ‘to preserve an area of coastal spruce forest’. The reserve lies at an altitude of 70–230 metres above sea level, south of Børmarka, south-east of County Road 715 and the Norddalselva river.

inner-vargfossnesa-naturreservat-natffe4.d: The Inner Vargfossnesa Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area on the Lonelva river in Roan, in Åfjord municipality, Trøndelag. The area is protected ‘to preserve a large, varied and typical bog landscape for this region, as well as to protect a beautiful landscape’. The reserve is a large bog area surrounded by mixed woodland. It was designated to preserve a large, varied and typical bog landscape. The Hofstaddalselva and Lonelva rivers are protected from hydropower development. The reserve lies at an altitude of 305–3,300 metres above sea level, east of County Road 715 and north-east of the Momyra Nature Reserve.

kariholet-naturreservat-natd60764fa.d: Kariholet Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area in Åfjord municipality in Trøndelag, around 2 km north-east of Årnes. At the heart of the area lies Hestskodalen, a stream valley that forms a sharp bend known as Kariholet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 17 December 2010, as part of efforts to conserve boreal rainforest. The reserve lies at an altitude of 60–230 metres above sea level on the hillside between the Norddalselva river and Vasstrandfjellet. The protected area covers 789 dekar and features elements of boreal rainforest.

melstein-naturreservat-natd393d6bf.d: Melstein Nature Reserve consists of a group of islands in Frohavet in Ørland municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 9 September 2005 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 March to 31 July inclusive, access to land within the conservation area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a distinctive and virtually untouched island and coastal area and the adjacent marine area with its natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding, moulting and wintering site for seabirds and is of scientific importance.’

momyra-naturreservat-natf789a282.d: Momyra Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area at the head of Norddalen in Åfjord municipality in Trøndelag. The area is protected ‘to preserve a type of bog that is typical of the coastal forest region and which is becoming rare both in Norway and in Europe’. Coastal and mountain plants coexist in the area, which also features a small lake that is in the process of developing from a lake into a bog. The reserve was designated as part of the efforts to preserve Central Norway’s finest extensive mire complex. The reserve lies at an altitude of 240–260 metres above sea level, just east of County Road 715, near the watershed between the Norddalselva and Hofstaddalselva rivers.

murudalen-naturreservat-nat94312698.d: Murudalen Nature Reserve is situated in a narrow, south-westerly-facing valley 6 km east of Botngård and west of Lake Gjøljavatnet in Bjugn municipality in Trøndelag, south of County Road 710. The area was designated a nature reserve in 2007 as part of efforts to conserve boreal rainforest. It lies at an altitude of 100–300 metres above sea level. The area covers 250 dekar. The area is covered by map sheet 1522 I in the ‘Norway 1:50,000’ map series. UTM coordinates: 32V 542600 E 7072600 N.

ma-yan-naturreservat-nat8160f0f5.d: The Måøyan Nature Reserve comprises an area off Skjørafjorden in Åfjord municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 9 September 2005 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, access to land within the conservation area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a distinctive and virtually untouched island and coastal area and the adjacent marine area with its natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding, moulting and wintering site for seabirds.”

skjerva-naturreservat-nat306b5ddc.d: Skjerva Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area in Åfjord municipality in Trøndelag. It is situated between Sørlia near Vardfjellet and Kringlathølen on the River Skjerva, around 4 km south-east of Årnes. The area was designated a nature reserve on 31 August 2001, as part of efforts to conserve boreal rainforest. The reserve lies at an altitude of 45–305 metres above sea level. The protected area covers 618 dekar and contains elements of boreal rainforest. There are Red Listed bogs in the area.

sves-ya-naturreservat-natcfc69f3a.d: Svesøya Nature Reserve consists of an island in Svesfjorden in Osen municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 9 September 2005 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, access to land within the conservation area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched island with its natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding site for seabirds.’

moffen-naturreservat-nat30375cb5.d: Moffen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve established by decree on 3 June 1983. The nature reserve comprises the island of Moffen and a marine zone extending 300 metres from the shore or skerries at low tide. The area is an important resting place for walruses. The protected area consists of an almost circular triangular island with a lagoon in the centre, shaped almost like an atoll. It lies immediately north of 80 degrees north latitude and is often ice-free during the summer.

grima-naturreservat-nat4637bf6c.d: Grima Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gulen municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. It is situated on the island of Grima, just north of Byrknesøyna. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve coastal marshland in the archipelago of Sognesjøen. The area covers 1,483 dekar and accounts for approximately a quarter of the total area of the six nature reserves in Gulen, excluding the Vassøyane Nature Reserve. The mire resources here and on eastern Sløvåg are categorised as highly important. On 18 June 2004, the Government presented a separate conservation plan for mires in Sogn og Fjordane, under which 20 mire areas in the county were protected. Grima is one of the larger areas in terms of size. The background to this was White Paper No.

kvern-yna-naturreservat-nat7e7d5e1f.d: Kvernøyna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve (bird sanctuary) in Gulen municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect breeding seabirds in the archipelago in Lake Sognesjøen. The area covers 1,427 dekar, which accounts for around a quarter of the total area of the six nature reserves in Gulen municipality, excluding the Vassøyane Nature Reserve. A total of 907 daa of land and 520 daa of water are protected. In 1993, the Government adopted the Seabird Conservation Plan, which designated 57 bird reserves totalling 11 km² along the coast of Sogn og Fjordane. The plan is based on the initial conservation proposals from 1977, as well as White Paper No.

lage-islendingen-naturreservat-nat7a6e36.d: The Låge Islendingen Nature Reserve consists of a skerry in Fensfjorden, north of Storestonga. The nature reserve is situated in Austrheim municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014: Black-backed gull, 2 pairs.

mag-yane-naturreservat-nate3b753d2.d: The Mågøyane Nature Reserve comprises an area near Storøyna in Solund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the oystercatcher, turnstone, black-tailed godwit, grey gull, lesser black-backed gull, common gull, common tern and red-billed tern.

oddeholmane-naturreservat-nat9e35e3e0.d: The Oddeholmane Nature Reserve comprises an area near Steinsundøyna in Solund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the eider, oystercatcher, turnstone, grey gull, black-backed gull and red-billed tern.

ramsbarden-naturreservat-nateb2fe591.d: Ramsbarden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gulen municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect breeding seabirds on the islets in Lake Sognesjøen. The area covers 173 dekar, of which 86 daa is land and 87 daa is water. In 1993, the Government adopted the Seabird Conservation Plan, which designated 57 bird sanctuaries totalling 11 km² along the coast of Sogn og Fjordane. The plan is based on the initial conservation proposals from 1977, as well as White Paper No. 68 (1980–81) ‘Conservation of Norwegian Nature’, which set out the objective of conserving a representative selection of natural areas in Norway, and the first consultation proposal on seabird conservation in Sogn og Fjordane from 1984. Between 1977 and 1988, 350 seabird sites in the county were surveyed and assessed.

vass-yane-naturreservat-nate25d4919.d: Vassøyane Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gulen municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve wetland areas with breeding sites and seabird habitats in the archipelago at the southernmost tip of Lake Sognesjøen. The reserve encompasses the Vassøyane archipelago in the far south-west of the municipality, near the border with Fedje municipality to the south. The area covers 6,180 dekar (6.18 km²), of which 1,870 dekar is land area, making it by far the largest protected area in the municipality. The Vassøyane Nature Reserve is almost twice as large as the other six nature reserves in Gulen combined. Sheep grazing, heather burning and the harvesting of seaweed and kelp on the islands are explicitly permitted under licence, with the exception of any landing on the islands during the breeding season.

gitter-y-naturreservat-nat06e55a43.d: Gitterøy Nature Reserve comprises Gitterøya, east of Røvær in Haugesund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 May 1982 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important seabird site with the plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to the seabirds and their breeding grounds.’

indrev-r-naturreservat-nat4bf77a14.d: Indrevær Nature Reserve consists of an islet east of Bjørkevær in Haugesund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 May 1982 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important seabird site with the plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to the seabirds and their breeding sites.’

skareholmen-naturreservat-nat7c4fe6e7.d: Skåreholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet north-west of Haugesund in Haugesund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 7 May 1982 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important seabird site with the plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to the seabirds and their breeding grounds.’

fjellheia-naturreservat-natf6b919a9.d: Fjellheia Nature Reserve comprises an area near Tvedestrand in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 26 June 2009 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests and rich deciduous woodlands. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a special area of varied deciduous and mixed woodland with all its natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular scientific importance as it contains especially species-rich forest types. Significant natural values are linked both to favourable growing conditions and to well-developed natural forest characteristics, with old, hollow deciduous trees and a large amount of dead wood from various tree species.”

nordskogen-naturreservat-nate5889284.d: The Nordskogen Nature Reserve comprises an area on Sandøya in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 13 December 2002 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna. Among its special qualities is the fact that the area is a relatively untouched coniferous forest in the outer archipelago of Southern Norway.’

lille-halsholmen-naturreservat-nat976e91.d: The Lille Halsholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve within Sandøyfjorden in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

lille-lestholmen-naturreservat-nat2a745b.d: Lille Lestholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve located within Lyngør in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

stakketoskj-ret-naturreservat-nat37adaf1.d: Stakketoskjæret Nature Reserve is a nature reserve near Tvedestrand in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

storskj-ret-naturreservat-nat000c5972.d: Storskjæret Nature Reserve is a nature reserve near Tvedestrand in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

st-ttv-ret-naturreservat-natf30ab236.d: Støttværet Nature Reserve is situated west of Støtt in Meløy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 11,436 dekar, of which 8,396 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect a special natural area on the coast of Sør-Salten.

teksmona-naturreservat-nate34679d5.d: Teksmona Nature Reserve is situated on the island of Teksmona in Meløy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 2,421 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a largely unspoilt, oceanic-influenced coniferous forest area, with vegetation typical of the region.

flatv-ret-varkgard-naturreservat-nat3cdc.d: The Flatværet/Varkgård Nature Reserve is situated in Meløy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises the islets of Flatværet and Varkgård, north of Bolga and west of Meløya. The area covers 16,584 dekar, of which 14,474 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to preserve a unique stretch of coastal nature, with interesting flora and a distinctive and vulnerable fauna.

galteskj-r-biotopvernomrade-natccf5e7c5.d: Galteskjær is a small islet situated right next to the shipping lane north-west of Lindøya in Oslo. Since 19 June 2009, the islet has been designated a protected biotope under the Wildlife Act. The islet is also known as ‘Galten’ on commercial nautical charts.

blafjell-naturreservat-natfa16f405.d: Blåfjell Nature Reserve is situated in Kjekstadmarka, west of Heggedal in Asker municipality. The reserve is bordered to the south-west by a power line. The bedrock in the area consists mainly of coarse granite, which is exposed in many places. The highest point is Brennåsen, 361 metres above sea level. On the higher ground, old and coarse pine forest predominates, whilst spruce dominates on the slopes in the form of blueberry spruce forest. The soil is generally thin, but in places with deeper soil, low-herb spruce forest and tall-shrub spruce forest occur. There is also some dead wood, but with relatively low continuity. Consequently, there are few indicator species associated with dead wood.

gardlaush-gda-naturreservat-natb3bf9226.d: The Gardlaushøgda Nature Reserve encompasses most of Gardlaushøgda in the very south of Bærumsmarka, right next to Stein Farm. The bedrock consists, amongst other things, of rhomboid porphyry, whilst to the east there is sandstone and limestone. This results in relatively calcareous soil and provides the basis for a rich flora. The summits are dominated by sparse blueberry spruce forest with patches of pine, some of which are quite large. Down the slopes, the proportion of deciduous trees gradually increases, and there are calcareous forests, elm-lime forests, tall-herb spruce forests and rich swamp forests. There are also, particularly in the south and east, vegetation types associated with landslide areas, featuring hazel and lime.

glitrelia-naturreservat-natb5a35e27.d: The Glitrelia Nature Reserve encompasses part of the hillside on the western side of Oppegårdskollen, as well as a large part of Djupdalen north of Glitre in Hakadal. Spruce is the dominant tree species, but the area is not particularly homogeneous and comprises a variety of forest and habitat types. Here, there is common blueberry spruce forest to the east, rich swamp forest to the north, and in places the vegetation is characterised by calcareous bedrock, including low-herb spruce forest. There are also many other tree species: pine, birch, aspen, hazel, ash, elm, grey alder, black alder, willow, rowan, hawthorn, juniper, spindle and yew. Wildlife and vegetation are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting is also permitted in accordance with other regulations.

lillomarka-naturreservat-nata161191c.d: The Lillomarka Nature Reserve comprises Grytedalen, stretching from Store Gryta in the south-west up to Nordre Langvann on the border between the municipalities of Oslo and Nittedal, as well as most of Slengfehøgda. Grytedalen is a rift valley with relatively steep valley sides, and in the south-east of the area there are some larger hills. The vegetation is varied, comprising both mature spruce forest on good-quality soil and deciduous forest with some pine, as well as, in places, broad-leaved deciduous forest. The bedrock consists of a type of syenite (nordmarkite). The purpose of the nature reserve is to protect a stretch of rare and vulnerable natural habitat of particular value for biodiversity.

rudskampen-naturreservat-nat817441ef.d: Rudskampen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated on the Rudskampen and Blekktjernflaka hills in the west of Nannestad municipality. Between these hills lie small valleys and marshy areas. The reserve was extended on 20 December 2023 to form the Rudskampen and Råbjørn Nature Reserve. The bedrock consists of ekerite, which is largely made up of nutrient-poor minerals (alkaline feldspar). The vegetation is dominated by blueberry spruce forest, but in places there are also small-fern spruce forest and large-fern spruce forest, as well as heather-and-skin-leaved pine forest at the summit. In damp areas within the depressions, there are also some spruce swamp forests and pine swamp forests. Other species present include birch, aspen, rowan, juniper and willow.

skotjernfjellet-og-snellingsr-ysene-natu.d: The Skotjernfjellet and Snellingsrøysene Nature Reserve lies at an altitude of 420–651 metres above sea level along the municipal boundary between Lunner and Nannestad in Akershus, in the far north-east of Oslomarka. The reserve was established through the expansion and amalgamation of two former nature reserves. It is therefore one of the largest forest reserves in the region. The terrain comprises large and small marshes, a few lakes, small valleys and flat hills. The highest point is Skotjernfjellet, at 651 metres above sea level. The bedrock consists of biotite syenite, feldspar and their associated porphyries. The topsoil is relatively thin. The reserve comprises a large, contiguous area of old-growth forest of particular importance for biodiversity.

enga-naturreservat-natedb1015e.d: Enga Nature Reserve is situated in Meløy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve consists of a small area just north-east of Engavågen and covers an area of 254 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect a northern elm population.

smavatnan-naturreservat-nat731283b0.d: Småvatnan Nature Reserve is situated north-east of Halsa in Meløy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 405 dekar, of which 215 dekar is land and 190 dekar is freshwater. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a rich and productive wetland area of great regional conservation value and to protect the associated birdlife and plant life, particularly given the area’s importance as a resting, foraging and breeding ground for a number of wetland birds.

kjerkvatnet-naturreservat-natdf0fecf0.d: Kjerkvatnet Nature Reserve is situated just south and west of Evenes Airport (Harstad/Narvik Airport, Evenes). The nature reserve covers an area of 2,235 dekar, of which 1,020 dekar is land. The area is protected to preserve a rich wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife. In 2011, the reserve, together with four other nature reserves, was designated a Ramsar site under the collective name ‘Evenes Wetland System’.

nauta-naturreservat-natb3ee866c.d: The Nautå Nature Reserve is situated just east of Evenes Airport (Harstad/Narvik Airport, Evenes). The nature reserve covers an area of 410 dekar, of which 70 dekar is land and 340 dekar is freshwater. The area is protected to preserve a rich wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife. In 2011, the reserve, together with four other nature reserves, was designated a Ramsar site under the collective name ‘Evenes Wetland System’.

gjelamyra-naturreservat-nat7750a0bf.d: Gjelamyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Aure municipality. It comprises an area south of Årvågfjorden, near the county border with Trøndelag. The area was designated a nature reserve on 13 December 1996. The reserve is included in the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a well-developed mire area with a rare type of precipitation mire. The site is of value as a national type area.’

eidsholmen-naturreservat-nat51084f4c.d: Eidsholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet off Eidestranda in Aure municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 August 2010 (approved on 28 May 2010) as one of 36 reserves in Møre og Romsdal. The reserve forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 31 July inclusive, access to the land within the protected area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of particular value for biodiversity and which contains threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats. The virtually untouched islet, together with the surrounding marine area and its naturally associated flora and fauna, constitutes an important breeding site for seabirds, including the common gull, other gull species and terns.”

kurefjorden-naturreservat-nat1d24de3f.d: The Kurefjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Moss and Råde, in Østfold. The nature reserve is situated in the shallow Kurefjorden between Larkollen in Rygge and Oven in Råde, and has had Ramsar site status since 1985 due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1978 because it is an important area for resting ducks and waders during their spring and autumn migrations, including teal, mallard, ruff and dunlin. Around 250 different bird species have been recorded here, and the area is considered the most important site for migratory waders in the Oslofjord region. Kurefjorden is a shallow fjord arm. No part of the fjord is deeper than 7 metres.

fugl-ya-naturreservat-natc093eb03.d: Fugløya Nature Reserve is situated on the western side of Fugløya in Gildeskål municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 5,482 dekar, of which 1,742 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding ground for birds, particularly puffins.

nupen-naturreservat-nat6e7080a5.d: The Nupen Nature Reserve is situated in Gildeskål municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses the island of Nupen, the southernmost island in the Fleinvær archipelago. The area covers 663 dekar, of which 512 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding site for seabirds.

skalsvikleira-ystleira-naturreservat-nat.d: The Skålsvikleira/Ystleira Nature Reserve is situated at Skålsvika in the municipality of Gildeskål in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 442 dekar, of which 324 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to preserve a site featuring unusually diverse salt marshes with significant topographical variation and well-developed ecological zones.

asen-kjeldalen-naturreservat-nat2e5bb051.d: The Åsen–Kjeldalen Nature Reserve is situated north-east of Inndyr in Gildeskål municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 931 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve an area with a generally rich flora, including rare and highly demanding plant species and the presence of hazel, as well as the associated fauna.

ya-langholmen-landskapsvernomrade-med-pl.d: The Øya/Langholmen Landscape Conservation Area is situated north of Inndyr in Gildeskål municipality in Nordland. The landscape conservation area is designated as a protected area for plant life, as it comprises a coastal landscape with varied seashore vegetation and rich fens. The area was established in 2002 and covers 1.4 km², of which 0.6 km² is marine area.

greipingen-naturreservat-nat343c1f7b.d: Greipingen Nature Reserve consists of an islet west of Rongøy in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland county on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (18 June): Black-tailed Godwit 3 pairs, Grey Gull 123 pairs, Great Cormorant 9–10 pairs, Lapwing 2 pairs, Common Pochard 70 individuals.

ullebroten-naturreservat-natf97d29d6.d: Ullebroten Nature Reserve consists of two islets north of Ulløyna in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. No breeding species were recorded in 2014.

teistholmen-naturreservat-nat59adf69a.d: Teistholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet to the west of Hjartøyna in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. Recorded breeding species in 2014 (18 June): Black-backed Gull, 2 pairs.

bredmosen-naturreservat-nat4edb7edb.d: Bredmosen Nature Reserve is a bog area in Marker municipality that was designated a protected area in 1978. The technical description is a precipitation bog, characterised as a concentric raised bog. The reserve covers an area of 665 dekar, of which 528 dekar is bog.

gjerimasan-naturreservat-nate1b63839.d: Gjerimåsan Nature Reserve consists of a bog area in the Romeriksåsene hills, on the border between the municipalities of Gjerdrum and Nannestad. Low, coniferous-forested mounds of solid ground surround the bog. Gjerimåsan is a precipitation bog divided into two large sections by a water-fed channel. Both sections have an eccentric structure, meaning that the bog’s highest point lies close to one of its edges. Gjerimåsan is representative of precipitation bogs in the central part of Akershus, and the purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a precipitation bog of this typical type. The eastern species, spruce sedge, is found here.

langrasta-naturreservat-nat4ed3a893.d: Langrasta Nature Reserve is situated just north of Kroksund, in the north of Marker municipality in Østfold. The area comprises the two mires, Langasta and Fossemyra, which lie in a bedrock depression surrounded by spruce forest. The mires are of the minerotrophic type and feature rich mire vegetation with many calcium-demanding species. It is therefore assumed that there is calcareous sand in the area which releases calcium-rich water. Calcareous mires in areas with acidic rock types, such as the bedrock in Østfold, are very rare. There are very few intact rich fens in Eastern Norway at all, and Langrasta is the only one that is protected in Østfold.

rismyr-naturreservat-natbe1dadf1.d: Rismyr Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated south-west of Konnerud, north of Sagdammen. The reserve encompasses Ristjern and the surrounding marshland, as well as the woodland north of the pond. The reserve was designated on 20 June 1986. According to maps, the area covers 47 dekar, whilst the land area is 50 dekar. The reserve’s regulations state that vegetation, dead shrubs and trees are protected. It is forbidden to remove plants or introduce new plant species. Motorised traffic is also prohibited in the area. Camping and pitching tents are also prohibited. Picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. The bog is a rich bog, with elements of a rain-fed bog. Bog asphodel is an important species in the area. The slope to the north of the bog is covered in rich low-herb spruce forest.

bremsa-naturreservat-nat10c22e8e.d: Bremsa Nature Reserve is situated approximately five kilometres south-east of Mjøndalen, north of Sagdammen. The bedrock consists of Cambrian-Silurian sediments. The river flowing between Bremsetjern and Sagdammen, along with the surrounding marshland, is also part of the reserve. According to the map, the area covers 51.9 dekar, whilst the land area is 55 dekar. The boundaries of the reserve are to be marked on the ground. The reserve’s regulations state that vegetation, dead shrubs and trees are protected. It is forbidden to remove plants or introduce new plant species. Motorised traffic in the area is also prohibited. Camping and pitching tents are also prohibited. Picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. The reserve was designated on 20 June 1986.

leirvika-naturreservat-nate7d70d9c.d: Leirvika Nature Reserve is situated at the innermost part of Beiarfjorden in Beiarn municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,071 dekar, of which 656 dekar is water. The area is protected to preserve a unique salt marsh area with its naturally associated flora and fauna. Leirvika Nature Reserve is situated right next to the Arstadlia–Tverviknakkan Nature Reserve.

vahcanjohka-naturreservat-nat163157a5.d: The Váhcanjohka Nature Reserve is situated in Beiarn municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located at Kyskmoen on the western side of the Gråtå Valley and covers an area of 525 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve an area with a variety of forest types and a rich diversity of species.

bjormyr-naturreservat-nat8d67bee6.d: Bjormyr Nature Reserve is a 40-dekar nature reserve in Arendal municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, the same day that Lusemyr Nature Reserve was also established. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to preserve a flat, precipitation-fed mire dominated by bear’s-beard. A specific type of bog which, in Southern Norway, has only been reliably recorded at altitudes of 100–300 metres above sea level.” The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. “Frequent occurrences of heather and pine islets, as well as low-lying soft-ground hollows.” The area lies at an altitude of approximately 55 metres above sea level.

breivigskj-ret-naturreservat-natd0c32c42.d: Breivigskjæret Nature Reserve consists of an islet near Grimstad in Grimstad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

bu-yskj-ra-naturreservat-nat538aeebf.d: The Buøyskjæra Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets off Buøya in Arendal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

eikasen-naturreservat-natea57ab07.d: Eikåsen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Tvedestrand in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 December 2015 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area of rich and varied deciduous and mixed woodland. The nature reserve contains low-herb oak woodland, old mixed oak woodland and boreonemoral mixed woodland. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity, especially in terms of several demanding old-growth forest species associated with oak and aspen. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to further develop them.”

farmyrane-naturreservat-nat51576892.d: Farmyrane Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Iveland municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, at the same time as Kyrelitjønn Nature Reserve in Valle municipality, Storslåtta Nature Reserve in Evje and Hornnes municipalities, and Melandsmyrane Nature Reserve in Iveland municipality. The County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder is the managing authority for the area, which covers 211 dekar and lies at an altitude of approximately 405 metres above sea level. The nature reserve is a bog area two kilometres south of Eptevatn, east of County Road 291 (Aust-Agder). Farmyrane is a flat bog with several small ponds. The area was previously a hay meadow. The area is surrounded by sparse heathland and pine forest. The most common plants are bear’s-beard, peat moss, warty peat moss and dwarf peat moss.

gulspettvannet-naturreservat-natd51a2ca9.d: The Gulspettvannet Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Sandnesfjord in Risør municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 13 December 2002 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna. Notable features include the fact that this is a coastal area in a gently undulating landscape with old and varied woodland, containing habitats that are extremely important for many species.”

hammartj-nn-naturreservat-natd9f19446.d: Hammartjønn Nature Reserve comprises an area near Hammertjenna in Risør municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 December 1977 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests/rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a well-developed and unusually large occurrence of black alder forest (Lycopo-Alnetum (glutinosae) and Carici (elongatae) – Alnetum (glutinosae))’

haugsjaknipen-naturreservat-nat7c79211f.d: Haugsjåknipen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the border between Tvedestrand municipality and Froland. The area was designated a nature reserve on 13 December 2002 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna’. Notable features include a high density of key elements such as old trees, deadwood and hollow trees, as well as a very high level of biodiversity with many threatened species.”

hellesunds-gr-nningen-naturreservat-nat5.d: The Hellesunds-Grønningen Nature Reserve comprises Store and Lille Grønningern and the surrounding area. The nature reserve is situated in Lillesand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

hell-yholmen-naturreservat-natab0af803.d: Helløyholmen Nature Reserve consists of islets off Helløya in Lillesand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April up to and including 31 July, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

hovassdalen-naturreservat-natca3ea650.d: Hovassdalen Nature Reserve is a protected coniferous forest area around Lake Hovatn in Hovassdalen, on the moorland west of Lake Dåsvatn in Dåsvannsdalen, Hornnes. A small part of the reserve, approximately 2,000 dekar, lies across the municipal boundary into Åseral. The reserve was designated by Royal Decree on 9 July 1993. It covers a total area of approximately 11,900 dekar. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a large coniferous forest area, the boundaries of which include most of the catchment area of this water-rich valley, with bogs in the flat valley floor. The pine forest remains intact, partly as large trees on the valley slopes, and partly as sparse woodland on bogs and heathland with shallow soil.

javnesmyrane-naturreservat-nat3cb9e566.d: Jåvnesmyrane Nature Reserve is a 162 dekar nature reserve in Vegårshei municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, the same day that Våjemyrane Nature Reserve was also established.
