The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to safeguard large, intermediate flat bogs of limnogenic character with a high diversity of species and rare plants.’ The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a mire reserve. “It is regularly flooded when the water level in the Vegår river is high. The area exhibits great variation in nutrient conditions, ranging from nutrient-poor, precipitation-dominated mires to rich mire complexes and limnogenic areas. A floristically rich mire, including, amongst others,

kongsholmen-naturreservat-nat475a5956.d: Kongsholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet near Homborsund in Grimstad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

lille-danmark-naturreservat-nat15f13f92.d: The Lille-Danmark Nature Reserve consists of an islet off Hesnes in Grimstad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

lusemyr-naturreservat-nataec3996a.d: Bjormyr Nature Reserve is a 146 dekar nature reserve in Arendal municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, the same day that Bjormyr Nature Reserve was also established. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. “The aim of the conservation is to safeguard one of the largest remaining undrained mires in the coastal areas of the county. The bog illustrates the connection between groundwater bogs and precipitation bogs and features distinctive southern vegetation types.” The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. “Flat bogs with small areas of flat, tussock-dominated precipitation bogs. Suboceanic flora.” The area lies at an altitude of approximately 151 metres above sea level.

lyngholmen-naturreservat-nat760f23fc.d: Lyngholmen Nature Reserve consists of the islet of Lyngholmen, situated at the southernmost tip of Lillesand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

malmen-naturreservat-nat9984a417.d: Malmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet near Homborsund in Grimstad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

mannskj-ret-naturreservat-nata854117c.d: The Mannskjæret Nature Reserve protects a breeding area for seabirds in Risør municipality. The area was designated a protected area on xxx and is included in the seabird conservation plan. Access is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

melandsmyrane-naturreservat-nate67232bd.d: Melandsmyrane Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Iveland municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, at the same time as Kyrelitjønn Nature Reserve in Valle municipality, Storslåtta Nature Reserve in Evje and Hornnes municipalities, and Farmyrane Nature Reserve in Iveland municipality. The County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder is the managing authority for the area, which covers 233 dekar and lies at an altitude of approximately 373 metres above sea level. The nature reserve is a bog area at Meland, three kilometres north-east of Birketveit. Melandsmyrane consists of flat bogs and gently sloping hill bogs. The area alternates between sparse pine forest and open bog.

olashei-naturreservat-nat78bbdcae.d: The Olashei Nature Reserve is situated in Lillesand municipality, Agder county. In total, the reserve covers an area of approximately 5,050 dekar spread across nine forest properties. The reserve is named after the Olashei ridge, which lies at the centre of the protected area and is the reserve’s highest point, at 162 metres above sea level. Olashei Nature Reserve was designated by Royal Decree on 9 July 1993 as part of the Conservation Plan for Coniferous Forests. The managing authority for Olashei Nature Reserve is the State Administrator in Agder. A management plan has been drawn up for the reserve. The Norwegian Nature Inspectorate is responsible for monitoring the reserve.

porsmyr-naturreservat-nata01ec552.d: Porsmyr Nature Reserve is a 169 dekar nature reserve in Birkenes municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to preserve flat mires with areas influenced by both precipitation and groundwater.’ The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. “Myrtle, bog bilberry, bog heather and bear’s beard are common species. It was a hay-making bog until around 1945.” The area lies at an altitude of approximately 247 metres above sea level.

reismyr-naturreservat-nat1278359a.d: Reismyr Nature Reserve is a 453 dekar nature reserve in Åmli municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to preserve a mire area with a particularly wide variety of hydrotopography and mire types. Gently sloping hill bogs are dominant, but string bogs, nutrient-poor flat bogs and many shallow bog pools are also present.” The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve.

r-rvikholmene-naturreservat-natccacf36e.d: The Rørvikholmene Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets off Strengereid in Arendal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

torehei-naturreservat-nat4975c401.d: Toreheia Nature Reserve is situated in Lillesand municipality in Agder county; it was established in 1977 and extended in 2017 and 2022 to 670 daa. The area lies in the north-west of Lillesand municipality and borders the areas adjacent to Sørlandsparken. To the east, it is a short distance from the Isefjærfjord. The area is a gently undulating woodland landscape dominated by oak, interspersed with small marshes. Several footpaths run through the area. Torehei, Toremyr, Torevann, Toredalen and Lille Toredalen are place names within or just outside the reserve. The nature reserve was originally established by royal decree on 9 December 1977 under the name Røyrmyråsen Nature Reserve. It was subsequently extended on two occasions.

r-yrtveit-naturreservat-nat7cd176de.d: Røyrtveit Nature Reserve was the first nature reserve to be designated in Aust-Agder. This took place on 21 July 1917. The nature reserve is a coniferous forest in the municipalities of Evje and Hornnes, covering 49 dekar, and consists of a wooded hill at an altitude of 520–550 metres above sea level. 76 per cent of the area is coniferous forest, described in Naturbase as a ‘primeval forest area dominated by spruce’. The County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder is the managing authority for the area. Anders Danielsen surveyed the site in June 1949. In addition to spruce, he found some oak trees, aspen, birch and pine. On the forest floor, he found blueberries, lingonberries, cowberries, heather, wood sorrel, woodruff, the grasses common bent-grass and blue moor-grass, some sedge species, wood anemone, yellow iris, bluebell and woodrush.

seilskj-rene-naturreservat-nate91ca1e4.d: The Seilskjærene Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets off Vågsnes in Arendal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

skiftenes-naturreservat-nat709180cb.d: Skiftenes Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Grimstad municipality. It comprises an area by Lake Holvannet. The area was first designated as the Skiftenes Deciduous Forest Reserve on 30 November 1973, covering an area of approximately 350 dekar. The reserve was renamed Skiftenes Nature Reserve following an expansion to approximately 710 dekar on 17 December 2010. On 6 December 2024, it was further expanded to 1,251 dekar in accordance with the regulations. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing roads and paths.

skoger-y-lyngholmen-naturreservat-nat610.d: The Skogerøy-Lyngholmen Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets off Skauerøya in Lillesand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

stangholmen-naturreservat-nata51060c2.d: Stangholmen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Flatholmen in Risør municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

store-makholmen-naturreservat-nat54c994f.d: The Store Måkholmen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Håøya in Grimstad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April up to and including 31 July, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

storemyr-naturreservat-natb6e22a9e.d: Storemyr Nature Reserve is a 154 dekar nature reserve in Froland municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to preserve a combination of flat bogs, initial string bogs and gently sloping hill bogs.’ The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. “The lowest-lying location for dwarf birch in Aust-Agder.” The area lies at an altitude of approximately 175 metres above sea level.

stormyrlia-naturreservat-nat85b19d4c.d: Stormyrlia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vegårshei municipality. The area was designated on 19 December 2008 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a large area of highly productive old-growth forest in the lowlands, and the area’s flora and fauna. Notable features include spruce and mixed forests with a great deal of dead wood and a few large, hollow deciduous trees.”

storslatta-naturreservat-nat0f42349b.d: Storslåtta Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Evje and Hornnes municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, the same day that Kyrelitjønn Nature Reserve in Valle municipality, Vestedjan Nature Reserve in Bygland municipality, Farmyrane Nature Reserve and Melandsmyrane Nature Reserve in Iveland municipality were also established. This reserve is a bog reserve. It covers an area of 506 dekar and is dominated by a community of poor fen with a firm mat, which covers more than 90 per cent of the area. Along the stream running through the bog, there are patches of floating peat. The most common plants are bear’s-beard and warty sphagnum moss. The rationale for the conservation is to preserve a typical bog area for the region in the west of Aust-Agder and the east of Vest-Agder at an altitude of 300–500 metres above sea level.

sundholmen-naturreservat-nat6825da34.d: Sundholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet near Homborsund in Grimstad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

tranmyra-naturreservat-nat30411a1a.d: Tranmyra Nature Reserve is an 84 dekar nature reserve in the east of Gjerstad municipality in Agder, on the border with Telemark. It was established on 10 October 1986, the same day that Fjosbumyra Nature Reserve was also established. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to preserve a unique combination of soil- and precipitation-influenced areas, which is reflected in the vegetation. At the same time, it contains an area with string/flark formations that are rare...” The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. It is a ‘mire area with a mosaic of hummocks and firm-mat depressions. There are some distinct flark formations and ridges in the south-east.’

vardeheia-naturreservat-nat1eb32c31.d: Vardeheia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åmli municipality. It comprises an area to the west of the River Nidelva, near the border with Telemark. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2011, extended on 15 December 2017 and again on 6 December 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to protect an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large and varied occurrence of low-lying boreonemoral–southern boreal broadleaf forest and rich mixed forest, including hollow oaks.’

vestedjan-naturreservat-nat551cd151.d: Veststedjan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bygland municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986 as Vestedjan Nature Reserve, at the same time as Kyrelitjønn Nature Reserve in Valle municipality, Storslåtta Nature Reserve in Evje and Hornnes municipalities, and Farmyrane Nature Reserve and Melandsmyrane Nature Reserve in Iveland municipality. On 15 August 1988, the name was changed to its current name. The County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder is the managing authority for the area, which covers 250 dekar and lies at an altitude of approximately 520 metres above sea level. The nature reserve is a marshland area west of Skomedal on the western side of Byglandsfjorden. The area is characterised by slopes covered with sparse pine forest and some birch.

vajemyrane-naturreservat-nat1f9bd528.d: Våjemyrane Nature Reserve is a 290 dekar nature reserve in Vegårshei municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, the same day that Jåvnesmyrane Nature Reserve was also established. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to safeguard a mire area characterised by great diversity and distinctive hydrotopography. Here, within a relatively small area, there are initial string bogs, gently sloping hill bogs, flat precipitation bogs, moist pine forests and blue-topped wet meadows.” The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. ‘Relatively nutrient-poor. It is also a habitat for wetland-associated bird species, including a breeding site for the rare little crake.’

ytre-lauvrak-naturreservat-nata02f4f0b.d: Ytre Lauvrak Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Froland municipality in Agder, established in 2013. The Government established the nature reserve on the following grounds: ‘Ytre Lauvrak Nature Reserve in Froland municipality, Aust-Agder county, has a remarkably large and varied population of old, large deciduous trees such as lime, oak and elm. The area is home to abundant populations of a number of threatened species, particularly fungi, lichens and insects.”

stre-ertholmen-naturreservat-nat99137d2c.d: The Østre Ertholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet off Ulvøysund in Lillesand municipality. The islet was designated a nature reserve on 28 March 1980, but had already been protected on 6 July 1944, and was protected again on 3 May 1946. The nature reserve forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, all access is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

agneskj-ret-naturreservat-nat89965c81.d: Agneskjæret Nature Reserve consists of an islet south of Spangereid in Lindesnes municipality. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

bj-rnen-naturreservat-natab52372a.d: The Bjørnen Nature Reserve consists of the islet of Bjørnen near Hille in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 2 October 1981 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

brattholmene-naturreservat-nat7d04f450.d: The Brattholmene Nature Reserve comprises the two Brattholmene islands and the surrounding marine areas in Kvåsefjorden in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. Access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

guleholmane-naturreservat-natcaab7d1b.d: The Guleholmane Nature Reserve comprises Indre and Ytre Guleholmen and Småskjæran in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

hummerholmen-naturreservat-natac957f50.d: Hummerholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet just south of the mouth of the Audna river in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

kile-naturreservat-natf21d4500.d: Kile Nature Reserve is a forest conservation area by Kilefjorden, in the north of Vennesla municipality in Vest-Agder. Kile is a mixed forest area with a rich variety of tree species. There are old trees within the area, particularly spruce, aspen, birch, willow and yew, but also a few old lime, oak and pine trees. Red-listed species of fungi and lichens have been recorded within the nature reserve. Kile Nature Reserve was established in December 2015.

kjorten-naturreservat-natc4514316.d: Kjorten Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets west of Hille in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

klovholmene-naturreservat-natea3c68f5.d: The Klovholmene Nature Reserve consists of two islets off Hille in Lindesnes municipality. olavskj-ran-naturreservat-nat925c7c7c.d: The Olavskjæran Nature Reserve consists of a couple of skerries off Svinør in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. paulen-naturreservat-nat2bff3be5.d: Paulen Nature Reserve is a woodland reserve in Vennesla municipality in Vest-Agder. The area was designated a protected area in 1993 to preserve a diverse and relatively undisturbed coniferous forest area with a wide variety of habitat types, ecosystems and species. Following a forest fire in 2007, the area was extended by 859 daa. Parts of the nature reserve bear clear signs of the fire.

revsund-naturreservat-natb616fa28.d: Revsund Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Kvåsefjord in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. There is a ban on access to the reserve from 15 April up to and including 15 July. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

r-dholman-naturreservat-nat2228c758.d: The Rødholman Nature Reserve consists of two islets off Abelnes in Flekkefjord municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

skjede-naturreservat-nate6b9965c.d: Skjede Nature Reserve comprises an area on the inner side of Flekkerøya in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. Access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

skj-ringen-naturreservat-natb7bc182a.d: Skjøringen Nature Reserve comprises the southern part of the island of Skjøringen in Lindesnes municipality. The area lies within the Oksøy-Ryvingen Landscape Conservation Area and is the nature reserve closest to Pysen. It was designated a nature reserve on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

skorskog-naturreservat-natd2493f60.d: Skorskog Nature Reserve is a 141 dekar nature reserve in Åseral municipality. It was established on 21 June 1996. The area lies at an altitude of just over 500 metres above sea level on Flåheia in Austerdalen, on the west bank of the River Logna, just west of the hamlet of Torsland. The conservation authority for the area is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. ‘The purpose of the conservation is to safeguard the natural environment in an area with a large high-altitude population of yew trees in the inland regions of Vest-Agder.’ In addition, holly also grows in Skorskog Nature Reserve.

skotholmen-naturreservat-nat50254b0e.d: Skotholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet in Skjernøysundet in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

slettingen-naturreservat-nat9431b0de.d: The Slettingen Nature Reserve comprises Slettingen, Lille Slettingen and Makrellskjæret, south of Ryvingen Lighthouse in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

smaskj-ran-naturreservat-natd3ff086a.d: The Småskjæran Nature Reserve consists of three islands in the Småskjæran group in Ramslandsvågen, in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April up to and including 31 July, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

store-lyngholmen-naturreservat-nat2fb0d2.d: The Store Lyngholmen Nature Reserve comprises an area east of Ny-Hellesund in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. Access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

store-vengelsholmen-naturreservat-natf89.d: The Store Vengelsholmen Nature Reserve consists of Store Vengelsholmen near Skjernøy. It is surrounded by the Oksøy-Ryvingen Landscape Conservation Area and is situated in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 March 1980 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

svingervann-naturreservat-natc925b3a8.d: Svingervann Nature Reserve is an area in Vågsbygdmarka, west of Kristiansand. Since the reserve was established in 2005, it has been expanded in 2017 and 2019. It covers (as of 2021) 2.5 square kilometres. The area is a popular destination for outdoor recreation, and the forest is old and virtually untouched by human intervention. There is a wide variety of vegetation types here, with lush deciduous forest and swamp forest in the valleys, and sparse pine forest on the hills. In places, the forest is dominated by oak; in some areas, there is also rich swamp forest with some yew. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic is prohibited. Furthermore, cycling and horse riding are only permitted on roads and paths marked for this purpose on the conservation map.

s-ndre-eggv-r-naturreservat-nat56167216.d: The Søndre Eggvær Nature Reserve consists of an islet situated between Udøy, Landøy and Valløy. The nature reserve is located in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

terneholmen-og-gr-nningen-naturreservat-.d: The Terneholmen and Grønningen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Grønningen Lighthouse in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. There is a ban on access to the reserve from 15 April up to and including 15 July. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

udvare-naturreservat-nat7106ea33.d: The Udvåre Nature Reserve comprises Udvåre in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April up to and including 31 July, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

vassland-naturreservat-nat833fa85e.d: Vassland Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Lyngdal and Hægebostad. It comprises an area east of Lake Gletnesvatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a forest area near the western boundary of the contiguous spruce forest in Southern Norway. Vassland is well suited to undergoing natural succession towards a contiguous spruce forest.’

asgjerdstigfjell-naturreservat-natd3c863.d: Asgjerdstigfjell Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Drangedal municipality. It comprises an area north of Toke. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 December 2017. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to protect a forest area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich deciduous forest, with elements of rich scree-slope lime forest, low-herb spruce forest, low-herb mixed forest and a rich occurrence of yew. Furthermore, the purpose of the nature reserve is to protect an area of particular scientific value due to the presence of a large number of old and large oaks, including hollow oaks and dead oak wood, as well as rare and threatened species of lichen and wood-dwelling fungi associated with oak.

bj-nnknuten-naturreservat-nat5aa5738b.d: The Bjønnknuten Nature Reserve is situated in the municipalities of Drangedal and Kragerø, south of Lower Toke and west of Farsjø. The majority of the area lies on land owned by Statskog SF, with a smaller portion on private land. The reserve is a forested area comprising lowland woodland, with elements of rich forest types such as broad-leaved deciduous woodland and low-herb woodland. The area is of particular scientific value due to the presence of old mixed oak woodland with large, coarse-grained oaks, as well as rare and threatened species of wood-dwelling fungi associated with oak and aspen.

bj-nntjenn-naturreservat-nat16a2d1bc.d: Bjønntjenn Nature Reserve forms the highest part of a low-lying hilly landscape in the south of Drangedal, near the border with Gjerstad. Pine and spruce are the dominant tree species, but to the west there is a mixed forest with a rich variety of tree species and elements of elm, lime, Norway maple and hazel. The area has a high level of biodiversity, and nine different and rare wood-dwelling fungi have been recorded.

bratterudskogen-naturreservat-nat9bf53ad.d: The Bratterudskogen Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Tinnsjøen in Tinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 1 December 2015 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest area of particular importance for biodiversity due to the presence of mature lowland coniferous forest with a high proportion of boreal deciduous forest and, in part, broad-leaved trees. The area has particular scientific value due to the presence of rich low-herb coniferous forest, such as low-herb pine forest and low-herb spruce-limestone forest, as well as the presence of yew at its northernmost limit in Telemark.”

bratt-ykollen-naturreservat-natbd6e4bd1.d: Brattøykollen Nature Reserve is the high hill in the north-western part of Brattøy, which is the largest island in the inner part of Kilsfjorden in Kragerø. Brattøy is home to one of the country’s largest populations of the rare species known as the shrubby vetch, which belongs to the pea family.

brokefjell-naturreservat-nat29e1fd1a.d: The Brokefjell Nature Reserve comprises an area between Seljordsvatnet and Kviteseidvatn in the municipalities of Kviteseid and Seljord. The area was originally designated as a nature reserve on 9 July 1993 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The area was extended through a new designation on 24 June 2025 to 26,702 dekar and now extends down to Kviteseidvatnet. The old conservation regulations stated that the purpose of the conservation was ‘to preserve a large, well-defined coniferous forest area with long forest continuity and a distinct old-growth forest structure’. The conservation regulations of June 2025 state that the purpose of the conservation is “to safeguard an area which a. represents specific types of nature in the form of fire-affected, high-altitude coniferous forest and rich mixed forest with plenty of deadwood b.

brarfjell-naturreservat-nata246f514.d: Brårfjell Nature Reserve is situated in Kleivgrend in Fyresdal, approximately 9 km north-west of Fyresdal town centre. The area lies on the east-facing slope of Nautefjell/Brårfjell, just north-west of Bondalsvatn. The area is of scientific value due to rare forest types such as elm-lime forest and low-herb forest, as well as many species of vascular plants, mosses, fungi and lichens that are rarely seen.

bukkholmskj-ra-naturreservat-nat02c53ec3.d: The Bukkholmskjæra Nature Reserve comprises two islets east of Bukkholmen in Hellefjorden, near Kragerø, which are protected. The islets serve as a breeding ground for seabirds. The conservation status also applies to the waters between the islets and the waters within a distance of 15–50 metres from the shore.

bumyr-naturreservat-natb485126f.d: Bumyr Nature Reserve is situated just north of the western end of Stølefjorden in Kragerø. Bumyr is an undisturbed coastal fen. Species found here include bog myrtle, bog myrtle, bell heather and blue moor grass. The area is surrounded by bare rock and low-productivity pine forest, meaning that the forest has little capacity to produce timber.

bur-ytjern-naturreservat-nat00dc1d14.d: Burøytjern Nature Reserve is situated on Skåtøy. The pond is connected to the sea and is exposed at low tide. The reserve borders the Burøy Archipelago Park. The nature reserve is an important wetland area surrounded by salt marshes and some black alder swamp forest, and is significant as a habitat for many bird species.

demningane-og-gravtjernasen-naturreserva.d: The Demningane and Gravtjernåsen Nature Reserve is situated in Bergsbygda and comprises a bog area (Demningane) and a landscape featuring rich deciduous woodland. The bedrock consists of larvikite. The area is protected to preserve specific types of habitat, namely rich deciduous forest and groundwater bogs, and to safeguard an area of high biological diversity featuring rare and endangered species of fungi and lichens.

furuholmen-naturreservat-natf2197883.d: Furuholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet north of Håøya in Porsgrunn municipality and the surrounding sea area within a 50-metre radius. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, access to the entire reserve is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

geitholmsundet-naturreservat-natadd2ee11.d: The Geitholmsundet Nature Reserve comprises four islets in Geitholmsundet, east of Gumøy in Kragerø. These are protected. The islets serve as a breeding ground for seabirds, and the protection also extends to the surrounding marine areas within a distance of approximately 50 metres from the shore.

gjermundsholmen-naturreservat-natcfd8529.d: Gjermundsholmen Nature Reserve is situated in the north-western part of Gjermundsholmen, near Stathelle. The bedrock consists of calcareous rocks from the Cambrian and Silurian geological periods (Cambrian–Silurian), and a steep, west-facing slope runs through much of the reserve. The area is home to several rare species of lichen, as well as the habitat types of seashore and calcareous grasslands, where several rare plant species are found.

gjuvet-naturreservat-natc12741db.d: Gjuvet Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Tinnsjøen in Tinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 25 November 2016 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest area of particular importance for biodiversity due to the extensive presence of intact low-lying forest in the southern boreal zone. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular scientific value due to the presence of old-growth natural forest on calcareous bedrock, with elements of broad-leaved deciduous forest and high biological diversity, including a number of rare and threatened species.”

grytdalen-natureservat-nat58c5ebe6.d: Grytdalen is a nature reserve situated in the north-west of Drangedal municipality in Telemark. Grytdalen was designated a nature reserve by royal decree on 9 July 1993.

gr-ssas-naturreservat-nat34ca4e94.d: Grøssås Nature Reserve is a wooded area situated in a hilly landscape sloping down towards Hellestveitvann and Mevann in Bamble. The reserve comprises an area featuring partly steep south- and south-east-facing slopes leading down to the lakes. On these south-east-facing slopes, there is an almost continuous area of low-herb oak (lime) woodland.

gardemma-naturreservat-natd314f95f.d: Gårdemma Nature Reserve is a shallow bay with adjacent land situated at the innermost part of the Bamble section of Vollsfjorden, south of Langøya. The area is distinctive, featuring salt marshes and varied coastal marsh vegetation, where several rare plant species can be found.

hellesengtjenna-naturreservat-nat6851980.d: Hellesengtjenna Nature Reserve is situated in the north-east of Skåtøy and comprises Hellesengtjenna and the surrounding coastal areas. The area features well-developed coastal marsh vegetation, where one can find the rare plant, the common sedge, as well as other rare species.

hellestveit-naturreservat-nat75e8d1d0.d: Hellestveit Nature Reserve is situated north of the Herreelva river, just east of the outlet of Lake Hellestveitvannet. The reserve comprises an area of low-herb oak woodland on a south-west-facing slope. Hellestveit is one of the north-easternmost occurrences of the ‘Sørland oak forests’ and is therefore of botanical interest. The bedrock in the area consists of gneiss.

hitter-d-naturreservat-nate0017190.d: The Hitterødbekken Nature Reserve comprises an area by Frierfjorden in Porsgrunn municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 30 June 2006 and extended on 7 December 2018. It forms part of the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity due to the presence of lowland forest in the boreonemoral zone and rich forest types such as low-herb-heather limestone forest, low-herb oak forest and limestone lime forest, and with elements of limestone spruce forest and open, shallow-soiled limestone terrain. The area is of particular scientific value due to the presence of several rare and threatened species of fungi and lichens, as well as a stream ravine where several nationally rare species of caddisflies have been found.

horsfjellmyra-naturreservat-natfd381acc.d: Horsfjellmyra Nature Reserve is situated north-east of Gonge in Bamble municipality. The reserve consists of a complex of mires comprising both rain-fed mires and groundwater mires. In the southern part of the reserve, there is a large, treeless area of rain-fed mire that is raised and higher than the surrounding terrain (raised bog). This is a rare complex of bogs in this part of the country. The bedrock in the area consists of gneiss with amphibolite veins.

h-stad-naturreservat-nat65cf279b.d: Hæstad Nature Reserve is situated north-west of Spokkeligrend and Veum Church in the northern part of Fyresdal. The reserve comprises a large area of hills and mountains east of Mjåvatn and north of the Hæstad farm. To the north, the reserve borders Tokke. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a large, contiguous area of largely undisturbed and pristine spruce forest.

j-njiljo-naturreservat-natc06cf59c.d: Jønjiljo Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Notodden municipality. It comprises an area to the west of Tinnsjå. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a varied and largely unspoilt spruce-dominated coniferous forest area as a supplementary area in the region.’

kammerfossasen-naturreservat-natda3f9776.d: The Kammerfossåsen Nature Reserve is situated north-west of Kragerø town, near Sluppan. The reserve comprises Sluppantjern, a steep, wooded area in Kammerfossåsen to the north of the pond, and a small marshy area on the south side of the pond.

kiletjernene-naturreservat-natcbe54970.d: The Kiletjernene Nature Reserve is situated south-west of Lake Haukedalsvannet in Bamble. The reserve is a nutrient-rich, overgrown fen surrounding two lakes, and is an important area for wetland birds. To protect breeding birds, access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July.

kjeholmskj-ra-naturreservat-nat26ac72a9.d: The Kjeholmskjæra Nature Reserve consists of five islets and the surrounding waters north-west of Kjeholmen in Kragerø. The reserve is situated in Haslumkilen, north of Ospvika. The area is a breeding ground for seabirds.

kj-r-naturreservat-nat4a0debed.d: Kjær Nature Reserve is situated in a south-east-facing valley just north of the E-18 at Kjær in Bamble. The reserve consists of three types of broadleaf forest: low-herb oak forest, elm-lime forest and a small black alder swamp forest. The tree layer is dominated by undisturbed oak woodland and, in places, large lime trees. The ground is mainly covered with grass.

knipheia-naturreservat-nat7265121b.d: Knipheia Nature Reserve is situated on the north side of Barlandskilen and is a south-facing, species-rich slope, owing to the calcareous soil in the area. Knipheia features stands of low-herb oak woodland and elm-lime woodland with patches of shrubby vetch.

korseikasen-naturreservat-natb568acc5.d: The Korseikåsen Nature Reserve is situated on the municipal boundary with Larvik, east-north-east of Langangen in Porsgrunn municipality. Following its expansion in December 2021, the reserve now covers not only Korseikåsen but also the western part of Lamåsen to the north and the northern part of Plankåsen to the south. The reserve contains the following habitat types: black alder swamp forest, rich mixed lowland forest and old, nutrient-poor deciduous forest, with a high proportion of old, hollow oak trees. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but the regulations provide for a number of exceptions. Among other things, it is permitted to gather edible mushrooms and berries, as well as to carry out ‘careful clearing of small shrubs’ in connection with big game hunting. Campfires are permitted in accordance with other legislation.

krogshavn-naturreservat-nat583b3607.d: Krogshavn Nature Reserve consists of an islet off Langesund in Bamble municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

kraka-naturreservat-nat226eef53.d: Kråka Nature Reserve is a protected island situated south-west of the Kråka archipelago, off Ivarsand/Prisgrunn Bay in Bamble municipality. The island is a breeding ground for seabirds; the protected status also applies to the waters within a distance of 0–50 metres from the shore. As in many seabird reserves, access is prohibited both on land and at sea in the Kråka Nature Reserve from 15 April to 15 July.

kralen-naturreservat-nat353a5c43.d: Krålen Nature Reserve is situated in the very north of Fyresdal municipality, near the border with Tokke municipality. The reserve is located on the east-facing slope of Skipsfjødd, north-west of Skredvatnet. The reserve is a forested area comprising an old coniferous forest. The area is of particular scientific value due to the presence of the endangered fungus species Lapland polypore and other species of wood-dwelling fungi that are endangered and rarely seen.

lagmannskj-r-naturreservat-natc610f78b.d: Lagmannskjær Nature Reserve consists of a skerry in Frierfjorden off Balsøya in Skien municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

lauvh-gdi-naturreservat-natc456f75f.d: The Lauvhøgdi Nature Reserve comprises an area near Miland in Tinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 2 September 2005 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched natural area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area is of particular educational and scientific significance as a representative example of high-altitude spruce forest in the region and is distinctive for its old-growth natural spruce forest, a high proportion of deadwood and many species of wood-dwelling fungi, as well as patches of tall herbaceous vegetation.”

lindheim-mannsmyr-naturreservat-nat87150.d: The Lindheim-Mannsmyr Nature Reserve is situated at an altitude of approximately 200 metres above sea level, south-west of Sannidal, on the county border with Agder. Of the total area of approximately 160 daa, around 95 daa consists of bogland. The solid ground consists mainly of bare rock. The rock is covered by pine forest, with heather, grey moss and reindeer lichen in the undergrowth. The area is a large and varied mire complex, most of which is flat mire.

middagskollen-naturreservat-nat597fc9ed.d: Middagskollen Nature Reserve was established in 2002 and is situated north-west of Kvelde, on the eastern side of Farris in Larvik municipality. The reserve comprises coniferous and mixed woodland, and a wide variety of lichens, fungi and mosses. There are numerous species that live on old and dead trees. On the peaks of the nature reserve there is pine forest, whilst the south-facing slopes are dominated by oak. The pine forest contains large, old trees. In the ravines there are spruce forests, with some heat-loving deciduous trees such as lime, ash and maple. Falkeberget is one of the prominent peaks in the reserve. Here there is a rock face, partly overhanging, at a height of around 150 metres. This is one of the nesting sites for gyrfalcons, which have their territory around the northern end of Farris.

m-lslia-naturreservat-natcfd89c46.d: Mælslia Nature Reserve comprises an area near Mæl in Tinn municipality. The area was designated on 2 September 2005 and extended on 7 December 2018 and 20 December 2023; it forms part of the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to protect an area of particular importance for biodiversity due to its large and species-rich areas of old-growth forest on calcareous bedrock. The area has particular scientific value as a reference area for herb-rich coniferous forest with a significant proportion of deadwood and mosaic-like mixed forest in the middle boreal and boreal zones. The area is home to several rare species of lichen and wood-dwelling fungi.’

nustad-naturreservat-nat3f33ea2c.d: Nustad Nature Reserve is situated north-west of Langesund and is a biodiverse area that remains largely untouched. The reserve consists mainly of calcareous pine forest, but one can also find patches of other vegetation types, such as black alder swamp forest. On the cliff edge facing the sea, twisted pine trees grow. The area is also home to the climbing plant ivy.

omborsnesholmane-naturreservat-nat8a78a0.d: The Omborsnesholmane Nature Reserve consists of three large islets and a number of skerries between Stathelle and Findal in Bamble. The area is a breeding ground for seabirds, and the reserve also includes the surrounding waters within a distance of 30–50 metres from the islets. As in many seabird reserves, access by land and water is prohibited within the reserve from 15 April to 15 July.

omnflug-naturreservat-nat0c546de2.d: The Omnflug Nature Reserve covers an area south of Blefjell in Notodden municipality, around Harvedalsvatn and Breivatn, stretching from Omnsflug in the south up the mountainside towards Sigridsfjell in the north. The bedrock in the area consists mainly of light-coloured quartzite, which results in relatively nutrient-poor soil. However, on the scree slopes below Omnflug in the far south, there is richer vegetation, with patches of deciduous broad-leaved forest. The reserve thus encompasses a gradient ranging from southern boreal vegetation right up to the upper mountain forest belt. The conservation values are particularly linked to a large area with plenty of old-growth forest and deadwood. Here there are a number of rare and threatened species of wood-dwelling fungi, and in places also a rich flora of vascular plants.

rognholmen-naturreservat-nat081ea6d2.d: Rognholmen Nature Reserve is situated north-west of Stavseng Lighthouse on Skåtøy. The islet is a breeding ground for seabirds; the reserve also includes the marine areas within a 50-metre radius of the shore. As in many seabird reserves, access is prohibited both on land and at sea in the Rognholmen Nature Reserve from 15 April to 15 July.

r-sskleiva-naturreservat-nat9d164456.d: Røsskleiva Nature Reserve forms part of the area stretching from Langesundstangen to Stathelle in Bamble, where some of Norway’s largest contiguous limestone pine forests are found. The area boasts a rich flora, including several rare species, and is also an important outdoor recreation area. The reserve is regarded as the most important reference area for calcareous pine forests in Grenland. Røsskleiva is also worthy of protection in a Nordic context.

selskj-ra-naturreservat-nat50206a76.d: The Selskjæra Nature Reserve comprises the Selskjæra archipelago, which lies north-west of Furholmene at the far end of Fossingfjorden. The nature reserve is a protected area. The islands are a breeding ground for seabirds, and the protection also extends to the waters within a 50-metre radius of the shore. As in many seabird reserves, access is prohibited both on land and at sea in the Selskjæra Nature Reserve from 15 April to 15 July.

skirvedalen-naturreservat-nat8b450d4c.d: The Skirvedalen Nature Reserve consists mainly of a forested valley running north-south between Veggli in Numedal and Rivsfjell in Tinn. The area is of great value as it comprises mature and largely undisturbed coniferous forest, some of which has the characteristics of primeval forest. The area also contains examples of the ‘tall-herb spruce forest’ habitat type, which is on the Red List. The reserve was extended in 2019 and now comprises a large and varied forest area of 24.7 square kilometres. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic is prohibited. Apart from existing roads and paths, cycling and horse riding are also prohibited.

skultrevassasen-naturreservat-nat5d1871a.d: Skultrevassåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Drangedal municipality. It comprises an area to the east of Henneseid. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. Parts of the area had previously been protected in 1916. The reserve was extended on 6 January 1967 and again in 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a varied and species-rich coniferous forest area with a core in a state close to that of primeval forest. The area has a large population of yew trees.’

storkollen-naturreservat-nat2a6ce1b2.d: Storkollen Nature Reserve is situated west of Kragerø town and east of Rekevika. The area is unique in that it boasts a species-rich and rare flora, with an exceptionally large number of threatened and vulnerable fungal species. The area has particular scientific value as a reference area. A reference area is an area where nature develops with minimal human impact, and which can be used as a basis for comparison when assessing the effects of various factors on nature.

storskog-naturreservat-nat921aeb7f.d: Storskog Nature Reserve is a wooded area situated below Raudbergnuten on the north side of Bandak. The area is of particular educational and scientific value as a specialised site for studying how vegetation regrows and changes following a forest fire. Storskog is unique in that it features natural forest with a wide variety of forest types and productivity levels at an altitude of nearly 900 metres above sea level.

stranda-naturreservat-nat3a1e1540.d: Stranda Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Frierfjord in Porsgrunn municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 30 June 2006. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area with its biological diversity in the form of special habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area also has particular scientific value as a reference area and is unique in terms of its calcareous pine forest, calcareous dry hills and highly species-rich calcareous dry grasslands.”

torskholmen-naturreservat-nat396de02a.d: Torskholmen Nature Reserve is situated on the north-western side of Arøya in Kragerø; Torskholmen and the surrounding marine areas within a distance of 50 metres from the shore are protected. The islet is a breeding ground for seabirds. To ensure that the seabirds are not disturbed during the breeding season, access to the reserve is prohibited both on land and at sea from 15 April to 15 July.

trollvann-naturreservat-nat4593adce.d: Trollvann Nature Reserve is situated south-west of Portør, near the border with Agder. The reserve comprises Trollvann itself, as well as the surrounding beach and vegetation areas. The lake is naturally nutrient-rich (eutrophic), but is also likely to be affected by nutrient runoff from agriculture. Around the lake, one can see belts of mature common reed (grass) and the marsh plant common cattail. On the western side there is a fine stand of black alder swamp forest. Trollvann is a good habitat for ducks, and the lake is rich in eel and roach.

valberg-naturreservat-nat6cd2b869.d: Valberg Nature Reserve is situated just east of Lovisenbergkollen and Bjørneknuten, north-east of Kragerø town. The reserve follows the water’s edge to the east down towards the quarry at Valbergåsen. The area is distinctive for its coastal, unspoilt mixed woodland, meaning that conifers and deciduous trees grow together in the same area. The forest is home to several rare plant and animal species and boasts a particularly favourable microclimate.

vestfjorddalen-naturreservat-nate50aefc0.d: The Vestfjorddalen and Øverland Nature Reserve comprises an area near Rjukan in Tinn municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 17 December 2010 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The Bøen Nature Reserve, which was designated in 2005, and the Ingulfsland Nature Reserve, which was designated in 2009, are both included within this nature reserve. On 23 June 2026, the protected area was further extended to also include Øverland. The original conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of particular scientific value as an example of mature mixed coniferous forest with a steep altitude gradient, featuring elements of productive southern boreal mixed forest and rich vegetation types.’

vestre-skj-ret-naturreservat-nat0d0d48af.d: The Vestre Skjæret Nature Reserve consists of a skerry north of Bukkøya in Porsgrunn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

vindfjell-naturreservat-nat76d387ee.d: The Vindfjell Nature Reserve was established in 2010. The nature reserve consists mainly of bare rock and poor soil. Spruce and pine are the typical tree species. The reserve extends from 500 to 622 metres above sea level. The forest has a natural dynamic and is rich in dead wood. Several rare species of birds and fungi have been found in the reserve. Vindfjell Nature Reserve is of great scientific value. The Telemark part of the reserve belongs to Siljan Vicarage, whilst the Vestfold part belongs to Fritzøe Skoger. Vindfjell Nature Reserve is the only protected area in Vestfold whose land area straddles the county border.

abyelva-naturreservat-nat23ed21f6.d: The Åbyelva Nature Reserve is situated at the innermost part of Åbyfjorden in Bamble. The reserve encompasses the lower reaches of the Åbyelva and the river delta itself. The area has intact river mouth vegetation and is distinctive in that it comprises a well-developed river mouth with black alder forest and salt marsh vegetation.

asstranda-naturreservat-nat41cf0179.d: Åsstranda Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Frierfjord in Porsgrunn municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 April 1978 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests/rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a stand of elm-lime forest (Ulmo-Tiletum) that is virtually untouched.’

degarden-naturreservat-natd4533f6c.d: The Ødegården Nature Reserve is situated on Skåtøy, to the west of the Burøytjern Nature Reserve. The area is unique, consisting of old-growth forest close to the coast with plenty of deadwood and a significant proportion of deciduous woodland. Ødegården has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a virtually untouched natural area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes.

lang-ya-landskapsvernomrade-nat90a8f816.d: The Langøya Landscape Conservation Area, which includes protected wildlife and plant life, is an area of limestone bedrock where several rare plant species grow. Many of these species are found only on limestone mountains, including several orchids such as the fly orchid and the spring lady’s slipper. The mountain avens is a mountain plant that has survived here since the end of the last ice age and is not found elsewhere in the lowlands. Langøya is also home to several rare species of fungi, lichens and snails, amongst others, which are found only on limestone mountains. Some of them have names such as the brain truffle, the fan-shaped lichen and the toothed cylinder snail.

m-svasstangen-landskapsvernomrade-nat4e1.d: The Møsvasstangen Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area in Vinje municipality, Telemark. The nature reserve is situated on a headland jutting out into Lake Møsvatnet (919 metres above sea level) and has had Ramsar Site status since 1996, due to its importance for migratory birds. The area was designated a protected area in 1989 to preserve a beautiful, distinctive and largely unspoilt natural landscape featuring interesting deposits from the last ice age, finely formed string bogs, a rich and rare birdlife, and abundant cultural heritage sites from the ironworks. The conservation area is relatively large, comprising a vast expanse of relatively undisturbed bog, some woodland and a few small water bodies. There are various types of bog in the area, ranging from nutrient-poor to nutrient-rich bogs.

kvitskj-rene-naturreservat-natb19671b1.d: Kvitskjærene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Færder municipality, Vestfold. It was established in 1978. Oslo City Council owns Kvitskjærene as part of the Hudø estate. Oslo City Council runs a holiday camp on Hudø. In 1969, around 250 black-headed gulls were resident on the skerries. By 1983, the number had risen to nearly 700. Over the next four years, the number of black-headed gulls fell to 200, and the decline in the population did not stop there. By 1992, there were only around 80 common terns in the reserve, and since 2000 the species has been virtually absent from the Kvitskjærene. Black-backed gulls, oystercatchers, greylag geese, eider ducks and common terns breed in varying numbers in the reserve.

borrevannet-naturreservat-nat379a04bf.d: Borrevannet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Horten municipality. It consists mainly of Lake Borrevannet. The area was designated a protected area on 2 October 1981. The reserve is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the particularly rich and interesting birdlife, vegetation and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’

langskj-rene-naturreservat-natc60c5e7c.d: The Langskjærene Nature Reserve was established in 1978. Langskjærene is a group of partly low skerries with rocky outcrops south of Hudø in Tønsbergfjorden, and is an important breeding ground for seabirds. The skerries have a small but stable population of breeding black guillemots. Langskjærene is an important habitat for several species of gulls, ducks, auks and great cormorants. During the winter months, there are substantial populations of seabirds here, particularly tufted ducks, eider ducks, goldeneyes, smews and great cormorants. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to the seabirds and their breeding sites.

kattholmane-naturreservat-nateab4c920.d: The Kattholmane Nature Reserve in Holmestrand was established in 1978. Four years before the reserve was designated, ornithologists found over 400 breeding seabirds on the skerries. These included black-headed gulls, yellow-legged gulls and common terns. Since then, great black-backed gulls have become established in the reserve, at the expense of lesser black-backed gulls and terns. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to the seabirds and their breeding sites.

bj-rk-ya-naturreservat-natc7f269f5.d: The Bjørkøya Nature Reserve on Bjerkøya in Holmestrand municipality was established in 1988. The nature reserve is of great value to research. Brachiopods are a group of animals that resemble mussels. The nature reserve contains good, informative cross-sections of rock types from parts of the Silurian period. The southern parts of Bjerkøya were one of the last habitats for otters in northern Vestfold, and the last known habitat in Vestfold for the red helleborine orchid. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve an important site for understanding the fossil-bearing rocks of the Oslo Field and the associated limestone pine forest worthy of protection.

tangenbekken-naturreservat-nat564ff5cc.d: The Tangenbekken Nature Reserve in Tønsberg municipality was established in 1980. Sometime around 1950, the spruce trees in the area were felled. Today’s deciduous forest is a result of this felling. The forest consists of grey alder-hawthorn, grey alder-ash and elm-lime forests. In the 1990s, Dutch elm disease killed most of the elm trees in the reserve. The active ravine landscape constantly leads to small landslides. Trees caught up in such small landslides remain where they fall, both as living trees and as deadwood. The Tangenbekken Nature Reserve is to be allowed to develop as freely as possible. However, spruce trees must not be allowed to displace the deciduous forest. The stream that gives the reserve its name flows through it. Every autumn, sea trout swim deep into the reserve to spawn.

bergan-naturreservat-nat6e3f1a9a.d: Bergan Nature Reserve was established in 1980 and is a lush, varied broadleaf forest with patches of grey alder-ash forest and elm-lime forest. Ash, elm, lime, oak, hazel, beech, maple and black alder are all broad-leaved trees. These are heat-loving trees that thrive in low-lying, sunny areas. In the Bergan Nature Reserve, the aim is to prevent spruce and beech from becoming dominant. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a lush and varied deciduous forest with elements of grey alder-ash woodland and elm-lime woodland.

vale-prestegardsskog-naturreservat-nat7f.d: The Våle Vicarage Wood Nature Reserve in Tønsberg municipality was established in 1980. Våle Vicarage Wood is a deciduous forest dominated by beech trees. The beech trees form a dense canopy. Once the leaves emerge in spring, very little light reaches the forest floor. Few plants thrive in the shady conditions beneath the beech canopy, but before the leaves block out the light, wood anemones bloom in vast carpets across the beech forest. Wood pigeons nest in hollow trees in Våle Vicarage Wood. There is a floodlit trail running through the reserve. The aim of the conservation area is to preserve a deciduous broad-leaved forest population, including, amongst other things, a large and rare fern-rich variety of beech forest.

breimyr-naturreservat-natf8895088.d: Breimyr Nature Reserve was established in 1980 and is a raised bog, or precipitation bog, which is nourished by rainwater. In the middle of Breimyr there is a low, protruding rock. The rock lies on the municipal boundary between Hof and Holmestrand. Attempts have been made to drain part of Breimyr. Conservation objective: To preserve a concentric raised bog.

langrudmyra-naturreservat-natee6b12ee.d: Langrudmyra Nature Reserve in Tønsberg municipality was established in 1980. Langrudmyra has rich vegetation in places. The rare orchid, the narrow-leaved marsh orchid, has been found in the reserve. Langrudmyra is a flat bog, or groundwater bog. In such bogs, plants are nourished by groundwater. The diversity of species therefore varies according to the nutrient content of the soil. Langrudmyra has moderately rich, and in places rich, vegetation. If the bog is not managed, it will slowly become overgrown with trees. The current rich flora will then disappear. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a bog complex with great variation in vegetation and several floristic features.

tolvmannsmyr-naturreservat-nat8ab9b863.d: Tolvmannsmyr Nature Reserve was established in 1980 and is an intact rain-fed bog. It derives most of its nutrients from rainwater. Closest to Tolvmannsmyrtjern, there are areas of flat bog, whilst the rest of the reserve comprises several domed bog areas. Parts of the bog have underground watercourses. The Tønsberg and Surrounding Area Tourist Association maintains a summer trail across the bog. The trail is board-walked to prevent wear and tear on the bog’s surface. In spring, black grouse leks can be found at Tolvmannsmyr. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a large rain-fed bog complex where distinct domes have developed.

strandvika-naturreservat-natda7e36e7.d: Strandvika Nature Reserve is situated at Yxney in the south of Østerøya in Sandefjord municipality. The tree layer consists largely of black alder. The area was drained shortly before it was designated a nature reserve, but after the designation, the drainage channel was blocked off so that the natural black alder swamp forest could gradually be re-established. Species found here include the sword lily and sweet woodruff. A number of red-listed fungi species have also been found in the area.

nordre-skarsholttj-nn-naturreservat-natb.d: The Nordre Skarsholttjern Nature Reserve is home to the only protected eccentric raised bog in Vestfold. Over the years, the peat moss on the bog, which lies north-east of Nordre Skarsholttjern, has risen above the water table. The bog has taken on a domed shape and is known as a raised bog. In the south of the reserve there is a nutrient-poor waterlogged bog. Great crested newts have been found in the pond and the surrounding pools. This increasingly rare species thrives in small, fish-free ponds and grows to a length of 10 to 15 cm.

robergvannet-naturreservat-natf4d5f54b.d: The Robergvannet Nature Reserve has changed from a lush pond with a black-headed gull colony and swimming waterbirds to a marsh and bog. Robergvannet is surrounded by marshland and lush mixed woodland. The shores are characterised by ongoing encroachment of vegetation. The area is important as a breeding ground for various wetland birds. Despite its limited size, the area is also of great importance as a resting place for migrating ducks. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state, and to protect the rich and interesting birdlife, vegetation and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.

akersvannet-naturreservat-nat092ba8cb.d: Akersvannet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Sandefjord and Tønsberg. It consists mainly of Lake Akersvannet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 2 October 1981. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. Camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area in its natural state and to protect the particularly rich and interesting birdlife, vegetation and other wildlife naturally associated with the area’. The reserve is an important resting place for migratory birds. Ducks, swans and geese find food and opportunities to rest here.

branakollane-naturreservat-nat1ffbecf0.d: Brånakollene Nature Reserve is home to a very rich insect life associated with old trees and dead wood. There is a great diversity of beetle species. All species of wild deciduous trees found in Norway grow in the reserve. From the northern peak of the reserve, there is a fine view over large parts of southern Vestfold and out towards the Oslo Fjord. The peak, which rises 225 metres above sea level, towers above the canopy of the reserve. The area around the summit is so heavily grazed by elk in winter that new forest is unable to establish itself. The nature reserve was previously assessed as being of very high conservation value and as an area for which, at the time, no equivalent had been found in Norway’s beech forest landscape, both in terms of its rich diversity and its unspoilt condition.

napper-dtjern-naturreservat-nat63e5c893.d: Napperødtjern Nature Reserve is a nature reserve featuring a distinctive combination of bog and swamp forest. Around the outlet stream from Napperødtjernet, there is a valuable stand of black alder. To the east of the pond lies swamp forest. Black alder swamp woodland is a rare habitat type.

elva-naturreservat-nat4a7c0f2e.d: Elva Nature Reserve is a large, flat nutrient-poor fen. A flat fen receives water both from rainfall and from the surrounding soil. The nutrient content of the surrounding soil determines the diversity of plant species in a flat fen. If the supply of nutrients is low, the diversity will be low. Elva has low species diversity and is therefore referred to as a nutrient-poor fen. Parts of the fen are transitional to swamp forest, characterised by the presence of cat’s-tail, common sedge and sword lily.

stormyr-naturreservat-nat761e242a.d: The Stormyr Nature Reserve was established in 1980. Stormyr is a species-poor flat bog. Pollen grains from the peat layers deep within the bog could provide us with insights into conditions several thousand years ago. Pollen analyses will be able to reveal when different tree species became established, as well as information about cultivation and settlement. Brown peat moss and coastal peat moss dominate the bottom layer at Stormyr. Peat mosses have the ability to absorb and retain water. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a large complex of nutrient-poor bogs with eruptive deep-seated rocks on the western side of the Oslo Field (the Larvikite Field).

geiter-ya-naturreservat-nat4dde1627.d: Geiterøya Nature Reserve is situated in Langesund Bay, just east of the county border with Telemark; there is an unusually large population of yew trees here. There are 900 of these evergreen trees growing in Geiterøya Nature Reserve, ranging from creeping shrubs to trees 13 metres tall. The yews are scattered across the whole island, but there is a large cluster of trees in the far south. The bedrock in the nature reserve is Cambrian–Silurian. The nature reserve is otherwise characterised by open limestone terrain and limestone pine forest, which are heavily influenced by wind and sea spray. The vegetation is rich in species, including many rare ones, such as the basket plant, deer’s-tongue.

kr-sstjernasen-naturreservat-nat342e212f.d: The Krøsstjernåsen Nature Reserve in Tønsberg municipality was established in 1980. Krøsstjernåsen is a deciduous broad-leaved forest that has retained its original character. The nature reserve is perhaps the most obscure protected area in Vestfold. It lies tucked away at the bottom of a valley with steep slopes. There are neither roads nor footpaths through the area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an elm-lime forest with its original character. The area is of Quaternary geological interest (a ‘skjæljastein’ deposit).

kringlemyr-naturreservat-nat0731f4b7.d: Kringlemyr Nature Reserve in Larvik municipality was designated a protected area in 1980 and is a precipitation bog. It lacks a fringe zone with grassy vegetation. The remains of a small pond are in the process of becoming completely overgrown. Kringlemyr was formed in one of the Lågen river’s old meanders. The formation of the bog began 4,000 years ago, when the river changed its course and one of the meanders became overgrown. The nature reserve is situated west of the Lågen river in the former municipality of Lardal. The bog lies in a delta area with extensive sand and gravel deposits. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a distinctive and rare type of rain-fed bog.

styggas-naturreservat-nat2de5dbaf.d: Styggås Nature Reserve was established in 2006 and consists of two low ridges on the Brunlane coast, halfway between Hummerbakkfjorden and Havnebukta near Nevlunghavn. Most of the reserve shows little or no sign of human activity. The calcareous bedrock provides good growing conditions. Here, there is a coastal calcareous pine forest with species that require calcareous soil. One of these is the rare plant Hartmann’s sedge. The bedrock is around 500 million years old, dating from the geological era known as the Cambrian–Silurian. The conservation objective is to protect this special natural area with calcareous vegetation.

fugl-yrogn-naturreservat-natf92e28ea.d: The Fugløyrogn Nature Reserve is an important breeding and rearing area for seabirds. In 2008, the bird population on the island was surveyed. Common gulls, black-backed gulls, oystercatchers, eider ducks, grey gulls and common terns were all nesting in the reserve. Right in the middle of the Mølen bird sanctuary, between the tip of Mølen and Fugløya (Larvik), lies a low islet. This is Fugløyrogn.

ryggsasen-naturreservat-nat31145762.d: The Ryggsåsen Nature Reserve was established in 2015 and, covering 1,422 dekar, is one of the larger areas of rich beech forest in Vestfold. Large parts are dominated by beech forest, whilst other sections feature a more mixed deciduous forest with a high proportion of beech. The area encompasses many of the broad-leaved forest types found in Vestfold. Ryggsåsen has moderately rich bedrock and fairly weathered rhomboid porphyry rocks. On stony slopes, along outcrops and beneath rock faces, there is rich deciduous forest comprising ash, Norway maple, elm and lime. In between, in more damp areas, black alder forest can be found.
