askilsasen-naturreservat-nat0ff2e486.d: The Askilsåsen Nature Reserve in Holmestrand municipality was established in 2015. Many rare and threatened species have been found in the area, most of which are associated with lying deadwood. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to further develop them.

lunde-naturreservat-nat6bab1279.d: The Lunde Nature Reserve was established in 2015. The area comprises, amongst other things, a particularly large and well-developed area of swamp forest, rich deciduous forest and rich mixed forest. The area also has an unusually high density of deadwood, particularly spruce. There are several rare and endangered habitats and species in the area. The purpose of the nature reserve is to conserve a particularly diverse area of old-growth forest in the lowlands, along with its associated biodiversity in the form of habitats, ecosystems and species, as well as the area’s natural ecological processes.

frebergsvik-naturreservat-nat819c453d.d: Frebergsvik Nature Reserve is a deciduous broad-leaved forest. The reserve is home to the rare vegetation type known as ‘snelle-ash forest’. Snelle-ash forest grows on wet ground with a steady flow of water. The snelle species ‘skavgress’ is a characteristic plant of the snelle-ash forest. In the northern part of the reserve, there are several large yew trees, well-formed with fine crowns. The yew is the tree species capable of reaching the greatest age in Europe, perhaps as much as 2,000 years. Just north of the reserve lies Frebergsvik itself.

storemyr-fagerbakken-landskapsvernomrade.d: The Storemyr-Fagerbakken Landscape Conservation Area covers an area of 276 dekar (traditional unit of measurement) at the south-easternmost tip of the island of Hvasser in Færder municipality, on the western side of the Oslofjord. It was originally designated a conservation area in 1980.

granslia-naturreservat-nat8d27e695.d: Granslia Nature Reserve was established in 2015. The purpose of the nature reserve is to conserve an area of old-growth forest, dominated by rich deciduous woodland and rich mixed woodland in the lowlands, along with the associated biodiversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems and species, as well as the area’s natural ecological processes.

hillestadasen-naturreservat-natb73b57e5.d: The Hillestadåsen Nature Reserve was established in 1980 and comprises a lush beech forest situated at the very northern limit of this forest type’s natural range on the European continent. Owing to its great scientific importance, the beech forest at Hillestad is to be allowed to develop as freely as possible. Hillestadåsen Nature Reserve is a classic botanical site. It was first described in botanical literature as early as 1924. The aim of the conservation area is to preserve a lush beech forest of great phytogeographical value in both a national and international context.

falkensten-naturreservat-natb6f7e204.d: Falkensten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve that encompasses the vertical rock face of Veggefjell within Falkensten Bay and the woodland below it. Falkensten is a distinctive area. Here there is a coastal, thermophilic broadleaf forest, with some hollow trees. The forest is characterised by great lushness and variation in tree species and age. The nature reserve is modest in area but extensive in terms of altitude. The elevation above sea level ranges from 5 to around 110 metres. Just south of the reserve lies the Falkenstendammen wildlife sanctuary.

refsholttj-nna-naturreservat-natb250a7af.d: Refsholttjønna Nature Reserve was established in 1981; half of its area is water. Refsholttjønna is a nutrient-rich lake with abundant vegetation along its shores. Black alder is a prominent feature along the lake’s edge. The tall reed grass has established itself along the shores, and there are signs of overgrowth around the lake. Refsholttjønna is important for migrating ducks, particularly in autumn. In September and October, hundreds of gadwalls, mallards and teals can be seen in the nature reserve. In this small wetland area, the ducks find rest and food before continuing their journey.

bliksekilen-naturreservat-nat4f44d35c.d: The Bliksekilen Nature Reserve is home to the nationally rare plant, dwarf eelgrass. The wetland area is also important for wading birds and waterfowl during migration. Bliksekilen is a typical example of the smaller shallow-water areas along the Oslofjord. The area is a shallow bay on the north side of Slagentangen. To the south and west, the bay is surrounded by narrow strips of coastal vegetation, whilst to the north it opens out towards the Oslo Fjord. At low tide, large parts of the bay are exposed.

bogen-naturreservat-nat80086818.d: The Bogen Nature Reserve was established in 2006. The nature reserve is home to the extremely rare orchid, the knottblom. There are now very few known populations of the knottblomst remaining in Norway. The lava escarpment known as Holmestrandsveggen, which runs from Holmestrand town centre to the former municipal boundary with Sande, reveals important aspects of the Earth’s history spanning 300 million years. Holmestrandsveggen was the last known breeding site for the peregrine falcon in Vestfold, before the species was re-established through reintroduction from Sweden. The last year of the original breeding was 1967, and the first year of the new breeding at Holmestrandsveggen was 1984.

fjugstad-naturreservat-natff4a3584.d: Fjugstad Nature Reserve is an area of ash forest on the slope leading down to the sea below Fjugstad Farm in Horten municipality. This unusually large stand is the result of management and forestry operations. From 1936, the sawmill at Fjugstad Farm focused particularly on ash, which has excellent strength properties. Some management is necessary to maintain the forest’s distinctive character. The moraine soil contains a fair amount of shell sand, which, together with litter from the deciduous trees, produces calcareous loam. These are favourable conditions for the bird’s-nest orchid found here.

adalstjern-naturreservat-nat32cac2c5.d: Adalstjern Nature Reserve is situated on Raet in the south of Horten municipality, right next to Vestfold University College at Bakkenteigen. At the heart of the area lies Adalstjern, surrounded by marshland. This is the only intact marshland area on Raet. The rest of the area consists largely of beech forest. Peat cutting took place on the marshes around the pond, particularly to the south, right up until the 1960s. The state purchased the marsh in 1967 with a view to placing it under conservation. Pollen analyses of the peat layers show that beech became established here around 650 AD. This is the oldest recorded date for beech in Norway, and it is believed that the species was introduced from the south by humans. In addition to cloudberries, two species of sundew also grow on the bog.

askvikmyra-naturreservat-nate238ac71.d: Askvikmyra Nature Reserve is situated 300 metres from the sea, just over a kilometre south-west of the village of Ula. It is a small wooded bog in undulating hill country. The bog lies around 30 metres above sea level, whilst the surrounding hills reach heights of between 70 and 90 metres. Dwarf varieties of pine and birch grow on the bog. In the wettest areas, there is black alder marsh with sword lilies. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a unique mire area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area is rare and distinctive in that it is one of the very last remaining bogs retaining its original character, situated very close to the sea.

veggermyra-naturreservat-nat8f94ed94.d: Veggermyra Nature Reserve is a slightly domed rain-fed bog, which derives the vast majority of its nutrients from rainfall. As a rule, few species are found in such bogs. The bog is partly wooded, mostly around the edges. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a slightly domed precipitation bog.

malm-ya-naturreservat-natf2990673.d: Malmøya Nature Reserve was established in 2006 and is an island featuring pebble beaches, sandy beaches and rocky shores, seaweed banks, dry grasslands, coastal scrub and wind-swept woodland. Malmøya lies at the far end of Viksfjord. The southern part of the island is a nature reserve. The yellow horned poppy, which is critically endangered, grows in Flaskebukta. Fjærehøymol, another critically endangered plant species, was found and documented in the south of the island in the early 1980s. There was a coastal fort in the southern part of the island. The Norwegian Armed Forces kept the fort in operational use right up until the turn of the millennium. The Armed Forces’ buildings have now been demolished, and the installations in the mountains have been bricked up. In 2001, Larvik Municipality entered into an agreement with Fritzøe Skoger to purchase Malmøya for outdoor recreation purposes.

hummerbakken-naturreservat-nate8694121.d: Hummerbakken Nature Reserve is a wetland area on the Brunlane coast, at the innermost part of Hummerbakkfjorden. The nature reserve features underwater meadows of eelgrass, black alder coastal woodland and coastal marshes. The Bergselva river flows into the reserve, forming a brackish water delta where it meets the sea. The lower reaches of the Bergselva are a very important spawning ground for sea trout. The nature reserve is home to the largest known population of dwarf eelgrass in Eastern Norway. The plant is critically endangered. In Norway, dwarf eelgrass is only known to occur in Rogaland, Hordaland and the Oslo Fjord.

gaserumpa-naturreservat-nat4be0df42.d: The Gåserumpa Nature Reserve in Holmestrand municipality was established in 1988 and is of great international interest to researchers. The beach profiles on the western side of the island reveal long, extensive surfaces deposited during the upper part of the Silurian period. In addition, the island has a varied limestone vegetation, including well-developed limestone grasslands. Gåserumpa was originally purchased by the state so that people could use the island for outdoor recreation. Camping is still permitted on parts of the island. The purpose of the conservation order is to protect an important site for understanding the fossil-bearing rocks of the Oslo Field, together with the calcareous vegetation, including calcareous dry grasslands, which is worthy of protection.

mellom-ya-plantefredningsomrade-nat3bba2.d: The Mellomøya Plant Conservation Area is a protected area situated in the east of Mellomøya. In 2006, an area of 13 dekar was designated as a conservation area to preserve a population of the rare hairy violet and its habitat. The whole of Mellomøya boasts rich vegetation and a diverse birdlife, and the island is largely undisturbed by human activity.

fokser-d-naturreservat-nat4d1bdd5e.d: Fokserød Nature Reserve is a protected area surrounded by commercial land and roads. The access road from the E18 to Sandefjord Airport Torp runs through the nature reserve. The beech forest at Fokserød was one of the first places in Norway where the hawfinch was found to breed. This was in the 1960s. The nature reserve was established in 1980 and covers an area of 38 dekar.

l-v-ya-naturreservat-nat71f69507.d: Løvøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve featuring deciduous broad-leaved woodland, hollow oak trees, a sheer rock face, insects that are rare at national level and at risk of extinction, and a rare bird of prey. Løvøya (Horten) is situated north-west of the town of Horten. The nature reserve boasts a wide variety of habitats and species. Løvøya is of high conservation value as a site for insects, particularly the steep-sloped elm and lime forest. The rare mistletoe parasitises several of the lime trees in the area, and the lichen flora features several unusual species, such as coastal lichen and stiff lichen.

s-nstegard-plante-og-dyrefredningsomrade.d: The Sønstegård Plant and Animal Conservation Area is situated on the beach at the southernmost tip of Hvasser in Færder municipality. The shell sand in the area provides a suitable habitat for plants that require lime, thrive in warm conditions and are drought-tolerant. A large number of insects also live here, including many butterflies. Like all other wildlife in the area, these are protected from harm and collection.

sandvikbukta-plantefredningsomrade-nat8f.d: The Sandvikbukta Plant Conservation Area was established in 2006 and is protected because the rare plant, the marsh marigold, grows there. Today, this plant is found in only a few locations in Vestfold, Østfold and Vest-Agder. The plant grows in Sandvikbukta because a botanist moved some specimens here from the Ringane Nature Reserve, a few hundred metres further east. Black alder trees also grow in the area.

mulasen-naturreservat-nat5e02f7ba.d: The Mulåsen Nature Reserve in Holmestrand municipality was established in 2006. One and a half kilometres south-east of Holmestrand town, a steep-sided headland juts out into the Oslo Fjord. Here, there is a thermophilic deciduous forest with a varied flora and fauna, including several nationally rare and endangered species of lichen and insects. The highest point in the Mulåsen Nature Reserve is 94 metres above sea level. The upper parts of the hill are covered with coniferous forest, whilst the steeper sections closest to the sea feature patches of largely undisturbed deciduous woodland. Several rare and endangered species inhabit the nature reserve, including a rare bird of prey found in Mulåsen. Yew trees grow sporadically throughout the area. There is a prominent burial mound within the reserve.

reverompa-plantefredningsomrade-nat95e57.d: The Reverompa Plant Conservation Area is one of three known habitats in Vestfold for this nationally rare and critically endangered plant. In addition, there are two known habitats in Østfold. The nationally rare and endangered species, the comb-leaved saxifrage, led to the establishment of the Reverompa Plant Conservation Area in 2006. The Reverompa Plant Conservation Area covers eight dekar and is situated partly on a headland jutting out to the west into Horten’s inner harbour basin, and partly along the road leading to this headland. The coastal path runs through the area.

ringane-naturreservat-nate74fedfc.d: Ringane Nature Reserve was established in 2006. The nature reserve is situated two and a half kilometres south-west of the village of Ula, on the outer part of the Torsøy Peninsula. The reserve comprises a pebble beach, rocky outcrops, coastal marshes, a few small salt meadows and calcareous dry grasslands. Furthest from the beach is a marsh with black alder woodland. The reserve is home to the rare plant vasskjeks, an umbellifer that in recent times has only been found in a few locations in Vestfold, Østfold and Vest-Agder. The conservation objective is specifically to protect this coastal area with its varied vegetation.

massasen-dyrefredningsomrade-natbfaef48b.d: The Massåsen Wildlife Reserve was established in 2006 and is one of Vestfold’s smallest nature reserves. Massåsen is a habitat for amphibians. Among the species found here are toads, common spadefoot toads and the rare species of small salamander and pointed-snouted frog.

pirane-naturreservat-natff400629.d: The Pirane Nature Reserve was established in 2006. Pirane is a varied coastal area, with a wide diversity of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The nature reserve is situated at the southernmost tip of Hvasser. The vegetation alternates between seaweed banks, salt marshes and coastal marshes, with the hinterland characterised by scrub, wetland, dry grasslands and rocky outcrops. Pirane is home to several rare plant species, such as strawberry clover and the critically endangered beach flat-backed spider. In Norway, this spider, which is barely four millimetres long, has only been observed in Vestfold. In 2009, the extremely rare crustacean Limnadia lenticularis was found in a pond within the reserve.

kinnhalv-ya-naturreservat-nat1023c903.d: The Kinnhalvøya Nature Reserve was established in 2006. Kinnhalvøya consists of rocky shores, pebble beaches and areas with a wide variety of vegetation types. Here you will find dry meadows, marshes, ponds and small pools, shell sandbanks and wind-swept scrub woodland. Two rare species of stonewort have been found in the area.

holtan-plantefredningsomrade-nat96137af8.d: The Holtan Plant Conservation Area is an open pine forest. The evergreen plant known as ‘bittergrønn’ is found only in south-eastern Norway. In Vestfold, the only known location where it grows is at Holtan. Bittergreen is a nationally rare and critically endangered species. At Holtan, the bittergreen’s habitat was designated a conservation area in 2006. In 2010, around 300 plants were found in the 12-dekar conservation area, all within an area of 30–40 square metres.

karlsvika-plantefredningsomrade-nata58d3.d: The Karlsvika Plant Conservation Area is a pond situated in a spruce forest, half a kilometre north-west of Karlsvikodden in Tønsberg municipality. The extremely rare plant, horse-chervil, used to grow in Karlsvika. In 2006, an area of three dekar was designated a nature reserve to protect a population of the plant and its habitat.

falkenstendammen-dyrefredningsomrade-nat.d: Falkenstendammen is a habitat for several nationally rare and endangered animal species, particularly waterbirds and insects. The diversity of insects at Falkenstendammen has given it national conservation value. A very rare species of caddisfly has been found at Falkenstendammen, which is known to occur at only one other site in Norway. Falkenstendammen is also important for migratory waterbirds. As long as the pond remains ice-free, a number of birds overwinter here. Rare bird species are regularly spotted here.

ilene-naturreservat-natdbe49559.d: The Ilene and Presterødkilen Ramsar Site is a wetland system in Tønsberg municipality, Vestfold, established in 1985. The site comprises two nature reserves: Ilene Nature Reserve and Presterødkilen Nature Reserve. Both nature reserves comprise extensive wetland areas, a large proportion of which are shallow areas that are exposed at low tide. Together, the two areas form a single Ramsar site. Presterødkilen is a shallow fjord arm with extensive mudflats at low tide. Ilene contains areas of marshland, wet meadows, pastures and woodland. Ilene lies to the west of Tønsberg town centre, whilst Presterødkilen lies to the east of the town centre.

flisefyr-og-hidalen-naturreservat-nata90.d: The Flisefyr-Hidalen Nature Reserve was established in 2009 and is a diverse nature reserve. The terrain is varied. The south-eastern part slopes down from the marked summit of Flisefyr, which lies 276 metres above sea level, and westwards towards a forest track. The central and northern parts are characterised by gently undulating hill country, with Hidalen running through as a valley. There are many types of vegetation, with various types of beech forest among the most common. On the hills there are pine forests with heather, whilst the valleys feature swamp forests. Seventeen species of wild trees have been found in the area. In the north-western corner of the reserve lies a stand of old, coarse aspen, acquired by the municipality for conservation purposes before the reserve was established.

gumser-d-ya-fuglefredningsomrade-nate587.d: The Gumserødøya Bird Sanctuary was established in 2009 and is a flat, elongated island with rocky outcrops. The island lies between Stavern and Naverfjorden and is an important breeding ground for gulls and common terns. Gumserødøya is surrounded by shallow waters. At low tide, it is possible to wade from the mainland out to the island. The reserve also includes a number of smaller islets. In the bird sanctuaries, seabirds are to be allowed to breed undisturbed by humans. The area is a breeding ground for the oystercatcher, the sandpiper, the black-headed gull, the common gull, the grey gull, the black-backed gull and the common tern. Conservation objective: to safeguard birdlife and the birds’ habitat associated with an important breeding area for a number of seabird species.

dalaasen-naturreservat-nat69060c8b.d: The Dalaåsen Nature Reserve was established in 2009 and is situated just north of Langevann, on the southern part of a larger ridge. The eastern side, facing Trolldalen, is in places very steep, whilst the terrain slopes more gently towards the south. Dalaåsen is a forest typical of this part of Vestfold. Beech woodland dominates the central parts of the area. Dalaåsen is of national conservation value and is of great scientific importance as a reference area. Large parts of the ridge are fenced off and grazed by cows. Dalasetra lies in the middle of the nature reserve. The old mountain pasture is no longer in use. A prominent outcrop at the top of the steep, east-facing slope is called Svervestolen. A ‘svervestol’ is a local term for a lathe.

bekkeskj-ret-biotopvernomrade-natf62f991.d: The Bekkeskjæret biotope conservation area in Holmestrand municipality was established in 2009. Bekkeskjæret can be seen from the road between Sande and Svelvik and from the recreational area at Bekkestranda. In 1974, around 500 black-headed gulls were recorded in the colony. In 1991, ornithologists counted over 300 black-headed gulls and around 10 common terns. In 2012, just over 50 black-headed gulls bred in the conservation area, in addition to a small colony of common terns. Conservation objective: To protect seabirds during the breeding season.

bueskj-r-biotopvernomrade-natf73ecee7.d: The Bueskjær biotope conservation area is a breeding ground for seabirds, particularly black-headed gulls and common terns. Bueskjær is a small islet in the western part of Horten’s inner harbour basin. The biotope conservation area covers 14 dekar, but only one dekar is land area. The area was designated a conservation area in 2009. Most black-headed gulls migrate out of Norway in winter, but some choose to stay. The first breeding black-headed gulls in Norway were observed on Jæren in 1867. The Norwegian population is estimated to number between 20,000 and 60,000 pairs. Black-headed gulls breed on islands and islets in the archipelago, in wetland areas and near freshwater. Bueskjær has also been known as Kruttskjær. It is said that the Navy used to burn off surplus gunpowder on the skerry.

saltbuskj-r-biotopvernomrade-nat1e389a96.d: The Saltbuskjær biotope conservation area was established in 2009 and consists of two almost contiguous islets to the west of Vrengensundet. The islets are an important breeding ground for common gulls. Other seabirds, such as common terns, breed here in smaller numbers. Human activity, both on land and at sea, can disturb the seabirds, and dogs running loose pose a major threat to birds that nest on the ground. Conservation objective: To protect seabirds during the breeding season.

lyngholmen-fuglefredningsomrade-nat53c4b.d: The Lyngholmen Bird Sanctuary was established in 2009. The site is situated in a typical outer archipelago setting and is a large, fairly hilly islet. Heather and shrubs grow on the islet. The breeding population consists of around 20 lesser black-backed gulls. The islet is also a breeding site for black guillemots, common terns, black-headed gulls, grey gulls, black-backed gulls, common terns and barnacle geese. Conservation objective: to protect the birdlife and the birds’ habitat associated with an islet that is an important breeding area for a number of seabird species.

mar-yskj-ra-fuglefredningsomrade-nat3254.d: The Marøyskjæra Bird Sanctuary was established in 2009 and consists of two rocky islets west of Natholmen. Marøyskjæra is a breeding ground for black-headed gulls and common terns, although breeding populations can fluctuate. Local observations in the 1980s suggested that Marøyskjæra was a stable breeding site for gulls. In the 1990s, over 500 black-headed gulls bred here. The area still has a significant population of breeding common terns.

b-lene-fuglefredningsomrade-natf94dd898.d: The Bølene Bird Sanctuary is home to one of the largest known breeding populations of black guillemots on the Skagerrak coast. Bølene consists of four large and several smaller skerries, north-east of Svenner. The skerries are gently undulating, with little or no vegetation. Bølene is a regionally very important breeding site for black guillemots. Up to 50 individuals have been observed during the breeding season, which is a high figure for a species that is otherwise scarce on the Skagerrak coast. Eider, lesser black-backed gulls, grey gulls and black-tailed gulls also use Bølene as a breeding site.

ertholmen-fuglefredningsomrade-nat5a020a.d: The Ertholmen Bird Sanctuary was established in 2009. Ertholmen is a large islet in the outer archipelago to the south of the Rauer area. The islet consists mainly of bare rocky outcrops and scree, with some shrubs and heather in the north. The highest point is 16 metres above sea level. In recent years, Ertholmen has been home to breeding populations of over 200 lesser black-backed gulls. In the seabird conservation areas in Vestfold, it is forbidden to go ashore from 15 April to 15 July. The access ban also applies at sea, in most areas up to 50 metres from the shoreline. Conservation objective: to protect birdlife and the birds’ habitat associated with an islet that is an important breeding ground for a number of seabird species.

str-msundholmen-biotopvernomrade-natb86e.d: The Strømsundholmen biotope conservation area was established in 2009 and is a steep-sided islet on the north side of Svenner. The islet is an important breeding ground for gulls. Strømsundholmen is a typical outer archipelago islet, with rocky outcrops and exposed rocks. Its highest point is 19 metres above sea level. Seabirds are an important feature of the archipelago’s natural environment, and the establishment of protected areas for seabirds is a measure to conserve birdlife in the archipelago. Conservation objective: To protect seabirds during the breeding season.

flatholmen-biotopvernomrade-natf3c0900c.d: The Flatholmen biotope conservation area was established in 2009. Flatholmen in Viksfjord is a breeding ground for seabirds and has been important for black-headed gulls and yellow-legged gulls. Flatholmen is a low islet. In recent years, it has gradually become overgrown with scrub and bushes. This has led to a deterioration in breeding conditions for gulls and other seabirds. Ducks and waders, such as the oystercatcher and the redshank, use Flatholmen as a breeding ground. Conservation objective: To protect seabirds during the breeding season.

langholmene-fuglefredningsomrade-natb22c.d: The Langholmene Bird Sanctuary was established in 2009 and consists of two large islets and a number of smaller skerries just south of Nevlunghavn. The islets consist mainly of rocky outcrops and scree, and the highest point is barely 10 metres above sea level. In Vestfold, access is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July in seabird conservation areas. Conservation objective: to protect birdlife and the birds’ habitats associated with a group of islets that are important breeding grounds for a number of seabird species.

ferjeholmen-fuglefredningsomrade-natb7c3.d: The Ferjeholmen Bird Sanctuary was established in 2009. Ferjeholmen is the largest of the islets west of Svenner. The islet is hilly, with outcrops and rocky shores of syenite. Ferjeholmen is a breeding ground for black guillemots, common terns, black-headed gulls, grey gulls, lesser black-backed gulls, black-tailed gulls and Arctic terns. Conservation objective: to protect birdlife and the birds’ habitat on an islet that is an important breeding ground for a number of seabird species.

torskerumpa-biotopvernomrade-natb5300817.d: The Torskerumpa biotope conservation area was established in 2009. Torskerumpa is a skerry in Tangekilen, just under a kilometre south of the Røssesund Bridge. In recent years, only black-backed gulls, common gulls, oystercatchers and mute swans have bred here, and only in small numbers. Previously, black-headed gulls and common terns also bred on the islet. Conservation objective: to protect an important islet for seabirds from disturbance during the breeding season.

sundskj-ra-biotopvernomrade-nat9fd229d4.d: The Sundskjæra biotope conservation area was established in 2009. Sundskjæra consists of two islets at the far end of Viksfjord, north-west of Malmøya. Sundskjæra was an important breeding site for black-headed gulls and common terns. In recent years, the breeding population on the two islets has been small. In recent years, black-backed gulls, lesser black-backed gulls and common gulls have bred here, but in modest numbers. Although the breeding populations have been small in recent years, the islets possess qualities that make them suitable as future breeding sites. Conservation objective: to protect seabirds during the breeding season.

st-yskj-ret-biotopvernomrade-natba834a9a.d: The Østøyskjæret biotope conservation area is a protected area covering ten dekar, but only one dekar of this is land. Surveys in 2002 and 2004 showed that the small islet had a breeding population of ten pairs of common terns. Since 2004, no common terns have bred on the islet. Østøyskjæret was designated a protected area because it was an important breeding site for common terns.

kausen-biotopvernomrade-nat5a7521d1.d: The Kausen biotope conservation area was established in 2009. Kausen is situated just outside the Ørastranda recreational area. The boundary of the conservation area extends right down to the beach on the eastern side of Kausen. This was done so as not to impose excessive restrictions on outdoor recreation. During the period when access is restricted, it is forbidden to moor boats at Kausen or to go ashore on the islet. Kausen is an important breeding ground for seabirds. Conservation objective: To protect seabirds during the breeding season.

veal-s-naturreservat-nat5524d41a.d: Vealøs Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the island of Vealøs in Horten municipality, which serves as a breeding and rearing ground for seabirds, and as a resting place for seabirds and other waterbirds during migration. The nature reserve was established in 2009 and covers 115 dekar. 15 dekar of this is land area. Vealøs is valuable both as a breeding and rearing ground for seabirds and as a resting place for seabirds and other waterbirds during migration.

r-ysa-naturreservat-nate8d4ad12.d: The Røysa Nature Reserve was established in 2002. Røysa is situated on the eastern side of Farris, north-west of Kvelde. One and a half kilometres further north lies the Middagskollen Nature Reserve. Two and a half kilometres to the south-east lies the Jordstøyp Nature Reserve. The nature reserve is diverse and has been little affected by logging. In the north of the reserve there is an old pine forest with large pine trees. The reserve also contains old, large trees of aspen, maple, elm, lime and ash. In areas with better soil, there are old spruce forests, and there is an abundance of spruce deadwood. Røysa is a small area in itself, but the presence of old oaks, a continuous supply of oak deadwood and the discovery of interesting species make the area worthy of regional conservation.

vemannsas-naturreservat-nat8ec8da2e.d: Vemannsås Nature Reserve was established in 2002 and is situated on the eastern side of Farris, south of Kvelde town centre. The reserve is gently undulating and consists of two distinct ridges with hills, ravines and slopes. A distinctive feature of Vemannsås is its old, coarse oak trees and the steady supply of dead oak wood at all stages of decomposition. Many species of insects, lichens and wood-dwelling fungi are entirely dependent on such living conditions. Vemannsås is home to a wealth of species. Several have been found in only a handful of locations in Norway. One of these is the oak knife fungus, a fungus that lives on coarse, old oak trees. The oak knife fungus is critically endangered in Norway.

jordst-yp-naturreservat-nat73aea896.d: Jordstøyp Nature Reserve was established in 2002. Jordstøyp is a hill situated west of Kvelde in Lågendalen. From the summit, which lies 318 metres above sea level, there are fine views over large parts of the southern county. The nature reserve is home to Europe’s most critically endangered fungus, the saffron milk cap. Much of Jordstøyp has been little affected by logging and consists of old broad-leaved trees. Many species are found here and elsewhere in the area, as there is plenty of dead wood.

krokskogen-naturreservat-natac845dd4.d: Krokskogen Nature Reserve (approximately 12,921 daa) is an extension of the former Merratjern/Søndagsbrenna Nature Reserve (7,055 daa). The new area lies on the border between the municipalities of Hole and Ringerike and was established by Royal Decree 16 December 2016 pursuant to the Act of 19 June 2009 No. 100 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), Section 34, cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The nature reserve is intended to preserve a large, varied and representative coniferous forest area in the higher-altitude parts of Krokskogen, with remaining large stands of old-growth forest exhibiting natural dynamics and containing threatened, rare and vulnerable natural features.

rundkollen-og-sortungsbekken-naturreserv.d: Rundkollen Nature Reserve is situated in the very north of Nittedal municipality, on the Romeriksåsene hills to the west of Hakadal. The bedrock is rich in quartz and the vegetation is sparse. Poor blueberry spruce forest is the most common type of vegetation, but on the most shallow-soiled sections, pine forest grows with plenty of heather and leathery sedge on the forest floor. The forest is very old, with a large proportion of deadwood and fallen trees. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a varied coniferous forest area that is largely unaffected by human activity.

viulkastet-naturreservat-nat28aa0cc3.d: The Viulkastet Nature Reserve (approximately 192 daa) was established by Royal Decree 10 June 2016 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The nature reserve is situated in Ringerike municipality in Buskerud. The nature reserve is intended to preserve a riverbank with calcareous sand pine forest and several different, rare spring forest communities, such as scabious spring forest and spring-influenced grey alder forest. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve the area’s importance for rare habitat types and rich biodiversity. The area has large populations of calcium-demanding vascular plants and fungal species.

rankedal-naturreservat-nat390421aa.d: Rankedal Nature Reserve (approximately 373 daa) was established by Royal Decree 10 June 2016 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The reserve is situated in Ringerike municipality, Buskerud, just south-west of the Viulkastet Nature Reserve. The nature reserve is intended to preserve a river slope with clay ravines and a unique transition from dry, rich sand pine forest to fresh broad-leaved forest and extreme grey alder forests. It is situated on the slope between Eggemoen and Randselva, south of Viulveien and west of the old Viul Træsliperi, precisely where the river makes a sharp bend and widens considerably.

hanangervann-og-krakenesvann-landskapsve.d: The Hanangervann and Kråkenesvann Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The area was designated a conservation area in 1988 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect two lakes that form key elements of the Lista wetland system. The lakes are among the most important wintering grounds for waterfowl and stopover sites during the spring and autumn migrations. Thirty-nine breeding bird species have been recorded.

fiskumvannet-naturreservat-nat1c4f10ec.d: Fiskumvannet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Øvre Eiker municipality in Buskerud. The reserve was established in 1974 ‘to preserve a special type of habitat, with a rich bird life that is of particular scientific and educational interest’. The nature reserve encompasses the northern and western parts of Lake Fiskumvannet; the riparian zone and a larger area of Hegstadmyra are also included within the reserve. Lake Fiskumvannet is a shallow, relatively nutrient-rich lake characterised by the surrounding agricultural landscape. Red List species such as the gadwall, common scoter and Lappish duck have been observed here, and the pink-footed goose rests here during its migration to and from Svalbard. The area was designated a Ramsar site in 2013.

kolbergtjernmyra-naturreservat-natfe694f.d: Kolbergtjernmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Øvre Eiker municipality, in Buskerud county. Kolbergtjernmyra lies approximately 4 km west of Vestfossen and is surrounded by low coniferous forest-covered hills. Kolbergtjern lies at the centre of the area, surrounded by an intermediate flat bog complex. The area is of value as a breeding and migratory habitat for birds. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 1986 and comprises a mire complex with varied and interesting vegetation, as well as an important bird habitat. A stream flows into the mire from the Eiker copper works. This is likely to have some impact on the vegetation. A seating area has been set up within the reserve.

brennvika-naturreservat-nata3c2274c.d: Brennvika is a bay south of Leines in Steigen municipality in Nordland, which extends eastwards from the Vestfjord onto the peninsula between Leinesfjorden and Folda. At the head of the bay lies the two-kilometre-long sandy beach Brennviksanden, and on the southern side are, amongst others, Stortinden (837 metres above sea level) and Brenntinden (754 metres above sea level). There is a skerry landscape on the northern side. The area is used as a hiking and recreational area by the local population. As for settlements, Helnessund – which is served by the Nordlandsekspressen ferry – is situated on the north side. A local road from Helnessund continues eastwards to Skår. There is a local road to the hamlet of Brennvika at the bottom of the bay. The south side has no roads and is uninhabited.

eggholmen-naturreservat-nat33c9e899.d: Eggholmen Nature Reserve comprises two small islets south of Kjellandsviktangen, as well as the surrounding waters extending for nearly 100 metres, on the eastern side of Jeløya in Moss municipality. The area is protected to preserve the habitat of flora and fauna, particularly seabirds. Access to the area is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July.

oterv-r-naturreservat-nat494b8365.d: Otervær Nature Reserve is situated in Rødøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 794 dekar, of which 537 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a protected area to preserve a traditional and typical eggvær.

esvikhatten-naturreservat-nate31c6152.d: Esvikhatten Nature Reserve is situated in Rødøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve lies just west of Esvika, on the north side of Tjongsfjorden. The area covers 294 dekar. It has been designated a nature reserve to preserve an area of rich dwarf birch forest, with a core of highly interesting primeval forest featuring sturdy hazel bushes and old willow trees.

sholman-naturreservat-natd04d8c50.d: The Æsholman Nature Reserve is situated in the municipality of Vestvågøy in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses the Æsholman archipelago, north-west of Utakleiv. The area covers 1,315 dekar, of which 1,176 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect an important breeding ground for seabirds.

storeidvatnet-naturreservat-nat5e078a53.d: Storeidvatnet Nature Reserve is situated near Storeid in the municipality of Vestvågøy in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 150 dekar, of which 143 dekar is freshwater. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area with a rich and interesting birdlife.

eggum-naturreservat-nat0bc169b1.d: Eggum Nature Reserve is situated in the municipality of Vestvågøy in Nordland. The nature reserve lies to the west of Eggum on the island of Vestvågøya. It covers an area of 1,010 dekar, of which 381 dekar is marine area. The area has been protected to preserve a well-developed pebble beach and a very well-developed marginal moraine.

brandvik-landskapsvernomrade-natd5ead721.d: The Brandvik Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Stord municipality in Vestland county. The landscape conservation area covers an area of 518 dekar. The area has been designated a conservation area to protect the forests containing yew and holly.

bleikjo-naturreservat-natd1c882cb.d: Bleikjo Nature Reserve consists of a skerry east of Huglo in Stord municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland county on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is “to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.” Recorded breeding species in 2014 (7 July): Black-backed Gull 2 pairs, Common Gull 1 pair.

perholmen-naturreservat-nat91b6b917.d: Perholmen Nature Reserve consists of two islets in Hauglandsosen in the municipality of Bjørnafjorden. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (28 June): Common Tern 3 pairs, Herring Gull 1 pair, Black-tailed Gull 1 pair, Arctic Tern 1 pair, Oystercatcher 1 pair.

ringaskjer-naturreservat-natd2a4175b.d: Ringaskjer Nature Reserve consists of a skerry in Raunefjorden in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland county on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. No breeding species were recorded in 2014.

kubbholmen-naturreservat-nata0424614.d: Kubbholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet off the coast of Drange in the municipality of Bjørnafjorden. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (28 June): Common gull 6 pairs, Arctic tern 2 pairs.

fj-raskjer-naturreservat-nat70a94405.d: Fjæraskjer Nature Reserve consists of a small islet north-east of Fjelbergøy in Kvinnherad municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ A survey of breeding species in 2014 (7 July) recorded one pair of black-backed gulls.

raudholmane-naturreservat-nat405d8513.d: The Raudholmane Nature Reserve comprises a number of islets south-east of Halsnøy in Kvinnherad municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’.

sandholmane-naturreservat-nat740ce624.d: Sandholmane Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets off Osøyro in the municipality of Bjørnafjorden. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. Recorded breeding species in 2014 (28 June) Common gull 17 pairs (179 in 1979), Herring gull 4 pairs, Lesser black-backed gull 7 pairs, Great black-backed gull 5 pairs, Black-headed gull 1 pair, Ringed plover 2 pairs.

skano-naturreservat-natcd9ee47f.d: Skåno Nature Reserve covers the northern half of the islet of Skåno in Etne municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland county on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. Registered breeding species in 2011 – common gull 14 pairs, lesser black-backed gull 1 pair, Arctic tern 30 pairs, ringed plover 2 pairs.

tr-ttebleikja-naturreservat-nat4797f9c4.d: Trættebleikja Nature Reserve consists of an islet to the west of Nordra Gissøya in Bømlo municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. A colony of 45 pairs of red-billed terns in 1981 formed the basis for the conservation status. The 2014 management plan states that trends have been negative and that the colony no longer resides on the islet.

eggv-r-naturreservat-nat4fe98443.d: Eggvær Nature Reserve consists of an islet in the Holsøyane archipelago on the western side of Bømlo in Bømlo municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (6 July): Black-backed Gull 10 pairs, Grey Gull 1 pair, Oystercatcher 1 pair.

her-y-naturreservat-nat3a64cf2d.d: Herøy Nature Reserve comprises the western part of Herøy in Masfjorden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland county on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. Recorded breeding species in 2014 (6 July): Grey Gull 1 pair, Oystercatcher 1 pair.

synn-y-naturreservat-nate8d55f58.d: Synnøy Nature Reserve consists of an island off Rossneset in Alver municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland county on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (6 July): Black-tailed Godwit 1 pair, Lapwing 2 pairs.

gr-ningane-naturreservat-natf3ae0735.d: Grøningane Nature Reserve consists of three islets on Lake Fonnebostsjøen in Alver municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. Recorded breeding species in 2014: Black-backed Gull 2 pairs, Common Tern 3 pairs, Arctic Tern 1 pair, Ringed Plover 2 pairs.

adn-y-naturreservat-natb5c43de8.d: The Ådnøy Nature Reserve comprises the southern tip of Ådnøyna in Alver municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland county on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. Recorded breeding species in 2014: Ringed plover, 1 pair.

stridsholmen-naturreservat-natb9ccf83a.d: Stridsholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet in the northern part of Lurefjorden in Austrheim municipality. nesvika-naturreservat-natf37e4f6a.d: Nesvika Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bergen municipality, in the Arna district of Hordaland. granvinsfjorden-naturreservat-nat65aa843.d: Granvinsfjorden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Voss municipality. Motorised traffic is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited except on the existing Haukanes cattle track, which is marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents specific types of nature such as elm-lime forest, low-herb hazel thicket and nutrient-poor pine-oak forest b.

sengane-naturreservat-nat1891943f.d: The Sengane Nature Reserve is situated in the sea to the west of Espevær in Bømlo municipality. kramyrane-naturreservat-nat3684d1c9.d: The Kråmyrane Nature Reserve near Trengereid in Bergen is a marshland area comprising rainwater marshes and groundwater marshes, with vegetation consisting of yellow sedge, twin-spike sedge and Sphagnum moss. There are also patches of carnivorous plants of the Utricularia genus. There are two small lakes at Kråmyrane: Nordsta Kråtjørna and Midttjørna. These flow via the Teinelva river into Øyjordsvatnet/Langavatnet at Gullbotn. There is a footpath running alongside the river. Krånipa rises to 703 metres above sea level east of Kråmyrane, but there are no usable paths leading up from here, so the mountain is most easily climbed from the southern side of Skulstadvatnet further up.

rambj-ra-landskapsvernomrade-nat0f8ad98c.d: The Rambjøra Landscape Conservation Area, which includes protected flora and fauna, is situated in Vestland County, in the municipality of Bergen. The landscape conservation area was established in 1981 and covers 0.3057 km². The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a rare combination of several distinctive habitat types, and to protect rare plant and animal species. The area is valuable for education, research and recreation. Rambjøra is a large, contiguous green space situated close to Nesttun, Paradis, Indre Sædal, Kringlebotn and Nattland. The landscape conservation area, with Lake Myravatnet at its centre, contains a unique combination of several distinctive habitat types, with a rich variety of flora and fauna.

hellis-y-naturreservat-nataf692fca.d: Hellisøy Nature Reserve consists of an islet situated close to Hellisøy Lighthouse in Fedje municipality. eggholmen-naturreservat-nat19efd8c8.d: Eggholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet in Selbjørnsfjorden in Fitjar municipality. hisdalen-naturreservat-nat91607260.d: Hisdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bergen municipality, Vestland county. It was established on 17 December 1999.

prestnesholmen-naturreservat-nat5077fdd2.d: Prestnesholmen Nature Reserve consists of a skerry west of Husnes in Kvinnherad municipality. reppadalen-naturreservat-nat30a5117b.d: The Reppadalen Nature Reserve, situated above Arnatveit in Bergen, is a mire area comprising rainwater mires, groundwater mires, flat mires and hill mires, with vegetation consisting of bottle sedge and pale peat moss. The area covers 400 dekar and was designated a nature reserve in 1983. It lies approximately 400 metres above sea level and is widely used as a recreational area in Arna via the Rambergsveien and Reppadalsveien footpaths. You can also follow the footpaths from Garnes across Ådnanipa. From Reppadalen, Repparåsen (609 metres above sea level) rises to the north; Herlandsfjellet (695 metres above sea level) lies to the south-east, Skåldalsfjellet (718 metres above sea level) to the south and Skåldalsnipa (603 metres above sea level) to the south-west. The nature reserve also contains a number of old mountain pastures: Garnessetra, Ådnasetra and Seimssetra.

karihavet-naturreservat-nat62b27165.d: The Karihavet Nature Reserve comprises the islet of Eliten in Melingsvågen, in the municipality of Bømlo. gjuvslandslia-landskapsvernomrade-natad1.d: The Gjuvslandslia Landscape Conservation Area is situated on Varaldsøy in Kvinnherad municipality in Vestland. The conservation area also contains holly, deciduous broadleaf woodland, calcareous pine forest and valuable, species-rich hay meadows.

dyr-ysundskjeret-naturreservat-nat4d89b6.d: The Dyrøysundskjeret Nature Reserve consists of a skerry in Dyrøysundet between Dyrøyna and Haugsøy. kolebakkane-naturreservat-nat95ecb342.d: Kolebakkane Nature Reserve is a protected coniferous forest reserve in Gloppen municipality. In the centre of the area lies Røsskleivvatnet, a pond created by landowners with an interest in fishing. Trout have been stocked in the pond.

ytter-yane-naturreservat-natf107bdf0.d: The Ytterøyane Nature Reserve comprises an area around the Ytterøyane lighthouse in Kinn municipality. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the great cormorant, greylag goose, eider, common scoter, oystercatcher, turnstone, little curlew, redshank, grey gull, black-backed gull, red-billed tern and black guillemot.

luster-allmenning-naturreservat-natf0ea6.d: The Luster Allmenning Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Lustrafjord in Luster municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 2 September 2005 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large, contiguous, forested fjordside area virtually untouched by modern technical interventions, with its diversity of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural, ecological processes. The area is of great scientific and biological value as a large, contiguous forested area with rare botanical and ornithological occurrences, and as a study area for natural spruce forest in potential expansion.”

aralden-naturreservat-nat1249e7fd.d: The Aralden Nature Reserve comprises an area near Hovden and Batalden in Kinn municipality. sandvikbotn-naturreservat-nat8dbd5c7f.d: Sandvikbotn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kinn municipality in Sunnfjord, Vestland, and is a protected area for all plant life east of Florø. The reserve is situated in Barlindbotn. The area consists of completely untouched primeval forest and is home to an abundance of different tree species and plants, in particular large numbers of the protected yew tree. Sandvikbotn Nature Reserve also boasts a rich and diverse wildlife. Sandvikbotn Nature Reserve was designated on 14 June 2002. The government’s management plan for the Sandvikbotn Nature Reserve states: ‘The Sandvikbotn Nature Reserve was designated on 14 June 2002 as part of the expansion of the conservation plan for coniferous forests in Western Norway.’

rognane-naturreservat-nat3bfc0533.d: The Rognane Nature Reserve comprises an area within Hovden in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally associated vegetation and wildlife’. The islets within the reserve are traditional breeding grounds for gulls. Confirmed breeding species include the eider, the oystercatcher, the turnstone, the common gull, the black-backed gull, the common tern and the red-billed tern.

flostranda-naturreservat-natb105c3ed.d: Flostranda Nature Reserve is situated on the mountainside above the county road running alongside Flostranda, by Lake Oppstrynsvatnet in Stryn municipality. The reserve faces south on a bedrock of gneiss and is the largest area of thermophilic forest in Northern Europe. The vegetation consists of a deciduous broad-leaved forest of the elm-lime type. The dominant tree species is lime, and the understorey is rich in species, including the white wood anemone. The internationally endangered leaf-rot beetle Microrhagus lepidus has also been recorded here. Following the establishment of the reserve in 1991, plans were drawn up to route the county road through a tunnel past the reserve. The boundaries of the protected area were therefore adjusted in 2019 and extended partly down to the water’s edge.

sildekruna-naturreservat-nat7fb6ce6f.d: The Sildekruna Nature Reserve consists of a small peninsula in the north of Silda in Kinn municipality. osen-naturreservat-natc2ee19c7.d: Osen Nature Reserve is situated at the mouth of the Gaular watercourse, at the innermost part of Dalsfjorden (Sunnfjord) in Sunnfjord municipality. The reserve consists of a river estuary in a shallow fjord bay. On the southern side, the terrain is steep, whilst to the east and north the reserve borders on flatter farmland. Around 40 species of wetland birds have been recorded, particularly ducks. The area also serves as a moulting and wintering site for Canada geese. Of particular interest is the presence of the aquatic plant stylopodium, which has only been recorded at three other sites in Scandinavia, all in Sunnfjord. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic is prohibited; this also applies to the use of model boats and aeroplanes.

smelv-r-naturreservat-nat44e127cf.d: Smelvær Nature Reserve comprises an area of sea off Stavenesodden in Askvoll municipality. gjerlands-yane-naturreservat-nat00429ba5.d: Gjerlandsøyane Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sunnfjord municipality covering an area of 195 dekar. The nature reserve consists of marshland on both sides of the Gjerlandselva river, with vegetation including bear’s beard, meat moss, warty moss, peat moss, cranberries and grey moss.

ku-yna-naturreservat-nat8edb7244.d: The Kuøyna Nature Reserve comprises an area off Herland on Atløyna in Askvoll municipality. yngsdalen-naturreservat-natd8eb57bd.d: Yngsdalen Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Veitastrondsvatnet in Luster municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 18 June 2004 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The area is of a size that is rare in Indre Sogn below the tree line, and features elements of rich mire and springs, as well as rare and interesting plant species. A distinctive feature of the area is that the bog fills the valley floor, with a meandering river and various aquatic habitats linked to an undisturbed river system.”

stallbrekka-naturreservat-nat6865ff20.d: The Stallbrekka Nature Reserve comprises an area on Vågsøy in Kinn municipality. kvinnafossen-naturreservat-nat40a71671.d: The Kvinnafossen Nature Reserve comprises an area on the Sognefjord in Sogndal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 19 June 2009 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests/rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large, virtually untouched forest area with special habitat types, including the full diversity of species and vegetation types and all natural ecological processes. The area has particular scientific and educational value, with its great diversity of forest and vegetation types in a particularly favourable warm climate, and a wide variety of species associated with warm and nutrient-rich environments, old-growth forest and deadwood.”

lysholmen-naturreservat-nat545661ab.d: Lysholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet between Vågsøy and Silda in Kinn municipality. engevik-naturreservat-natfb0d8bf4.d: Engevik Nature Reserve comprises an area on Sula in Solund municipality. The aim of such conservation is to protect the area as a habitat for flora and fauna, and as a natural gene bank for pine and other endemic outlier populations with special genetic adaptations.”

steiehalsen-naturreservat-nat043da3b3.d: The Steiehalsen Nature Reserve consists of an almost untouched south-facing fjord shore on the Dalsfjord in Askvoll municipality. The area has particular scientific and educational value with its lush broad-leaved forest and rich combination of thermophilic and coastal species and communities.’

loi-naturreservat-nat7866ffb0.d: The Loi Nature Reserve comprises an area between Urnes Stave Church and Munthehuset in Luster municipality. husum-naturreservat-nate0facc57.d: Husum Nature Reserve comprises an area near Borgund in Lærdal municipality. The area has particular scientific and educational value as an unusual continental broad-leaved forest in Western Norway, with a high species diversity associated with species-rich rock and meadow communities, and as a highly productive forest ecosystem with a significant altitude gradient, well-suited to the study of future climate change.”

mjata-naturreservat-nat2e95d504.d: The Mjåta Nature Reserve comprises an area on Sula in Solund municipality. The area is of particular scientific value due to its diversity of broad-leaved forests and other vegetation types, its species diversity and its biological productivity, and is unique as a lush outpost facing the sea, in a landscape otherwise characterised by bare rock.”

stedjeberget-naturreservat-nat11044a73.d: Stedjeberget Nature Reserve comprises an area by Sogndalsfjøra in Sogndal municipality. eiterstrondi-naturreservat-nated98f4c5.d: The Eiterstrondi Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Arnafjord in Vik municipality. guleskjeret-naturreservat-natdf7f341e.d: Guleskjeret Nature Reserve is a nature reserve (bird sanctuary) in Gulen municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect breeding seabirds in the archipelago in Lake Sognesjøen. The area covers just 20 dekar, of which 2 daa is land and 18 daa is water. In 1993, the Government adopted the Seabird Conservation Plan, which designated 57 bird sanctuaries totalling 11 km² along the coast of Sogn og Fjordane. The plan is based on the initial conservation proposals from 1977, as well as White Paper No. 68 (1980–81) ‘Conservation of Norwegian Nature’, which set out the objective of conserving a representative selection of natural areas in Norway, and the first consultation proposal on seabird conservation in Sogn og Fjordane from 1984. Between 1977 and 1988, 350 seabird sites in the county were surveyed and assessed.

krokholmen-naturreservat-nat8e154375.d: The Krokholmen Nature Reserve comprises an area south of Atløy in Askvoll municipality. b-ya-yra-naturreservat-nat8bcd7003.d: The Bøyaøyra Nature Reserve comprises an area at the head of the Fjærlandsfjord in Sogndal municipality. refvikvatnet-naturreservat-nat7e72d3d4.d: Refvikvatnet Nature Reserve is a 520 dekar nature reserve south of the village of Refvik in Kinn municipality. ‘The purpose of the conservation order is to safeguard an important wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife, particularly with regard to the coastal lake as a habitat type and the area’s value for wetland birds during migration periods.’ The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 December 1991. The County Governor of Vestland is the managing authority for the area. Refvikvatnet is a coastal lake situated just four metres above sea level. It has been dammed by sediment from the sea and is a habitat type that is extremely rare in Vestland and indeed throughout Norway. The lake is nutrient-poor but is of great value as a stopover and wintering site for ducks and waders.

askvika-naturreservat-nat5ca0b73a.d: The Askvika Nature Reserve comprises Askvika, Leira and Kyllaren in Askvoll municipality. bukta-fuglefredingsomrade-nat05db57af.d: The Bukta Wildlife Sanctuary (official name: Bukta Bird Sanctuary) is situated in the Bukta area, south of Sandane in Gloppen municipality, Sogn og Fjordane. skilbreivatnet-naturreservat-nat4fea5187.d: The Skilbreivatnet Nature Reserve is situated just under a mil south-south-west of Førde in Sunnfjord. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.’

tenn-yane-naturreservat-nat5cfe6e68.d: The Tennøyane Nature Reserve consists of two islands in Gulen, between Nordgulen and Midtgulen. The nature reserve is situated in Bremanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. The reserve is of particular value as a breeding ground for gulls, but also serves as a wintering area and breeding ground for wetland birds.

kvalsteinane-naturreservat-nat2915ec44.d: The Kvalsteinane Nature Reserve consists of islets and skerries south of Reksta in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the grey gull, black-backed gull, greylag goose, eider, oystercatcher, lapwing, turnstone, little curlew, redshank, common gull, common tern, red-billed tern, Arctic skua and black guillemot.

senholmen-naturreservat-nat75dc6065.d: Senholmen Nature Reserve comprises an area between Atløy and Værlandet in Askvoll municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the great cormorant, greylag goose, eider, oystercatcher, turnstone, common gull, herring gull, black-backed gull and kittiwake.

flatholmen-naturreservat-nat7530171e.d: Flatholmen Nature Reserve consists of an islet situated between the islands of Barmøya and Silda, in the southern part of Sildegapet in Stad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the eider, oystercatcher, turnstone, lesser black-backed gull, grey gull, black-tailed godwit, red-billed tern, dunlin, lapwing and little curlew.

gulholmen-naturreservat-nat91004ba8.d: Gulholmen Nature Reserve consists of islets and skerries south-west of Askrova in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding and migration site for seabirds with its naturally associated vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the greylag goose, eider, oystercatcher, turnstone, lesser black-backed gull, grey gull, black-tailed gull, common gull, common tern and red-billed tern.

trefotskjera-naturreservat-natcead7bf8.d: The Trefotskjera Nature Reserve comprises an area between Askrova and Svanøy in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.’ Confirmed breeding species include the eider, goldeneye, oystercatcher, turnstone, redshank, common gull, Arctic tern, red-billed tern and black guillemot.

hovdefjell-naturreservat-nat6b88a3b8.d: The Hovdefjell Nature Reserve comprises an area on and around the northern end of Hovden in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally associated vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the greylag goose, eider, common scoter, oystercatcher, turnstone, black-tailed godwit, lesser black-backed gull, Arctic skua and black guillemot. Until around the year 2000, this was home to the largest grey gull colony in southern Norway.

raud-y-naturreservat-nat3b5ee534.d: The Raudøy Nature Reserve comprises an area south of Atløyna in Askvoll municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the greylag goose, eider, common scoter, golden plover, lapwing, little curlew, turnstone, common gull, black-backed gull and kittiwake.

bunesholmane-naturreservat-natf96d0326.d: The Bunesholmane Nature Reserve consists of two large and five smaller islets near Geita Lighthouse in Askvoll municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the greylag goose, eider, common scoter, oystercatcher, turnstone, Arctic skua, grey gull and black-backed gull.

myrb-rskjera-naturreservat-nat8e41a716.d: The Myrbærskjera Nature Reserve comprises an area to the west of Lutelandet in Fjaler municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions and to preserve an important breeding and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the eider, oystercatcher, turnstone, Arctic skua, common gull, lesser black-backed gull, red-billed tern, Arctic tern and black guillemot.

krakksfjellet-naturreservat-nat19ff455a.d: The Krakksfjellet Nature Reserve comprises an area on Sula in Solund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 11 December 2020 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large and largely undisturbed forest area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old pine forest that has adapted over a long period to oceanic climatic conditions.’

ytamo-naturreservat-natf6fe31b8.d: The Ytamo Nature Reserve comprises an area in Jostedalen in the municipality of Luster. The area was designated a protected area on 19 June 2009 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests / rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large, virtually untouched forest area with special habitat types, encompassing the full diversity of species and vegetation types and all natural ecological processes. The area has particular scientific and educational value due to its diversity of broad-leaved forests, floodplain forests, aspen forests, swamp forest and river terraces in a state of natural integrity that is unusual in the southern boreal zone, which, together with interesting species occurrences, gives the area great reference value.”

vetlefjords-yra-naturreservat-nat2c02b0b.d: The Vetlefjordsøyra Nature Reserve comprises an area at the head of Vetlefjorden in Sogndal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 December 1991 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife, particularly with regard to the delta area as a habitat type (geomorphologically and with well-developed salt marshes) and the area’s value for wetland birds during the migration season.”

sakris-y-naturreservat-nat35f67461.d: Sakrisøy Nature Reserve comprises an area at the mouth of Åfjorden in Hyllestad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 20 December 1991 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. Access is prohibited from 1 April to 1 August inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important marine island and shallow-water area with its natural vegetation and wildlife, particularly in view of the area’s value as a wintering and breeding site for wetland birds.”

torsholmane-naturreservat-nat4994abba.d: The Torsholmane Nature Reserve comprises an area near Losna in Solund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the eider, oystercatcher, black-tailed godwit, grey gull, lesser black-backed gull, common gull, red-billed tern, Arctic tern and Arctic skua.

eggholmane-lisjeholmen-naturreservat-nat.d: The Eggholmane-Lisjeholmen Nature Reserve consists of a number of small islands, islets and skerries off Kvamsøya in Sande municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 August 2010 (approved on 28 May 2010) as one of 36 reserves in Møre og Romsdal. The reserve forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard an area of particular value for biodiversity.
