gas-ya-geitholmen-naturreservat-nat18a27.d: The Gåsøya/Geitholmen Nature Reserve is situated north of Skogsøya in Øksnes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises Gåsøya, Geitholmen and several other small islets and skerries. The area covers 6,655 dekar, of which 6,170 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard a rich breeding habitat for seabirds.

sel-ya-naturreservat-nat8e7e1318.d: Seløya Nature Reserve is situated in Hadsel municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises Seløya and Litlseløya, north-west of Fiskebøl, as well as a number of smaller islets. The area covers 751 dekar, of which 449 dekar is water. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds.

hongv-ret-galtholmen-naturreservat-nate7.d: The Hongværet/Galtholmen Nature Reserve is situated south-east of Ramberg in Bø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve consists of a number of flat islets with lush vegetation. The area covers 795 dekar, of which 725 dekar is water. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding and rearing ground for seabirds.

sau-ya-naturreservat-nat8266bbe4.d: The Sauøya Nature Reserve is situated in Ånnfjorden in the municipality of Øksnes in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 184 dekar, of which 100 dekar is water. The area has been designated a protected area to safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds.

ulv-yv-ret-naturreservat-nat8cc80d68.d: The Ulvøyværet Nature Reserve is situated in Hadsel municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises an area of islets and skerries to the west of Hadseløya. The area covers 8,879 dekar, of which 8,808 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds.

grunnf-r-dyrefredningsomrade-natde559997.d: The Grunnfør Bird Sanctuary is situated in Hadsel municipality in Nordland. The sanctuary is located at Grunnfør on the island of Austvågøya. The area covers 1,650 dekar, of which 671 dekar is land. The bird sanctuary was established to preserve the area’s rich birdlife and its habitat, particularly in view of the area’s key importance as a migration route for the pink-footed goose. The Lågen Nature Reserve is situated within the bird sanctuary.

lagen-naturreservat-nateaf0d85d.d: The Lågen Nature Reserve is situated in Hadsel municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses the small lake Lågen at Grunnfør on Austvågøya. The area covers 70 dekar, of which 55 dekar is land. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife, particularly due to its significance as a breeding and migration area for wetland birds. The nature reserve lies within the Grunnfør bird sanctuary.

laukvik-yene-naturreservat-nat7f867520.d: The Laukvikøyene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Vågan municipality in Nordland. The reserve was established to ‘preserve a valuable coastal area, with its naturally associated flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding ground for wetland birds and as a wintering ground for seabirds. Smaller sites within the area are of great botanical value in terms of coastal vegetation.’ The area lies north of Kabelvåg and south of Laukvik on Austvågøya, and covers an area of 10,888 dekar, of which 7,372 dekar is marine area. The area consists of shallow waters and islands. On the main island, there are marshlands with several freshwater ponds. Several bays and larger inlets extend into this area.

sundsvollsundet-naturreservat-nat71f578f.d: Sundsvollsundet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on Helløya in Harstad municipality, Troms. The nature reserve is situated at the southernmost tip of the island, on the mountainside facing Sundsvollsundet, which separates Helløya from Bjarkøya. It covers a total area of 234 dekar, of which 77 dekar consists of exposed rock, 108 dekar consists of scrub forest and 19 dekar consists of marshland. The nature reserve was established on 4 June 2004 to protect the bird cliff and its flora and fauna. The western part of the area is home to the largest colony of black guillemots in Troms. Great cormorants, grey gulls and kittiwakes are other bird species found in the nature reserve.

laugen-landskapsvernomrade-nat973689bc.d: The Laugen Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area on the Trondenes Peninsula in Harstad municipality, Troms. The area lies between Altevågen in the north and Trondenes in the south and comprises Altevågholmen, Sølvskeivågen, the Laugen pond and the neighbouring land areas bounded by Trondenesveien to the east. It has a total area of 153 dekar, of which 85 dekar consists of salt or fresh water and 56 dekar consists of deciduous woodland. The landscape conservation area was established on 8 December 1995 to protect the old cultural landscape and the pond, which serves as a breeding ground for wetland bird species such as horned grebes and common goldeneyes. The area has aquatic vegetation with a limited variety of species.

tjeldneset-naturreservat-nat402e63d3.d: Tjeldneset Nature Reserve is situated in Tjeldsund municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve lies south of Tjeldnes, in the south-west of Tjeldøya. The area covers 3,205 dekar, of which 1,585 dekar is water. The area is protected to safeguard the most botanically valuable coastal site in Ofoten.

storberget-naturreservat-nataffa4c8e.d: Storberget Nature Reserve is situated east of Kilstad on Tjeldøya in Tjeldsund municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,605 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a woodland area with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes.

kvannesvatn-naturreservat-nata6b3fba4.d: Kvannesvatn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Harstad municipality in Troms. The nature reserve is situated approximately 14 kilometres south of Harstad town centre, between Sørvikvågen to the north and Brokvika to the south, and encompasses Lake Kvannesvatnet and the neighbouring wetland area. It has a total area of 125 dekar, of which 46 dekar consists of water or marshland and 68 dekar consists of deciduous forest. The nature reserve was established on 14 February 1975 to preserve a nutrient-rich calcareous lake and its surroundings, along with the associated flora and fauna. It is a breeding ground for species including horned grebes, tufted ducks, gadwalls and common scoters.

froholman-naturreservat-nat8a933a7d.d: Froholman Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the northern part of Harstad municipality in Troms. The nature reserve encompasses the Froholman archipelago in Andfjorden, north-west of Bjarkøya. It has a total area of 433 dekar, of which 373 dekar comprises marine areas between the islands. The nature reserve was established on 4 June 2004 to protect an area of islets and skerries with surrounding shallow waters that are of great importance to seabirds. It is a breeding ground for, amongst others, the lesser black-backed gull, herring gull, black-headed gull, black-tailed godwit, red-billed tern, common tern, black guillemot, eider and oystercatcher. The area has lush vegetation, partly due to the birds’ fertilisation.

fjelldalslia-naturreservat-natfc0e3281.d: Fjelldalslia Nature Reserve is situated south-east of Fjelldal in Tjeldsund municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 754 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a lush, varied and largely unspoilt birch forest with a good population of wood anemone.

steinav-r-landskapsvernomrade-natd596a47.d: The Steinavær Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area in the northern part of Harstad municipality in Troms. The area comprises Ytre and Indre Steinavær, which are situated in Andfjorden between Andøya to the west and Senja to the east. It has a total area of 5,766 dekar, of which 368 dekar is land area. The landscape conservation area was established on 4 June 1994 to preserve an archipelago and a cultural landscape of great importance to seabirds. Species that breed in the area include the common gull, herring gull, black-backed gull, black guillemot, kittiwake, shag and eider. There are coral formations in the sea area between Indre and Ytre Steinavær.

forfjorddalen-naturreservat-nat032558de.d: The Forfjorddalen Nature Reserve is situated in the municipalities of Sortland and Andøy in Nordland. The nature reserve is located in the Forfjorddalen valley on the island of Hinnøya and covers an area of 9,065 dekar. The area has been protected to preserve a large valley with its woodland and marshland. Among other things, the area is home to some of the oldest pine trees in Scandinavia.

forfjorden-naturreservat-nat432ea7cf.d: The Forfjorden Nature Reserve is situated in the inner part of Forfjorden in the municipalities of Sortland and Andøy in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 3,103 dekar, of which 1,872 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect an area of great Quaternary geological value.

gullesfjordbotn-naturreservat-natef7a84e.d: Gullesfjordbotn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gullesfjordbotn, in the municipality of Kvæfjord in Troms. The nature reserve encompasses land areas between the Vesterelva river in the west and the Lakselva river in the east, as well as marine areas around the inner part of Gullesfjorden. It covers an area of 317 dekar, of which 183 dekar is water. The nature reserve was established in 1995 to protect a well-developed salt marsh complex, situated between two river mouths, along with its associated birdlife. The land area consists mainly of clay and gravel beaches surrounded by birch forest.

godfjordbotn-naturreservat-nat72df706c.d: Godfjordbotn Nature Reserve is situated at the innermost part of Godfjorden in Sortland municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 125 dekar, of which 85 dekar is land, 2 dekar is freshwater and 38 dekar is sea. The area is protected to preserve an unspoilt salt marsh and its associated birdlife, which is representative of a specific type of salt marsh complex associated with the most sheltered fjord bottoms on Hinnøya, in Lofoten and Vesterålen.

endletvatn-naturreservat-natf0c846a0.d: Endletvatn Nature Reserve is situated in Andøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses Einlettvatnet (37 metres above sea level) and the surrounding bogs, south of Andenes and west of Skarstein on Andøya. The area covers 600 dekar, of which 270 dekar is water. The area is protected to preserve typical nutrient-poor flat bogs of great importance for research into the history of vegetation.

bleiks-ya-naturreservat-nat763af4e4.d: Bleiksøya Nature Reserve is situated off the coast of Bleik in Andøy municipality in Nordland. The area comprises Bleiksøya and a few small islets off the coast. The nature reserve covers 393 dekar, of which 248 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to safeguard a valuable bird colony and protect the breeding grounds of several vulnerable seabird species.

kolas-naturreservat-natd21de127.d: Kolås Nature Reserve is situated in a valley basin stretching from the northern end of Kolåstjern and northwards between Kolåsen and the settlements along Kolåsveien, north of Son in Vestby municipality. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a diverse area of broad-leaved deciduous forest. Today’s broad-leaved deciduous forest sites are remnant habitats from a previously warmer climate, and the forests also constitute northern outposts of Central European forest types. Norway therefore has the world’s northernmost deciduous broad-leaved forests, but these have been greatly reduced as the areas have been put to other uses. Many types of deciduous broad-leaved forest are represented within the reserve. In addition to the extremely rare grey alder-ash forest, these include grey alder-hawthorn forest and grey alder-ash forest, black alder swamp forest and elm-lime forest.

kl-vstadh-gda-naturreservat-nat1e7c9721.d: Kløvstadhøgda Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the western side of Biskopåsen, south-east of Brøttum in Ringsaker municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 2002 to protect a forested area with intact stands of elm-lime forest and low-herb spruce forest. The bedrock consists of conglomerate, which is calcareous in places, providing a habitat for rare plant species. Both wildlife and vegetation are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting is also permitted in accordance with other regulations. Cycling and horse riding are prohibited outside the roads and paths marked on the conservation map.

asermarka-naturreservat-natf6337874.d: Åsermarka Nature Reserve is a protected area in the municipality of Indre Østfold in Østfold. The area is approximately 1.5 km long and is connected to the Åsermarka hiking area to the north-west of Askim town centre. It lies along the south-eastern bank of the River Glomma between Solbergfoss and Øyeren, on north-west-facing, partly steep terrain. This shady and damp area is home to a very old spruce forest; the oldest spruce has been measured at 350 years, and many others are over 200 years old. The undergrowth is home to several rare plants, including Red List species. The forest was designated a nature reserve in 2002. The area also includes Sandholmen, which boasts the country’s largest concentration of pit dwellings from the Early Stone Age.

apalviken-naturreservat-natdee62760.d: The Apalviken Nature Reserve consists of a rocky outcrop on the western side of Hankø in Fredrikstad municipality. A black alder swamp forest grows in the shallow, narrow rock crevice; particularly in the south, it is heavily exposed to the wind. The trees are short, gnarled and full of twigs. This stands in stark contrast to the more bare granite outcrops in the surrounding area. There are also trees whose roots form stilts, known as pedestals, where water often pools. Elsewhere in the ground layer, sword-leaved lily and tall sedge are particularly common, but shield-leaved saxifrage and yellow star-of-Bethlehem are also found. The vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees, is protected against damage and destruction.

vestre-vansj-naturreservat-natadc54390.d: The Vestre Vansjø Nature Reserve comprises the south-western basin of Lake Vansjø, including the adjacent shoreline areas, as well as the island of Feøya. The area is shallow, with an average depth of 3.5 metres, and is heavily overgrown. There is a great deal of marsh vegetation, including common reed and common bulrush. Feøya is largely covered in coniferous forest, whilst the rest of the area consists of large tracts of black alder. The area serves as an important migration, resting, foraging and breeding ground for many bird species. As of 1986, 59 different species had been recorded here.

altervatn-naturreservat-natae5cc5fc.d: Altervatn Nature Reserve is situated in Dønna municipality in Nordland. The area lies south-west of Dønnes, in the north of the island of Dønna. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area with rich and productive water and marshlands and a rich and interesting birdlife. The nature reserve covers 2,200 dekar, of which 650 dekar is water.

rols-ya-naturreservat-nat043f37b0.d: The Rolsøya Nature Reserve comprises the island of Rolsøya and the surrounding waters. The land area is 38 daa, and the total area is 87 daa. The island is situated in Børgin, a side fjord of Trondheimsfjorden, which is divided between Inderøy and Steinkjer municipalities in Trøndelag. The area was designated a nature reserve in 2003. The purpose of the protection is to preserve the island, as well as the adjacent marine areas, with their naturally associated flora and fauna. Rolsøya is of particular value as a breeding ground for seabirds. The vegetation is dominated by spruce, mixed with tree species such as hawthorn, rowan, grey alder, elm and maple. During the New Year’s storm of 1992, a significant number of spruce trees were blown down. The southernmost part of the island is treeless, and the vegetation is dominated by grasses and herbs.

hiesten-naturreservat-nat64042852.d: Hiesten Nature Reserve is an area of coniferous forest surrounding Store Hiesten (238 metres above sea level). The reserve is situated entirely on property gnr. 31 bnr. 1 in the north of Rakkestad municipality in Østfold. The area features a variety of forest types, much of which is old-growth. Among other things, bear’s-ear grows here – the only place in Østfold where it is found. There are also a number of Red Listed species of fungi and lichens.

eidsfjellet-naturreservat-nat71ecd036.d: Eidsfjellet Nature Reserve is a forested area in the far west of the municipalities of Våler and Åsnes. The area consists largely of old-growth forest, with many small bogs. Between Odalsfjellet and Fjellråknappen there is also a somewhat larger bog area. The bedrock consists mainly of gneiss, which results in nutrient-poor soil, but there is also some gabbro. The bogs are of the nutrient-poor type. The forest has been significantly affected by past logging and, particularly in the south, is characterised by even-aged spruce forest with little litter and deadwood. Nevertheless, three Red List species have been found in the area, and according to the Norwegian Environment Agency, the reserve has ‘potential to develop an interesting sub-oceanic-style flora and fauna’.

fiskvagvatnet-naturreservat-nat0271f086.d: Fiskvågvatnet Nature Reserve is situated in Saltdal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses Fiskvågvatnet, just west of Rognan. The area covers 160 dekar, of which 105 dekar is water. The area is protected to preserve a natural, nutrient-rich wetland area. Fiskvågvatnet Nature Reserve is situated right next to Fiskvågflåget Nature Reserve.

eine-naturreservat-nat39c9dc69.d: The Eine Nature Reserve comprises a forested area on Eineåsen, north of Rykkinn in the municipality of Bærum. The terrain is gently undulating, set on a bedrock of rhomboid porphyry. The soil is rich in the depressions, but poorer on the hilltops. The vegetation consists largely of old spruce forest, but also includes deciduous broad-leaved woodland and deadwood at various stages of decomposition. There are many signs of selective felling, but in places there is also intact forest, some of which even has the character of natural forest. A number of Red Listed fungi species associated with old spruce forest have been recorded, in some cases in large concentrations. These include the flame polypore, the spotted polypore and the rose-coloured polypore, amongst many others.

innstrandfj-ra-fuglefredningsomrade-natf.d: The Innstrandfjæra Wildlife Reserve is a protected habitat in Ørland municipality, Sør-Trøndelag. The area was designated by Royal Decree on 23 December 1983; it covers approximately 1.1 km², of which approximately 0.1 km² is land area. The remainder is a marine area with a varied seabed and tidal pools; it is an important breeding and resting area for seabirds and migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1983 to safeguard a specific waterbird habitat of particular importance during the migration seasons, and forms an important part of the Ørland wetland system. It is the smallest of the four sub-areas within the Ørland Wetland System Ramsar site. The area lies on the southern side of Bjugnfjorden and the northern side of the Ørland Peninsula, between Uthaug and Ervika.

hovsfj-ra-fuglefredningsomrade-nat49ef11.d: The Hovsfjæra Wildlife Reserve is a protected habitat in Ørland municipality, Trøndelag. The area was designated by Royal Decree on 23 December 1983; it covers approximately 1.2 km², of which approximately 0.07 km² is land area. The remainder is a shallow intertidal zone and serves as an important foraging and resting area for seabirds and migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1983 to conserve the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitats in the area, particularly with regard to waders and ducks. It is the second smallest of the four sub-areas within the Ørland Wetland System Ramsar site. The area is situated on the southern side of the Ørland Peninsula, between Brekstad and Austrått.

vinstradalen-naturreservat-nate9aa0992.d: Vinstradalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Nord-Fron municipality. It comprises an area near Vinstra. The area was designated a nature reserve on 22 June 2018 and extended on 6 December 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling is prohibited outside the existing tractor tracks marked on the conservation map and on footpaths. Horse riding and the use of horse and cart are prohibited outside the existing tractor tracks marked on the conservation map.

eld-ya-naturreservat-nat04975e6c.d: The Eldøya Nature Reserve encompasses the north-western part of Eldøya, including the shallow bay off its coast, in the municipality of Moss. The nature reserve is surrounded by the Eldøya-Sletter Landscape Conservation Area. The bedrock consists mainly of rhomboid porphyry conglomerate, whilst the unconsolidated deposits consist of moraine (the Onsøy step), particularly in the southern part of the reserve. The vegetation is of the salt marsh type, with a fringe of woodland at the rear. In damp areas, strawberry clover is found, amongst other species, whilst in drier places there is common rockrose. The area is of particular value as a breeding ground for seabirds, including the mute swan, eider and the large gull species. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. All vegetation is protected from destruction, including that under water.

vesle-sletter-naturreservat-natcab890c2.d: The Vesle Sletter Nature Reserve comprises the entire small headland on the south side of the island of Store Sletter, as well as the surrounding coastal waters. The reserve is surrounded by the Eldøya-Sletter Landscape Conservation Area. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect the habitat of flora and fauna. The sea area to the south of the reserve serves as a refuge for eider duck broods when there is heavy small boat traffic. Access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July, both on land and at sea. The highest point in the reserve is 5.8 metres above sea level. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry conglomerate, a rock type that is very rare globally and is found on the chain of islands in Østfold from Søster and northwards.

s-ndre-sletter-naturreservat-nat2f068fa6.d: The Søndre Sletter Nature Reserve comprises the majority of the island of Søndre Sletter, as well as the sea area extending approximately 50 metres from the island, in Råde municipality in Østfold. The reserve is surrounded by the Eldøya-Sletter Landscape Conservation Area. In the north-east of the island there is a public recreation area with toilets; the rest of the island is part of the reserve. Access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July, both on land and at sea. The island’s highest point is 16.6 metres above sea level. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry conglomerate, a rock type that is extremely rare globally and is found along the entire chain of islands in Østfold from Søster and northwards. The island is home to a rich variety of birdlife. In 2000, breeding barnacle geese were discovered there for the first time.

krakstadfjorden-naturreservat-natee3a18b.d: The Kråkstadfjorden Nature Reserve is situated in the inner part of Krokstadfjorden in Råde municipality. The reserve comprises shallow-water areas on both sides of the fjord, and a deep channel running through the middle. It also includes a narrow stretch of shoreline, totalling 70 dekar of land area. Just outside the reserve lies the Hestevold wastewater treatment plant, which treats wastewater from Råde municipality before it is discharged into the fjord. The area is a breeding ground for around 11 bird species, including the reed warbler, lapwing, redshank and common shelduck. However, the area is also of great importance as a feeding and resting place for other seabirds and waders. As of 1986, 69 species had been recorded in the area, of which 23 were duck species and 24 were wader species. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment.

solbralia-og-stordalsberget-naturreserva.d: The Solbrålia and Stordalsberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Nord-Fron and Sør-Fron. It comprises an area along the Gudbrandsdalslågen river between Vinstra and Hundorp. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 December 2015 and was extended in 2017 and 2018. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling is prohibited outside existing tractor tracks and paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of well-developed calcareous spruce forest, low-herb forest with both spruce, birch and pine, tall-herb forests, grey alder–hawthorn forests and weeping birch forests, as well as calcareous southern mountain, rock face and scree habitat types and natural pastureland.”

sula-naturreservat-nat77feb519.d: The Sula Nature Reserve comprises a three-kilometre-long ravine along the River Sula in Nord-Fron. The ravine is one of the least disturbed in the Gudbrandsdalen valley, although there are also traces of past selective felling and little deadwood. The purpose of the reserve is to protect a well-rounded stream gorge with considerable diversity and a rich flora of lichens and vascular plants. It is home to what is perhaps the largest population of huldregras in Norway.

kvamsholman-biotopvernomrade-nate9596e28.d: The Kvamsholman Biotope Conservation Area comprises two islets with a combined land area of 15 dekar, situated in Trondheimsfjorden in Inderøy municipality, Trøndelag. The total area is 69 dekar. The area was designated a conservation area in 2003. The purpose of the protection is to safeguard an important breeding area for seabirds. The vegetation on the islets consists mainly of grasses and herbs (meadowsweet, marsh violet, etc.), but also includes some thickets of rowan, juniper and rosehip. Kvamsholman is a diverse seabird site in an area of high human activity and an important breeding ground for eider ducks and common gulls. Large numbers of individuals from several species contribute to the area’s biodiversity.

islandselve-naturreservat-nat0f3a12bc.d: The Islandselve Nature Reserve comprises an area near Bagn in the municipality of Sør-Aurdal. The area was designated a protected area on 21 June 2019 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a relatively large stream gorge with a very high degree of ecological diversity, where the forest comprises, amongst other things, very damp, highly productive and lush tall-shrub forest, as well as rich low-herb forest and grey alder–elm forest, and where the wettest sections feature a lichen community that is extremely rare in Eastern Norway.”

malfjell-naturreservat-nat13ac8ae4.d: Malfjell Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Drangedal municipality. It comprises an area bordering Toke. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to protect a forest area of particular importance for biodiversity due to the presence of rich deciduous forest in the form of low-herb oak forest, with elements of rich scree linden forest, calcareous pine forest and low-herb spruce forest. Furthermore, the purpose of the nature reserve is to protect an area of particular scientific value due to the presence of a very rich, seasonally moist mixed oak forest and rare and threatened species of vascular plants and soil-dwelling fungi.

asbj-rnasen-naturreservat-nat35ba29c2.d: Asbjørnåsen Nature Reserve is situated in the south-east of Våler and the north of Sarpsborg, 2–3 kilometres west of Mingevannet. The topography is characterised by the hills of Haukåsen and Kallen to the west, and Kjerringa to the east, with Asbjørnåsen being less prominent. Just to the east of the reserve lies the Kjerringåsen Alpine Centre. The hills are separated by small, narrow rift valleys. The bedrock consists mainly of gneiss, with some more nutrient-rich rock types in places. There is little loose material, but some marine deposits and peat bogs in the depressions. The vegetation is dominated by heather-pine forest, but there are also blueberry spruce forests and some birch in wetter areas. There are also patches of other deciduous trees.

ytter-ya-naturreservat-nat832fd6c0.d: Ytterøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated on an island in the Glåma river in Elverum municipality, in the Innlandet region. The island lies just north of the hamlet of Øksna, and the reserve protects an area of approximately 57 dekar. The nature reserve was established on 14 February 2014. The purpose of the reserve is to protect a flood-affected island in the Glåma river. The island features grey alder and hawthorn woodland, as well as vegetation types of particular importance.

moskj-ra-naturreservat-nat7502fb7f.d: Moskjæra Nature Reserve is situated on Lake Vansjø in the municipality of Råde, and comprises the shallow Danskebukta bay, the peninsula on its eastern side and the waters to the east of it, as well as Moskjæra and the waters between Moskjæra and the mainland. The vast majority of the reserve is therefore marine area; only 85 dekar is land area. Danskebukta contains areas of common reed and sea rush. Behind these lie marshy areas and a fringe of black alder. Higher up on the peninsula, the vegetation consists mainly of nutrient-poor pine forest. With the exception of the two largest islets, all the islets are treeless. The reserve thus encompasses breeding grounds both for gulls out on the islets and, amongst others, for mute swans, reed warblers and reed buntings in the reed beds.

korpreiret-naturreservat-nat3e1f195c.d: Korpreiret Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Elverum municipality. It comprises an area near Øksna. The area was designated a nature reserve on 25 November 2016 and extended on 6 December 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside the paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve, as an ecosystem, a reasonably intact stream gorge environment with old spruce forest that is of particular importance for biodiversity as it contains demanding and threatened plant, fungus and lichen species. Korpreiret consists of a well-developed west-east-running ravine with continuous older spruce forest on both sides of the River Øksna.

kalvmyra-naturreservat-natcdb9d761.d: Kalvmyra Nature Reserve, sometimes referred to as Nordteigen Nature Reserve, is a nature reserve in Elverum municipality in the Innlandet region. The purpose of the nature reserve is “to preserve a ravine landscape with old spruce forest that is of particular importance for biodiversity as it contains demanding, rare and vulnerable plant species”. The nature reserve is situated on the southern side of Holshaugen in Strandbygda. At the bottom of the ravines there is a relatively rich swamp forest, with records of, amongst other things, the rare swamp forest species wood sweetgrass. All vegetation (including dead shrubs and trees) is protected against damage and destruction. However, it is permitted to pick berries and edible mushrooms within the reserve.

hakaskallen-naturreservat-nat374fe92f.d: Hakaskallen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Elverum municipality in the Innlandet region. The purpose of the reserve is to protect an area comprising old spruce forest, bogs and stream valleys. The area is home to several rare species of lichen and fungi. The reserve covers 1,190 dekar and is situated on the north-western side of the Hakaskallen hill. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 December 2014. An access path to the Finnskogleden trail runs through a small part of the nature reserve, and there is a hut here associated with this trail.

telemarkslunden-og-ekebylunden-naturrese.d: The Telemarkslunden and Ekebylunden Nature Reserve was established in 2010 as an extension of the Telemarklunden Natural Monument, east of Fuglevik in Moss municipality. The reserve comprises Telemarkslunden in the north-east, a section of the Gunnarsbybekken stream in the west, and an area in between that links these two together (Ekebylunden). The reserve is entirely surrounded by the Værne Monastery Landscape Conservation Area. The reserve lies 3–18 metres above sea level, on marine clay sediments. In the upper part of the reserve, the vegetation is characterised by mature beech and oak woodland planted around 1890. The shrub layer also includes hazel, rowan, maple and ash. Further down, the forest contains a greater proportion of black alder and elm, with hawthorn, spindle and wild currant in the shrub layer.

kajalunden-naturreservat-nat5955fabb.d: The Kajalunden Nature Reserve encompasses a hill south of the farmyard at Evje Manor in Rygge. The reserve is surrounded by a golf course and bordered to the south by a power line. The hill is covered with deciduous woodland, specifically a beech forest. The beech trees originate from a planting carried out around 1870, and there are trees believed to be over 150 years old. In the southern part of the area there are also some spruce and pine trees, but the spruce is in the process of being displaced by beech, which is highly competitive. There is therefore an ongoing process of succession within the reserve, which is of ecological interest. The beech forms a fairly dense canopy, creating a shady forest floor and, consequently, a rather sparse ground layer. In the south-west, there is deciduous forest dominated by ash.

refsnes-naturreservat-natd7d80892.d: Refsnes Nature Reserve is a predominantly west-facing slope on Jeløya in Moss municipality. The reserve was first designated in December 1981, covering an area of 83 dekar. The aim was to protect an area of deciduous broad-leaved forest. The reserve was extended to 220 dekar on 16 April 2010 and now encompasses a wide variety of forest types. The bedrock consists of basalt and rhomboid porphyry. In the steepest areas, there is very little loose material, whilst further down there is plenty. Here there are elm-lime forests, grey alder-ash forests and a narrow strip of black alder-beach forest down towards the sea. In places, there are pedunculate oaks and other tree species. On the north-facing slope at Rambergnebba, where the sun’s heat is not quite as intense, there are more pine and birch trees.

stuttgonglie-naturreservat-nat3a92c1ab.d: The Stuttgonglie Nature Reserve is situated on the east bank of the River Sjoa in Vågå municipality. The reserve encompasses the hillside up towards Stuttgongkampen and southwards past the eastern shore of Nedre Sjodalsvatnet and up to the bare mountain there. The reserve is relatively large, consisting mainly of primeval-style creeping pine forest and low-growing pine forest. Both the noun forms ‘Stuttgonglie’ and ‘Stuttgonglia’ are used.

veogjelet-naturreservat-nat3ea9ec84.d: The Veogjelet Nature Reserve encompasses the lower reaches of the River Veo and the area to the south of the eastern slope of Hindsæterkampen in Vågå municipality. The bedrock in the area is varied, comprising gabbro, gneiss, mica schist, phyllite, quartzite and olivine. The topography is also varied, with rock faces and ravines along the river, and gentler sections where there are thick layers of loose deposits. With such varied ground conditions, the vegetation is also diverse. Much of the forest has been affected by logging, but there is still plenty of windfall and deadwood at all stages of decomposition. In Veogjelet, there are also large trees with many dry branches (pine with dry branches), where crustose lichens can be found.

buberget-naturreservat-nat0e4b325e.d: Buberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Våler municipality. It comprises an area in the very north of the municipality and borders Sweden. The Kjølberget wind farm is situated in an area just north of the reserve. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a natural area dominated by old spruce forest, with elements of bog and pond, and which is of great importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for rare and vulnerable species of fungi and lichens. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to further develop them.”

klingerhaugen-naturreservat-nata3c447f1.d: The Klingerhaugen Nature Reserve comprises the south-western slope of Klingerhaugen, three kilometres east of Strandlykkja in Stange municipality. The area features relatively old woodland with a wide mix of tree species and a fair amount of deadwood, which provides the basis for varied vegetation types and species diversity. There is a large number of vascular plants here, including the night-flowering violet and thermophilic species such as the spring snowflake and the Norway maple. Wildlife is protected against harm and unnecessary disturbance. The same applies to all vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees. However, hunting and the gathering of berries and mushrooms are permitted. Lighting fires using dry twigs from the ground is also permitted in accordance with other regulations, but the use of horses, bicycles and motor vehicles is prohibited.

hopslia-naturreservat-nat372a4932.d: Hopslia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Bjørnafjorden and Samnanger. It comprises an area by Samnangerfjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 19 March 2021. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing tractor tracks, the use of bicycles, horses and carts, and horse riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats in an area that forms part of a larger forest landscape, and which features a wide variety of natural habitats and vegetation types, including, amongst others, rich deciduous broadleaf woodland, mature pine forest, rich bogs and rich swamp woodland. Important tree species include yew, elm, ash, hazel, grey alder and black alder.

roms-terberget-naturreservat-nat6eef20af.d: The Romsæterberget Nature Reserve was established on 19 March 2021, as a continuation of the former Stange Nature Reserve. The latter was established by royal decree on 16 February 1923. It is thus one of the oldest protected areas in Norway, and also one of the smallest, covering an area of just three decares. The reserve is situated at Romsætra, a good three kilometres east of Strandlykkja Church in Stange. The reserve contains a stand of spruce forest which, according to the original resolution, ‘shall be protected against felling and logging of any kind’.

nordre-munksj-berget-naturreservat-nata2.d: Nordre Munksjøberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Trysil municipality in the Innlandet region. The reserve, covering approximately 2.9 km², is situated on the northern part of the Munksjøberget mountain. The nature reserve was established on 19 March 2021. The purpose of the reserve is to protect a forested summit with stands of old spruce, pine and birch. There is a great deal of hanging lichen in the area, including old man’s beard and split beard.

bogenlia-naturreservat-nat05d110c9.d: Bogenlia Nature Reserve is situated on the island of Rauer, to the west of Fredrikstad municipality. The reserve comprises an east-facing slope with rock faces and scree, where the bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry conglomerate. The vegetation is a deciduous forest of the elm-lime type. The ground vegetation is sparse but nevertheless relatively species-rich, dominated by wood anemone and blue anemone. Wildlife and plant life are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. It is prohibited to carry out activities that alter the natural conditions. Open fires and motorised traffic are not permitted. The site is located within a military area and is not open to the public.

rognhaugen-naturreservat-nat6344f25f.d: Rognhaugen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated on the ridge between Romerike and Hadeland, in the municipalities of Hurdal and Gran. The forest in the area belongs to the middle boreal vegetation zone and is dominated by old, coarse spruce. Around the hill there are flatter areas of marshland, including large and small forest islands. The reserve is home to the Red Listed species hollow-stemmed sedge, yellow-stalked sedge, black-stemmed sedge and old man’s beard. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, as are dead trees and fallen timber. However, it is permitted to light a fire using dry twigs, subject to the relevant regulations. Furthermore, ordinary hunting is permitted, as is the gathering of berries and edible mushrooms. Motorised traffic is prohibited, with certain exceptions specified in the conservation regulations.

kvitv-r-naturreservat-natc894f3fb.d: The Kvitvær Nature Reserve consists of islets and skerries north-west of Grøtøya in Karlsøy municipality. The area lies within the Ytre Karlsøy Marine Protected Area, which was designated on 23 June 2020. The nature reserve was designated on 4 June 2004 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 15 August inclusive, access to land within the conservation area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is “to preserve an area comprising a group of small islets and skerries with adjacent shallow waters, together with its flora and fauna. The area is of particular importance for seabirds.”

ed-ya-landskapsvernomrade-nat49a99898.d: The Edøya Landscape Conservation Area, which includes a wildlife sanctuary, is a landscape conservation area in the far south-west of Tromsø municipality in Troms. The area comprises Edøya, Gardsholmen and Kanikholmen and is situated approximately four kilometres south-west of Sommarøy. It has a total area of 1,616 dekar, of which 114 dekar is sea. Edøya was designated as a bird sanctuary from 1869 to 1982. The landscape conservation area was established in 2004 to preserve the island, which is important for seabirds, and the natural and cultural landscape with its wildlife. Herring gulls, black-backed gulls, black-tailed godwits, eider ducks, black guillemots, shags and greylag geese breed on the island.

s-rlenangsbotn-naturreservat-nat74f16606.d: Sørlenangsbotn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lyngen municipality in Troms. The reserve was established on 8 December 1995 and encompasses the innermost part of the Sørlenangen fjord, from a line between Blokkøra in the east and Engneset in the west, southwards to Sørlenangsbotn, as well as adjacent areas on land. The area was designated a nature reserve to preserve a large intertidal zone with extensive salt marshes, where the vegetation is highly varied and a number of waterbird species are found in large numbers, particularly during the migration periods. The reserve covers an area of 3,240 dekar, of which 860 dekar is on land, 2,360 dekar is marine area and 20 dekar is freshwater. The protected area consists of a large mudflat that is exposed at low tide.

djupvika-naturreservat-nat4fa58958.d: Djupvika Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Nordkapp. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an ice-marginal delta with raised shorelines and a clearly defined beach ridge at present-day sea level, and an area characterised by Arctic coastal nature with extremely sparse vegetation.

rein-ykalven-naturreservat-nata2c8b995.d: The Reinøykalven Nature Reserve comprises Reinøykalven, just north of Reinøya in Måsøy municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 January 1983 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area.’

lakselvbukt-naturreservat-natfd0516d1.d: Lakselvbukt Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tromsø municipality in Troms. It comprises a wetland area near the village of Lakselvbukt in Sørfjorden (the inner part of Ullsfjorden), around 12 kilometres from the head of the fjord. The western part of the area comprises the outer part of the Lakselva estuary, whilst the smaller Leirelva river flows into the eastern part of the area. The reserve consists of a large salt marsh complex with northern-type vegetation, ranging from salt marshes to brackish water marshes. Pools with thread-leaved rush are well developed, which is rare in Troms. The area is of regional botanical importance. The reserve was established in 1995 to conserve a large salt marsh complex in a bay with a river estuary.

auv-r-naturreservat-nat08110bb0.d: The Auvær Nature Reserve consists of numerous islets, skerries and shoals far out to sea to the west. The reserve is situated in the municipality of Tromsø. The area was designated a protected area on 4 June 2004 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 August inclusive, access to land within the protected area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area with typical archipelago nature facing the open sea, comprising islets, skerries and shallow waters with their flora and fauna. The area is of particular importance for seabirds.’

bug-ynes-plantelivsfredning-nat618008e0.d: The Bugøynes Plant Life Conservation Area is a protected area in Bugøynes, in the municipality of Sør-Varanger in Finnmark. The protected area covers the eastern part of Bugøynes cemetery, with an area of two decares. It is the only known location in Scandinavia where the plant species polar flokk grows. The population was discovered in 1868 and was designated a protected area on 4 October 1919.

adamsfjord-naturreservat-nat88e7f60f.d: Adamsfjord Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lebesby municipality in Finnmark. It was established on 20 December 1991, and the purpose of the conservation was to preserve an area of tidal flats and shallow waters that is important as a resting place for wetland birds, and a terraced landscape that illustrates land uplift following the last ice age. The reserve is situated in the inner part of Adamsfjorden.

stormyra-lapphaugen-naturreservat-nat451.d: The Stormyra (Lapphaugen) Nature Reserve is situated south-east of Fossbakken in Lavangen, Troms, approximately 500 metres south of Lapphaugvatnet. The nature reserve extends almost five kilometres southwards from where the Spanselva (Ruŋgujohka) bends eastwards and flows down through the flat valley floor between Sølvfjellet (Silbavárri) and Storsteinaksla in the west and Melkefjellet (Mielkevárri) to the east. 51 per cent of the reserve’s area consists of bogs; in the northern part there are hill bogs, and further south grassy bogs with sedges and vegetation typical of waterlogged areas. There are almost no precipitation-fed bogs in the reserve. Furthermore, 38 per cent of the area consists of deciduous forest, whilst 105 daa is water, mainly the Spanselva river, its tributaries and meandering lakes along the river.

komagv-rstranda-naturreservat-nat6fb1f2d.d: Komagværstranda Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the far south-east of Vardø municipality in Finnmark. The nature reserve encompasses the sandy bay between the Komagelva river in the north and the Kommagnes river in the south, together with the surrounding land areas, approximately six kilometres north of Skallelv. It has a total area of 6,485 dekar, of which around 1,000 dekar consists of sea or freshwater and 429 dekar consists of marshland. The nature reserve was established in 1991 to preserve the sandy bay and a system of sand dunes with a distinctive configuration. The vegetation consists of sea rye, sheep’s fescue, yarrow, silk pimpernel, sea sandwort, Finnmark sedge, sea thrift, sand spurge, bow sedge, narrow-leaved bog-asphodel and bluebell. The area is rich in birdlife, and the beach serves as a breeding ground for several species of waders.

s-rkjosleira-naturreservat-nat29b1bdd3.d: Sørkjosleira Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Balsfjord municipality, Troms. The nature reserve faces north on the shores of Balsfjorden, east of Grønvoll, and has Ramsar Site status due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1995 to preserve a large intertidal zone with adjacent beach areas. The area comprises well-developed brackish water meadows and salt marshes, pools, salt pans and coastal marshes. It is the county’s most important stopover site for wetland birds, and 18 of the country’s 32 duck species, as well as a total of 25 out of 56 wetland bird species, have been observed and recorded here. The area serves as grazing land in both summer and winter and is an important breeding ground during the summer months.

skipsfjord-landskapsvernomrade-nat5cd54b.d: The Skipsfjord Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Karlsøy municipality in Troms. The landscape conservation area includes protected plant life and was established in 1978. It covers 54.1 km² of land and 10.7 km² of sea. The purpose of the conservation is to ‘preserve a beautiful natural area with a cultural landscape typical of the outer coastal regions of Troms, featuring an unspoilt watercourse, geologically significant formations of scientific interest, and a distinctive and, in parts, rich floraand wildlife’.” The conservation area encompasses Skipsfjorden within a line drawn between Skotallneset and Kvalkjeften, as well as Skipsfjorddalen and that part of the mountains on Vanna from which water drains into Skipsfjord. Skipsfjorddalen has relatively flat terrain with rich peat bogs.

tennvatn-naturreservat-nat2d27217c.d: Tennvatn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Tjeldsund municipality in Troms. The reserve was established in 1995 ‘to preserve a nutrient-rich, calcareous lake with aquatic vegetation of international conservation value, which is important as a breeding and migration area for many species of wetland birds’. Tennvatnet lies approximately 5 km north of Evenes Airport and forms part of the Kvitfors watercourse. The lake is nutrient-rich, with dense aquatic vegetation comprising bottle sedge, river sedge, eight species of pondweed and three species of stonewort. Plant species such as stiff pondweed and slender pondweed reach their northernmost limit here. The lake serves as a migration and breeding area for several species of wetland birds.

virvassdalen-naturreservat-nat13da14bd.d: Virvassdalen Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area, established in 2011, in Virvassdalen in Rana municipality, Nordland county. The nature reserve is situated at the head of the Dunderlandsdalen valley, in an uninhabited, south-east-facing side valley that runs towards Sweden. At the far end of the valley lies Lake Virvatnet, at an altitude of 645 metres above sea level. Virvassdalen has a slight U-shape. On the western side, there are several steep rocky outcrops at the tree line, probably associated with changes in rock type. A couple of small rivers flow down from the west through narrow gorges. The eastern side of the main valley has gentler slopes. The valley opens out towards Lake Virvatnet. Virvassdalen is dominated by limestone bedrock.

lian-naturreservat-nata5546819.d: Lian Nature Reserve is situated on the south-eastern side of the Dunderlands Valley in Rana municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 4,858 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve and safeguard a forest area with all its species and ecological processes.

veten-naturreservat-natca4df909.d: The Veten Nature Reserve is situated on the southern side of the Øynes Peninsula in Fauske municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 690 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a rich calcareous pine forest with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes.

loddvatnet-naturreservat-natf442146e.d: Loddvatnet Nature Reserve is situated in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses Loddvatnet in Misværdalen. The area covers 45 dekar, of which 15 dekar is land and 30 dekar is freshwater. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a small wetland area of great regional conservation value, particularly due to its important functions as a migration, foraging and breeding ground for wetland birds.

skanland-naturreservat-nate9bfe4c1.d: Skånland Nature Reserve is situated near Skånland in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of approximately 6,700 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a woodland area with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes.

mosaksla-naturreservat-natbb6ca989.d: Mosaksla Nature Reserve is situated in Brønnøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 342 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve one of the most floristically rich areas in Helgeland. Among other things, the world’s northernmost population of lime trees is found in the area.

spjeltfjelldalen-naturreservat-nat1ca0a6.d: The Spjeltfjelldalen Nature Reserve is situated in Hemnes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located in the Spjeltfjelldalen valley between Gresvatnet and Røssvatnet. The area covers approximately 30,250 dekar, of which approximately 30,000 dekar is land and approximately 250 dekar is freshwater. The area is protected to preserve a productive high-altitude wetland area of great regional conservation value, particularly due to its rich and varied birdlife.

stor-graddis-naturreservat-nat143db3b4.d: The Stor-Graddis Nature Reserve is situated on the north-eastern bank of the Graddiselva river in Saltdal municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of approximately 4,600 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a diverse and unique pine forest, with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes.

urskar-naturreservat-nat06c04830.d: Urskar Nature Reserve is situated east of Valnesvatnet in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,169 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve an area characterised by a high degree of undisturbed natural conditions and exceptionally species-rich forest types, particularly orchid-rich dwarf birch forest.

vard-ya-naturreservat-natea81f892.d: The Vardøya Nature Reserve is situated in Herøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises part of Vardøya, as well as a number of islets to the south of the island. The area covers 1,433 da, of which 614 da is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard a valuable coastal area, with its naturally associated flora and fauna. The plant species are representative of both salt marshes (particularly brackish water marshes) and seaweed-covered shores. Among other species, sea grass and sea purslane grow here.

risv-ret-naturreservat-nat15ebbc27.d: Risværet Nature Reserve is situated in Lurøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 4,425 dekar, of which 3,225 dekar is marine area. The area has been protected to preserve a valuable coastal area, with its naturally associated flora and fauna.

nystadneslia-naturreservat-nat140aace6.d: Nystadneslia Nature Reserve is situated in Saltdal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located near Borkamo in the Saltdalen valley. The area covers 1,690 dekar. It has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a rich forest landscape with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes.

engasjyen-naturreservat-natcd908348.d: Engasjyen Nature Reserve is situated in Rana municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve consists of a shallow-water and delta area at the mouth of the Ranelva river where it flows into Ranfjorden. The area covers 279 dekar, of which 244 dekar is water. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area.

skeilia-naturreservat-nat3d4197d6.d: Skeilia Nature Reserve is situated in Alstahaug municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located near the Skei farm on the island of Alsten. The area covers 396 dekar and has been designated a nature reserve to safeguard one of the most floristically rich and interesting woodland areas on the Helgeland coast, and one of the most valuable stands of broad-leaved deciduous forest in Nordland.

kvannlia-s-lvjodalen-naturreservat-nat4c.d: The Kvannlia-Sølvjodalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rana municipality in Nordland. The reserve lies entirely within the catchment area of the Helgåga river and covers a total of 5,696 dekar. The area was designated a nature reserve by royal decree on 4 December 1992 to preserve two of the north-westernmost spruce stands in Europe. The area lies to the east of Lake Helgåvatnet, approximately 3 km north of Nordsjona. Sølvjodalen is the innermost part of the reserve and is difficult to access, whilst Kvannlia is far more accessible via a tractor track from the Øvre Helgå farm. Sølvjodalen is the north-westernmost occurrence of natural spruce forest in Europe, but is otherwise characterised by a poor flora.

ytre-klungset-naturreservat-nat757d8e13.d: The Ytre Klungset Nature Reserve is situated at Ytre Klungset in Fauske municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 85 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a section of woodland characterised by great diversity and lush vegetation, as well as the presence of yellow bedstraw and spring vetch.

sundsbukta-naturreservat-nate42f1748.d: Sundsbukta Nature Reserve is situated south of Hemnesberget in Hemnes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 151 dekar, of which 136 dekar is water. The area has been protected to safeguard what is perhaps Nordland’s most interesting brackish-water intertidal zone, and one of the most valuable individual sites in the fjord areas south of Saltfjellet.

solhaug-naturreservat-nat79705b66.d: Solhaug Nature Reserve is situated in the Dunderlandsdalen valley in the municipality of Rana in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 356 dekar and has been designated to preserve the most compact pine forest in the easternmost part of the valley, up towards Saltfjellet.

fuglberg-ya-naut-ya-naturreservat-nat9ae.d: The Fuglbergøya/Nautøya Nature Reserve is situated in Vågan municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises the two small islands of Fuglbergøya and Nautøya, just south-east of Skrova. The area covers 524 dekar, of which 239 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding and rearing ground for great skuas.

amundsgjerdlia-naturreservat-nate1352a65.d: Amundsgjerdlia Nature Reserve is situated near the Amundsgjerdet farm in Sømna municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve covers 83 dekar. The area is protected to safeguard a particular type of elm. Other trees and shrubs growing here include aspen, hazel, birch and European whitebeam. There is also a rich variety of herbaceous flora, including the common spleenwort, spring snowflake, finger sedge, bog bilberry, wood violet, hairy St John’s wort, wood anemone, wood vetch, spring snowflake, wreath mint and sweet woodruff. Amundgjerdsfjellet is the world’s northernmost location for the lesser pasque flower. The Amundsgjerdlia Nature Reserve is situated right next to the Gjerdevatnet Nature Reserve.

eidemsliene-naturreservat-nat712ecbc6.d: The Eidemsliene Nature Reserve is situated in Vega municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located near Eidem on the island of Vega and covers an area of 2,920 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to safeguard a natural and phytogeographical area that is unique in Nordland. The pine forest in the area is considered to be of great conservation value and was proposed for protection by Helgeland Skogselskap as early as 1911.

storvatnet-naturreservat-natd843916e.d: Storvatnet Nature Reserve is situated in the east of Steigen municipality in Nordland, approximately 5 km south-east of the hamlet of Store Straumfjorden. The nature reserve encompasses land areas around the central and northern parts of the nine-kilometre-long lake Storvatnet; to the west, it extends approximately one kilometre from the lake up Sagdalstindan. To the north, it extends approximately 1.5 km up Malåskardet, and north-eastwards towards the border with Hamarøy. To the east, it includes the summit of Stordalstinden, Stordalen, southwards to Storvikodden, around Storvika halfway to Rypvikodden, and southwards towards Storvikvatnan. The difference in altitude ranges from 56 metres above sea level at the water’s edge to 1,065 metres above sea level (Stordalstinden).

veggen-naturreservat-nat5186a911.d: Veggen Nature Reserve is situated in the south-east of Evenes municipality in Nordland, between the hamlets of Forra and Veggen. The nature reserve comprises a strip of land approximately 4.7 kilometres long along the Herjangen river, stretching from Sølvsteinvika, around Gammelveggen, towards Segelnes. The area extends about 100 to 250 metres up the slope of Veggfjellet, and has an elevation difference of approximately 200 metres. Of the area’s total 917 dekar, 906 daa consists of deciduous woodland, mainly grey alder and hawthorn, which in many places also overhangs the sea. A number of plant species grow scattered throughout the hillside, some of which are thermophilic species considered to be of Central European origin.

norddalen-naturreservat-nata851fdd7.d: Norddalen Nature Reserve is situated in the south-east of Narvik municipality in Nordland, approximately 14 km south-east of Elvegården, in a northern branch of Skjomdalen, or between Lossitinden to the north and Tverrfjellet and Durmålstinden to the south. The protected area extends from Nordelvkorset in the west, and approximately 4.5 km eastwards along the Nordelva river, approximately 700–800 metres north of the river and approximately 300–400 metres south of it. The nature reserve covers a total area of 4,789 dekar. Preserving the natural environment within the nature reserve is important for Sámi culture and economic activities. The area is to be available for reindeer herding.

salvatnet-naturreservat-nata76e1c73.d: Salvatnet Nature Reserve is situated on Nord-Herøy in Herøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 230 dekar, of which 145 dekar is land and 85 dekar is freshwater. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a productive wetland area of great regional conservation value and to protect the associated birdlife, particularly given the area’s great importance as a migration and breeding ground for wetland birds with specific habitat requirements.

seinesodden-naturreservat-nat46b103e3.d: Seinesodden Nature Reserve is situated in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located by the river Seines on the island of Straumøya. The area covers 580 dekar, of which 190 dekar is land. The area is protected to preserve a rich wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife, particularly in view of the area’s rich birdlife and the vulnerable salt marsh vegetation.

kjellerhaugvatnet-naturreservat-nat8a7e2.d: The Kjellerhaugvatnet Nature Reserve is situated on Vega in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,955 dekar, of which 1,610 dekar is land. The area has been protected to preserve a key part of a larger wetland complex of international conservation importance. The nature reserve was established on 19 December 1997.

votnmyra-naturreservat-natd4256260.d: Votnmyra Nature Reserve is situated on the border between the municipalities of Bindal and Brønnøy in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 600 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a wetland area in its natural state, together with its associated flora and fauna, particularly in view of the rich and varied types of bogs found there.

engelv-r-naturreservat-nat1c1a4cd1.d: Engelvær Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Steigen. It consists of just over 100 inner islands, situated close to the coast of Steigen. The islands are home to a large bird population and several rare species, such as the Eurasian golden plover, the goosander and the little auk. There are also large populations of, amongst others, the grey gull, black-backed gull, common gull, terns, oystercatcher and eider. The nature reserve covers an area of 16,829 dekar, of which 15,318 dekar is marine area.

skardmodalen-naturreservat-nat67b5305a.d: Skardmodalen Nature Reserve is situated on the southern side of Skardmodalen in Hattfjelldal municipality in Nordland, east of Lake Unkervatnet and extending up to the border with Sweden. The nature reserve covers an area of 9,643 dekar and has been designated to preserve a highly valuable, largely undisturbed continental coniferous forest area containing rare species and forest types. On the Swedish side, there is an adjacent nature reserve with the corresponding name: Skalmodals Nature Reserve.

herringbotn-naturreservat-nat7967598b.d: Herringbotn Nature Reserve is situated in Herringbotn in Vefsn municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,956 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a distinctive and varied landscape and an interesting wetland area with its associated flora, fauna and birdlife.

fiskvagflaget-naturreservat-nat0e41b17e.d: The Fiskvågflåget Nature Reserve is situated in Saltdal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve consists of a steep mountain slope just west of Rognan and covers an area of 1,025 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a rich limestone pine forest. The Fiskvågflåget Nature Reserve is situated right next to the Fiskvågvatnet Nature Reserve.

verengmoen-naturreservat-natb216f515.d: The Øverengmoen Nature Reserve is situated east of Røssåga, between Korgen and Bjerka in Hemnes municipality, Nordland. Øverengmoen is a relatively large rainforest site, home to one of the last major intact ravine systems with old-growth spruce forest in Norway.

dillern-rnes-naturreservat-nat170c5593.d: The Dillern-Ørnes Nature Reserve is situated in a south-facing valley between the farms of Dillra and Saura, in the south-west of Handnesøya in Nesna municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve covers a total area of 445 dekar, of which 421 dekar consists of deciduous and coniferous woodland. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve one of Norway’s largest and northernmost populations of hazel. It is the northernmost known location where the herb wood anemone occurs, and one of the northernmost occurrences of spring snowflake. The flora also includes grey alder, willow, aspen, rowan, elm, spruce and Sitka spruce.

storveltlia-valmasen-naturreservat-natb2.d: Storveltlia Nature Reserve is situated between Brenna and Unkervatnet in Hattfjelldal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 321 dekar. The area is protected to preserve the largest red-flanged/reindeer rose limestone forest south of Saltfjellet.

b-rsvatnet-naturreservat-nat06050ef2.d: The Børsvatnet Nature Reserve is situated in Narvik municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises the hillside on the north-eastern side of Lake Børsvatnet within Ørntuvneset. The area covers 4,129 dekar. It has been designated a nature reserve to preserve an area of undisturbed and highly productive grey alder and birch forest with tall herbs and large ferns.

kvikkleir-yran-landskapsvernomrade-nat80.d: The Kvikkleirøyran Landscape Conservation Area is situated east of Herøyholmen in Herøy municipality in Nordland. The landscape conservation area is designated for the protection of plant life, as it is a coastal landscape with varied seashore vegetation. The area was established in 2002 and covers 2.7 km² of land, of which 1.2 km² is sea area.

reppen-naturreservat-nat38859e3c.d: Reppen Nature Reserve is situated in Bindal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve lies on the north side of Reppsundet in Bindalsfjorden. The area covers 213 dekar. It has been designated a nature reserve to protect the core population of the Nordland aspen, a tree species unique to Bindal and found worldwide only in a few locations along Tosenfjorden, as well as to preserve the area’s deciduous broadleaf forest.

sandv-ret-landskapsvernomrade-natc782c8d.d: The Sandværet Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Lurøy municipality in Nordland. The landscape conservation area is designated for the protection of plant life, as it is a coastal landscape with varied seashore vegetation and rich limestone outcrops. The area was established in 2002 and covers 6.8 km², of which 5.9 km² is marine area.

skarfjellet-naturreservat-nat2a99ab5e.d: Skårfjellet Nature Reserve is situated south-east of Vennesund in Sømna municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 410 dekar and has been designated to safeguard a varied and species-rich woodland area, featuring significant stands of elm, hazel and rowan.

blindkj-len-naturreservat-nat7254304a.d: Blindkjølen Nature Reserve is situated in Åbygda in the municipality of Bindal in Nordland. The nature reserve covers 3,816 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve an area with a wide variety of vegetation types.

lovunda-lundeura-naturreservat-natacb129.d: Lovunda/Lundeura Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site on the island of Lovund in Lurøy municipality in Nordland. The reserve was established to ‘preserve a special breeding area for seabirds (a puffin colony), together with the naturally associated flora and fauna.’ Lovunda is a steep island, with its highest point at 623 metres above sea level. The protected area also includes the small island of Alkøya, just west of Lovund. The area covers 1,533 daa, of which 350 daa is marine area. The greatest value of this area lies in the puffin (Fratercula arctica) breeding colony at Lundeura. In 1979, this colony was estimated to number around 40,000 pairs.

alterhaug-naturreservat-natd66b2d5f.d: Alterhaug Nature Reserve is situated near the Alterhaug farm in Rana municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 14.5 dekar. The area has been protected to preserve a dense stand of elm trees and a lush mixed woodland with a rich variety of herbs and fungi.

kvannskogen-naturreservat-nate19bbcb9.d: The Kvannskogen Nature Reserve is situated in Hamarøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is a small area of 705 dekar between Lake Kvannvatnet to the north and Lake Varpvatnet to the south, approximately 1.2 kilometres north-west of the Drag junction. The short Kvannelva river flows between the lakes; it forms the eastern boundary of the reserve and is also one of the boundary rivers between Hamarøy and Tysfjord. From the river, the area extends 360–770 metres westwards towards Kvannåsen and the power lines. Approximately 190 metres of the E6 route runs through the nature reserve in the far north. 82.3 per cent of the area is deciduous forest, 4.8 per cent is coniferous and mixed forest, 9.6 per cent is marshland and 2.7 per cent consists of water.

ramnholmen-naturreservat-nat836e45e3.d: Ramnholmen Nature Reserve consists of a small islet off the coast of Vestfjorden, approximately one and a half kilometres south-west of Tysnes (Diksná) in Hamarøy, Nordland. The nature reserve covers a total area of 54 dekar, of which 17 daa is exposed rock and 37 daa is water. The islet is at most eight metres high and is covered with grass and a rich variety of herbaceous plants, which is thought to be the result of bird droppings. It is an important breeding area for the grey gull, the black-headed gull and the eider, but there are also populations of the black-backed gull, the kittiwake, terns and the oystercatcher. The purpose of the conservation order is to safeguard an important and undisturbed breeding and rearing area for seabirds. Ramnholmen falls under the jurisdiction of the Norwegian Nature Inspectorate’s local office in Fauske.

tiltvika-naturreservat-nat189c95e6.d: Tiltvika Nature Reserve is situated in the very north of Hamarøy in Nordland, 2.5 kilometres north-east of Storjord. Tiltvika features a highly varied sandy area with landforms that may be unique to this region and a range of species that is not entirely representative of sandy beaches. The nature reserve is an important Quaternary geological site: there are deposits on both sides of the bay and up the relatively steep mountainside to the east. In the southern part of the area, two lateral moraines lie side by side. The terminal moraine lies below sea level but can be seen as a shoal off Tiltvika. The southernmost lateral moraine is the most prominent and rises to around 300 metres above sea level.

straum-ya-naturreservat-natf9c102bc.d: Straumøya Nature Reserve is situated between Seivåg and Seines on the island of Straumøya in Bodø municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 4,470 dekar, of which 3,890 dekar is land and 580 dekar is water. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve an important wetland area of great regional conservation value, particularly due to its ornithological, bog botanical and limnological significance, and its role as a migration and breeding ground for birds.

holandsosen-naturreservat-nat86ee865c.d: The Holandsosen Nature Reserve is situated at Holand on Vega in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 2,502 dekar, of which 1,700 dekar is land, 90 dekar is freshwater and 710 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect a key part of a larger wetland complex of international conservation importance, particularly due to the area’s great significance for wetland birds throughout the year.

holmholmen-naturreservat-nata31955c7.d: Holmholmen Nature Reserve is situated on Holmholmen in Hemnes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises Holmen and the shallow waters between the islet and the mainland (Hemnesøya) to the south. The area covers 189 dekar, of which 165 dekar is water. The area is protected to safeguard one of the largest and densest eider duck colonies currently found in Nordland. This site, situated within the fjord, is an exception to the rule that the largest eider duck breeding grounds are usually found out on the coast.

lj-nes-ya-naturreservat-natef6892ae.d: Ljønesøya Nature Reserve is situated in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses Ljønesøya in Skjerstadfjorden and the surrounding seabed. The area covers 3,524 dekar, of which 3,037 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard the most important breeding site for eider ducks in Skjerstadfjorden.

fauskeeidet-naturreservat-nat1727ab24.d: Fauskeeidet Nature Reserve is situated at Fauskeeidet in Fauske municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 3,500 dekar, of which 2,000 dekar is water. The area is protected to preserve a productive and species-rich wetland area and a beautiful landscape.

andas-naturreservat-nat7cab9e3f.d: Andås Nature Reserve is situated on the Andås farm, just outside Mosjøen in Nordland. The nature reserve covers 54.8 dekar. The area has been designated a protected area to safeguard a representative grey alder forest.

tverlandet-naturreservat-nat546135f8.d: The Tverlandet Nature Reserve is situated between Ilstad and Godøynes on Tverlandet in Bodø municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,047 dekar, of which 611 dekar is marine area. The area has been protected to preserve a valuable coastal area, with its naturally associated flora and fauna.

sj-forsen-naturreservat-nata783bc46.d: Sjøforsen Nature Reserve is situated in Hemnes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located on the east bank of the River Røssåga near Korgen. The area covers 1,151 dekar and has been designated a nature reserve to preserve and protect an area of boreal rainforest, with all its species and ecological processes.

hammarnesflaget-naturreservat-natbb3b11e.d: Hammarnesflåget Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern shore of Langvatnet in Rana municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 548 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to safeguard one of the largest and botanically richest elm populations in inner Helgeland.

sterdalen-landskapsvernomrade-nat5e7cc45.d: The Østerdalen Landscape Conservation Area is situated in the municipalities of Bodø and Saltdal in Nordland. The landscape conservation area is protected for its flora, as it is a beautiful landscape with interesting zoology, geology and wildlife. The area was established in 1983 and covers 25.5 km².

b-rvatnet-naturreservat-natb8534dfd.d: The Børvatnet Nature Reserve is situated by Lake Børvatnet in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers 588 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect the second-largest known population of marsh marigold in Norway.

steinosen-sj-myrpollen-naturreservat-nat.d: The Steinosen/Sjømyrpollen Nature Reserve is situated on Nordneset, south/south-east of Tranøy and west of Sommersel, in Hamarøy in Nordland. The nature reserve covers a total area of 1,342 dekar and comprises Steinosen, the two branches of Sjømyrpollen, a few small islets and a relatively narrow strip of land around the headlands. Steinosen is a narrow wedge between Osen and Sjømyrpollen, bounded by low granite ridges to the north and south. In the innermost part, there is a continuous salt marsh with brackish-water vegetation (including, amongst other things, eelgrass and sea arrowgrass) which transitions to more saline conditions further out into the bay. Sjømyrpollen is divided into a south-western and a south-eastern part, which is almost completely cut off at the mouth of Steinsosøya.

gjerdevatnet-naturreservat-nat09989505.d: Gjerdevatnet Nature Reserve is situated at Ånnvika in Sømna municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises Lake Gjerdvatnet (25 metres above sea level) and the areas surrounding the lake. The nature reserve covers an area of 195 dekar, of which 60 dekar is water. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area. Gjerdevatnet Nature Reserve is situated right next to Amundsgjerdlia Nature Reserve.

veikdalen-naturreservat-natccbf2136.d: Veikdalen Nature Reserve is situated between Øvre and Nedre Veikvatnet in Sørfold municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 3,250 dekar. The area is protected to preserve an isolated and largely undisturbed pine forest, with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes.
