The palsmyren bogs are vulnerable to trampling, but the area is nevertheless not considered to be under threat.

grakletten-naturresevat-natfa8956ab.d: Gråkletten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Stor-Elvdal municipality. It comprises an area between the River Glomma and the southern end of Lake Storsjøen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a large and contiguous area of natural forest dominated by various types of spruce forest. The area is of great importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for a number of vulnerable and rare species of fungi and lichens. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to further develop them.”

skottvatnet-naturreservat-natd4b53b82.d: Skottvatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sel municipality. It consists of a lake and surrounding wetland area in the Gudbrans Valley, north of Otta. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. Camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography are prohibited. From 15 April to 30 June inclusive, all access to the reserve is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to migratory, breeding and moulting waterbirds and a rich and interesting variety of vegetation and flora.’

hjerkinnholen-naturreservat-natcfea5d3d.d: Hjerkinnholen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Dovre municipality, right on the border with Folldal municipality. It comprises an area on Hjerkinn. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a relatively undisturbed coniferous forest area near the tree line with interesting flora and fauna, particularly with a view to research and education.’

juvberget-naturreservat-nat4f39dfd9.d: Juvberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åsnes municipality. It comprises an area near the border with Sweden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 December 2015 and extended on 15 December 2017 from approximately 637 dekar to 879.0 dekar. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited, except on tractor tracks and paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area of rich, old low-herb spruce forest with elements of deciduous woodland and old mixed coniferous and deciduous forest, both of which are of particular importance for biodiversity as they contain demanding and rare species of vascular plants, fungi and lichens.

s-terasskaret-naturreservat-nat353aa5db.d: Sæteråsskaret Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Stor-Elvdal municipality. It comprises an area west of Koppang on the western bank of the Glomma. The area was first designated as a nature reserve on 20 December 2019 and extended on 24 June 2025. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic on land and water is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited except on tractor tracks marked on the conservation map and on footpaths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of old, high-altitude coniferous forest’.

j-vika-og-t-nnerud-naturreservat-nat424e.d: The Jøvika and Tønnerud Nature Reserve comprises an area by Randsfjorden in Gran municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of a relatively large and varied limestone forest site comprising limestone spruce forest, herb-rich limestone pine forest and patches of limestone heathland. Furthermore, the area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for many threatened fungal species and a rich flora of vascular plants, including orchids.’

nordre-dyttholknatten-naturreservat-nat5.d: Nordre Dyttholknatten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sør-Aurdal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 June 1985 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve typical high-altitude coniferous forest slopes that are of particular importance to wildlife.’

vesleaa-naturreservat-nataf57b735.d: The Vesleåa Nature Reserve comprises an area near Våja in Gran municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 March 2019 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of a well-developed and varied forest ravine with relatively large areas of old-growth forest. Furthermore, the aim is to protect an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it is a key habitat for rare and vulnerable species.’

odnesberga-naturreservat-natf95c0df2.d: Odnesberga Nature Reserve comprises an area near Odnes at the northern end of Randsfjorden in Søndre Land municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 14 February 2014 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a natural forest area comprising mainly calcareous and thermophilic forest types associated with southern slopes and scree slopes, which contain large populations of rare and vulnerable calcareous forest species and wood-dwelling fungi. Furthermore, the purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve an area of particular value for biodiversity in terms of habitat types, ecosystems, plant and animal species, and natural ecological processes.

svendstu-yene-naturreservat-nat12c5647e.d: Svendstuøyene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Stor-Elvdal municipality. It consists of a number of islands in the River Glomma near Opphus. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of flood-influenced woodland and open, scrub-covered riverbanks associated with alluvial islands in the course of the River Glomma. The area is also a habitat for rare and endangered species of plants, fungi and lichens. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

r-ykenvika-fuglefredningsomrade-nat35686.d: The Røykenvika Bird Sanctuary consists of a cove in Randsfjorden near Brandbu in Gran municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitat in the area, particularly with regard to migratory waterbirds.’

t-rasen-naturreservat-nat8aba06f5.d: Tøråsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Stor-Elvdal municipality on the border with Rendalen. It comprises an area between Storsjøen and the Glomma. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited, except on the path marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large natural area with a wide variety of coniferous forest types and occurrences of old-growth and primeval-style forest, with elements of rich fens, rich spruce swamp forest and tall-herb spruce forest. The area is of great importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for a number of rare and vulnerable species of fungi and lichens.

brenninga-naturreservat-nat51b232f5.d: Brenninga Nature Reserve is a forest and wetland area in Finnskogen, approximately 17 kilometres north-east of Flisa in Åsnes municipality. Half of the area lies within the middle boreal vegetation zone, whilst the other half lies within the southern boreal zone. The southern part of the area is dominated by damp spruce forest, whilst pine grows on the edges and on small islands in the marshland to the north. The area is of great importance for biodiversity, and a number of Red List species have been found here, including the bearded sedge, the spreading sedge and the wrinkled sedge. There are ditches to the east, left over from previous drainage of the marsh. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic is prohibited. Cycling and horse riding are also not permitted.

aurdals-terberga-naturreservat-natb1c9f9.d: The Aurdalsæterberga Nature Reserve comprises an area within the Vassfaret and Vidalen Landscape Conservation Area in the municipality of Sør-Aurdal. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 June 1985 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve typical high-altitude coniferous forest slopes that are of particular importance to wildlife.’

sandehorten-naturreservat-nat36fa9816.d: Sandehorten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vågå municipality. It is situated to the north of Lake Vågåvatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Open fires are prohibited, as is ‘camping’. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are only permitted on existing roads. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a distinctive calcareous pine forest for the purposes of research and education, and to safeguard special plant communities with extremely rare flora, whilst at the same time preserving a distinctive cultural landscape.’

volaberget-og-kvemskj-len-naturreservat-.d: The Volaberget and Kvemskjølen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Engerdal municipality. It comprises an area between the southern end of Lake Femunden and the border with Sweden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 2 September 2005. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a large and unique area of natural forest with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area’s special qualities include relatively large tracts of primeval pine forest, rich bog vegetation and areas with a high concentration of threatened and vulnerable species.

asjo-naturreservat-nat172447b6.d: Åsjo Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lom municipality. It comprises an area near Lom. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 October 1990. The reserve is part of the wetland conservation plan. Camping, pitching tents and setting up camouflaged hides for photography are prohibited. From 15 April to 30 June inclusive, all access to the reserve is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with vegetation, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, particularly with regard to breeding waterfowl.’

avrillen-naturreservat-nat86e9e720.d: Avrillen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gran municipality. The area was designated on 15 March 2019 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of a relatively large area dominated by biologically old and largely undisturbed forest, where there are patches in places characterised by primeval forest with good continuity of old trees. Furthermore, the purpose is to protect an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it is a vital habitat for rare, vulnerable and endangered species and because it strengthens the regional network of protected areas.”

hemberget-naturreservat-nata7d1f593.d: Hemberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Våler municipality. It comprises an area near the border with Sweden, north of Halsjøen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a large area of forest and marshland comprising old spruce forest and patches of rich deciduous woodland. The area is of great importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for rare and vulnerable species of fungi and lichens. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to enhance them.’ The highest point is Hemberget itself, 642 metres above sea level, at the westernmost end of the reserve.

einunndalsranden-naturreservat-nat76d0d7.d: Einunndalsranden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Folldal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 22 December 1989 and forms part of the conservation plan for Quaternary geology. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area of natural historical interest with a well-developed esker that forms an important part of a larger drainage system in the Einunndalen valley.’

breie-naturreservat-nat12cf2228.d: Breie Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Etnedal and Nord-Aurdal. It comprises an area north of Bagn. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017 and extended on 20 June 2023 from approximately 2,650 dekar to approximately 2,953 dekar. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited except on existing tractor tracks marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a relatively large forested area with good ecological diversity, rich forest types, other rich natural habitats and nutrient-demanding vegetation types, as well as old, coarse-grained spruce forest with hanging lichen and other rare species.

lille-s-lensj-naturreservat-nat30b0dcde.d: Lille Sølensjø Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rendalen municipality. It comprises an area north of Lake Sølensjøen. The current area was designated on 21 June 2017, as an amendment to the reserve that was designated on 18 December 1981. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited, except on paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of distinctive landscape features, wetland areas with a rich bird life, and old spruce and pine forests that are of particular importance for biodiversity.’

bj-nnhaugen-naturreservat-nat1fcc81f3.d: Bjønnhaugen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Gjøvik and Nordre Land. The area was designated a protected area on 15 December 2017 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area with a specific type of natural environment in the form of old spruce forest, which, amongst other things, contains rich populations of the endangered species Huldrestry. Furthermore, the area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it contains a fair amount of dead wood and old trees, and serves as a habitat for endangered lichen and fungus species, as well as examples of the habitat types ‘rich fen’ and ‘rich swamp forest’.”

valetjern-naturreservat-nat59dc7caf.d: Våletjern Nature Reserve lies 220 metres above sea level, about two kilometres south-east of Stange station. The reserve consists of a naturally nutrient-rich pond, the surrounding forest edge and part of the marshland to the north-west. The pond has wide belts of common reed and bulrush, and is home to several species of duck, divers and waders. The pond also serves to some extent as a stopover site, and the area is considered to be of particular national conservation value. The aim of the conservation is to prevent the pond from becoming overgrown and to protect a bog complex of great pollen-analytical interest. All wildlife is protected against any damage and unnecessary disturbance. The same applies to all vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees.

kattugleh-i-naturreservat-nat2cf968e6.d: The Kattuglehøi Nature Reserve consists of a bog area right next to Kattuglehøe. The nature reserve is situated in Dovre municipality. It was designated a protected area on 18 January 1985 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The reserve is situated within Dovre National Park. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a rich, high-altitude mountain bog/pals bog with intact and beautifully formed pals.’

oddelia-naturreservat-natc787a250.d: Oddelia Nature Reserve is situated on the west bank of the Dokkaelva river at Åmodt in Nord-Torpa, in the municipality of Nordre Land. The reserve was established on 25 January 2013 and covered 894 daa at that time. On 12 December 2014, the King in Council decided to extend the nature reserve by approximately 170 mål. Following the expansion, the area covers 1,063 daa. It consists of steep slopes descending towards the river. A small north-west-facing ravine (Djupbekken), on the east bank of the river, is also included within the protected area. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a relatively large stream gorge with a high proportion of rich forest types and significant populations of threatened species. The area has abundant populations of the red-listed species thread-leaved sundew, which is rare outside the Namdalen/Helgeland region.

nordre-brynsaa-naturreservat-nat050d47a7.d: Nordre Brynsåa Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Øyer municipality which was granted protected forest area status in 2013. The Government decided to grant the area protected status on the following grounds: ‘Nordre Brynsåa Nature Reserve in Øyer municipality, Oppland county, is an important ravine, a type of woodland for which Norway has an international responsibility. It is home to, amongst other things, rare forest types such as boreal rainforest, tall-shrub forest and rich low-herb forest, as well as a species-rich and lush flora of vascular plants, including the ‘huldre plant’, the wood sorrel.”

trya-naturreservat-nat1d7c436e.d: Trya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Stor-Elvdal municipality. It comprises an area near Koppang along the Trya river on the west bank of the Glomma. The area was first designated as a nature reserve on 20 December 2019 and extended on 24 June 2025. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic on land and water is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited, except on existing paths and tractor tracks marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of damp deciduous and coniferous woodland and a stream gorge environment with a waterfall spray zone’.

vistehorten-naturreservat-nat4e476e0b.d: Vistehorten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vågå municipality. It is situated to the north of Lake Vågåvatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Open fires are prohibited, as is ‘camping and similar activities’. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are only permitted on existing roads. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a distinctive calcareous pine forest for the purposes of research and education, and to safeguard special vegetation communities with extremely rare plant life, whilst at the same time preserving a distinctive cultural landscape.’

budeiberget-naturreservat-natea70b0f0.d: The Budeiberget Nature Reserve is situated in Østsinni in Nordre Land, in the Innlandet region. The area is a coniferous forest reserve covering 1,004 dekar, and lies just south of the boundary with the former municipality of Torpa. The reserve was designated on 15 December 2017. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a natural forest area consisting mainly of old, damp spruce forest. Furthermore, the area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it provides habitats for several threatened species and contains one of the richest known populations of hollow-stemmed birch in Oppland. The nature reserve is well suited to enhancing its conservation value through undisturbed development.

lind-ya-naturreservat-nat2800223e.d: Lindøya Nature Reserve covers the central and northern parts of Lindøya in Oslo. The nature reserve was established on 9 July 1993. Under the conservation plan for the Inner Oslo Fjord, the area was extended on 27 June 2008. The nature reserve now covers an area of approximately 95 dekar and encompasses most of the calcareous pine forest on the island. This is a rare habitat type that forms where there is limited water availability and a thin layer of topsoil over calcareous bedrock. Calcareous pine forest is important because it is home to many rare, threatened and vulnerable species. However, introduced species such as lilac and Russian milk-vetch have in places displaced the original vegetation. This poses a major threat to biodiversity.

nakkeskj-r-biotopvernomrade-nat742cceb2.d: The Nakkeskjær biotope conservation area comprises Nakkeskjæret at the southern tip of Nakkholmen in Oslo. At the time of the 2011 census, the skerry was home to the largest colony of common terns in the entire Oslofjord. The common tern is listed as Vulnerable (VU) on the Norwegian Red List, and the population has declined in the Oslo Fjord over the last 30 years. All birdlife is protected on the islet and 50 metres out to sea, and access to the area is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July.

furu-yene-biotopvernomrade-natd9639a16.d: The Furuøyene Biotope Conservation Area (approximately 15 daa, of which approximately 0.5 daa is land area) is situated off Skarvhella (near Tyristrand) in Tyrifjorden and was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Section 34 of the Act of 19 June 2009 No. 100 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 38 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The protected area is situated in Ringerike Municipality, Buskerud, and forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. It consists of a few small islets and skerries and a zone of approximately 50 metres around them. The biotope conservation area is intended to preserve an area of particular importance as an ecological functional area, serving as a breeding site for the common tern, the black-headed gull and the common gull.

nordre-sauholmen-fuglefredningsomrade-na.d: The Nordre Sauholmen Bird Sanctuary comprises the northern tip of Nordre Sauholmen and the sea area 50 metres offshore, at the entrance to Sonsbukta in Vestby municipality. The southern part of the islet is a state-protected outdoor recreation area. Species breeding on the islet include the common tern, the black-headed gull and the black-tailed gull, all of which are on Norway’s Red List, the latter classified as ‘critically endangered’ (CR). The birdlife in the reserve is protected against harm and unnecessary disturbance, and it is prohibited to carry out any activities that impair the birds’ habitat. All access is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving. Furthermore, dogs must always be kept on a lead.

langasen-naturreservat-nat83efd063.d: Langåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Flesberg and Rollag. It comprises an area north-east of Blefjell. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. It should not be confused with Langåsen Nature Reserve in Agder. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment, in that it largely consists of old-growth forest with occurrences of old natural forest and areas close to primeval forest, as well as old spruce forest of good quality and south-facing steep slopes with deciduous forest and a rich southern mountain flora.

dokkene-naturreservat-nata4650c43.d: Dokkene Nature Reserve is situated in Vestre Spone, west of the Snarumselva river in Modum municipality, Buskerud. The reserve was established in 2005 to protect one of the very few old ravine forests of any size in Eastern Norway.

kallakmosen-naturreservat-nat6a51e5ef.d: Kallakmosen Nature Reserve is a wetland area in the municipalities of Indre Østfold and Aurskog-Høland, which was designated a protected area in 1992 to safeguard a gently sloping rainwater bog with small patches of groundwater-fed bog. To the west, the reserve borders on agricultural land; the rest is surrounded by coniferous forest and bog. Several of the bird species associated with bogs are found here, and the area is an important breeding ground for such species. As of 1986, 21 species had been recorded in the area, 12 of which were breeding species. The bog forms part of a larger wetland bird system extending across extensive areas in both Østfold and Akershus. Kallakmosen was originally proposed for protection in the conservation plans for bogs in Østfold in 1977.

stakaskj-r-biotopvernomrade-natc72c6539.d: The Stakaskjær Biotope Conservation Area consists of a skerry off Furuholmen in Hallangspollen, in Frogn municipality, together with the surrounding sea area within a 50-metre radius. The skerry is an important breeding ground for seabirds. There used to be many breeding black-headed gulls here, but a census in 2011 found none. The black-headed gull is listed as ‘critically endangered’ (CR) in Norway. The birdlife in the reserve is protected against harm and unnecessary disturbance, and it is prohibited to carry out any activities that impair the birds’ habitat. All access is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving. Furthermore, dogs must always be kept on a lead.

vestre-risenh-gda-og-fuglemasan-naturres.d: The Vestre Risenhøgda and Fuglemosen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve covering a large forested area stretching from the western shore of Lake Store Risen in Marker municipality and across the municipal boundary towards Aurskog-Høland, where it also encompasses the former nature reserve at Vestre Fuglemosen. The bedrock consists mainly of various types of gneiss, resulting in relatively nutrient-poor soil. The vegetation is therefore predominantly sparse, but richer vegetation can be found in certain places, including north of Svartevika. The forest is generally old, dominated by spruce and pine interspersed with other boreal tree species such as birch, willow, aspen and rowan. The reserve also contains significant areas of rain-fed bogs, which lend the area a varied character.

sletner-naturreservat-natc2f71e43.d: Sletner Nature Reserve is situated in the municipality of Indre Østfold in Østfold, north-east of Eidsberg between the farms of Sletner and Garsegg and south of the railway line. The area covers 512 da and is characterised by deep ravines with a large, old spruce forest on high-quality soil, with individual trees as old as 128 years. The flora is characterised as very species-rich, with several rare species, including those on the Red List.

skipstadsand-naturreservat-nat423e4925.d: Skipstadstrand Nature Reserve is situated in a bay to the east of Asmaløy in Hvaler, surrounded by quays on the south side, a road to the west and north, and private jetties to the east. The area is quite small, but it is home to the habitat type ‘salt marsh, south-eastern variant’, which is critically endangered in Norway. The reserve is home to several Red Listed plants, including centaury, dwarf centaury, sea rocket and strawberry clover. It is also home to the honey flower, which is critically endangered and found in Norway at only two locations on Hvaler. Several Red Listed butterflies and other insects have also been recorded. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction, and it is forbidden to carry out any activities that alter the natural conditions.

hellvik-gamle-brygge-plantefredningsomra.d: The Hellvik Old Quay Plant Conservation Area forms a narrow strip along the coast just north of Hellvik Quay on the eastern side of Nesodden in Akershus. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect the extremely rare plant species white-flowered rock cress and its habitat. The species is listed as Critically Endangered (CR) on the 2010 Norwegian Red List of Species. The species has only been recorded at a few sites in the Oslofjord area. The population at Hellvik Old Quay, together with that on the Løkenes Peninsula in Asker, is probably one of the only viable populations of the species in Norway.

stensdalen-naturreservat-nate575c874.d: Stensdalen Nature Reserve consists of a narrow valley flanked on both sides by steep hills of Østfold granite. The reserve is situated at Papper, just north-east of Papperhavn, and forms a continuation of Sandbukta to the south-east. The valley floor ranges from 0 to 10 metres above sea level. The vegetation consists of black alder beach forest, with some birch, elm and wild pear. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a black alder coastal forest that has aesthetic and educational value. All vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees, is protected from destruction. However, picking berries and mushrooms is permitted.

lekum-naturreservat-natadd9165c.d: Lekum Nature Reserve is an area of broadleaf forest on the clay slopes where the Lekumelva river flows into the innermost part of Lekumevja, near the Glomma river in Indre Østfold municipality. The forest is dominated by grey alder down by the river, whilst there are more maple and elm trees to the north, and ash trees to the south. Such deciduous broadleaf woodland is rare in this region. To the west of the reserve, there is also an area of grey alder and hawthorn woodland.

ertsrudberget-naturreservat-nat61c239d2.d: Ertsrudberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the north of Nes municipality in Akershus and Sør-Odal in Innlandet. The area was designated a nature reserve in 2017 and covers 1,610 hectares. The bedrock consists mainly of granitic gneiss, whilst the surface deposits comprise moraine and some bog. The vegetation is dominated by blueberry spruce forest, with some patches of low-growing forest and poor bog vegetation. The area is of great importance as a habitat for, amongst other things, rare lichen and fungus species that depend on forests with long-term continuity.

regimentsmyra-naturreservat-nata6ddf913.d: Regimentsmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Fredrikstad municipality. It comprises an area near Gamlebyen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling and horse riding are prohibited, except on the footpaths and trails marked on the conservation map; however, cycle races and horse rides are permitted on existing footpaths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area of threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats, comprising varied deciduous woodland and oak, as well as spruce and pine forests, with their associated flora and fauna. The area represents a special habitat type in low-lying areas below the marine limit in south-eastern Norway.

hatterasen-naturreservat-nat904e78fb.d: Hatteråsen Nature Reserve is situated about six to seven kilometres east of Eidsvoll town centre in Akershus. The area mainly comprises the two hills, Hatteråsen and Tretjennshaugen, and is home to some of the oldest woodland in the region. In places, however, the area is still somewhat characterised by past logging, with some even-aged woodland. To the north, the woodland is more varied, with a greater proportion of wind-felled trees and deadwood. The area is home to the yellow parasitic lichen, which is on the Red List. The bedrock consists of primary rocks, with gabbro/amphibolite in the south-west and granitic gneiss/migmatite in the north-east.

fagermasan-naturreservat-nat7733e77b.d: Fagermosen Nature Reserve is a wetland area in Setskog, in the municipality of Aurskog-Høland, which was designated a protected area in 1981 to preserve a large, unspoilt rain-fed bog and an area of botanical interest. The nature reserve lies north of Lake Setten and comprises a large, contiguous bog area surrounded by coniferous-forested hills to the west and east. To the south and north, cultivated land lies close to the bog. Fagermosen is a rain-fed bog with several elevated areas, which are particularly well developed in the northern part. Small areas influenced by groundwater can be found in the edge zone. In the centre of the bog there is a larger marshy area with a lot of loose soil. To the east and west there are areas with lush edge vegetation.

hvitmasan-naturreservat-nat85ba2389.d: Hvitmåsan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve established in 1981. It is situated right next to Lake Sagstusjøen, south-east of Årnes in Nes municipality, Akershus. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect an eccentric raised bog, which, together with Sakkhusmåsan and Vindmyra, demonstrates the range of variation in such bogs in the district.

stor-ya-biotopvernomrade-nat92478e5c.d: The Storøya Biotope Conservation Area (approximately 29 daa, of which Storøya accounts for approximately 6 daa of land area) is situated north of Svangstrand in Holsfjorden (part of Tyrifjorden), right next to the two islands of Kavringen and Midtøya, and was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 38 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The protected area is situated in Lier municipality, Buskerud, and forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. It consists of a single island and a zone of approximately 50 metres around it. The biotope conservation area is intended to protect an area of particular importance as an ecological functional area, serving as a breeding site for the black-headed gull.

skand-la-naturreservat-natc319bdce.d: Skandøla Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hurdal municipality. It comprises an area along the River Skandøla. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling and horse riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of one of the last intact, moist and highly productive old-growth spruce forests in Hurdal municipality. Furthermore, the area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it is home to several threatened and demanding species that are specific to this type of forest, such as the rare lichen species Trådragg.”

prestebakkefjella-naturreservat-nat6bed2.d: Prestebakkefjella Nature Reserve is situated in Halden municipality, approximately 19 km south-east of Halden town and approximately 3 kilometres east of Prestebakke Church. Prestebakkemosen is Østfold’s largest contiguous area of marshland. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a forested area comprising several different habitat types. Prestebakkefjella consists of a mixture of coniferous forest, ponds, watercourses and bogs. The area was significantly expanded on 14 February 2014 by 2,422 dekar to a total of 6,893 dekar.

enghaugberget-naturreservat-natb84a0104.d: Enghaugberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Fredrikstad municipality. It comprises an area near Slevik. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horses and carts, and horse riding off existing paths is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a calcareous pine forest containing a number of rare plant species’. Species growing here include comb-leaved saxifrage, fly orchid, bridal veil, red helleborine, broad-leaved helleborine, globe thistle and wood sorrel.

asebutjernet-biotopvernomrade-nat897366b.d: The Åsebutjernet biotope conservation area is situated to the west of Asmaløy in Hvaler. The pond is a habitat for, amongst others, the small salamander and four species of dragonfly. One of these is the southern metal-coloured damselfly (Lestes dryas), which is one of Norway’s rarest species. It breeds in very shallow, vegetation-rich small ponds and has been found in only a very few ponds in Norway. The biotope conservation area covers the smooth newt and the southern metal-coloured damselfly. The vegetation is protected against damage and destruction, and the two animal species covered by the biotope protection are protected against collection, damage, destruction and unnecessary disturbance. It is prohibited to carry out any measures that may affect or disturb the protected species or their living conditions.

raen-naturreservat-nat9507a777.d: Råen Nature Reserve was established on 19 June 1970. This deciduous forest area is situated in Øvre Eiker, in Buskerud County, alongside County Road 2754 between Darbu and Krekling. The reserve covers an area of approximately 15 dekar and has been designated to preserve a stand of elm and lime forest, which also forms a beautiful feature of the landscape.

t-rrhalasen-naturreservat-natdfe3326c.d: Tørrhalåsen Nature Reserve is situated in the far north-east of Aurskog-Høland municipality, on the ridge between Bjørknessjøen/Viksjøen and Havsjøen. The woodland areas in this region have been significantly affected by long-term active forestry. Areas where the forest has developed naturally over time without logging are rare, but at Tørrhalåsen there is a large area of older, naturally regenerated forest. In places, old-growth forest qualities can be found, and a few indicator species have been recorded, as well as some species listed as ‘near threatened’ (NT) on the Red List. Nevertheless, it will still take a long time before the forest here reaches its climax stage. The area is dominated by nutrient-poor vegetation types such as pine bog woodland and blueberry woodland, but contains patches of richer vegetation with birch and aspen.

brattasen-naturreservat-nat4fe3aa01.d: Brattåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated north of Lake Kløsa, in the south-east of Rakkestad municipality. The reserve mainly covers the south-western slope of Brattåsen and, as the name suggests, it is relatively steep. There are some rock faces and boulder fields here, but also gentler slopes with loose material. The bedrock consists of gabbro, amphibolite and quartz diorite. These are basic rocks that provide the basis for nutrient-rich soil and abundant vegetation, in contrast to most of the district, which is dominated by gneiss. The vegetation consists of varied forms of mixed woodland, with elements of willow, rowan, birch and plenty of aspen, as well as spruce and pine. There are also occurrences of the thermophilic species hazel, pedunculate oak and lime.

tj-st-l-naturreservat-nat934da166.d: Tjøstøl Nature Reserve is situated on the western side of Store Le, in the far north-east of Aremark municipality. The bedrock consists of granitic gneiss and hornblende gneiss with amphibolite. This weatherises easily and provides favourable soil conditions. The area is largely unspoilt and contains some of the finest, most diverse coniferous forests remaining in the lowlands of Eastern Norway. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve the rich coniferous forest with its diversity of species, ecosystems and ecological processes.

raknerud-og-gimmingsrud-naturreservat-na.d: The Raknerud and Gimmingsrud Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the eastern side of Lake Øyeren, near its southern end, in the municipality of Indre Østfold. The reserve lies on a thick layer of marine clay, which provides nutrient-rich soil. The area lies 100–160 metres above sea level, and the topography is characterised by ravine valleys 15–40 metres deep. This is a vulnerable and threatened habitat type. The vegetation is dominated by deciduous broad-leaved forest and rich mixed woodland. The area is important for rare species associated with dead wood, of which there is a great deal in places. Of particular note are the Red Listed hazel polypore and elm polypore. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but ordinary hunting is permitted, as is the gathering of berries and edible mushrooms.

fyrsteilene-plantefredningsomrade-natcf5.d: The Fyrsteilene Plant Conservation Area encompasses one of the islands in the Steilene archipelago in Nesodden municipality. The island was designated a conservation area in 2008 to preserve rare plant species and their habitats. Calcareous grasslands and rock-cress communities are the dominant plant communities. A survey carried out in 2002 identified 81 species, several of which are rare. Among others, honey cress, deer’s-tongue and spiked speedwell were found; the latter is listed as critically endangered on the Red List. The site is of great educational value.

gansr-d-naturreservat-nat5e8e9f52.d: Gransrød Nature Reserve is situated on the south side of County Road 107 in Fredrikstad municipality, right next to Regimentsmyra Nature Reserve and Søndre Haugstenåsen Nature Reserve. The conservation values are linked to the vegetation, which comprises several types. In part, there is low-herb oak woodland with patches of hazel thickets. In higher areas with less loose soil, there is pine forest, and in some areas there is mixed forest with boreal deciduous trees such as birch and aspen. The forest shows signs of past felling and management, with little deadwood in places. Nevertheless, there are many rare species of fungi in the reserve, such as the red-listed golden-tube fungus. It is believed that the conservation value of the area will increase over time.

stavlum-naturreservat-nat29e67eef.d: Stavlum Nature Reserve was established on 19 June 1970. The deciduous broad-leaved forest area is situated in Øvre Eiker, in Buskerud County, by County Road 2754 between Darbu and Krekling. The reserve covers an area of approximately 17 dekar and has been designated to preserve a stand of elm and lime forest, which also forms a beautiful feature of the landscape.

kisselbergmosen-naturreservat-nat2753e0b.d: The Kisselbergmosen Nature Reserve is situated just west of County Road 21, in the very north of Marker municipality. The area consists mainly of bogs, and its most significant conservation values lie in the varied hydrotopographical structure of the bogs: ombrotrophic bogs with minerotrophic areas at their edges.

fjellstulfjellet-naturreservat-natfdea38.d: The Fjellstulfjellet Nature Reserve is an area north of the main road between Kongsberg and Notodden, in Meheia. The reserve consists of a mountainous area surrounded by wooded slopes. The bedrock is granite, in many places exposed as bare rock. The topsoil is otherwise quite thin. The vegetation comprises both primeval-like mountain spruce forest and natural pine woodland with many old trees and plenty of deadwood. Several species of wood-dwelling fungi are found here, which are of great importance to biodiversity. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic and horse riding are prohibited.

svantjern-naturreservat-nat66cdc29e.d: Svantjern Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Halden municipality. It comprises an area to the west of Nordre Kornsjø. It borders Sweden to the south. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling and horse riding are prohibited except on the timber haulage routes indicated on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of mature pine-dominated forest, as well as a threatened type of natural environment on a burnt area with a large number of standing and fallen fire-damaged pine and birch trees, and which is of particular importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for specialised species.

juvsasen-naturreservat-natec6d6613.d: Juvsåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sigdal municipality. It comprises an area north of Prestfoss. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 December 2015 and extended on 15 December 2017 from approximately 2,655 dekar to 2,793.2 dekar. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of predominantly old-growth natural forest rich in deadwood and bearing clear traces of past forest fires. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity due to the large extent of highly productive, low-lying forest, the abundance of old trees and deadwood at various stages of decomposition, and the abundance of deciduous trees, particularly aspen.

kvernemyr-naturreservat-natb91122f2.d: Kvernemyr Nature Reserve is a bog surrounded by outcrops of bedrock, situated roughly in the centre of Asmaløy in Hvaler municipality. The bedrock consists of granite, which results in nutrient-poor soil, and the mire is therefore a nutrient-poor waterlogged mire dominated by mat-forming vegetation. There is an abundance of blue moor grass and bog myrtle here, and a particularly abundant occurrence of bog asphodel. This plant is coastal (sub-oceanic), but is nevertheless more common at higher altitudes and is therefore rare on the islands in the Oslo Fjord. Towards the north, the proportion of low-growing woodland increases. Here one finds birch, grey willow, wayfaring tree, aspen and pine; in the undergrowth, common species such as wood sorrel, blueberry, lingonberry, cloudberry and wood anemone are also present. The open bog area does not appear to be subject to significant encroachment by vegetation.

haugbergfjellet-naturreservat-nat8e26dc1.d: Haugbergfjellet Nature Reserve is situated in Halden municipality, approximately 21 km south-east of Halden town. Most of the area lies between 160 and 180 metres above sea level and consists of extensive bogs nestled amongst gentle pine-covered ridges. There are also some dense spruce forests, with almost no vascular plants growing on the moss-covered ground. A few rare plant species have been recorded in the reserve, such as beard lichen, as well as the wood-dwelling fungus Antrodiella pallasii, which has not been found elsewhere in Østfold. There is a diverse range of birdlife in the area, including more unusual species such as the three-toed woodpecker, the beech warbler, the hazel grouse, the curlew and the crane. The aim of the conservation measure is to preserve an area comprising mainly nutrient-poor forest types on bedrock above the marine limit in south-eastern Norway.

stiksasen-naturreservat-nat50dcba4a.d: Stiksåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the eastern shore of Lake Stiksvannet, in the very south of Rakkestad municipality. The reserve comprises two ridges and the valley between them. The bedrock consists mainly of gneiss, which results in relatively nutrient-poor soil. The area lies at an altitude of 125–209 metres above sea level and features poor to moderately rich forest types near the maritime forest boundary. Where the soil is shallow, and in damp areas near bogs, pine dominates. Where the soil is deeper and more nutrient-rich, there is more spruce. Furthermore, birch is found throughout the area, and on south-facing slopes there are also some thermophilic species such as oak and hazel. The forest is relatively old, but there is little dead wood and few Red List species have been found.

grenimasan-naturreservat-natf5e437c5.d: Grenimåsan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve that was established in 2007. It is situated north-west of Vormsund in Nes municipality in Akershus, on the border with Ullensaker. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve one of the finest remaining concentric raised bogs in the country.

samsj-berga-naturreservat-natf03c8079.d: Samsjøberga Nature Reserve is situated in the far north-west of Jevnaker municipality, on the ridge between Randsfjorden and Ådalen. The bedrock consists of gneiss, which results in acidic soil. The vegetation is predominantly sparse, but there are also some areas with somewhat richer vegetation. In hollows and damp areas, there are blueberry spruce forests and swamp spruce forests, whilst on ridges and in dry areas, pine is the dominant species. There is a great deal of old-growth forest in the area, and pine trees up to 380 years old have been recorded. All the oldest pine trees have survived a previous forest fire, as they all bear fire scars. It is believed that the fire took place around 200 years ago.

lerdalen-naturreservat-nat90c8edd3.d: Lerdalen Nature Reserve is situated in a rift valley to the west of County Road 108, in the north of Vesterøy in Hvaler municipality. The bedrock consists of granite, which results in poor soil, but down in the valley there are marine, clay-rich sediments that provide much more nutrient-rich soil. The vegetation in the valley, with its lush spruce forest, therefore stands out markedly from the surrounding hills with their poorer pine forest. The vegetation types lie almost as parallel bands, ranging from the lushest large-fern spruce forest down by the stream, through low-herb spruce forest, blueberry spruce forest, a mixed forest of heather and conifers, to low-growing pine forest at the top. At the bottom by the lake, there is a black alder riparian forest and a small salt marsh containing, amongst other things, dwarf goldenrod. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve: ‘a.

gravningen-naturreservat-nat5187c9a5.d: The Gravningen Nature Reserve is situated on the southern side of Storskausberg, in the west of Asmaløy in Hvaler municipality. The reserve covers a relatively small area, but nevertheless encompasses Hvaler’s largest oak forest. The forest is a low-herb oak forest with some lime and hazel, and stands on boulder-strewn terrain formed from a pebble beach dating from the time when the sea level was 10–20 metres higher following the last ice age. The forest boasts a high diversity of plant species and an exceptionally rich butterfly fauna, with over 800 recorded species, 72 of which are on the Norwegian Red List. In the long term, the forest also has great potential for beetles worthy of conservation that are associated with old trees and dead wood. The golden oriole, a bird species that is rare in Norway, has also been observed at the site.

flaen-naturreservat-natda674fdf.d: Flaen Nature Reserve is situated at Asak, east of Leira, in a fairly central part of Lillestrøm municipality. The area lies in the upper part of a ravine system leading up to the marine boundary. The ground consists mainly of marine deposits, but with some glacial river deposits at the edges. There are several ravine valleys characterised by springs, and the vegetation is dominated by a wide variety of spring forest species. The area also has a rich bird life. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but hunting is permitted in accordance with other legislation. It is also permitted to gather edible mushrooms and berries, but lighting fires is prohibited.

sakkhusmasan-naturreservat-natb09dba78.d: Sakkhusmåsan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the south-east of Nes municipality in Akershus. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect an unusual raised bog, which, together with Hvitmåsan and Vindmyra, demonstrates the range of variation in such bogs in the district.

hamrefjell-naturreservat-natd220100c.d: Hamrefjell Nature Reserve is a protected area covering 20 dekar in Øvre Eiker municipality, in Buskerud county. The reserve is situated on Hamrefjellet on the eastern side of Lake Eikeren. The nature reserve was established on 16 November 1984 and forms part of the Oslo Field. The protected area consists mainly of the rock type Ekerite, but also includes marble and hornfels where vesuvianite has crystallised within the marble. There are also significant local variations in the flora of the area; some areas are rich in species, whilst others are species-poor.

b-ensmosen-og-berbymosen-naturreservat-n.d: The Bøensmoen and Berbymosen Nature Reserve is a complex of mires on both sides of the River Storetjæra, on the northern shore of Lake Store Krokvann, in the north-east of Rakkestad municipality in Østfold. The mires contain both minerotrophic and ombrotrophic elements. The vegetation comprises western, eastern and coastal species. The area is also a breeding ground for species such as the green sandpiper and the meadow pipit.

nord-stre-askeskj-r-naturreservat-nat94a.d: Nordøstre Askeskjær is the easternmost of the Askholmene islets in the sound between Håøya and Hallangstangen in Frogn municipality. The highest point on the islet is 5.8 metres above sea level. The Askholmene lighthouse stands on its northern tip. The purpose of designating the Nordøstre Askeskjær Nature Reserve is to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites. In 2005, approximately 140 breeding pairs were recorded, of which 36 were eider ducks and 81 were lesser black-backed gulls. These are the largest colonies of these species in the Oslo and Akershus section of the fjord.

bleiken-naturreservat-nat9a57f97b.d: Bleiken Nature Reserve is situated in the far south-west of Rømskog in the municipality of Aurskog-Høland, on the ridge between Store Risen and Slavasshøgda. The area comprises marshes, ponds and islands on firm ground, and is important for wetland birds.

demmekilskj-ra-biotopvernomrade-natdc1db.d: The Demmekilskjæra Biotope Conservation Area is a biotope conservation area comprising three small skerries in the coastal zone at Høvik, between Båtstø and Ramton in Asker municipality, as well as the sea area 50 metres offshore. The skerries serve as a breeding ground for a number of seabirds. All access is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving.

sagasen-og-stueasen-naturreservat-natdb8.d: The Sagåsen and Stueåsen Nature Reserve is situated on the western shore of Lake Mingevannet, near Sætre in Sarpsborg municipality. The southern part was designated as the Sagåsen Nature Reserve in 2019. The following year, Stueåsen to the north was also designated, and the areas were linked by the intervening slope down towards Lake Mingevannet, east of Sætre Farm. The altitude ranges from 24 metres above sea level at Lake Mingevannet to just over 130 metres above sea level on the hills. The bedrock consists mainly of gneiss, partly covered by loose marine sediments. On the hills, there is a great deal of bare rock, with some moraine deposits in places.

sandungasen-naturreservat-nate8b9c3b7.d: Sandungåsen Nature Reserve is situated in the north of Hurumlandet in the municipality of Asker. The nature reserve was established on 14 February 2014 and extended by 897 dekar northwards towards Vardeåsen and Kringlefjell in Røyken on 14 December 2018. The reserve comprises a west-facing slope from Sandungåsen down towards the Drammensfjord, parts of Grauteruddalen to the east, and the south-eastern part of Vardeåsen and Kringlefjell. There is great ecological diversity, with a relatively large number of vegetation types having different requirements in terms of nutrients, moisture and topography. Moderately rich vegetation predominates, but there are also both barren hills and rich deciduous broad-leaved woodland.

braneasen-naturreservat-nat05ba0186.d: Bråneåsen Nature Reserve is situated on a hill in the far north-west of Sarpsborg municipality. The reserve is bordered to the east and west by forest tracks. The reserve comprises a remnant area of naturally regenerating spruce and pine forest, in an area that is otherwise heavily logged. The bedrock consists mainly of gneiss, covered only in places by sparse loose material. This results in poor nutrient conditions, and the vegetation is characterised by hardy heather species such as heather and blueberry. Deciduous trees are sparse, but there are some birch trees. Indicator species are also scarce, but old spruce lichen has been found. The forest is considered to have great potential for restoration to mature old-growth forest.

lysakermoa-naturreservat-nat94f699f3.d: Lysakermoa Nature Reserve covers 160 ha, and is situated in the far south-west of Eidsberg in the municipality of Indre Østfold, just south of Eidsberg Church, stretching from Buskelsrud in the north to just north of Skjørshammer Quay, and westwards to the municipal boundary with Skiptvet in the middle of the River Glomma. The River Glomma flows quite slowly here, and large clay banks have formed, creating a shallow-water area. These provide excellent foraging grounds for ducks and waders on the riverbanks. The river does not usually freeze over here, making the area very important as a wintering ground for several bird species. As of 1986, 69 bird species had been recorded within the area, of which 16 were ducks and 25 were waders. On land, the area is dominated by a ravine landscape with extensive birch forest.

storskj-r-fuglefredningsomrade-nat62b633.d: The Storskjær Bird Sanctuary comprises a skerry situated roughly in the centre of the inner part of Hallangspollen in Frogn municipality, as well as the sea area 50 metres offshore. The islet is a breeding ground, typically for red-listed little gulls and common terns. The birdlife in the reserve is protected against harm and unnecessary disturbance, and it is forbidden to carry out any activities that impair the birds’ habitat. All access is prohibited between 15 April and 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving. Furthermore, dogs must always be kept on a lead.

vindmyra-naturreservat-natb0f836b5.d: Vindmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve east of Årnes in Nes municipality, Akershus. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect an eccentric raised bog, which, together with Hvitmåsan and Sakknusmåsan, demonstrates the range of variation in such bogs in the district.

gj-lsj-en-naturreservat-nat91e9233d.d: Gjølsjøen Nature Reserve is a wetland area in Marker municipality that was designated a protected area in 1992. The area is home to a unique and zoogeographically interesting population of breeding birds. The lake is also an important migration route, and an observation tower has been erected in the south-western corner. A new tower was built in the north-west, near the Lømbo farm, in 2009. The reserve covers an area of 1,198 dekar, of which approximately 211 dekar is land area.

lurkevann-naturreservat-nat213ce050.d: Lurkevann Nature Reserve is situated west of Enningdalen, in the south of Halden municipality in Østfold. The reserve borders Sweden to the west. It was established in 2009 and slightly extended in 2013. The aim of the conservation is to preserve an area of coniferous forest that has been little affected by human activity. The vegetation is mainly sparse, with pine and heather dominating. However, there is also richer vegetation, including blueberry spruce forest and patches of more noble deciduous trees in favourable locations.

geitmyrasen-naturreservat-nate79ebc85.d: The Geitmyråsen Nature Reserve in Asker municipality was established on 14 December 2018. The nature reserve is situated on the southern slope of Villingstadåsen, by the Drammensfjord south-east of Hyggen, between Gjerdalsbukta to the south and the Herstadhei hill to the north. The area is characterised by old-growth forest, particularly coniferous forest, but there is also some deciduous forest in the lower-lying areas. There are also a number of yew trees. The nature reserve was established as part of the voluntary forest conservation scheme and has not been optimally demarcated. Some of the area’s most biologically valuable parts lie outside the nature reserve.

bergsj-h-landselva-dyrefredningsomrade-n.d: The Bergsjø-Hølandselva Wildlife Reserve is a wetland area in the municipality of Aurskog-Høland which was designated a protected area in 1992 to preserve the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitats in the area. The bird sanctuary covers an approximately 2.5 km stretch of the Hølandselva river and Bergsjø, together with the surrounding area, north of National Road 125. The bedrock consists of gneiss, which is mainly covered by marine clay. Here, the Hølandselva river flows across a flat floodplain, and spring and autumn floods form a shallow lake up to two kilometres in length. In the Bergsjø area, there are patches of scrub and marsh vegetation. Marsh plants such as common reed and sweet flag grow here, as well as river sedge and tufted sedge.

storesand-naturreservat-nat0481c6c0.d: Storesand Nature Reserve is situated on the west bank of the Glomma, in the south of Skiptvet municipality, with a small body of water also extending into Rakkestad municipality. The area is bounded by Ulvetangen to the north and Glennetangen to the south, and consists of a shallow bay with clay and mud banks. The shallow areas are exposed and flooded as the water level fluctuates throughout the year. The reserve forms part of a particularly important migration and resting route for birds. And because the River Glomma rarely freezes over, the area is also significant as a wintering site. Forty species of wetland birds have been recorded here. Also of botanical interest are the wet meadows with marsh plants.

ilemyr-naturreservat-natce69958f.d: The Ilemyr Nature Reserve comprises a large minerogenic flat bog and its surrounding area in a depression just west of Bankerødkollen, in the centre of Vesterøya in Hvaler municipality. The bog was formed by the overgrowth of a former pond. The flora is dominated by soft-mat and loose-soil vegetation, and common sundew is very common. This is the largest bog on the islands in the Oslo Fjord. The conservation objective is therefore twofold: to preserve a minerogenic bog formed by the overgrowth of open water, and to protect the largest bog on the islands in the Oslo Fjord. All vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees, is protected from destruction. However, picking berries and mushrooms is permitted. Furthermore, all birdlife, including eggs and nests, is protected from destruction and unnecessary disturbance.

vikertjernet-biotopvernomrade-natb795260.d: The Vikertjernet biotope conservation area consists of a small wetland area amongst granite hills in the south-east of Asmaløy in Hvaler. The area includes Vikertjernet itself as well as several smaller marsh ponds. A total of seven dragonfly species live here, including the southern metal-coloured damselfly, which is very rare in Norway. The mountain damselfly is also found here, at its lowest known location. It otherwise lives primarily in the mountains. The reserve is also home to the small salamander and the pointed-snouted frog, both of which are on the Red List. The habitat protection covers the four species mentioned. The vegetation is protected against damage and destruction, and the four animal species covered by the habitat protection are protected against collection, damage, destruction and unnecessary disturbance.

spernesmosen-naturreservat-natcb631368.d: Spernesmosen Nature Reserve is situated east of Klund Church in Marker municipality, five kilometres north of the village of Ørje. The area is technically described as an intact lowland bog and characterised as a well-developed raised bog. The vegetation consists of species that thrive in rainwater bogs, such as bear’s-ear moss. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve one of the few intact concentric raised bogs in Østfold.

styggdalen-naturreservat-nat97d560e6.d: Styggdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Nannestad and Lunner. It comprises an area in the Romeriksåsene hills. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling and horse riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, in that it consists of primeval, damp and mature spruce forest with good populations of a number of very rare and demanding fungiand lichen species.

pipra-og-storrsj-h-gda-naturreservat-nat.d: The Pipra and Storrsjøhøgda Nature Reserve is situated in the Romeriksåsene hills between Harestua and Råsjøen, in gently undulating terrain at an altitude of around 500–600 metres above sea level. The bedrock consists of syenite porphyry, which results in acidic soil. The vegetation is dominated by old spruce forest, but also includes some younger woodland. The amount of deadwood is increasing, and the area will gradually become more valuable for natural forest species. A few scattered occurrences of hollow-stemmed sedge and a single find of parasitic sedge have been recorded. Both are Red Listed. The area forms part of an ecologically functional network of nature reserves in the Romeriksåsene hills and is, amongst other things, of great value to space-demanding bird species such as the goshawk.

tretjernh-la-naturreservat-nataa63c588.d: The Tretjernhøla Nature Reserve comprises a partly marshy area and a steeper hillside to the east, between Drettvannet and Skålsjøen in Lørenskog municipality. The area lies at an altitude of approximately 250 to 310 metres above sea level. It is unspoilt and dominated by various types of spruce forest, including the Red Listed habitat type ‘tall herb spruce forest’. The area has great potential for rare species associated with dead wood; amongst others, the critically endangered Lapland flycatcher has been found here. One of the aims of the nature reserve is to protect an area of particular value for biodiversity.

s-rbyskogen-naturreservat-natd629b3d6.d: The Sørbyskogen Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern side of Nesodden, between County Road 156 and Bunnefjorden. The Sørbybekken stream flows through the reserve from Sørbydammen in the south-west to its outlet in Bunnefjorden in the north-east. The vegetation is particularly rich and varied along the stream, with a significant area of rich deciduous forest. In addition, there is rich mixed woodland, rich swamp forest and old coniferous forest. Sørbydammen is an important site for amphibians. Furthermore, the reserve is home to a number of Red Listed fungi species, including the clinging polypore and the hollow-stemmed waxcap. Along the shore, blood cranesbill and the Red Listed tuberous meadowsweet grow. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but it is permitted to forage for edible mushrooms and berries.

s-ter-naturreservat-nat3cc518ac.d: Sæter Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Indre Østfold. It comprises an area by Lake Øyeren. The area was designated a nature reserve on 23 June 2020 and extended on 6 December 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads, tractor tracks and footpaths, the use of bicycles, horses and carts, as well as horse riding, is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that a. represents specific types of natural environment in the form of mature, high-quality forest with elements of old-growth broadleaf forest and mixed forest with rich ground vegetation; b. contains threatened, rare or vulnerable natural features, such as the vulnerable ‘clay ravine’ habitat type.

h-vikskj-ra-fuglefredningsomrade-natb898.d: The Høvikskjæra Bird Sanctuary is a habitat conservation area comprising a two-part skerry, the seabed to the north and the surrounding waters extending 50 metres out. The skerries serve as a breeding ground for a number of seabirds, particularly great skuas. It is prohibited to carry out any activities within the conservation area that could damage the birds’ habitat. Furthermore, all access is prohibited on land and at sea during the period from 15 April to 15 July, including flying below 300 metres and all water sports and diving.

surtebergflaget-naturreservat-nat89e8c1f.d: Surtebergflaget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Krødsherad municipality. It comprises an area on the western side of Lake Krøderen, near Norefjell. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017 and extended on 14 September 2023 from approximately 1,457 dekar to 1,479.2 dekar. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old-growth natural forest, comprising old lowland mixed forest and a stream ravine. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for a number of species, particularly fungi and vascular plants.

lienskj-ret-biotopvernomrade-nat7e4855c2.d: The Lienskjæret biotope conservation area (approximately 8 daa, of which approximately 0.1 daa is land area) is situated off Utstranda in Tyrifjorden, just south of Lia and south-east of Utøya along the mainland, and was established by Royal Decreeof 22 June 2018 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 38 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The conservation area is situated in Hole municipality, Buskerud, and forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. It consists of a single islet and a zone of approximately 50 metres around it. The biotope conservation area is intended to protect an area of particular importance as an ecological functional area, serving as a breeding site for the black-headed gull.

aurstadmasan-naturreservat-natda863662.d: Aurstadmåsan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve comprising a large rain-fed bog and was established in 1981. It is situated east of Nordkisa and north-west of Vormsund in Nes municipality in Akershus, and borders County Road 480 to the north-east. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a well-developed concentric raised bog; Aurstadmåsan and the neighbouring Grenimåsan are considered to be among the finest remaining examples of their kind in the country.

stubberud-naturreservat-nat2ef12f14.d: Stubberud Nature Reserve is situated on the steep slope above County Road 33, south of Skreikampen, in the very north of Eidsvoll municipality. The bedrock is granitic, but the vegetation is characterised by calcareous seepage water. This results in a mosaic of varied vegetation types, depending on the availability of seepage water. The world’s northernmost inland population of yew is found here. There are also calcareous pine forests, as well as, amongst other species, wayfaring tree, sweet woodruff and wood anemone.

arhanemyra-naturreservat-nat6c8f7329.d: Århanemyra Nature Reserve is situated in gently undulating terrain on the Romeriksåsene hills, in the north of Nittedal municipality. The vegetation consists largely of old, largely undisturbed mixed pine and spruce forest of good quality. The bedrock is slightly alkaline, yet in places within the depressions there are rich fens where abundant spring water rises to the surface. On one of these rich fens, the small fen sedge has been found; it is listed as ‘Endangered’ (EN) on the Red List. Furthermore, the reserve’s old-growth forest is important for birdlife, including vulnerable birds of prey. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected, but picking berries and foraging for edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting, trapping and fishing are also permitted in accordance with current legislation.

h-ra-naturreservat-nat2cf13c0e.d: The Hæra Nature Reserve in Trøgstad, in the municipality of Indre Østfold, encompasses the Hæra watercourse from Lake Kallaksjøen to Lake Skottasjøen, together with adjacent areas. The area boasts a wide variety of habitats and, in addition to the river itself, includes wet meadows, bogs, coniferous and deciduous woodland, as well as fallow land. This results in a rich diversity of species. Among other things, 68 different species of wetland birds have been recorded, and the site is the most important resting place for cranes in Østfold.

veia-naturreservat-nat4ed5a7ad.d: Veia Nature Reserve forms a small but distinct and well-developed, north-facing ravine south of Mjøndalen, between Dammyrtjern and Portåsen. The bedrock consists of Cambrian–Silurian limestone; the ravine is dominated by calcareous spruce forest and low-herb spruce forest. Further up along the ridges, there is some calcareous pine forest. There are a few footpaths and old forest tracks within the reserve. Lake Dammyrtjern is an artificial lake. The reserve covers 390.7 dekar and lies at altitudes ranging from 0 metres above sea level to 1,500 metres above sea level.

leirfalla-naturreservat-nat990855c8.d: Leirfalla Nature Reserve is situated on the steep slope between Lake Mjøsa and County Road 33, north of Minnesund in Eidsvoll municipality. The area is covered with deciduous forest, mainly elm-lime forest and grey alder-ash forest. The bedrock consists of metamorphic rocks, mostly hornfels.

sislemyrene-naturreservat-natee77bf75.d: Sislemyrene Nature Reserve is situated in undulating woodland terrain in the far west of Hurdal municipality, towards the county border with Innlandet, north of County Road 180. The area consists of several contiguous flat bogs. The vegetation is characterised centrally by soft mats and floating mats with sparse vegetation, but with richer areas to the south and west. The area serves as a complementary addition to the Vindflomyrene Nature Reserve. The purpose of designating the Sislemyrene Nature Reserve is to conserve a complex of flat bogs and its associated wildlife.

vassmyrasen-naturreservat-natb7a0ea2b.d: Vassmyråsen Nature Reserve is situated in the heart of Vestmarka, in the far west of Bærum municipality. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry, which provides relatively nutrient-rich soil. The vegetation consists of spruce forest of good quality. The forest is old, and there are significant quantities of dead wood, both standing (snags) and lying (logs). In places, there is also a great deal of hanging lichen, and a few Red List species have been recorded. Former ditches are in the process of becoming overgrown, and parts of the forest will eventually regain their swamp forest character. Along the Korselva river, there are also well-developed floodplain forests and valuable rock face habitats. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted.

tranemosen-naturreservat-nat39828c5f.d: The Tranemosen Nature Reserve consists of a bog area with peripheral zones in the south-east of Halden municipality. The area is dominated by minerotrophic flat bogs, with elements of gently sloping ombrotrophic bogs, and in places also pine bog woodland and a few bog pools. Towards the dry land to the north, there is a distinct transition zone with somewhat richer vegetation.

trestikle-naturreservat-nat18f69c25.d: Trestikle Nature Reserve is a nature reserve south of Drammen town centre. The nature reserve is situated in gently undulating terrain and encompasses Risåsen, Finnefjell, Lake Trestikle and the surrounding woodland areas. The area is characterised by mature woodland with large, old trees. Trestikle Nature Reserve was formally approved by the Council of State on 15 March 2019.

sandsbakken-naturreservat-nat550a260c.d: Sandsbakken Nature Reserve was established on 18 April 1986. The deciduous forest area is situated in Øvre Eiker, in Buskerud County, alongside County Road 35 at the northern end of Lake Eikeren. The reserve covers an area of approximately 94 dekar and has been designated to preserve a stand of elm and lime forest, which also forms a beautiful feature of the landscape.

gyrihelleren-naturreservat-natd95c5a5c.d: Gyrihelleren Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Indre Østfold. It comprises an area on the border with Sweden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 23 June 2020 and extended on 6 December 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling and horse riding are prohibited, except on paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of a relatively undisturbed forest area in low-lying regions just above the marine limit on bedrock, as well as to preserve fire-affected forest. The area consists of large tracts of old-growth forest, predominantly comprising nutrient-poor forest types with pine and spruce, as well as several ponds and bogs.

hovsenga-naturreservat-nat002c3724.d: Hovsenga Nature Reserve (approximately 337 daa, of which approximately 203 daa is land area) is a beautiful outdoor recreation area by the River Randselva, just on the outskirts of the town of Hønefoss in Ringerike municipality, Buskerud. The area has a long history as a bathing and fishing spot for local residents, who also use it for occasional summer festivities. The nature reserve was established by Royal Decree on 22 June 2018.
