The area is situated below Hov Farm, where the river meanders. A footpath has been laid out leading down to the meadow, which also features a designated barbecue area. However, a wooden bridge makes access difficult for wheelchair users. There are good fishing opportunities there, as well as a rich variety of flora and fauna.

svartvannet-naturreservat-nata010f88b.d: Svartvannet Nature Reserve is a forested area in Marker municipality, which was designated a nature reserve in 2005. The area was designated as part of the voluntary forest conservation programme.

mysutjernene-naturreservat-natc8df8c03.d: Mysutjernene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kongsberg municipality, covering an area of 95 dekar. The nature reserve was established on 24 April 1992. The reserve consists of Vesle Mysutjern, Midtre Mysutjern and Store Mysutjern. The reserve is situated approximately 12.5 kilometres south of Kongsberg town centre, in the direction of the Styggemann mountain peak. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a rare type of water body found only on calcareous bedrock and characterised by abundant occurrences of stonewort algae. The Mysutjern lakes have a high calcium content, resulting in a high pH (above 8.0). It is the calcareous bedrock that provides the basis for the development of such waters.

kn-lltjenna-naturreservat-nat235b6842.d: Knølltjenna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the north of Aurskog-Høland municipality in Akershus. The area was designated a nature reserve in 2013 and covers 614 hectares. The reserve comprises a relatively small area of old spruce forest with a significant proportion of aspen. There is a high density of so-called ‘mis-biotopes’ here – areas registered under the ‘Environmental Registration in Forests’ (MiS) programme. Among other things, the Red Listed fungus ‘furuplett’ is found here.

katterompa-plantefredningsomrade-natd84b.d: The Katterompa Plant Conservation Area is a biotope conservation area comprising an islet in the coastal zone between Brønnøya and Furuholmen in Asker municipality. The bedrock consists of calcareous sedimentary rocks, and the site features the habitat type ‘open, shallow-rooted calcareous grassland’, including calcareous dry grassland. A total of 103 different plant species have been recorded on the islet, including the Red Listed species spiked speedwell, sea campion and tuberous meadowsweet, as well as dragon’s head, which is a species for which Norway has a special responsibility. The plant communities are protected against damage and destruction, and any activities that may impair the plants’ habitat are prohibited. Furthermore, pitching tents is prohibited, and campfires and barbecues are only permitted in designated areas.

hjelpskj-ra-biotopvernomrade-nat33aed2e1.d: The Hjelpskjæra Biotope Conservation Area is a biotope conservation area comprising two islets on the eastern side of Torvøya near Sætre in Asker municipality, and the surrounding sea area within a 50-metre radius. The bedrock consists of granite, which results in barren growing conditions. The skerries are virtually devoid of vegetation. The skerries serve as a breeding ground for a number of seabirds. Access is prohibited both on land and at sea during the period from 15 April to 15 July, including flying below 300 metres as well as all water sports and diving. An exception is made for access in connection with commercial fishing.

kloppa-naturreservat-nat1a967307.d: Kloppa Nature Reserve in Bærum municipality was established on 20 December 2019. Kloppa is situated just east of Engervannet in an area of the Oslo region where there is very high pressure on land use. It comprises a north-west-facing slope and a ridge south of the Øverlandselva river, surrounded by residential areas. The bedrock in the area consists of limestone, claystone and sandstone. The hilltop area to the south is gently undulating, with a number of limestone outcrops and small depressions containing fresher, deeper soil. To the north is a relatively steep slope, before the terrain levels out. Further north, the terrain slopes down even more towards the river.

hurdalselvdeltaet-naturreservat-natdf21c.d: The Hurdalselv Delta Nature Reserve is situated where the Hurdalselva river flows into the northern end of Lake Hurdalssjøen. The natural environment consists of a mire and delta area. It is mainly composed of sedge marshes, but also features more mire-associated vegetation dominated by peat mosses and bladderwort. Goose willow is also found here, probably one of the southernmost occurrences in Eastern Norway. The area is a breeding ground for ducks and waders, and is also an important resting place for migratory birds.

lineh-gda-naturreservat-nat29a20afc.d: Linehøgda Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the Swedish border in Marker municipality, on the Nebba peninsula in Lake Store Le. The bedrock consists mainly of mylonitic gneiss, which results in relatively nutrient-poor soil. In places, however, there is richer vegetation, including bluebells, wood anemone, wood sorrel, red campion and spring snowflake. In the west of the reserve, towards Modal, the fairy flower has also been observed. Many years may pass between each time it flowers in a particular spot. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but ordinary hunting is permitted, as is the gathering of berries and edible mushrooms. Motorised traffic is prohibited, with certain exceptions specified in the conservation regulations.

arekilen-naturreservat-nat8e43bf6e.d: Arekilen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hvaler municipality in Østfold. It comprises an area at Arekilen on Kirkøy, north-west of Skjærhalden. The area was first designated as a nature reserve in 1976, and the designation was revised on 5 November 2011. The reserve forms part of the conservation plan for deciduous broad-leaved forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of threatened, rare and vulnerable nature, featuring special habitat types in the form of a rich swamp forest with black alder and a water body with varied marsh vegetation’.

veikulasen-naturreservat-natafbb2f2e.d: Veikulåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gol municipality. It comprises an area to the east of the Hallingdalselva river near Gol. The area was designated a nature reserve on 22 December 2006, and was extended in 2014 and on 15 December 2017 from approximately 4,665 dekar to 6,077.2 dekar. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing tractor tracks and footpaths, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large regional forest area with significant topographical variations. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for species of fungi associated with dead wood and a distinctive lichen flora.

beengen-fuglefredningsomrade-nat68ef9549.d: The Beengen Wildlife Reserve comprises a shallow-water area with banks at the mouths of several streams on the eastern bank of the Glomma, south of Udenes Church. The purpose of the reserve is to preserve the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitats in the area. All birdlife in the area is protected throughout the year. With certain exceptions, motorised traffic is not permitted.

gukilh-gda-og-abbortjernh-gda-naturreser.d: The Gukilhøgda and Abbortjernhøgda Nature Reserve is situated on a north-facing slope on the western shore of Lake Hemnessjøen, just south of the Gukil farm in Aurskog-Høland municipality. Until its expansion on 21 June 2024, the name of the reserve was Gukilhøgda Nature Reserve. The vegetation consists largely of very productive spruce forest on, in places, thick (deep) layers of loose soil. Such areas have been cultivated in many places, and forests like this are therefore very rare. In the higher areas to the south, the forest is characterised more by pine, most commonly of the low-growing pine and berry-heather pine types. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted.

lagabakkane-naturreservat-natcf4d5d74.d: The Lågabakkane Nature Reserve was established in 2018 and is a small area situated at an altitude of approximately 40–90 metres above sea level, east of the Numedalslågen river in the north-west of Larvik municipality. The bedrock consists of syenite, whilst the alluvial deposits consist mainly of somewhat alkaline marine and fjord deposits, as well as some river deposits. The area also features old ravine spruce forest on marine alluvial deposits, as well as fragments of sand pine forest. Such forest types are rare and valuable for biodiversity. Several Red List species have been recorded here.

nedre-r-nningkasene-naturreservat-nat962.d: Nedre Rønningkåsene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Nome municipality. It comprises an area near Ulefoss. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from the existing road, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large, well-developed and highly varied ravine system with spruce-dominated coniferous forest, spruce-dominated rich boreonemoral mixed forest, grey alder and hazel forest, small-fern forest, low-herb forest and tall-shrub and large-fern forest, which contain good stocks of deadwood.

fj-revardasen-naturreservat-nat27743f60.d: The Fjærevardåsen Nature Reserve was established in 2017. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve an area that represents a specific type of landscape, comprising old mixed beech and oak woodland in the lowlands, with patches of rich beech woodland and hillsides covered in poor, old pine woodland. Furthermore, the aim is to protect an area that contains threatened and rare species and habitat types. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to further develop them. Fjærevardåsen represents a small but valuable forest area, which, amongst other things, contains a remnant fragment of old mixed beech forest of a richer composition.

nordre-lia-naturreservat-nat44e19275.d: Nordre Lia Nature Reserve is situated on south-facing scree and boulder fields at the foot of a steep, bare mountainside beneath Lifjell, at the far end of Kleivgrend in Fyresdal. The area is of particular scientific value due to the presence of pure deciduous woodland comprising ash, hazel and elm. There are also several endangered and rare species of lichen and fungi growing on dead wood.

urdalen-naturreservat-nat2f35e88c.d: The Urdalen Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Tinnsjøen in Tinn municipality. The area was designated on 7 December 2018, extended on 20 June 2023, and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity due to the presence of mature lowland coniferous forest with a high proportion of boreal deciduous forest and, in part, broad-leaved trees. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular scientific value due to the presence of rich low-herb coniferous forest, such as low-herb pine forest and low-herb spruce-limestone forest, as well as the presence of yew, at its inner boundary in the Telemark region.”

holtsasen-naturreservat-nat033ea020.d: Holsåsen Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern side of Eidangerfjorden, south of Døvika in Porsgrunn municipality. The area contains a rich variety of habitat types, including oak woodland, lime woodland on scree slopes and patches of mixed spruce forest. Of particular value are the old oak trees, along with the associated rare fungi species that are important for biodiversity. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but ordinary hunting is permitted, as is the gathering of berries and edible mushrooms. Motorised traffic is prohibited, and it is also not permitted to light campfires.

krogshavn-plantefredningsomrade-nat55007.d: The Krogshavn Plant Conservation Area in Bamble is a 100-metre-long, 4-metre-wide and 1-metre-deep ditch at the Krogshavn campsite. The area is worthy of protection due to the presence of the rare vascular plant, the spiked sweetgrass. Spiked sweetgrass is classified as critically endangered on the Norwegian Red List of Species. Species found in the reserve include brook speedwell, common reed, branched milkwort, wood rush, cat’s tail, sea arrowgrass, meadow saxifrage, field bindweed and toadflax.

st-hansasen-naturreservat-nat69d54923.d: St. Hansåsen Nature Reserve was established in 2018 and is a small area of natural woodland situated at an altitude of approximately 150–254 metres above sea level, east of Lake Bergsvannet in Holmestrand municipality. The area is dominated by mature, naturally regenerated natural woodland of spruce and pine. There is a fairly high proportion of aspen and some broad-leaved trees, including Norway maple, oak, lime, hazel and black alder. Several Red List species have been recorded, and the area has the potential to support a number of species with specific habitat requirements, including insects, woodpeckers and cavity-nesting birds. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of mature, naturally regenerated natural lowland forest, with its naturally occurring species, habitat types and ecological processes.

h-gvollane-naturreservat-nat08189e30.d: Høgvollane Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Skien municipality. It comprises an area to the west of Fjellvannet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from on existing roads, the use of horse and cart and horse riding are prohibited, and cycling is prohibited off existing roads and paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old and relatively undisturbed spruce forest and lowland mixed forest, with a considerable amount of dead wood in places. Furthermore, the purpose is to protect an area of particular scientific value due to the presence of threatened and vulnerable species of hanging lichen, wood-dwelling lichen and fungi.

sandvikheia-naturreservat-nat46581313.d: Sandvikheia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Drangedal municipality. It comprises an area south of Bjorvann. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from on existing roads, the use of horse and cart and horse riding are prohibited, and cycling is prohibited off existing roads and paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to protect a forest area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of old boreal deciduous forest, rich mixed forest, old broad-leaved forest, rich broad-leaved forest, old coniferous forest and old lowland mixed forest.

fisketj-nnjuvet-naturreservat-nat025c346.d: Fisketjønnjuvet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kviteseid municipality. It comprises an area by the Fjågesundstraumen strait between Kviteseidvatnet and Flåvatn. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 December 2017. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is: ‘The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich forest types, including particularly large and rich lime forests, some of which have the character of natural forest, large areas of seasonally moist calcareous pine forest and low-herb pine forest, as well as patches of aspen and large stands of yew.”

brennevinsholmen-stre-biotopvernomrade-n.d: The Brennevinsholmen Eastern Biotope Protection Area consists of a medium-sized islet and two smaller skerries situated approximately 50 metres from the shore at Finnmarkstrand in Trosbyfjorden, Bamble, and is designated as a ‘biotope protection area’ under the Wildlife Act. The site is thought to be home to the largest black-headed gull colony in Telemark. The black-headed gull is listed on Artsdatabanken’s Red List of species at risk of extinction in Norway.

birkelid-naturreservat-nata2189a8a.d: Birkelid Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kristiansand municipality. It comprises an area approximately 10 km west of Kristiansand. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited, except on existing roads or routes approved in the management plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area with a specific type of natural environment in the form of a contiguous, relatively undisturbed forest area with rich deciduous woodland comprising elm-lime forest and low-herb oak forest formations. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity due to its wide variety of tree species and rich diversity of plant species.

rosst-l-naturreservat-nat356c3e42.d: Rosstøl Nature Reserve comprises an area by Øynesvann in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 15 December 2017 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of a local climatic low-herb oak forest area with a high diversity of oak-associated species on mineral-rich bedrock. The area is to safeguard, in particular, scattered old oak trees and the great diversity of soil-dwelling fungi.’

prestvannet-fuglefredningsomrade-nat9bbe.d: The Prestvannet Wildlife Reserve is a protected habitat at Prestvannet in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The area was designated a protected area in 1988 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve a migration and wintering area for wetland birds. Over 100 bird species have been recorded at the small lake, which is nestled amongst built-up areas. Species that overwinter here include ducks, little grebes, moorhens and snipes. Breeding species include the reed warbler, sedge warbler and marsh warbler. Teal and great crested grebes have also been observed here. The lake is also used as a kayaking course.

kviteflogi-naturreservat-nat10df103f.d: Kviteflogi Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bygland municipality. It comprises an area to the west of Byglandsfjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017 and extended on 17 December 2021. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of elm-lime forest, old coniferous forest and south-facing rocky slopes and scree with a rich diversity of species and many endangered and rare species. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

heddeviksfjell-naturreservat-nat0e6e2dbf.d: Heddeviksfjell Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bygland municipality. It comprises an area near Åraksbø. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017 and extended on 6 December 2024 to 593 dekar. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads or routes marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of nature with great variety, such as hay meadows, coppiced woodland, rich deciduous forest, rich mixed woodland, old coniferous forest, old deciduous forest, south-facing rock faces and scree slopes, low-herb spruce forest and the northernmost outpost of oak in Setesdal.

bjynnustadfjellet-naturreservat-nat458cc.d: Bjynnustadfjellet Nature Reserve (known as Bjørnstadfjell Nature Reserve until 6 December 2019) is a nature reserve in Gjerstad municipality. It comprises an area on the border with Telemark. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017 and extended on 6 December 2019 from approximately 833 dekar to approximately 1,539 dekar. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of low-herb oak woodland, old pine forest and highly productive spruce-dominated forest’.

underforlii-naturreservat-natcf334c6b.d: Underforlii Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bygland municipality. It comprises an area on the north side of the Otra river, below Sordalsheii. The area was first designated as a nature reserve on 21 June 2019 and extended on 24 June 2025. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised land traffic is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents specific types of natural habitat in the form of well-developed old scree-linden forest, old pine forest and rich mixed forest; b.

h-kjenkleiv-naturreservat-nat366c7349.d: Hækjenkleiv Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åmli municipality. It comprises an area to the north and north-east of Varpsfoss and to the east of Toftefjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017 and extended on 20 June 2023 from approximately 902 dekar to 3,105.2. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old and rich low-herb oak woodland, rich scree-slope lime woodland and old sun-warmed pine woodland.’

vassvannet-naturreservat-nat9766c0ad.d: Vassvannet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kristiansand municipality. It comprises an area bounded by Vassvannet to the north, Røyrvann to the north-west, Eidsvann to the south-west and Stemvann to the south. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of low-lying, coastal, highly productive and old broad-leaved forest. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it provides a habitat for a number of species.

dasvassdalen-naturreservat-nat92336302.d: Dåsvassdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipality of Evje and Hornnes. It comprises an area to the west of Uleberg. The area was designated a nature reserve on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited, except on existing tractor tracks and tractor trails marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area with a specific type of natural environment in the form of distinctive steep, north-east-facing slopes with open, meadow-like deciduous woodland. The slopes feature stands of old broad-leaved trees and a large, intact population of yew, including some very old and very large yew trees in Svarteberglia.

kvasfossen-naturreservat-nat9e97d7c0.d: Kvåsfossen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lyngdal, Agder. Its purpose is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of an east-facing vegetation gradient from Lygna, with rich elm and lime forest in the block terrain and black alder at the bottom, rich deciduous forest in the middle and pine and aspen forest in the upper parts. Furthermore, the aim is to protect an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it provides habitats for a large number of species.”

vasselen-naturreservat-nat66cb5670.d: Vasselen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tingvoll municipality. It comprises an area by Lake Storvatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 November 2020 and extended on 8 March 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Apart from the existing tractor track and footpaths, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a diverse forest area containing threatened and rare natural features in the form of rich deciduous forest and old pine forest. The forest is well-developed and home to several rare and demanding species.’

austadmarka-naturreservat-nat72c9f191.d: Austadmarka Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Drammen municipality, south of Drammen town and east of the village of Konnerud. The terrain consists mainly of limestone in the north-east, whilst the southern part consists of sandstone. The vegetation is dominated by pine forest and calcareous plant communities. The reserve lies at an altitude of approximately 215–330 metres above sea level. Austadmarka Nature Reserve was established in 2021 and covers an area of 1,585 dekar.

nideng-naturreservat-nat831beaac.d: The Nideng Nature Reserve is situated in a well-developed ravine system north of Tanem in Klæbu, Trondheim municipality. The reserve covers the eastern parts of the ravine system, which features deeply incised ravines. The area contains the following habitat types: tall-herb spruce forest, spruce swamp forest, coastal spruce forest and floodplain woodland, with a rich lichen flora. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, including dead shrubs and trees. However, the regulations provide for a number of exceptions, including ‘the careful collection of small timber for individual outdoor recreation and the lighting of campfires on site’.

larshus-naturreservat-nat0d7d1cb9.d: Larshus Nature Reserve is situated in Hadeland Østås, to the west of Lake Skjerva. The reserve covers a gently undulating area with several bogs, some of which are classified as rich fens. The forest is dominated by various types of spruce woodland, with unusually large quantities of deadwood. Selective felling has previously taken place in the area, but very little since the Second World War. The reserve is home to an abundance of wood-dwelling fungi, including four Red List species. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but the regulations allow for a number of exceptions. Among other things, it is permitted to erect temporary mobile hunting towers for big game hunting, and to gather edible mushrooms and berries. Campfires are permitted in accordance with other legislation.

muttj-nn-naturreservat-natc4dfafd3.d: The Muttjønn Nature Reserve covers an area stretching from Ramsås in the south and around Øvre and Nedre Muttjønn, as well as Stulsdalen, south-east of Follsjå in Notodden municipality. The forest in the area is old, and its conservation value is particularly linked to old, fire-influenced lowland pine forest, which is home to a wide variety of species. In the past, forestry operations took place in the area. Log driving took place during the spring floods on the Lona river, which flows out of Muttjønna. There were regulation dams in both Øvre and Nedre Muttjønn. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but the regulations allow for a number of exceptions. Among other things, it is permitted to gather edible mushrooms and berries, as well as to carry out ‘careful clearing of small shrubs’ in connection with big game hunting.

havikberget-og-nordberg-naturreservat-na.d: The Havikberget and Nordberg Nature Reserve is situated on a south-facing slope on the eastern shore of Lake Mjøsa, 7–8 kilometres north of Moelv in Ringsaker municipality. The bedrock consists of Biskopåskonglomerat with limestone lenses, and traces of limestone and shale. The variation from nutrient-poor to calcareous bedrock results in diverse vegetation, comprising both nutrient-poor pine forest and rich low-herb forest and broad-leaved deciduous forest. The reserve is home to a number of rare and vulnerable moss and lichen species, including the Red Listed and highly calcareous crustose lichen Anema nummularium, as well as other crustose lichen species. Vulnerable bird species are also found here, and the area is important for cliff-nesting birds of prey. All vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees, is protected from destruction.

br-skjahagan-naturreservat-nat27c62e75.d: Brøskjahagan Nature Reserve is a steep area of broadleaf forest on the headland between Surnadalsfjorden and Stangvikfjorden in Surnadal municipality, Møre og Romsdal. The reserve stretches from the sea on the north side up to nearly 300 metres above sea level, and above the settlement on Stangvikvegen on the west side. The forest is well-developed and is home to several demanding species that are important for biodiversity. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, and motorised traffic is prohibited. Open fires are also not permitted.

holstadlia-naturreservat-natb9dc6f9a.d: Holstadlia Nature Reserve is a steep, east-facing slope on the west bank of the Flagstadelva river, in the far east of Ringsaker municipality. The bedrock is rich in limestone, which fosters a rich variety of vegetation. The forest in the reserve consists of spruce with a mix of various deciduous trees, including birch, maple and hazel. Easily weathered rock in very steep terrain means that trees fall regularly, resulting in a large amount of deadwood from various tree species and at all stages of decomposition. Together with high humidity along the river, this provides the basis for a high level of biodiversity. Several Red List plants in the ‘Near Threatened’ (NT) category have been recorded in the reserve, including hollow-stemmed grass, grubbe’s beard and green-shoe.

galtedalstjerna-naturreservat-nataaae233.d: Galtedalstjerna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve west of Vassjø in Grindvoll, in the municipalities of Jevnaker and Lunner. The reserve encompasses the western part of Galtedalstjernet, as well as a prominent limestone ridge on the north side and a steeper slope on the south side. The limestone-rich bedrock gives rise to species-rich limestone coniferous forest, rich fens and limestone lakes. The area is virtually untouched and is home to a number of Red List species. The lake contains endangered stoneworts, which are typical of limestone lakes. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but the regulations allow for a number of exceptions. Among other things, it is permitted to erect temporary mobile hunting towers for big game hunting, and to gather edible mushrooms and berries.

mj-sj-dalen-naturreservat-natdb16da64.d: The Mjøsjødalen Nature Reserve lies on both sides of the municipal boundary between Lillestrøm and Aurskog-Høland, along the valley depression extending north-east from Søndre Mjøsjøen. The reserve contains old spruce and pine forest, particularly in three core areas. There is dead wood in all stages of decomposition, and Red Listed species of fungi and lichens have been recorded. The forest here has been little affected by logging, unlike many surrounding areas. There is also ecological value associated with the transition (gradient) from pine forest in the drier areas at the top of the valley to richer spruce forest in the wetter areas further down the valley. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Vegetation and wildlife are protected from destruction, but ordinary hunting is permitted.

skaraura-naturreservat-nat24f7cc1d.d: Skåraura Nature Reserve is a steep area of hazel thicket south of Skåradalen on the eastern side of Syvdefjorden in Vanylven municipality, Møre og Romsdal. The reserve stretches from the power line along County Road 652 up towards Vardegga, at an altitude of nearly 400 metres above sea level. The forest is well-developed and is home to several demanding species that are important for biodiversity. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, and motorised traffic is prohibited. Open fires are also not permitted.

berdalen-naturreservat-nat0032bdf1.d: The Berdalen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Lærdalsøyri in Lærdal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 17 December 2021 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve rare natural features in the form of a large and largely untouched forest area. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area that is particularly important for biodiversity, as it contains many types of forest and vegetation, a great deal of dead wood, and has great potential as a habitat for rare and demanding species.”

torshov-naturreservat-nat2785ab1d.d: Torshov Nature Reserve is an area of largely undisturbed ravine forest on the west bank of the River Leira in Gjerdrum municipality. The area lies on marine clay, and the vegetation is dominated by old spruce forest. There is a relatively large amount of deadwood here, which provides opportunities for rare species. The area also contains patches of floodplain woodland, a habitat type of which very little is protected in Norway. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but ordinary hunting is permitted, as is the gathering of berries and edible mushrooms. Motorised traffic is prohibited, and it is also not permitted to light campfires.

barlinddalen-naturreservat-nat86437fb7.d: Barlinddalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Midt-Telemark municipality. The area was designated on 11 February 2022 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard an area of particular value for biodiversity due to the presence of the habitat types: calcareous and low-herb pine forest, rich mixed lowland forest, old coniferous forest and a rich and varied flora of vascular plants. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area that contains several rare and threatened species of fungi and lichens.”

middagsberget-naturreservat-natfdc73951.d: Middagsberget Nature Reserve comprises the eastern slope of Middagsberget, just west of County Road 24 in the south of Stange municipality. The area features an old spruce forest with plenty of deadwood. This is a habitat for several species of lichen and fungi, including the Red Listed species ‘gubbeskjegg’ and ‘rosenkjuke’. Wildlife is protected against damage and unnecessary disturbance. The same applies to all vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees. However, hunting and the picking of berries and mushrooms are permitted. Lighting campfires using dry twigs gathered from the ground is also permitted, subject to the other rules. Motorised traffic is prohibited, as is cycling and horse riding off existing paths.

dalasen-naturreservat-natd6649a5a.d: Dalåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hjartdal municipality. It comprises an area in the outlying countryside of Fossegrenna in the village of Sauland. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing paths, cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents specific types of natural habitat, such as limestone and low-herb pine forest, rich mixed lowland forest and old lowland coniferous forest that has been little affected. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area that contains rare and endangered species of fungi and lichens, and which is of particular importance for biodiversity due to its rich and varied flora of vascular plants.

sata-naturreservat-nat9cff056e.d: Såta Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Ringerike and Flå. It comprises an area east of Krøderen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing roads and paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large, high-altitude hilltop plateau and its slopes, with mature woodland that is representative of high-altitude woodland in this region.’

tennelia-naturreservat-natf995f98a.d: Tennelia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Senja municipality. It comprises an area by Solbergfjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents specific types of natural habitat in the form of rich boreal deciduous forest, in this case calcareous birch forest with elements of aspen, rowan, goat willow, pine and grey alder. Another objective is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as the forest is well-developed with plenty of deadwood and features species-rich ground vegetation comprising thermophilic and calcareous vascular plants.”

ki-rmarka-naturreservat-natfc19aac3.d: Kiærmarka Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rakkestad municipality. It comprises an area along the River Glomma. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents specific types of nature in the form of rich forest types such as old lowland mixed forest, floodplain forest and overgrown cultivated land with hazel. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

verpelva-naturreservat-nat82204497.d: Verpelva Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tønsberg municipality. It comprises an area near Revetal. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing footpaths and tractor tracks, cycling, horse riding and riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a ravine valley with rich deciduous woodland, rich swamp woodland, spring woodland and riparian woodland, as well as old spruce woodland in the lowlands. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular scientific value due to the presence of rare and threatened species and habitat types.”

buggastrondi-naturreservat-nat8b1e805a.d: The Buggastrondi Nature Reserve comprises an area at the far end of the Lustrafjord in Luster municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 16 December 2022 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of calcareous pine forest and rich deciduous forest with a stream ravine habitat, and which represents a range of different natural and vegetation types from fjord to mountain. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area of particular value for biodiversity, as it is extensive and provides a habitat for many species.”

iselva-naturreservat-nat97298126.d: Iselva Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Narvik municipality. It comprises an area at the southern end of Storvatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a stream gorge. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it provides a habitat for a number of species associated with wet environments. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to enhance them further.

aspa-naturreservat-nat621bc051.d: Aspa Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tingvoll municipality. It comprises an area by the Freifjord. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich deciduous forest. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as the forest is well-developed and provides a habitat for several species with specific requirements. The aim is to preserve the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

kastnesasen-og-gr-nlikollen-naturreserva.d: The Kastnesåsen and Grønlikollen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Dyrøy municipality. It comprises an area by the Faksfjord. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited, and during the period from 1 February to 15 August inclusive, low-altitude flying below 300 metres, as well as the use of drones, model aircraft and the like, is prohibited.

lerheim-naturreservat-nata247363f.d: Lerheim Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rauma municipality. It comprises an area at the innermost part of Rødvenfjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a varied forest area containing threatened and rare natural features in the form of old and well-developed broadleaf forest. The aim is to preserve the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.”

styggvannsdalen-naturreservat-nat02fc24a.d: The Styggvannsdalen Nature Reserve covers most of the Styggvannsdalen valley and the slopes on the western and eastern sides of the valley. The valley lies east-northeast of Losby in Lørenskog municipality. The vegetation consists of mature spruce and pine forest, with large amounts of deadwood in various stages of decomposition in places. Several Red List species have been recorded. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting, trapping and fishing are also permitted in accordance with current legislation. Campfires are only permitted using dry twigs from the ground or wood brought from elsewhere.

knausnakken-naturreservat-nat4fea617d.d: Knusnakken Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vestnes municipality. It comprises an area by Tomrefjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a varied forest area containing threatened and rare natural features in the form of old and well-developed boreal deciduous forest. The aim is to preserve the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

storberget-naturreservat-nat9f1a924f.d: Storberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Narvik municipality. It comprises an area near Skjomen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited, except on the existing path shown on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of calcareous birch forest and aspen-dominated forest. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it provides a habitat for a number of species associated with these forest types.

l-nnsasen-naturreservat-nat674fa768.d: Lønnsåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Nord-Odal municipality. It comprises an area by Lake Storsjøen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old coniferous forest with a high proportion of deadwood. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area that is important for several rare and threatened species of wood-dwelling fungi and lichens. The objective is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where possible, to further develop them.”

ramshylla-naturreservat-nat3040369d.d: Ramshylla Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vanylven municipality. It comprises an area by the Syvdefjord. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing paths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a forest area containing threatened and rare natural habitats in the form of rich deciduous forest. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as the forest provides a habitat for several species with specific requirements. The objective is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

grisetstranda-naturreservat-nat8427795a.d: Grisetstranda Nature Reserve comprises an area on the Innfjord in Rauma municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest area containing threatened and rare natural features in the form of a well-developed, rich deciduous forest with species such as elm and ash.’

torselva-naturreservat-natc6f8362c.d: The Torselva Nature Reserve comprises an area on the south-western side of Innerfjorden in Kanstadfjorden, in the municipality of Lødingen. The area was designated a protected area on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a stream gorge with rich, damp and old deciduous woodland, featuring lichen flora of particular scientific value.’

asli-naturreservat-nat6e75f594.d: Åsli Nature Reserve comprises an area overlooking Dokka Airport, Tomlevold in Nordre Land municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of an old, moist, partly low-lying and highly productive spruce forest with relatively large areas of deadwood, and which also features humid and, in places, rich rock faces. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve a habitat for threatened species within several groups of organisms, particularly lichens.’

buberget-naturreservat-nat815b9ac7.d: The Buberget Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Tinnsjøen in Tinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity due to the presence of calcareous and low-herb pine forests, old pine forests, rich mixed pine forests and spruce forests in the lowlands, as well as occurrences of rare and threatened species of fungi and lichens.’

liberget-naturreservat-nat87a4834c.d: Liberget Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern slope of Liberget, west of Furnesfjorden in Ringsaker. The area is in places very steep, with rock faces, crevices and outcrops. The bedrock is rich in limestone, and the forest consists of spruce, pine, birch, aspen and grey alder. There are also some hawthorns, ash trees, wild hawthorns, European whitebeam and jointed wood. There is also a rich variety of vascular plants and fungi. Of particular interest is the discovery of the grove white-footed fungus (Antrodia malicola) in 2010. It has been found only four times in Norway.

munkerudevja-naturreservat-nat30cbd50c.d: Munkerudevja Nature Reserve is situated at Haga, north of Auli in Nes municipality, Akershus. The reserve lies on marine deposits, 120–145 metres above sea level. The vegetation consists largely of single-layered spruce forest that has been affected by logging. There is also some boreal deciduous woodland, as well as some grazing land. The purpose of the reserve is to conserve a low-lying and highly productive ravine woodland area on marine deposits. This habitat type is rare in an international context.

h-kleberget-naturreservat-nat9b8ef070.d: The Høkleberget Nature Reserve comprises an area by Randsfjorden in the very north of Gran municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of a partly rich and old coniferous forest in the lowlands, dominated by dry vegetation types in a warm microclimate, where there is also, in places, a great deal of deadwood in the form of windfall and snags. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve a habitat for rare and vulnerable species within several groups of organisms. The area has the potential [sic] to provide increased conservation value for threatened, rare and vulnerable species.”

anes-naturreservat-nate1b4b933.d: The Ånes Nature Reserve comprises an area at the mouth of the Kumperudelva river in Randsfjorden, in the municipality of Søndre Land. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a partly old, coarse and rich low-herb spruce forest with windbreaks, and which also contains elements of large, old pine forest. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area containing a very rich and rare soil-dwelling fungal flora, with the presence of many vulnerable and endangered species, as well as several rare and vulnerable bird species. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it contains a rich flora of vascular plants.”

skagelidalen-naturreservat-natf78e06c5.d: Skagelidalen Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Fedafjord in Farsund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a regionally rare occurrence of poor boreonemoral rainforest.’

vakerknatten-og-n-klefjell-naturreservat.d: The Vakerknatten and Nøklefjell Nature Reserve comprises an area west of Songe in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated on 20 June 2023, extended on 20 December 2023, and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich lowland deciduous forest. Low-herb deciduous forest is the dominant vegetation type in the vicinity of Vakerknatten.’

taranli-naturreservat-nat15b14b90.d: The Tårånli Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Vråvatn in Kviteseid municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area of threatened, rare and vulnerable natural features in the form of old spruce forest with elements of tall herbaceous woodland and low-herb woodland, and the presence of rare and threatened species of fungi and lichens. The area is of particular scientific value due to the presence of yew.”

arneslia-naturreservat-nat615f7352.d: Årneslia Nature Reserve consists of a steep hillside on the western side of Losna, near Fåvang Church and Fåvang Nature Reserve in Ringebu municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a varied, rich and old forest with a significant proportion of low-herb forest, tall-shrub forest and rich rock faces and scree slopes, and which in places contains a great deal of deadwood. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve a habitat for threatened and vulnerable species, particularly vascular plants and mosses.’

korpekl-vet-naturreservat-nat9204feff.d: The Korpekløvet Nature Reserve comprises an area at Korpekløvet in Sør-Aurdal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area representing a specific type of natural environment in the form of a partly rich and old coniferous forest in the lowlands, dominated by dry vegetation types in a warm microclimate, where there is also, in places, some deadwood in the form of windfalls and snags. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area containing rare and vulnerable species within several groups of organisms, such as fungi, lichens and vascular plants.”

klippa-naturreservat-nat1790ca7b.d: Klippa Nature Reserve is situated at Hestås, south-west of Lake Fiskumvannet, in Øvre Eiker. The reserve encompasses the summit of the hill and the steep slopes to the south-east. The bedrock is rich in limestone, and there are large areas of largely undisturbed limestone pine forest here. There is also some calcareous spruce forest in the wetter depressions. In places, there are also limestone outcrops and rich fens. A number of Red List species have been recorded in the area, including yew.

svenningvika-naturreservat-nata50b9f1c.d: The Svenningvika Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Storsvenningvatnet, east of the E6 in Grane municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old spruce forest. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for a number of species associated with this type of forest.’

ubergsfjell-naturreservat-nat2222d6d5.d: The Ubergsfjell Nature Reserve comprises an area at Ubergsmoen in Vegårshei municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich deciduous forest. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it contains mature, rich deciduous forest with a high proportion of oak-dominated woodland, as well as deadwood and hollow oaks.”

bj-nndalen-og-kompasmyra-naturreservat-n.d: The Bjønndalen and Kompåsmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Ringsaker municipality. The area was designated on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old spruce forest with mature trees and deadwood. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve occurrences of threatened, vulnerable or rare natural habitats, such as tall-herb spruce forest and hollow-stemmed spruce.”

rykkhustj-nnin-naturreservat-natd62e5332.d: The Rykkhustjønnin Nature Reserve comprises an area in and around the Gudbrandsdalslågen river at Hundorp in the municipality of Sør-Fron. storamyr-naturreservat-nataea0a6f4.d: Storamyr Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sola municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

oppsj-myrene-naturreservat-natf9f5a27e.d: The Oppsjømyrene Nature Reserve consists of five separate, small bog areas in Vardåsmarka in Asker municipality. The bogs are scattered across a gently undulating forested landscape, on calcareous bedrock. Several of the mires also contain small ponds. The mires comprise both precipitation mires and groundwater mires, resulting in a diverse range of vegetation. Several Red Listed plant species are found here, including the very rare bog asphodel.

kraker-y-skj-rgarden-naturreservat-natac.d: The Kråkerøy Archipelago Nature Reserve is situated on the western side of Kråkerøy and comprises 22 islands, islets and skerries, as well as the surrounding sea area and a section of the mainland at Randholmen. The reserve contains several shallow bays and sounds, which are of great importance to foraging waders and ducks. The largest of these soft-bottomed inlets is Gonvad (also known as Nygårdsmoa) in the north-east of the reserve. The reserve encompasses a variety of vegetation types, including salt marshes, bogs, swamps and pine-covered hills. Furthermore, the many islets are of great importance as breeding grounds for seabirds.

steinsbuskardet-hisdal-biotopvernomrade-.d: The Steinsbuskardet-Hisdal biotope conservation area is a 39,900 dekar conservation area designated under the Wildlife Act in the west of Bykle municipality. The area lies south of Blåsjø and also extends eastwards on the southern shore of Botsvatn. The area was designated for conservation on 28 April 2000 and, 15 years later, on 27 April 2015, a management plan for the area was adopted. Regarding the purpose of the conservation, the regulations state: ‘The purpose of the Steinsbuskardet–Hisdal biotope conservation area is to safeguard a particularly important year-round habitat, including migration routes and calving grounds for wild reindeer in Setesdal Vesthei.’

dronningberget-naturreservat-natc7d6ff82.d: Dronningberget is a hill on Bygdøy in the Frogner district of Oslo, which was developed as a park in the 18th century. The restoration and re-establishment of Dronningberget as a park was the Government’s gift to King Harald V and Queen Sonja on their 70th birthdays on 21 February and 4 July 2007 respectively. Dronningberget was designated a nature reserve in 2012.

bj-rn-ya-naturreservat-nat1eb65216.d: The Bjørnøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve whose establishment was approved by the Council of State on 16 August 2002. The nature reserve encompasses the whole of Bjørnøya, including the marine areas extending out to twelve nautical miles. The reserve covers approximately 177 km² of land area (including freshwater) and approximately 2,805 km² of the marine areas surrounding the island. An area of approximately 1,200 dekar around the meteorological station in the north of the island is excluded. In 2011, the reserve was also designated as a Ramsar site.

fugldalen-naturreservat-nat23fa1beb.d: Fugldalen Nature Reserve is situated at Kleivgrend in Fyresdal municipality, approximately 15 km north-west of the northern end of Lake Fyresvatn. To the west, the boundary of the reserve largely follows the county boundary with Agder. The landscape is characterised by large and small valleys with small and large bogs, set amongst partly prominent mountain peaks and ridges. The area has educational and scientific value as a representative high-altitude northern boreal forest and heathland area in the West Telemark/Setesdal region.

kyrelitjern-naturreservat-nat0c49cdd1.d: Kyrelitjønn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Valle municipality. The reserve covers an area of 132 dekar north of Kyrelitjønn, a small lake situated north of County Road 45 on the stretch between Rotemo and Ofte. The nature reserve was established as Kyrelitjern Nature Reserve on 10 October 1986, together with Vestedjan Nature Reserve in Bygland municipality, the Storslåtta Nature Reserve in Evje and Hornnes municipalities, and the Farmyrane and Melandsmyrane Nature Reserves in Iveland municipality. On 19 October 2012, the name was changed to its current one. The purpose of the conservation area is to safeguard species-rich hill bogs. Kyrelitjønn Nature Reserve is one such area, featuring patches of rich bog vegetation.

randvik-store-furu-ya-leiker-ya-naturres.d: The Randvik-Store Furuøya-Leikerøya Nature Reserve comprises an area in the archipelago off Risør in Risør municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a coastal pine forest in Southern Norway. The forest contains several species-poor vegetation types typical of the district, and there is a gradient from more sheltered woodland out towards exposed rocky shores where the pine forest extends far out to sea.”

rosasmyr-og-ospasmyr-naturreservat-nateb.d: The Rosåsmyr and Ospåsmyr Nature Reserve is a 56 dekar nature reserve in Lillesand municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. “The aim of protecting Ospåsmyr is to preserve a groundwater-fed flat mire in this part of the county. For Rosåsmyr, the aim is to preserve the lowest-lying registered initial string bog in the county.” The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. “The reserve consists of two physically separate bog areas located on different map sheets (M711): - Rosåsmyr: 1511 II (36 daa) - Ospåsmyr: 1511 I (22 daa)’ Rosåsmyra lies at an altitude of approximately 134 metres above sea level.

ruholmen-naturreservat-nat26b47b57.d: Ruholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated within Sandøyfjorden in Tvedestrand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

urdvatn-og-kallingshei-naturreservat-nat.d: The Urdvatn and Kallingshei Nature Reserve is a large coniferous forest area on Kallingsheia, in the centre of Åmli municipality in Agder. A small part of the area, near Barlindtjern in the south, was designated a nature reserve in 1996. This is home to what is considered to be the largest stand of yew in inner Agder. The rest of the forest consists of spruce and pine, with patches of rich deciduous and mixed woodland. There are also areas of deciduous broad-leaved woodland. The area is hilly with significant differences in altitude, ranging from the banks of the River Gjøv at just under 200 metres above sea level in the east, to Høgeknatten at 703 metres above sea level in the west. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, and motorised traffic is prohibited.

geislafoss-naturreservat-nata25d2e42.d: Geislafoss Nature Reserve is a protected area in Lyngdal municipality on the border with Lindesnes in Agder. The nature reserve was established on 14 February 2014 and consists of four sub-areas. Three of these are situated on the east bank of the River Audna, whilst the largest sub-area borders the Audna to the west. The area on the west bank of the river is particularly rich in biodiversity. Here there is a rich variety of deciduous broad-leaved woodland of various types. The area to the east lies on the western boundary of the spruce’s natural range and is therefore of educational interest. The nature reserve was extended by 45 daa to the north-east on 11 December 2015.

gaseholmen-og-slettholmen-naturreservat-.d: The Gåseholmen and Slettholmen Nature Reserve comprises the two islands of Gåseholmen and Slettholmen, along with the surrounding skerries and marine areas, in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 March 1980 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. Access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

her-ya-naturreservat-nat26528047.d: Herøya Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Herøyfjord in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. There is a ban on access to the reserve from 15 April to 15 July inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

kjellingen-naturreservat-nat691bfe52.d: The Kjellingen Nature Reserve consists of an island and a number of islets off Kniblingen, comprising three separate areas. It is surrounded by the Oksøy-Ryvingen Landscape Conservation Area and is situated in Lindesnes municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 March 1980 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

songvaar-hellers-ya-og-kubb-ya-naturrese.d: The Songvaar, Hellersøya and Kubbøya Nature Reserve comprises an area off Ny Hellesund in Kristiansand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. There is a ban on access to the reserve from 15 April to 15 July inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

vall-y-naturreservat-nat187af455.d: The Valløy Nature Reserve comprises Valløy, Valløyholmen, Kollholmen and Valløytaklene in Lindesnes municipality. The area lies within the Oksøy-Ryvingen Landscape Conservation Area. It was designated a nature reserve on 28 March 1980 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

vre-og-nedre-svinholmen-naturreservat-na.d: The Upper and Lower Svinholmen Nature Reserve consists of two islets off Andabeløy in Flekkefjord municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

ykjeheia-naturreservat-natab4cf632.d: Øykjeheia Nature Reserve is a woodland reserve in Sirdal municipality in Vest-Agder. The area was designated a protected area in 1993 to preserve a diverse and relatively undisturbed coniferous forest area with a wide variety of habitat types, ecosystems and species. The area was extended in 2014 as part of a voluntary forest conservation scheme and the conservation of properties owned by the Opplysningsvesenet Fund. The total area of the conservation area is now 13,091 daa. In addition to large areas of coniferous forest, the expanded conservation area also comprises rich deciduous forests and coppiced woodland with a large number of old, hollow oak trees. The name of the conservation area has been changed from Øykeheia to Øykjeheia.

lindholmane-naturreservat-natd9f75703.d: The Lindholmane Nature Reserve covers three separate islets at Lindholmane, east of Kjønnøya in Bamble. The conservation area also includes the waters surrounding the islets within a distance of 0–50 metres from the shore. As in many seabird reserves, access is prohibited both on land and at sea in the Lindholmane Nature Reserve from 15 April to 15 July.

lone-naturreservat-natb18981e7.d: Lone Nature Reserve is a large forested area between Lone and Singusdal in Drangedal municipality. The reserve is of particular value as it encompasses all vegetation zones, from the thermophilic boreonemoral zone to the northern boreal zone up towards the mountains. The area also has scientific value due to its great diversity of vascular plants, lichens and fungi, including many rare and endangered fungal species. Parts of the area were first designated as a nature reserve in 2013. It was extended in 2017, but certain pockets within the area remain excluded, including around the southern part of Vihusvatnet. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic is prohibited all year round. Furthermore, cycling and horse riding are prohibited off existing roads and paths.

skrim-og-sauheradfjella-naturreservat-na.d: The Skrim-Sauheradsfjella Nature Reserve is situated in a large forested area on the border between the municipalities of Skien, Midt-Telemark and Notodden in Telemark, and Kongsberg in Buskerud. The reserve covers 123 km², and large parts of it are untouched or virtually untouched. The area provides a habitat for a number of vulnerable and priority species. The highest point in the area is Styggmann (872 metres above sea level).

stavnes-naturreservat-natc9c7c5d3.d: The Stavnes Nature Reserve in Fossingfjorden is a topographically and botanically diverse area, featuring patches of mature coniferous and deciduous woodland and a large number of dead trees at various stages of decomposition. The Torgrimshull archipelago park area forms part of the Stavnes Nature Reserve.

tokkeai-naturreservat-natb51da1ff.d: The Tokkeåi Nature Reserve is situated on the steep slopes along the Tokkeåi river in the municipalities of Tokke and Vinje, and has been extended to include the steep south-facing slopes on both sides of the Berglibekken stream above Dalen. The area has particular educational and scientific value as one of the largest recorded gorge systems in Norway. It is home to an unusually well-developed community of evergreen lichens, rich communities of micro-lichens on elm, and rare and endangered species. The extended area around Berglibekken is characterised by rich vegetation types, including several thermophilic species that are rare this far inland.

karljohansvern-plante-og-dyrefredningsom.d: The Karljohansvern Plant and Animal Conservation Area is situated to the east of the canal in Horten municipality. The area is divided into two zones with different conservation regulations. The zones are separated by the access road to the Naval Society. In the smaller zone, there are several hollow oak trees believed to be many hundreds of years old. Such hollow trees are crucial for biodiversity. In this area, 27 different species of beetle have been found; all are on the Red List, and two of them have not previously been recorded in Norway. In the larger zone, limited felling takes place in accordance with an approved management plan. Here, mistletoe can be found in the tree crowns, and there is a rich variety of birdlife.

melsom-plante-og-dyrefredningsomrade-nat.d: The Melsom Plant and Animal Conservation Area is a protected area, which in turn consists of two sections. The largest is situated at the innermost part of Melsombukta, featuring oak trees and other broad-leaved trees. The smaller one consists of five large oak trees on a ridge on the south-facing slope. The areas are protected because of their great biodiversity, particularly in terms of insects. The oak is often referred to as a ‘habitat object’. This means that, throughout its life, the tree provides a range of different habitats for various organisms, particularly insects, fungi and lichens. Old oak trees can be home to up to 1,500 different species.

m-len-fuglefredningsomrade-natf0bd7f39.d: The Mølen Bird Sanctuary covers the waters around the Mølen Peninsula, from the western side of Oddane to Omlidrogn and north to Arøya and Stokkøya. Sauesundsholmen and Fugløya are included within the area. The bird sanctuary encompasses the Fugløyrogn Nature Reserve and the Låven Natural Monument; separate regulations apply to these two protected areas. The Mølen Bird Sanctuary was established in 1981. Mølen is one of Norway’s finest birding sites and forms part of the Gea Norvegica Geopark. Mølen’s beaches and mudflats are vital for birds during the spring and autumn migrations. At Mølen, the birds can rest and feed before setting off on the next leg of their journey. Mølen is also an important wintering area for waterbirds.

bj-nnesholmen-biotopvernomrade-nat3d887d.d: The Bjønnesholmen biotope conservation area in Viksfjord is a very important breeding ground for common gulls. On the north side of Bjønnesholmen, facing Flatholmen, there is a shallow-water area. The breeding population on Bjønnesholmen must be considered in conjunction with the breeding population on Flatholmen. Bjønnesholmen is a low islet in Viksfjord east of Bjønnes, approximately 2.3 km south of Tjølling Church. The eastern part of the islet consists of loose sediment with meadow vegetation, whilst the central and western parts have more rocky outcrops (syenite) and some shrub vegetation. To the north of the islet are shallow water areas. The highest point is 6 metres above sea level.

hemskilen-fuglefredningsomrade-nat092261.d: The Hemskilen Wildlife Sanctuary and Nature Reserve is a regionally important foraging and rearing area for waterbirds during the breeding season, and a stopover and resting place for ducks, waders, geese and passerines during migration. The protected area lies partly in Sandefjord and partly in Larvik municipality, just off Storøya. Hemskilen is a shallow brackish water delta. The Hemskilen Nature Reserve was established in 1981 and consists largely of water bodies and mudflats. The Hemskilen Bird Sanctuary was established in 2009 as a buffer zone around the Hemskilen Nature Reserve. All hunting is prohibited within the bird sanctuary.

kviljo-plantefredningsomrade-nat4c697182.d: The Kviljo Plant Conservation Area and the Kviljo Plant and Bird Conservation Area are protected habitats in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The areas cover 0.8 km² and 3.0 km² respectively. The areas were designated in 1987, and the larger of the two has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect a rich and varied flora and the abundant birdlife. The area contains the longest continuous stretch of sand dunes on Lista. The sand dunes are particularly imposing, rising to a height of 5 m. Kviljoodden juts out into the sea, and many migratory birds, particularly waders, use Kviljoodden as their final resting place before leaving the country.

skardberga-naturreservat-natfb095e38.d: Skardberga Nature Reserve is situated in Synnfjellet in the municipalities of Nordre Land and Gausdal. The nature reserve covers 11,641 daa and was designated on 11 March 2011. Skardberga features undulating terrain with old mountain spruce forest. Rare plants, lichens and mosses grow here. The area boasts a wide variety of vegetation, woodland and habitat types, including wetlands. The reserve is considered representative of mountain spruce forest in the region. The nature reserve also contains an old, disused slate quarry, which was used for the local extraction of slate for roofing. Skardberga Nature Reserve borders Langsua National Park and is included in its conservation plan.

granosmyrane-naturreservat-nat0c427fe6.d: Grånosmyrane Nature Reserve is an area of approximately 3.4 km² situated in Aurland municipality in Sogn og Fjordane and Voss municipality in Hordaland. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 1995 due to its rich and vulnerable birdlife in a mountainous and wetland area. At the heart of the area lies Vassetelvi, which is surrounded by marshes and small lakes.
