Both waders and passerines, such as the snow bunting, Lapland bunting, dunlin, red-necked phalarope, rock pipit, golden plover and rock ptarmigan, breed in the nature reserve. The area is adjacent to the Nærøyfjord Landscape Conservation Area and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List as part of the West Norwegian Fjord Landscape in 2005.

steglholmen-og-gaseskjer-naturreservat-n.d: The Steglholmen and Gåseskjer Nature Reserve comprises Gåseskjer and parts of Steglholmen, situated close to Strandvik in the municipality of Bjørnafjorden. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (28 June): Common gull 20 pairs (350 in 1979), Ringed plover 2 pairs.

raun-y-lang-y-skardholmen-storholmen-og-.d: The Raunøy, Langøy, Skardholmen, Storholmen and Høgholmen Nature Reserve comprises a number of islets and parts of islands near Holsøya. The nature reserve is situated in Masfjorden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Registered breeding species in 2014: Black-backed Gull 2 pairs, Common Gull 2 pairs, Greylag Goose 5 pairs, Lapwing 1 pair.

tjongspollen-naturreservat-nata982c69b.d: Tjongspollen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bømlo municipality. It comprises an area on and around Bømlo. The nature reserve borders Sagvatnet Nature Reserve to the north and Skogafjellet Nature Reserve to the south, both of which were designated on 17 December 1999. The area was designated on 21 June 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Outside existing tractor tracks, the use of bicycles, horses and carts, as well as horse riding, is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard rare and vulnerable natural habitats within a larger, unspoilt forest and coastal landscape free from significant human intervention’.

sandholmane-ysteinen-og-hesjeta-naturres.d: The Sandholmane, Øysteinen and Hesjetå Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets and skerries between the islands of Fedje and Radøy. The nature reserve is situated in Alver municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ According to the 2015 management plan, there has been little breeding activity in the area for some time.

kvernholmen-og-rosmunnen-naturreservat-n.d: The Kvernholmen and Rosmunnen Nature Reserve consists of two islets to the west of Tofterøy in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (6 July): Black-backed Gull 37 pairs, Grey Gull 105 pairs, Herring Gull 9 pairs, Oystercatcher 1 pair, Eider 150 individuals.

litle-gas-y-skarv-y-og-store-lambholmen-.d: The Litle Gåsøy, Skarvøy and Store Lambholmen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Telavåg in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (6 July): Black-backed Gull 5 pairs, Grey Gull 14 pairs, Lesser Black-backed Gull 15 pairs, Oystercatcher 1 pair, Eider 1 brood, White-tailed Eagle 1 pair in the immediate vicinity.

ku-yni-skag-yni-teistholmen-og-teistholm.d: The Kuøyni, Skagøyni, Teistholmen and Teistholmskjeret Nature Reserve comprises two islands, a islet and a skerry off Rongevær in Austrheim municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014: Black-tailed Godwit 2 pairs, Lapwing 3 pairs.

kortknappskjer-og-hors-y-naturreservat-n.d: Kortknappskjer and Horsøy Nature Reserve comprises the southern part of Horsøyna and a skerry. It is situated in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ No breeding species were recorded in 2014.

litle-frils-y-hovden-svarteskjeret-og-in.d: The Litle Frilsøy, Hovden, Svarteskjeret and Innesøyane Nature Reserve consists of a group of islands, islets and skerries out at sea to the north-west of Fedje in Fedje municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Registered breeding species in 2014 (18.

otter-y-og-hestholmen-naturreservat-natb.d: The Otterøy and Hestholmen Nature Reserve comprises part of Otterøy and Hestholmen in Bømlo municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Species recorded as breeding in 2014 were: Black-backed Gull (11 pairs with chicks), Common Tern (8 pairs), Lesser Black-backed Gull (6 pairs), Herring Gull (10 pairs) and Ringed Plover (2 pairs).

havarden-og-klubben-naturreservat-nat8c5.d: The Håvarden and Klubben Nature Reserve comprises part of Håvarden and a nearby islet. The nature reserve is situated close to Mongstad in Alver municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014: Black-tailed Godwit, 1 pair.

hillekalven-og-pasholmen-naturreservat-n.d: The Hillekalven and Pasholmen Nature Reserve consists of islets and skerries off Hille in Klosterfjorden, in Kvinnherad municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (7 July): Black-backed Gull 3 pairs, Common Tern 1 pair (100 in 1980), Lapwing 1 pair, Greylag Goose 4 individuals on the main island of Hille.

geitaknottane-naturreservat-nat1fb913a2.d: The Geitaknottene Nature Reserve is situated on the peninsula between Hardangerfjorden to the east and Bjørnafjorden to the west. The aim of the conservation area is to preserve an unspoilt area stretching from lowland to mountain, home to both flora and fauna. The highest point is Gravdalshorga, at 673 metres above sea level. The tree line here is around 500 metres above sea level, though in places it is considerably lower. The reserve is home to by far the largest population of great crested newts (Triturus cristatus) in Norway, and probably in the whole world. The great crested newt is listed as Vulnerable (VU) on the Red List.

flu-yane-med-flu-yskjeret-lyng-y-vees-ya.d: The Fluøyane archipelago, comprising Fluøyskjeret, Lyngøy, Veesøyane and the Terneskjeret Nature Reserve, consists of a group of islands north of Tysnesøya in Tysnes municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area’. This is one of the most important areas for seabirds and is currently a national research area for the grey gull and the lesser black-backed gull.

bleiken-vlingen-og-h-gskjeret-naturreser.d: The Bleikenøvlingen and Høgskjeret Nature Reserve consists of two islets west of Seløy in Øygarden municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (18 June) Black-backed Gull 4 pairs, Grey Gull 130 pairs, Herring Gull 6 pairs, Red-billed Tern 15 pairs, Great Cormorant 12 pairs, Oystercatcher 4 pairs, Black Guillemot 6 individuals on 9 July.

aksnesholmane-naturreservat-nat16f06602.d: The Aksnesholmane Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets off Aksnes, near Norheimsund in Kvam municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. According to the 2015 management plan, these islets were protected as early as 1923, making them Norway’s first nature reserve. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (27.

utslette-y-jo-y-og-ups-ykalven-naturrese.d: The Utsletteøy, Joøy and Upsøykalven Nature Reserve comprises three islets north-west of Espevær in Bømlo municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (6 July): Black-backed Gull 2 pairs, Grey Gull 2 pairs, Great Cormorant 30 individuals, Black Guillemot 4 individuals

vestre-og-indre-magab-l-myrb-rholmen-og-.d: The Vestre and Indre Mågabøl, Myrbærholmen and Kvitingen nature reserves comprise a number of islands and islets to the west of Møkster in Austevoll municipality. The birdlife on Myrbærholmen was protected as early as 1953. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to preserve an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (6.

vagsholmen-gulaskjer-brattholmen-og-gras.d: The Vågsholmen, Gulaskjer, Brattholmen and Grasholmen Nature Reserve comprises five islets between Strøno and Søre Øyane in the municipality of Bjørnafjorden. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ Recorded breeding species in 2014 (28 June): Common gull 7 pairs (48 pairs in 1979), Lesser black-backed gull 2 pairs, Black-tailed godwit 1 pair, Arctic tern 1 pair.

hovs-y-laters-y-melne-melneklubben-lyngs.d: The Hovsøy, Låtersøy, Melne, Melneklubben, Lyngsøy, Oksøy and Raudholmane Nature Reserve (also known as Sørøyane) consists of seven islets east of Ryvarden Lighthouse in Bømlo municipality. The area was designated as one of 69 nature reserves in what was then Hordaland County on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’ The 2014 management plan states that the nature reserve “is currently, without parallel, the most important seabird area in Hordaland.”

einevarden-naturreservat-nat514feb6d.d: The Einevarden Nature Reserve encompasses what was once the largest seabird colony in Sogn og Fjordane. Breeding activity here has now declined. The reserve is situated on Vågsøy in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 May 1993 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.’ Confirmed breeding species include the fulmar, shag, grey gull, black-backed gull, razorbill, guillemot, puffin and kittiwake.

nordheimsdalen-naturreservat-nat86e92cb1.d: The Nordheimsdalen Nature Reserve covers an area of around 13 km² and is situated in the municipalities of Aurland and Lærdal in Vestland County. The forest area, with all its flora and fauna, was designated a nature reserve on 17 December 1999. The valley is a hanging valley formed during the last ice age. The area features woodland stretching from the fjord to the mountains and boasts a great diversity of pine forest types, some of which have the character of primeval forest. The timber from the forest has been used for local building projects. There are a number of traces of timber harvesting in the area, such as the road leading up from the quay. The area has also been used for grazing and mountain farming on Øygarden and in Nordheimsdalen.

bleia-naturreservat-nat1744513d.d: Bleia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lærdal municipality covering an area of 21.8 km². The reserve is listed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List as part of the West Norwegian Fjord Landscape. The nature reserve is characterised by Mount Bleia, which rises 1,717 metres from the Sognefjord. Bleia is the highest peak in the outer part of the peninsula between the Sognefjord and the Aurlandsfjord. Beneath it, Bleia overlooks a magnificent fjord landscape with deep gorges and mountain ridges, and is a landmark in the Sognefjord. The reserve borders the Bleia-Storebotnen Landscape Conservation Area. The greatest natural asset is the population of the relict poppy (Papaver radicatum ssp. relictum) at Indste Drøfti below Bleia. The relict poppy grows in only two locations in Norway.

dr-gnismorki-yttrismorki-naturreservat-n.d: The Drægnismorki-Yttrismorki Nature Reserve comprises an area near Skjolden in Luster municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 11 December 2015 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of particular value for biological and geological diversity in the form of special habitat types, species occurrences and landforms in as natural a state as possible. This is a large and varied pine forest area on phyllite bedrock with distinctive hydrology linked to post-glacial faults and large boulder fields, dense and mature pine forest and broad-leaved deciduous forest, and high biological productivity.

nigardsbreen-naturreservat-natfdfe3138.d: The Nigardsbreen Nature Reserve comprises an area near the Nigardsbreen glacier in Luster municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 July 1985. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a distinctive valley with a well-developed glacial margin zone that is of great value for the study of glacial variations throughout history, glacial and glacial river activity, and plant succession.’

ramsholmen-naturreservat-nateff45bf0.d: Ramsholmen Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets north of Leknøyna in Solund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the eider, oystercatcher, common sandpiper, Arctic skua, black-headed gull, grey gull and black-backed gull.

r-nset-naturreservat-nat76a52767.d: Rønset Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Sørefjord in Hyllestad municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 19 June 2009 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests/rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a forest area with special habitat types, including the full diversity of species and vegetation types and all natural ecological processes. The area has particular scientific and educational value as one of the most well-developed hazel forests in Outer Western Norway, with a wide range of environments from dry to damp, spring-fed broadleaf forests and interesting species occurrences.”

haukedalsholmane-naturreservat-nat7e29e0.d: The Haukedalsholmane Nature Reserve consists of three islets and a few smaller skerries south of Rugsundøy in Bremanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the eider, goldeneye, mallard, lesser black-backed gull, grey gull, black-tailed godwit, common gull, common tern and red-billed tern.

nekk-ytaa-naturreservat-nat67cba1d0.d: The Nekkøytåa Nature Reserve comprises three areas between Florø and Reksta in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the shore is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally associated vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the lesser black-backed gull, herring gull, greylag goose, eider, common goldeneye, oystercatcher, redshank, little curlew, common snipe, turnstone, black-headed gull and black-tailed godwit.

utv-r-naturreservat-natd47b4ead.d: Utvær Nature Reserve comprises an area surrounding the fishing village of Utvær, including Utvær Lighthouse, in Solund municipality. The fishing village itself, including the lighthouse, is not included within the protected area. The area was designated a nature reserve on 28 May 1993 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the great cormorant, greylag goose, eider, shelduck, oystercatcher, turnstone, redshank, the Arctic skua, the common gull, the grey gull, the black-backed gull, the black guillemot, the red-billed tern, the common tern, the guillemot, the razorbill, the puffin and the kittiwake.

lihellene-naturreservat-nat6a1f2796.d: Lihellene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gulen municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect breeding seabirds in the archipelago in Lake Sognesjøen. This bird sanctuary is situated slightly further east in Lake Sognesjøen than the four other bird sanctuaries in the municipality, close to the mainland towards the mouth of the Sognefjord. The area covers 403 dekar, of which 107 daa is land and 296 daa is water. In 1993, the Government adopted the Seabird Conservation Plan, which designated 57 bird sanctuaries totalling 11 km² along the coast of Sogn og Fjordane. The plan is based on the initial conservation proposals from 1977, as well as White Paper No.

indrev-r-naturreservat-natb277d3ef.d: Indrevær Nature Reserve comprises an area off Ytre Sula in Solund municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally associated vegetation and wildlife’. Confirmed breeding species include the greylag goose, eider, wigeon, mallard, oystercatcher, little curlew, turnstone, redshank, dunlin, spotted skua, common gull, grey gull, lesser black-backed gull, black-tailed godwit, red-necked phalarope, turnstone, redshank, common sandpiper, common tern, Arctic tern, black-headed gull and black-tailed godwit.

s-restrandvatnet-naturreservat-natf3fe8c.d: The Sørestrandvatnet Nature Reserve comprises an area north of the Sognefjord in Høyanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 20 December 1991 and is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with its natural vegetation and wildlife, particularly in view of the area’s value as a migration and breeding site for wetland birds.’

s-rdalen-naturreservat-nata44b2421.d: Sørdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bremanger municipality that was designated on 17 December 1999. In May 2013, permission was granted for a power line to be built through the area, a decision that was highly controversial. The nature reserve is divided into two parts by County Road 614 between Svelgen and Ålfoten. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve pine forest with an unusually strong character of primeval forest.

fimreiteholmane-naturreservat-nat6080626.d: The Fimreiteholmane Nature Reserve comprises an area near Fimreite in Sogndal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is “to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.”

klovningen-naturreservat-nat99fc7da4.d: The Klovningen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Vågsøy in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the island is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.’ Confirmed breeding species include the common murre, shag, eider, oystercatcher, turnstone, black guillemot, grey gull, black-backed gull, razorbill, guillemot, puffin and kittiwake.

eikefjordholmane-naturreservat-natd5eb2e.d: The Eikefjordholmane Nature Reserve consists of three areas comprising islets at the innermost part of Eikefjorden in Kinn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is: ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.’

fimreiteasen-naturreservat-natf755f9bb.d: The Fimreiteåsen Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Sognefjord in Sogndal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 December 2015 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a large, contiguous natural area stretching from the fjord to the mountain forest, which is of particular value for biodiversity and which contains rare and endangered species. The aim is to preserve this area in as undisturbed a state as possible, with the full range of habitat types found there, which are of great value to many groups of plants, fungi and animals, and as a reference area for natural forest with natural regeneration dynamics.

sogneoksen-naturreservat-nat3c67819c.d: Sogneoksen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve (bird sanctuary) in Gulen municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect breeding seabirds on the islets in Lake Sognesjøen. The area covers 137 dekar, of which 27 daa is land and 110 daa is water. In 1993, the Government adopted the Seabird Conservation Plan, which designated 57 bird sanctuaries totalling 11 km² along the coast of Sogn og Fjordane. The plan is based on the initial conservation proposals from 1977, as well as White Paper No. 68 (1980–81) ‘Conservation of Norwegian Nature’, which set out the objective of conserving a representative selection of natural areas in Norway, and the first consultation proposal on seabird conservation in Sogn og Fjordane from 1984. Between 1977 and 1988, 350 seabird sites in the county were surveyed and assessed.

kvitingane-naturreservat-nat77d4fd99.d: The Kvitingane Nature Reserve comprises around 30 islands, islets and skerries in Vilnesfjorden in Askvoll municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding, migration and wintering site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.’ Confirmed breeding species include the greylag goose, eider, mallard, wigeon, oystercatcher, lapwing, turnstone, Arctic skua, common gull, grey gull, black-backed gull, common tern and red-billed tern.

storholmen-naturreservat-natc4443b8c.d: The Storholmen Nature Reserve comprises an area just west of the Vadheimsfjord in Høyanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 May 1993 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to provide seabirds with good and safe living conditions, and to preserve an important breeding site for seabirds with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife.’

surna-naturreservat-natd627daef.d: Surna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Surnadal municipality. It comprises an area at the mouth of the Surna river, at the innermost part of Surnadalsfjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 May 1988. The reserve is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife.’

mardalen-naturreservat-nat52996bca.d: Mardalen Nature Reserve is a protected area in Molde municipality in Møre og Romsdal. The protected area was established in 2014 and subsequently extended. Following the expansion, which took place on 23 June 2026, the nature reserve now covers a total of 6,390 daa.

raud-ya-landskapsvernomrade-nat42e47ff8.d: The Raudøya Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area with protected plant life, situated in Ørsta municipality in Møre og Romsdal. The area was established in 2000 and covers 0.371 km². The landscape conservation area was established to protect cultural and natural landscapes featuring holly. The area has a large and thriving population of holly. Raudøya is also referred to as ‘den Øe Primsignd’, which, according to Snorre Sturlasson, was the site of the Battle of Hjørungavåg. Raudøya Nature Reserve is situated on the same island.

vassgardsvatnet-naturreservat-nate515965.d: Vassgårdsvatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hustadvika municipality. It comprises an area near Eide. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 May 1988. The reserve is included in the wetland conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an important wetland area with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife’. The reserve borders the Svanvikmyra Nature Reserve, which was designated on 13 December 1996 under the conservation plan for mires. On the other side of the bog area, separated by power lines, some buildings and a road, lies the Einsetvågen/Nåsvatnet wildlife sanctuary. This wildlife sanctuary was also designated on 27 May 1988.

svanvikmyra-naturreservat-nat9ca78729.d: Svanvikmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hustadvika municipality. It comprises an area south of Eide. The reserve borders the Vassgårdsvatnet Nature Reserve to the south, and the Einsetvågen/Nåsvatnet Wildlife Sanctuary lies close by to the north. The area was designated a nature reserve on 13 December 1996. The reserve is included in the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a large and varied mire complex of conservation value as a nationally representative area’.

knarrashaugmyra-naturreservat-nat57d75a9.d: Knarrashaugmyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hustadvika municipality. It borders the Sandblåst/Gaustadvågen Nature Reserve to the north and west. The area was designated a nature reserve on 13 December 1996. The reserve is part of the conservation plan for mires. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a small raised bog area of value as a regional example of its type, and as a supplement to the adjacent Sandblåstvågen/Gaustadvågen wetland reserve.’

sandblast-gaustadvagen-naturreservat-nat.d: The Sandblåst/Gaustadvågen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hustadvika municipality in Møre og Romsdal. The nature reserve comprises a continuous estuary – that is, an almost enclosed fjord arm or river delta – with two large basins into which the Sandblåstelva flows. The reserve was established in 1988 to ‘preserve an important wetland area’. In 1996, it was designated a Ramsar site due to its importance for migratory birds. The protected area is the county’s most distinctive estuary and is of conservation interest in several fields: botany, zoology, landscape and Quaternary geology. There are extensive tidal zones and salt marshes here, with a rich and, in part, unique diversity of species.

hyskjet-naturreservat-nat8c3af6a8.d: Hyskjet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Stranda municipality. It comprises an area by the Geirangerfjord. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 June 2003. The reserve is part of the conservation plan for deciduous broad-leaved forests. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve one of the best-developed areas of broad-leaved deciduous forest in the fjord region of Sunnmøre, together with its natural flora and fauna.’

raud-ya-naturreservat-nate92563f9.d: Raudøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on Raudøya in Ørsta municipality in Møre og Romsdal. The nature reserve was established by royal decree on 13 October 2000. The nature reserve covers 90 daa and was established to protect a particularly vigorous stand of holly in the south of Raudøya. The rest of Raudøya was designated as the Raudøya Landscape Conservation Area on the same day.

muldalslia-naturreservat-natd54a4cf4.d: Muldalslia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Fjord municipality. It comprises an area right next to Tafjord, at the innermost part of Tafjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 June 2003. The reserve forms part of the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests rich in species. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and riding off existing roads are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a highly species-rich, thermophilic deciduous forest habitat with its natural flora and fauna’. At least 160 vascular plants have been recorded. Notable species include barberry, mountain avens, bridal veil, dwarf medlar, pine wintergreen, sweet woodruff, sanicle, spring snowflake, golden saxifrage, mountain thistle, giant fescue and spring snowflake.

s-r-sm-la-landskapsvernomrade-nat8fa3c7c.d: The Sør-Smøla Landscape Conservation Area is a protected area in Smøla municipality. The flora and fauna in the area are protected. The area is a coastal cultural landscape with plant communities dominated by grasses and herbs, alongside areas of heather moorland and salt marshes, typical of grazing lands. Several fishing villages are situated in the area, lending it significant cultural and historical value. It is also a rich marine area with abundant kelp forests and seaweed beds. There are bays, inlets and ponds ranging from pure salt water through brackish water to pure fresh water. This makes the area rich in seabirds, otters and white-tailed eagles. In winter, large numbers of birds stay in the area. The area is also characterised by local overgrowth, feral mink and large amounts of litter along the beaches.

vesteinvika-naturreservat-natbbdf8831.d: Vesteinvika Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Haram municipality. It comprises an area at Stavneset on the western side of Haramsøya. The area was designated a nature reserve on 8 November 2002. The reserve forms part of the conservation plan for seashores and river mouths. Cycling and horse riding off existing paths are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a species-rich, long gravel and pebble beach which is a special area for one of the best occurrences of oysterweed and sea rocket in the county, as well as to safeguard a landscape rich in archaeological remains.’ To the north, the reserve borders the Haramsøya West Side Nature Reserve.

sand-ya-vatt-ya-naturreservat-natb92320d.d: The Sandøya-Vattøya Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Ulsteinfjord in Ulstein municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 August 2010 (approved on 28 May 2010) as one of 36 reserves in Møre og Romsdal. The reserve forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 31 July inclusive, access to land within the protected area is prohibited. The reserve borders the Flø wildlife sanctuary. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to safeguard an area of particular value for biodiversity and which contains threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats’.

fl-rauden-naturreservat-nat113ad819.d: Flørauden Nature Reserve consists of a group of skerries north of Flø in Ulstein municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 August 2010 (approved on 28 May 2010) as one of 36 reserves in Møre og Romsdal. The reserve forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 31 July inclusive, access to land within the protected area is prohibited. The reserve is situated within the Flø wildlife sanctuary. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to safeguard an area of particular value for biodiversity and which contains threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats. The area consists of a group of unspoilt small islets facing the open sea, sheltered shallow-water basins with seaweed banks, and the surrounding marine area.

harams-ya-vestside-naturreservat-nat895f.d: The Haramsøya West Side Nature Reserve consists of a west-facing mountainside at the westernmost point of Haramsøya in Haram municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 1 August 2010 (approved on 28 May 2010) as one of 36 reserves in Møre og Romsdal. The reserve forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 31 July inclusive, access to the protected area by land is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard an area of particular value for biodiversity and which contains threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats’.

gims-ymyrene-naturreservat-nat068c6e28.d: The Gimsøymyrene Nature Reserve is situated on Gimsøya in Vågan municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 6,400 dekar, of which 4,900 dekar is marshland and 1,700 dekar (?) consists of shallow water areas and saltwater areas. The area is protected to preserve a diverse mire landscape comprising several different types of mire and adjacent wetland areas.

borgv-ret-naturreservat-natdcf48fc5.d: Borgværet Nature Reserve is situated in Vestvågøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises several small islands north of Vestvågøya. It covers an area of 9,842 dekar, of which 9,377 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard a valuable coastal area which, amongst other things, serves as a breeding and wintering ground for seabirds. The Borgværet Landscape Conservation Area is also situated within this area.

lofotodden-naturreservat-nat55442e79.d: The Lofotodden Nature Reserve is situated just west of Lofotodden in Moskenes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses Nordholmen and Sørholmen, as well as a number of smaller islets and skerries. The area covers 688 dekar, of which 504 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds.

mastadfjellet-landskapsvernomrade-nat284.d: The Måstadfjellet Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area and a Ramsar site on the island of Værøy in Værøy municipality, Nordland. The area was designated to ‘preserve a distinctive natural and cultural landscape, safeguard the zoological, geological and cultural-historical features that contribute to the area’s distinctive character, and protect the botanical species associated with Sanden.’ The Måstadfjellet Landscape Conservation Area covers 5,145 dekar – of which 3,210 dekar is marine area – and borders the Måstadfjellet Nature Reserve to the west. The nature reserve comprises the western, steep part of Værøy. The landscape conservation area encompasses Måstad Bay, with the exception of the old settlement and farmland in the hamlet of Måstad.

mastadfjellet-naturreservat-natc0c32fdd.d: Måstadfjellet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site on the island of Værøy in Værøy municipality, Nordland. The reserve was established to ‘preserve a valuable coastal area, with its naturally associated flora and fauna. Particular value is attached to the area’s function as a breeding ground for a number of seabird species.’ The nature reserve comprises the western, steep part of Værøy and covers an area of 2,870 dekar, of which 817 dekar is marine area. The entire south-western part of Værøy is an important breeding ground for seabirds. Throughout the area, there are good populations of breeding seabird species, such as the puffin, black guillemot, razorbill and guillemot. To a somewhat lesser extent, there are also fulmars and shags.

nykan-naturreservat-nata97c4b6b.d: Nykan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and a Ramsar site in the archipelago and municipality of Røst in Lofoten, Nordland. The nature reserve comprises the three bird cliffs of Ellevsnyken, Trenyken and Hernyken, as well as a number of smaller islets and skerries associated with these islands. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,055 daa, of which 574 daa is marine area and is protected to safeguard the most important breeding sites for seabirds. The Nykan Nature Reserve lies within the Røstøyan Landscape Conservation Area, which also includes, amongst other things, the two larger bird cliffs, Vedøy and Storfjellet. Together with these two major bird cliffs, the Nykan Nature Reserve constitutes the most significant breeding site for puffins in Norway.

r-st-yan-landskapsvernomrade-nat49f94430.d: The Røstøyan Landscape Conservation Area was established in 2002 and is situated in Røst municipality in Nordland. The area is a wildlife sanctuary and covers an area of 69,864 daa, of which 66,929 daa is marine area. The landscape conservation area was established on account of its natural and cultural landscape, including its botany, geology and wildlife, and is protected under the 2011 Ramsar Convention. Within the landscape conservation area, Norway’s largest population of puffins (Fratercula arctica) nests on the five important seabird islands of Vedøya, Storfjellet, Ellevsnyken, Trenyken and Hernyken. On Hernyken, there is also a dedicated field station used for research into seabirds.

floholman-naturreservat-nat87303e2c.d: Floholman Nature Reserve is situated to the west of Skogsøya in Øksnes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 891 dekar, of which 732 dekar is water. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds, particularly puffins.

morfjorden-naturreservat-nat004ed71f.d: Morfjorden Nature Reserve is situated in Hadsel municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve is located at Sommarhus in Morfjorden on Austvågøya. The area covers 358 dekar, of which 54 dekar is water. The area has been designated a nature reserve to safeguard a large and unique area of intact, well-established dune vegetation.

gap-ya-naturreservat-nat24792b34.d: Gapøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the north-western part of Kvæfjord municipality in Troms. The nature reserve covers most of Gapøya, which is situated at the mouth of Kvæfjorden. It covers an area of 4,399 dekar, consisting mainly of deciduous woodland, open land and marshland. The southernmost and formerly inhabited part of the island is not part of the nature reserve. The nature reserve was established on 27 August 1976 with the aim of conducting reindeer experiments, involving the introduction of Svalbard reindeer from 1975 to 1977. The aim is to protect the island – which is an important breeding ground for species including gulls, great cormorants and grouse – and its flora and fauna. One kilometre north-east of Gapøya lies the Gapøyholman Nature Reserve.

flat-ya-landskapsvernomrade-nat618a5518.d: The Flatøya Landscape Conservation Area is a landscape conservation area in the northern part of Harstad municipality in Troms. The area encompasses large parts of Flatøya, including neighbouring islets and skerries, and Kvitholmen, approximately one kilometre east of Flatøya. It has a total area of 1,468 dekar, of which 839 dekar consists of land and 364 dekar consists of marshland. The landscape conservation area was established on 4 June 2004 to preserve the natural and cultural landscape and its wildlife. Of the approximately one hundred bird species recorded on Flatøya and in the surrounding marine area, around 45 are breeding species. The vegetation consists mainly of rain-fed bogs, nutrient-poor bogs, heather moorland, woodland and, on Kvitholmen, herb-rich grassland.

eikeland-naturreservat-nat7ec1a4d6.d: Eikeland Nature Reserve is situated in Andøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve consists of a mire area by the Buksnesfjord on Hinnøya. The area covers 9,100 dekar, of which 1,400 dekar is water. The area has been protected to preserve a site featuring interesting types of bog and a diverse flora, and to safeguard a habitat for the river pearl mussel. Adjacent to the Eikeland Nature Reserve lies the Eikefjelldalen Landscape Conservation Area. Both the nature reserve and the landscape conservation area were designated in 1983.

skogvoll-naturreservat-nat960a3307.d: Skogvoll Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Andøy municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve is situated at Skogvoll on the north side of Andøya, both along the coast and in a marshland area within Skogvollvatnet, and has had Ramsar site status since 2002, due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1983 to preserve a large and important wetland area with its associated flora and fauna, particularly in view of the protected marshlands and the rich birdlife. The area covers approximately 55 km², of which around 30 km² is water. It contains several different types of bog and plant species, and exhibits great morphological and vegetational diversity.

lundsneset-naturreservat-nat5c1d99f1.d: The Lundsneset Nature Reserve covers 26 km² and is the largest protected area in Østfold. The area lies within the municipalities of Halden and Aremark and borders Tresticklan National Park on the Swedish side to the east. In 2013, the nature reserve was extended to also include the part of Søndre Boksjø that lies in Norway. Søndre Boksjø is home to an interesting variety of birdlife. Among other species, ospreys, black-throated divers and goosanders nest on the islets in the lake.

skaarnja-naturreservat-natfaaa2659.d: Skåarnja is a nature reserve in Strömsund Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden. The area has been a nature reserve since 2017 and covers 366 square kilometres.

eld-ya-sletter-landskapsvernomrade-nat59.d: The Eldøya-Sletter Landscape Conservation Area is situated in the municipalities of Moss and Råde in Østfold County. The area was established in 1997, has protected flora and covers 12,649 dekar of land, of which 11,017 dekar is water. The landscape conservation area was established to preserve the natural and cultural landscape of the area, where the Quaternary geology and botany are of particular interest. The land areas within the landscape conservation area consist of five islands and a peninsula. Farthest to the north lies the island of Kollen, which is largely covered in forest and scrub. Next comes Eldøya, which consists of a mosaic of woodland, scrub and open meadows. There is also a small lake here. At the north-eastern tip of the island is a sandy beach where boats can moor.

rambergasen-naturreservat-nat4d20830c.d: Rambergåsen Nature Reserve is situated in the centre of Jeløya in Moss municipality, Østfold. The reserve was established in 2018 and expanded in 2023. The purpose of the reserve is to conserve an area with varied, rich forest types, including ‘spruce forest with abundant low-growing herbaceous vegetation, calcareous pine forest, blueberry pine and oak forest, elm and lime forest, fern forest and rich swamp forest’. Biodiversity is high; 21 tree species have been recorded, along with at least ten Red List species of plants and animals.

sanda-og-henestangen-naturreservat-nat3c.d: The Sandå and Henestangen Nature Reserve comprises Henestangen and the Lefseholmene islets to the south-east of Lake Vansjø, as well as an area around Sandå on the eastern shore of the lake, Tombøya and the north-eastern part of Gressøya. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a large and relatively undisturbed area of forest and landscape representing poor to moderately rich forest types with spruce and pine in low-lying areas below the marine limit in the bedrock region of south-eastern Norway. The bedrock consists mainly of gneiss, which has a low buffering capacity and results in relatively acidic soil. The vegetation comprises various types of spruce and pine forest.

lagendeltaet-naturreservat-nat50ef7a66.d: The Lågendeltaet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lillehammer municipality in the Innlandet region, at the mouth of the Gudbrandsdalslågen river where it flows into Lake Mjøsa. The reserve was established in 1990 to ‘preserve an important and unique wetland area in its natural state, with its vegetation and wildlife, and to protect a particularly rich and interesting birdlife.’ The Lågendeltaet is one of Norway’s largest inland deltas, and the reserve stretches from the municipal boundary with Øyer in the north to approximately two kilometres south of Vingnes Bridge. In addition to the river and the lake, the area also includes all the islands and some stretches of shoreline, but excludes a few bays near Vingnes and the town.

fjellsbergtangen-naturreservat-nat5445cf.d: Fjellsbergtangen Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern side of the island of Rauer, to the west of Fredrikstad municipality. The reserve borders the Rauerfjorden Marine Protected Area to the east. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry conglomerate and forms part of the Oslo Field (in contrast to the granite on the mainland). The vegetation is varied, comprising thermophilic woodland, partly consisting of broad-leaved deciduous forest. Rocky outcrops with juniper are also present. Furthermore, there are both older and larger trees, both living and dead, as well as younger oak saplings. The area provides good conditions for thermophilic invertebrates, particularly insects. Several Red List species have been recorded, including the dark-coloured beetle Prionychus ater, and remains of the hermit beetle have been found.

teineholmen-naturreservat-nat9464c9aa.d: Teineholmen Nature Reserve is situated just south of Engelsvikøya, to the west of Fredrikstad municipality. The reserve comprises Teineholmen itself and the sea surrounding it for approximately 50 metres from the islet. To the west, the reserve borders the Rauerfjorden Marine Protected Area. The islet is a very important breeding site for the Red Listed birds: the common gull, the black-headed gull and the common tern. All three species have declined sharply in the Oslofjord, and the common tern is now classified as Endangered (EN). Wildlife and plant life on land and in the water are protected against damage and destruction, but seabird hunting is permitted in accordance with current regulations. It is prohibited to carry out measures that alter the natural conditions. During the period 15 April to 15

rauer-naturreservat-nat0b77a0bc.d: Rauer Nature Reserve is situated along the western side of the island of Rauer in Fredrikstad municipality. The beach on this side is exposed and characterised by coarse material. Here there are rauks, which are rock formations created by sea erosion. The woodland behind the beach consists of deciduous broad-leaved forest. There are also a few very old oak trees here; the two largest died between 1997 and 1999. Remains of the hermit beetle (Osmoderma eremita) have been found in these oak trees, indicating that the species once lived here. In Norway, this species is otherwise only found in Tønsberg, and is listed as Critically Endangered (CR) on the Red List. There used to be moose on the island, but all of them were culled in 2003 due to a severe tick infestation.

paradisbukta-naturreservat-nat0d9f9536.d: Paradisbukta Nature Reserve consists of a sandy beach that is not subject to significant erosion, and is situated on the sheltered eastern side of the island of Rauer, to the west of Fredrikstad municipality. Along the shoreline to the east, the reserve borders the Rauerfjorden Marine Protected Area. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry conglomerate and belongs to the Oslo Field (in contrast to the granite on the mainland). The reserve is bounded to the north by a rocky escarpment and to the south by exposed rock. There is a small area here with rauks, which are rock formations created by erosion caused by the sea and ice. Within the open sandy beach there is a pine forest, mainly with grass species in the ground layer. However, there are also some herbaceous plants. Of particular note are the red-listed sodawort and sea rush.

rauerfjorden-marine-verneomrade-nata3a6b.d: The Rauerfjorden Marine Protected Area comprises the marine area around the islands of Rauer, Nordre Missingen and Søndre Missingen in Fredrikstad municipality. The area extends as far as the Teineholmen Nature Reserve and the Garntangen Nature Reserve to the north. To the south, the conservation area adjoins Ytre Hvaler National Park. Encircled by the conservation area are the Teineholmen Nature Reserve, the Rauerkalven Nature Reserve, the Rauer Nature Reserve, the Paradisbukta Nature Reserve, the Fjellsbergtangen Nature Reserve and the Søndre Missingen Nature Reserve. The purpose of the protected area is to preserve an area containing threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats.

rauerkalven-naturreservat-nat76c18e8d.d: The Rauerkalven Nature Reserve is situated in the west of Fredrikstad municipality and comprises Rauerkalven itself, the two islets of Kalveskjær and Veslekalven, and the stretch of sea between them. Rauerkalven is connected to Rauer via a tombolo – that is, a sand and gravel spit formed by the sea’s waves. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry conglomerate, which provides favourable growing conditions. The vegetation is varied, with elements of deciduous forest. The sandy beaches are very little affected by outdoor recreation. Among other species, the yellow horned poppy, which is a protected species, has been recorded here. Norwegian aspen has also been recorded. This is a species for which Norway bears special responsibility, growing almost exclusively along the coast from Halden to Rogaland, as well as in a few places in Bohuslän and Dalsland in Sweden.

s-ndre-missingen-naturreservat-nata79983.d: The Søndre Missingen Nature Reserve encompasses most of the two islands, Søndre Missingen and Ovnskjær, as well as the surrounding coastal waters, south-west of Hankø in Fredrikstad municipality. An area on both sides of the sound between the two islands, Missinghavna, is excluded from the reserve. The reserve is otherwise completely surrounded by the Rauerfjorden Marine Protected Area. The bedrock consists of the rare rock type rhomboid porphyry conglomerate and forms part of the Oslo Field. The protection is otherwise justified by the islands’ value as a breeding site for seabirds. In 2000, ten nests of the red-listed species, the common tern, were recorded, amongst others. There is also a small colony of black guillemots.

flatv-r-naturreservat-nat624d11a5.d: The Flatvær Nature Reserve consists of two areas. One area comprises Flatværet and the islets and skerries north of Nordkvaløya. The other area comprises Store and Lille Lyngøya and the islets and skerries a few kilometres further east. The entire nature reserve is situated in Karlsøy municipality. The area is situated within the Ytre Karlsøy Marine Protected Area, which was designated on 23 June 2020. The nature reserve was designated on 4 June 2004 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, access is prohibited near cormorant breeding colonies.

barvikmyran-og-blodskytodden-naturreserv.d: The Barvikmyran and Blodskytodden Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Vardø municipality. The nature reserve was established to preserve a large mire complex, an area of beautifully formed beach ridges, and a coastal strip featuring landforms that reveal the effects of marine erosion on layered rock formations. Around Blodskytodden, there are continuous fields of beach ridges at various elevations, as well as well-developed beach ridges formed by present-day sea levels. There are also well-developed marine erosion features in steeply standing, sedimentary rocks. Most of the marshland consists of tussocky soil surrounding numerous ponds and small bodies of water. In Næringsdalen to the west, the marshes are of the hill marsh type. The birdlife is rich, with the red-throated loon, common snipe, Arctic skua and Lapland bunting as characteristic species.

nord-fugl-ya-naturreservat-natf39ff2e7.d: The Nord-Fugløya Nature Reserve comprises Nordfugløya in Karlsøy municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 4 June 2004. From 1 April to 31 July inclusive, it is prohibited to go ashore or move about on land within the nature reserve. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a large island and its adjacent marine areas, together with their flora and fauna. The area is home to one of Norway’s largest and most important bird cliffs and is of great importance as a breeding and resting area for birds, as well as for its interesting flora.”

makkaurhalv-ya-naturreservat-natadc503ce.d: The Makkaur Peninsula Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Båtsfjord municipality in Finnmark. It covers the north-eastern part of the Makkaur Peninsula and was established in 1983. The purpose of the reserve is to conserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area, as well as to preserve the area as a representative site for the coastal region of East Finnmark. The Syltefjordstauran bird cliff is a key feature of the reserve. Syltefjordstauran is a breeding ground for seabirds and a moulting and moulting site for guillemots.

grasmyrskogvatn-naturreservat-nat6ceb81e.d: Grasmyrskogvatn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Senja municipality in Troms. It covers an area of 1.912 km² and is situated in a wetland area on the eastern side of the island of Senja. The reserve was established in 1995 to preserve Grasmyrskogvatnet and the adjacent marshlands on the western and eastern sides of the lake. It is an important breeding ground for a number of species of ducks and waders, such as the pintail and the common snipe. In autumn, Grasmyrskogvatnet serves as a moulting area for diving ducks and dabbling ducks. The area is also important for wetland-dependent passerines. There are some wooded areas with herb-rich birch forest and willow thickets. North of the outlet of the Lakselva river lies a sedge marsh (Svåan) with abundant river sedge.

myrvatn-naturreservat-nat8b688e58.d: Myrvatn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Tjeldsund municipality in Troms. The reserve was established in 1995 ‘to preserve a small, nutrient-rich lake with adjacent groundwater marshes that are important as a breeding ground for wetland birds and which feature interesting vegetation’. Myrvatnet lies approximately 7 km north-east of Evenes Airport and forms part of the Kvitfors watercourse. The lake is surrounded by extensive groundwater bogs, alternating between poor, moderately rich and rich bogs. The lake is nutrient-rich, with common reed and other vegetation. It serves as a breeding and migration area for wetland birds.

faueldalen-naturreservat-nata89142df.d: Faueldalen Nature Reserve (also spelled Fugldalen and Fauldalen) is a nature reserve in the eastern part of Tromsø municipality. It encompasses the lower part of the Fugldalelva catchment area. To the east, the reserve borders the Lyngsalpan landscape conservation area, and otherwise the boundary largely follows the valley of the Fugldalselva river, except for the lowest 200 metres or so before the river flows into Sørfjorden. The conservation objective is to protect coastal pine forest with its natural flora and fauna, linked to the establishment of vegetation in an area of interesting Quaternary geology. Parts of the gravel deposits (sandur, terminal moraines and lateral moraines) are devoid of vegetation. Nutrient-rich flora is establishing itself on bedrock consisting of gabbro, amphibolite and diorite.

syltefjorddalen-naturreservat-nat97ef70a.d: Syltefjorddalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Båtsfjord municipality in Finnmark. It is situated in the Syltefjord Valley, around 15 kilometres (as the crow flies) south-east of the village of Båtsfjord, and was established in 2006. The purpose of establishing the reserve was to preserve a virtually untouched area of deciduous woodland near the river in the lower part of the Syltefjord Valley, as well as a limestone scree slope in the side valley of Reindalen, along with the area’s biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes.

masv-r-naturreservat-nat3c3a1e1b.d: The Måsvær Nature Reserve comprises Store Måsværet, parts of Lille Måsværet and numerous islets and skerries. The reserve is situated in Karlsøy municipality. The area lies within the Ytre Karlsøy Marine Protected Area, which was designated on 23 June 2020, and is surrounded by the Nordkvaløya–Rebbenesøya Landscape Conservation Area, which, like the Måsvær Nature Reserve, was designated on 4 June 2004. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area with typical archipelago nature in outer Troms, comprising a group of small islands and islets with adjacent shallow-water areas and their flora and fauna. The area is of particular importance for seabirds.’

haja-r-ssholmen-landskapsvernomrade-nat0.d: The Håja-Røssholmen Landscape Conservation Area, which includes a wildlife sanctuary, is a landscape conservation area in Tromsø municipality in Troms. The area lies to the west of Kvaløya and comprises Håja in the south, Hersøya and a marine area with islets and skerries in the north, stretching from Vadholmen to Røssholmen and Angmeholmen. It has a total area of 7,479 dekar, of which 3,170 dekar is land. The landscape conservation area was established in 2004 to preserve the natural and cultural landscape, including its wildlife. The area consists of islets and skerries surrounded by shallow waters that are of great importance to seabirds. It serves as a breeding ground for gulls, eider ducks, black guillemots and red-billed terns.

rystraumen-marine-verneomrade-nat48b8f46.d: The Rystraumen Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Troms County. It comprises an area in Straumsfjorden. The area was designated on 23 June 2020. The conservation area is part of the marine conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a strong tidal current, with specific current conditions determined by the geological structures, with a wide range of variation and a rich diversity of wildlife, including sessile organisms such as sea anemones, bivalves, sponges and corals. The aim is to preserve these conservation values without significant external impact, and the area is intended to serve as a reference site for research and monitoring. The conservation objective relates to the seabed.

store-folles-ya-naturreservat-nat768e54a.d: The Store Follesøya Nature Reserve comprises an area on Store Follesøya in Skjervøy municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 30 March 1990. Access is prohibited from 1 April to 15 August inclusive. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for birdlife in the area and to preserve an important breeding site for the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’

skorpa-n-klan-landskapsvernomrade-nat7ad.d: Skorpa – Nøklan Landscape Conservation Area, which includes protected plant life, is situated in Kvænangen municipality in Troms. The landscape conservation area comprises the islands of Skorpa and Nøklan and the two Høyholman islets. The islands and islets are situated in Kvænangen Fjord. The area covers 12,713 dekar of land and was designated a protected area in 2004. The area was designated to ‘preserve two distinctive islands and two islets with their natural and cultural landscapes, as well as flora associated with calcareous birch forest intermixed with pine, calcareous vegetation with occurrences of creeping bent-grass, and culturally influenced meadow vegetation.’ (Quote from the conservation regulations.)

stabbursdalen-landskapsvernomrade-med-pl.d: The Stabbursdalen Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Porsanger municipality in Finnmark, and borders Stabbursdalen National Park. The area was established in 2002 and covers 189.4 km². The landscape conservation area has protected plant life and was established on account of its Quaternary geology, its natural landscape and its pine forest.

ytre-syltevika-naturreservat-natd4be3ad6.d: Ytre Syltevika Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Båtsfjord municipality in Finnmark. It lies to the east of the mouth of Syltefjorden and stretches from Ytre Syltevika in the west to Skjåvika, west of Hamningberg, in the east. The reserve was established in 1983 and aims to preserve a system of beach ridges that illustrate post-glacial land uplift, a coastal strip that reveals marine erosion in layered rock formations, and an area of Arctic-style coastal landscape with very sparse vegetation.

store-ris-ya-landskapsvernomrade-nat7007.d: The Store Risøya Landscape Conservation Area, which includes a wildlife sanctuary, is a landscape conservation area in the north-western part of Tromsø municipality in Troms. The landscape conservation area comprises Risøya, which lies approximately eight kilometres west/north-west of Ringvassøya, and has a total area of 1,213 dekar, of which 57 dekar is sea. Risøya is home to a former trading post with older buildings. The landscape conservation area was established in 1995 to preserve the coastal trading post, including its buildings, the cultural landscape, and the flora and fauna. The island is one of the largest breeding grounds for eider ducks and long-tailed ducks in Norway. To the north, south and west, the landscape conservation area borders the Risøya Nature Reserve.

karnes-naturreservat-nat783c0493.d: The Karnes Nature Reserve consists of a number of islets and shallow areas in the fjord within Lyngseidet in Lyngen municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 4 June 2004 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 1 May to 15 July inclusive, access to land is prohibited in most of the conservation area. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area with diverse habitats for plants and animals’. The area features a richly developed salt marsh vegetation alongside lush deciduous woodland. The islets are of great importance as a breeding ground for seabirds in the inner fjord areas of Troms, whilst the tidal flats are an important stopover site for wetland birds.’

sandbukta-naturreservat-nat1cd18a2d.d: For the nature reserve in Buskerud, see Sandbukta-Østnestangen Nature Reserve. Sandbukta Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tromsø municipality and was established on 4 June 2004. It is situated at the mouth of the Breivikelva river in Ullsfjorden, close to the village of Breivikeidet. Sandbukta is a coastal area containing one of the largest fields of beach ridges in Troms.

sandfjordneset-naturreservat-nat1dec46d0.d: Sandfjordneset Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Båtsfjord municipality in Finnmark. It is situated at the mouth of the Sandfjordelva river, four kilometres south of Hamningberg. The reserve was established in 1983 with the aim of preserving a drifting sand field with interesting beach vegetation. The nature reserve comprises a well-developed system of sand dunes in a wide bay that faces the sea and forms a headland between the beach and the Sandfjordelva river. Within the dune field, there are several active, well-formed parabolic dunes, 10–15 metres high. The vegetation zonation is typical of Varanger, with only a narrow foreshore of Arctic sea radish and merely a faint belt of grey dunes within the light-coloured beach grass dunes.

hakstein-naturreservat-nat622f62be.d: The Hakstein Nature Reserve comprises Hakkstein and Små-Hakksteinan in Skjervøy municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 4 June 2004. From 1 May to 15 July inclusive, access to Små-Hakksteinan is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve two small islands in North Troms, together with their flora and fauna. The area is of particular importance as a breeding ground for seabirds.’

kongs-ya-hell-ya-og-skarholmen-naturrese.d: The Kongsøya, Helløya and Skarholmen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Berlevåg municipality in Finnmark. The nature reserve comprises Kongsøya, Helløya and Skarholmen, which are situated in Kongsfjorden, and the surrounding marine areas around each island. It has a total area of 2,869 dekar, of which 2,050 is sea. The nature reserve was established in 1983 to preserve important bird cliffs, along with the plants, birds and other wildlife associated with the area. It is a breeding ground for great cormorants, shags, black guillemots, razorbills, puffins, eider ducks, kittiwakes and gulls. Among the marine mammals found there are otters and porpoises.

rossfjordstraumen-marine-verneomrade-nat.d: The Rossfjordstraumen Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Troms County. It comprises Lake Rossfjordvatnet and Rossfjorden near Malangen. The area was designated on 23 June 2020. The protected area forms part of the marine conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to safeguard a fjord system connected to a virtually meromictic lake, with fresh water at the surface and seawater at depth, where the conservation values are linked to the integrity of theand current system with extreme environmental conditions, including the high sulphide content which renders the bottom sediments and deeper water layers oxygen-free and unaffected by animals and plants, as well as a genetically distinct herring stock.”

grunnvatnet-naturreservat-nate32483a2.d: The Grunnvatnet Nature Reserve is situated in Narvik municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises Grunnvatnet, together with Knutvatnet, Djupvatnet and part of the Børselva river. The area covers 4,450 dekar, of which 3,300 dekar is freshwater. The area is protected to preserve a wetland of clear national and, to some extent, international importance. It is one of the most important breeding areas for wetland birds in Nordland.

kj-ls-yv-ret-valv-r-naturreservat-natf53.d: The Kjølsøyværet/Valvær Nature Reserve is situated in Rødøy municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 32,433 dekar, of which 30,764 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds. Among other things, the area is home to several large and small colonies of great cormorants.

lanan-flov-r-og-skj-rv-r-fuglefredningso.d: The Lånan, Flovær and Skjærvær bird sanctuary is situated in Vega municipality in Nordland. The bird sanctuary consists of three separate parts, all of which lie within the Lånan/Skjærvær nature reserve. The bird sanctuary covers an area of 714 dekar, of which 371 dekar is marine area. The sanctuary was established to preserve a suitable and undisturbed breeding and rearing area for seabirds. The area is situated within the Vega World Heritage Site.

horsv-r-naturreservat-natd130b67d.d: Horsvær Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in the municipalities of Brønnøy, Sømna and Bindal in Nordland. The reserve was established to ‘preserve a coastal area of national importance, with its naturally associated flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding, moulting and wintering ground for seabirds’. The area comprises several small islets, including Gimsan, Terjan, Gjøvan, Horsvær, Hensteinen and Storbraken. It covers an area of 170.4 km², of which 169.1 km² is marine area. Within the nature reserve lie the Hensteinen, Horsvær and Gimsan bird sanctuaries. A large proportion of South Helgeland’s breeding sites for the lesser black-backed gull are found here.

lilandsvatnet-naturreservat-nat4cdd34b3.d: The Lilandsvatnet Nature Reserve is situated south of Liland and east of Haukås, in the eastern part of the Hamarøya peninsula in Nordland. The nature reserve covers a total area of 2,383 dekar, of which approximately 38 per cent consists of coniferousdeciduous and mixed woodland, around 8 per cent consists of bogs and 46.4 per cent is water, the largest lake being Lilandsvatnet itself, which covers 526 daa. Like the Steinslandsvatnet Nature Reserve, this is an important sub-area within a larger wetland system in the western part of Kaldvågfjorden. The reserve is situated in a flat marsh landscape, bordered by agricultural land to the north and west. The dense reed beds in the bays and inlets are dominated by river sedge, bottle sedge and broad belts of floating-leaf vegetation.

hensteinen-horsv-r-og-gimsan-fuglefredni.d: The Hensteinen, Horsvær and Gimsan Bird Sanctuary is situated in the municipalities of Brønnøy, Sømna and Bindal in Nordland. The bird sanctuary comprises several small islets. The area covers 4,448 dekar, of which 2,790 dekar is sea area. The bird sanctuary was established to preserve a suitable and undisturbed breeding and rearing area for seabirds. The bird sanctuary is situated within the Horsvær Nature Reserve.

junkerdalsura-naturreservat-nat2c3f6ea1.d: Junkerdalsura Nature Reserve is situated in Junkerdal in Saltdal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 13,725 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a large forest area stretching from the valley floor to the bare mountain peaks, with all its natural flora and fauna and all the natural ecological processes. Among other things, the area is home to one of the largest limestone birch forests in the Nordic region. Adjacent to the Junkerdalsura Nature Reserve lies Junkerdal National Park.

varnvassdalen-naturreservat-nat9ff0b919.d: The Varnvassdalen Nature Reserve is situated on the southern side of the Varnvassdalen valley in Hattfjelldal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve was extended on 11 February 2022 and covers an area of 19,957 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a highly valuable, largely undisturbed coniferous forest dominated by pine. The nature reserve borders the Favnvassdalen landscape conservation area to the east.

trollpollen-naturreservat-nat5f766e01.d: The Trollpollen Nature Reserve lies between Varpvatnet to the north and Sagpollen to the south, 4.5 kilometres north/north-east of Innhavet in Hamarøy, Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses the land areas around Trollpollen, south of Varpelva and Varpvågen, north of Sag- and Hillingspollen, and eastwards past Hillingspolltjønna. The total area is 5,385 dekar, of which 5,071 dekar consists of various types of woodland. The area is a forested hilly landscape, mainly comprising two elevation levels, with bedrock consisting of granite and granodiorite. Along the shallow coastal inlets, there are gentle gradients between the beach vegetation and the sparse coastal pine forest. The oldest trees in the pine forest are probably between 5 and 600 years old.

steinslandsosen-naturreservat-nat7d5b8c3.d: Steinslandsosen Nature Reserve is situated just east and south-east of Skutvik in Hamarøy, Nordland, between Steinslandsåsen and Nes at the southernmost tip of the Hamarøya peninsula in Nordland. The nature reserve covers a total area of 2,248 dekar, of which approximately 12 per cent consists of coniferous and deciduous woodland, approximately 1.7 per cent is marshland and 62.6 per cent is water.
