Osen is an important wetland area, surrounded by granite hills, comprising three parts: the outer part, which is an open shell sand plain divided by rocky ridges and skerries. Here, there are salt marsh edges in the bays and gravel beach vegetation around the ridges and skerries. The inner part features an extensive system of pools, with little vegetation, situated between a network of gravel ridges with dry salt marsh vegetation.

semska-st-di-naturreservat-nat31e8fe2d.d: The Semska-Stødi Nature Reserve is situated in Saltdal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses the high-mountain plateau on Saltfjellet between Semska in the north and Stødi in the south, to the east of European Route 6 and the railway line crossing the mountain. The area covers approximately 13,000 dekar and was designated a nature reserve in 1976. The area has been protected to safeguard a valuable wetland area as a habitat for the associated flora and fauna and a distinctive landscape of glacial deposits, and to preserve this area in its natural state.

stranda-os-landskapsvernomrade-med-tilh-.d: The Strandå/Os Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Kjerringøy in Bodø municipality, Nordland. The landscape conservation area is designated as a wildlife sanctuary due to the vulnerable birdlife in the valley. The area was established in 1983 and covers 16.6 km². The landscape conservation area borders the Strandåvassbotn Nature Reserve. The nature reserve encompasses the valley floor and the lakes, whilst the landscape conservation area encompasses the slopes and surrounding mountainsides.

fj-re-naturreservat-nat9379b676.d: Fjære Nature Reserve is situated on Kjerringøy in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 687 dekar, of which 386 dekar is marine area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect a valuable coastal area, which includes a distinctive system of sand dunes.

innervisten-marine-verneomrade-natf2b75d.d: The Innervisten Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Nordland County. It comprises an area at the innermost part of Vistenfjorden. The area was designated on 23 June 2020. The conservation area is part of the marine conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a narrow sound with a distinctive threshold basin within it and underwater caves, with distinctive habitat types in the fjord, including the seabed, benthic organisms and organisms in the water column, and a unique fauna featuring Arctic and northern cold-water species.

kaldvagfjorden-og-innhavet-marine-verneo.d: The Kaldvågfjorden and Innhavet Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Hamarøy municipality in Nordland county. It comprises an area along Kaldvågfjorden and Innhavet. The area was designated on 23 June 2020. The conservation area is part of the marine conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a relatively undisturbed and distinctive estuarine system, with thresholds that regulate water exchange and the physical framework conditions, and a wide range of natural conditions with the potential for the occurrence of rare or new species. The aim is to preserve the conservation values without significant external impact, and the area is intended to serve as a reference area for research and monitoring.

bliksv-r-naturreservat-nat66a55f8c.d: Bliksvær Nature Reserve is situated in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve comprises the main island of Bliksvær, as well as Kjærvær, Terra, Sjursholmen, Grønnholmen, Skjoldsholmen, Tørrisøya and Einarsholmen. The total area is 43,195 dekar, of which 37,355 dekar is marine area. The area is protected to preserve a virtually untouched coastal area of great scientific value in both zoology and botany. Bliksvær Nature Reserve is a wildlife sanctuary. In August 2002, Bliksvær Nature Reserve was established and, at the same time, designated as a Ramsar site. The area had previously been a wildlife sanctuary since 1970.

sundstraumlian-naturreservat-nat5f2da9ec.d: Sundstraumlian Nature Reserve is situated on the southern side of Straumøya in Bodø municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve encompasses the hillside sloping down towards Sundstraumen and Indre Sundan. The area covers 1,275 dekar and is protected to preserve a varied pine and mixed forest with all its natural flora and fauna and all its natural ecological processes.

lanan-skj-rv-r-naturreservat-nat29062e73.d: The Lånan/Skjærvær Nature Reserve is situated in Vega municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of approximately 112.9 km², of which approximately 110.5 km² is marine area. The area is protected to safeguard a nationally valuable coastal area, with its naturally associated flora and fauna. Within the Lånan/Skjærvær Nature Reserve lies the Lånan, Flovær and Skjærvær Bird Sanctuary. To the south, the nature reserve borders the Hysvær/Søla landscape conservation area. The area is situated within the Vega World Heritage Site.

sommervatnet-naturreservat-nat0d15b46a.d: Sommervatnet Nature Reserve is situated in Evenes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 155 dekar, of which 85 dekar is freshwater. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area with its naturally occurring vegetation and wildlife. In 2011, the reserve, together with four other nature reserves, was designated a Ramsar site under the collective name ‘Evenes Wetland System’.

favnvassdalen-landskapsvernomrade-tilh-r.d: The Favnvassdalen Landscape Conservation Area is situated on the south side of the Bolvasselva river between Lake Famvatnet and the Swedish border in Hattfjelldal municipality in Nordland. The landscape conservation area is designated as a wildlife sanctuary due to the vulnerable birdlife in the valley. The area was established in 1983 and covers 14.5 km². The landscape conservation area borders the Storslettmyra Nature Reserve to the north and the Varnvassdalen Nature Reserve to the west.

nordfjorden-marine-verneomrade-nat30ae6d.d: The Nordfjorden Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Nordland County. It comprises Nordfjorden near Melfjorden. The area was designated on 23 June 2020. The protected area is included in the marine protection plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to safeguard a long, narrow and deep fjord, surrounded by an alpine landscape, with special environmental conditions, which are influenced, amongst other things, by a threshold basin and meltwater from glaciers, and the wildlife on the seabed and in the water column. The aim is to preserve the conservation values without significant external impact, and the area is intended to serve as a reference area for research and monitoring. The conservation objective relates to the seabed and the water column.

blakkadalen-naturreservat-nat06ce106a.d: Blakkådalen Nature Reserve is situated in Blakkådalen in the municipality of Rana in Nordland. The nature reserve covers 3,080 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a unique coniferous forest area, parts of which consist of genuine primeval forest. Two spruce stands in the area are among the northernmost in Europe. The nature reserve borders Saltfjellet-Svartisen National Park.

arstadlia-tverrviknakkan-naturreservat-n.d: The Arstadlia–Tverviknakkan Nature Reserve is situated near Arstad in Beiarn municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers 887 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve what is probably the world’s northernmost elm population (Arstadlia) and a calcareous pine forest of national conservation value (Tverviknakkan) with a rich variety of orchids, as well as the intervening limestone outcrops at Stihammaren, which feature a frequent occurrence of lowland birch and many other demanding plant species. The Arstadlia–Tverviknakkan Nature Reserve is situated right next to the Leirvika Nature Reserve.

fisklausvatnet-naturreservat-nata4ce2c95.d: Fisklausvatnet Nature Reserve is situated in Grane municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 38,500 dekar, of which 4,000 dekar is water. Lake Fiskelausvatnet accounts for the majority of this water area. The area has been designated a nature reserve to protect a high-altitude wetland area of national conservation importance.

fisktj-nna-naturreservat-nat99983afe.d: Fisktjørna Nature Reserve is situated south of Svartisen in Rana municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 2,690 dekar. The area has been designated a nature reserve to preserve a stretch of primeval forest.

karls-yv-r-naturreservat-nat42c972da.d: Karlsøyvær Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bodø municipality, Nordland. The nature reserve comprises a marine area and a number of islands west of Kjerringøy, and has held Ramsar Site status since 2002, due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1977 to protect a coastal area of high botanical and ornithological conservation value. Within the reserve, there are significant assets in terms of both seabirds and coastal botany. The area is an important breeding ground for seabirds, although the range of species is unremarkable. It is an important area for white-tailed eagles. 42.7 km² of the area is marine, with the remainder being land. There are some buildings on Karlsøya, and traces of former eider duck houses.

strandavassbotn-naturreservat-natc6726c2.d: Strandåvassbotn Nature Reserve is situated by the Strandå river in Kjerringøy, in the municipality of Bodø in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 6,300 dekar, of which 600 dekar is water. The area is protected to preserve a large, undisturbed wetland area in its natural state and to safeguard its particularly interesting flora and birdlife. The nature reserve borders the Strandå/Os landscape conservation area. The nature reserve encompasses the valley floor and the lakes, whilst the landscape conservation area encompasses the slopes and surrounding mountainsides.

steinslandsvatnet-naturreservat-natb0b28.d: The Steinslandsvatnet Nature Reserve is situated between Skutvik and Nes, in the south-east of the Hamarøya peninsula in Nordland. The nature reserve covers a total area of 4,178 dekar, of which approximately 32 per cent consists of various types of woodland, approximately 18 per cent consists of bogs and 40.9 per cent is water. Like Lilandsvatnet, this is an important part of a larger wetland system in the western part of Kaldvågfjorden. The reserve comprises shallow waters with well-developed vegetation, bog areas and adjacent shallow marine waters. Along the shoreline there are several salt marshes. It is an important breeding area, particularly for ducks and waders, but also for black-throated divers and whooper swans.

dypen-naturreservat-nat6b07a425.d: The Dypen Nature Reserve is situated in Saltdal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve lies on the east bank of the Lønselva river, in the area east of Lønsdal station. It covers an area of 6,855 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a relatively undisturbed stand of pine trees. The area was previously part of the Saltfjellet Landscape Conservation Area, but its protection has since been extended as a nature reserve.

vallabotn-breivika-og-r-ssaauren-naturre.d: The Vallabotn, Breivika and Røssåauren Nature Reserve is situated in Hemnes municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve consists of three parts, to the south, north and north-west of Bjerka. In total, the area covers 463 dekar, of which 365 dekar is water. The area is protected to safeguard what is, from a botanical perspective, the most important brackish water area in Nordland.

hysv-r-s-la-landskapsvernomrade-med-dyre.d: The Hysvær/Søla Landscape Conservation Area is situated in Vega municipality in Nordland. The area is a wildlife sanctuary; it was established in 2002 and covers 93,172 dekar, of which 86,028 dekar is marine area. The landscape conservation area was established on account of its cultural landscape, zoology, botany and geology. Adjacent to the Hysvær/Søla Landscape Conservation Area lies the Lånan/Skjærvær Nature Reserve. The area is situated within the Vega World Heritage Site.

storslettmyra-naturreservat-nat50314ff8.d: Storslettmyra Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern shore of Lake Famvatnet in Hattfjelldal municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 1,100 dekar. The area is protected to preserve a wetland area with its associated flora and fauna, particularly in view of the type of bog and the area’s exceptionally interesting birdlife. The nature reserve borders the Favnvassdalen landscape conservation area to the south.

karls-yfjorden-marine-verneomrade-nat20e.d: The Karlsøyfjorden Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Nordland County. It comprises an area north of the town of Bodø. The area was designated as a protected area on 23 June 2020. The conservation area is part of the marine conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an open coastal area with an undulating seabed landscape, including a deep channel of more than 500 metres and thresholds of approximately 250 metres, as well as exposed rocky coasts and an undulating archipelago, with a wide range of habitat types representative of the coastal area and conservation values associated with the seabed landscape, including the seabed and its organisms.”

s-rfugl-ya-naturreservat-nat37bf22a5.d: The Sørfugløya Nature Reserve comprises Sørfugløya and numerous islets and skerries off Rebbenesøya in Karlsøy municipality. The area lies within the Ytre Karlsøy Marine Protected Area, which was designated on 23 June 2020. The nature reserve was designated on 4 June 2004 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 1 April to 31 August inclusive, camping and pitching tents are prohibited within the conservation area. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of typical archipelago nature in outer Troms, comprising an island and adjacent islets, skerries and marine areas, together with their flora and fauna. The area is home to one of Norway’s most important seabird cliffs and is of great importance as a breeding ground for seabirds.”

ytre-karls-y-marine-verneomrade-nat53ba7.d: The Ytre Karlsøy Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Troms County. It comprises an area off the coast of Rebbenesøya and Nordkvaløya. The area was designated on 23 June 2020. The conservation area is part of the marine conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a large, contiguous coastal area that is representative of the coastal environment in Troms. The area features well-developed Quaternary geological landscape features and traces of rich cultural traditions dating from the Stone Age right up to the present day.

gr-velsj-en-naturreservat-nat70c2e9af.d: Grøvelsjøen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Engerdal municipality. It borders Femundsmarka National Park to the west and Långfjället Nature Reserve across the border in Sweden to the east. The Norwegian part of Grøvelsjøen borders the nature reserve. The area was designated a protected area on 22 December 1989. The reserve forms part of the conservation plan for Quaternary geology. Carl von Linné described the area as early as 1734. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of natural-historical interest with important Quaternary geological features, including a number of well-developed mountain pastures at various levels.’

langaskj-len-naturreservat-natac1a1f23.d: Langåskjølen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Klæbu, Trondheim. The nature reserve was established on 21 December 1990 to protect a large, varied area of oceanic-influenced bogs. The area comprises a mosaic of nutrient-poor forest types and bogs of varying richness. Towards the forested ridges in the east and north-west, there are rich and, in some cases, extremely rich bog types. Brown sedge dominates most of the extremely rich bogs. The nature reserve contains large quantities of meadow sedge and beaked sedge, and significant occurrences of oceanic species such as bell heather, bog myrtle, flea sedge and marsh cinquefoil.

gudfjell-ya-naturreservat-nat3d75a15c.d: Gudfjelløya Nature Reserve is situated on Gudfjelløya in Lake Tunnsjøen, in the municipalities of Røyrvik and Lierne. The nature reserve was established on 4 September 1981 and comprises a 0.61 km² forested area on the southern side of the island with a high proportion of elm trees.

steinan-og-flottra-naturreservat-natc958.d: The Steinan and Flottra Nature Reserve consists of two archipelagos with associated islets, skerries and marine areas off Otterøya and Jøa in Namsos municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 19 December 2003 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, access to land within the nature reserve is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to safeguard two archipelagos, together with associated islets, skerries and marine areas, and their naturally associated flora and fauna. Steinan and Flottra are of particular value as breeding grounds for seabirds.’

froan-naturreservat-nat92f590fb.d: The Froan Nature Reserve and Landscape Conservation Area is a nature reserve, landscape conservation area and biotope protection area (wildlife sanctuary) in Frøya municipality, Trøndelag. The protected area is situated in the Froan archipelago and has Ramsar site status due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1979 to preserve the habitats and breeding grounds of birds and seals, and is the largest contiguous marine area designated as a nature reserve in Norway. The area includes the inhabited islands of Sørburøy and Sauøy. The Froan Nature Reserve and Landscape Conservation Area comprises a 400 km² nature reserve stretching from Vingleia Lighthouse in the south-west to Halten in the north-east, and an 80 km² area to the south-east of the nature reserve that is protected as a landscape conservation area.

bjugnholmen-naturreservat-nat7622aee5.d: The Bjugnholmen Nature Reserve consists of two areas at the eastern and western ends of Bjugnholmen in Ørland municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 9 September 2005 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, access to land within the conservation area is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve parts of a virtually untouched island and adjacent marine areas with their natural flora and fauna. The area is of particular value as a breeding ground for seabirds.’ The nature reserve borders the Kråkvåg and Bjugnfjorden Marine Protected Area, which was established on 13 February 2026 and encompasses the marine areas in which Bjugnholmen is situated.

flaman-naturreservat-nat6c3f6545.d: Flåman Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Folldal, Dovre and Oppdal. The reserve was established in 1989 to preserve ‘an area of natural historical interest with important Quaternary geological features’. The reserve lies entirely above the tree line at the head of the Einunndalen valley and links the two areas that make up the Knutshø Landscape Conservation Area. The area contains many Quaternary geological features such as moraines, terraces and glacial channels.

skarnsundet-marine-verneomrade-nat913c6e.d: The Skarnsudet Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Inderøy municipality in Trøndelag, established in 2020. The conservation area covers most of Skarnsundet, as well as areas extending approximately 2 km into Beitstadfjorden and Trondheimsfjorden; it is generally bounded on the landward side by a depth of 5 metres, but with the exception of regulated marine areas at Kjerringvika, Venneshamn and Vangshylla, and small boat jetties. In total, the protected area covers 18.5 km². Hoøya Nature Reserve lies within the area covered by the Skarnsundet Marine Protected Area; Ørdalen Nature Reserve borders the protected area to the east; and Skavdalen Nature Reserve extends almost as far as Skarnsundet to the west.

horta-naturreservat-natfa8944f3.d: Horta Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the Horta archipelago in Leka municipality, Trøndelag. The area was established in 2003, together with the Horta Wildlife Sanctuary. In 2013, the two protected areas were designated as a Ramsar site. The nature reserve comprises three areas totalling 5.5 km², including on and around Fuholmen. The 24 km² wildlife sanctuary acts as a supplementary buffer zone around and between the three sites. Horta is an important breeding ground for the lesser black-backed gull, the shag, the great cormorant, the black guillemot and the red-throated loon.

lomundsj-myra-naturreservat-natdae0926e.d: Lomundsjømyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rindal municipality in Trøndelag. The area was designated a nature reserve on 13 December 1996 with the aim of preserving one of the finest string bogs in the county (at that time Møre og Romsdal), as well as ensuring its integrity with the adjacent Lomundsjøen Nature Reserve. Lomundsjømyra Nature Reserve lies north-east of Lomundsjøen, south-east of County Road 6170 (Lomunddalsvegen), and borders the Lomundsjøen Wetland Reserve. The bog is situated in a limestone mountain zone; it is surrounded by herb-rich birch forest and cultivated land, with lush scrub forest growing along the river. The bog areas are varied, and large sections are subject to flooding.

borgan-og-frels-y-dyrelivsfredning-nat5f.d: The Borgan and Frelsøy Nature Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary is a nature reserve and an adjacent biotope conservation area which, together, also constitute a Ramsar site in Nærøysund municipality in Trøndelag. The area was designated to ‘maintain a harmonious mix of wildlife in the area’, as part of a wider conservation plan in 2003. The nature reserve comprises Kalvøya and Sandvær, including the archipelago and islets, whilst the biotope conservation area is situated on Borgan and Frelsøya, to the east and north of the nature reserve. The Kvaløy and Raudøy conservation area lies to the north-east. The area is a breeding ground for seabirds such as the greylag goose, eider, turnstone, Arctic skua, grey gull, black-backed gull, red-billed tern and black guillemot. It is also an important moulting site for greylag geese.

sklinnaflesin-biotopvernomrade-natb70aa5.d: Sklinnaflesin Biotope Reserve is a biotope reserve and a Ramsar site in Nærøysund municipality in Trøndelag. The area was designated to ‘safeguard an important breeding ground for seabirds’, as part of a wider conservation plan in 2003. The conservation area consists of two zones comprising islets and the surrounding waters, situated slightly south of Sklinna and west of Leka. In 2013, the area was designated a Ramsar site as one of ten sub-areas within the Vest-Vikna coastal landscape.

lomundsj-en-naturreservat-nat1ddce62f.d: Lomundsjøen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rindal municipality in Trøndelag. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 May 1988 with the aim of preserving an important wetland area with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife. The nature reserve is situated in the Lomund Valley, south-east of County Road 6170 (Lomunddalsvegen), and is crossed by County Road 6172 (Rørdalsvegen). The area consists mainly of wetlands, namely Lake Lomund, a low-lying marshy area north of the lake, and the River Lomunda, stretching for approximately 700 to 800 metres south-west from the lake. Slate, which weathers easily, provides the area with nutrient-rich soil, and a marble vein to the south of the watercourse makes the lake rich in calcium. The reserve is of great importance for birds.

vre-forra-naturreservat-nat9dfd48b1.d: The Øvre Forra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Meråker, Verdal, Levanger and Stjørdal, in Trøndelag. The nature reserve is situated at the point where Lake Feren flows into the River Forra, and has Ramsar status due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1990 to protect a large area of marshland with rich flora and fauna, virtually untouched by human intervention. According to the Norwegian Directorate for Nature Management, the area covers 102,538 dekar, whilst the regulations state that the area is approximately 108 square kilometres.

nord-yan-naturreservat-nat9dc9efb9.d: Nordøyan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site located on the Nordøyan archipelago in Nærøysund municipality, Trøndelag. The area was designated as a protected area to ‘preserve a distinctive island and archipelago area, where botanical, zoological and geological features, both on land and at sea, contribute to the area’s unique character’, as part of a wider conservation plan in 2003. The conservation area consists of two zones comprising islands and islets to the west of the Sør-Gjæslingan cultural heritage site. The area is of great natural value. It is of particular value as a breeding habitat for seabirds. The Sørøyan Nature Reserve lies just south-east of this area. In 2013, the area was designated a Ramsar site as one of ten sub-areas within the Vest-Vikna coastal landscape.

s-r-yan-naturreservat-nat03513129.d: Sørøyan Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Nærøysund municipality in Trøndelag. The area was designated as a protected area to ‘preserve a distinctive island and archipelago area, where botanical, zoological and geological features, both on land and at sea, contribute to the area’s unique character’, as part of a wider conservation plan in 2003. The protected area consists of two zones comprising islands and islets to the west of the Sør-Gjæslingan cultural heritage site. The area is of great natural value. It is of particular importance as a breeding habitat for seabirds. The Nordøyan Nature Reserve lies just north-west of this. In 2013, the area was designated a Ramsar site as one of ten sub-areas within the Vest-Vikna coastal landscape.

minilldalsmyrene-naturreservat-nat9f6a4c.d: The Minnilldalsmyrene Nature Reserve is situated in the municipalities of Oppdal and Rennebu and comprises 1,878 dekar of flat marshland. The nature reserve was established in 1990. Minilldalsmyrene is a large and distinctive marshland area with unique flora and a rich variety of birdlife. The area is entirely surrounded by the Trollheimen Landscape Conservation Area.

skj-kra-landskapsvernomrade-nateca37166.d: The Skjækra Landscape Conservation Area is situated in the municipalities of Steinkjer and Snåsa in Trøndelag. The area lies on the western side of, and borders, the Blåfjella-Skjækerfjella National Park. The landscape conservation area covers 96 km² and was established in 2004. Norway’s geographical centre lies at the heart of the landscape.

kval-y-og-rau-y-naturreservat-og-dyreliv.d: The Kvaløy and Raudøy Nature Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary is a nature reserve and an adjacent biotope conservation area which, together, also constitute a Ramsar site in Nærøysund municipality in Trøndelag. The area was protected to ‘maintain a harmonious mix of wildlife in the area’, as part of a wider conservation plan in 2003. The biotope protection area comprises land areas on Kvaløya and Raudøya, whilst the nature reserve comprises the marine areas to the north and west of the islands. Access is prohibited here during the breeding season. The Borgan and Frelsøy conservation area lies to the south-west. The area is a breeding ground for seabirds such as the greylag goose, eider, turnstone, Arctic skua, grey gull, black-backed gull, red-billed tern and black guillemot. It is also an important moulting site for greylag geese.

apoteket-naturreservat-nat692bd28e.d: Apoteket Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on Byneset in Trondheim. The nature reserve was established on 6 February 1987 to protect an area of broad-leaved deciduous forest and to preserve the area’s wildlife. Apoteket Nature Reserve is situated on a species-rich hillside sloping down towards Gaulosen, where several types of thermophilic plant communities can be found. Parts of the area also have the character of primeval forest.

tjuvholmen-klumpholmen-naturreservat-nat.d: The Tjuvholmen/Klumpholmen Nature Reserve consists of the islets of Tjuvholmen and Klumpholmen off Foldøy. The nature reserve is surrounded by the Foldøy Bird Sanctuary and is situated in Tysvær municipality. Both the nature reserve and the bird sanctuary were designated on 7 May 1982 and form part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the nature reserve is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the area’s birdlife and the birds’ habitats, as well as all plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the reserves.’

kvanndalen-landskapsvernomrade-nat51d499.d: The Kvanndalen Landscape Conservation Area is situated in the far north of Suldal municipality in Rogaland and forms a natural transition to Hardangervidda to the north; it is connected to the Holmavassåna Biotope Conservation Area and the Dyraheio Landscape Conservation Area to the south. The valley has its source at the watershed between Ståvassdalen and Kvanndalen, with Kistenuten to the east and Høghellernuten to the west. Kvanndalen extends from there for approximately 10 km in a south-south-westerly direction before ending at the steep slope down towards Roaldkvam and Suldalsvatnet. The aim of the landscape conservation is ‘to preserve a distinctive mountain area with unspoilt nature, rich plant life, valuable mountain farm areas and carved landscapes, as well as older and more recent cultural heritage sites associated with mountain farming, heathland grazing, hunting, fishing and trapping.’

dyraheio-landskapsvernomrade-natb3a06bea.d: The Dyraheio Landscape Conservation Area lies to the east of Lake Suldalsvatnet and stretches from Bleskestadmoen in the north to Strandalen and Odden in the south. The Dyraheio Landscape Conservation Area is linked to the Kvanndalen Landscape Conservation Area, the Holmavassåna Biotope Conservation Area and the Setesdal Vesthei Ryfylkeheiane Landscape Conservation Area. The aim of the landscape conservation is ‘to preserve a distinctive mountain area with unspoilt nature, rich plant life, valuable mountain pasture areas and carved landscapes, as well as older and more recent cultural heritage sites associated with mountain farming, heathland grazing, hunting, fishing and trapping.’

store-og-litle-fokksteinen-naturreservat.d: The Store and Litle Fokksteinen Nature Reserve consists of two islets within the Fokksteinane Wildlife Sanctuary. The reserve is situated off Jøssingfjord in Sokndal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 7 May 1982 and forms part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the area’s birdlife and the birds’ habitats, as well as all plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the reserves.’

hagavagen-naturreservat-nat76834f98.d: Hagavågen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sola municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area is situated on the western side of Hafrsfjorden and was designated a protected area in 1996 to preserve a marine wetland. The whole of Hafrsfjorden is of international importance as a resting and wintering area for wetland birds. The most important foraging areas consist of large mudflats with intertidal zones, and these are protected under Ramsar status. Hagavågen also has saltmarsh vegetation of ecological conservation value. The area is one of 22 protected areas forming part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

aatholmane-m-fl-naturreservat-nat14704ec.d: The Aatholmane (et al.) Nature Reserve comprises Aatholmane, Alneskjæra, Austre Flatholmane, Anisholmen, Kobbholmane and the eastern and western parts of Sandøy. The reserve forms part of Vignesholmane in Stavanger municipality and lies within the Vignesholmane wildlife sanctuary. Both the nature reserve and the wildlife sanctuary were designated on 7 May 1982 and form part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the nature reserve is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the area’s birdlife and the birds’ habitats, as well as all plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the reserves.’

orrevatnet-naturreservat-nat8ec19a8f.d: Orrevatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Klepp municipality on Jæren, Rogaland. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1996 to preserve a wetland of international importance. Orrevatnet is a large, shallow and weather-exposed lake situated close to the sea, largely on drifting sand. Few places in the country have recorded so many bird species. 65 species have been recorded, and up to 3,000 ducks have been counted in the area, including mallards, tufted ducks, gadwalls, garganey and scaup. The area is one of 22 protected areas that form part of the Jæren Wetland System Ramsar site, due to its importance for migratory birds. The Jæren Wetland System was established in 1985, and the number of sub-areas was expanded to 22 in 2002.

lind-y-tednholmen-og-slattholmen-naturre.d: The Lindøy, Tednholmen and Slåttholmen Nature Reserve comprises part of Lindøy and a number of islets and skerries east of Strong in Nedstrandsfjorden. The nature reserve is surrounded by the Lindøy Bird Sanctuary and is situated in Tysvær municipality. Both were designated on 7 May 1982 and form part of the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 1 August inclusive, landing on the nature reserve is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the area’s birdlife and the birds’ habitats, as well as all plant communities and animal species naturally associated with the reserves.’

illholmane-naturreservat-nat48169ad8.d: The Illholmane Nature Reserve consists of two islets in Bjoafjorden, north of Bjoa in Vindafjord municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 3 April 1987 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to ensure the best possible conditions for seabirds in the area and to safeguard an important breeding site with the plant and animal species naturally associated with the area.’

synesvarden-landskapsvernomrade-nat991f3.d: Synesvarden is a recreational area in Høgjæren, 360 metres above sea level. The Synesvarden Landscape Conservation Area was designated in 1993 and covers approximately 14 km² of heathland in the municipalities of Hå and Time. It offers views over large parts of Jæren. About 3 km south-west of Synesvarden stands Steinkjerringa, or ‘Mother Norway’ as it is also known.

j-rkysten-marine-verneomrade-natf669aacd.d: The Jærkysten Marine Protected Area is a marine protected area in Rogaland County. It comprises an area off the coast stretching from Feistein Lighthouse in the north to Sirevåg in the south. The area was designated a protected area on 17 June 2016. The protected area is part of the marine conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard an area that represents a specific type of natural environment, contains distinctive ecosystems, threatened, rare and vulnerable natural features, constitutes a special geological formation and has particular scientific value. The main objective is to preserve the conservation values without significant external impact. The area is intended to serve as a reference area for research and monitoring.

herdla-naturreservat-natdc8dd2f5.d: Herdla Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Askøy and Meland in Hordaland, and encompasses shallow marine areas between Store Agnøy and Herdla, around Lammøya, Kvitholmane and parts of Herdla. The area is a distinctive and highly productive wetland with a rich and varied birdlife. The reserve was established on 28 June 1985.

kvist-naturreservat-natdc1ddeea.d: Kvist Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Sognefjord in Høyanger municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 21 June 2019 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to protect a forest area that is particularly important for biodiversity, as it contains many types of forest and vegetation, including rich deciduous forest and high-altitude pine and birch forests. Furthermore, the aim is to protect an area that represents a specific type of natural environment, as large parts of it consist of primeval mountain forest, in addition to highly productive old lowland pine forest, and a continuous gradient from the fjord to the mountains.”

sagvatnet-naturreservat-natead0fbb2.d: Sagvatnet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bømlo municipality. It comprises an area on Bømlo. The nature reserve borders the Tjongspollen Nature Reserve to the south, which was designated on 21 June 2017. The area was designated on 17 December 1999. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Outside existing roads, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard a forest area with all its natural flora and fauna. Among its special features, it is worth noting that the area constitutes one of the largest and westernmost pine forest sites in outer Western Norway.’

yddal-naturreservat-natda6ac2de.d: Yddal Nature Reserve is situated on the peninsula between Hardangerfjord to the east and Bjørnafjord to the west. The three Yddal farms, which lie at the heart of the area, were in operation until the 1950s. Apart from a short stretch of road leading to Botsvatnet in the west, most of the reserve lies more than 1 km away from major human interventions such as roads, power lines, etc. There are very few such areas left in the lowlands. To the east, the reserve borders the Geitaknottene Nature Reserve. Together, they cover an area of 33 km². One of the threats to the natural environment is the spread of Sitka spruce from plantations established in the 1960s–80s.

skogafjellet-naturreservat-natcf9f1360.d: Skogafjellet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bømlo municipality. It comprises an area on Bømlo. The nature reserve borders the Tjongspollen Nature Reserve to the north, which was designated on 21 June 2017. The area was designated on 17 December 1999. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Outside existing roads, the use of bicycles, horses and carts, as well as horse riding, is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard a forest area with all its natural flora and fauna’. Notable features include the area’s continuous elevation gradient from 0 to 100 metres above sea level, where the landscape transitions from a rich calcareous pine forest with mountain avens and holly to a well-developed and unique purple heather pine forest.”

skarvatun-naturreservat-nate21b003c.d: Skarvatun Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kvinnherad municipality. It comprises an area by the Kvinnheradsfjord. The area was designated a protected area on 11 December 2020. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats in one of the most productive and varied forest areas in the lowlands of Western Norway’. Important habitat types include rich deciduous broad-leaved forest, rich swamp forest, calcareous pine forest, hollow oak trees and rich coastal scree slopes. Rare species of amphibians, vascular plants, lichens and insects have been recorded.

helin-plantepark-plantelivsfredning-nat9.d: Helin Plant Park was established by royal decree as early as 4 April 1930 under the name Helin National Botanical Park; today it is known as Helin Plant Park. The flora in the park is fully protected. The area covers 28,758 daa and is situated in the northern and south-western parts of Gilarfjellet near Helin in Vang, Valdres, Innlandet. On the western side of Gilarfjellet, and particularly beneath the peaks of Kruk and Skolt, there are extensive areas of scree. The bedrock, mainly phyllite, provides good soil and consequently a rich variety of vegetation. The area was first discovered as early as 1840 by Professor Matthias Numsen Blytt.

hovdsj-myrene-naturreservat-nat8de5cd0e.d: The Hovdsjømyrene Nature Reserve forms part of a large mire landscape in Stor-Elvdal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 7 December 2001. The reserve is included in the mire conservation plan. The nature reserve borders the Hemmeldalen Nature Reserve to the west. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve, in its natural state and as a landscape feature, part of a large, intact bog landscape consisting of mixed-stratified bogs, flat bogs and hill bogs, with associated vegetation and fauna, particularly birdlife.’ Bird species observed breeding in the reserve include the lapwing, the black-throated diver and the crane.

tufsingdalseskeren-naturreservat-natc6d0.d: The Tufsingdalseskeren Nature Reserve consists of two areas to the east of Tufsinga in Os municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 22 December 1989 on the basis of its Quaternary geology. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of natural historical interest with a long, continuous and well-formed esker, which is an important element in understanding the glacial retreat process in the Femund area.’

hynna-naturreservat-nat7df119f1.d: Hynna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gausdal municipality in the Innlandet region. The nature reserve is situated between Hornsjøen and Ropptjern in the Gausdal Vestfjell mountains, and has held Ramsar Site status since 2002 due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established in 1990 to preserve a large and varied wetland area and a bog. The area comprises a large and varied wetland landscape featuring bogs, marshes, lakes, ponds, streams, rivers and wooded glades. It is an important breeding ground for wetland birds. There are many birds and many bird species in the area, and vulnerable bird species have also been recorded.

steinfjellet-naturreservat-natbc644f6d.d: Steinfjellet Nature Reserve is a forested area on the western side of Steinfjellet’s northern peak, in Rendalen municipality. The reserve borders the Sølen Landscape Conservation Area to the east. Its conservation value lies in the old pine forest, which contains dead wood at all stages of decomposition. The forest is probably the oldest in the entire Sølen area, with trees aged between 400 and 500 years. The reserve therefore serves as an important dispersal site for species associated with old pine forest, including Red Listed species. In particular, wolf lichen is common here. Both the vegetation and wildlife within the reserve are protected against damage and destruction.

heggshuselva-naturreservat-natddc274bb.d: Heggshuselva Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Østre Toten municipality. It consists of a river gorge around the Heggshuselva river. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 November 2020 and extended on 6 December 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic on land and water is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Except on footpaths, Kongevegen and existing tractor tracks marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited.

bjellneset-naturreservat-nat104b718d.d: Bjellneset Nature Reserve is a three-part reserve in Eidskog municipality, comprising 1) Bjellneset itself in Helgesjøen, 2) the largest island in Vesle Helgesjøen, and 3) the largest section south of the Ingelsrudøya/Øya Indre property, between Vesle Helgesjøen, Possevatnet and the Swedish border. The area is gently undulating with hills and hollows. The bedrock consists of gneiss, which results in nutrient-poor soil. The hills are covered in heather-pine forest, whilst blueberry-spruce forest dominates the slopes and hollows. In places, there is richer vegetation, such as low-herb spruce forest, rich fens and swamp forest. The presence of more demanding species such as bluebells suggests runoff from more mineral-rich soil or richer alluvial deposits.

brettingsmoen-naturreservat-nat8df87c20.d: Brettingsmoen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lom municipality. The area borders Reinheimen National Park to the north and the Finndalen Landscape Conservation Area to the south. The reserve was designated on 24 November 2006. It forms part of the conservation plan for national parks and other major protected areas. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a largely untouched natural area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area is of particular value because it is a well-defined natural forest area of pine that has not been subject to recent human intervention.”

r-ssj-en-naturreservat-natd3e71636.d: The Røssjøen Nature Reserve is situated adjacent to Langsua National Park in the municipalities of Etnedal, Nord-Aurdal and Nordre Land. The area covers 24,102 daa and was designated a nature reserve on 11 March 2011. The nature reserve contains lakes of varying sizes, large bogs and dry ridges with old coniferous and tall herbaceous woodland. The area is influenced by grazing and is important for rare bird and plant species. The Røssjøen Nature Reserve forms part of the management plan for Langsua National Park.

myldingi-naturreservat-natf6419d14.d: Myldingi Nature Reserve is a nature reserve situated west of the River Atna in the municipalities of Sør-Fron and Folldal in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 1989 to ‘preserve a distinctive landscape in which Quaternary geological features constitute a significant part of the landscape’s character’. The reserve was extended in 1993 as part of the conservation plan for Rondane. It lies between 700 and 1,300 metres above sea level, north-west of Lake Atnsjøen, east of Rondane National Park and west of the Atnsjømyrene Nature Reserve.

melasmoen-naturreservat-nat6ce7559d.d: Melåsmoen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Heradsbygda, in the municipality of Elverum in the Innlandet region. The reserve protects an area of approximately 120 dekar of sandy pine forest near the Jømna/Heradsbygd ski stadium. There are several mounds of drifting sand in the area. The nature reserve was established on 7 December 2018. Such dry sand pine forests are an important habitat for, amongst other things, soil-dwelling mycorrhizal fungi. In Norway, one of the core areas for this habitat type lies along the Glåma river in the municipalities of Elverum and Åmot. The reserve is considered to be of great importance in both a regional and national context, as there are very few protected areas specifically designated to safeguard the vegetation in sandy pine forests.

galaskarven-natureservat-natcf30865b.d: The Gålaskarven Nature Reserve is an area in Stor-Elvdal on the southern side of Imsdalen and around the Gålaskarven mountain peak, excluding a wedge-shaped section to the east along the road from Gålaveien. The area is connected to the Imsdalen Nature Reserve at Bjørnskarven and the municipal boundary with Ringebu to the west. The area is of great value as it comprises old and almost untouched coniferous forest. Parts of the area lie within the middle boreal vegetation zone, whilst the remainder lies within the northern boreal zone. Several Red Listed species of lichen are found here, including taiga needle lichen and spruce-grey lichen, as well as the fungi taiga skin, wrinkled skin and rose-coloured polypore. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic is prohibited.

eldaa-naturreservat-nat11626159.d: Eldåa Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Stor-Elvdal municipality. It comprises an area on the border with Øyer municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 December 2015 and extended on 7 December 2018. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited, except on paths, tractor tracks and roads marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area with a specific type of natural environment in the form of a stream gorge and large areas of old-growth forest with primeval forest characteristics, and forest with natural dynamics, in addition to the various types of demanding and rare plant, lichen and fungus species found in the area.

skjeftkj-len-naturreservat-nat0ff69e34.d: Skjeftkjølen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Trysil municipality. It consists of a bog area by Lake Rysjøen and borders the Rysjøen Wildlife Sanctuary. The area was designated a nature reserve on 18 December 1981 and extended on 15 March 2019. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large natural area comprising a mosaic of forest and marshland, with a wide variety of coniferous forest types, including stands of old spruce forest. Furthermore, the aim is to protect an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it provides a habitat for a number of vulnerable and rare species associated with wetland areas characterised by a rich variety of birdlife, old-growth forest and deadwood.

imsdalen-naturreservat-nat6e70810d.d: The Imsdalen Nature Reserve is situated on both sides of the Ims Lakes in the far east of Ringebu municipality, along the border with Stor-Elvdal municipality. The reserve also extends some distance south-west into Samdalen and north-west along the River Åsta. In the far south-east, the reserve borders the Gålaskarven Nature Reserve in Stor-Elvdal. The area is relatively unspoilt and boasts an unusually rich diversity of lichens and fungi associated with old-growth forest.

lagendeltaet-fuglefredningsomrade-natfe5.d: The Lågendeltaet Bird Sanctuary is situated on the western side of the Lågendeltaet Nature Reserve in Fåberg and stretches from the mouth of the Gausa river southwards between the Gudbrandsdalslågen and Jørstadmoen. The area is an important breeding and wintering ground for birds, with a very high diversity of species. It is also a very important migration site along the inland migration route in Eastern Norway. The bird sanctuary comprises a large proportion of cultivated land, which complements the varied natural and landscape features of the adjacent nature reserve. Birdlife is protected against harm and destruction. All hunting and the use of firearms, as well as letting dogs run free, are prohibited.

honnsr-ve-naturreservat-nat320fc057.d: Honnsrøve Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Skjåk municipality. It comprises an area by Lake Vuluvatnet. It borders Breheimen National Park. The area was designated a protected area on 10 June 2005. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna’. Notable features include the area’s large size, the fact that it has been largely unaffected by human intervention, that parts of the area consist of pine forest, and that it is home to one of Europe’s largest known populations of the species wolf lichen.”

fuggdalen-naturreservat-nat654a0117.d: The Fuggdalen Nature Reserve covers the entire catchment area of the River Fugga, between Steinfjellet and Fuggsjøvola/Kvernnesvola, down to its confluence with the River Mistra. The reserve borders the Sølen Landscape Conservation Area to the east. The conservation values are linked to an entire catchment area free of roads or other human interventions, apart from a mountain farm and a few holiday cottages. The reserve contains habitat types such as ravines, stream gorges, spring outcrops with spring vegetation, spruce swamp forest and berry-heather pine forest. The forest shows traces of past felling but now has a good age distribution, including deadwood and windfalls. Both the vegetation and wildlife in the reserve are protected against damage and destruction.

bergevika-naturreservat-nat2c63fbf2.d: Bergevika Nature Reserve comprises an area at Bergevika on Helgøya in Ringsaker municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 December 2014 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area containing threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats’. The reserve comprises two sub-areas, both of which are important for understanding the fossil-bearing rock formations of the Oslo Field and which feature herb-rich dry calcareous pine forest, moss-rich shallow-rooted calcareous coniferous forest, sun-exposed limestone cliffs, rich low-herb spruce forest, riparian forest and pasture woodland with ash and grey alder. These regionally rare vegetation types contain a large number of rare plants and fungi.

atnsj-myrene-naturreservat-nat4fe08d39.d: The Atnsjømyrene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site along the River Atna in the municipalities of Folldal, Stor-Elvdal and Sør-Fron in the Innlandet region. The reserve was established in 2001 ‘to preserve the area in its natural state and as a landscape feature, and to conserve its associated flora and fauna’. Atnsjømyrene is a complex of large flat bogs comprising overgrown pools, tall sedge marshes and fringe zones with willow. The bogs are of great importance to birdlife. The bogs are situated at an altitude of approximately 700 metres above sea level, north-west of Lake Atnsjøen, east of Rondane National Park and the Myldingi Nature Reserve. The area was designated a Ramsar site in 2011.

oppsj-myra-naturreservat-natf11e74ac.d: Oppsjømyra Nature Reserve is situated in the Gausdal Vestfjell/Synnfjell area, in the municipalities of Gausdal and Nordre Land. The nature reserve covers 14,802 daa and was established on 11 March 2011. Oppsjømyra is a large marshland area comprising rich fens, natural pastureland, old spruce forest and tall-shrub birch forest. The area boasts great biodiversity and a rich and distinctive birdlife. The reserve is considered to be of great educational importance. Oppsjømyra Nature Reserve borders Langsua National Park and is included in its conservation plan.

h-vringslia-naturreservat-nat16a0f625.d: Høvringslia Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sel municipality. It is situated on a west-facing valley slope in Gudbrandsdalen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve forms part of the forest conservation plan. Open fires are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a specific type of natural environment in the form of lowland forest comprising relatively rich, coarse-grained, highly productive pine forest and rich boreal deciduous forest. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it is home to threatened lichen species that are typical of parts of the main valley in Gudbrandsdalen and for which the region has a special responsibility. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’ As of

gammeldalsberget-naturreservat-nat71acee.d: The Gammeldalsberget Nature Reserve borders the Gammeldalen Nature Reserve and is situated in Tynset municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 25 November 2016 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve an area comprising various types of old coniferous forest with elements of springand tall herbaceous vegetation, and which is of particular importance for biodiversity as it contains, and has the potential to support, demanding and Red Listed plant and fungus species. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

bj-rndalen-naturreservat-nat13fc080c.d: Bjørndalen Nature Reserve is situated in a western side valley of Einunndalen in Folldal municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 22 December 1989 and is included in the conservation plan for Quaternary geology. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a distinctive landscape and an area of natural historical interest with important Quaternary geological features, including well-formed terraces at various levels.’

grimsdalsmyrene-naturreservat-nat16ddcdb.d: The Grimsdalsmyrene Nature Reserve consists of a mire area near Grimse in Dovre municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 18 January 1985 and is included in the conservation plan for mires. The nature reserve borders Rondane National Park to the south-east and lies not far from Dovre National Park in the opposite direction. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a particularly rich and varied area of bogs and wetlands with very interesting vegetation and flora, particularly with a view to phytogeographical and plant sociological studies.’

bukollen-naturreservat-natd0995190.d: The Bukollen Nature Reserve was established on 28 June 1985 to ‘[p]reserve typical high-altitude coniferous forest slopes, which are of particular importance to wildlife.’ The nature reserve covers an area of 3,199 dekar and is surrounded on all sides, except to the south, by the Vassfaret and Vidalen landscape conservation area. The reserve is mainly situated in Flå municipality, but parts of it (approx. 400 da) extend into Sør-Aurdal municipality in Innlandet. Just to the east of the Bukollen Nature Reserve lies the Vikerfjell Nature Reserve in Ringerike municipality in Buskerud.

nordhueh-gda-naturreservat-nat8d51e58a.d: The Nordhuehøgda Nature Reserve is situated in the north-west of Elverum municipality, on the northern side of Mount Nordhue. The terrain is gently undulating and varied, featuring marshy areas and, in places, old spruce forest, interspersed with some pine and deciduous woodland. This provides favourable conditions for a number of Red List species. Species such as old man’s beard, spreading beard and wolf lichen have been recorded in the area. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised vehicles are not permitted. Cycling and horse riding are also prohibited outside existing roads and paths.

gitvola-og-nordre-kletten-naturreservat-.d: The Gitvola and Nordre Kletten Nature Reserve has been established in the south-west of Åmot municipality, on the north-eastern side of the Gitvola mountain. The lower peak of Nordre Kletten is also situated to the north-east of the area. Between these peaks lies the Storkjølen marshland, which forms the watershed between the rivers Jernåa and Gita. The area is covered with old spruce forest interspersed with large areas of marshland, and is of great importance for biodiversity. Several Red List species have been found here, such as the hollow-stemmed sedge, the grey soot cup, the spruce lichen and the rusty dog’s-tooth. The flora and fauna are protected against damage and destruction. Motorised traffic is not permitted. Cycling and horse riding are also prohibited outside existing roads and paths.

tors-ter-naturreservat-nat8208bc5f.d: The Torseter Nature Reserve comprises three small areas along the River Brumunda, just north of Torsætra in Ringsaker municipality. The exposed river banks reveal a complete stratigraphic profile through the layered, sedimentary rocks from the Ordovician and Silurian periods. These are the northernmost outcrops discovered in the Oslo Field. The shales contain abundant graptolite fossils. Within the reserve, all interference with the ground is prohibited, including the removal and deposition of earth, as well as hammering, chiselling, blasting and the collection of samples. It is also forbidden to scratch or paint on rocks and boulders, or to light fires.

hersj-myrin-naturreservat-nat232bd2ce.d: Hersjømyrin Nature Reserve is situated on the west bank of the River Vinstra, in the south-west of Nord-Fron municipality. The reserve also encompasses a small part of Sør-Fron municipality (Nedre Hersjøen). To the south, the reserve borders Langsua National Park, and it is included in the conservation plan for Langsua. The reserve contains several different habitat types, including mountain birch forest, old coniferous forest, natural pastureland, springs and open water, as well as various types of bog. The area boasts a great diversity of both plants and animals. Seventy-two bird species have been recorded, of which 62 are documented as breeding or likely to breed within the reserve. Furthermore, 26 Red List species have been recorded, 21 of which are birds. Of these, the lapwing and the black-headed gull are classified as critically endangered (CR).

engene-naturreservat-nat3de3a1fc.d: Engene Nature Reserve consists of a delta area where the rivers Haugsåa and Trautåa meet and flow into Lake Råsen in Nord-Odal municipality. A small area along the Trautåa has been excluded from the reserve, which is otherwise surrounded by farmland to the east and west. The area comprises meanders, cut-off oxbow lakes, floodplains and swamp forest. The vegetation varies from floating-leaf vegetation in open water bodies, through sedge marshes with rushes, bog areas with extensive tussock-rich fens dominated by bog myrtle and blue moor grass, to spruce-dominated woodland with many deciduous trees. Wildlife is protected against damage and unnecessary disturbance. The same applies to all vegetation, including dead shrubs and trees. However, hunting and the gathering of berries and mushrooms are permitted.

s-len-landskapsvernomrade-natfd4b2d8e.d: The Sølen Landscape Conservation Area comprises the mountainous area around Sølen in Rendalen municipality, including Lake Sølensjøen south of Fiskevollen, as well as Mistdalen down to its confluence with the Renåa. The area borders the Fuggdalen Nature Reserve to the south-west. The purpose of the conservation is to safeguard a natural and cultural landscape with geological features and biological diversity. Here, the public should have the opportunity to enjoy simple outdoor recreation with a minimal level of infrastructure. The conservation regulations set out a wide range of prohibited activities, including road construction, the building of bridges and footbridges, the clearing and marking of paths, landfilling, and the removal of boulders, stones and fossils, amongst many other things.

einstullie-naturreservat-nat32e54d23.d: Einstullie Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Skjåk municipality. It comprises an area near Billingen. It borders Reinheimen National Park to the north and east. The area was designated a nature reserve on 25 January 2013. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and horse riding are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area of old-growth pine forest characterised by the presence of several rare and vulnerable species of fungi and lichens, including healthy populations of wolf lichen. Furthermore, the aim of the nature reserve is to preserve an area of particular value for biodiversity in terms of habitat types, ecosystems, plant and animal species, and natural ecological processes.

hemmeldalen-naturreservat-nat99f3f0f0.d: Hemmeldalen Nature Reserve is situated on the Hedmarksvidda plateau between Åstadalen and Østerdalen, south of the Birkebeinervegen. The reserve was established as a follow-up to the New National Plan for National Parks and Other Major Protected Areas in Norway (White Paper No. 62 (1991–92)). The area is an important summer grazing and calving ground for the wild reindeer in southern Rondane. It is also the only remaining wilderness area of any size in central Østerdalen. The conservation measures will also help to preserve a diversity of vulnerable habitat types, along with their associated flora and fauna, associated with bogs, wetlands and coniferous forests. In the interests of the wild reindeer, the area has been added to the portfolio of the Rondane-Dovre National Park Board.

gammeldalen-naturreservat-nata7d5c457.d: The Gammeldalen Nature Reserve borders the Gammeldalsberget Nature Reserve and is situated in Tynset municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 22 December 1989 on account of its Quaternary geology. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a distinctive landscape and an area of natural historical interest with important Quaternary geological features, including eskers, terraces and kettle holes.’

h-yrokampen-naturreservat-nat7e189c6a.d: Høyrokampen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lom municipality. The area borders Breheimen National Park and the Høydalen Landscape Conservation Area. The area was designated a nature reserve on 7 August 2009. The reserve forms part of the conservation plan for national parks and other major protected areas. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area containing rare and endangered vascular plants, lichens, mosses and fungi. The area is of particular value as a botanical site. Furthermore, the aim of the nature reserve is to preserve an area of particular value for biodiversity in terms of habitat types, ecosystems, plant and animal species, and natural ecological processes.

dokkajuvet-naturreservatet-natbb8516e2.d: The Dokkajuvet Nature Reserve comprises an area in Nordre Land municipality, north of Dokka, where the River Dokka flows through a deep ravine. The area was designated a protected area on 19 March 2021 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large, varied and well-developed ravine with rich forest types such as low-herb forest and tall-shrub spruce forest. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity as it provides a habitat for a great many rare, vulnerable and endangered species, particularly lichens, fungi and mosses.

akersvika-naturreservat-nat02bee676.d: Åkersvika Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Ramsar site in Åkersvika, in the municipalities of Hamar and Stange in the Innlandet region. Åkersvika Nature Reserve is an important area for a number of different bird species. It was designated by royal decree on 26 July 1974, making the reserve Norway’s first Ramsar site. The reserve was extended in 1984 and 1992. The purpose of the designation was to preserve an important wetland area with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. In particular, the area is important as a resting and breeding ground for wetland birds. Bird counts in the reserve between 1974 and 2013 show that the most common species in both spring and autumn is the mallard.

ekebergskraningen-naturreservat-natcf9ad.d: The Ekeberg Slope, or Ekebergskråninga, is a nature reserve covering approximately 800 dekar (mål) adjacent to Oslo city centre. The slope lies partly in the Gamle Oslo district and partly in the Nordstrand district, and forms the sun-drenched western slope of Ekeberg, which descends towards the Oslo Fjord and Bjørvika. The slope is largely wooded and lies close to Oslo city centre. The lower part of the woodland – that is, roughly the area within the 1878 city boundary – is often referred to as Ekebergskauen. The slope is an important hiking and recreational area for residents of the eastern part of the city centre and the Nordstrand district. The Oslo region’s oldest recorded cultural heritage sites are also located here.

gressholmen-ramberg-ya-naturreservat-nat.d: The Gressholmen-Rambergøya Nature Reserve was established in 1992. In 2008, the neighbouring Heggholmen was also designated a nature reserve. The nature reserve covers both land and water and is a wetland reserve intended to preserve a shallow-water area with rich plant and animal life, as well as valuable flora and geological features. Motorised traffic is prohibited all year round. Between 1 April and 15 July, windsurfing, rowing boats and other boats are also prohibited. As with the other islands in the Inner Oslo Fjord, there are many rare plants on Gressholmen and Rambergøya. ‘The number of Red List species is high, and the area contains large tracts of threatened vegetation types that are rare even by international standards.’

l-rensetertjern-naturreservat-nat28e053b.d: The Lørensetertjern Nature Reserve is situated south-east of Blankvann in Nordmarka, Oslo municipality, and is surrounded by the Blankvann Landscape Conservation Area. The purpose of designating the Lørensetertjern Nature Reserve is to preserve a mire landscape consisting of many small mires with varied vegetation, where several rare and demanding species are found. The bogs lie in depressions in the terrain, interspersed with low ridges covered in coniferous forest. Several streams flow through the site, with Hølbekken from Blankvann being the main watercourse. The area forms a mire complex comprising many small mires within a relatively sparse coniferous forest landscape. Mires influenced by groundwater are most common, but areas of rain-fed mires also occur.

karussputten-naturreservat-nat012f42e8.d: Karusspytten Nature Reserve is situated in Oslomarka, east of Sørkedalen, bordering the Blankvann Landscape Conservation Area. The name is also often spelled Karussputten. The area is a largely unspoilt forest and bog landscape featuring many distinctive types of vegetation.

adalselva-naturreservat-nat7f66f33a.d: The Ådalselva Nature Reserve (approximately 2,012 daa, of which approximately 103 daa is land area) was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Act No. 19 June 2009 No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the management of biodiversity (the Nature Diversity Act), Section 34, cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The nature reserve forms part of the Ådalselva river in Ringerike municipality, Buskerud, and is part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. The purpose of the nature reserve is to conserve a habitat type in the form of a distinctive and coherent river system with several meanders, bays, inlets and ponds connected to the main channel. The shallow sections of the Begna are particularly important for overwintering whooper swans and other wetland birds.

finnemarka-naturreservat-nat957ec4f6.d: Finnemarka is a forested area covering around 430 square kilometres, situated in Buskerud county. Finnemarka is bordered by Tyrifjorden to the north, Lierdalen to the east, and the built-up areas along the Drammenselva to the west and south. Finnemarka is divided between the municipalities of Modum, Lier, Drammen and Øvre Eiker. The south-eastern part of Finnemarka is also known as Drammensmarka. Finnemarka is named after the Finns who settled in the area in the 17th century. However, west of Glitre, there are traces of settlements dating as far back as the 14th century. The highest point is Brennåsen (703.5 metres above sea level), in the north of Finnemarka. The bedrock consists of Drammen granite. The northern part of the forest is protected as the Finnemarka Nature Reserve.

trollmyr-naturreservat-nat8a100c46.d: Trollmyr Nature Reserve is situated just west of Ringiåsen, and adjoins Ringiåsen Nature Reserve in the west of Bærum municipality. The area consists of a black alder swamp forest in a wide stream valley. The water table is high, and Skvallerbekken flows through the area from north to south. Parts of the area are periodically flooded. The purpose of the reserve is to preserve a well-developed swamp forest with a rich variety of plant species.

dem-rk-naturreservat-nat8f039540.d: The Ødemørk Nature Reserve is situated at the southernmost tip of Vestby municipality, east of European Route 6 between Kambo and Rød. The reserve borders the Ishavet Nature Reserve to the east and Mossemarka to the south. The area is widely used for recreation and outdoor activities. The entire area lies below the marine limit. The bedrock consists of various types of granitic gneiss, and the soil is thin in many places. The vegetation is dominated by calcareous coniferous forest, but with a significant proportion of deciduous trees and variation depending on the topography. The area is highly productive in places, and this type of forest is rare here, as such areas are often cultivated. Five core areas are considered important for biodiversity.

furuasen-og-hagahogget-naturreservat-nat.d: The Furuåsen and Hagahogget Nature Reserve in Asker Municipality was established on 16 December 2016 following an extension of the Hagahogget Nature Reserve. The nature reserve is situated approximately four kilometres west of Asker town centre and borders the Semsvannet landscape conservation area to the east. It consists of gently undulating terrain, steep slopes, ravines and flatter areas. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a varied forest area of particular importance for biodiversity. The nature reserve features a wide variety of vegetation types and rich transition zones between deciduous and coniferous forests. South-facing mountain slopes serve as breeding grounds for birds of prey.

fjella-og-burumtjern-naturreservat-natur.d: Fjella Nature Reserve is a forested area in the municipalities of Marker and Rakkestad that was designated a nature reserve in 2013. The Regulations on the Protection of the Fjella Nature Reserve, Marker and Rakkestad Municipalities, Østfold describe the purpose of establishing the nature reserve as follows: ‘The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a large area of mature pine and spruce forest, together with its naturally occurring species, habitat types and ecological processes. The reserve serves as a reference area for this habitat type and is of particular scientific value. The area is of particular importance for biodiversity, with the presence of rare and vulnerable species and habitat types.

gas-ya-naturreservat-nat2e4a29bc.d: The Gåsøya Nature Reserve comprises two separate areas on the north-western side of Gåsøya in Bærum municipality. The areas feature coastal marshes, salt meadows and rocky shores, with a rich variety of plant life. The southern area is home to, amongst other things, a large population of sea rush. In the northern area (Rosenholmen), we find the red-listed Norwegian priority species dragon’s head. Other species found here include spiked speedwell, deer’s-tongue and liquorice. Both the vegetation and wildlife in the reserve are protected against damage and destruction, and it is not permitted to carry out activities that may alter the natural environment. Furthermore, camping and pitching tents are prohibited in the reserve, and campfires are only permitted in designated areas.

vestfjella-naturreservat-nat8f1346fd.d: The Vestfjella Nature Reserve is situated to the west of Lake Aremarksjøen, on the border between the municipalities of Aremark and Halden. The area is a relatively flat plateau just above the marine limit, approximately 200 metres above sea level. The forest here exhibits late-stage developmental characteristics and is one of the closest things to primeval forest found in the lowlands of the county. The area is characterised by bogs, small ponds and sparse pine forest. The Eurasian thrush and the redstart are characteristic species here.

viksasen-naturreservat-nat61eb03ae.d: The Vikåsen Nature Reserve and the Biliåsen Landscape Conservation Area are situated in Hole municipality in Buskerud and cover a combined area of 535 dekar. The areas lie just north of the centre of Vik and were designated as protected areas on 12 February 1982. Calcareous and nutrient-rich soil, limited water availability and high summer temperatures form the basis for the distinctive vegetation found in the conservation area. Common species include red campion, bluebell, lily of the valley and blood-red cranesbill. White and yellow rock cress and mountain mint are also typical. The limestone that makes up Vikåsen and Biliåsen (cuesta ridges) was formed during the Silurian period, between 440 and 395 million years ago. At that time, the area was covered by a shallow sea. Large numbers of corals, shells and other animals lived on the seabed.

v-leren-biotopvernomrade-nat24d06142.d: The Væleren Biotope Conservation Area (106 daa, of which approximately 16 daa is land area) was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 100 of 19 June 2009 on the management of biodiversity (the Nature Diversity Act), Section 34, cf. Sections 38 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The area is situated in Lake Væleren in Holleia, near Tyristrand in Ringerike Municipality, Buskerud, and forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. The biotope conservation area covers the islets of Geitøya, Flatøya and Lomøya, together with Nordre, Midtre and Søndre Lomøyskjæret, Smalskjæret and Gåseskjæret in Lake Væleren, and a 50-metre zone around each islet. South of Søndre Lomøyskjæret, towards Høgøya, the boundary of the conservation area runs through the middle of the sound.

fuglemoseh-gde-naturreservat-nat86d39098.d: Fuglemosehøgda Nature Reserve is situated in the northern part of Trømborgfjella, on the border between the municipalities of Marker and Indre Østfold in Østfold. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a relatively undisturbed forest area that is representative of low-lying regions above the marine limit on bedrock in south-eastern Norway. The area possesses important qualities as a habitat for capercaillie.

isi-naturreservat-nat3cc85b86.d: The Isi Nature Reserve largely comprises a south-west-facing slope up towards Gaupeberget, east of Kjaglidalen in Bærum.
