The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry and basalt. The area features a very wide variety of vegetation types, many of which are in a relatively undisturbed state. There is a high density of key elements for biodiversity here. Several Red List species are found here, including one of our northernmost populations of wild garlic.

stilla-og-brauterstilla-naturreservat-na.d: The Stilla and Brauterstilla Nature Reserves consist of two separate oxbow lakes with riparian zones and vegetation along the banks of the lower reaches of the Leira, north-east of the town of Lillestrøm. The two areas border on and are linked by the Holmen Nature Reserve to the east. The reserve also includes meanders, which are a Red Listed habitat type in Norway. Red Listed plant and animal species are also found here, including the critically endangered corncrake. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but it is permitted to pick edible mushrooms and berries. Campfires are also permitted in accordance with current regulations.

ishavet-naturreservat-nat480c4e89.d: The Ishavet Nature Reserve is a bog area in the very south of Vestby municipality, extending slightly into Moss municipality. The bog lies in a valley running north-west to south-east and is a groundwater-fed (minerotrophic) flat bog. Flat bogs are typical of the south-western parts of Akershus, and Ishavet is one of the few such bogs that remain intact. The small orchid, the bog orchid, is found here; this species has been in decline since the 1980s and is therefore being considered for inclusion on the Red List.

linnesstranda-naturreservat-natc6c99675.d: Linnesstranda Nature Reserve is situated in the municipality of Lier, at the mouth of the Lierelva where it flows into the Drammensfjord, and was established by royal decree on 28 June 1985. On 14 December 2007, the protected area was extended as part of the conservation plan for the Oslofjord. The area now covers 593 dekar.[1] It is a wetland area that has been formed as the mouth of the River Lierelva has shifted over time, depositing large amounts of alluvial material. The area is of great botanical and ornithological value. The reserve is incredibly lush, and this has only increased since it was designated a nature reserve in 1985. It is probably one of the closest things you’ll find to a tropical primeval forest in Norway.

holmen-naturreservat-nata6925d58.d: Holmen Nature Reserve is situated on a river plain within a meander bend on the west bank of the River Leira in Lillestrøm municipality. The area borders on farmland to the west and on the River Leira elsewhere; the woodland grows on marine clay and is frequently flooded. The vegetation type is grey alder-hawthorn forest with a fringe of goat willow thickets along the river. The tree layer is dominated by grey alder. The shrub layer is very dense, comprising hawthorn, red elder and wayfaring tree, whilst the ground layer is lush with an abundance of large ferns. This is a homogeneous and well-developed grey alder-hawthorn forest within a distinctive cultural landscape.

mellemskj-r-naturreservat-nata8b75220.d: The Mellemskjær Nature Reserve comprises a skerry and the surrounding waters, on the north side of Gåsøya in the municipality of Bærum. The skerry was once home to one of the Oslofjord’s largest colonies of black-headed gulls. In 2005, an increasing number of grey gulls were recorded, though there were still significant numbers of black-headed gulls. In addition, lesser black-backed gulls, oystercatchers and eider ducks breed here. The reserve is connected to the Terneskjær Nature Reserve to the east. Access to the area is prohibited, both on land and at sea, from 15 April to 15 July.

skaugumsasen-og-astad-naturreservat-nat3.d: The Skaugumsåsen and Åstad Nature Reserve comprises the steep south-western and south-eastern slopes of Skaugumsåsen, as well as the valley floor at Åstad in Asker municipality. The nature reserve was established on 27 November 2020 through the merger of the Skaugumsåsen Nature Reserve and the Åstad Nature Reserve. The area is characterised by rock faces with underlying scree slopes. The bedrock is quite similar to that found at Kolsås, with sedimentary rocks from the Cambrian–Silurian period at the base, overlain by the lava rocks basalt and rhomboid porphyry. This provides nutrient-rich soil and a suitable habitat for deciduous broad-leaved forest. The reserve contains ‘one of the country’s finest examples of a stable elm-lime forest, with its associated ground vegetation and wildlife’.

nordre-skaugumsasen-naturreservat-nat56b.d: The Nordre Skaugumsåsen Nature Reserve in Asker municipality was established on 20 December 2019. The nature reserve is situated in the south-eastern part of the plateau on Skaugumsåsen. To the west, south and east, the area borders Skaugumsåsen and Åstad Nature Reserves, with steep cliffs and deciduous broad-leaved woodland. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an area representing a habitat type characterised by a species-rich spruce forest and a varied mix of deciduous woodland and rich swamp forest. The bedrock on the plateau consists mainly of rhomboid porphyry. The birdlife in the area is rich in species diversity. The forest is to be allowed to develop naturally, without any management measures. The area is widely used as a local outdoor recreation area, and there is a marked trail running through it.

alv-naturreservat-nat087e8299.d: The Alv Nature Reserve encompasses the islet of Alv, west of Langodden/Fornebulandet in Bærum municipality. There used to be a large colony of black-headed gulls on the islet, but by 2005 they had disappeared. The site is now home to black-headed gulls, grey gulls and eider ducks. Access to the area is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July, and dogs are not permitted at any time of year.

kolsasstupene-naturreservat-nat39381f78.d: The Kolsåsstupene Nature Reserve encompasses the steep slopes and cliffs on the western, southern and eastern sides of Kolsåstoppen in Bærum. The area’s conservation values lie in both its geological features and its vegetation. In the lower part, the mountain consists of sedimentary rocks from the Silurian period: limestone at the base, overlain by sandstone, clay shale and conglomerate. At the top are lava rocks from the Permian period: basalt and rhomboid porphyry. The vegetation is rich, with nutrient-demanding plants on ledges in the cliffs, and otherwise largely deciduous broad-leaved woodland.

m-rrapanna-naturreservat-natc6a2266e.d: Mærrapanna is a nature reserve and a recreational area with a bathing spot in Fredrikstad municipality in Østfold. The area is situated on the south side of Hankøsundet, near County Road 117 between Vikane and Slevik. The site features extensive smooth granite outcrops, stunning rock formations and varied vegetation. The granite is more or less orange in colour. Mærrapanna Nature Reserve was established on 21 June 1996 and covers an area of just over 96 dekar. The area comprising the bathing spot features a large grassy plain and low-growing vegetation of pine and deciduous trees, interspersed with the occasional stray fruit tree dating from the time when the area contained several smallholdings belonging to Slevig Østre farm.

peters-tra-og-trestikledalen-naturreserv.d: The Petersætra and Trestikledalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the border between the municipalities of Drammen and Holmestrand. The terrain in the area consists of coarse-grained granite with bare rock, peat and marshland. The vegetation in the area consists mainly of spruce forest, pine forest and mixed coniferous forest. The reserve covers a total of 3,392 dekar spread across two areas. The area is hilly with forested peaks reaching up to 323 metres above sea level. The reserve was established in 2020.

elnestangen-naturreservat-nat95dd9515.d: Elnestangen Nature Reserve in Asker municipality was established on 15 January 1988. It is situated at Elnestangen, south of Vollen, between Håkavik and Sjøstrand. The nature reserve encompasses large parts of the shoreline at Elnestangen, spread across three separate areas. The purpose of the conservation is to protect an important site for understanding the fossil-bearing rocks of the Oslo Field. The rock strata on the eastern side of Elnestangen reveal a long, continuous stratigraphic profile through the oldest parts of the Middle Ordovician.

hvaler-prestegardskog-naturreservat-nat3.d: Hvaler Vicarage Wood Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hvaler municipality. It comprises an area adjacent to Hvaler Church. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing paths is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a sand pine forest, which is the only occurrence of this forest type recorded during the conservation planning process. The northernmost stand is the largest and best-preserved sand pine forest, with several stages of development represented, but the southern site also has interesting features, in addition to containing a slightly richer community such as low-herb pine forest.”

str-nes-naturreservat-nat21f8ce62.d: Strønes Nature Reserve is situated in a ravine landscape by Mønstervika at the southern end of Øyeren. The area is dominated by rich deciduous woodland, comprising grey alder-hawthorn woodland, grey alder-ash woodland and elm-lime woodland. This is the largest contiguous area in the county containing such broad-leaved woodland. Strønes Nature Reserve was granted protected forest status in December 2013.

gjellebekkmyrene-naturreservat-nat698c24.d: Gjellebekkmyrene Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Lier municipality in Buskerud. It is situated between the E18 at Liertoppen and Gamle Drammensvei, which runs parallel to the motorway on the north side. The nearest settlement is Hennummarka in Tranby. The nature reserve is home to several rare species of flowers. The area was designated a nature reserve on 30 June 1978. It covers an area of 458 da.

saltskj-r-biotopvernomrade-nat3437639b.d: The Saltskjær Biotope Conservation Area is situated almost in the centre of the Drammen Fjord, south of Svelvik. The bedrock consists of Drammen granite, and the skerry has little vegetation. The conservation area encompasses the skerry and the surrounding sea area within a 50-metre radius. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect seabirds, particularly great skuas, from disturbance during the breeding season. There is therefore a ban on access to the area, including the sea, from 15 April to 15 July.

langskj-r-naturreservat-nat99e6643b.d: Langskjær Nature Reserve consists of a skerry with the surrounding sea area 50 metres offshore, just north of Torvøya in Bærum municipality. The reserve is bordered to the north, east and south by Torvøya and the Bjerkholmen Nature Reserve. The islet features a well-developed limestone heath and salt marsh, home to the red-listed plant centaury. There used to be a large colony of black-headed gulls on Langskjær, but the site is now dominated by eider ducks, as well as a few pairs of breeding geese. It is not permitted to remove plants or parts of plants, such as flowers, from the area. There is also a ban on access to the area from 15 April to 15 July.

j-ndalsasen-med-flere-tjern-og-vann-dyre.d: The Jøndalsåsen Wildlife Sanctuary encompasses the Jøndalsåa river from Øvre Holsjøen down to its confluence with the Vorma, as well as a 10-metre-wide strip of shoreline. The area also includes Morttjernet, Ørekyttjernet and Fiskeløysa. All birdlife in the area is protected throughout the year. The boundaries marked on Norgeskartet.no do not correspond to the provisions of the conservation regulations, as Ørkytetjennet is not included in the area on the map. County Road 181 crosses the area in several places.

spirodden-naturreservat-nat2c5835a8.d: Spirodden Nature Reserve is situated on the south-eastern side of the Løkenes Peninsula, facing Blakstad Bay and Spire Bay in Asker municipality. The bedrock consists of fossil-bearing shale with limestone dating from the Silurian period. The calcareous soil provides a breeding ground for large populations of Red List species. The area features habitats such as calcareous pine forest, calcareous heathland and limestone outcrops, but in particular calcareous lime-tree forest, which is a designated habitat under the Nature Diversity Act. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected; it is also forbidden to chisel or grind on the rock, or to take samples from stones or solid rock. Camping and lighting fires are also prohibited.

torv-ya-og-bjerkholmen-naturreservat-nat.d: The Torvøya and Bjerkholmen Nature Reserve consists of two small islands and the surrounding sea area, west of Fornebulandet in Bærum municipality. The islands are virtually untouched and feature species-rich vegetation, including several Red List species. Motorised traffic is prohibited within the reserve, and it is not permitted to remove plants or parts of plants (flowers). For several years, Torvøya has been home to the largest colony of black-headed gulls in the inner Oslo Fjord.

steinsvika-naturreservat-nat787d465d.d: The Steinsvika Nature Reserve (approximately 263 daa) was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the management of biodiversity (the Nature Diversity Act), Section 34, cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The bay is situated in Steinsfjorden, between the Stein estate and Loretangen in Hole municipality, Buskerud. The nature reserve forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA and is directly adjacent to the Steinsfjorden biotope conservation area. The nature reserve is intended to preserve a wetland area of particular importance for biodiversity and a very rich flora and fauna. Steinsvika is of particular importance as a resting, breeding and foraging area for a large number of wetland birds.

trolldalen-naturreservat-nat8a25593c.d: Trolldalen Nature Reserve is situated in Svartskog, in the west of Nordre Follo municipality. The nature reserve borders the Svartskog Landscape Conservation Area on the plateau to the east, and slopes down towards Bunnefjorden to the west. In large parts of the reserve, the bedrock is exposed or covered by a thin layer of loose material, whilst in the valley bottoms there are thicker layers of moraine and possibly some river sediments. On the plateau to the east, there are also thin layers of marine sediments. The bedrock consists mainly of garnet-biotite gneiss and biotite-muscovite gneiss. The west-facing terrain, with plenty of sunshine and proximity to the fjord, provides a favourable local climate with warm summers and mild winters. In terms of plant geography, the area lies within the boreonemoral vegetation zone, in the slightly oceanic section.

rud-naturreservat-nat12304a8b.d: Rud Nature Reserve is situated on the slope rising from the western shore of Lake Øyeren, near Flateby in Enebakk municipality. The bedrock in the area consists of sandstone, alum shale and conglomerate, overlain by loose marine deposits. The vegetation consists of mature spruce forest with flood-influenced deciduous woodland in the form of grey alder and hawthorn forest below. There are also some exceptionally large and old ash trees here. Deadwood in various stages of decomposition and of varying sizes is also significant. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected, but picking berries and foraging for edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting, trapping and fishing are also permitted in accordance with current legislation.

steinsfjorden-biotopvernomrade-nat501233.d: The Steinsfjorden Biotope Conservation Area (approximately 3,825 daa, of which approximately 83 daa is land area) is situated in Steinsfjorden and was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 38 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The protected area forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. The biotope protection area includes the area from Garntangen and Vik and northwards along the western side and northern end of the lake, right up to Åsatangen. The protected area also includes the islands and the waters immediately surrounding Småøyene, Tjuvholmen, Maurøya, Bøtet, Gåsa, Suserudskjæret and Østbråtaskjæret, where boat traffic is prohibited during the breeding season.

dyna-naturreservat-nat065a5b41.d: xxx consists of four small islets off Slemmestad in Asker municipality. The area was designated a protected site on 15 December 1978 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 15 July inclusive, landing on the islets is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’ It is primarily black-headed gulls and common terns that breed here.

spannslokket-naturreservat-nata8803896.d: The Spannslokket Nature Reserve comprises the south-eastern and south-western parts of the islet of Spannslokket, situated between Furuholmen and Langåra in Asker. The bedrock consists of sedimentary rocks from the Cambrian–Silurian period. These areas in the Oslo Field are world-renowned and rich in fossils. At Spannslokket, the transition between the Ordovician and Silurian periods is clearly evident. The site is therefore of immense scientific value. Within the nature reserve, all interference with the ground is prohibited, including the removal and deposition of earth, as well as hammering, chiselling, blasting and the collection of samples. It is also forbidden to carve or paint on rocks and boulders, or to light fires.

langara-naturreservat-nat78ba6a05.d: The Langåra Nature Reserve comprises two separate areas on the island of Langåra off Brønnøya in Asker. The island consists of sedimentary rocks from the Ordovician and Silurian periods. The stratification of the rocks is clearly visible towards the south-east, and the south-western protected area is the type locality for the Langåra Formation. The calcareous rocks provide fertile ground for rich vegetation, including in the ‘calcareous dry grassland’ habitat type. Species found here include liquorice, wood clover, red campion and sea thistle. In the north-eastern part, there are also bays with marshes and salt meadows. On the salt meadows, we find, amongst others, sea arrowgrass and the red-listed centaury. Other species include sheep’s sorrel, ragwort, dwarf goldenrod and asparagus, amongst others.

terneskj-r-naturreservat-nat513efe78.d: Terneskjær Nature Reserve consists of a skerry and the sea extending approximately 50 metres around it, at the north-eastern tip of Gåsøya in Bærum municipality. The reserve borders Mellemskjær Nature Reserve to the south-west. The purpose of the reserve is to protect the habitat of flora and fauna, particularly seabirds. All access to the reserve is prohibited from 15 April to 15 July inclusive.

vassbunn-naturreservat-nat2fa7d9e9.d: The Vassbunn Nature Reserve (approximately 119 daa, of which approximately 57 dekar is land area) was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Act No. 19 June 2009 No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the management of biodiversity (the Nature Diversity Act), Section 34, cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The protected area is situated at Geithus in Modum municipality, Buskerud, and forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. The nature reserve is intended to preserve a rich wetland area of great value for biodiversity. The protected area is of particular importance as a breeding ground for wetland birds and other bird species associated with this habitat type. The objective is to maintain the conservation values in the best possible condition and, where possible, to further enhance them.

r-dsasen-naturreservat-nat8a578437.d: Rødsåsen Nature Reserve is situated on the south-western tip of Jeløya in Moss municipality, Østfold. The purpose of the reserve is to ‘preserve a forested area as an ecosystem, with all its natural flora and fauna, on Permian bedrock in the warmest summer regions of the country, in an exposed location adjacent to the Oslo Fjord’. With its strategic location almost in the middle of the Oslo Fjord, the summit of Rødsåsen was used in earlier times as a signal fire site, as marked on maps dating from 1776.

fosseterasen-naturreservat-nata1144110.d: Fosseteråsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Øvre Eiker municipality, in Buskerud county. Fosseteråsen is situated on the hill approximately 3 km west of Hakavik on the western shore of Lake Eikeren, in the hilly landscape between Lake Eikeren and the River Lågen. The reserve is situated beside the large, interconnected lakes of Øksne, Tistillen and Burvannet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 December 2015 and covers a total area of approximately 1,877 dekar. The purpose of the nature reserve is to preserve a varied forest area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area is distinctive in that it consists almost exclusively of mature and old-growth forest. Of particular importance are the stands of old natural spruce forest rich in deadwood.

frilset-naturreservat-nat8373f9fd.d: The Frilset Nature Reserve lies along the eastern bank of the Vorma, stretching from Jøndalsåa in Eidsvoll almost down to the border with Nes municipality. The area is characterised by ravines formed by ancient fjord and marine deposits. The vegetation consists largely of high-quality grey alder-elm and grey alder-hawthorn woodland. This is a rare and endangered habitat type. There is also some mixed woodland on shallower ground, which contributes to the area’s rich biological diversity.

stor-ysundet-s-labonn-naturreservat-nat2.d: The Storøysundet–Sælabonn Nature Reserve (5,733 daa, of which approximately 353 daa is land area) was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. Storøysundet–Sælabonn forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA and is situated in Hole municipality, Buskerud. The nature reserve is part of Tyrifjorden and encompasses Sælabonn and Storøysundet (including Haraøya and the skerries east of the island) and aims to conserve threatened and vulnerable natural habitats in the form of a large, contiguous wetland area of great ecological importance for flora and fauna.

ringiasen-naturreservat-nat7c90450b.d: The Ringiåsen Nature Reserve encompasses most of Ringiåsen, just south-west of Lake Stovivannet in western Bærum. The bedrock consists of rhomboid porphyry to the east and sandstone to the west. The soil is generally thin, but the vegetation is rich, particularly in the south-east. Here there is mixed woodland with long continuity, and plenty of deadwood at all stages of decomposition. There are grey alder-hawthorn forests, low-herb forests and elm-lime forests, as well as a number of vulnerable and endangered species. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Plants and animals are protected, but picking berries and foraging for edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting, trapping and fishing are also permitted in accordance with current legislation.

solgardhavna-naturreservat-nata01a3456.d: Solgårdhavna Nature Reserve is situated on the northern slope of the Ågårdselva river, just north of Solli Brug in Sarpsborg municipality. The vegetation consists of a black alder forest that is unique to Østfold. The bedrock consists of gneiss, and the mineral soil on the sloping terrain is suitable for spruce growth.

vikersund-bergsj-biotopvernomrade-natea5.d: The Vikersund–Bergsjø Biotope Conservation Area (approximately 3,232 daa, of which approximately 200 dekar is land area) was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Natural Diversity (the Nature Diversity Act), cf. Sections 38 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The protected area is situated entirely within Modum municipality in Buskerud, and forms part of the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA. The biotope protection area is intended to preserve an area of particular significance as an ecological functional area, serving as an important feedingand overwintering area for whooper swans, mute swans, goldeneyes, coots, mallards, tufted ducks, dippers, goosanders and great cormorants, as well as a spawning and rearing area for a stock of large trout.

slemmestadasen-morberg-naturreservat-nat.d: The Slemmestadåsen–Morberg Nature Reserve is situated on the western side of the Oslo Fjord, between Slemmestad and Nærsnes in the municipality of Asker. The reserve is divided into two parts, with Slemmestadåsen to the north and Morberg to the south, and encompasses the rocky slope from the sea and the settlements by the sea, up to around 100 metres above sea level. The vegetation consists largely of rich deciduous forest, as well as some calcareous pine forest. There are large populations of the red-listed plants vetch and fly orchid. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but hunting is permitted in accordance with other legislation. It is also permitted to gather edible mushrooms and berries, but lighting fires and using barbecues is prohibited outside designated areas.

svenstadlia-naturreservat-nat1bdcfe80.d: Svenstadlia Nature Reserve is a two-part area situated on the lower side of County Road 33 in the north of Eidsvoll municipality, in Feiring on the western shore of Lake Mjøsa. The southernmost part is the smallest and comprises a headland and a small islet. On the headland there is a burial ground with two round barrows. The northern part is larger and contains several different types of rich and rare woodland. In the centre there is grey alder and hawthorn woodland, as well as mature spruce forest. Along the Trilterudbekken stream, there is rich deciduous forest, and to the east we find grey alder and ash forest. A large area of the forest floor is dominated by yellow bedstraw, constituting a rare and distinctive forest type. In the north of the area, the bedrock consists of granitic gneiss and monzodiorite. In the south, there is graphite schist.

s-ndre-tyrifjorden-naturreservat-natd348.d: The Søndre Tyrifjorden Nature Reserve (approximately 5,848 daa, of which approximately 147 dekar is land area) was established by Royal Decree of 22 June 2018 pursuant to Section 34 of Act No. 100 of 19 June 2009 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The nature reserve forms part of the largest protected individual area within the Tyrifjorden wetland system IBA, and it is directly adjacent to the Vikersund–Bergsjø biotope conservation area (approximately 3,232 daa) and the Vassbunn Nature Reserve (119 daa), both of which form a continuation in the upper reaches of the Drammenselva river where it originates at the outlet of Tyrifjorden.

bogslunden-naturreservat-nat301ec723.d: Bogslunden Nature Reserve is situated 20–30 metres above sea level near Carlberg Farm in the former municipality of Rygge. The reserve is bounded to the north by the railway line, and borders the Værne Monastery Landscape Conservation Area to the west, south and east. The bedrock consists mainly of gneiss, overlaid with loose material of rich topsoil. The vegetation comprises a varied deciduous forest, largely consisting of grey alder–ash and elm–lime forests. The reserve has a rich bird life; species that breed here include the lesser spotted woodpecker, the yellowhammer and the whitethroat.

s-rumsneset-naturreservat-nat19e9c2b3.d: Sørumsneset Nature Reserve (1,100 dekar) is situated in the municipalities of Lillestrøm and Rælingen in Akershus County and was designated a protected area in 1992. Sørumsneset borders the Nordre Øyeren Nature Reserve to the south, which is the Nordic region’s largest inland delta and has Ramsar status. The Sørumsneset Nature Reserve comprises a wetland area of approximately 1,100 dekar, the majority of which lies within the municipality of Lillestrøm. The area has a distinctive landscape formed by the meanders of the River Leira and its stagnant lagoons. The shallow-water lagoons are considered one of the country’s most species-rich wetland areas, and the area as a whole boasts particularly high biodiversity.

selskj-r-fuglefredningsomrade-natfbe56d7.d: The Selskjær Wildlife Sanctuary consists of a small islet and a larger islet, as well as the sea area 50 metres offshore, to the west of Fornebulandet in Bærum municipality. On the eastern side, the area adjoins the Torvøya and Bjerkholmen Nature Reserve. The islet was previously a breeding ground for both common terns and a large colony of black-headed gulls, but has since come to be dominated by eider ducks and lesser black-backed gulls, as well as a few geese. The shallow waters also support a varied seabird fauna. Access to the area is prohibited, both on land and at sea, from 15 April to 15 July.

ultvedttjern-naturreservat-nat22ee2e61.d: The Ultvedttjern Nature Reserve (185 daa) – comprising a small lake, a calcareous fen and an adjacent section of the stream – was established on 20 June 1986 and is situated in a hilly, calcareous ridge landscape approximately 2 km north of Steinsfjorden, in Ringerike municipality. The nature reserve is completely surrounded by the Ultvedt landscape conservation area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a calcareous fen as a habitat for rare and interesting plant and animal species, including the shiny pondweed and the freshwater snail. A further aim is to preserve a rare Chara lake, a very calcareous lake characterised by calcium carbonate precipitation and the presence of stoneworts.

prekestolen-og-ryggevanna-naturreservat-.d: The Prekestolen and Ryggevanna Nature Reserve is situated in the southern part of the Romeriksåsene hills in the municipalities of Gjerdrum and Nittedal. The bedrock consists of granite, and the soil is thin on the ridges. In the depressions there are bogs and peat. The forest is described as ‘natural forest in an older optimal phase’. It is characterised by past selective felling, which presumably ceased in the 1950s. There is generally little deadwood, though somewhat more in places. There are also few indicator species for old spruce and pine forest, but the yellow parasitic polypore and the black-zone polypore are present, both of which are on the Red List. The reserve is an extension of the Prekestolen Nature Reserve, which was designated in 2015. Here, there is more deadwood at all stages of decomposition. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment.

nordre-yeren-naturreservat-nat0246892b.d: Nordre Øyeren Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Lillestrøm, Rælingen and Enebakk, Akershus. The nature reserve is the largest inland delta in the Nordic region and encompasses Lakes Svellet and the northern part of Øyeren, as well as the river delta areas associated with the outlets of the Glomma, Leira and Nitelva rivers into these lakes, and has Ramsar site status due to its importance for migratory birds. The reserve was established on 5 December 1975 and was granted Ramsar status in 1985. The area is of some importance as a breeding ground, but is of greatest significance to birdlife as a stopover site during the spring and autumn migrations.

grunnane-naturreservat-nat86d0dafa.d: Grunnane Nature Reserve comprises the bay between Bokerøya and Krokåsen in Drammen municipality in Buskerud, formerly part of Svelvik municipality in Vestfold. The main part consists of shallow-water areas and a small coastal zone between the sea and County Road 319. This is one of the most unspoilt shallow-water areas in Eastern Norway. Here, salt water from the Oslo Fjord meets fresh water from the Drammen Fjord, forming large mudflats that are exposed at low tide. The reserve is an important wintering site for large birds such as swans, geese, grey herons and cormorants. It is also an important resting place for many migratory birds, but the area is of little significance as a breeding ground.

l-kenesskogen-naturreservat-nat4c5ebad9.d: The Løkenesskogen Nature Reserve is situated on the northern side of the Løkenes Peninsula, sloping down towards Leangbukta in Asker municipality. The reserve is divided in two by a narrow wedge of the Løkenes Peninsula Landscape Conservation Area extending down towards Esvika. The area is home to an exceptionally high level of biodiversity, which is attributed, amongst other things, to its interaction with the surrounding cultural landscape. Over 500 species of vascular plants have been recorded here, including centaury and sea rush. An abundance of deadwood from hazel and other broad-leaved deciduous woodland also provides a habitat for Red Listed species of fungi, lichens and mosses, as well as insects. The birdlife is also rich. Of all the biological species in total, 70 are listed on the Norwegian Red List of vulnerable and endangered species. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment.

oust-naturreservat-nat0efef373.d: Oust Nature Reserve is situated on Ostøya in the inner Oslo Fjord, in the municipality of Bærum. The bedrock consists mainly of sedimentary limestone and shale from the Cambrian–Silurian period, interspersed with veins of Permian igneous rocks. The reserve comprises several sub-areas; the largest is the last remaining major area of woodland associated with the low-lying, calcareous and summer-warm Cambrian–Silurian areas of the inner Oslo Fjord. Around 460 different plant species have been recorded here, several of which have a very limited distribution in Norway. A number of rare, vulnerable and endangered species have been identified in the reserve, such as the heron moth.

skj-l-ysundet-naturreservat-natbfbe3f39.d: Skjæløysundet Nature Reserve comprises the sound between Skjeløya and the mainland in the north-west of Fredrikstad municipality, as well as the shallow waters to the north of the island and the adjacent beaches. A small part of the reserve, the islet of Steinene, was designated as the Steinene Nature Reserve in 1978. The area was subsequently extended on 16 April 2010. The bedrock consists of granite, but the reserve is characterised by loose material, largely clay. The exception is the outer parts of Terneskjær and Steinene, where there are more pebbles. The site features a seashore with great diversity and rare species. It is home to one of the largest and most diverse salt marshes in Østfold, of national importance. The reserve serves as a breeding and wintering ground for wetland birds.

koksabukta-naturreservat-nat29b3fdbf.d: The Koksabukta Nature Reserve encompasses the northern part of Koksabukta and the adjacent coastal zone on Storøya at Fornebu in the municipality of Bærum. The bedrock consists of sedimentary rocks with a high limestone content dating from the Cambrian–Silurian period. The bay is shallow and has varied vegetation, including a number of rare species. Parts of the shoreline and the dry slopes inland are particularly valuable. The wetland area has a rich bird life and constitutes a very important stopover and resting place for birds during migration. It is also a breeding ground for several species, including the reed bunting and the marsh warbler. The site is also important as a wintering ground for many passerines. To the west, the nature reserve adjoins the Torvøya and Bjerkholmen nature reserves.

enli-naturreservat-nat4adc8712.d: Enli Nature Reserve is a 135 daa broadleaf forest reserve situated on the hillside north of Rykkinn in Bærum. The area was designated a nature reserve in 1982. As well as significant natural value, the area contains ancient cultural heritage sites such as stone-walled bridleways and old mine tunnels. The area is easily accessible.

nordre-skj-lholmen-naturreservat-nat8980.d: Skjælholmene are two small islands in the middle of Bunnefjorden in Nesodden municipality, owned by Oslo municipality. The islands have long been known as Skjærholmene, but their names were changed following a decision by the Norwegian Mapping Authority in 1992. The 2008 Conservation Plan for the Oslofjord includes the islands.

j-lsen-naturreservat-nat9b1f20d0.d: Jølsen Nature Reserve is situated on the eastern bank of the River Leira, more precisely on the north side of one of the river’s meanders, in the municipality of Lillestrøm. The area borders on farmland and the River Leira. The woodland grows on marine clay, and the area is frequently flooded. This means that the forest structure remains relatively stable. The tree and shrub layer consists mainly of almond willow, with some grey alder in places. The purpose of designating the Jølsen Nature Reserve is to preserve a well-developed and rare stand of almond willow with its associated ground vegetation.

vikerfjell-naturreservat-nat592b4d91.d: The Vikerfjell Nature Reserve (approximately 80,186 daa) was established by Royal Decree 10 June 2016 pursuant to Section 34 of the Act of 19 June 2009 No. 100 on the Management of Biodiversity (the Biodiversity Act), cf. Sections 37 and 62. Proposed by the Ministry of Climate and Environment. The nature reserve is situated in Strømsoddbygda (Soknedalen) and Ådalsfjellene (Ådalen) in Ringerike municipality. The part that was previously part of the Vassfaret and Vidalen Landscape Conservation Area is now included in the new Vikerfjell Nature Reserve, which therefore borders on it. The Vikerfjell Nature Reserve is the physically largest nature reserve in Ringerike municipality.

askevann-naturreservat-nat20c75571.d: Askevann Nature Reserve is situated in the Degernesfjella mountains in the south of Rakkestad municipality in Østfold. The reserve stretches from the forest track at Holmetjern northwards, past Søndre Askevann, to the shores of Nordre Askevann. The area encompasses several habitat types, including both woodland and bog, but with a bedrock of nutrient-poor gneiss, the vegetation is not particularly rich. However, several Red Listed plants are found here, such as narrow-leaved marsh orchid and old man’s beard. The area bears some traces of past logging. Nevertheless, an area of this size that has not been subject to recent human intervention is still considered worthy of protection.

buvika-r-dskj-r-naturreservat-nat4799b5b.d: Buvika serves as both a ‘resting place’ and a ‘refuelling station’ for migratory birds. Gulls and cormorants nest at Rødskjær. Common terns also thrive in the nature reserve. Every spring and autumn, tens of thousands of birds use the ancient migration route along the Oslo Fjord. Bastøya lies right in the middle of this migration route, with the nutrient-rich wetland area at Buvika. Migratory birds need food and rest. They find both at Buvika. Flocks of over 400 tufted ducks, 270 common scoters and around 2,500 eider ducks have been recorded in the reserve. Furthermore, the summer population of greylag geese has increased significantly in recent years. Rødskjær is a low islet, characterised by pebbles and gravelly beaches. The islet is an important breeding ground for seabirds.

tangvald-naturreservat-nat54cd8740.d: Tangvald Nature Reserve is situated south of Lake Stokkevannet in Bamble. The reserve borders Rognsflauane Nature Reserve to the south-east. The dominant tree species in the area are ash and elm, with occasional patches of lime and lowland birch. Among the shrubs and small trees, several heat-loving species can be found. Closer to the ground, there is a rich variety of species, including spring snowflake, wild garlic, woodruff, toothwort, blood cranesbill, spring pasque flower and wood violet. The bedrock consists of sediments from the Cambrian and Silurian geological periods (Cambro-Silurian).

rognsflauane-naturreservat-natb8f6fd3e.d: The Rognsflauane Nature Reserve is situated on limestone bedrock at the head of Rognsfjorden. The area is characterised by species-rich woodland dominated by several types of limestone pine forest and low-herb spruce forest, with elements of broad-leaved deciduous woodland. A stand of yew can be found in the limestone pine forest. Together with the adjacent Tangvald Nature Reserve, this is a forested area containing many rare species and vegetation types. The neighbouring Rognstranda is a state-protected outdoor recreation area.

gr-nnasliane-naturreservat-nat1dbabba6.d: Grønnåsliane Nature Reserve is situated in the heart of Kragerø municipality, on the north side of Kilsfjorden. The reserve consists of coastal deciduous woodland with elm, lime and ash, interspersed with black alder and grey alder-ash woodland. Grønnåsliane is home to, amongst other things, large populations of the nationally protected species Sjelbuskvikke, Sørlandsvikke and Raggarve. There are also occurrences of rare species of moss, fungi and lichen.

tj-nna-naturreservat-nat841a7429.d: The Tjønna Nature Reserve in Holmestrand municipality was established in 1980. Tjønna is a groundwater bog with diverse vegetation. In the northern part of the reserve there is a marsh with black alder. The nature reserve is largely unaffected by human activity. The rare white-backed woodpecker has been sighted in the reserve. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a groundwater bog with moderate to rich vegetation.

langesundstangen-naturreservat-nat7bb8ec.d: Langesundstangen Nature Reserve is situated south of Langesund town centre in Bamble. The area is situated close to the coast, and the reserve contains habitats associated with saltwater and saltwater-influenced environments (seashore). The reserve is important for the conservation of several rare and threatened species, including vascular plants, lichens and insects.

sj-mannsheia-naturreservat-nat839822da.d: The Sjømannsheia Nature Reserve is dominated by pine forest on barren ground, partly comprising old trees. Some of the trees are thought to be over 400 years old. At Sjømannsheia, one can find several types of pine forest, such as lingonberry pine forest, low-growing pine forest and blueberry pine forest.

killingholmen-naturreservat-natd5e46de2.d: The Killingholmen Nature Reserve on Killingholmen in Holmestrand was established in 1988 and features calcareous pine forest, calcareous grasslands and alternating layers of limestone and shale dating from the Silurian period. There are good populations of the fly orchid in the reserve. The fly orchid is a protected species. The Drammen branch of the Norwegian Ornithological Society has an ornithological station on the island. From the station, ornithologists study the birdlife in Sandebukta. The purpose of the conservation order is to protect an important site for understanding the fossil-bearing rocks of the Oslo Field.

presteseter-naturreservat-nata305d388.d: Presteseter Nature Reserve in Holmestrand municipality was established in 2005 and expanded in 2017. Presteseteråsen, in the north-east of the reserve, rises to 568 metres above sea level and is one of the highest points in the county. Presteseter is the third-largest protected area in Vestfold, after Færder National Park and the Mølen Bird Sanctuary. Presteseter was designated a protected area to preserve an unspoilt forest with all its natural flora and fauna. The forest boasts a rich diversity of lichens, with several species that depend on continuity and high humidity. Presteseter is likely home to the county’s only viable population of the rare lichen Huldrestry.

gullkronene-naturreservat-nat127bc889.d: The Gullkronene Nature Reserve is situated on the plains north-west of Tønsberg town, on the grounds of Jarlsberg Manor in Tønsberg municipality. The reserve consists of two neighbouring areas of deciduous woodland, including ash, hawthorn, beech, oak and maple. The area is a very old cultural landscape, with several burial mounds dating from the Viking Age and the Iron Age. The nature of the reserve requires some management. Wild hops also grow here, having been introduced in 1831. And in 1995, a population of the fungus ‘safrankjuke’ was rediscovered for the first time since 1883. The avenues through the forest were laid out around 1720 as part of a large Baroque-style park.

indre-viksfjord-naturreservat-nat48bb652.d: Indre Viksfjord Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Larvik, established in 1981. It is home to a very rich and diverse birdlife, particularly during the spring and autumn migration periods. The nature reserve is of great value as a foraging and resting area, particularly for ducks and waders during the spring and autumn migrations. Wintering waterbirds remain in the fjord until the ice sets in. The area attracts both large numbers and a wide variety of birds. Uncommon species such as the Alaskan sandpiper, the avocet, the little egret, the great egret and the white-winged black tern have visited the area. A Long-billed Dowitcher, which visited in 2000, normally breeds on the tundra in eastern Siberia and in North America, and has only been sighted a few times in Norway.

frierflogene-naturreservat-natd8ed0333.d: The Frierflogene Nature Reserve is situated above the entrance to the Kjørholt Tunnel, west of Brevik in Porsgrunn municipality. The area comprises a distinctive landscape and is of great value for research and education. It features both interesting geology and a range of representative and valuable vegetation types, including calcareous pine forest, low-herb spruce forest and broad-leaved deciduous forest. To the east, the reserve borders a landscape conservation area surrounding the five dammed lakes known as Dammane. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Motorised traffic is prohibited.

storas-og-spiras-naturreservat-natd8847e.d: The Storås and Spirås Nature Reserve was established in 2017. The area represents a distinctive type of landscape characterised by rapid changes in topography and vegetation types, and features a varied and, in places, rich mix of tree species, including areas of rich, old beech woodland as well as endangered and rare species. The conservation objective of the nature reserve is to preserve a relatively large area of deciduous and coniferous woodland in the lowlands.

steinvika-naturreservat-nat0cfe4655.d: Steinvika Nature Reserve is situated on a municipal open space south of Langesund. To the west, the boundary of the reserve follows the shoreline. In Steinvika, one can clearly see, in several places, the layered rocks typical of the Oslo Field. These date from the Ordovician geological period. In the exposed rock, several types of fossils can be seen. Steinvika Nature Reserve also contains areas with distinctive vegetation, and the flora itself is of great conservation interest.

hemskilen-naturreservat-nat3cc26131.d: Hemskilen Nature Reserve is a Norwegian nature reserve. It is situated on the border between Larvik (formerly Tjølling municipality) and Sandefjord. It is one of the largest and most important nature reserves of its kind in Vestfold. Hemskilen Nature Reserve covers 335 dekar. 215 dekar consists of brackish water and seawater. It boasts a particularly rich and interesting variety of birdlife, vegetation and other wildlife, and is a regionally valuable foraging and rearing area for waterbirds during the breeding season, as well as a resting and feeding area for ducks, waders, geese and passerines during migration.

blekebakken-naturreservat-natdd34051d.d: Blekebakken Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Frierfjord in Porsgrunn municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 30 June 2006 and is included in the conservation plan for broad-leaved forests/rich deciduous forests. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched natural area with its biological diversity in the form of habitat types, ecosystems, species and natural ecological processes. The area also has particular scientific value as a reference site and is unique in that it comprises a lime-rich linden, hazel and oak forest of high conservation value. The area is of particular importance for preserving the species diversity of threatened and vulnerable fungi at national level.’

gausdalen-naturreservat-natc7f7c953.d: The Gausdalen Nature Reserve comprises an area near Gaustatoppen in Tinn municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a particularly high-altitude and relatively unspoilt forest area.’

bast-y-landskapsvernomrade-nat83d18f36.d: The Bastøy Landscape Conservation Area is a protected area, home to valuable geological formations and a rich variety of plant and animal life. The island also has a long history. The climate, bedrock and loose soil on the island provide the conditions for a varied flora. Spruce, with extensive patches of deciduous trees in places. In parts of the forest there are areas of bluebells. On the western side of the island there are large lime trees. The protected mistletoe grows on rowan, lime and wild pear trees. The dry grasslands on Bastøya are home to many rare species. One of these is the bellflower; another is the wild onion. Bastøya is 3 km long and at its widest point 1.4 km wide. It was probably the forest that gave the island its name. ‘Bast’ is the inner part of a tree’s bark.

lagasmyr-naturreservat-nat0c29c762.d: Lågåsmyr Nature Reserve is an elongated bog surrounded by low hills. The reserve borders Sjømannsheia Nature Reserve. The surface of the bog is mostly quite wet, and a stream runs through most of it. There is also a small area of rain-fed bog.

lun-naturreservat-nat7889fff8.d: Lun Nature Reserve is situated on the north-eastern side of Kilsfjorden in Kragerø, and is a varied woodland area dominated by deciduous forest and some pine. A distinctive feature of the area is the presence of yew trees close to the coast. The yews are usually 7–8 metres tall, but some trees reach heights of up to 10 metres. The bedrock consists of gabbro, which provides a relatively high level of plant nutrients.

nevlungstranda-naturreservat-nat3e3968bd.d: The Nevlungstranda Nature Reserve encompasses the beach areas between Saltstein and Oddane Sand, and a stretch of land to the north of the beach. To the south, the nature reserve borders the Mølen Bird Sanctuary. The nature reserve was established in 1980. The Larvik coastal path runs through the protected area. Black alder forest dominates the reserve. Right at the water’s edge, the black alder forest is surrounded by low scrub, shaped by the wind. Further inland, the forest becomes progressively taller. In drier areas, birch, spruce, pine, pedunculate oak, maple, ash and elm grow. Planted spruce and Sitka spruce have been removed from the reserve through management measures.

korpen-og-sagkollen-naturreservat-nat1ea.d: Korpen Nature Reserve was established in 2002. The nature reserve is situated east of the River Lågen, just south of Hvarnes. Oak and beech are common trees in the reserve. There are also elm, lime, alder and ash, and in places a good number of yews. There is a large proportion of old, coarse woodland, and several hollow oak trees. In many places, there is an abundance of dead wood at all stages of decomposition. This provides a habitat for rare mosses, fungi and lichens. From the summit of Knappen, at the easternmost point of the nature reserve, 390 metres above sea level, there are views over large parts of southern Vestfold. The nature reserve is of national conservation importance.

nordhasselvika-fuglefredningsomrade-nat1.d: The Nordhasselvika Bird Sanctuary is a protected habitat in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The area was designated a sanctuary in 1987 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitats in the area. Nordhasselvika is regarded as a beautiful natural and cultural landscape. The bay is so shallow that the 6-metre isobath lies 700 metres from the shore. The area features both a pebble beach and sandy beaches. It is the most important migration site for waders on Lista, particularly in Sævika and at Litle-Rauna, and is also of great importance as a wintering area.

hisdal-naturreservat-nat5994f653.d: Hisdal Nature Reserve is a nature reserve covering 16,392 dekar in Bykle municipality. It was established on 19 December 2008 and is situated south of Botsvatn and the Steinsbuskardet-Hisdal biotope conservation area. To the south lies the Ljosådalen Nature Reserve, and to the west, the Hisdal Nature Reserve borders the Setesdal Vesthei Ryfylkeheiane Landscape Conservation Area. The Conservation Area Board for the Setesdal Vesthei Ryfylkeheiane Landscape Conservation Area is the managing body for the area. The purpose of the conservation is to safeguard an important calving area for wild reindeer and a large forest and heathland area that is representative of Inner Agder, featuring a pine forest where the trees are unusually large.

ris-ya-naturreservat-nat46c02f3b.d: Risøya Nature Reserve consists of a number of islands and islets off Kalvøya in Lillesand municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islands is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

rivingen-naturreservat-nat05c92e60.d: Rivingen Nature Reserve consists of an islet near Homborsund in Grimstad municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 28 March 1980 and is included in the seabird conservation plan. From 15 April to 31 July inclusive, landing on the islet is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve the habitat for the flora and fauna in the area, particularly with regard to seabirds and their breeding sites.’

fjosbumyra-naturreservat-natd5330435.d: Fjosbumyra Nature Reserve is a 132 dekar nature reserve in Gjerstad municipality. It was established on 10 October 1986, the same day that Tranmyra Nature Reserve was also established. The nature reserve forms part of the Conservation Plan for Mires in Aust-Agder. ‘The aim of the conservation is to preserve a western outpost of concentric raised bogs – the only one of its kind in Agder – as well as a blue-topped wet meadow.’ The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. This reserve is a bog reserve. It is a “slightly raised, concentric raised bog of the sub-oceanic type. The eastern part of the bog is influenced by groundwater, whilst the rest is influenced by precipitation and has relatively sparse vegetation.” The area lies at an altitude of approximately 177 metres above sea level.

ljosadalen-naturreservat-nate44830cd.d: The Ljosådalen Nature Reserve is situated on the western side of Setesdalen in Valle municipality. The reserve was established in 2015 to preserve an area of woodland and heathland with, in places, a high density of old pine trees, and a particularly important calving area for wild reindeer. The reserve stretches from the valley floor at 430 metres above sea level up to Slurvenuten, Voienuten and Skammevarden, at 1,300–1,400 metres above sea level. To the north, the reserve borders the Hisdal Nature Reserve. The area contains almost all the forest types found in inner Agder.

vidmyr-naturreservat-nat02ad7d72.d: Vidmyr Nature Reserve is a nature reserve covering 9,583 dekar in Bykle municipality. It was established on 5 September 1986 and lies north of the settlement at Hovden, stretching from National Road 9, south of the Lislevatn Nature Reserve, westwards until it meets the Setesdal Vesthei Ryfylkeheiane Landscape Conservation Area. To the east, it borders the Hovden Landscape Conservation Area. The area is a large mire complex comprising hill mires and string mires. At its easternmost point, there is a flat mire. The vegetation consists of poor fen vegetation, with bear’s-beard and blue moor grass as the most common species, though there is also rich vegetation. Large parts of Vidmyr were hay meadows until after the Second World War, and there were plans to cultivate parts of the area before it was designated a protected area.

steinodden-plante-og-fuglefredningsomrad.d: The Steinodden Wildlife Reserve and the Steinodden Plant and Wildlife Reserve are protected habitats in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The areas cover 2.3 km² and 0.2 km² respectively. The areas were designated as protected in 1987 and have formed part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect a rich and varied flora and the abundant birdlife. The conservation area is situated in an open and weather-beaten location at the very tip of Lista, within a beautiful cultural landscape featuring long stone walls. The geology of the area contains remnants of the Lista moraine. The rich birdlife includes waders in particular, but also ducks and cormorants.

urfjellheia-og-dalsheia-naturreservat-na.d: The Urfjellheia and Dalsheia Nature Reserve comprises an area by Lake Dalsvann in Risør municipality. The area was designated a protected area on 27 November 2020 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The protected area was extended on 8 March 2024. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited, except on existing tractor tracks and paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich deciduous forest, with occurrences of oak-lime forest, elm-lime forest and scree-lime forest, as well as old coniferous forest.’

fuglevika-fuglefredningsomrade-nat93a0a8.d: The Fuglevika Wildlife Reserve is a protected habitat in Farsund municipality in Agder. The area was designated a protected area in 1987 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitats in the area. Large quantities of seaweed and kelp are washed ashore in this bay, providing an important food source for the birds. The area plays a vital role for breeding, migratory and wintering waterbirds. Other conservation interests include the diverse algal vegetation in the sea, as well as spawning and nursery grounds for fish.

lislevatn-naturreservat-nata9f8347d.d: Lislevatn Nature Reserve is the oldest nature reserve in Bykle municipality. It is situated west of National Road 9, just north of Hovden, and was designated a nature reserve on 7 May 1982. The reserve covers an area of approximately 1,100 dekar and lies at an altitude of around 992 metres above sea level. It encompasses both the mountain lake Lislevatn and the surrounding area. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve an important wetland area with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. The managing authority for the area was originally the County Governor of Aust-Agder, but has since been transferred to the management board of the Setesdal Vesthei Ryfylkeheiane Landscape Conservation Area.

listeid-naturreservat-natb4e72a4c.d: Listeid Nature Reserve is a protected natural area in the village of Herad in Farsund municipality, Agder county. The nature reserve is also of interest as a cultural landscape. Listeid is a deciduous forest offering favourable conditions for cavity-nesting bird species. Elm, lime, oak and black alder are the main species of deciduous trees in the area. The area provides a good example of a deciduous forest on the coast of Southern Norway. The vegetation composition in the area is of scientific and educational interest, according to the factual information about the area, which also bears traces of traditional farming practices, including ‘Lauing’. A management plan is in place. These old, moss-covered deciduous trees provide a habitat for nearly 1,000 species.

fossbufjellet-naturreservat-nate1c7fe84.d: Fossbufjellet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gjerstad municipality. It comprises an area on the border with Telemark. To the north-west, it borders Fjosbumyra Nature Reserve. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of oak forest, mature sun-warmed pine forest and old spruce forest, as well as richer lowland mixed forest with large, old yew trees.’

rukkevatn-naturreservat-nat44308acf.d: Rukkevatn Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åmli municipality. It comprises an area just south of Nesvatn. The area was designated a nature reserve on 9 July 1993. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding off existing roads is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a large and well-defined coniferous forest area that encompasses a large catchment area. Large areas of water and bogs form part of the mosaic in the area, which also features a vertical gradient up towards northern boreal birch forest and bare mountain terrain. The site features gradients ranging from nutrient-poor pine forest to relatively nutrient-rich coniferous forest. Large parts of the area are completely untouched by modern forestry practices.”

havika-fuglefredningsomrade-nat77d30099.d: The Havika Wildlife Reserve is a protected habitat in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The area was designated a protected area in 1987 and has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The purpose of the conservation area is to protect the rich birdlife and the birds’ habitats in the area. The landscape is characterised by large sand dunes interspersed with trough-like areas and patches of mound dunes.

solhomfjell-og-kvenntj-nnane-naturreserv.d: The Solhomfjell and Kvenntjønnane Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Drangedal, Gjerstad and Nissedal. It comprises an area around the border between Telemark and Agder. The area was designated a nature reserve on 11 February 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard an area of particular importance for biodiversity, as it contains largely undisturbed low-lying forest in the boreonemoral zone, and featuring stands of old oak woodland with large, hollow oaks. Furthermore, the aim is to preserve an area of particular scientific value due to the presence of rare and threatened species of fungi, lichens and insects.”

einarsneset-plantefredningsomrade-nat0a3.d: The Einarsneset Plant and Animal Conservation Area is a protected habitat in Farsund municipality, Vest-Agder. The area was designated a conservation area in 1987, together with the adjacent Einarsneset Plant Conservation Area (0.59 km²). The area has been part of the Lista Wetland System Ramsar Site since 1996. The landscape consists of a deep beach with sand dunes covered in creeping bent and marram grass. At the outer edge are mountains and rocky outcrops. There is a rich variety of plant life here, including sea thistle. The area’s importance for birdlife lies primarily in its role as a wintering ground for birds. Einarsneshalsen plays a vital role as a breeding ground for waders and serves as a foraging area for waders and ducks during their autumn and spring migrations.

ardalen-naturreservat-natc62ada51.d: Årdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bygland and Åmli municipalities. It was established on 17 December 1993. The area covers 21,280 dekar, or 21.3 km². Of this, 15.5 km² is in Åmli and 5.8 km² in Bygland. The area lies between 450 and 800 metres above sea level and borders the Rukkevatn Nature Reserve to the east and the Furebuheii Nature Reserve. Together, these three nature reserves constitute a protected area of 42.7 km². The managing authority is the County Governor of Aust- and Vest-Agder. The purpose of protecting the Årdalen Nature Reserve is to preserve a large, contiguous natural area that is largely unaffected by human activity and features a varied natural environment that, taken as a whole, is representative of the central parts of Aust-Agder County.

aslands-ya-og-kje-ya-naturreservat-natbd.d: The Åslandsøya and Kjeøya Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Åmli municipality. It consists of islands in the River Nidelva. The area was designated a nature reserve on 15 December 2017. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing roads and paths marked on the conservation map, the use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of low-lying and relatively unspoilt pine forest with a rich variety of flora and fauna. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.’

hopen-naturreservat-nata3504add.d: Hopen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Svalbard that was established on 26 September 2003 and mainly comprises the island of Hopen and the surrounding coastal area. The protected area covers a total area of approximately 3,208 square kilometres, of which 46 square kilometres is land. The conservation area encompasses the entire island, with the exception of a small area around the Norwegian Meteorological Institute’s station, as well as the surrounding territorial waters. In 2011, the reserve was also designated a Ramsar site. Hopen is an elongated, rocky island situated south-east of Edgeøya. The purpose of the conservation is to preserve a virtually untouched Arctic island and its adjacent marine areas, including the seabed.

jan-mayen-naturreservat-nat82995eaa.d: The Jan Mayen Nature Reserve comprises almost the entire land area of Jan Mayen and a marine area surrounding the island. The area was designated a nature reserve on 19 November 2010. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to preserve a virtually untouched Arctic island and adjacent marine areas, including the seabed, with distinctive landscapes, active volcanic systems, unique flora and fauna, and numerous cultural heritage sites, including in particular: the island’s magnificent and unique landscape; the island’s distinctive volcanic rocks and landforms; the island as a very important habitat for seabirds; the close connection between life in the sea and on land; the distinctive ecology that develops on isolated islands; and the historical perspective provided by culturalheritage from all the major eras in

slettsvaet-naturreservat-nat8dfad925.d: Slettsvaet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rauma municipality. It consists of an area situated a little way up the Romsdalen valley from Døntefossen, on the opposite side of the valley. A little further up the valley lies Verma. The area was designated a nature reserve on 27 June 2003. The reserve is part of the conservation plan for deciduous forests and rich deciduous woodlands. Cycling, horse-drawn carts and riding off existing paths are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve a thermophilic deciduous forest with elm in the inner part of the county, together with its natural flora and fauna.’ The nature reserve comprises woodland with elm and elements of birch, rowan, hawthorn, aspen and hazel.

berg-naturreservat-nat94f3dae1.d: Berg Nature Reserve is an area of highly productive coniferous forest in a ravine landscape below the marine limit in the municipality of Indre Østfold in Østfold. The area is situated in the former municipality of Eidsberg, between County Road 124 and County Road 690, and borders on cultivated land along the roads to the north-east and north-west. The soil is nutrient-rich, consisting of sandy clay over a bedrock of quartz-rich gneiss. The vegetation is dominated by rich, low-herb spruce forest, with a significant proportion of aspen, birch, elm and hazel. On the other side of a farm track to the south-west lies a plateau with somewhat poorer soil. Here, there is more pine and mixed coniferous forest. In areas below the marine limit with such high site quality as here, it is rare to find vegetation that is so little affected by human activity.

bergsasen-naturreservat-natebf1baaa.d: Bergsåsen Nature Reserve is a nature conservation area at the eastern end of Lake Snåsavatnet in Snåsa municipality in Trøndelag. The area lies just west of the Bergsåsen Plant Conservation Area and is protected ‘to preserve particularly rich vegetation, including calcareous plant communities and a number of less common plant species’. The reserve lies at an altitude of 85–273 metres above sea level on Bergsåsen, between the Nordland Railway to the north and County Road 7006 to the south. The area was extended to 2,839.1 dekar in February 2022.

sulustaddalen-naturreservat-naturreserva.d: Sulustaddalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Østre Toten municipality. It comprises an area on Totenåsen. The area was first designated as a nature reserve on 5 March 2010, extended on 2 November 2022 and extended again on 24 June 2025. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic on land and water is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing tractor tracks, old roads and footpaths.

nedre-timenes-naturreservat-naturreserva.d: Nedre Timenes Nature Reserve is a 2,249 dekar nature reserve in Kristiansand municipality. The reserve was established on 16 December 2011, and its purpose is to protect and preserve deciduous broad-leaved woodland, including habitats such as black alder riparian woodland and rich deciduous broad-leaved woodland, as well as hay meadows. The nature reserve is a habitat for several endangered and near-threatened species of butterfly, plant wasps and fungi, and is of particular scientific value as a reference area for large, typical South Norwegian oak forests. The managing authority is the State Administrator in Agder. Nedre Timenes is a forest reserve. At the centre of the area lies Lake Fivvannet, which is 7.5 metres above sea level. A management plan has been drawn up for the area.

svartdalstjerna-naturreservat-natd25b198.d: Svartdalstjerna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on Totenåsen, east of Torsætra in Østre Toten municipality. The reserve was first designated in 2010 and extended to the north-west and north-east in 2021. The area now possesses ‘large-scale qualities’, as it covers over 10 km². It lies within the northern boreal vegetation zone, with blueberry spruce forest as the dominant vegetation type. The reserve is believed to host Europe’s largest population of the Norwegian priority species, the Huldrestry. This species is listed as ‘Endangered’ (EN) on the Red List. In addition, there are several other Red List species that are important for biodiversity. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment. Animals and plants are protected, but the regulations provide for a number of exceptions.

flastranda-og-hisdalen-naturreservat-nat.d: Flåstranda and Hisdalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Sunndal and Tingvoll. It comprises an area along the Sunndalsfjord. The area was designated as the Hisdalen Nature Reserve on 12 December 2014, covering an area of approximately 3,302 dekar, and was extended on 17 December 2021 to 4,771 dekar. It was further extended on 8 March 2024 to an area of 8,461 dekar. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing paths shown on the conservation map, cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited.

leitjernsfjellet-naturreservat-natd076dc.d: Leitjernsfjellet Nature Reserve is situated on the ridge between Eikeren and the River Drammen, at an altitude of between 500 and 550 metres above sea level. The bedrock consists of ekerite and volcanic rocks, which, together with a thin layer of loose material, results in sparse vegetation in the higher-altitude areas. In valley depressions and lower-lying areas, there are richer areas with higher productivity. At the southernmost part of the area lies Løkmyr, a low-lying hill bog dominated by sedges. This bog was first designated a nature reserve in 1986. The purpose of the nature reserve is to protect an old and largely undisturbed forest with plenty of deadwood, as well as the hilltop bog in the south. It is not permitted to alter the natural environment.

lj-godttjern-naturreservat-nat074725aa.d: Ljøgodttjern lies in a shallow depression in the Gardermo moraine, just west of Jessheim in Akershus. The shores drop off quite steeply, with a maximum depth of 16 metres. The lake is the southernmost of several kettle hole lakes in the Gardermo moraine, and Ljøgodttjern has very distinctive chemical conditions. There is a high calcium content and high concentrations of iron and phosphorus in the bottom waters and sediments. The water level varies with the groundwater level. The lake is home to a wide variety of plant species, including the vulnerable water-plantain.

simskarmyra-naturreservat-nat57a2ba6a.d: Simskarmyra Nature Reserve is situated between Øvre and Nedre Fiplingvatnet in Grane municipality in Nordland. The nature reserve covers an area of 5,066 dekar. The area is protected to preserve an important wetland area with its associated flora and fauna, particularly in view of the diversity of bog types and the particularly interesting birdlife.

stavaa-skauma-og-orkla-naturreservat-nat.d: The Stavåa, Skauma and Orkla Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Rennebu municipality. It comprises an area east of the Orkla, north of Ulsberg and south of Berkåk. The area was first designated on 14 December 2018 as the Stavåa Nature Reserve, expanded on 16 December 2022 to become the Stavåa and Skauma Nature Reserve, and most recently expanded on 8 March 2024. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic on land and water is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling is prohibited outside existing paths.

bjerke-naturreservat-nat5e0adffa.d: Bjerke Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Larvik municipality. It comprises an area along the River Lågen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing bridleways. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents specific types of nature in the form of mature woodland consisting of rich mixed woodland in the lowlands, rich deciduous woodland and old coniferous woodland. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to develop them further.’

skolten-naturreservat-nate85f9106.d: Skolten Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Gulen municipality. It comprises an area to the east of Brossvikvatnet. The area was designated a nature reserve on 16 December 2022. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The use of bicycles, horse-drawn carts and horse riding is prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard a larger area containing threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats in the form of western Norwegian rainforest, old mixed pine and deciduous forest, as well as rich deciduous forest with stream ravine habitats. The aim is to preserve the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and to allow the diversity of species and their habitats to develop as naturally as possible.”

rotnedalen-naturreservat-natded08801.d: Rotnedalen Nature Reserve is situated on the west side of Rotnebergsvegen, partly on both sides of the River Rotna in Grue municipality. When it was established in 1989, the reserve was larger and contiguous, but in 2023 part of the reserve was separated to form the Viertjenna Nature Reserve, with a slightly different conservation objective. The remaining Rotnedalen Nature Reserve thus comprises three separate areas, all of which border on and are linked by the Viertjenna Nature Reserve. Rotnedalen Nature Reserve encompasses parts of a 12-kilometre-long esker system. These are ridges of sand and gravel deposited by rivers carrying meltwater from beneath glaciers towards the end of the last ice age. The vegetation is dominated by lichen- and heather-rich pine forest.

viertjenna-naturreservat-nat1a0ec12c.d: Viertjenna Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Grue municipality, near Grue Finnskog. The reserve was established on 20 June 2023 as part of the forest conservation plan. The area borders the three sections of the Rotnedalen Nature Reserve to the north and east, and links them together. The reserve lies along the River Rotna and consists mainly of open pine forest with eskers. It includes several walking trails and the Rovdyrhula campsite, which features a lavvo and shelters. The aim of the conservation is to preserve rich sandy pine forest with its associated natural values and habitats for threatened and vulnerable species.

reierskogen-naturreservat-natd2511812.d: Reierskogen Nature Reserve is situated in the Søndre Jeløy Landscape Conservation Area in the south of Jeløya in Moss municipality, Østfold. The reserve was established in 2010 and extended in 2023. The purpose of the reserve is to preserve an area containing threatened, rare and vulnerable natural habitats, with varied deciduous woodland and old coniferous forest. The bedrock consists of sandstone, basalt and porphyry, which provide nutrient-rich soil and a good foundation for a high level of biodiversity. The reserve is home to, amongst other things, Red Listed tree species such as ash, wild pear and elm.

os-yra-naturreservat-naturreservat-nat0f.d: Osøyra Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kinn municipality. It comprises an area on both sides of Osstrupen.
