The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Outside the paths marked on the conservation map, cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve a large and varied forest area with a diversity of threatened, rare and vulnerable natural features in the form of habitat types and species. The area represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a western Norwegian rainforest with a strong oceanic influence, including sites of national importance.”

kringler-naturreservat-nat6a6b80f3.d: The Kringler Nature Reserve is situated on both sides of the River Leira in the centre of Nannestad municipality, Akershus county. The area on the east side of the river at Nordre Kringler was the first to be protected, on 16 December 2022. On 20 June 2023, an area on the west side of the river, at Søndre Kringler, was added. The reserve lies on marine clay at an altitude of 150–190 metres above sea level and comprises a ravine landscape with deeply incised stream valleys and very lush vegetation. Along the Leira in the southern part of the area, the landscape is characterised by floodplain woodland and open, flood-resistant land. The vegetation is varied in both the ground layer and the tree layer, comprising both spruce and many different deciduous trees. Ravine landscapes on clay are a vulnerable habitat type and rare in an international context.

eriksrud-naturreservat-nat7676c382.d: Eriksrud Nature Reserve is a small, two-part area on the western shore of Lake Mjøsa, just north of Mjøsbrua. The reserve is situated on a steep hillside with a dry and warm local climate. There are areas of scree here and vegetation of various types. The forest is highly productive, comprising both calcareous spruce forest and pure stands of elm-lime forest. It is also largely natural forest, with plenty of deadwood from all tree species, not least lime. The ground layer is home to a great many endangered species of fungi and vascular plants. Both wildlife and vegetation are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting is also permitted in accordance with other regulations.

vassfaret-naturreservat-nat64ff52a2.d: Vassfaret Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Flå, Nesbyen and Sør-Aurdal. The area was designated a protected area on 20 June 2023 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area that represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of a large, varied and well-defined forest valley encompassing the entire cross-section of the valley, including the main watercourse running through it, where the forest in the area is representative of high-altitude forest in central parts of Eastern Norway. Furthermore, the purpose is to preserve an area of particular scientific value, in that parts of the area contain elements of old-growth natural forest with reference values for such forest.”

h-nsejuvet-naturreservat-nat8cc28ea5.d: Hønsejuvet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Seljord municipality. It comprises an area to the east of Seljordsvatn. The area was designated a nature reserve on 20 June 2023. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Apart from existing footpaths, cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to safeguard an area of particular importance for biodiversity due to the presence of a major ravine with great ecological variation across an elevation gradient from the lowlands to the mountains, dominated by rich habitat types such as elm-lime forest, low-herb deciduous forest, grey alder-elm forest, tall-herb forest and low-herb spruce forest, as well as a great deal of dead wood and a rich diversity of species.

turrtind-naturreservat-nat69dd7165.d: The Turrtind Nature Reserve comprises an area south of Synnfjell in Nordre Land municipality. loppa-naturreservat-nat7085b579.d: Loppa Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Loppa municipality. The reserve covers an area of 6.33 km² in the north-west of Loppa Island. Approximately 2.4 km² of this is land area. The purpose of the conservation area is to preserve an important bird cliff with its associated plant communities, birdlife and other wildlife naturally associated with the area. The bird cliff has a good population of auks. To the west, a cliff face approximately 200 metres high plunges into the sea. The interior of the island consists of a mountain plateau.

stmarka-nasjonalpark-vernesone-a-nat66f6.d: Østmarka Nature Reserve was a nature reserve in Østmarka that was established in 1990, expanded in 2002 and incorporated into Østmarka National Park in 2023. Zone A of the national park corresponds to the former nature reserve. The level of restrictions and the safeguarding of conservation values have largely been maintained. The reserve was situated in the municipalities of Rælingen, Lørenskog and Enebakk, in the heart of Østmarka. Oslo Municipality took over ownership of the forest area in 1965, and the area was placed under administrative protection at that time. The purpose of the protection was to preserve a forest area as an ecosystem with all its natural flora and fauna. This large nature reserve constitutes a valuable habitat for its region.

abj-rdalen-naturreservat-nat2021983a.d: Åbjørdalen Nature Reserve (Southern Sámi: Diedtjienvuemien eatnemereservaate) is a nature reserve in Bindal municipality. sk-rsasane-naturreservat-nat90012d2b.d: Skørsåsane Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Sandefjord municipality. It comprises an area near Andebu. The objective is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.”

eidbo-naturreservat-nat36eb9cd6.d: The Eidbo Nature Reserve comprises an area near Eidbo in Tvedestrand municipality. leine-og-m-lumsberget-naturreservat-nat6.d: The Leine and Mælumsberget Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Ringsaker municipality. It comprises an area between Brumunddal and Moelv. loreasen-naturresevat-nat56acca7e.d: Loreåsen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Hole municipality. It comprises an area by Steinsfjorden. nordneset-og-akkarvika-naturreservat-nat.d: The Nordneset and Akkarvika Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Senja municipality. It comprises an area south of Finnsnes on Senja. store-rekke-og-h-lvannet-naturreservat-n.d: Store Rekke and Hølvannet Nature Reserve is a two-part reserve situated in the far east of Aurskog-Høland, near the border with Sweden. The reserve lies on a gently undulating plateau some 240–300 metres above sea level, where small ridges rise from a landscape dominated by marshland. To the east of the reserve lies Hølvannet, which is dammed by an old dam at its north-eastern outlet. This has created a lake with numerous islets and skerries, which is unusual for the region. The bedrock consists of granitic gneiss, tonalitic gneiss and mica gneiss. These result in acidic soil and provide the basis for sparse vegetation. The soil is generally thin, and the vegetation is dominated by sparse pine forest.

vik-naturreservat-nat97408903.d: Vik Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Aure municipality. It comprises an area by the Aursundet strait. The area was designated a nature reserve on 8 March 2024. The aim is to preserve the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.”

iverstadfjellet-naturreservat-nat285b85d.d: Iverstadfjellet Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Risør municipality. It comprises an area near Sandvann. h-gsmasan-naturreservat-nat616e8312.d: Høgsmåsan Nature Reserve comprises a large rain-fed bog, situated on a wooded plateau north-west of Skedsmokorset in Akershus. The area is important for black grouse and also serves as a resting place for certain migratory birds.

midtstrondbekken-naturreservat-nat8eeb2e.d: Midtstrondbekken Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tinn municipality. It comprises an area at the northern end of Tinnsjå. aurstadklumpen-naturreservat-nat6f659980.d: Aurstadklumpen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in the municipalities of Høylandet and Grong. The area was designated a protected area on 21 June 2024. h-ymyr-naturreservat-nate97b5f46.d: Høymyr Nature Reserve was established in 1980. Høymyr is a groundwater bog with moderately rich, and in places rich, vegetation. Rain-fed bogs have few species. Along the southern edge of the Høymyr Nature Reserve, there are springs with calcium-rich groundwater. Water flows from these springs into the bog, providing the basis for the richest patches of vegetation. The purpose of the conservation order is to preserve a flat bog with moderately rich, and in places rich, vegetation.

storvika-naturreservat-nat034a06b7.d: Storvika Nature Reserve is a nature reserve on the northern shore of Lake Selbusjøen, in the west of Selbu municipality in Trøndelag. Spruce forest dominates, but there are also deciduous trees (elm and hazel) and old pine trees. Both wildlife and vegetation are protected against damage and destruction, but picking berries and edible mushrooms is permitted. Hunting is also permitted in accordance with other regulations.

It comprises an area at Igletjenn, between Tønnesølvannet to the west and Røynevannet to the east. The area was designated a nature reserve on 24 June 2025. The reserve forms part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised land transport is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside the existing tractor tracks and paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents a specific type of natural habitat in the form of low-herb oak forest intermingled with elm-lime forest to the east and boreonemoral mixed forest to the west b.

kvitingsmorki-naturreservat-nat56d075ff.d: The Kvitingsmorki Nature Reserve comprises an area by the Årdalsfjord in Årdal municipality. The area was designated a nature reserve on 17 December 1999 and is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the designation is ‘to safeguard a forest area with all its natural flora and fauna’. Notable features include the fact that the area constitutes a large, contiguous forest area with a wide variety of vegetation types, and with a forest gradient from the fjord to the mountains.’

brattset-naturreservat-nat61469056.d: Brattset Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Aure municipality. It comprises an area on Ertvågsøya facing the fjord. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 December 2025. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited except on existing paths marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich deciduous forest and a stream gorge; b. contains threatened, rare or vulnerable natural features such as elm-hazel forest and associated species.”

fl-ystaddalen-naturreservat-nat76e87f35.d: Fløystaddalen Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Tingvoll municipality. It comprises an area on the north-eastern side of the Tingvoll Peninsula, facing Halsafjorden and Trongfjorden. The area was designated a nature reserve on 12 December 2025. The reserve is included in the forest conservation plan. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the protection is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of boreal deciduous forest and old-growth pine forest; b. contains threatened, rare or vulnerable natural features such as tall-herb noble deciduous forest and elements of elm-lime forest and boreonemoral rainforest with associated species of lichen and fungi. The aim is to maintain the conservation values in as undisturbed a state as possible, and, where appropriate, to further develop them.”

branas-naturreservat-natc7dfddf9.d: Brånås Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Bamble municipality. It comprises an area north of Bamlevann. The area was designated a nature reserve on 24 June 2025. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic is prohibited, including the take-off and landing of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses outside existing tractor tracks, farm tracks and paths marked on the conservation map are prohibited. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents specific types of natural habitat in the form of old pine and spruce forests, as well as well-developed, rich deciduous broad-leaved forest in the boreonemoral zone; b.

anas-naturreservat-nat6dad3254.d: Ånås Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Kviteseid municipality. It comprises an area by the Fjågesundstraumen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 24 June 2025. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing tractor tracks and footpaths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of rich mixed woodland in the boreonemoral zone and old coniferous forest containing an abundance of deadwood b.

heggeneset-naturreservat-nat91ea307c.d: Heggeneset Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Seljord municipality. It comprises an area by Lake Seljordsvatn. The area was designated a nature reserve on 24 June 2025. The reserve is part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside existing tractor tracks and footpaths. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to safeguard an area in the lowlands which a. contains threatened, rare or vulnerable natural features, such as the threatened habitat types of calcareous and low-herb pine forest, low-herb deciduous forest, southern calcareous rock and waterfall rock highly susceptible to drought, as well as many rare and threatened species within several groups of organisms, particularly insects; b.

yen-naturreservat-natca776aa2.d: Øyen Nature Reserve is a 590 dekar nature reserve in Sør-Odal municipality. It consists of wooded areas spread across several islands in Lake Storsjøen. The area was designated a nature reserve on 24 June 2025. The reserve forms part of the forest conservation plan. Motorised traffic on land is prohibited, including the landing and take-off of aircraft. Cycling, horse riding and the use of horses are prohibited outside the existing tractor tracks marked on the conservation map. The conservation regulations state that the purpose of the conservation is ‘to preserve an area which a. represents a specific type of natural environment in the form of old coniferous forest with elements of old deciduous forest; b. is of particular significance for biodiversity as it is an important habitat for species associated with old coniferous forest, deciduous forest and deadwood.

furuberget-naturreservat-nata0e1547f.d: Furuberget Nature Reserve is a 435-dekar nature reserve situated in Hamar municipality, bordering Lake Mjøsa to the west and Ringsaker municipality to the north. The area was established on 9 July 1993 and extended on 24 June 2025 on the basis of both its vegetation and geology. Furuberget is a limestone formation dating from the Middle Ordovician period, around 450 million years ago, with the northern part consisting of rock formed from Mjøsa limestone with a high calcium oxide (CaO) content, known as the Mjøsa Formation, containing up to 90 per cent CaO. The bedrock is fissured and therefore drains away a great deal of water.

leirfossen-nat85e7fd23.d: Leirfossen is the highest waterfall in the upper reaches of the River Alna in Oslo. The waterfall is approximately 15 metres high. It provided the power for industrial development when the Lerfossen Clothing Factory was established in 1867. At its peak, the factory employed 200 workers, many of whom were housed in four workers’ cottages on the upper side of the waterfall. Two of these have been preserved; they are located at Sagstuveien 1a and 1b. In the 1970s, the waterfall was dammed and the river was culverted. However, in 1985, the city council decided that the closure of rivers and streams was no longer permitted, and that piped sections should be reopened wherever possible. In 2011, the waterfall was reopened, and in 2013 the area was rehabilitated as part of the Groruddal initiative.

nieidagorzi-pikefossen-natdd2f68ff.d: Pikefossen (Northern Sami: Nieidagorži) is a waterfall on the Kautokeino River in Kautokeino municipality in Finnmark. It is 8 metres high and lies approximately 18 kilometres south of Masi. There is a good view of the waterfall from a rest area on European Route 45.

ringeriksfossen-nata2cbee7f.d: Ringeriksfossen is a waterfall in Muradalen in Kvinnherad municipality, Hordaland. The waterfall consists of two large drops, the largest of which is around 100 metres. After the first drop, there is a series of cascades, before the waterfall forms another drop of around 100 metres. In some places, the waterfall is described as having a much greater drop, which probably refers to the drop in the river that can be utilised for hydroelectric power generation.

tysvikjofossen-natddc54b5b.d: Tysvikjofossen is a waterfall in Måbødalen in Eidfjord municipality, Hordaland. The waterfall is situated right next to Vøringsfossen.

trollfoss-nat47564215.d: Trollfoss in Larvik municipality is Vestfold’s largest waterfall. The waterfall forms part of the Dalelva river, which flows from Svartangen and into the Numedalslågen.

nedre-foss-natad9fe444.d: Nedre Foss is a waterfall and was once a farm in Grünerløkka, Oslo, with a mill for grinding grain dating back to before 1200 and in continuous operation until 1985. In 2008, Oslo City Council decided that the area around the main building, where Bellona had offices from 1998 to 2010, should be developed into a new city park. Nedre Foss Park opened in 2017. The main building was restored and opened as a restaurant in 2015. On 30 December of the same year, parts of the farm were completely destroyed in a fire. In November 2017, the Nedre Foss Gård restaurant reopened.

labrofossen-nat76f7b697.d: Labrofossen is a waterfall on the Numedalslågen river at Labro, south of Kongsberg town centre, in Kongsberg municipality. It has a drop of 41 metres. The waterfall was developed in 1910 for hydroelectric power generation; in 1983, it was replaced by the Skollenborg power station. Following its closure, the power station at Labro was converted into a museum; it now houses the Labro Watercourse Museum, the Numedalslågen Log-Floating Museum and the Buskerud branch of the Norwegian Road Museum. Labrufossen is a popular subject in art, and many well-known artists have drawn inspiration from it. Below are a few examples.

grongstadfossen-nat043fb1b9.d: Grungstadfossen, also spelled Grongstadfossen, is situated in Høylandet municipality in Trøndelag. The waterfall forms part of the Nordåa river, approximately 1.5 km west of the village of Høylandet and 3 km north of Grungstad. The drop is 75 metres. A watermill operated at the waterfall in the 16th century and sawmills were in operation in the 18th century. A timber flume for log driving was built around 1860. It remained in use for 15 years before being replaced by a new timber flume at the same location. The remains of the approximately 300-metre-long flume were still visible in 1991. Høylandet municipality built a power station at Grungstadfossen, which was completed in the summer of 1916. It remained in operation until the power station burnt down on 9 April 1940.

bj-lsenfossen-nata7676fba.d: With a drop of 16 metres, Bjølsenfossen is the highest waterfall on the Akerselva in Oslo. It is situated south of Treschow’s Bridge at Bjølsen, and takes its name from the Bjølsen farm. In the 14th century, Bjølsen Mill was built by the waterfall. In the 19th century, the waterfall was important for industrial development in the area, supplying power to, amongst others, Bjølsen Valsemølle. Valsemølla eventually became the largest flour producer in Norway. The waterfall is situated within the rolling mill’s industrial estate, so the general public does not normally get close to it. Just above the waterfall lies Bjølsendammen, which served as the town’s water intake from 1860 to 1867.

feigefossen-nat850872c9.d: Feigefossen, or Feigumfossen, is a 229-metre-high waterfall in Luster municipality in Sogn og Fjordane. It is situated on the Feigedalselvi river, just above the hamlet of Feigum on the eastern side of the Lustrafjord. It has Norway’s fourth-highest vertical drop, with a total drop of 293 metres and a near-vertical drop of 200 metres, and a horizontal length of 300 metres. Other sources state a vertical drop of 218 metres. According to a list compiled by Finn Alnæs, this is the 46th highest in the world in terms of total drop. Henrik Wergeland visited Luster in 1832 and produced a coloured drawing in which he noted his estimate of the waterfall’s height: ‘500 feet vertical’. The watercourse was assessed for hydroelectric power in the 1980s.

skala-nat9d6ccdb5.d: Skåla is a mountain in Molde municipality in Møre og Romsdal. It rises to a height of 1,128 metres above sea level. The mountain’s primary elevation is 1,030 metres. The mountain is situated on the Skåla Peninsula and, until the municipal merger on 1 January 2020, was the highest mountain in Molde municipality. Following the merger with Nesset and Midsund municipalities, Høgbøra (Kleneggen), at 1,964.4 metres above sea level in Eikesdalen, is now the highest mountain in the municipality. Skåla lies within a belt of quartz monzonitic gneiss that runs along the peninsula. On both sides, the bedrock consists of granitic gneiss.

s-re-tverradalskyrkja-nata5112f28.d: Søre Tverrådalskyrkja is a mountain in Luster municipality in Vestland county. It rises to a height of 2,033 metres above sea level. 700 metres to the north-east lies the higher peak, Tverrådalskyrkja (2,089 metres above sea level).

kronprins-olavs-bre-natdc75a0a8.d: The Crown Prince Olav Glacier is the larger of the two glaciers on Jan Mayen. The glacier is situated in Nord-Jan, the north-western half of the island, on the southern side of Mount Beerenberg, which rises to 2,270 metres above sea level. Sørbreen is a glacier tongue extending southwards from Kronprins Olavs Bre between Vulkanlia and Sørhallet. On the north-eastern side of Beerenberg lies Kronprinsesse Märthas Bre.

kronprinsesse-marthas-bre-nat9a6a571c.d: Crown Princess Märtha’s Glacier is the smaller of the two glaciers on Jan Mayen. The glacier is situated in Nord-Jan, the north-western half of the island, on the north-eastern side of Mount Beerenberg, which rises 2,270 metres above sea level. On the southern side of Beerenberg lies Crown Prince Olav’s Glacier.

gruvfonna-nat2861c00a.d: Gruvfonna is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, situated between Reindalen and Kjellströmdalen in south-eastern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies 10 km north of the settlement of Sveagruva. It is the fifth-largest glacier in Nordenskiöld Land, surpassed only by the Fridtjov Glacier, the Grønfjord Glacier, the Slak Glacier and the Drøn Glacier. It is a glacier measuring approximately 4 × 3 km, which begins immediately east of the Slak Glacier and north of the Sjakt Glacier and the Höganäs Glacier. The glacier runs north-east of the mountains Skonuddan and Feiselen, and continues north-eastwards until it reaches the nunataks that form the boundary with the Props Glacier, the Martha Glacier and the Helsingborg Glacier. The glacier is a pure summit glacier that does not flow into any valley.

friggkapa-nat81c7f5d1.d: Friggkåpa is a glacier in Dickson Land on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It covers the central parts of Friggfjella, and has branches extending to Hugindalen in the north, Lyckholmdalen in the west, and Odindalen in the east. Friggkåpa is named after Frigg, a goddess in Norse mythology.

ahlmannfonna-natdc505ca3.d: Ahlmannfonna is a glacier on Nordaustlandet in Svalbard. The glacier is approximately 6 kilometres in diameter and is situated in the southern part of Prince Oscar’s Land. It is named after Hans Wilhelmsson Ahlmann (1889–1974). See also Ahlmannfjellet.

longyearbreen-nat41b6c03b.d: Longyearbreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south-west of Longyearbyen. It is an icefield approximately 4.5 km long, starting at Teltberget (1,025 metres above sea level) and running from there north-eastwards between Lars Hiertafjellet (876 metres above sea level) and Nordenskiöldfjellet (1,053 metres above sea level) to the west, and into the upper reaches of the Longyeardalen valley, south of Adventfjorden in Nordenskiöld Land. It is easily visible from Longyearbyen and has deposited large moraines at its front, situated at the foot of the mountain Sarkofagen, near Nye Gruve 1 and Gruve 4. The glacier lies to the west of Larsbreen and is named after Longyearbyen. A large quantity of rock containing fossils of deciduous trees from the Cretaceous period has been washed out in front of the glacier, and these can be found along the Longyearelva river down the valley.

larsbreen-nat33286e5b.d: Larsbreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south of Longyearbyen. It is an icefield approximately 3.5 km long, stretching from Trollsteinen (850 m) and Lars Hiertafjellet (876 m) in the south, and flowing north-westwards into the Longyeardalen valley, south of Adventfjorden in Nordenskiöld Land. It is easily visible from Longyearbyen and has deposited large moraines at its front, which lie at the foot of the mountain Sarkofagen. Rock containing fossils of deciduous trees from the Cretaceous period has been washed out in front of the glacier, and these can be found along the Longyearelva river down the valley. The glacier is named after the Swedish publisher and politician Lars Johan Hierta (1801–1872).

stensiobreen-nat078d23d5.d: The Stensiö Glacier is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is situated at the head of the Hugindalen valley in the central part of Dickson Land. The glacier is named after the Swedish palaeontologist Erik Stensiö.

granutbreen-nat60a72da8.d: Grånutbreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that flows eastwards from Grånutane (752 m) and Kleivdalsnuten (606 m), along the north face of Hanekammen (620 m) and eastwards to the southernmost part of the Fridtjov Glacier. It forms part of Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The glacier is named after Grånutane, which lies to the north-west.

sagabreen-nat521a615c.d: Sagabreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that flows eastwards from the north face of Ingeborgfjellet (620 m) towards Hanekammen (620 m) and eastwards to the outlet of the Fridtjov Glacier in Fridtjovhamna. It forms part of Nordenskiöld Land National Park, but lies just outside the boundary of the Ramsar site, which otherwise encompasses the whole of Ingeborgfjellet. The glacier is named after the ‘Fridtjov’s Saga’, from which Ingeborgfjellet takes its name.

v-ringbreen-nat42acd5f0.d: The Vøring Glacier is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, just west of Barentsburg on the other side of Grønfjorden. It is around 1.5 km long and lies near the mountains Vøringen (676 m) and Sokolovtoppen (542 m). The glacier lies on the fault line between the south-western terrain, with bedrock to the west, and Spitsbergen’s central Tertiary basin, with sediments to the east. The glacier slopes eastwards from the fault line. The glacier is named after the ship ‘Vøringen’, which was used on the Norwegian North Atlantic Expedition.

klausbreen-nate5f73e63.d: Klausbreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that extends from Thuefjellet in the west and flows into the slightly larger Dahlfonna glacier from the west – in the far west of Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies on the fault line between the south-western terrain, with bedrock to the west, and Spitsbergen’s central Tertiary basin, with sediments to the east. The glacier slopes eastwards from the fault line. The glacier lies in a trough between Klosterfjellet (820 m) in the south-east and Thuefjellet (607 m) in the west. The entire glacier forms part of Nordenskiöld Land National Park and the Nordenskiöld Coast Ramsar site. The glacier is named after the trapper Klaus Thue (1856–1929; born in Skjåk in Gudbrandsdalen), who spent many winters on Svalbard.

gleditschfonna-nat4bb8c9fa.d: Gleditschfonna is a 4 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 2.5 km long glacier that stretches from Nordbergfjellet (624 m) near Baalsrudbreen in the north-west to Snøsalen (677 m) in the north-east, and flows south-eastwards into Berzeliusdalen north of Van Mijenfjorden, in the west of Nordenskiöld Land. The entire glacier lies within Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The glacier is named after the officer Kristen Gran Gleditsch (1867–1946), who worked on the mapping of Svalbard.

dahlfonna-nat5c227391.d: Dahlfonna is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier stretching from Erdmannbreen in the south to Orustdalen and Grønfjordbreen in the north, in the far south-west of Nordenskiöld Land. The smaller Klausbreen flows down into Dahlfonna from the west. The entire glacier forms part of Nordenskiöld Land National Park and the Nordenskiöld Coast Ramsar Site. The glacier lies in a trough between Haroldfjellet (664 m) to the east and Thuefjellet (607 m) to the west. To the north, where the glacier flows into the Orust Valley, there are some small moraine deposits. The glacier lies on the fault line between the south-western terrain with bedrock to the west and Spitsbergen’s central Tertiary basin with sediments to the east. The glacier slopes eastwards from the fault line.

innerbreen-nat013184f6.d: Innerbreen is a 4 km long glacier covering an area of 3.5 km² on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, in the mountain range situated between the upper Kjellströmdalen and the upper Sassendalen, far to the south-west of Sabine Land. Innerbreen is a western side glacier of the large Hellefonna, and carries large masses of moraine before it, which end at the very top of Oppdalen in the south (a side valley of Lundströmdalen). To the north lies the mountain Skrinnfjellet (906 m). The name means ‘the innermost glacier’.

vrabreen-nated13060c.d: Vråbreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen in Svalbard. It is situated at the head of the Kjellström Valley, between Storslengja to the south and Svenfjellet and Cösterfjellet to the north. The glacier is around four kilometres long. The Kjellströmelva river rises from the glacier’s terminus. The word ‘vrå’ in the name comes from the Old Norse ‘vrá/ró’, meaning ‘bend’ or ‘remote place’, which in this context may refer to the fact that the valley in which the glacier lies makes a bend, and is therefore winding.

jinnbreen-nate9fc11d8.d: Jinnbreen is a 4 km long and 4 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, in the mountain range situated between the upper Kjellströmdalen and the upper Sassendalen, far to the south-west of Sabine Land. Jinnbreen is a western lateral glacier of the large Hellefonna, and carries large masses of moraine before it, which end in the Vendom Valley in the north-west – together with the loose material from the Vendom Glacier. To the north lies the mountain Dalsnuten (621 m). Jinnbreen takes its name from the desert spirits known as djinn in Islamic mythology.

marmorbreen-nat48fd10ed.d: The Marmorbreen is a 3 km long and 3 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, in the mountain range situated between the upper Kjellströmdalen and the upper Sassendalen, far south-west in Sabine Land. Marmorbreen is an eastern lateral glacier of the large Hellefonna, and carries large moraine masses in front of it that end at the very top of Fulmardalen in the north and at Jøkulvatnet in the east. To the south lies the mountain Raggfjellet (571 m). The Marmorbreen takes its name from the play of colours in the glacier.

klauvbreen-nata25116cb.d: The Klauvbreen is an 8 km long glacier covering an area of 16 km², and a western tributary of the much larger Nordmannsfonna on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier arm lies in the mountain range between Storfjorden and the upper Sassendalen valley, in the heart of Sabine Land. It runs east of Moskushornet and west of Klauva – and down into Rabotbreen, which continues into the upper Sassendalen valley, where Klauvbreen forms a long belt of moraine and loose material in the ice-covered valley floor to the east. Klauvbreen takes its name from the mountain Klauva, which derives from the word ‘klauv’.

skrottbreen-nat52579fa6.d: Skrottbreen is a glacier 4 km long and covering an area of 3 km², and a western tributary of the much larger Nordmannsfonna on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier’s tongue lies in the mountain range between Storfjorden and the upper Sassendalen valley, in the heart of Sabine Land. It runs east of Wallenbergfjellet and west of Skrottnuten, north of Lumpen – and down towards Rabotbreen in the upper Sassendalen valley, where it deposits some moraine and loose material in the valley high above the ice-covered valley floor. Skrottbreen takes its name from the mountain Skrottnuten, which in turn is named after the Norwegian mountain Skrott in Kvam, Hordaland.

klunsbreen-nataafa7cea.d: Klunsbreen is a glacier 2.5 km long and covering an area of 3 km², and an eastern branch of the larger Elfenbeinbreen in the southern part of Nordmannsfonna on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier’s tongue lies in the mountain massif between Storfjorden and the upper Sassendalen valley, in the heart of Sabine Land. It runs southwards from the glacial head Iskaka, north of Roslagenfjellet and south of the gentle slope of Klunsen, and down into the Elfenbein Glacier before reaching Agardhdalen. The Kluns Glacier takes its name from the mountain Klunsen.

isrosa-natbbd3f37f.d: Isrosa is a 6 km long glacier covering an area of 20 km², and a south-eastern tributary of the larger Nordmannsfonna on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier’s tongue lies in the mountain range between Storfjorden and the upper Sassendalen valley, in the heart of Sabine Land. It runs eastwards from the glacier head at Iskaka and south of Buckhøgda (614 m), and via Buckfallet down to Ulvebreen, where it meets this glacier with large surface deposits of moraine and boulders. To the south, the glacier descends towards Eistradalen and Væringsdalen, but without following these valleys down towards Agardhdalen. The glacier stops on the high plateau above the two valley floors, carrying very little moraine or loose material with it.

lumpbreen-natea6f167c.d: The Lumpbreen is a 3 km long glacier covering an area of 3 km², and a western tributary of the much larger Nordmannsfonna on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier arm lies in the mountain range between Storfjorden and the upper Sassendalen valley, in the heart of Sabine Land. It runs south of Wallenbergfjellet and Lumpen and north of Ryssen, down into the upper Fulmardalen, where it forms a fan of moraine and loose material nearly 2 km wide, extending all the way down to the Fulmarelva. Lumpbreen takes its name from the mountain Lumpen.

dolkbreen-nat00cfc893.d: The Dolk Glacier is a 3 km long glacier covering an area of 3 km², and a north-western tributary of the larger Elfenbein Glacier in the southern part of Nordmannsfonna on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier arm lies in the mountain massif between Storfjorden and the upper Sassendalen valley, in the heart of Sabine Land. It runs north of Prospektryggen and south of the gentle Dolken ridge, flowing down into the Elfenbeinbreen glacier before reaching Agardhdalen. Dolkbreen takes its name from the mountain Dolken.

vassdalsbreen-nat71572cb9.d: The Vassdalsbreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south of the Marstranderbreen. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that extends from Vassdalsnuten (748 m) and flows southwards along the eastern face of Snøkampen (763 m) and into the upper reaches of Vassdalen, north of Van Mijenfjorden – in the south-west of Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies entirely within Nordenskiöld Land National Park. It is named after Vassdalen.

kalvdalsbreen-natc1bf7bd9.d: The Kalvdalsbreen is a 3 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south of the Marstranderbreen. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that extends from Vassdalsnuten (748 m) and flows eastwards along the southern face of Kalvhøgda (784 m) and into the upper reaches of Kalvdalen, just north of Van Mijenfjorden – in the south-west of Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies entirely within Nordenskiöld Land National Park. It is named after Kalvdalen.

skavlefjellbreen-nat237274c5.d: The Skavlefjell Glacier is a glacier west of the Tungebreen Glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an icefield approximately 1.5 km long, extending from Skavlefjellet (839 m) and touching Tungebreen to the south, before flowing northwards into Grøndalen, in the west of Nordenskiöld Land. The southernmost part of the glacier borders Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The glacier is named after Skavlefjellet, which lies to the south of it.

tungebreen-nat72308c89.d: Tungebreen is a glacier west of Tavlebreen on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that extends from Lovberget (777 m), touching Tungebreen, Skavlefjellbreen and Marstranderbreen to the south, and flows northwards into Grøndalen, in the west of Nordenskiöld Land. The southernmost part of the glacier borders Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The glacier is named after the landform.

stenehjembreen-natc7a85a83.d: The Stenehjembreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south-east of the Iskollbreen and north of the Kolfjellbreen. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that extends from Iskollen (602 m) in the west, flowing eastwards along the north face of Iskollen and into Vassdalen just north of Van Mijenfjorden – in the south-west of Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier is named after the Norwegian Arctic explorer Ivar Stenehjem, who built the hut at Camp Morton.

kolfjellbreen-nat009a3a28.d: The Kolfjell Glacier is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south-east of the Iskoll Glacier and south of the Stenehjemb Glacier. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that extends from Hesselbergaksla (661 m) in the west, and flows eastwards along the north face of Kolfjellet (707 m) into Vassdalen just north of Van Mijenfjorden – in the south-west of Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier is named after Kolfjellet.

rypefjellbreen-nat33642310.d: The Rypefjell Glacier is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south of the Kalvdals Glacier. It is an approximately 2 km long glacier that extends from Rypefjellet (761 m) and flows eastwards along the southern face of Kjuklingtoppane (692 m) and into the lower Kalvdalen valley, just north of Van Mijenfjorden – in the south-west of Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies entirely within Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The mountain and the glacier are named after the rock ptarmigan.

blekumbreen-natfc617fc0.d: The Blekumbreen is a 3 km long glacier covering an area of 1.5 km² on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, situated between Adventdalen and Isfjorden in northern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies near Birkafjellet (976 m) and Operafjellet in the mountain range north-east of Longyearbyen. To the north lies Mälarbreen; to the east, there is a direct transition via a ridge to Tellbreen. Blekumbreen carries a moraine mass some 500 metres in front of it down towards Mälardalen, which flows directly into Adventdalen at the delta of Adventfjorden. Blekumbreen is named after the Norwegian mining manager Sverre Blekum (1886–1944), who carried out research into the coal seams in the area in 1921. He later became director of the Knaben mines.

altbreen-natfd4b10ee.d: Altbreen is a 2 km long and 1.5 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, situated between Adventdalen and Isfjorden in northern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies between Operafjellet to the west and Helvetiafjellet to the east, in the mountain range north-east of Longyearbyen. To the north lies Tellbreen; to the west, there is a direct transition via a ridge to Blekumbreen. Altbreen carries just over 200 metres of moraine deposits down towards Koslådalen, which opens directly into Adventdalen opposite Gruve 7-fjellet. Altbreen takes its name from the musical term ‘alt’ and derives from the glacier’s close association with Operafjellet and the three neighbouring peaks: Dirigenten (928 metres above sea level), Tenoren (655 metres above sea level) and Bassen (968 metres above sea level).

tellbreen-nat2a1f19dc.d: Tellbreen is a 3 km long glacier covering an area of 2.5 km² on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, between Adventdalen and Isfjorden in northern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies near Birkafjellet (976 m) and Operafjellet in the mountain range north-east of Longyearbyen. To the north lies Fangenbreen, whilst to the west there is a direct passage via a ridge to Blekumbreen. Tellbreen carries a moraine deposit just over 200 metres in front of it down towards Helvetiadalen, which flows directly into Adventdalen north of Janssonhaugen. Tellbreen is named after the legendary Swiss figure Wilhelm Tell.

brandtbreen-nat24e04ae2.d: Brandtbreen is a 3 km long glacier covering an area of 1.5 km² on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, situated between Adventdalen and Isfjorden in northern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies near Telgefjellet (921 m), Stäket (1,030 m) and Kjødetoppen (769 m) in the mountain range north-east of Longyearbyen. Brandtbreen carries a moraine over 200 metres wide down towards the Hanaskogelva river, which flows directly into Adventfjorden just west of Revneset. To the east lies Blackbreen. Brandtbreen is named after the German oceanographer and polar explorer Karl Brandt (1854–1931).

malarbreen-natdcedefe8.d: The Mälarbreen is a 3 km long glacier covering an area of 2 km² on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, situated between Adventdalen and Isfjorden in northern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies near Birkafjellet (976 m), Kjødetoppen (769 m) and Stäket (1,030 m) in the mountain range north-east of Longyearbyen. To the south lies the Blekumbreen glacier. The Mälarbreen glacier carries a moraine over 200 metres wide down towards Mälardalen, which flows directly into Adventdalen at the delta of Adventfjorden. The Mälarbreen glacier is named after the Swedish lake Mälaren.

bogerbreen-nat35d3dc9d.d: Bogerbreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, south of Longyearbyen. It is an approximately 4 km long glacier that extends from Westbytoppane (983 m) and Bingtoppen (912 m) in the south, flowing northwards into the snowmobile-free Endalen valley, south of Adventdalen in Nordenskiöld Land. It lies by the pass leading towards Fardalen and has deposited small amounts of moraine in front of it. The glacier lies east of Dryadebreen and is named after the Norwegian mining manager Finn Boger (1902–), who for a time headed the Kings Bay Kull Company AS.

vesljuvbreen-nat84539cfc.d: Vesljuvbreen is a small glacier in Jotunheimen, in the municipality of Lom in the Innlandet region. It is situated close to Juvasshytta, north-east of Galdhøpiggen. On 11 November 1957, a 15-year-old girl died after falling into a crevasse. The Galdhøpiggen summer ski centre is located on the glacier.

svellnosbrean-nat2ea25af4.d: The Svellnos Glacier is a glacier in Jotunheimen, situated in the municipality of Lom. It is 10,000 years old and is shrinking every year.

storskavlen-natbcd47168.d: Storskavlen is a glacier in the south of Aurland municipality in Vestland. Its highest point is now ice-free and lies 1,729.3 metres above sea level.

fornesbreen-nat478a902a.d: Fornesbreen is a glacier in Ullsfjord in the municipality of Tromsø, Troms. It is situated in Lyngsalpan, on the southern side of Kjosen. The glacier covers an area of 6.34 km². It stretches for around 3.5 kilometres from its highest point in the south, at 1,684 metres above sea level, to its lowest point in the north, at 654 metres above sea level. One of the main tributaries of the Forneselva river has its source at the glacier front.

styggebrean-nat19d5d76d.d: Styggebreen is a glacier in Jotunheimen, on the eastern side of Galdhøpiggen in Lom municipality in Innlandet. Many people cross the Styggebreen on their way up to the summit of Galdhøpiggen from Juvasshytta. On 20 July 1993, a man fell into a crevasse on the glacier and died.

vinnufonna-nat2fc99b82.d: Vinnufonna is a glacier in Sunndal municipality in Møre og Romsdal county. Vinnufonna covers an area of 0.96 km² and is 1.8 km long. As of 2012, its area was 1.16 km². It is the largest glacier in Møre og Romsdal. Sunndalsfjella has 259 glaciers and 23 mountain peaks over 1,800 m. Vinnufonna ranges in altitude from 1,150 to 1,800 metres above sea level.

nupsfonn-nat51810f79.d: Nupsfonn is a glacier in Ullensvang municipality in Vestland and Vinje municipality in Telemark. The glacier lies in the south of Hardangervidda, on the western side of Nupsegga (1,674 metres above sea level). The glacier covers an area of 2.31 km² and consists of three glacier tongues: Store Nupsfonn (0.47 km²), Nupsfonn West (1.15 km²) and Nupsfonn East (0.68 km²). Nupsfonn East, which lies on the border between Ullensvang and Vinje, is no longer connected to the rest of the glacier, which lies entirely within Ullensvang. The highest point is on Store Nupsfonn in the north, which rises to 1,641 metres above sea level.

vestre-memurubrean-nate00ac63c.d: Vestre Memurubreen is a glacier in Jotunheimen. Hellstugubreen is a northern branch of the same glacier. The glacier lies to the east of the Hellstugutindene peaks and to the south of Vestre Memurutinden in Lom municipality, Innlandet county.

storjuvbrean-nat27dd52f9.d: Storjuvbrean (Storjuvbreen) is a glacier in Jotunheimen on the north-facing slope of Galdhøpiggen in Lom municipality in the Innlandet region. Two people taking part in the TV programme ‘71 Degrees North’ in 2001 were injured when they were struck by a rockfall from the moraine ridge by the glacier.

sm-rstabbreen-natf8e7ecdd.d: The Smørstabbreen is the largest glacier in Jotunheimen and is situated near Smørstabbtindan, east of Sognefjellet. The Smørstabbreen is a plateau glacier with three glacier arms: Bøverbrean and Leirbrean to the west, and Sandelvbrean to the north-east. The glacier is easily accessible from Krossbu via County Road 55 and from Leirvassbu. In summer, there is a fixed route across the glacier between these two mountain huts. For many years, the Norwegian Trekking Association (DNT) has run glacier courses on the Smørstabbreen, starting from Krossbu.

skagast-lsbreen-natd2f1eef0.d: Skagastølsbreen is a glacier situated between Store Dyrhaugstindane and Skagastølsryggen in Hurrungane, in the western part of Jotunheimen. The path to Skagastølsbu from the north crosses Skagastølsbreen.

gunvordalsbreen-nat50649769.d: The Gunvordalsbreen is a glacier at the head of the Gunvordalen valley in Sogndal, Vestland. The glacier used to cover the summit of the mountain, but the summit, at 1,604 metres above sea level, is now ice-free. The name Gunvordalsbreen has also been used to refer to the mountain peak, which forms the boundary with the former neighbouring municipality of Leikanger. This is the highest point in Leikanger.

tverrbotnbreen-nateb8aebb6.d: The Tverrbotn Glacier is a glacier in Breheimen, on the border between Luster in Vestland and Skjåk in Innlandet. The glacier lies between the Grein Glacier to the west and the Harbards Glacier to the east. The highest point on the glacier is Rivenoskulen, at 1,943 metres above sea level.

greinbreen-nat44742d84.d: Not to be confused with Greinbreane on Spitsbergen. Greinbreen is a glacier in Breheimen on the border between Luster in Vestland and Skjåk in Innlandet. The glacier lies between Tverrbotnbreen to the east and Jostedalsbreen to the west. It extends up towards a mountain peak to the west. The summit was previously covered by the glacier but is now ice-free. The highest point, at 1,847.6 metres above sea level, marks the county boundary between Innlandet and Vestland, and can be regarded as the summit of Greineggi.

ringsbreen-natfe4acb0d.d: Ringsbreen is a glacier in the Hurrungane range in Jotunheimen. The glacier lies north of Ringstindane in the municipalities of Luster and Årdal in Vestland county. Ringsbreen actually consists of several, partly disjointed valley glaciers, with a total area of 2.09 km². Ringsbreen extends far up the eastern flank of Store Ringstind and offers an excellent opportunity for a ski ascent of this distinctive peak.

styggedalsbreen-nate8b5bbcf.d: The Styggedalsbreen is a glacier in the Hurrungane range in Jotunheimen. The glacier lies to the east of Skagastølstindane in Luster municipality in Vestland county.

bergsetbreen-nat66e1dc83.d: Bergsetbreen is a glacier tongue of the Jostedalsbreen. Bergsetbreen is situated in Krundalen in Jostedalen, in the municipality of Luster in Vestland county. Bergsetbreen is about an hour’s walk from the road at Bergset farm. In 1986, three Dutch hikers were killed by an ice avalanche on the path leading to Bergsetbreen. The avalanche originated from Baklibreen, another glacier tongue of Jostedalsbreen that could not be seen from the path.

brenndalsbreen-nat5c5eba88.d: The Brenndalsbreen is a glacier arm of the Jostedalsbreen, and is situated in a side valley of the Oldedalen in Stryn municipality. The glacier is the neighbouring glacier arm of the better-known Briksdalsbreen, which lies further south in the valley on the other side of Svartenibba. The glacier drains via the River Brenna. During the cold periods of the 18th century, Brenndalsbreen expanded significantly.

breifonna-natbb6f2462.d: Breifonna is a glacier in the far north of Jostedalsbreen National Park in Stryn municipality in Vestland. Due to glacial retreat, the summit is now bare rock. This summit has not been given a name other than that of the glacier, but the name of the mountain next to it (Storskredfjellet) is sometimes used. The highest point is 1,814 metres above sea level.

skalabreen-nat5934fc2f.d: Skålabreen is a glacier in Jostedalsbreen National Park in Stryn municipality in Vestland. The glacier is situated on the mountain between Lovatnet and Oppstrynsvatnet, north-west of Tindefjellbreen.

nautbreen-nat17444f43.d: Nautbreen is a free-standing glacier on the north-eastern side of the Sandskarhyrna mountain, in Stryn municipality. The glacier can be reached via Glomsdalen from Glomnes in Oppstryn.

skjerdingdalsbreen-nat950592dd.d: The Skjerdingdalsbreen is a glacier on Strynefjellet in the municipalities of Stryn and Stranda. The highest point on the glacier is 1,651 metres above sea level. The glacier drains into both the Geirangerelva and the Otta.

tuftebreen-natf04a9f9f.d: Tuftebreen is a glacier arm of the Jostedalsbreen in Luster municipality in Vestland. The glacier is situated in Tufteskardet, in a side valley of Krundalen in Jostedalen, approximately 3 km south-west of Nigardsbreen. It covers an area of 6.5 km² and is 6.5 km long. The highest point on the glacier is 1,920 metres above sea level and the lowest is 860 metres above sea level. Until the early 20th century, Tuftebreen was usually known as ‘Tverrbreen’. On 1 April 2002, the glacier broke away and injured two people near the glacier. On 14 July 2001, a 45-year-old man fell into a crevasse here and was seriously injured. During the Little Ice Age in the 17th and 18th centuries, the Tufte Glacier advanced rapidly through Tufteskardet and reached all the way down to the valley floor in Krundalen.

austdalsbreen-nat58c0d7e1.d: The Austdalsbreen is a glacier arm in the north-eastern part of the Jostedalsbreen in Luster municipality. The glacier lies between Rundeggi to the north, Austdalsnuten to the south and calves into Austdalsvatnet to the south-east. Glaciological surveys of the glacier have been carried out since 1986, in connection with the regulation of the Jostedøla river and Austdalsvatnet for hydroelectric power. From the regulation of the Jostedøla river in 1988 until 2022, the glacier front has retreated by approximately 700 metres and the area of the glacier has decreased by over 0.56 km². The glacier receives four to five metres of snow during a normal winter. Near the glacier front, the glacier moves at a rate of approximately 50 metres per year, although this movement depends on the regulation of Austdalsvatnet.

lokebreen-nat90433527.d: Lokebreen is a glacier tongue on the Jostedalsbreen glacier and is one of three glacier tongues extending down towards the Austerdalsbreen glacier. Lokebreen is situated at Veitastrond in Luster municipality in Vestland county. Lokebreen is not connected to Austerdalsbreen, but contributes mass to it through ice avalanches.

sekkebreen-nat8eb6fbf0.d: Sekkebreen, or Sikilbreen, is a glacier in Breheimen in Skjåk municipality in the Innlandet region. It has a total area of 21 km², making it the 18th largest glacier in Norway, excluding Svalbard. Sikilbreen is also the name of a glacier situated just to the west of this glacier, on the border with Vestland. The highest point on the glacier was long given as 1,930 metres above sea level, but the elevation has now fallen to 1,906.9 metres above sea level. A peak that has now become ice-free on the western edge of the glacier reaches 1,904 metres above sea level.

raudeggbreen-nat0ef370ca.d: Raudeggbreen is a glacier in Skjåk municipality in the Innlandet region. It is situated on Strynefjellet, just south of Gamle Strynefjellsvegen. The glacier covers an area of 1.94 km² and lies between 1,478 and 1,868 metres above sea level. It is named after the mountain Raudeggi (1,939 metres above sea level), which lies just south of the glacier. The entire glacier lies within Breheimen National Park.

sealggajiek-a-nat4870539c.d: The Storsteinsfjell Glacier (Northern Sami: Sealggajiekŋa) is a glacier in Narvik municipality in Nordland. The glacier lies to the east of Skjomen, around 10 kilometres from the Swedish border. It covers an area of 12 km² and is thus the 30th largest glacier on the Norwegian mainland. The glacier is situated on Storsteinsfjellet (1,894 metres above sea level), between Sealggajávri in the north and Norddalen in the south.

mj-lkedalsbreen-nat501bf893.d: The Mjølkedalsbreen is a glacier in Jotunheimen on the border between the counties of Innlandet and Vestland. It is situated in the municipalities of Vang and Luster, north-west of Lake Bygdin and north of Lake Tyin. It covers an area of 3.3 km² and is 3.3 km long. The glacier lies between Mjølkedalspiggan in the north and Langekalvtinden in the south. It borders the Uranos Glacier at Uranostinden in the west. Skogadalsbreen lies just west of Ureknatten, with which it shares a border. Mjølkedalsbreen previously experienced regular jökulhlaupar – large, sudden floods – during the 19th century and the first half of the 20th century. At that time, the water flowed via the rivers Vinstra and Mjølkedøla through the Mjølkedalen valley from Øvre Mjølkedalsvatn. The largest such event of the 20th century occurred on 3.

glitterbrean-natb7864828.d: Glitterbreen is a glacier on the south-eastern side of Glittertinden, the second-highest mountain peak in Norway, in Jotunheimen in the municipality of Lom in the Innlandet region. The glacier borders Gråsubreen to the north-west, and Grotbreen lies on the northern side of Glittertinden. On 16 July 2001, a 50-year-old British man fell on the ice and slid 250 metres down the steep glacier, striking a rocky area and losing his life.

hellstugubrean-nat31e9fb27.d: Hellstugubreen is a glacier in Jotunheimen. Vestre Memurubreen is an eastern branch of the same glacier. The glacier lies east of Hellstugutindene, west of Memurutindan and flows into Visdalen near Spiterstulen in Lom municipality in Innlandet county. The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE) has been carrying out mass balance measurements of the Hellstugubreen glacier since 1962. Front measurements have been carried out since 1901.

leirbrean-nate280cad3.d: Leirbreen is a glacier in Jotunheimen on the western side of Smørstabbtindan and just north of Smørstabbreen and Storebjørn. It is situated in Lom municipality in the Innlandet region, just east of Sognefjellhytta. The glacier covers an area of 4.9 km² and is 3.8 km long.

sandelvbrean-nata752f3d3.d: Sandelvbrean (Sandelvbreen) is a glacier arm of the Smørstabbreen in Jotunheimen, in the municipality of Lom in the Innlandet region. The glacier lies between Søre Smørstabbtinden and Surtningstinden and covers an area of 1.6 km². In 1946, a man fell into a crevasse and died. His remains were not found until 1978.

b-verbrean-nata3134f14.d: Bøverbrean or Bøverbreen is a glacier tongue of the Smørstabbreen in Jotunheimen and Lom municipality in Innlandet. It stretches 7 km westwards towards the nearby Sognefjellshytta. The glacier reaches a maximum altitude of 2,143 metres above sea level and a minimum of 1,432 metres above sea level. It lies on the western side of Smørstabbtindan, between Leirhøe to the north and Falkeberget to the south.

bohrsbreen-nat68935576.d: The Bohr Glacier is a glacier tongue of the Jostedal Glacier in Stryn municipality in Vestland. It is situated on the western side of the glacier, just west of Lodalskåpa.

b-dalsbreen-nat7df46f66.d: Not to be confused with Bødalsbreen (Svalbard), which lies between Barentsburg and Longyearbyen. Bødalsbreen is a glacier in Stryn municipality in Vestland county. The glacier is a tributary of the Jostedalsbreen glacier, flowing down towards Bødalen. The glacial stream from Bødalsbreen flows into the small lake Sætrevatnet, which lies just above Bødalsseter.

veitbreen-natc391a8b0.d: Veitbreen is a glacier 5 km long and covering an area of 3 km², and is a north-western parallel glacier to the larger Elfenbeinbreen, in the south-west of Nordmannsfonna on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. The glacier’s tongue lies in the mountain massif between Storfjorden and the upper Sassendalen valley, in the heart of Sabine Land. It runs west of Prospektryggen and east of Storfjellet, descending into the upper Agardhdalen, where it forms a moraine and loose material embankment nearly 1 km wide. Veitbreen takes its name from ‘veit’, meaning ‘ditch’, referring to the narrow, long ditch-like shape at the bottom of the glacier’s course.

vardebreen-nat240456f6.d: Vardebreen is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, just west of Barentsburg on the other side of Grønfjorden. It is around 1.5 km long and lies near the mountains Vardeborg (588 m) and Vardåsen (567 m). The glacier is named after the mountain Vardeborg, which it borders, and its name derives from the shape of a ‘varde’ (a type of cairn). The glacier lies on the fault line between the south-western terrain, with bedrock to the west, and Spitsbergen’s central Tertiary basin, with sediments to the east. The glacier slopes eastwards from the fault line. Below the glacier there are a number of moraine deposits, and the river Festningselva flows eastwards into Grønfjorden.

marstranderbreen-natd6509c29.d: The Marstrander Glacier is a 5 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 3.5 km long glacier that extends from Kalvhøgda (784 m) in the east, flowing westwards into Berzeliusdalen north of Van Mijenfjorden, in the west of Nordenskiöld Land. The entire glacier lies within Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The glacier is named after the civil servant Fredrik Kristian Marstrander (1881–1946), who worked on Svalbard matters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

baalsrudbreen-natb1d060e4.d: The Baalsrud Glacier is a 3.5 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is approximately 2 km long and stretches from Nordbergfjellet (624 m) in the south to Gleditschfonna and Jamdalsnuten (569 m) in the north. The glacier flows north-westwards into the Grønfjord Valley south of Grønfjorden, in the west of Nordenskiöld Land. The eastern side of the glacier borders Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The glacier is named after the optician Sigurd Baalsrud (born 1881), who manufactured and repaired the theodolites for many Norwegian expeditions to Svalbard.

iskollbreen-nat48d4e1d6.d: The Iskoll Glacier is a glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It is an approximately 1 km long glacier that extends from Hesselbergaksla (661 m) in the south, flowing north-westwards into Berzeliusdalen north of Van Mijenfjorden, in the west of Nordenskiöld Land. The entire glacier lies within Nordenskiöld Land National Park. The glacier is named after the nearby mountain Iskollen (602 metres above sea level).

blackbreen-nat3c171ba4.d: Blackbreen is a 3 km long and 2 km² glacier on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, between Adventdalen and Isfjorden in northern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies near Telgefjellet (921 m), Stäket (1030 m) and Knorringfjellet (948 m) in the mountain range north-east of Longyearbyen. Blackbreen carries a moraine over 500 metres long down towards Tobredalen, which flows directly into De Geerdalen, which in turn runs north to Isfjorden. Blackbreen is named after the American David Black, who was mine manager for the Spitsbergen Coal and Trading Co. from 1904 to 1906 or 1907.

knorringbreen-nat635ca89a.d: The Knorring Glacier is a 2 km long glacier covering an area of 3 km² on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, situated between Adventdalen and Isfjorden in northern Nordenskiöld Land. The glacier lies near Telgefjellet (921 m), Knorringfjellet (948 m) and Wimanfjellet (912 m) in the mountain range north-east of Longyearbyen. Knorringbreen carries a moraine over 500 metres long down towards the Hanaskogelva river, which flows directly into Adventfjorden just west of Revneset. A lateral glacier to the north descends towards the upper Wimandalen valley. The Knorring Glacier is named after the Swedish officer and polar explorer Otto Wilhelm von Knorring (1863–1933).

mareminnehollet-nat29e0ec6b.d: Mareminehollet, Mareminehullet or Niels Klim’s Cave is situated in Rothaugsfjellet, a hill between Skuteviken and Sandviken in the Bergenhus district of Bergen. The Bergen City Encyclopaedia links the name to the Danish word ‘mareminde’, meaning ‘little mermaid’; according to legend, one such creature is said to have lived here. In Danish, the form ‘marminde’ can also mean ‘little sea man’, cf. ‘marmæle’, which means the same thing. Children would stand outside Mareminehullet and sing: ‘Mare, mare minde, if you’re in there, you must come out here. Another interpretation is that ‘maremine’ means ‘quarry by the sea’, as stone is said to have been quarried for ballast below the hole in the 19th century.

nordenskiold-fjellet-natc5d9f420.d: Nordenskiöldfjellet is a mountain in Nordenskiöld Land on Spitsbergen, Svalbard. It rises to a height of 1,051 metres above sea level and lies to the west of the Longyear Glacier and around 7 kilometres south-west of Longyearbyen. The mountain is named after the Swedish geologist and polar explorer Professor Adolf Erik Nordenskiöld, who led five research expeditions to Svalbard between 1858 and 1873. At the summit of the mountain stands a Swedish hut that was built for research purposes during a Swedish scientific expedition in 1930–32.

nedalshytta-nat4686510d.d: Nedalshytta is a tourist cabin in Sylan, in the municipality of Tydal in Trøndelag. The lodge is run by Trondheim Tourist Association and is situated at the south-eastern end of Lake Nesjøen, with marked trails leading to Stugudal, Storerikvollen and Sylarnas Fjällstation. The current Nedalshytta was built in 1971, replacing the old Nedalshytta, which was submerged when Lake Nesjøen was dammed. It lies at the foot of Storsylen, and the annual Storsylen Opp uphill race starts from here.

rondvassbu-natd968401e.d: Rondvassbu (1,173 metres above sea level) is a tourist lodge in Rondane, and is the largest lodge owned by DNT Oslo og Omegn in this area. Rondvassbu was built in 1903 and purchased by the Norwegian Tourist Association in 1929. Rondvassbu has 128 beds. These are divided between twin rooms, four-bed rooms and dormitories.

bj-rnhollia-natc1e10cdd.d: Bjørnhollia is a staffed tourist cabin in eastern Rondane, owned and run by the Norwegian Trekking Association (DNT). From 1714, the farms Loftsgård, Øvre Dale and Øvre Veggem in Sel held the right to operate mountain pastures in the area. Bjørnhollia had various owners until 1941, when it was purchased and refurbished by the DNT. The building was completed in 1947 with 24 beds (based on a modified design by the architects Henrik Nissen the Younger and Gunnar Brynning), as well as a cart track to Atnsjøen. From 1959, the site was run by Jenny and Hans Øyen. A tractor track was built from Gammelgarden to the cabin in 1966, and from 1972 Bjørnhollia was run by Storm Øyen. Today it has 90 beds and is managed by Beate Øygarden and Svein Aaseng, Heidal in Sel.

finsehytta-natd39eb34a.d: Finsehytta is a tourist chalet in Ulvik in Vestland. The chalet is situated by Finse station on the Bergen Line, 1,222 metres above sea level, and belongs to the Norwegian Trekking Association (DNT). Finsehytta was taken over from the Directorate of Enemy Property by the DNT in 1947 and has been run as a staffed tourist lodge since 1949. The building was originally used as a test facility for aircraft engines by the Germans during the Second World War. The building was taken over by the DNT and converted into a tourist lodge in 1947–1948, and was extended and modernised in 1952, 1961 and 1976. In 2021, a major renovation project was completed, featuring a new entrance hall, reception area, several new bedrooms and shower rooms, a new drying room and a larger dining room.

fondsbu-nataf715e14.d: Fondsbu is situated in the south-west of Jotunheimen. The main building at Fondsbu was originally called ‘Den glade vandrer’ (The Happy Wanderer); it was built in 1932 and owned by the Eidsbugarden Hotel. At the time, it was intended for those who did not fit in with the ‘high society’ at the hotel, where the dress code was a tuxedo (or, if necessary, a dark suit) for dinner. In 1989, Fondsfinans bought the cabin and the name Fondsbu was born. Since 1993, the Norwegian Trekking Association (DNT) has rented the cabin for 1 krone a year as a symbolic amount.

fannarakhytta-nat38811813.d: Fannaråkhytta (2,068 metres above sea level – the outdoor toilet is at 2,065 metres above sea level) on the summit of Fannaråki is Norway’s highest DNT mountain hut. The hut is staffed during the summer season from late June to mid-September; outside the season, it is closed. Fannaråkhytta can be reached from, amongst other places, Skogadalsbøen, Sognefjellshytta, Krossbu and Turtagrø. During the summer season, you can park your car at Hjelle Car Park – not far from the waterfall of the same name, Hjellefossen. From Hjelle, there is a shuttle bus to Turtagrø. It’s a good idea to check the timetable, as this bus doesn’t run nearly as often as you might think.

kr-kkja-nat2f758493.d: Krækkja is a staffed tourist cabin in Hol municipality, Buskerud. The cabin is situated at 1,161 metres above sea level by Lake Storekrækkja, with views towards Hallingskarvet. Krækkja was the Norwegian Tourist Association’s first cabin on Hardangervidda, and the original building dates from 1878. From the cabin, there are marked trails leading to destinations including Finse, Kjeldebu, Tuva and Haugastøl.

fagerheim-fjellstugu-natb278e2e8.d: Fagerheim Mountain Cabin is a private tourist cabin in Hol municipality in Buskerud. The cabin is situated at an altitude of 1,150 metres above sea level on National Road 7 across the Hardangervidda plateau, at the south-eastern end of Store Krækkja. Fagerheim Mountain Lodge was originally built in 1936 and was requisitioned by the Germans during the Second World War. After the war, Fagerheim was rebuilt and converted into a tourist lodge.

storerikvollen-natca9dadf9.d: Storerikvollen is a staffed tourist cabin in the Sylan mountain area in Tydal municipality, Trøndelag. The cabin is run by the Trondheim Tourist Association and is situated on the farmyard of the mountain pasture belonging to the Sjursgarden Vestre farm, at the northern end of Lake Essandsjøen. The tourist cabin was first built in 1896 as an extension to an old mountain farmhouse that stood there, and since then, a series of extensions have meant that Storerikvollen now has 65 beds when the lodge is staffed and 16 during the self-catering season. The cabin is situated in the middle of the ‘Norway Across’ mountain hike from Stjørdal to Sweden, between Ramsjøhytta and Nedalshytta. The tourist cabin lies 769 metres above sea level.

schulzhytta-nat44b4b500.d: Schulzhytta is a staffed tourist cabin situated in the mountain farming village of Stormoen in Skarvan and Roltdalen National Park, in Selbu municipality in Trøndelag. It is owned and run by the Trondheim Tourist Association and is named after Carl Schulz, the association’s first chairman. Schulzhytta is situated halfway between the two mountain ranges surrounding Fongen (1,441 metres above sea level) and Skarvan (Storskarven, 1,171 metres above sea level). The cabin forms part of the ‘Across Norway’ mountain hike from Stjørdal to the Swedish border, together with Kvitfjellhytta, Prestøyhytta, Ramsjøhytta, Storerikvollen and Nedalshytta.

joatkajavri-fjellstue-natbbcf93cc.d: Jotka Mountain Lodge (or: Joatkajávri Mountain Lodge, Northern Sami: Joatka), is a mountain lodge situated south-east of Joatkajávrrit (Sami jávrrit, ‘water’ (plural)) on the Finnmarksvidda plateau in the municipality of Alta. Jotka Mountain Lodge is one of the state’s three mountain lodges situated on the old transport route between Alta and Karasjok. In winter, the snowmobile trail between Alta and Karasjok passes the lodge; in summer, it is about an hour’s walk from the nearest road. Checkpoint on the Finnmarksløpet race. The mountain lodge is staffed and has over 30 beds and a restaurant. The lodge also offers various activities and equipment hire. The Alta–Karasjok route is T-marked, takes four days and includes visits to three of the state-run mountain lodges.

gargia-fjellstue-nat2002dc76.d: Gargia Mountain Lodge is a mountain lodge situated in the village of Gargia in Alta municipality, Finnmark. It was built around 1850 as one of the state-run mountain lodges, and provided accommodation for travellers crossing the Beskades. During the Second World War, the mountain lodge was burnt down by the Germans, but it was rebuilt in 1947 as what is now the main building on the farm. As of 2019, the mountain lodge comprises five buildings, with a restaurant and 12 rooms available for rent.

geiterygghytta-nat76d33d90.d: Geiterygghytta is a staffed tourist association cabin belonging to DNT Oslo og Omegn, situated in Skarvheimen (Buskerud) at an altitude of 1,224 metres. The hut first opened in 1914. It is situated on Geiteryggen at the very top of the Aurlandsdalen valley and is widely used as a starting point for hikes in the valley. Another popular hiking route is Finse–Geiterygghytta. The hut is situated 2 km from County Road 50. The Eira family have managed the hut since 1950. The new managers, as of 2017, are Marit and John Wøllo. Near the hut, you’ll find potholes, Kittilsbuhøla – which was inhabited by a man for 20 years – and animal burrows.

trollheimshytta-natd0e2fe63.d: Trollheimshytta is a staffed tourist lodge situated in the Trollheimen mountain range in Møre og Romsdal and Sør-Trøndelag. The lodge is owned by Trondheim Tourist Association. The lodge has 80 beds during the peak seasons and 26 beds during the self-catering period, when it is locked with the DNT key. It is named after the mountain range in which it is situated, namely Trollheimen.

j-ldalshytta-nateb051e6b.d: Jøldalshytta is a staffed tourist cabin in Trollheimen in Trøndelag. The cabin is owned by Trondheim Tourist Association. The lodge has 80 beds during the season and 16 outside the season, and is locked with a DNT key when it is self-catering, i.e. outside the peak seasons (Easter and summer).

r-yrivannskoia-nata44e3403.d: Røyrivannskoia is an unstaffed overnight cabin in Østmarka, near Oslo. The cabin is run by DNT Oslo og Omegn and is available for use in both summer and winter. The cabin is beautifully situated at 190 metres above sea level by Lake Røyrivannet and just outside the Østmarka Nature Reserve. Guests have access to a canoe, and there are excellent conditions for canoe trips both north and south.

vre-fjellstul-natd3c669f6.d: Øvre Fjellstul is a mountain farmstead that now serves as an unstaffed tourist cabin, rented and run by the Kongsberg and Surrounding Areas Tourist Association, a local branch of the Norwegian Tourist Association (DNT). Øvre Fjellstul is situated in Tinn municipality in Telemark, between Blefjell and Rivsfjell. Until 1967, Øvre Fjellstul was used as a mountain farm. In the summer of 1971, a community work project was organised to restore the farm so that it could be used as a tourist cabin. Øvre Fjellstul is situated at an altitude of approximately 815 metres above sea level.

trollvassbu-nata7c70955.d: Trollvassbu is a tourist cabin in Tromsø municipality in Troms. The cabin is situated 255 metres above sea level and is the north-easternmost of the four cabins on the hiking trail from Snarbyeidet to Tromsdalen. Trollvassbu is unstaffed all year round and has 16 beds. The hut was built in 1916.

sandvatn-nat896a8962.d: Sandvatn Tourist Cabin is a tourist cabin situated by Lake Sandvatnet in the Frafjordheiene mountains in Sirdal municipality, Vest-Agder. The lodge is owned and run by Stavanger Tourist Association. Sandvatn (910 metres above sea level) is easily accessible via a three-hour walk from Lortabu at the head of Hunnedalen. Apart from a fairly steep climb at the start of the walk from Hunnedalen, the route is considered easy, and it is well marked with red ‘T’s and cairns. The walk to Sandvatn Tourist Cabin is well suited to families, and the cabin is often filled with over 30 walkers at weekends during the season. Sandvatn Tourist Cabin has 12 beds, but mattresses for many more. Sandvatn Tourist Cabin is unstaffed and remains open all year round.

patchellhytta-nated08bef8.d: Patchellhytta is a tourist cabin in the western part of the Habostad Valley in Stranda municipality, Sunnmøre. The cabin is situated just a few metres from the municipal boundary with Ørsta, between Brekketindane and Smørskredtindane, just east of the mountain Slogen. The first cabin, built by Charles Watson Patchell (1861–1943) himself, was a small stone cabin completed in 1927. This was used by Patchell and others as a base for climbing the peaks in the area. The surrounding peaks can generally be reached directly from Øye by the fjord (where Patchell himself stayed at a hotel), but a cabin in the Habostad Valley significantly reduced the elevation gain. In 1964, a new and larger cabin was built a couple of hundred metres away.

nordlysobservatoriet-halde-nat5a2d6939.d: The Northern Lights Observatory, Tromsø Geophysical Observatory, is a research institution under the Faculty of Science and Technology at the University of Tromsø. It was established in 1928 and merged with the University when it was founded in 1972. The Northern Lights Observatory is situated near Prestvannet in Tromsø and has six staff members. The Northern Lights Observatory’s first building was constructed in 1927–28 and opened in 1930, after the Rockefeller Foundation had granted $75,000 towards its establishment. Leiv Harang became the observatory’s first director.

kongeveien-over-dovre-oppdal-skaun-nate7.d: The pilgrimage route across Dovrefjell forms part of the medieval road from Oslo to Trondheim. The pilgrimage to the shrine of St Olav in Kristkirken in Nidaros began shortly after his death in 1030 and continued until the Reformation in 1530. Much of the traffic passed over Dovrefjell, the highest and most demanding section of the route in earlier times. King Øystein had shelters built for travellers crossing the mountain. At Vesle Hjerkinn, which lies along the route across Dovrefjell, the Museum of Cultural History has excavated several house foundations dating from the Viking Age and the Middle Ages. Eysteinskyrkja is situated at Hjerkinn. Today, the pilgrimage route is signposted from Oslo along old pilgrimage paths all the way to Nidaros.

gra-ya-naturreservat-natda315078.d: Gråøya Nature Reserve is a Norwegian nature reserve situated in the municipality of Asker in Akershus county.

dokkskj-ret-biotopvernomrade-natf74fe471.d: The Dokkskjæret Biotope Conservation Area is a Norwegian nature reserve situated in the municipality of Bærum in Akershus county.

ytre-vassholmen-naturreservat-nat6cbd0cd.d: The Ytre Vassholmen Nature Reserve is a Norwegian nature reserve situated in the municipality of Bærum in Akershus county.

raudholmane-naturreservat-natc0102d8e.d: Raudholmane is a Norwegian island in Hordaland county, which falls under the administrative jurisdiction of Os.

husberg-ya-naturreservat-natc3b1a346.d: Husbergøya Nature Reserve is a Norwegian nature reserve situated in the municipality of Nesodden, in Akershus county.

bor-ya-naturreservat-nat7b20c87a.d: The Borøya Nature Reserve is a Norwegian nature reserve situated in the municipality of Bærum in Akershus county, south-east of Sandvika.

ebbabreen-natc7a6159d.d: The Ebba Glacier (Ebbabreen in Norwegian) is a glacier in Svalbard.
